The article description gives a steering-system defect that fails technical-safety standards as an example, with a stated fine of 1,000,000–2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (256, 5055); Relationships (840)]

This establishes that technical condition is among the regulatory concerns represented here, but the data does not provide information about actual accident rates, enforcement outcomes, or compliance levels.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two different Article 13 provisions are noted
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 13 entity warns that one description refers instead to Article 13 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, which concerns lane-use rules when vehicles move ahead of others on roads with two or more same-direction motor-vehicle lanes. It identifies that as a separate provision from Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (256)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the community's references: the traffic-condition penalties summarized here belong to the decree provision, while the lane-use topic is described as a separate law provision.

v.tieu_de: Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its provisions on penalties and driving-licence point deductions for specified road-traffic violations by drivers of cars and certain similar vehicles. The connected entities describe several towing- and pushing-related violations, a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified towing conduct, and a separate provision imposing a 10-point deduction for certain referenced violations. The data describes regulatory rules, not evidence that any particular person committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the article’s practical importance for traffic compliance and its stated financial and licence consequences, while the records provide no evidence of actual violations or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 is the community’s regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 is linked to the towing fine, three specific towing or pushing violations, broader driver-violation provisions, and a clause on licence-point deductions. This makes it the central source for the rules represented in the community. [Data: Entities (503); Relationships (2376, 2387, 2388, 2381, 2384, +more)]

The article’s described scope covers drivers of cars, motorized four-wheel passenger vehicles, motorized four-wheel cargo vehicles, and similar vehicles. Its provisions include penalties and point deductions, but the supplied records do not set out every violation or sanction in the article. [Data: Entities (503); Relationships (2384)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified towing violations carry a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified towing-related violations. Article 6 is directly linked to this fine, and the fine is linked in turn to pushing another vehicle or object with a car and two towing violations. [Data: Entities (2115); Relationships (2376, 7105, 7106, 7107)]

The available information does not establish that this range applies to every towing-related act; it applies to the specified violations described in the records. [Data: Entities (2115, 503); Relationships (2376)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pushing another vehicle or object with a car is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, clause 3, identifies driving a car while pushing another vehicle or object as a violation subject to a fine. The records connect this conduct to the specified towing-violation fine. [Data: Entities (4008, 2115); Relationships (2381, 7105)]

The description identifies the conduct but provides no further detail about circumstances, enforcement, or consequences beyond its inclusion as a violation and its connection to the stated fine. [Data: Entities (4008, 2115); Relationships (7105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The article distinguishes prohibited towing from specified exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving a car while towing another vehicle or object is identified as a clause 3 violation, with exceptions for towing a trailer or semi-trailer and for towing a disabled specialized vehicle that cannot move under its own power. The record connects the violation to the stated fine, subject to those exceptions. [Data: Entities (4973, 2115); Relationships (2388, 7107)]

A separate violation concerns towing an additional trailer, vehicle, or object while already towing a trailer or semi-trailer. Article 6 identifies this conduct as subject to a fine, and the fine record is linked to it. [Data: Entities (4970, 2115); Relationships (2387, 7106)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 covers a broader set of driver violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a general entry for road-traffic rule violations by drivers, describing Article 6 as addressing conduct by drivers of cars and motorized four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles, among similar vehicles. It notes fines of 400,000 to 600,000 đồng for certain violations, distinct from the 800,000 to 1,000,000 đồng range associated with specified towing violations. [Data: Entities (4435, 503, 2115); Relationships (2384, 2376)]

The records do not specify which violations attract the 400,000 to 600,000 đồng range, so that amount should not be attributed to any particular conduct in this community. [Data: Entities (4435)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate clause specifies a 10-point licence deduction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 16 of Article 6 states that drivers committing violations specified in point a of clause 9, clause 10, and point đ of clause 11 lose 10 points from their driving licences. The relationship record confirms that clause 16 belongs to Article 6 and describes this deduction. [Data: Entities (895); Relationships (2365)]

The supplied information does not identify those referenced violations as the towing or pushing conduct described elsewhere in the community. Accordingly, the 10-point deduction should be understood as applying to the listed cross-referenced provisions, not assumed to apply to the towing violations. [Data: Entities (895, 4008, 4973, 4970); Relationships (2365, 2381, 2388, 2387)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Road-Rescue Towing Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 29 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its provisions concerning road-rescue vehicles. Clause 3a is linked to a penalty of VND 5,000,000–10,000,000 for towing a vehicle that is not eligible for rescue. The records also distinguish this from the separate Article 6 violation for an unsafe towing connection, which Article 6 excludes from its stated penalty. The information describes regulatory rules, not a particular violation or enforcement case.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory importance because it describes specific road-safety penalties, but the records concern a narrow set of rules and do not identify an actual incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 29 is the community's central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 29 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the central entity, connected both to Clause 3a and to the separately described unsafe-connection violation. Its description says the article sets fines and driving-licence point deductions for drivers of road-traffic rescue vehicles, while also noting an exception identified by Article 6. [Data: Entities (355); Relationships (1447, 1449)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized towing carries a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a penalty for a road-rescue vehicle towing a vehicle that is not eligible for rescue under Clause 1, Article 54 of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. The stated fine is VND 5,000,000 to VND 10,000,000. [Data: Entities (3647)]

Clause 3a of Article 29 is linked to this penalty, and its description likewise specifies the same fine for towing an ineligible vehicle. [Data: Entities (943); Relationships (3458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3a connects the penalty to Article 29
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 3a is identified as part of Article 29 and as the provision specifying the fine for unauthorized towing. This establishes a direct relationship between the broader decree article and the particular penalty rule. [Data: Entities (943, 3647); Relationships (1447, 3458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unsafe towing connections are treated as a distinct violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The unsafe-connection description concerns failing to connect the towing vehicle and the vehicle being towed securely and safely under Article 6, clause 3. It expressly excludes the separately specified violation under Article 29, clause 3a, point b. [Data: Entities (5265); Relationships (1449)]

Accordingly, the records distinguish an unsafe connection from towing a vehicle that is not eligible for rescue; they do not provide the penalty amount for the unsafe-connection violation itself. [Data: Entities (3647, 5265); Relationships (1449)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence concerns rules, not a documented enforcement event
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied entities and relationships describe provisions, violation categories, and a fine amount. They do not identify a driver, a specific towing event, or an enforcement outcome, so the information supports analysis of the regulatory framework rather than conclusions about an actual case. [Data: Entities (355, 3647, 5265, 943); Relationships (1447, 1449, 3458)]

v.tieu_de: Driver’s License Point Deduction and Specified Road-Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns an administrative traffic-penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and the road-traffic violations associated with it. The relationship record links specified violations to a two-point deduction when a transport-business individual directly operates the vehicle. The source also describes Article 8, clause 4 violations with a monetary fine, while cautioning that the cited material does not establish a point deduction for every violation. The available information describes regulatory penalties, not evidence of noncompliance by a particular person or organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory relevance because it describes license-point deductions and fines, but the supplied records indicate no specific case, broader harm, or individual compliance finding.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative measure for deducting driver’s license points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driver’s license point deduction is described as an administrative traffic-penalty measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, applied by an authorized official when a driver commits a covered violation. Depending on the applicable provision, it may accompany a fine or another penalty. [Data: Entities (1562)]

The entity description lists several provisions and vehicle or operator categories, but also notes that the scope and consequence depend on the particular provision. [Data: Entities (1562)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two-point deduction tied to certain transport-business drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a two-point deduction for specified Article 26 violations committed by an individual engaged in transport business who directly drives the vehicle. The relationship record connects those specified violations to the deduction. [Data: Entities (1562, 4727); Relationships (6295)]

This condition is specific to the described driver and conduct; the records do not establish that the same deduction applies to every driver or every violation. [Data: Entities (1562, 4727)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 8, clause 4 violations carry a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified violations entity includes prohibited or hazardous U-turns—such as at railway crossings, on narrow or steep roads, or where visibility is obstructed—and turns made where signs prohibit them. It states a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for these Article 8, clause 4 violations. [Data: Entities (4727)]

The supplied description does not establish that these Article 8 violations also result in a point deduction; the deduction should not be inferred from the separate Article 26 example. [Data: Entities (1562, 4727)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The applicable consequence varies by provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The point-deduction measure is addressed across multiple articles and categories of vehicles and operators, but the source cautions that cited excerpts may state only a fine or mention deduction in a heading without specifying the deduction. [Data: Entities (1562)]

Accordingly, the relationship between the two community entities should be read within the stated conditions and the relevant provision, rather than as a universal penalty for all listed traffic violations. [Data: Entities (1562, 4727); Relationships (6295)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Records describe enforcement details, not an individual case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The measure may involve recording the license holder’s and license details, points before and after deduction, and relevant timing. These are described as possible administrative record details, not as evidence that a particular person’s license has been deducted. [Data: Entities (1562)]

The supplied records identify no named driver, enforcement incident, or finding of misconduct. They therefore support a description of the penalty framework but not conclusions about any individual’s legal compliance or reputation. [Data: Entities (1562, 4727); Relationships (6295)]

v.tieu_de: Article 43, Confiscation Powers, and Social Order Police
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its described administrative-enforcement powers. The article is linked to confiscation of evidence and vehicles and to the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order. The supplied descriptions identify a 30,000,000 đồng confiscation ceiling in one place but also report conflicting limits of 30,000,000 đồng and 45,000,000 VND; they also describe the department director’s remedial-measure and fine powers. The records describe legal authorities, not evidence of particular enforcement actions or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (453, 1084, 3802); Relationships (2078, 2084)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s material administrative-enforcement authority, while the records do not establish actual enforcement activity, violations, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 43 is the community’s legal anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting out administrative-penalty powers for specified People’s Public Security officials. It connects the legal provision to both confiscation authority and the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order. [Data: Entities (453); Relationships (2078, 2084)]

The records therefore indicate a community centered on the allocation of administrative enforcement powers. They do not establish how those powers have been used in practice or whether any particular enforcement action was lawful. [Data: Entities (453, 1084, 3802); Relationships (2078, 2084)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Confiscation authority is described, but its value ceiling is inconsistent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43, Clause 4 is described as identifying officials authorized to confiscate evidence and vehicles used in administrative violations, subject to a specified value ceiling. [Data: Entities (453); Relationships (2078)]

The descriptions conflict on that ceiling: the Article 43 entry gives 30,000,000 đồng, while the confiscation entry says the descriptions give limits of 30,000,000 đồng and 45,000,000 VND and that the applicable ceiling cannot be determined from the provided information. The discrepancy should be resolved against authoritative legal text before relying on a specific limit. [Data: Entities (453, 1084); Relationships (2078)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The social-order police department is linked to remedial powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order is identified as a People’s Public Security department. Article 43, Clause 7 is described in the relationship record as granting its director authority to apply specified remedial measures. [Data: Entities (3802); Relationships (2084)]

The entity description also refers to specified remedial measures, but does not detail what those measures are. The available information supports the existence of described authority, not an assessment of its precise scope or application. [Data: Entities (3802); Relationships (2084)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The department director is described as having a fine ceiling
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The department description states that its director is authorized under Article 43, Clause 6 to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. This is a stated maximum in the supplied description; the records do not provide examples of fines imposed or additional conditions governing that authority. [Data: Entities (3802)]

The relationship record separately associates Article 43, Clause 7 with remedial measures. These descriptions distinguish the reported fine authority from the remedial-measure authority, but the source material does not independently verify the legal text. [Data: Entities (3802); Relationships (2084)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other police officials are referenced, but their powers are not fully specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 43 description says Clause 5 addresses the powers of certain division heads within the Traffic Police Department. It does not identify those officials or state the specific powers in the supplied material. [Data: Entities (453)]

Accordingly, the available records support only a limited characterization of that part of Article 43. They provide no basis for evaluating operational capability, actual conduct, or compliance by those officials. [Data: Entities (453)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Articles 6, 23, and 41
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which describes traffic violations and associated penalties for specified vehicle drivers. Article 41 connects Article 6 and Article 23 by identifying provisions whose violations fall within the penalty authority of specified police units. The records also identify entering an electronic toll lane without a vehicle tag as a violation under Article 6 and associate Article 6 with a monetary fine range of VND 12,000,000–14,000,000 for listed violations, without specifying which violation that range applies to. The information describes regulatory provisions and enforcement authority; it does not establish actual violations, enforcement actions, or compliance by any person or organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it links specified road-traffic penalties with the allocation of police enforcement authority, but the records do not describe actual incidents or compliance outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 sets out administrative penalties and driving-licence point deductions for specified road-traffic violations by drivers of cars, motorized four-wheeled passenger and cargo vehicles, and similar vehicles. Its described scope includes certain stopping, parking, reversing, or turning conduct in road tunnels, as well as entering an electronic toll lane without the required vehicle tag. [Data: Entities (495)]

Article 6 is also linked to Article 41, which refers to specified points and clauses of Article 6 when identifying violations that listed police officials may sanction. This makes Article 6 central both to the described prohibited conduct and to the enforcement-authority relationship in the records. [Data: Relationships (2030)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 41 connects the rules to police penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 41 allocates authority to impose administrative penalties for road-traffic order and safety violations to specified police units. The records do not name the units or provide further detail about their procedures. [Data: Entities (446)]

Article 41 refers to specified points and clauses in Article 6, and to paragraphs 2 through 5 of Article 23, when identifying violations within the described penalty authority. The community therefore links two sets of substantive traffic provisions to the allocation of enforcement authority. [Data: Relationships (2030, 1290)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 identifies electronic toll-lane entry without a tag as a violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe entering a lane reserved for automatic, non-stop electronic toll collection without the required onboard terminal tag as a road-traffic violation. Article 6 identifies this conduct as subject to a fine. [Data: Entities (1800); Relationships (2303)]

The provided information does not specify the fine amount associated with this particular violation, nor does it report an actual instance of the conduct. The separate monetary fine range in the records should not be assumed to apply to toll-lane entry without a tag. [Data: Entities (1800, 3058); Relationships (2303, 2309)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records associate Article 6 with several penalty ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6’s description identifies fines of VND 2,000,000–3,000,000 for certain tunnel-related violations and VND 20,000,000–22,000,000 for certain more serious violations. The description does not enumerate all underlying conduct associated with those ranges. [Data: Entities (495)]

A separate relationship states that Article 6 specifies a fine range of VND 12,000,000–14,000,000 for listed violations. The associated fine entity describes it as a monetary penalty for a driver committing one of the specified violations, but the supplied records do not identify which violation the range applies to. [Data: Entities (3058); Relationships (2309)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 23 covers dangerous-goods transport violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 23 describes penalties and driving-licence point deductions for automobile drivers who violate regulations on transporting dangerous goods. It also provides corrective measures when such violations cause environmental pollution. [Data: Entities (326)]

Article 41 refers to paragraphs 2, 3, 4, and 5 of Article 23 when specifying violations subject to penalties. This establishes a link between the dangerous-goods provisions and the enforcement authority described in Article 41, but the records do not establish any specific violation or pollution event. [Data: Relationships (1290); Entities (326, 446)]

v.tieu_de: Alcohol-Related Motorcycle Violation and Fine
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a defined alcohol-related motorcycle traffic violation and the monetary fine prescribed for it. The violation is linked to a fine of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Article 7, Clause 8 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP; the description also says deduction of driving-license points may result. The records describe a legal rule, not a specific incident or enforcement case.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to road-safety compliance and a specified financial penalty, while the records provide no evidence of a particular incident, enforcement action, or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is defined by specified alcohol-concentration ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described motorcycle or similar-vehicle violation applies when blood alcohol concentration is above 50 and up to 80 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood, or breath alcohol concentration is above 0.25 and up to 0.4 milligrams per liter of breath. These thresholds define the scope of the violation in the provided record. [Data: Entities (151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The prescribed fine is 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich: The monetary penalty associated with the specified violation is stated as 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese dong. The fine is represented both in the violation description and as a separate fine entity. [Data: Entities (151, 3178); Relationships (491)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records cite a specific legal basis
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation record attributes the penalty to Article 7, Clause 8 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, while the fine record describes the same penalty as prescribed under Clause 8 of Article 7 of that decree. The provided information identifies the legal provision but does not include further details about its application or interpretation. [Data: Entities (151, 3178)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-license point deduction may also apply
phat_hien.giai_thich: In addition to the monetary fine, the violation description states that deduction of driving-license points may result. The record does not specify the number of points or when a deduction is imposed, so no further conclusion about those details is supported. [Data: Entities (151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A direct relationship links the violation to its fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community has a simple structure: the alcohol-related motorcycle traffic violation is connected to the motorcycle traffic violation fine, and the relationship explicitly identifies the fine as the monetary penalty prescribed for that violation. The supplied records do not identify a specific driver, vehicle, incident, or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (151, 3178); Relationships (491)]

v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes statutory vehicle requirements and multiple financial and administrative consequences, while providing no evidence of a specific violation or broader operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition violations are the community’s central topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:

[Data: Entities (1284, 5481); Relationships (5611)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Consequences include sanctions beyond monetary fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes a narrow regulatory-compliance community

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community concerns road-traffic violations and administrative penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its central connection is between violations and driving-license point deductions, with Article 7 addressing penalties for motorcycle and similar-vehicle operators and a separate record specifying a fine of 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain violations. The available descriptions indicate that consequences depend on the conduct and provision involved; they do not establish that every violation incurs each penalty. [Data: Entities (1710, 4433, 542, 3059); Relationships (6552, 2548, 8990)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public relevance because it covers a broad set of road-traffic rules and sanctions, while the records do not establish the prevalence or consequences of particular violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Broad regulatory coverage of road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe road-traffic violations addressed by Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP across multiple vehicle categories. Article 6 covers drivers of cars and similar vehicles, Article 7 addresses motorcycle and similar-vehicle operators, and other provisions cover rudimentary vehicles and additional road-traffic rules. [Data: Entities (4433)]

The described penalties vary by vehicle and conduct. The data therefore supports viewing this as a broad regulatory framework, but does not provide a complete catalogue of all covered violations or their consequences. [Data: Entities (4433)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-license point deductions depend on the specific conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:

The relationship records connect the deduction measure with the broader category of road-traffic violations. [Data: Entities (1710, 4433); Relationships (6552)]

The provided description gives examples of deductions of two, three, or four points for specified conduct, but cautions that many other excerpts do not state an amount or establish that a deduction applies to the particular violation. phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 7 covers penalties for motorcycle and similar-vehicle operators
phat_hien.giai_thich:

Its described provisions include fines and driving-license point deductions, and the entity record identifies fines of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain violations. [Data: Entities (542)]

The relationship between Article 7 and point deductions confirms that the article addresses this penalty for covered violations. The data does not specify that every Article 7 violation results in a deduction. [Data: Relationships (2548); Entities (542)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate record specifies a high monetary fine for certain violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:

The provided information does not identify the specific conduct associated with this amount, so the fine should not be attributed to all road-traffic violations or to a particular vehicle category based on these records alone. [Data: Entities (3059); Relationships (8990)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalties are provision- and conduct-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions distinguish among fines, point deductions, and possible vehicle confiscation, and indicate that the applicable consequences depend on the vehicle and the conduct involved. Some excerpts refer to provisions without listing the underlying violations or penalties. [Data: Entities (4433, 1710, 542)]

Accordingly, the records support a general picture of varied administrative consequences, but not a determination of the penalty for any individual case without the specific violation and applicable provision. [Data: Entities (4433, 1710)]

v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical significance because it links vehicle-document and registration violations to substantial fines and license-point deductions, although no specific incidents or enforcement outcomes are provided.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized or altered vehicle documents are a central violation

Its degree of 7 is higher than the other listed entities, making it the most connected entity in this dataset. [Data: Entities (5340)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalties include fines and driver’s-license point deductions

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data supports compliance relevance, but not a finding of actual misconduct

This is relevant to understanding regulatory compliance exposure for vehicle use and documentation. [Data: Entities (5340, 5482, 2260); Relationships (7328, 7329)]

No individual, organization, vehicle, incident, investigation, or enforcement outcome is identified in the supplied records. Accordingly, the information supports describing the rules and their stated consequences, but not attributing a violation or assessing the conduct of a particular party.

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Road-Traffic Regulation
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, a broad administrative framework for road-traffic order and safety. Its connected provisions address conduct by drivers, vehicle owners, transport operators, and organizations involved in manufacturing, assembly, inspection, testing, driver training, and related services. The decree combines monetary fines and driving-licence point deductions with remedial measures, vehicle or document sanctions, and enforcement powers assigned to designated officials. The records also highlight freight and passenger-transport controls, monitoring and image-recording requirements, and specified effective-date and transitional rules. [Data: Entities (1282); Relationships (5302, 5175, 5429, 5039, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the decree has wide reach across road users, transport businesses, vehicles, and enforcement, with substantial penalties and compliance requirements.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad, central regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the hub of this community: the listed relationships connect it to provisions and violations spanning traffic conduct, transport services, vehicle condition, licensing, and enforcement. The decree’s stated scope includes individuals and organizations, including Vietnamese and foreign parties operating in Vietnam. [Data: Entities (1282); Relationships (5302, 5241, 5598, 5485, +more)]

The entity description also identifies a broad range of covered road users and activities, from drivers and pedestrians to vehicle owners and transport, rescue, inspection, training, and testing services. This breadth makes the decree important to both individual compliance and organizational operations. [Data: Entities (1282)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Multiple enforcement tools and sanctioning authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree uses monetary fines, driving-licence point deductions, and other measures. The records specifically identify vehicle confiscation for specified violations and point deductions for certain driver and vehicle-owner violations. [Data: Entities (5381, 3054, 1711, 1713); Relationships (5568, 5250, 5031, 5032)]

Enforcement authority is assigned to designated officials and bodies. For example, the records identify a head of a Traffic Police Department professional division and a border-gate police post chief as having sanctioning authority under specified provisions. The decree’s entity description also notes procedures for violation records, technical-equipment detections, temporary custody, and licence-point administration. [Data: Entities (2437, 664, 1282); Relationships (5175, 2882)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Serious driving conduct can attract substantial penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed provisions cover conduct that can create significant road-safety risks. The records identify speeding while chasing and weaving or swerving as violations associated with fines of 40,000,000–50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng; the decree also provides for fines and point deductions for specified violations. [Data: Entities (3054, 4733, 5633); Relationships (5459, 5605, 5250)]

Other examples include improper lane changes on expressways, failure to yield to priority vehicles, and failure to yield at intersections, each with specified fines in the supplied records. These examples demonstrate that the framework addresses both high-penalty conduct and more routine traffic-rule breaches. [Data: Entities (2603, 2064, 2063); Relationships (5204, 5100, 5099)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Freight and commercial transport obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree links freight compliance to vehicle dimensions, load limits, permits, signage, and technical documentation. Transporting oversized or overweight cargo beyond dimensions allowed by a valid permit is associated with an 8,000,000–10,000,000 đồng fine and a driving-licence point deduction; transporting such cargo without required size signage is associated with a 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng fine. [Data: Entities (3506, 5144); Relationships (5302, 5513)]

Separate records address overloading beyond the capacity stated in an inspection certificate, correction of permitted cargo weight before road use, and dangerous goods transported without required labels or warning signals. These provisions make cargo documentation and vehicle configuration salient compliance issues for operators. [Data: Entities (4516, 3699, 5134); Relationships (5429, 5334, 5509)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monitoring and image-recording data are regulated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify violations involving falsified journey-monitoring data, use of an ineffective journey-monitoring device, and failure to record or store required driver-image data. They also describe falsification of driver-image data as a violation. These provisions make device operation and data integrity part of the decree’s compliance framework. [Data: Entities (2083, 3391, 2023, 2081); Relationships (5106, 5289, 5088, 5105)]

The decree’s passenger-compartment image-recording provisions have a specified effective date of January 1, 2029. The supplied records therefore distinguish that future effective date from other monitoring-related rules, although they do not provide further implementation detail. [Data: Entities (1740); Relationships (5039)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Accountability extends to owners and organizations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree does not address only the person driving at the time of a violation. Its vehicle-owner provisions include fines and driving-licence point deductions, and the records describe penalties where an owner directly commits, or allows an employee or representative to commit, specified conduct. Some listed owner fines differ between individuals and organizations. [Data: Entities (3633, 5587, 1711); Relationships (5321, 5599, 5031)]

The covered organizational landscape also includes vehicle manufacturing, assembly, inspection, and testing establishments, while other provisions address driver training and testing. This indicates that regulatory exposure in the community includes service providers and businesses as well as road users and vehicle owners. [Data: Entities (2977, 589, 3091, 4911); Relationships (5241, 2730, 5256, 5485)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Remedial measures, document controls, and timing rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Beyond fines, the decree includes corrective and administrative measures. The records describe required return of licences or professional practice certificates that have been altered to falsify their contents, and procedures for recovering expired, unauthorized, altered, or improperly issued documents, subject to the stated handling of cases showing signs of a crime. [Data: Entities (2972, 4047); Relationships (5239, 5370)]

The decree also includes transitional rules tied to its effective date, and a separately specified January 1, 2029 effective date for passenger-compartment image-recording provisions. The supplied information does not establish the decree’s general effective-date value, so no specific date is asserted here. [Data: Entities (1734, 1740); Relationships (5037, 5039)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32, Clause 3: Traffic-Disrupting Vehicle Equipment
v.tom_tat: This community links Clause 3 of Article 32 to a defined road-traffic violation: installing or using sound or lighting equipment on motorcycles, mopeds, or similar vehicles in a way that disrupts traffic order and safety. The clause sets fines for individual and organizational vehicle owners, and points a and b are identified as provisions covering the sanctionable violations. The information describes a focused regulatory and road-safety topic; it does not provide fine amounts or further enforcement details. [Data: Entities (929, 1409); Relationships (3440)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest impact because it concerns a defined traffic-safety violation and fines, but the records provide no information about its scale, enforcement, or consequences beyond that scope.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 is the central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 32 is the central entity in this community and is described as setting fines for specified vehicle owners who install or use disruptive sound or lighting equipment.

Its sole recorded relationship connects the clause to the traffic-disruption violation it addresses, making the community narrowly focused on that rule and conduct. [Data: Entities (929); Relationships (3440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The covered conduct concerns disruption of traffic order and safety
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is defined as installing or using sound or lighting equipment on a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle in a way that disrupts road-traffic order and safety.

The relationship explicitly connects this conduct to the fines established by Clause 3. The records do not specify examples of disruptive use or how disruption is assessed. [Data: Entities (1409); Relationships (3440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Both individual and organizational owners are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 is described as applying fines to individual and organizational owners of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles when the specified equipment-related conduct disrupts traffic order and safety.

The provided information does not distinguish the applicable treatment of individuals from organizations, or provide details about responsibility where an owner did not personally install or use the equipment. [Data: Entities (929)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sound and lighting equipment are both within scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provision covers installing or using sound equipment as well as lighting equipment on motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles, provided the conduct causes the described disruption.

The records do not identify particular equipment types, technical capabilities, or thresholds for determining when use disrupts traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (929, 1409); Relationships (3440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify the sanction framework but not its details
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available description states that Clause 3 sets fines and notes that points a and b are referenced as provisions covering the sanctionable violations.

No fine amounts, enforcement procedures, incident frequency, or outcomes are included. Consequently, the community supports identifying the rule's general subject and covered parties, but not assessing implementation or the severity of specific penalties. [Data: Entities (929)]

v.tieu_de: Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Permit-Contrary Oversized or Overweight Transport
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the specified transport violation, and its stated fine of VND 13,000,000 to VND 15,000,000. The article connects the conduct—carrying oversized or overweight goods that do not match the type listed in a valid circulation permit—to the monetary penalty. The records describe a regulatory provision and sanction, not a particular driver, enforcement action, or incident.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the practical importance of a defined transport-compliance rule and substantial stated fine, while the records identify no specific incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22 is the community’s central regulatory reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the central entity, linked both to the specified conduct and to the applicable fine. Its description also notes provisions concerning oversized or overweight goods and carrying more people than permitted, although the other records in this community focus on the goods-permit violation. [Data: Entities (322); Relationships (1270, 1271)]

The records therefore establish a narrow regulatory connection: the article provides the basis for the violation and its stated penalty. They do not describe how the rule is enforced in any particular case. [Data: Entities (322); Relationships (1270, 1271)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The specified violation concerns a mismatch with the circulation permit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The conduct identified is transporting oversized or overweight goods under a valid circulation permit when the goods carried do not match the type specified in that permit. Article 22 is linked directly to this violation. [Data: Entities (5145, 322); Relationships (1271)]

The records describe this as a defined compliance issue; they do not identify a driver, vehicle, shipment, or actual occurrence of the conduct. [Data: Entities (5145, 322); Relationships (1271)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is VND 13,000,000 to VND 15,000,000
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 22 is described as prescribing a monetary fine of VND 13,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 for the specified permit-related transport violation. The penalty is connected both to Article 22 and to the violation itself. [Data: Entities (2238, 5145, 322); Relationships (1270, 7298)]

This is the fine range recorded for the described conduct; the supplied information does not detail aggravating or mitigating factors, additional sanctions, or how a fine would be determined within the range. [Data: Entities (2238, 5145)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data distinguish the rule, the conduct, and the sanction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s three entities represent separate parts of the regulatory relationship: Article 22 is the legal reference, transporting goods contrary to the permit is the conduct, and the VND 13,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 range is the penalty. The relationships explicitly connect these elements. [Data: Entities (322, 2238, 5145); Relationships (1270, 1271, 7298)]

This structure makes the stated compliance consequence clear, but it is limited to the rule and penalty as described in the records and does not establish outcomes in any individual case. [Data: Relationships (1270, 1271, 7298)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information is regulatory rather than incident-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe a legal provision, a type of violation, and a fine. They do not name an individual or organization subject to the rule, report an enforcement action, or provide evidence of a specific violation. [Data: Entities (322, 2238, 5145); Relationships (1270, 1271, 7298)]

Accordingly, the community supports an assessment of the described compliance requirement and its stated financial penalty, but not conclusions about a particular entity’s compliance history, technical capabilities, or reputation. [Data: Entities (322, 2238, 5145); Relationships (1270, 1271, 7298)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Transport Violations and 3–5 Million Đồng Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to four specified transport violations. One is operating without a required or valid transport permit, which is identified under Article 37, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The other three concern carrying animals, foul-smelling goods, or other goods that may affect passengers’ health in a passenger vehicle, and are described as subject to the fine under Article 20. The records provide regulatory information but no evidence about actual violations, enforcement outcomes, or the conduct of any particular person or organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it summarizes monetary penalties for permit and passenger-vehicle transport violations, but the records show no specific incident, actor, or wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single monetary penalty connects four specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. Its recorded relationships connect it to operating without a valid transport permit and to three categories of goods or animals carried in a passenger vehicle. This makes the fine the organizing point of the community rather than an individual, company, or enforcement case. [Data: Entities (2180, 3358, 5125, 5136, 5141); Relationships (7187, 7188, 7189, 7190)]

The records describe prescribed penalties; they do not establish that a violation occurred or that a fine was imposed in any particular case. [Data: Entities (2180); Relationships (7187, 7188, 7189, 7190)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit-related violation is tied to Article 37, Clause 3
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The permit violation is described as operating a vehicle without the required inter-transport or international road transport permit, or operating with an expired permit. The stated fine for this violation is 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (3358, 2180)]

Article 37, Clause 3 is identified as the provision specifying penalties for drivers of road motor vehicles with foreign registration plates, including the violation of operating without a valid transport permit. The relationship records that the provision identifies this conduct as punishable. [Data: Entities (419); Relationships (1776)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-vehicle restrictions cover three categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify transporting animals in a passenger vehicle and transporting foul-smelling goods in a passenger vehicle as violations subject to the stated fine under Article 20. [Data: Entities (5125, 5136, 2180); Relationships (7188, 7189)]

A third listed category is transporting other goods in a passenger vehicle that may affect passengers’ health. It is also described as subject to the same fine. The records do not specify further examples or explain how the potential health effect is assessed. [Data: Entities (5141, 2180); Relationships (7190)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the most connected entity in this community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity has a recorded degree of 6, while the permit violation has degree 3 and Article 37, Clause 3 has degree 2. Each of the three passenger-vehicle violation entities has degree 1. This pattern reflects the fine’s role as the shared connection among the listed violations. [Data: Entities (2180, 3358, 419, 5125, 5136, +more)]

The relationship records likewise show the fine connected to all four violation categories, while Article 37, Clause 3 is connected to the permit violation. [Data: Relationships (7187, 7188, 7189, 7190, 1776)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support regulatory scope, not conclusions about enforcement or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available information describes legal provisions, violation categories, and an associated fine amount. It contains no named drivers, transport operators, enforcement actions, court outcomes, compliance history, technical capabilities, or reputation assessments. Accordingly, the community can be characterized as a compact regulatory-information network, but the records do not support claims about real-world compliance or enforcement impact. [Data: Entities (2180, 3358, 419, 5125, 5136, +more); Relationships (7187, 7188, 7189, 7190, 1776)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32, Clause 9: Inspection-Related Car-Part Violations
v.tom_tat: This small community links the violation of renting or borrowing car parts while a vehicle is undergoing inspection with the monetary fines and driving-license point deductions specified for that conduct. The records describe fines of 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng for individuals and 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizations that own the specified vehicles, and identify Article 32, clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as the provision. The data do not specify point-deduction amounts or establish any particular person's or organization's compliance status.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory relevance because it concerns fines and license-point consequences for a defined vehicle-inspection violation, but the records identify no specific case, affected party, or broader operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a specific inspection-related violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The conduct described is renting or borrowing car components or accessories while the vehicle is undergoing inspection. The record associates this violation with Article 32, clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (4123)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fines differ by vehicle-owner category
phat_hien.giai_thich: The stated fine range is 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng for individual vehicle owners and 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizational vehicle owners who commit the listed violation. The records therefore distinguish the stated penalties according to the owner category. [Data: Entities (3069, 4123)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalty record also refers to driving-license point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The monetary-penalty entity describes driving-license point deductions as also addressed by the provision. It does not give a number of points or further detail about how deductions are applied, so those particulars cannot be determined from these records. [Data: Entities (3069)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The entities are directly connected through the stated fines
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship links the fines and driving-license point deductions to renting or borrowing car parts during inspection, stating that the fines apply to vehicle owners who commit this inspection-related violation. This makes the penalty description and the conduct the two connected elements of the community. [Data: Relationships (8996); Entities (3069, 4123)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a regulatory topic, not an individual compliance finding
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied data describe a violation and its stated penalties but do not identify a person or organization that committed it, a specific enforcement action, or any determination of compliance. The community is therefore relevant to understanding the stated rule and consequences, but it does not support conclusions about actual violations or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (3069, 4123); Relationships (8996)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Vehicle Restoration and Re-Inspection
v.tom_tat: This community links three Article 32 provisions—Point D, Clause 11; Point H, Clause 14; and Point C, Clause 16—to a shared remedial process: restoring a vehicle to its original condition and technical safety, then passing re-inspection before returning to traffic. The data describes the provisions and process but does not identify specific cases, enforcement outcomes, or responsible authorities. [Data: Entities (5490, 3782, 3787, 3776); Relationships (9641, 9640, 9638)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it connects multiple provisions to a safety-related vehicle remedy, while the data shows no specific incident or enforcement outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: One remedial process connects three provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Each of the three listed Article 32 provisions is connected to Vehicle Restoration and Re-Inspection, with each relationship stating that conduct covered by that provision triggers the measure. This makes the remedial process the community's central entity. [Data: Relationships (9641, 9640, 9638)]

The descriptions identify the provisions as referenced in Clause 19 of Article 32, but do not provide the underlying text of that clause or define the conduct covered by each provision. [Data: Entities (3782, 3787, 3776)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The measure combines restoration with a return-to-traffic condition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The process requires a vehicle to be restored to its original shape and dimensions and returned to a technically safe condition. It must then pass re-inspection before it can be used in traffic again. [Data: Entities (5490)]

The described sequence establishes re-inspection as a condition for the vehicle's return to traffic; the data does not specify inspection standards or who conducts the inspection. [Data: Entities (5490)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three distinct provisions are tied to the same measure
phat_hien.giai_thich: Point D, Clause 11; Point H, Clause 14; and Point C, Clause 16 are each separately linked to the restoration and re-inspection process. This indicates that the measure applies to conduct associated with multiple provisions, without establishing that the provisions cover the same conduct. [Data: Entities (3782, 3787, 3776); Relationships (9641, 9640, 9638)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on vehicle safety remediation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The process description explicitly requires the vehicle to be returned to a technically safe condition before it can be used in traffic again. This gives the community a direct vehicle-safety dimension, although the records do not describe actual vehicles, hazards, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (5490)]

The connected provisions are described as triggering this process, but the available information does not specify the nature or severity of the conduct involved. [Data: Entities (3782, 3787, 3776); Relationships (9641, 9640, 9638)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specific enforcement and compliance outcomes are not provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe a required remedial process and its connection to three provisions, but provide no case details, inspection results, penalties, compliance rates, or information about the authorities responsible for implementation. Accordingly, the material supports describing the stated process, not assessing how it is applied in practice. [Data: Entities (5490, 3782, 3787, 3776); Relationships (9641, 9640, 9638)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, a provision addressing penalties for vehicle owners in specified road-traffic violations. Its connected entities cover registration and restricted-use violations, cross-referenced provisions in Articles 21 and 34, possible driving-licence point deductions, and a vehicle-restoration measure. The supplied information describes regulatory requirements but does not identify specific cases, affected people, fine amounts, or enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the provision’s broad relevance to vehicle-owner compliance and associated remedies, while the data contains no specific enforcement cases or quantified penalties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is the hub connecting the identified violation types, cross-referenced provisions, point deductions, and remedial action. Its description says it sets penalties for vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations or allow or direct others to do so, including fines and, where applicable, driving-licence point deductions. [Data: Entities (372); Relationships (1610, 1593, 1237, 1609, 1611, +more)]

The supplied material describes the scope of a legal provision; it does not establish that any particular owner has committed a violation or faced a penalty. [Data: Entities (372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision covers owner conduct involving other drivers and vehicle use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32’s description includes conduct involving employees or representatives, such as assigning or permitting a vehicle to be used by someone who does not meet legal requirements, and allowing a vehicle to carry more passengers than permitted. This indicates that the described scope extends beyond an owner’s own driving. [Data: Entities (372)]

The data does not specify particular instances, affected parties, or the applicable fine amounts for these types of conduct. [Data: Entities (372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration and restricted permissions are linked violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One connected category is operating a vehicle without a registration certificate, or with a document that is expired or no longer valid. The description notes an exception where the original certificate is held by a credit institution or foreign bank branch and required supporting documents are carried. [Data: Entities (3365); Relationships (1610)]

Another category concerns use of a vehicle with temporary registration or restricted operating permissions beyond its allowed period, route, or area. Article 32 is described as specifying penalties for this conduct. [Data: Entities (3343); Relationships (1609)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 incorporates provisions from Articles 21 and 34
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 13 of Article 32 refers to violations defined in Article 21, Clause 6, points a and b. The supplied entity description identifies this cross-reference but does not describe the underlying violations themselves. [Data: Entities (316); Relationships (1237)]

Article 32 also cites Article 34, Clause 4(c), and Article 34, Clause 5, point a, as bases for penalties against a vehicle owner. The data does not specify the nature of those underlying violations, so their substance cannot be assessed from this material. [Data: Entities (408, 409); Relationships (1593, 1594)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Potential consequences include point deductions and vehicle restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provision is associated with deductions from driving-licence points for covered violations, in addition to fines. The supplied data does not state the number of points deducted or which specific violations trigger a deduction. [Data: Entities (1702, 372); Relationships (1604)]

Clause 19 is described as requiring restoration of a vehicle’s registered brand and paint colour in specified cases, so the provision includes a remedial measure as well as penalties. The exact circumstances requiring restoration are not detailed in the supplied text. [Data: Entities (4192, 372); Relationships (1611)]

v.tieu_de: Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Passenger-Capacity Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its penalties for passenger-vehicle traffic violations. The connected records address carrying more passengers than permitted, the related per-passenger administrative fine, and conduct such as evading inspection, threatening or insulting passengers, and competing for or soliciting passengers. The records describe legal provisions and fines, but do not provide enforcement outcomes or information about specific operators. [Data: Entities (301, 735, 43, 1068, 4945); Relationships (1112, 98, 1126, 1128, 1130, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects a traffic-regulation provision to passenger-capacity violations, monetary penalties, and several forms of conduct addressed by the provision.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as governing penalties and driving-licence point deductions for drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles who violate traffic-order and safety requirements. Its stated scope includes route-information requirements, oversized or overweight cargo, and carrying more passengers than permitted. [Data: Entities (301)]

The relationships make Article 20 the hub of the community, linking it to the excess-passenger violation and to several forms of conduct addressed under Clause 6. This structure indicates that the records concern regulatory requirements and consequences, rather than a particular transport business or enforcement case. [Data: Relationships (1112, 1126, 1128, 1130, 1117)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess passenger capacity is addressed through distinct penalty descriptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Carrying more passengers than a vehicle is permitted to carry is identified as a violation, with penalties depending on the vehicle type and the applicable provision. The descriptions include a cited range of 1,000,000–2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Article 28 and, for passenger cars or other covered vehicles, 400,000–600,000 đồng per excess passenger, subject to a stated maximum and exception. [Data: Entities (735)]

Article 20 is connected to this violation, while the description of the connection notes a stated exception. The records therefore do not support treating all cited amounts as one universal penalty. [Data: Relationships (1112); Entities (735)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The administrative fine is described per excess passenger, with a maximum
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The administrative fine record specifies a penalty of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for each excess passenger, capped at 75,000,000 đồng. The relationship records connect this fine both to Article 20, which establishes the per-passenger fine and maximum, and to the underlying excess-passenger violation. [Data: Entities (43); Relationships (98, 99)]

The broader violation description also refers to Article 32 provisions concerning per-person fines and maximum total fines for vehicle owners. These are described as provisions applicable in different circumstances, so the available information does not establish that every cited amount applies in every case. [Data: Entities (735)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify multiple ways of evading overloading or passenger-capacity detection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 6 of Article 20 is linked to other acts intended to avoid detection of excessive cargo or too many passengers. A specifically identified example is making passengers get off to evade inspection. [Data: Relationships (1126, 1128); Entities (3447, 4009)]

These entries describe conduct covered by the provision; they do not report that any particular driver committed it or provide information about investigations or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (3447, 4009); Relationships (1126, 1128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 6 also addresses passenger treatment and passenger solicitation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect Article 20, Clause 6 to threatening or insulting passengers and to competing for or enticing passengers. The Article 20 description states that Clause 6 sets fines of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations, including threatening or insulting passengers and attempts to evade detection of excess passengers or cargo. [Data: Entities (301, 4945, 1068); Relationships (1130, 1117)]

These entries establish that the regulatory community extends beyond vehicle capacity to specified driver conduct involving passengers. They describe the rules, not actual incidents, compliance rates, or the reputation of any driver or operator. [Data: Entities (301, 4945, 1068); Relationships (1130, 1117)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Owner Penalty Procedure and Acquisition or Transfer
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a procedure concerning penalties for vehicle owners and a related vehicle acquisition-or-transfer concept. The relationship states that people or organizations acquiring a vehicle by purchase, transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance may be treated as its owner for penalty purposes. The material establishes this connection but does not specify particular penalties, a jurisdiction, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (3656, 5366); Relationships (9511)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has potential practical relevance because vehicle acquisition can affect who is treated as an owner for penalty purposes, but the supplied information is limited to a narrow procedural connection.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalty procedure is the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The procedure is described as covering principles for penalizing vehicle owners, including people or organizations treated as owners under the decree. It is the central entity in the supplied relationship, which connects the procedure to acquisition or transfer. [Data: Entities (3656); Relationships (9511)]

The record does not provide the procedure's specific steps, penalties, or enforcement details, so those aspects cannot be assessed from this information. [Data: Entities (3656)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Acquisition or transfer can determine owner treatment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship states that people or organizations who acquire a vehicle by purchase, transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance may be treated as its owner for penalty purposes. This makes acquisition or transfer relevant to the procedure's owner classification. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

The wording describes possible treatment for penalty purposes; it does not establish that every acquirer is automatically treated as an owner in every circumstance. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described rule includes both individuals and organizations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The acquisition-or-transfer description applies to an individual or organization, and the relationship likewise refers to people or organizations who acquired a vehicle. The scope described is therefore not limited to individual vehicle holders. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

No further distinctions between individuals and organizations, or between different kinds of organization, are provided. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several forms of acquisition are identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied text lists purchase, transfer, exchange, gift, and inheritance as ways a vehicle may be acquired for purposes of the owner classification. These categories define the acquisition scenarios explicitly represented in this community. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

The information does not describe how these categories are documented or whether additional conditions apply to any of them. [Data: Entities (5366)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports only a limited procedural assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records establish a connection between a vehicle-owner penalty procedure and a rule that may treat certain acquirers as owners for penalty purposes. They do not identify a jurisdiction, particular cases, actual penalties imposed, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (3656, 5366); Relationships (9511)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is best understood as a potentially relevant classification rule within a vehicle penalty procedure; broader conclusions about enforcement, legal compliance, or impact are not supported by the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3656, 5366); Relationships (9511)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger-Vehicle Traffic Violations and 600,000–800,000 Đồng Fine
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a category of traffic-order and safety violations by drivers of passenger-carrying cars and similar vehicles, and a monetary fine range. The relationship states that the 600,000–800,000 đồng fine applies to one of the violations covered by Article 20; the data does not identify the specific violation or provide further legal or enforcement details.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a narrow regulatory topic and a specified fine range, without evidence of broader community reach or impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Community centers on passenger-vehicle traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The primary entity describes violations of traffic-order and safety regulations by drivers of passenger-carrying cars and similar vehicles. It identifies these as violations for which Article 20 provides penalties. [Data: Entities (5034)]

The records do not enumerate the conduct covered or provide details about the number or frequency of violations. [Data: Entities (5034)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine range is linked to the violation category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity specifies a monetary penalty range of 600,000 to 800,000 đồng. The relationship record says this range is specified for one of the violations covered by Article 20. [Data: Entities (2222); Relationships (7263)]

The record does not identify which particular violation attracts this range. [Data: Entities (2222); Relationships (7263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 is the stated penalty framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation-category description says Article 20 provides penalties for the covered traffic-order and safety violations. The available data does not provide the text of that article or other details about its scope. [Data: Entities (5034)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a simple, direct structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records contain two entities joined by one relationship: the violation category and the fine range. The relationship connects the fine to one covered violation, rather than establishing that the range applies to every violation in the category. [Data: Entities (5034, 2222); Relationships (7263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to the stated category and penalty range
phat_hien.giai_thich: No additional entities or relationships are provided to establish enforcement practices, legal outcomes, affected parties, or broader effects. Accordingly, the supported finding is limited to the described violation category and its stated connection to a fine range. [Data: Entities (5034, 2222); Relationships (7263)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger-Vehicle Badge Violation and Administrative Fine
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a defined passenger-vehicle badge violation and the administrative fine associated with it. The violation covers operating a passenger vehicle without a required badge, failing to display one, using an expired badge, or using a badge not issued by a competent authority. The stated penalty is a fine of 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 VND. The supplied information establishes this legal penalty relationship but provides no further details about enforcement, affected parties, or broader impacts.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a specific administrative violation and monetary penalty, with no evidence of broader or more severe impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation covers several passenger-vehicle badge failures
phat_hien.giai_thich: The defined violation includes operating a passenger vehicle without the required badge, not displaying the badge, using an expired badge, or using a badge not issued by a competent authority. These conditions form the stated scope of the violation. [Data: Entities (3586)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine of 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 VND is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify an administrative fine with a lower bound of 5,000,000 VND and an upper bound of 7,000,000 VND. The amount is linked specifically to the passenger-vehicle badge violation. [Data: Entities (63, 3586); Relationships (137)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship is a direct violation-to-penalty link
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied relationship states that the passenger-vehicle badge violation is subject to the specified fine. It establishes a direct administrative consequence, rather than documenting an individual enforcement case or a separate legal dispute. [Data: Relationships (137)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a narrow, two-entity structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The provided records identify two entities: the badge violation and the fine. The single listed relationship connects the fine to the violation, so the available data describes a compact regulatory topic rather than a broader network of organizations or individuals. [Data: Entities (3586, 63); Relationships (137)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish enforcement or wider consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich: The information specifies the covered conduct and the associated fine, but does not identify actual enforcement actions, affected operators, compliance rates, or further consequences. Accordingly, the evidence supports describing the stated penalty, but not drawing conclusions about how often it is applied or its wider effects. [Data: Entities (3586, 63); Relationships (137)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 47 Road-Traffic Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 47, which refers to provisions in two Vietnamese legal instruments: Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Its relationships connect the article to drivers, Chapter II penalty procedures, passenger and goods transport, and violations involving passenger capacity, road use, loads, and dimensions. The material describes regulatory requirements and enforcement processes, but does not establish that any particular person or vehicle has violated them.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the broad regulatory relevance of the provisions to road safety, transport activity, and traffic enforcement, while the data identifies no specific incident or actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 47 has two distinct legal meanings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The name “Article 47” refers to provisions in both Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Law No. 36/2024/QH15, so its meaning depends on which instrument is cited. The decree concerns procedures and principles for sanctioning road-traffic violations, while the law addresses order and safety when specified vehicles transport passengers or goods. [Data: Entities (462)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the community’s connected topics: the data links Article 47 both to penalty procedures and to transport safety requirements. [Data: Entities (462); Relationships (2141, 2156, 2150)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions connect drivers to traffic enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47 is linked to vehicle drivers through procedures and principles for sanctioning drivers who violate road-traffic rules. The entity description also says drivers are subject to applicable traffic rules and enforcement procedures. [Data: Entities (5394); Relationships (2159)]

The supplied information describes potential enforcement consequences, not evidence that a particular driver has committed an offense. It also notes that specified violations may result in vehicle confiscation under Article 35, but does not identify any actual case. [Data: Entities (5394)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overlapping violations are addressed through Chapter II
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47(3) is connected to Chapter II of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The relationship describes how penalties are applied when the same person’s conduct violates multiple provisions of that chapter. [Data: Entities (803); Relationships (2141)]

This indicates that the community includes rules for handling overlapping provisions, including circumstances involving the same person or a vehicle owner who was also the direct operator. The data does not provide a specific enforcement decision or outcome. [Data: Entities (462)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger and goods transport is a central safety topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47 is linked to road transport of passengers and goods and to passenger and goods transport using two-wheeled and rudimentary vehicles. The described requirements address safe loading and limits on passengers, cargo weight, and vehicle dimensions. [Data: Entities (4488, 3556); Relationships (2156, 2150)]

The transport description also states that loose goods, construction materials, and waste must not spill onto roads or cause noise or dust. These are stated regulatory requirements; the data does not report whether any operator complied with them. [Data: Entities (4488)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community covers several categories of road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Connected violation topics include carrying more passengers than permitted, using roadways or sidewalks for other purposes, and exceeding vehicle or road load and dimension limits. Each is linked directly to Article 47 in the relationship data. [Data: Entities (1872, 4582, 5436, 5434); Relationships (2147, 2157, 2162, 2161)]

Passenger-capacity violations appear both as a general transport issue and as a distinct violation category addressed by Article 47. The records establish the scope of the provisions, but do not identify actual violations or their frequency. [Data: Entities (3579); Relationships (2151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law includes visible cargo-marking requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description for Article 47 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 states that cargo extending beyond a vehicle must be marked in red at the front and rear during daylight; in darkness, lights or other signals must be used. [Data: Entities (462)]

This requirement forms part of the community’s broader emphasis on safe transport by motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and rudimentary vehicles. No evidence is provided about a particular vehicle, transport operator, or compliance inspection. [Data: Entities (462, 3556); Relationships (2150)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Sanctioning and Load-Compliance Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative sanctioning of road-traffic violations under procedures described as covered by Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The sanctioning framework is linked to load and dimension violations, environmental-protection violations, and failure to secure transported goods.
