phat_hien.tom_tat: Ineligible issuance is a stated ground for revocation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The dataset identifies issuance of a permit to someone who was not eligible to receive it as a circumstance stated in Article 22(3). It explicitly connects that circumstance to revocation of the permit. [Data: Entities (2763); Relationships (8106)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit expiration is a separate stated ground
phat_hien.giai_thich: Expiration is described as a circumstance in which a permit has passed its period of validity. The relationship data identifies an expired permit as a ground for revocation, distinct from issuance to an ineligible recipient. [Data: Entities (1905); Relationships (6843)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is limited to permit validity and eligibility
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe two specific conditions tied to revocation: recipient ineligibility and expiration. No other grounds for revocation are identified in the provided records, so the report cannot establish whether the list is exhaustive. [Data: Entities (1905, 2763, 4237); Relationships (8106, 6843)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No enforcement or outcome details are provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records define the circumstances associated with revocation but do not describe who administers the rule, how a revocation is carried out, or what penalties or consequences may follow. Accordingly, the community supports a description of the stated grounds, not conclusions about implementation or real-world outcomes. [Data: Entities (1905, 2763, 4237); Relationships (8106, 6843)]

v.tieu_de: Minister of Public Security and Police Traffic Regulation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the unnamed Minister of Public Security, whose statutory responsibilities connect police forces and police drivers with rules for training, licensing, examinations, and age requirements. The minister also sets standards for driving examiners and examiner-card issuance, and has responsibilities concerning vehicle registration plates and traffic-control technology. The information describes regulatory authority and operational provisions; it does not establish whether those rules are being followed or identify wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (3001, 3807, 1608, 1609, 1607, +more); Relationships (8734, 1761, 6359, 6357, 8733, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high institutional importance because one ministry role is linked to broad road-traffic regulation and to specialized rules affecting police personnel, licensing, examinations, and traffic systems.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The minister is the community’s central regulatory authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister of Public Security is the central node, with connections to police forces, police drivers, driving examiners, examiner training, examiner-card issuance, and vehicle registration plates. The entity description attributes a broad range of road-traffic and ministry-related responsibilities to this unnamed office. [Data: Entities (3001); Relationships (8734, 1761, 6359, 6357, 8733, +more)]

The supplied information identifies legal authority and assigned functions, not an individual officeholder or evidence of how the responsibilities have been exercised in practice. [Data: Entities (3001)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Special rules govern police personnel’s driving qualifications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The minister prescribes driver training, driving tests, and minimum age requirements for police forces performing national-security or security duties. The police-force description also notes that members’ licence formats, issuance, and use are governed by ministerial regulations and, where applicable, those of relevant ministers. [Data: Entities (3807, 3803, 3211); Relationships (8734, 8733, 9138, 9669)]

The rules apply to a defined operational context: police members performing the stated security duties. The supplied records do not specify the actual age thresholds or training requirements. [Data: Entities (3807, 3803, 3211); Relationships (8734, 8733)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The minister sets standards for driving examiners and their training
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving examiners are subject to minister-prescribed eligibility and qualification standards, and the minister also prescribes the organization of their training. The records connect examiner training to the examiners who receive it. [Data: Entities (1608, 1609); Relationships (6359, 6357, 6356)]

The minister additionally prescribes requirements for issuing examiner cards, which are issued to driving examiners. These provisions establish an administrative framework for examiner qualification and identification, but the records provide no specific standards or information about implementation. [Data: Entities (1607, 1609); Relationships (6355, 6354)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle registration and traffic rules are part of the minister’s remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 36 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is linked to the minister’s authority to prescribe other types of vehicle registration plates. The minister’s entity description also identifies responsibilities for specified registration-certificate and plate issuance and revocation procedures, subject to an exception in Article 39. [Data: Entities (414, 3001); Relationships (1761)]

The minister’s stated remit extends beyond registration to driving-licence examinations and use, road-traffic-law training, traffic patrol and control, and procedures for investigating and resolving road-traffic accidents. These records describe assigned regulatory functions rather than outcomes or compliance findings. [Data: Entities (3001)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community includes traffic technology and operational systems
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The minister is described as issuing national technical regulations and prescribing rules for the construction, management, operation, and use of traffic command centers and specified road-traffic monitoring and technical systems. This gives the office a stated role in the regulatory framework for traffic-related technology. [Data: Entities (3001)]

The supplied records do not identify particular systems, their technical specifications, deployment status, or operational performance; conclusions about those matters are therefore not supported.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police forces have defined vehicle and data arrangements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Police vehicles are designated priority vehicles when used for urgent duties and may use priority signal devices when responding to emergencies. This is a stated operational provision and does not, by itself, indicate misuse or any particular incident. [Data: Entities (3807)]

The police-force description also says that specified police vehicle-inspection data and data relating to driver training, licensing, road-traffic-law certificates, and vehicle operators are excluded from the databases and responsibilities assigned to the Ministries of Transport and Construction. The records do not explain the resulting data-management arrangements beyond that exclusion. [Data: Entities (3807)]

v.tieu_de: Foreigners and Foreign Vehicle Tourism in Vietnam
v.tom_tat: This community centers on foreign nationals bringing and operating foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam for tourism under an approved arrangement. Vietnamese international travel-service businesses may organize such trips, subject to an approval procedure, while the foreign nationals are connected to legal requirements for entry, exit, residence, and transit. The information provided describes a regulatory and administrative framework, including itinerary and residence requirements and possible suspension for violations; it does not establish particular cases of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (2357, 2340, 5550, 5084, 1903); Relationships (7519, 7560, 6741, 7555, 7556, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it involves regulated cross-border travel, vehicle approval, and several legal procedures, but the provided records describe a framework rather than specific violations or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign nationals are the central participants
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around foreign nationals who bring and operate foreign motor vehicles on Vietnam’s roads for tourism under an approved arrangement. The records connect them to the vehicle-approval procedure, travel-service businesses, the tourism activity itself, and the entry, exit, residence, and transit procedures. [Data: Entities (2357, 2340, 5550, 2321, 5084); Relationships (7519, 7560, 6741, 7555, 7556, +more)]

The description states that participants must follow applicable entry and exit procedures, adhere to the registered program and itinerary, and declare temporary residence as required by law. These are stated requirements, not evidence that any particular participant has complied with or breached them. [Data: Entities (2357); Relationships (6741, 6840, 7555)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vietnamese travel-service businesses organize eligible tourist trips
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnamese international travel-service businesses are described as licensed businesses that may organize tourist trips in which foreigners bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam, subject to approval. Their role makes them an organizational link between foreign participants and the regulated tourism activity. [Data: Entities (5550, 2321); Relationships (7560)]

To obtain approval, these businesses must submit the prescribed dossier to the Traffic Police Department. The records identify this filing requirement but do not specify the dossier’s contents, processing times, or approval outcomes. [Data: Entities (5550, 2340); Relationships (7519, 7560)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A dedicated procedure governs foreign-vehicle arrangements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The foreign vehicle approval procedure applies to arrangements involving foreigners bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism when organized by Vietnamese international travel-service businesses. This makes prior administrative approval a central feature of the described tourism arrangement. [Data: Entities (2340, 5550, 2357); Relationships (7519, 7560)]

The procedure’s stated scope is broader than tourism alone: it also covers organizations or individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes. The available records do not provide further details on requirements for that separate category. [Data: Entities (2340)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The tourism activity is bounded by program and stay requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The regulated activity is specifically described as foreigners bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism. The foreign nationals must adhere to the registered program and itinerary, and declare temporary residence as required by law. [Data: Entities (2321, 2357); Relationships (7443, 7555)]

The relevant decree is described as addressing departure timing and the permitted period of stay. The records do not state the specific time limits or other detailed conditions, so those particulars cannot be assessed from this information. [Data: Entities (2357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Multiple immigration and residence procedures apply
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s legal framework includes procedures for foreigners’ entry into Vietnam, departure from Vietnam, residence in Vietnam, and transit through Vietnam. The relationships explicitly link these procedure categories to foreign nationals, showing that vehicle tourism sits alongside broader movement and residence rules. [Data: Entities (1817, 1903, 2356, 5084, 2357); Relationships (6741, 6840, 7555, 7556)]

The records establish that these procedures are governed by Vietnamese law or must be completed under applicable law, but they do not supply their detailed steps, documentation, or timelines. [Data: Entities (1817, 1903, 2356, 5084); Relationships (6741, 6840, 7555, 7556)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violations may lead to suspension, but no specific incidents are documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of the foreign-national framework states that violations of Vietnamese law may result in suspension of the arrangement. This indicates a stated enforcement consequence for the regulated arrangement. [Data: Entities (2357)]

The provided records do not identify any individual or business that violated the rules, any suspension that occurred, or any resulting harm. Accordingly, the material supports describing regulatory consequences, but not asserting actual noncompliance or reputational damage. [Data: Entities (2357, 5550, 2340)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Foreign Vehicle Traffic and Entry Regulation
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around Vietnam and the legal and administrative framework governing foreign motor vehicles and their drivers. Its connected activities include tourism-related vehicle entry, general road use, convoy traffic, and the separately regulated use of right-hand-drive vehicles. The records describe application and approval processes, driver-document and immigration requirements, monitoring, enforcement, and possible re-export measures; they establish regulatory significance but do not document specific violations or incidents. [Data: Entities (5538, 2348, 2325, 2314, 5456); Relationships (7543, 7453, 7420, 10670, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public and administrative importance because it covers cross-border vehicle movement, road safety, and enforcement in Vietnam, although the records describe rules and procedures rather than actual violations or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vietnam is the central jurisdiction and regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnam is the common jurisdiction for the community’s activities, including foreign vehicle entry and exit, tourism, road use, and right-hand-drive vehicle participation. The entity description identifies Decrees 151/2024/NĐ-CP and 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Law 36/2024/QH15 as part of the applicable legal framework, and references national and local public bodies and road-traffic databases. [Data: Entities (5538); Relationships (6737, 7543, 7453, 7428, +more)]

The breadth of these subjects makes the community relevant to transport administration, public safety, and cross-border mobility. The provided records describe the framework and responsible bodies, but do not establish how effectively the rules are implemented. [Data: Entities (5538)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicle tourism is subject to an approval and service arrangement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign Vehicle Tourism in Vietnam is described as an activity in which visitors bring foreign motor vehicles into the country through an approved Vietnamese international travel service enterprise. The records also identify foreign visitors and foreign motorists as participants in this activity. [Data: Entities (2348, 2352, 2324, 2744); Relationships (7543, 7553, 7451, 8063)]

The framework also covers temporary vehicle entry for purposes such as tourism, fairs, exhibitions, sporting events, and conferences. [Data: Entities (4964, 2074, 1901, 4745, 1080); Relationships (10526, 7062, 6838, 10453, 3894)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign drivers face traffic, licensing, and document requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign national drivers operating foreign vehicles in Vietnam are required to comply with Vietnamese road-traffic order and safety laws and carry required documents. The descriptions also refer to valid driving documents, international driving permits, and mutual recognition arrangements under agreements signed by Vietnam. [Data: Entities (2325, 2317, 2306, 2734); Relationships (7453, 7428, 7394, 8043)]

A driver using a foreign motor vehicle must carry and present the vehicle’s temporary import and re-export customs declaration when requested by a competent authority. The community also connects these traffic activities with applicable entry, exit, transit, and residence requirements for foreign nationals. [Data: Entities (2320, 1818); Relationships (7442, 6743)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Right-hand-drive vehicle use is treated as a distinct regulated case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars participating in Vietnamese traffic from other foreign vehicle use. They describe tourism and non-tourism scenarios, including non-tourism use arranged by organizations or individuals and subject to approval under the cited provisions. [Data: Entities (2335, 2355, 4261, 4257, 4263); Relationships (7508, 7554, 9996, 9993, 9998)]

Vietnamese individuals and organizations are also identified as potential participants in non-tourism right-hand-drive vehicle use, while the descriptions specify a procedure or approval requirement. This indicates a defined regulatory pathway, not unrestricted use; the records do not state approval outcomes. [Data: Entities (5543, 5551, 2658, 2659, 3720); Relationships (10691, 10695, 7941, 7942, 9611)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Convoy traffic includes real-time monitoring and reporting
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign motor vehicle convoy traffic is described as being monitored and reported in real time through a mobile application. The activity is situated within Vietnam’s road-traffic environment, connecting operational oversight with the broader national regulatory framework. [Data: Entities (2314, 5538); Relationships (7420)]

The supplied information does not specify the application’s operator, the data collected, or how reports are acted upon. Accordingly, the records support the existence of the described monitoring arrangement, but not conclusions about its effectiveness or privacy practices. [Data: Entities (2314)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes enforcement and potential re-export measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe responsibilities for handling certain violations by foreign drivers and identify re-export of a foreign-plated vehicle from Vietnam as a remedial measure. This links road-traffic compliance with consequences affecting a vehicle’s continued presence in the country. [Data: Entities (2325, 5456, 5538); Relationships (7453, 10670)]

Diplomatic missions may be notified about specified legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign vehicles, and the records also refer to accidents involving diplomatic personnel or vehicles. These are described as procedural circumstances; no particular accident or violation is reported. [Data: Entities (1359); Relationships (5821)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Applications and cross-border rules involve multiple authorities and legal instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes applicant organizations, individuals, and international travel service businesses seeking approval for foreign vehicle entry or use. It also identifies a competent Vietnamese authority in connection with driving-licence issuance, showing that the described processes involve both private applicants and public authorities. [Data: Entities (198, 197, 2744, 1044); Relationships (599, 598, 8063, 3761)]

International treaties and agreements on mutual recognition of international driving permits are part of the described legal context. The text states that an applicable international treaty may govern when its provisions differ from the relevant Vietnamese traffic rules, indicating that some cases may involve international as well as domestic requirements. [Data: Entities (2748, 2734); Relationships (8069, 8043)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Right-Hand-Drive Traffic Violations

v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is limited because the community concerns a specific regulatory issue, while the available records provide no evidence of actual violations, enforcement scale, or broader impact.

phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity RESOLUTION OF VIOLATIONS describes the handling of violations involving certain foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. phat_hien.giai_thich: RIGHT-HAND-DRIVE VEHICLE TRAFFIC PARTICIPATION is specifically defined as non-tourism use of a right-hand-drive car in traffic in Vietnam by an organization or individual. The record states that this topic is addressed by Article 33, but does not provide the article’s full text or identify a particular actor. [Data: Entities (4262)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship directly links this traffic activity to violation handling
phat_hien.giai_thich: The sole recorded relationship states that the provision includes handling violations involving right-hand-drive cars used in Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes. phat_hien.tom_tat: The broader resolution scope also includes a tourism-related category
phat_hien.giai_thich: The RESOLUTION OF VIOLATIONS description covers violations involving previously approved arrangements for foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism, as well as non-tourism use of right-hand-drive cars. The supplied relationship focuses on the latter category; no further details about the tourism-related cases are given. [Data: Entities (4183); Relationships (9954)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish compliance or enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data describes the subject matter of a provision and its relationship to a type of vehicle use. It does not identify a specific violation, regulated person or organization, enforcement action, penalty, or compliance status, so conclusions about actual conduct or enforcement effectiveness are not supported. [Data: Entities (4183, 4262); Relationships (9954)]

v.tieu_de: Articles 11 and 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP

Article 12, Clause 2 identifies a source for information referenced in Article 11, Clause 6: the driver training and licensing database. The records establish a narrow regulatory link concerning information in the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database, but provide no evidence about implementation, compliance, or operational effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has some regulatory and data-governance importance because it links two decree provisions to a specified information source, but the evidence describes only this limited statutory relationship.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 provides the information-source link
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is titled “Collection of information in the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database.” Its Clause 2 specifies a source for information referenced in Article 11, Clause 6. [Data: Entities (245); Relationships (726)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 11, Clause 6 is the referenced provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 11 is identified as a provision of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, and its Clause 6 contains the information to which Article 12, Clause 2 refers. phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated source is a driver training and licensing database
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description for Article 11 states that, according to Article 12, Clause 2, the information in Article 11, Clause 6 is collected from the driver training and licensing database. phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions form a narrowly defined regulatory connection
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship record describes Article 12, Clause 2 as referring to information specified in Article 11, Clause 6. The connection is thus a targeted reference about the source of information within the decree’s Road Traffic Order and Safety Database context. [Data: Entities (238, 245); Relationships (726)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records do not establish implementation or compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied descriptions identify the provisions, their cross-reference, and the stated database source. They do not provide information about how the provisions are implemented, whether any entity complies with them, or what operational outcomes result; those matters cannot be assessed from this evidence. [Data: Entities (238, 245); Relationships (726)]

v.tieu_de: Priority Vehicle Signal Device Permit Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community consists of two administrative procedures under Article 21 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: new issuance and reissuance of permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. The procedures are linked because both concern the same type of permit and are listed together in Article 21. The supplied records establish their subject and relationship but do not describe eligibility, processing requirements, responsible authorities, or outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it covers two related permit procedures for signal devices on priority vehicles, while the supplied information does not establish broader effects or implementation details.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two procedures form the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains a procedure for new issuance and a procedure for reissuance of permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. Their relationship record explicitly groups them as permit procedures for the same purpose. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083); Relationships (9147)]

The records describe only these two procedures and do not identify additional entities in the community. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083); Relationships (9147)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Both procedures are associated with Article 21
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The new-issuance procedure is described as referenced in Article 21 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The reissuance procedure is likewise described as referenced in that article. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083)]

The relationship record also says the procedures are listed together in Article 21, providing a shared statutory reference for the pair. [Data: Relationships (9147)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The procedures distinguish new issuance from reissuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One procedure concerns issuing a new permit, while the other concerns reissuing a permit. This distinction is explicit in the names and descriptions of the two entities. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083)]

The supplied records do not explain what circumstances qualify for reissuance or how its requirements differ from those for a new permit. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The subject is narrowly focused on priority-vehicle signal devices
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Both procedures concern permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles, rather than describing a broader range of permits or vehicle-related processes. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083); Relationships (9147)]

The records establish the administrative subject matter but provide no details about the devices, vehicle categories, or operational rules for their use. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operational and implementation details are not provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions identify the procedures and their reference to Article 21, but do not state who administers them, what documents applicants must submit, how long processing takes, or what outcomes are possible. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083)]

Accordingly, the supplied information supports identifying and relating the procedures, but does not support conclusions about compliance performance, technical capabilities, or practical effects. [Data: Entities (3228, 4083); Relationships (9147)]

v.tieu_de: Article 13 and Road Traffic Safety Database Updates
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Article 13 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and the activity of updating information in the road traffic order and safety database. The sole relationship states that clause 1 of the Article describes that activity. The available information identifies a regulatory provision and a database-maintenance function, but does not specify the data sources, implementation details, or whether any compliance issue exists. [Data: Entities (257, 5285); Relationships (848)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has bounded but relevant importance because it connects a cited legal provision to updates in a road traffic order and safety database, while the evidence provides little detail about implementation or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 is the stated regulatory reference
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community identifies Article 13 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, specifically clause 1, as the provision describing the database-update activity. The supplied records do not provide the text of the decree beyond this description. [Data: Entities (257); Relationships (848)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The activity concerns updates to a road traffic safety database
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described activity is adding and adjusting information in the database on road traffic order and safety. This establishes the subject of the activity, but the records do not enumerate the information being added or adjusted. [Data: Entities (5285)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision and activity are directly linked
phat_hien.giai_thich: The single recorded relationship states that clause 1 of Article 13 describes the activity of updating information in the database. This makes the legal provision the community's connection to the database-maintenance function. [Data: Relationships (848)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Updates are described as using specified sources
phat_hien.giai_thich: The activity description says that information is added or adjusted using specified sources. The sources themselves are not named in the available records, so their nature and reliability cannot be assessed from this evidence. [Data: Entities (5285)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and implementation cannot be assessed from the available evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify a provision and describe an associated activity, but do not state whether a particular organization or person performed the activity, how it was carried out, or whether it complied with the provision. Accordingly, the supplied information does not establish either compliance or a violation. [Data: Entities (257, 5285); Relationships (848)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: Priority Signal Requirements
v.tom_tat: This small regulatory community links Article 19 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP with Appendix I: Article 19 addresses signals and technical requirements for signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles, while Appendix I sets out technical requirements for priority signal lights. The records specify permitted flashing-light colors but do not establish whether any vehicle or organization complies with those requirements. [Data: Entities (191, 292); Relationships (574)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has focused regulatory and technical significance for priority-vehicle signaling, but the provided records show no broader operational impact or evidence of compliance outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A narrowly focused regulatory community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community consists of two provisions associated with Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: Article 19 and Appendix I. Their relationship concerns technical requirements for priority signal lights, making the community focused on regulatory requirements rather than a wider set of actors or activities. [Data: Entities (191, 292); Relationships (574)]

The records do not identify vehicle operators, enforcement bodies, or implementation activity, so the scope supported here is limited to the provisions and their stated connection. [Data: Entities (191, 292); Relationships (574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 19 addresses priority-vehicle signals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 19 is described as addressing signals and technical requirements for signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles. Its paragraph 1 specifies that priority signals may use flashing red lights, flashing blue lights, or flashing blue and red lights. [Data: Entities (292)]

The record identifies the permitted signal colors but does not provide further technical specifications or explain how the provisions are applied in practice. [Data: Entities (292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Appendix I contains technical requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Appendix I to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting out technical requirements for priority signal lights. This makes it the community's identified location for those technical requirements. [Data: Entities (191)]

The supplied description does not enumerate the requirements themselves, so no further detail about equipment design or performance can be established from this record. [Data: Entities (191)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship assigns a complementary role to each provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole recorded relationship states that Article 19 specifies that the technical requirements for priority signal lights are set out in Appendix I. This links Article 19's treatment of priority-vehicle signals to the appendix's technical requirements. [Data: Relationships (574)]

The data therefore supports a connection between the provisions, but does not describe additional legal interpretation or how the requirements are enforced. [Data: Relationships (574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and implementation outcomes are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe regulatory content, including permitted flashing-light colors and the location of technical requirements, but do not identify any vehicle or organization as compliant or noncompliant. [Data: Entities (191, 292); Relationships (574)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is evidenced as regulatory and technical in scope; the supplied information does not support conclusions about compliance rates, enforcement, or real-world effects. [Data: Entities (191, 292); Relationships (574)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police Department and Director
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Traffic Police Department, led by a Director and supported by professional divisions. Its documented responsibilities span vehicle-entry and signal-device permits, traffic-law examinations, administrative sanctions, and management of violation data. The Department also interfaces with foreign diplomatic and consular bodies and local authorities through application and coordination procedures. The supplied information describes statutory responsibilities and capabilities, but does not establish compliance outcomes, misconduct, or operational performance beyond specified procedures. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 3256, 182); Relationships (5861, 4514, 9211)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high institutional importance because it combines national traffic-administration, permitting, examination, data-management, and enforcement responsibilities.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department is the community’s central administrative hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Department is described as a department of Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security and as a channel for reporting implementation issues to the Ministry. Its relationships connect it to the Director, professional divisions, application procedures, diplomatic bodies, and government authorities, indicating a broad coordinating role. [Data: Entities (5026); Relationships (5861, 5938, 9211, 7817, 3944)]

The listed functions make the Department consequential to road-traffic administration, but the supplied records do not quantify its activity levels or demonstrate results. The evidence supports an assessment of institutional importance rather than a finding of effectiveness or compliance. [Data: Entities (5026)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Director holds broad leadership and enforcement responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director is identified by office rather than by personal name and heads the Department. The role includes oversight of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA implementation, management of road-traffic legal-knowledge examinations, and organization of research and science-and-technology activities. [Data: Entities (1385, 2556, 4173, 2884); Relationships (5861, 5856, 5857, 5859)]

The Director also manages and operates the administrative-violation database and has specified authority to impose sanctions and remedial measures. These are substantial administrative powers; the records describe the powers but do not identify individual enforcement cases or assess their use. [Data: Entities (1385, 2951); Relationships (5858)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-entry procedures include applications from foreign and diplomatic parties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department receives applications to authorize right-hand-drive vehicles for non-tourism use in Vietnam. The described procedure accepts dossiers through the Ministry of Public Security’s public service portal, by post, or by direct submission; for complete and valid applications under the relevant procedure, the Department is described as issuing written approval or refusal within five working days. [Data: Entities (3256, 5026); Relationships (9211)]

Consular agencies, foreign diplomatic missions, and representative offices of intergovernmental organizations may provide diplomatic notes or official dispatches explaining a vehicle’s purpose. The Department is identified as the recipient of dossiers involving these materials, demonstrating a formal interface with foreign entities. [Data: Entities (1101, 2304, 2305, 2730); Relationships (3944, 7390, 7392, 8036)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department issues permits and coordinates with other authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department is named as an authority for issuing, reissuing, and revoking permits to use signal devices on eligible priority vehicles associated with central-level ministries, sectors, and agencies. The stated exception is military vehicles on urgent missions. [Data: Entities (5026, 753, 754, 1272); Relationships (4514, 3058, 3059)]

The Department also issues operating permits for intelligent transport vehicles, except those serving national-defense purposes, and sends specified approvals to relevant provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees for coordination. These duties place it within a wider administrative network. [Data: Entities (5026, 3671); Relationships (9540)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Statutory sanctioning powers are extensive, but case outcomes are not provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the Department’s Director and heads of professional divisions have specified administrative-sanctioning authority. The Director’s listed powers include fines up to 75 million Vietnamese đồng, confiscation of objects or vehicles involved in violations, temporary revocation of permits or professional certificates, suspension of operations, and designated remedial measures. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 3908)]

The Director is also described as able to restore driving-licence points in specified cases, while the Department’s website publishes or updates information about vehicles involved in violations and licences whose points have been deducted or restored. The records establish these powers and publication functions, not the number, fairness, or outcomes of enforcement actions. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department has examination and digital-system responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department receives examination applications, checks their validity, and can provide an expected examination time and place. It organizes training and issues examiner cards for legal-knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety; the Director is responsible for managing this examination work. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2884); Relationships (5857, 8556)]

The Department’s test computers connect over the Ministry’s WAN to a server hosted by the Department, which supports the testing system and stores connection and data-editing logs. The Director also manages the administrative-violation database, indicating responsibility for both examination technology and enforcement-related information systems. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2951)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Professional divisions support specialized functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department includes professional divisions covering vehicle registration and inspection, driver training, testing and licensing, road and rail patrol and control, traffic control and escort, traffic-safety communication and accident resolution, and data management and digital transformation. These divisions are identified as organizational units within the Department. [Data: Entities (1433, 1420, 1422, 1423, 1424); Relationships (5938, 5913, 5914, 5915, 5916)]

The supplied records also identify the head of a vehicle-registration and inspection division among officials with sanctioning authority. This links specialized administration with enforcement, although the available information does not specify the divisions’ staffing, resources, or performance. [Data: Entities (1433, 3908); Relationships (9751)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Regulatory procedures include refusal or suspension grounds
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described amendment to Article 33 under Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP concerns approval procedures for foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and right-hand-drive vehicles used for non-tourism purposes. It includes grounds for refusal, notification, and suspension, and directs applicants to submit dossiers to the Department. [Data: Entities (182); Relationships (560)]

The records identify legal-violation cases and violations of previously approved conditions as possible grounds for refusal or suspension by the competent authority that previously issued approval. This indicates procedural controls, but the data does not provide specific cases or establish how often these grounds are applied. [Data: Entities (2879); Relationships (8545)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and Road-Traffic Safety
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, a Vietnamese government decree dated November 15, 2024, implementing the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Its connected provisions cover road-safety education, traffic databases, priority-vehicle signals, intelligent-vehicle permits, and the participation of foreign vehicles and drivers in Vietnam. Related entities include prescribed application forms, technical appendices, administrative processes, and the earlier Decree 109/2009/NĐ-CP, which the newer decree repeals upon taking effect. The material describes a broad regulatory framework; it does not provide evidence about implementation outcomes or specific compliance violations. [Data: Entities (1270); Relationships (4262, 4387, 4389, 573)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad national scope across road-safety rules, data governance, vehicle operations, and foreign-vehicle participation, rather than evidence of specific harms or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A central framework spanning multiple road-safety domains
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is the central entity in this community and is described as implementing the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Its scope includes education, traffic-safety data, vehicle equipment and operation, and foreign vehicles and drivers in Vietnam. [Data: Entities (1270)]

The relationships connect the decree to many specific procedures and regulated activities, indicating that it serves as an umbrella framework rather than addressing a single traffic issue. The records establish the breadth of its subject matter, but do not establish how effectively its provisions are being applied. [Data: Relationships (4387, 4406, 4483, 4445, 4056)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic-safety database provisions establish information-governance requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree’s Articles 9–15 address principles for building, managing, using, connecting, and sharing the road traffic order and safety database and related specialized databases. The described data may cover vehicles, drivers, insurance, accidents, violations, transport businesses, journeys, and driver images. [Data: Entities (1270)]

The decree identifies results of administrative procedures and information from related professional activities as sources for database updates. This indicates a framework for collecting and updating regulatory information, although the records do not describe the database’s technical architecture, security controls, or actual operation. [Data: Entities (94, 4095); Relationships (247, 4469)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education is part of the decree’s preventive approach
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 4–8 address legal education on road traffic order and safety across preschool, primary, lower-secondary, upper-secondary, and vocational education. The decree also provides for safe motorbike-riding instruction for students and assigns responsibilities to education authorities and institutions. [Data: Entities (1270)]

The education activity is explicitly linked to the decree, which specifies its content. The records establish the inclusion of education in the regulatory framework, but do not report participation levels or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4389); Relationships (4483)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signals are governed by technical and licensing provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 17–24 regulate signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles, including technical requirements, eligible vehicles, installation, permits, renewals or replacements, revocation, and management. Appendix I is described as setting technical requirements for signal devices, including sirens. [Data: Entities (1270, 190); Relationships (573)]

The decree also specifies the signal used by an ambulance on an emergency response mission: a flashing red light and a priority siren. Form No. 02A in Appendix II is identified as the prescribed form for a new permit to use a signal device on a priority vehicle. [Data: Entities (168, 2360); Relationships (4389, 524)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent and smart transport vehicles are subject to operating permits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses licensing and operation of intelligent or smart transport vehicles, including application documents, licensing authorities, permit replacement or reissuance, and grounds for revocation. The records identify an application procedure and a process for granting a smart-traffic-vehicle operating permit. [Data: Entities (1270, 2715, 2409); Relationships (4406, 4394)]

These provisions show that operation is tied to administrative authorization in the described framework. The available information does not specify the vehicles’ technical capabilities or establish how many permits have been granted. [Data: Entities (2907, 3407); Relationships (4413, 4445)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicle participation involves eligibility, customs, and operating conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 32–36 address foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers participating in road traffic in Vietnam. The described requirements include eligibility, registration and licensing, customs and temporary import or re-export procedures, permitted routes and periods, documentation, insurance, and compliance with Vietnamese traffic laws. [Data: Entities (1270, 2345); Relationships (4387, 4056)]

The decree also covers approval and responsibilities for international travel businesses arranging foreign-vehicle tourism, and for organizations or individuals arranging right-hand-drive vehicle entry for non-tourism purposes. The records establish these regulatory conditions but do not indicate whether any particular entrant or organizer has complied or violated them. [Data: Entities (3438, 2643); Relationships (4447, 4397)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree assigns broad coverage and includes enforcement-related information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is described as applying to domestic and foreign agencies, individuals, and organizations involved in matters related to road traffic order and safety in Vietnam. This gives the framework a broad range of covered actors. [Data: Entities (1436, 1437, 1438); Relationships (4371, 4372, 4373)]

The decree’s database provisions include information about the handling of administrative violations, and a related entity identifies administrative violation handling as an enforcement activity under the decree. These records indicate that violations are within the framework’s scope, but they do not document particular violations or enforcement results. [Data: Entities (117, 1270); Relationships (371)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP replaces an earlier priority-signal decree
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 109/2009/NĐ-CP is described as a 2009 government decree regulating signals of vehicles entitled to priority. The relationship data states that Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP repeals it from the newer decree’s effective date. [Data: Entities (1262, 1270); Relationships (4262)]

This establishes a regulatory transition for the subject matter covered by the earlier decree. The records do not provide the effective date or detail the practical effects of the transition beyond the stated repeal.

v.tieu_de: Priority-Vehicle Signaling Equipment Regulation
v.tom_tat: This community consists of two related regulatory subjects: management, installation, and use of signaling equipment on priority vehicles, and the issuance, reissuance, and revocation of permits for that equipment. The records link the subjects as parts of the same regulatory area, but provide no specific rules, enforcement outcomes, or claims about compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has regulatory relevance to priority-vehicle signaling equipment, but the available data describe only two connected subjects and provide no evidence of broader impact or compliance issues.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two connected subjects define the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains two entities: one covering management, installation, and use of priority-vehicle signaling equipment, and another covering permits for that equipment. Their only listed relationship describes them as related regulatory subjects. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784); Relationships (8127)]

This supports treating them as a narrowly defined regulatory community, rather than as separate, unrelated topics. The records do not identify additional participants or connected subject areas. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784); Relationships (8127)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulatory scope includes equipment activities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One subject explicitly concerns the management, installation, and use of signaling equipment on priority vehicles. This identifies the activities covered by that part of the community, but the data do not specify technical standards, permitted equipment types, or operating requirements. [Data: Entities (2960)]

Accordingly, the record supports a description of the subject matter, not an assessment of whether any particular installation or use meets applicable requirements. [Data: Entities (2960)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permitting procedures are a distinct component
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The second subject concerns administrative procedures for issuing, reissuing, and revoking permits to use signaling equipment on priority vehicles. It complements the equipment-activity subject by addressing authorization procedures. [Data: Entities (2784); Relationships (8127)]

The available description does not provide eligibility criteria, decision timelines, grounds for revocation, or information about any actual permit decisions. [Data: Entities (2784)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a relationship, not specific regulatory mechanics
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole listed relationship says the two subjects are related regulatory topics concerning the use of signaling equipment on priority vehicles. It does not explain how permit decisions interact with management, installation, or use in practice. [Data: Relationships (8127)]

Consequently, the data support identifying the topics as connected, but not inferring a particular sequence of approvals, enforcement process, or institutional responsibility. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784); Relationships (8127)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and enforcement outcomes are not documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe regulatory subject areas and permit procedures, but include no compliance findings, violations, enforcement actions, or claims about specific entities. The community therefore cannot be characterized from this evidence as compliant or noncompliant. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784); Relationships (8127)]

The impact rating reflects the limited, focused scope documented here; it should not be read as a conclusion about the real-world importance or effectiveness of any underlying regulation. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784); Relationships (8127)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP and Its Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP, identified as a Vietnamese government decree. Article 27 is described as amending and supplementing provisions of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, while a separate provision concerns Article 2 ceasing to have effect on 1 March 2027, subject to exceptions. The available records establish the decree’s structure and a specified expiration date but do not provide the details of the amendments, exceptions, or an assessment of compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The decree has moderate potential importance because it is a government legal instrument with an amendment provision and a specified future expiration, while the records provide little detail about its practical effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP is identified as a Vietnamese government decree and is the entity connected to both Article 27 and the Article 2 expiration event. This makes it the organizing point for the provisions represented in the community. [Data: Entities (1295); Relationships (1400, 1059)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 27 concerns amendments to another decree
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 27 is described as amending and supplementing provisions of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The records do not specify which provisions are changed or describe the substance or consequences of those changes, so their precise regulatory effect cannot be assessed from this data. [Data: Entities (343, 1295); Relationships (1400)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 2 has a stated future expiration date
phat_hien.giai_thich: The decree establishes that Article 2 ceases to have effect on 1 March 2027, subject to stated exceptions. The available information does not identify those exceptions, so the scope of the expiration cannot be determined here. [Data: Entities (295, 1295); Relationships (1059)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree’s entry into force is mentioned, but not dated
phat_hien.giai_thich: The decree’s description says Article 28 addresses entry into force as well as when Article 2 ceases to have effect. No entry-into-force date or further details of Article 28 are supplied in the records, so a timeline beyond the stated Article 2 expiration cannot be established. [Data: Entities (1295)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support structural, not compliance, conclusions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data identifies the decree and describes a limited set of provisions, but contains no information about implementation, enforcement, affected parties, or compliance outcomes. Accordingly, the community’s legal significance is apparent at a high level, while specific operational effects and compliance status remain undetermined from the available evidence. [Data: Entities (1295, 343, 295); Relationships (1400, 1059)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Law 118/2025/QH15 and Article 7 Amendment
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnamese Law 118/2025/QH15 and its Article 7 amendment to the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. The law sets a general effective date of July 1, 2026, while point a, clause 20, Article 7 takes effect earlier, on January 1, 2026. The supplied records establish the law, amendment, and timing relationships, but provide no further information about implementation, enforcement, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (2822, 537, 1739); Relationships (2515, 6617)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public-policy impact because it concerns a Vietnamese law amending road-traffic provisions and specifies dates when those provisions take effect.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Law 118/2025/QH15 is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The law is the main connecting entity: the Article 7 amendment is described as part of it, and Article 11 of the law specifies the effective timing of a referenced provision. Its description identifies it as a Vietnamese law concerning the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. [Data: Entities (2822); Relationships (2515, 6617)]

The records do not provide details about the law's practical implementation or effects beyond the provisions and dates described.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 7 amends road-traffic legislation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes an Article 7 amendment that amends and supplements provisions of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. The relationship record explicitly places this amendment within Law 118/2025/QH15. [Data: Entities (537, 2822); Relationships (2515)]

No specific amended provisions beyond this general description are supplied, so the extent or substantive effect of the changes cannot be assessed from these records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law has a general effective date of July 1, 2026
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Law 118/2025/QH15 states that Article 11 generally makes the law effective on July 1, 2026. This date establishes the broad commencement schedule given in the available information. [Data: Entities (2822)]

The records do not indicate how the general commencement date will be implemented or whether any operational preparations are underway.

phat_hien.tom_tat: One specified Article 7 provision takes effect earlier
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Point a, clause 20, Article 7 is identified as an exception to the general commencement date. The entity describing this provision states that it takes effect on January 1, 2026, and the relationship record connects its timing to Article 11 of the law. [Data: Entities (1739, 2822); Relationships (6617)]

This creates a distinct earlier commencement date for that provision, but the supplied records do not explain its content or why it has a separate date.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Available evidence supports a limited legal and timing assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records establish the law's stated subject area, the existence of its Article 7 amendment, and the general and exceptional effective dates. These make the community relevant to tracking a legislative change affecting road-traffic law. [Data: Entities (2822, 537, 1739); Relationships (2515, 6617)]

There is no supplied evidence about regulatory compliance, enforcement actions, technical capabilities, public or institutional reactions, or adverse outcomes. Those matters therefore cannot be concluded from this community's records.

v.tieu_de: Transport Business Unit and Transport Operator
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a transport business unit and a transport operator linked through the unit’s record, which includes operator information. The unit is described as providing transport services, and its database record may include business identification, licensing, address, authority, operator, and business-type details. It is also identified as a data field in records used to manage drivers’ vehicle operating time. The available information describes administrative and operational recordkeeping, but does not establish the unit’s licensing status, compliance, performance, or reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the unit’s connection to transport operations and licensing-related records, while the limited information provides no evidence of misconduct, noncompliance, or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport Business Unit is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Order and Safety Law
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety and provisions connected to its implementation. Article 34 identifies categories of rudimentary vehicles covered by operating conditions in Article 26 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, while Clause 1 of Article 54 concerns eligibility for road rescue. The records also identify a restriction excluding funeral processions from groups eligible to install priority-vehicle signal devices. The law’s described scope includes road-safety rules, driver and vehicle requirements, database information-sharing, and violation identification; the supplied records do not establish how these rules are implemented in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the law concerns broadly significant road-safety requirements and information use, but the records provide no evidence of specific implementation outcomes or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law is the community’s central legal framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety is the principal entity in this community and is described as governing road traffic order and safety in Vietnam. Its stated scope includes a legal basis for connecting and sharing information between the road traffic order and safety database and other databases, and for using database information to identify violations. [Data: Entities (2851)]

The law is also described as establishing or supporting requirements for drivers and vehicles, permitted driving times, rescue eligibility, priority signals, and vehicles transporting preschool children and pupils. These descriptions indicate broad regulatory relevance, but do not by themselves show enforcement activity or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (2851)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 34 and Decree 151 link vehicle categories to operating conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 34 of the law identifies categories of rudimentary vehicles to which operating conditions in Article 26 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP apply. The relationship records that Article 34 is part of the law and that Article 26 refers to vehicle categories specified in Article 34. [Data: Entities (404, 331); Relationships (1711, 1356)]

Article 26 is described as establishing conditions for rudimentary vehicles, including front lighting or reflectors and rear signal lights or reflectors. The records therefore show a connection between statutory vehicle categories and specified equipment conditions, but do not indicate inspection or compliance rates. [Data: Entities (331, 404); Relationships (1356)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law provides a basis for road-rescue eligibility rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 1 of Article 54 is identified as the provision defining which vehicles are eligible for road rescue, as referenced by a penalty rule. The record states that this clause is part of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. [Data: Entities (867); Relationships (3341)]

The supplied information establishes the existence and subject of the provision, but does not specify the eligible vehicle types, the penalty, or any particular case of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Funeral processions are excluded from priority-signal device eligibility
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a funeral procession as a category of priority-vehicle convoy, while stating that funeral processions are expressly excluded from the vehicle groups eligible to have priority-vehicle signal devices installed under the cited rules. [Data: Entities (2380)]

The relationship connects that exclusion to the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. The available information does not provide further details about other eligible groups or the practical application of the restriction. [Data: Relationships (7587)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal and information provisions, not practical performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The law’s description refers to database connectivity and sharing, as well as using database information to identify violations. This supports characterizing the law as providing a legal basis for information use, but the records do not identify specific databases, technical systems, operators, or operational capabilities. [Data: Entities (2851)]

Likewise, the supplied entities and relationships describe provisions and their links rather than particular enforcement actions, organizations’ compliance, or measured road-safety effects. Any assessment of implementation success or actual risk would therefore require evidence beyond this community’s records. [Data: Entities (2851, 867, 331, 2380); Relationships (3341, 7587, 1356)]

v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has institutional relevance because it concerns government agencies and officials assigned to implement a decree, but the available information is too limited to establish broader impact.

phat_hien.giai_thich: The two entities are agencies subordinate to the Government and the heads of those agencies. The relationship record states that the officials lead the agencies, making this a governance-focused community. [Data: Entities (145, 2471); Relationships (482)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Agency heads are identified as decree implementers
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of the agency heads identifies them as responsible for implementing Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. The data does not provide the decree’s subject matter, the specific implementation duties, or evidence of implementation progress. [Data: Entities (2471)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The agencies are described as subordinate to the Government
phat_hien.giai_thich: The agency entity is described as covering agencies subordinate to the Government. No individual agencies are named, so the record supports only a general characterization of the group, not conclusions about any particular agency’s remit or operations. [Data: Entities (145)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No named officials or agencies are provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records refer to categories of agencies and agency heads rather than identifying specific organizations or individuals. phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and implementation outcomes cannot be assessed
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data assigns responsibility for implementing the decree but reports no actions, results, or compliance findings. v.tieu_de: Articles 17 and 18 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP
v.tom_tat: This small regulatory community consists of Article 17, concerning management of signal devices for priority vehicles, and Article 18, which specifies the types of vehicles eligible to have and use those devices. Article 17 refers to Article 18 for the eligibility categories. The supplied information describes their subject matter and connection but does not establish how the provisions are implemented or whether any party complies with them. [Data: Entities (275, 280); Relationships (988)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The provisions concern management and eligibility for priority-vehicle signal devices, but the supplied data establishes only their regulatory relationship and provides no evidence of implementation, violations, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A two-provision regulatory community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains two provisions of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP: Article 17 and Article 18. The sole listed relationship connects them, making their shared subject the management and eligible use of priority-vehicle signal devices. [Data: Entities (275, 280); Relationships (988)]

The records do not identify other organizations, individuals, or enforcement bodies in this community.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 17 addresses signal-device management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 17 is described as concerning the management of signal devices for priority vehicles. This establishes its stated regulatory topic, but the provided data does not specify the management procedures or responsible authorities. [Data: Entities (275)]

Article 17 refers to Article 18 for the types of vehicles eligible to use the devices, linking its management subject to a separate eligibility provision. [Data: Relationships (988)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18 specifies eligible vehicle types
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18 is described as specifying the types of vehicles on which priority-vehicle signal devices may be installed and used. The supplied information does not enumerate those vehicle types, so no particular category can be identified from these records. [Data: Entities (280)]

Its role in the community is clarified by Article 17's reference to it for the eligible vehicle types. [Data: Relationships (988)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The cross-reference links management and eligibility
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The recorded relationship states that Article 17 refers to Article 18 for the types of vehicles eligible to use priority-vehicle signal devices. This makes Article 18 an explicit reference point for the eligibility aspect of Article 17's subject matter. [Data: Relationships (988)]

The relationship establishes a textual connection between the provisions; the records do not provide the full text needed to assess how the provisions interact in practice.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation and compliance cannot be assessed from these records
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records describe the provisions' topics and their cross-reference, but contain no information about implementation, enforcement, compliance, violations, or operational outcomes. Accordingly, no conclusion about compliance or actual effects is supported by this dataset. [Data: Entities (275, 280); Relationships (988)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Order and Safety Database
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Vietnam’s nationwide Road Traffic Order and Safety Database, built and managed by the Ministry of Public Security and operated and exploited by the Traffic Police Force. It connects road-safety administration—including vehicle registration, driver licensing, violation handling, accidents, transport businesses, and related services—with information sources and other databases. Provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees have state-management responsibilities, while competent agencies may access and use information under applicable rules. The system’s national scope and broad personal, vehicle, health, and enforcement data make it highly consequential; the supplied information describes its legal framework and intended operation, not evidence of implementation outcomes or security performance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the community describes a nationwide, legally governed system that integrates extensive road-safety and personal data for use across multiple public agencies.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A nationally significant administrative data hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Order and Safety Database is described as a nationwide shared information system supporting state management of road traffic order and safety. The Ministry of Public Security builds and manages it, and the Traffic Police Force operates and exploits it, placing the system at the center of this community. [Data: Entities (4388)]

The decree addresses its construction, management, operation, use, maintenance, and upgrading, indicating an ongoing government information capability rather than a database for a single administrative process. [Data: Entities (4388); Relationships (8756)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Broad and consequential data coverage
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database is described as holding vehicle and owner information, specifications, inspections and modifications, journeys and driver operating times, and vehicle purchase and sale invoices. It also covers driver training, tests, licences, certificates, health, and licence-point history. [Data: Entities (4388)]

Other recorded areas include transport businesses and vehicle badges, compulsory liability insurance and compensation, traffic accidents, traffic-organization recommendations, and administrative violation processing and outcomes. This breadth links vehicle and driver administration with safety, insurance, and enforcement functions. [Data: Entities (4388); Relationships (10182, 9015, 10095, 368, 150)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Integration with other government and specialist databases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database is intended to connect and share information with the National Population Database, the Road Database, specialized databases, and other relevant databases. The relationship records also identify sources such as the Road Traffic Accident Database and Road Motor Vehicle Journey Database. [Data: Entities (4388, 3198, 4277, 4686, 4318); Relationships (9124, 10019, 10174, 10095, 10047)]

The described collection framework includes information from national, ministerial, specialized, and other designated databases, including population and business-registration sources. These connections can support joined-up administration, while also making lawful access and data governance important considerations. [Data: Entities (4388, 3195, 3462); Relationships (9108, 9105, 9368)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative enforcement and compliance records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database records road-traffic administrative violation handling, including applicable penalties, fines, supplementary sanctions, remedial measures, compliance deadlines, and licence-point management. The associated process is described as using the database to maintain information about how violations are processed and their results. [Data: Entities (4388, 115, 71); Relationships (368, 150)]

Administrative fine proceeds are identified as one funding source for the database. The supplied information establishes this funding link but does not specify amounts or indicate the proportion of overall funding that fines provide. [Data: Entities (42); Relationships (97)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Defined public-sector roles and authorized use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees have state-management responsibilities for the database within their assigned authority. The decree also addresses funding for ministries, ministerial-level agencies, and government agencies involved in its construction, operation, use, maintenance, and upgrading. [Data: Entities (3686, 3684, 3685, 3008); Relationships (9569, 9566, 9564, 8756)]

The system is intended for connection, access, extraction, sharing, and use by competent state agencies, and for shared use by competent agencies and organizations under applicable rules. The source describes these authorities as regulated; it does not establish how access is implemented in practice. [Data: Entities (1096, 4755, 1040); Relationships (3932, 10177, 3651)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal and records-management framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database is governed in the supplied description by Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, including provisions on construction and operation, information content and collection, and funding. The database is also required to store records in accordance with archival law. [Data: Entities (4388, 2843); Relationships (8496, 8756)]

The stated operational requirements are that information be complete, accurate, timely, continuous, stable, and accessible for lawful use by competent agencies, organizations, and individuals. Access excludes information related to national defense and security. These are described requirements, not independent evidence that the requirements have been met. [Data: Entities (4388)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized services and emergency-response information are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database includes information about ambulance units and traffic rescue units, connecting emergency-response services to the wider road-safety information system. The source does not provide operational performance measures for these services. [Data: Entities (170, 5035); Relationships (526, 10180)]

It also records information associated with driver-licence issuance, exchange, and reissuance, and certificates related to courses supplementing road-traffic-law knowledge. These links show that the community spans both ongoing safety administration and driver credential processes. [Data: Entities (1242, 1454, 1553, 1554, 1556); Relationships (4228, 6037, 6273, 6274, 6277)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Order and Safety Database Network
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety, an information system for maintaining road-safety-related records. It is connected to vehicle registration, finance, and administrative-violations databases as information sources, and to the activity of updating its records. The described functions include collecting specified information under Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and maintaining driver-training, testing, licensing, and road-traffic-law certificate information. The records establish a significant administrative data-integration role, but provide no evidence about security controls, implementation status, or actual compliance outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has notable administrative importance because it consolidates information from several government databases for road-traffic safety purposes, while the available records do not establish operational risks or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Central role of the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety is the community’s central information system. Its stated purpose is to collect and maintain information concerning road traffic order and safety, and it is linked to multiple information sources and to database updates. [Data: Entities (1248); Relationships (4234, 4240, 4231, 4242)]

Its described records include information on driver training, testing, and licensing, as well as certificates for training in road traffic law, including for operators of specialized motorcycles. [Data: Entities (1248)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Information is collected from several specialized databases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle registration and management database is identified as a source of information for the road traffic database. The source database is described as containing information related to the registration and management of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles and as being built and managed by the Ministry of Public Security. [Data: Entities (1246); Relationships (4234)]

The network also links the National Database on Finance and the database on handling administrative violations concerning road traffic order and safety to specified information collected for the central database. The records do not enumerate the underlying data fields beyond the referenced provisions and clauses. [Data: Entities (3196, 1244); Relationships (4240, 4231)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Updates are described as a defined administrative activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Updating Database Information is defined as adding or adjusting information in the road traffic database. The relationship record describes this as an activity associated with the central database. [Data: Entities (5284); Relationships (4242)]

The entity description says updates use information from administrative procedures, administrative violation handling, and related professional activities. The available information describes the process in general terms but does not specify update frequency, validation procedures, or responsible operational teams. [Data: Entities (5284)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The database has a stated legal and regulatory basis
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central database description refers to Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP for information collected for inclusion, including specified information from the database on compulsory civil liability insurance for motor vehicle owners.
