It also notes that Article 13 addresses adding or adjusting records using information from sources prescribed by law. [Data: Entities (1248)]

These details establish that the described collection and update functions are framed by legal provisions. They do not, on their own, demonstrate that the system is fully implemented or that its operation has been independently assessed for compliance. [Data: Entities (1248)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative significance is evident, but security and operational evidence is absent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database’s connections to vehicle registration, finance, and administrative-violations information, alongside its stated road-safety recordkeeping functions, indicate a meaningful role in government administration. [Data: Entities (1248, 3196, 1246, 1244); Relationships (4234, 4240, 4231)]

The supplied records do not describe access controls, cybersecurity safeguards, data quality, privacy practices, incidents, or measurable effects on road safety. Accordingly, the community’s administrative importance can be assessed from its stated purpose and connections, but those records do not support conclusions about its security posture or real-world performance. [Data: Entities (1248, 3196, 1246, 1244); Relationships (4234, 4240, 4231, 4242)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Article 55 and Immigration Management Authority
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Article 55 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and the Immigration Management Authority. Article 55 covers road-traffic safety requirements for specified foreign vehicles and requires the licensing authority to notify the immigration authority immediately in the circumstances it describes. The available records establish a legal notification relationship, but do not show whether any notification occurred or whether the entities complied with the requirements.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory importance because Article 55 links vehicle-related requirements to an immediate immigration notification, but the records show no specific incident or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 55 establishes a vehicle-related regulatory requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 55 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets out road-traffic safety requirements for foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars and foreign motor vehicles brought into Vietnam by foreign visitors for tourism. The supplied information does not specify further requirements or describe any particular case [Data: Entities (2835)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Immigration Management Authority is the designated notification recipient
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship identifies the Immigration Management Authority as the recipient of a notification from the licensing authority under Article 55. This defines an administrative link between the legal provision and the authority responsible for managing immigration matters in Vietnam [Data: Entities (2554, 2835); Relationships (7814)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision calls for immediate notification
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 55 requires the licensing authority to notify the Immigration Management Authority immediately in the circumstances specified by the article. The records do not establish that a notification was made, identify a particular licensing authority, or describe a specific instance triggering the requirement [Data: Entities (2835); Relationships (7814)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is a narrow legal-administrative connection
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records connect one legal provision with one government authority through a notification relationship. They do not identify additional organizations, individuals, events, or operational systems involved in this community [Data: Entities (2835, 2554); Relationships (7814)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: No compliance outcome or adverse finding is documented
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information describes the legal requirement and the authority designated to receive notice, but provides no evidence of compliance, noncompliance, enforcement action, or a specific road-safety or immigration incident. Accordingly, no conclusion about actual implementation or legal violations is supported by these records [Data: Entities (2835, 2554); Relationships (7814)].

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Inspection and Safety Certification
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a motor vehicle and specialized-use motorcycle inspection process and the related technical safety and environmental protection inspection certification. The relationship indicates that the certification is associated with inspection of vehicles participating in traffic. The records describe inspection-related information but do not establish the compliance status of any vehicle or the performance of an issuing authority.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate public-interest importance because it concerns vehicle inspection and safety certification, but the provided records describe processes rather than specific compliance outcomes or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection and certification are directly linked
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central relationship connects motor vehicle and specialized-use motorcycle inspection with the technical safety and environmental protection inspection certification. The relationship describes the certification as associated with inspection of vehicles participating in traffic. [Data: Relationships (9016)]

This establishes a connection between an inspection process and a certificate, but does not specify how inspections are conducted or whether any particular vehicle passed. [Data: Entities (3096, 5500); Relationships (9016)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The inspection scope includes motor vehicles and specialized-use motorcycles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The inspection entity specifically covers motor vehicles and specialized-use motorcycles. Its description also identifies registration and inspection certificates, inspection cycles, useful-life limits, and issuing-authority details as types of associated records. [Data: Entities (3096)]

The record describes the subject matter and associated information, not the number of vehicles covered or the operating practices of any inspection organization. [Data: Entities (3096)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certification records may contain identifying and administrative details
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The certification entity describes a technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate for a vehicle participating in traffic. It indicates that the database may record a certificate number, issue date, and issuing authority. [Data: Entities (5500)]

These fields could support identification of a certificate and its administrative origin, but the supplied data does not provide actual certificate records or confirm that the database contains these fields for any specific vehicle. [Data: Entities (5500)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection records may cover cycles and useful-life limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The inspection entity states that associated records include inspection cycles and useful-life limits, in addition to registration and inspection certificates and issuing-authority details. [Data: Entities (3096)]

This indicates that the described record scope extends beyond the certificate itself. No specific cycle, limit, vehicle, or authority is identified in the available data. [Data: Entities (3096)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information does not establish compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify an inspection process and its associated certification, but do not provide a specific vehicle’s inspection result, certificate number, issue date, or compliance status. [Data: Entities (3096, 5500); Relationships (9016)]

Accordingly, the data supports describing the community’s administrative subject matter, but not conclusions about whether vehicles or authorities comply with applicable requirements. [Data: Entities (3096, 5500)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Registration and Intelligent Transport Permits
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Vehicle Registration and Management System, which stores and manages registration data used in intelligent transport vehicle operating permit applications. The application process requires registration information alongside vehicle quality or inspection-exemption information and owner documents. The competent authority consults the system through a vehicle-registration lookup within seven working days after receiving an application. The records indicate an important administrative role but provide no assessment of security, reputation, or broader compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the system’s central role in vehicle registration and permit processing, while the supplied records do not establish harmful conduct or technical or compliance risks.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration system is the community’s central data resource
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Vehicle Registration and Management System records and manages vehicle registration data and supplies information for intelligent transport vehicle operating permit applications. It is also the source consulted for registration-data lookups, making it the shared data hub across the described process. [Data: Entities (5467); Relationships (8027, 10674)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit applications depend on several categories of documentation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The intelligent transport vehicle operating permit application process requires vehicle quality or inspection-exemption information, registration data, and vehicle-owner documents. The relationship records specifically identify registration data from the system as part of the application documentation. [Data: Entities (2722, 5467); Relationships (8027)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The competent authority performs a time-bounded registration lookup
phat_hien.giai_thich: The vehicle registration data lookup is described as an action by the competent authority, conducted within seven working days after an application is received. The lookup obtains registration data from the Vehicle Registration and Management System. [Data: Entities (5475, 5467); Relationships (10674)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The system also receives certain license-plate records
phat_hien.giai_thich: The system description states that vehicle license plates not selected for auction are transferred to the system for registration in accordance with the law. This establishes an additional registration function beyond supplying data for permit applications. [Data: Entities (5467)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence describes administrative functions, not system security or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records explain data storage, application documentation, and the authority’s lookup process. They do not provide details about technical controls, system performance, or reputation, so no conclusion about those areas is supported by this material. [Data: Entities (5467, 2722, 5475); Relationships (8027, 10674)]

v.tieu_de: Intelligent Transport Vehicle Operating Permit Process
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative pathway for issuing or refusing an operating permit for an intelligent transport vehicle. The licensing authority receives an application, reviews it against requirements and vehicle registration data, and then either issues a permit after a successful review or provides a written refusal with reasons. The issuance process is subject to a five-working-day period starting from receipt of the application. The records establish procedural importance but provide no evidence of actual applications, decisions, compliance breaches, or broader reputational or technical issues.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it defines a time-bound licensing process with distinct approval and refusal outcomes, but the records describe procedure rather than evidence of actual impact or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application review is the decision point
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The licensing authority reviews an application and compares its information with vehicle registration data to determine whether requirements are met. The review connects to both possible outcomes: successful applications proceed to permit issuance, while applications that fail the requirements result in refusal. [Data: Entities (220); Relationships (645, 646)]

This makes the review the central decision point in the documented process. The records describe the criteria and branches, but do not identify particular applicants or report any completed reviews. [Data: Entities (220); Relationships (645, 646)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Successful review leads to permit issuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When an application meets the requirements, the process provides for an operating permit to be issued on the prescribed form. The issuance record specifies that this should occur within five working days after the application is received. [Data: Entities (3378); Relationships (645, 633)]

The described outcome is conditional on meeting the requirements; the records do not establish that any specific permit has been granted or that the deadline has been met in a particular case. [Data: Entities (3378); Relationships (645, 633)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-qualifying applications receive written refusals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An application found not to meet the requirements results in a refusal communicated in writing, with the reasons for refusal provided. This is the alternative outcome to issuance following the application review. [Data: Entities (3382); Relationships (646)]

The information specifies a reason-giving procedure but does not describe grounds for any individual refusal, appeal mechanisms, or actual refusal decisions. [Data: Entities (3382); Relationships (646)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application receipt starts the issuance timeframe
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Receipt of the application by the licensing authority starts the period within which an operating permit must be issued. The documented period is five working days after receipt. [Data: Entities (215, 3378); Relationships (633)]

The records identify receipt as the timing trigger, but do not give details on how receipt is documented, how the deadline is calculated in individual cases, or what happens if the period is exceeded. [Data: Entities (215, 3378); Relationships (633)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to the formal licensing workflow
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information covers application receipt, review, and the two conditional outcomes of issuance or written refusal. It therefore supports an assessment of the process structure and stated timing, rather than conclusions about the performance of the licensing authority or the conduct of applicants. [Data: Entities (215, 220, 3378, 3382); Relationships (633, 645, 646)]

No specific applications, permit decisions, compliance violations, operational capabilities, or reputation-related claims are included in these records. Accordingly, the community's demonstrated impact is procedural and administrative; broader effects cannot be established from the supplied information. [Data: Entities (215, 220, 3378, 3382); Relationships (633, 645, 646)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Ministry of Public Security Road-Traffic Community
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security (MPS), which has a broad coordinating, regulatory, enforcement, and database-management role in road traffic order and safety. Its network connects the Ministry to a public-service portal, citizen mobile applications, driver-testing and licensing systems, other government bodies, and procedures involving foreign vehicles and international organizations. The supplied information describes substantial administrative and data capabilities, but does not provide evidence evaluating implementation outcomes or compliance in practice. [Data: Entities (3019, 3023, 839, 4105, 2316); Relationships (8845, 8864, 8889, 7426, 4230)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s high institutional importance, given the Ministry’s broad regulatory, enforcement, interagency, public-service, and road-traffic data responsibilities.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry is the community’s central coordinating authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Public Security is described as Vietnam’s focal agency for assisting the Government with unified state management of road traffic order and safety. Its responsibilities include coordinating implementation with other ministries and sectors and leading international cooperation in this policy area. [Data: Entities (3019, 4105); Relationships (8864, 8750)]

The Ministry is also linked to a wide range of specialized functions and entities, including public services, vehicle and driver databases, licensing, and enforcement. This makes it the principal hub in the supplied community data, although the records do not independently assess how effectively these responsibilities are carried out. [Data: Entities (3019, 3023, 1243, 1665); Relationships (8845, 4230, 6473)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Extensive road-traffic databases are a significant capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is responsible for building and managing databases covering driving tests and license issuance, foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, road-vehicle journeys and driver images, and driver vehicle-control time. The descriptions specify that the journeys, images, and control-time databases exclude military vehicles. [Data: Entities (3019, 2316, 1243, 1511, 4511); Relationships (7426, 4230, 8878, 6163, 6473)]

The Ministry’s broader database description includes vehicle registration, driver training and testing, licenses, violations, and accidents, with information-sharing connections to other agencies. This represents substantial administrative information-management capacity; the supplied material does not describe access controls, retention practices, or independent oversight, so those aspects cannot be assessed here. [Data: Entities (3019)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Public-service portal and citizen application provide digital channels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry’s Public Service Portal supports submissions such as notices, applications, and examination-related dossiers. It also provides access to shared information from the road-traffic database and a channel for sending administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts. [Data: Entities (3023); Relationships (8845)]

The Ministry also manages and operates a citizen mobile traffic application for reporting relevant changes. The records refer to both a citizen mobile traffic application and a traffic application for citizens; they establish Ministry management of each named entry but do not establish whether these are separate applications or alternate references to the same service. [Data: Entities (839, 4990); Relationships (3303, 8889)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry has a substantial role in driver testing and licensing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister of Public Security is assigned authority over driver-license examination and issuance, including the form, content, and procedures for examinations. The Ministry is also responsible for databases relating to driving tests and license issuance, and regulations cover international driving licenses and permits. [Data: Entities (3019, 1532, 1641, 2759, 2739); Relationships (6219, 6398, 6473, 8097, 8057)]

One specified theoretical legal-knowledge test lasts 26 minutes, contains 45 multiple-choice questions, and requires a score of at least 41; incorrectly answering its disqualifying question results in failure. The supplied records also associate the test requirements with Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, which took effect on January 1, 2025. [Data: Entities (4933, 1732); Relationships (8884, 6613)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Interagency and international coordination are built into the mandate
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry coordinates with relevant ministries and sectors on implementing road-traffic rules and undertakes international cooperation in this area. It assists the Government with negotiating and signing relevant international treaties and agreements, or may propose that an authorized competent authority sign them. [Data: Entities (3019, 4105, 3227, 610); Relationships (8864, 8852, 2768)]

The Ministry’s responsibilities also include notifying foreign diplomatic, consular, and intergovernmental representative offices about specified violations, accidents, or incidents. These relationships indicate an administrative interface with international organizations and representatives, but the records do not specify the number or outcomes of such notifications. [Data: Entities (4151, 1363, 1102); Relationships (8867, 5831, 3945)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign motor vehicles and associated organizers are subject to oversight
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry manages a database relating to foreign motor vehicles driven by foreigners in Vietnam and coordinates relevant procedures with other government bodies. Its responsibilities include inspection and handling of violations involving organizations and individuals who arrange for foreign nationals to drive such vehicles. [Data: Entities (2316, 4092, 3019); Relationships (7426, 8860)]

Article 36 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP is identified as specifying agency responsibilities for managing foreign nationals who drive foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. The Ministry’s notification duties concerning specified incidents provide an additional coordination link with foreign representative offices. [Data: Entities (412, 4151); Relationships (1756, 8867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic enforcement and operational capabilities span multiple functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry’s described functions include traffic patrol and enforcement, accident investigation, vehicle registration, inspection, traffic-command systems, and monitoring equipment. It also directs functional units in managing, installing, and using signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, subject to the stated exception for vehicles managed by the Ministry of National Defence. [Data: Entities (3019, 2378); Relationships (7582)]

The Ministry is also assigned technical and administrative responsibilities concerning road motor vehicle driving test centers, including prescribing their national technical regulations. These records establish a broad formal remit but do not provide operational performance data or findings about compliance with the relevant rules. [Data: Entities (4297, 3019); Relationships (8869)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal responsibilities, not implementation outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions and relationships principally document assigned roles, regulatory topics, databases, and service channels. They do not provide audit results, enforcement statistics, privacy assessments, litigation outcomes, or independent findings that would establish whether the Ministry or connected entities comply with all applicable requirements in practice. [Data: Entities (3019, 3023, 4105); Relationships (8845, 8864)]

Accordingly, the community’s high rating reflects the breadth and importance of its described public-sector functions and information systems, not evidence of misconduct or demonstrated adverse impact.

v.tieu_de: Article 19 and Specialized Motorcycle Insurance Penalty
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of Article 19 and the violation of operating a specialized motorcycle without the legally required compulsory civil liability insurance certificate. Their sole recorded relationship states that Article 19 specifies a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong for the violation. The Article 19 entry also refers to provisions in two different Vietnamese decrees, covering distinct subjects: priority-vehicle signal equipment and administrative penalties and operator requirements for specialized motorcycles. The available information establishes a narrow regulatory connection, but provides no evidence about enforcement, compliance outcomes, reputation, or broader technical capabilities.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a specific regulatory violation and a limited monetary fine, without evidence of broader community reach or demonstrated impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 19 is the community’s central reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 19 is the central entity, linked to the specialized-motorcycle insurance violation by the sole recorded relationship. The entry describes Article 19 as referring to provisions in two separate Vietnamese decrees, so the label does not identify a single provision without further context. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

The records do not establish additional organizations, individuals, or enforcement bodies connected to this community. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The cited decrees address different subjects
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 19 description says Article 19 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out signals and technical requirements for signal-generating or signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles. It separately says Article 19 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP lists violations subject to administrative penalties and addresses requirements for operators of specialized motorcycles. [Data: Entities (290)]

These are distinct topics associated with the same article number; the record does not indicate that the priority-vehicle equipment requirements are part of the insurance violation. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The identified violation concerns missing compulsory insurance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation entity describes operating a specialized motorcycle without the compulsory civil liability insurance certificate required by law. The Article 19 entry likewise connects the specialized-motorcycle provisions to this insurance requirement and states a fine for the conduct. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

The records describe the conduct and its stated penalty, but do not indicate how frequently it occurs or whether any particular operator committed it. [Data: Entities (290, 3334)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 19 description specifies a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong for operating a specialized motorcycle without the legally required compulsory civil liability insurance certificate. The recorded relationship directly links Article 19 to this violation by stating that it specifies the fine. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

No further consequences, enforcement procedures, or case-specific penalties are described in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports a narrow regulatory assessment, not a broader profile
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available records support identifying a regulatory provision, the conduct it penalizes, and the stated fine. They do not provide evidence about compliance rates, enforcement activity, legal disputes, public reputation, or practical effects. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

The records also do not document operational technical capabilities for the entities in this community; the technical requirements mentioned apply to signal-generating or signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles, but no equipment or operator is identified. [Data: Entities (290)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 151/2024/ND-CP Road-Traffic Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, a Vietnamese regulatory framework connecting road-safety education, traffic databases, permits, vehicle technology, monitoring data, and foreign vehicles operating in Vietnam. The decree assigns implementation roles to relevant agencies and includes transitional provisions and rules on commencement and repeal. Its breadth makes it significant for road-traffic governance, but the supplied records describe legal requirements rather than actual compliance, enforcement results, or reputational assessments. [Data: Entities (1265, 4097, 420, 1813, 4126); Relationships (4327, 1778, 4269, 4329)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the decree spans multiple important areas of Vietnamese road-traffic governance and assigns responsibilities to relevant agencies, although the records provide no evidence of implementation outcomes or adverse incidents. [Data: Entities (1265, 4097); Relationships (4327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad, multi-domain regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/ND-CP is the central entity in this community. Its described scope includes road-safety education, traffic databases, signaling equipment for priority vehicles, permits for intelligent traffic vehicles, journey-monitoring data, and foreign vehicles and drivers. [Data: Entities (1265)]

The decree also covers commencement, repeal of specified legal provisions, and implementation responsibilities, making it a framework that connects substantive rules with administrative and legal-transition matters. The supplied information establishes the decree's scope, but not whether its provisions are being followed in practice. [Data: Entities (1265, 1813, 4126); Relationships (4269, 4329)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation is assigned to relevant agencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 36 assigns responsibilities to relevant agencies for implementing the decree. The agency group includes bodies involved in managing foreign nationals who operate foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, as well as agencies that address traffic congestion and coordinate with road-management bodies to identify its causes. [Data: Entities (4097); Relationships (4327, 7488)]

The records identify administrative responsibilities, but do not name all agencies or document their actions, performance, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (4097)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic databases are a major governance component
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree's Articles 9–16 provide for a road traffic order and safety database and specialized databases, including rules on management, funding, access, sharing, use, collection, and updating. The described data categories include vehicle and driver records, licences, training, operating time and health, insurance, administrative violations, foreign vehicles, and vehicles involved in violations. [Data: Entities (1265)]

The database provisions also encompass vehicle registration details and information about vehicle quality, technical-safety, and environmental-protection certificates. These records indicate a broad data-management capability prescribed by the decree; they do not establish that the databases are operational or describe their security controls. [Data: Entities (3130, 5454); Relationships (4308, 4350)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle monitoring and driver-image recording have technical requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 27–29 address the use, sharing, transmission, management, and storage of data from journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices. Article 28 requires driver-image recording equipment for specified vehicle categories, including certain passenger, tractor, ambulance, and road-rescue vehicles. [Data: Entities (1265)]

The decree links the required equipment to a national technical regulation specifying technical requirements for journey-monitoring and driver-image recording equipment. The supplied records describe regulatory and technical requirements, but do not provide details of specific deployments or assess their effectiveness. [Data: Entities (3215); Relationships (4313)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permits govern priority-vehicle signals and intelligent traffic vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 17–23 regulate signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, including eligible vehicles, signal and technical requirements, permits, application procedures, permit terms, and the authorities responsible for issuing, reissuing, or revoking permits. Use is described as restricted to authorized vehicles and official duties. [Data: Entities (1265, 805); Relationships (3156)]

Article 25a sets out procedures for permitting intelligent traffic vehicle operations, including applications and changes, renewals, or reissuance of permits. The records describe authorization processes, not particular permit holders or completed licensing decisions. [Data: Entities (1265, 2908); Relationships (4287)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicles and drivers are subject to agency oversight
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 32–36 address foreign motor vehicles and foreign nationals driving in Vietnam. The decree describes vehicle and driver requirements, including inspection documentation, approval procedures for foreign vehicles entering for tourism, and rules for certain right-hand-drive vehicles. [Data: Entities (1265)]

Relevant agencies are responsible for managing foreign nationals operating foreign motor vehicles in traffic in Vietnam. No individual foreign drivers, specific vehicle movements, or compliance findings are identified in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (2329, 4097); Relationships (7488)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education is included in the decree
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 4–8 address road-safety education in educational institutions, including legal-knowledge instruction for students at different levels and safe moped-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary or vocational education. The provisions also assign responsibilities to schools, families, and the Ministry of Education and Training. [Data: Entities (1265)]

The decree's educational content includes handling traffic incidents. The records specify subject matter and responsibilities but do not provide evidence about the delivery or results of educational programs. [Data: Entities (5007); Relationships (4346)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transition and commencement provisions affect existing approvals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 37 allows programs approved before the decree took effect to continue under their approval terms. It also preserves certain existing permits until expiry, while requiring holders in other specified groups to apply for a new permit under Chapter IV. [Data: Entities (420, 805); Relationships (1777, 1778)]

Article 38 concerns the decree's entry into force and the repeal of specified legal provisions from that point. The supplied records do not state a commencement date or identify the repealed provisions in detail. [Data: Entities (1813, 4126); Relationships (4269, 4329)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory scope, not compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available information describes legal provisions, assigned responsibilities, and technical or administrative procedures. It does not document violations, enforcement actions, measured compliance, operational performance, or reputational assessments for the decree or relevant agencies. Accordingly, the community's importance is supported by the breadth of the framework, while claims about actual outcomes would go beyond the supplied evidence. [Data: Entities (1265, 4097); Relationships (4327)]

v.tieu_de: Foreign Vehicle Administrative Approval Procedure
v.tom_tat: The community consists of the administrative approval procedure for certain foreign vehicles entering or operating in Vietnam and the receiving agency that handles applications under it. The procedure covers specified tourism and non-tourism circumstances, changes to previously approved information, and application review. The available information describes administrative responsibilities but does not establish the procedure’s outcomes, the agency’s identity, or any associated compliance, technical-capability, or reputation findings.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it governs review and approval of specified foreign-vehicle activities, but the provided data indicates no broader impact or adverse conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A procedure focused on approval for specified foreign-vehicle activities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The procedure described in Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerns approval for Vietnamese international travel service businesses organizing foreign nationals bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as organizations or individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes. The information defines the procedure’s scope but does not describe particular approvals or outcomes. [Data: Entities (39)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The procedure also covers changes and application review
phat_hien.giai_thich: Beyond initial approval, the described procedure covers changes to information that was previously approved and review of submitted applications. This indicates that its administrative scope includes both application assessment and updates, without specifying the criteria or timelines for those processes. [Data: Entities (39)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Receiving agency handles application intake and review
phat_hien.giai_thich: The receiving agency is described as the authority that receives and reviews applications and documents, notifies applicants when submissions do not meet requirements, and accepts qualifying applications. The relationship record confirms that the agency processes applications under the procedure. [Data: Entities (4040); Relationships (87)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is organized around a single procedural relationship
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data identifies the approval procedure and the receiving agency as the two entities, linked by the agency’s role in reviewing and processing applications. No other organizations, applicants, or connected processes are identified in the provided records. [Data: Entities (39, 4040); Relationships (87)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance, technical capability, and reputation are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the procedure’s scope and the receiving agency’s stated administrative functions, but provide no evidence about individual compliance outcomes, the agency’s technical systems or capabilities, or its reputation. These matters therefore cannot be assessed from the available information. [Data: Entities (39, 4040); Relationships (87)]

v.tieu_de: Licensing Authority and Vehicle Permit Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on the LICENSING AUTHORITY, a public authority connected to application review, in-person acceptance, receipts and appointments, and procedures for priority-vehicle signaling permits and smart traffic vehicle operating permits. It also has broader licensing responsibilities, including certain foreign vehicles in Vietnam and transport businesses. The records describe administrative responsibilities and processing timelines, but do not establish a compliance breach, reputational issue, or harmful conduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the authority’s broad, central role in vehicle and transport licensing and the operational importance of the permit procedures connected to it.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Licensing Authority is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The LICENSING AUTHORITY is linked to most of the procedures and administrative steps in the community, including application review, qualifying in-person submissions, and issuance of receipts and appointments. Its entity description also assigns it responsibility for receiving, reviewing, and deciding applications for several types of permits and licenses. [Data: Entities (2904); Relationships (8593, 8590, 636, 53, 8111)]

This concentration of responsibilities makes the authority the key operational hub in the records. The evidence describes its mandate and connections, rather than documenting the quality or outcomes of its decisions. [Data: Entities (2904); Relationships (600, 8599, 8600)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority covers a range of licensing functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Beyond the procedures represented as separate entities, the authority’s description says it may issue, replace, renew, reissue, or revoke permits for priority-vehicle signaling devices and smart or intelligent traffic vehicles. It also licenses certain foreign vehicles to participate in traffic in Vietnam and issues transport business licenses. [Data: Entities (2904)]

These stated functions indicate that the authority’s significance extends beyond one permit type. The records do not provide volumes of applications, numbers of affected operators, or details on enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2904)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application review is a recurring administrative control
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify application receipt and review as a step in the priority-vehicle signaling permit reissuance procedure, and separately describe document review for smart traffic vehicle operating permits. The authority is explicitly responsible for receiving and checking applications and supporting documents. [Data: Entities (217, 199, 3696, 3379); Relationships (636, 638, 600)]

For intelligent-vehicle permits, the authority’s description says it may verify vehicle registration details against the application. It may also notify applicants about incomplete, inaccurate, insufficient, or otherwise ineligible submissions, request supplemental documents, or provide a written refusal. [Data: Entities (2904, 3379)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Different permit processes have specified processing steps and timelines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The operating permit issuance procedure describes a review in which vehicle registration data are checked against the owner’s application within seven working days, followed by issuance for eligible applications or a written explanation for refusals. [Data: Entities (3379)]

Replacement or reissuance of a smart traffic vehicle operating permit is described as taking place within two working days after the authority receives the application dossier. The authority’s relationship to this procedure confirms its assigned role in carrying it out. [Data: Entities (2904, 4662, 4664); Relationships (8599, 8597)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Qualifying in-person submissions receive an acknowledgment and expected result date
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority accepts applications and accompanying documents submitted in person when they meet the requirements. After accepting a qualifying in-person application, it prepares a receipt and gives notice of when the result is expected. [Data: Entities (25, 2769); Relationships (53, 8111)]

These steps are also represented within the priority-vehicle signaling equipment reissuance procedure: application receipt and review precede acceptance, and a receipt and scheduled result date follow acceptance. [Data: Entities (217, 25, 2769, 3696); Relationships (638, 8112, 52)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports procedural importance, not a finding of noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the authority’s duties, application checks, possible notices or refusals, and specified processing periods. They do not identify a particular legal violation, adverse decision, complaint, or failure to meet a deadline. [Data: Entities (2904, 3379, 3696, 4667); Relationships (8590, 8593, 8600)]

Accordingly, the community’s impact rating reflects the authority’s central administrative role and the importance of the licensing processes described. The records provide no direct basis for assessing the authority’s reputation or for concluding that its procedures are being followed or breached in practice. [Data: Entities (2904, 3379)]

v.tieu_de: Eligible Direct Submission and Receipt Appointment Process
v.tom_tat: This community describes a two-step administrative process: a licensing authority accepts an eligible application or document submitted in person, after which a receipt is prepared that acknowledges receipt and specifies when the result is expected. The records establish the sequence and purpose of these steps but provide no further information about the authority, legal compliance, technical capabilities, or reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a narrow administrative workflow with one documented relationship and provide no evidence of broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Acceptance is the first step in the documented sequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The process begins when the licensing authority accepts an application or document submitted in person, provided it meets the permit conditions. This defines the stated eligibility condition for the initial step. [Data: Entities (24)]

The relationship record explicitly places acceptance before preparation of the receipt and result appointment. [Data: Relationships (49)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process concerns eligible in-person submissions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The acceptance entity is specifically about a direct submission made in person and meeting permit conditions. The data does not describe other submission channels or criteria beyond this eligibility condition. [Data: Entities (24)]

Accordingly, the documented scope is limited to this type of submission rather than licensing applications generally. [Data: Entities (24); Relationships (49)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A receipt and result appointment follow acceptance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After acceptance, the next documented step is preparing a document that acknowledges receipt and specifies when the result is expected. [Data: Entities (2777); Relationships (49)]

The relationship establishes the order of these steps, but does not state how or when the receipt is delivered to the submitter. [Data: Relationships (49)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The receipt communicates acknowledgment and expected timing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The receipt is described as acknowledging receipt of an eligible in-person submission and specifying when the result is expected. These are the two functions explicitly associated with the document. [Data: Entities (2777)]

No further details are provided about the format of the receipt, the appointment mechanism, or whether the expected result date is guaranteed. [Data: Entities (2777)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is a compact administrative workflow
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records identify two process entities and one relationship linking them: eligible direct submission acceptance is followed by receipt and result appointment preparation. [Data: Entities (24, 2777); Relationships (49)]

The information supports describing the workflow, but does not establish legal compliance beyond the stated permit-condition requirement, or provide evidence about technical capabilities, reputation, or wider effects. [Data: Entities (24, 2777); Relationships (49)]

v.tieu_de: Licensing Application Deficiency Notices and Responses
v.tom_tat: This community consists of three administrative notices or actions associated with applications or documents that do not meet licensing conditions. The Notice of Ineligible Submission is linked to two possible responses: a request to supplement or complete the application, and a refusal to process an administrative procedure. The records describe these procedural relationships but do not establish how often they occur, their outcomes, or any specific legal or operational impact.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate procedural importance because it describes possible licensing responses to deficient submissions, but the available records provide no evidence about scale, outcomes, or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Notice of Ineligible Submission is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The notice is described as being sent when an application or document does not meet licensing conditions, with the reason stated as required by regulations. It is connected to both other entities in the community. [Data: Entities (3271); Relationships (9225, 9226)]

This makes it the clearest organizing point in the available records. The data does not identify a particular licensing authority, application, or recipient. [Data: Entities (3271); Relationships (9225, 9226)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A deficient submission may be followed by a request to supplement or complete it
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Request to Supplement or Complete an Application is described as asking for an application or document that does not meet licensing conditions to be supplemented or completed. The relationship record identifies this request as one possible notice or action for such an application. [Data: Entities (4157); Relationships (9226)]

The records do not say what information must be supplied, whether the request is mandatory in any particular case, or whether the application is later accepted. [Data: Entities (4157); Relationships (9226)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Refusal to process is another stated possible response
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Refusal to Process an Administrative Procedure is described as a notice refusing to process an administrative procedure when an application or document does not meet licensing conditions, with the reason stated. The relationship data characterizes refusal as another possible response to an ineligible submission. [Data: Entities (4058); Relationships (9225)]

No record establishes that refusal necessarily follows a request to supplement, or that the two actions occur in a fixed sequence. [Data: Entities (4058); Relationships (9225)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records connect the actions through a shared licensing-condition issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions of all three entities concern applications or documents that do not meet licensing conditions: the central notice communicates ineligibility, while the other entities describe a request for completion or a refusal to process. [Data: Entities (3271, 4157, 4058)]

This supports treating them as related procedural actions, but the records do not specify a complete decision tree, governing jurisdiction, or circumstances that determine which response applies. [Data: Entities (3271, 4157, 4058); Relationships (9225, 9226)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to definitions and possible relationships
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied data defines the three administrative concepts and states that the request and refusal are possible responses associated with an ineligible submission. It contains no case-level records, dates, named organizations, or measured outcomes. [Data: Entities (3271, 4157, 4058); Relationships (9225, 9226)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is procedural rather than evidence of a specific compliance violation or adverse outcome. The records do not support conclusions about frequency, enforcement, or the effects on applicants. [Data: Entities (3271, 4157, 4058); Relationships (9225, 9226)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam National Public Service Portal and Administrative Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s National Public Service Portal, a government channel connected to four administrative procedures: smart traffic vehicle operation licensing, smart traffic vehicle operating permits, new permit issuance for signal devices on priority vehicles, and road traffic law examination registration. The relationships describe the portal as a submission channel for several procedures and as a channel for notices during the smart traffic vehicle permit procedure. The portal’s stated functions also include application tracking, receipt of notices and documents, and public access to road traffic safety information. The supplied data establishes the portal’s administrative role but does not assess its operational security or legal compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the portal’s broad public-service role and its connections to multiple licensing, permitting, and examination procedures, rather than evidence of harm or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The National Public Service Portal is the community’s central hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The portal is described as Vietnam’s national online government service platform and as a channel for individuals, vehicle owners, representatives, agencies, and organizations to submit applications, forms, follow-up documents, and written requests to authorities. Its degree of 25 is the highest among the listed entities, consistent with its central position in the supplied network. [Data: Entities (3209)]

Four listed relationships connect the portal to procedures for smart traffic vehicle operation licensing, examination registration, smart traffic vehicle operating permits, and new permit issuance. [Data: Relationships (9132, 6796, 9131, 9128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The portal supports application pathways for distinct licensing and permit procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the smart traffic vehicle operation licensing procedure described under Article 25a of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, the portal is one of the stated channels for submitting an application. The procedure description says the vehicle owner submits the required application to the competent licensing authority. [Data: Entities (4665); Relationships (9132)]

The portal is also identified as a channel for applications and written requests under the procedure for newly issuing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles, described as Article 21(1) of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. The supplied information identifies these legal provisions but does not determine whether any particular application or implementation complies with them. [Data: Entities (3883); Relationships (9128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The portal has a role in notices and application handling
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The smart traffic vehicle operating permit procedure includes receiving and checking applications, notifying applicants when submissions are insufficient, and accepting eligible in-person submissions with a receipt and expected-result date. The portal is specified as one channel for notices during this procedure. [Data: Entities (4663); Relationships (9131)]

More broadly, the portal description says applicants can track application processing and receive notices, including notices that applications or documents are incomplete, refused, or ineligible. It is also identified as a channel for delivering administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts. [Data: Entities (3209)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Online examination registration is another public-facing service
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Examination registration concerns applying to take the road traffic law knowledge examination. The listed process includes submitting a registration dossier containing an application and health certificate; online applicants select a testing authority and examination date. [Data: Entities (1859)]

Applicants may submit examination registration documents online through the National Public Service Portal, making it a direct online channel for this examination process. [Data: Relationships (6796)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The portal’s stated reach spans applications, follow-up, and public information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The portal’s described functions extend beyond initial application submission: users can provide follow-up documents, track processing, and receive notices. The description also says it provides public access to information from the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (3209)]

These functions indicate that the portal serves several administrative and informational roles in the listed community. The supplied records do not provide evidence about technical architecture, security controls, service availability, user volumes, or actual outcomes, so no conclusions about those matters are warranted. [Data: Entities (3209)]

v.tieu_de: Smart Traffic Vehicle Permit Change or Reissuance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the administrative procedure for changing or reissuing a smart traffic vehicle operating permit. An authorized representative may submit the application on the vehicle owner's behalf; the procedure also allows the owner or representative to use designated electronic services or send or deliver a request to the authority that issued the permit. The data describes the process and roles, but does not establish any compliance outcome or broader impact.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the community describes a focused administrative permit process and authorized application channel, with no evidence of broader operational impact or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The permit procedure is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The main entity is the administrative procedure for changing or reissuing a smart traffic vehicle operating permit. Its description identifies the procedure's purpose and the people who may submit a request. [Data: Entities (4666)]

The available data characterizes an administrative process rather than a vehicle operator, issuing authority, or technology system. It does not provide evidence about the procedure's implementation or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4666)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Applications can be submitted through multiple channels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The permit owner or an authorized representative may submit an electronic form through designated services. The description also allows a request to be sent or delivered to the authority that previously issued the permit. [Data: Entities (4666)]

The data identifies these channels but does not specify the services, the authority's identity, processing times, or any requirements beyond submitting the request. [Data: Entities (4666)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An authorized representative may act for the vehicle owner
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authorized representative is defined as a person authorized by law to act on behalf of a vehicle owner in matters concerning the vehicle's operating permit. The described matters include requesting a change or reissue and surrendering a permit subject to revocation. [Data: Entities (623)]

The data supports a role defined by legal authorization; it does not identify any representative or indicate whether a particular person has been authorized. [Data: Entities (623)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The representative's application role is directly linked to the procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship record states that a representative authorized under the law may submit the application on the owner's behalf. This connects the representative role directly to the permit change or reissuance procedure. [Data: Relationships (2794)]

Together, the entity descriptions and relationship establish who may apply and the representative's stated basis for acting, but do not provide evidence about a specific application or its approval. [Data: Entities (4666, 623); Relationships (2794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data does not establish compliance or adverse activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a procedure and the roles permitted to take part in it. They do not report a violation, dispute, security issue, or failure to follow the process. [Data: Entities (4666, 623); Relationships (2794)]

Accordingly, the information supports an assessment of the community as a limited administrative process, but not a conclusion about actual compliance, effectiveness, or broader consequences. [Data: Entities (4666, 623); Relationships (2794)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam National Identification Application and Connected Services
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s National Identification Application, which connects permit reissuance, applications by international travel service businesses, electronic identity verification, and driver’s-license point-status updates. It functions as an administrative and identity-services channel; some described capabilities depend on the relevant system and technical infrastructure being available. The records establish the service roles and links but do not describe security incidents, compliance failures, or adverse outcomes. [Data: Entities (3205, 3695, 2745, 1752, 1566); Relationships (9116, 8064, 6634, 6306)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the application’s broad administrative and identity-related importance across several connected services, rather than evidence of harmful activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The National Identification Application is the community’s central hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The application is described as Vietnam’s national digital-identity service and an online channel for administrative procedures. It is linked to each of the other entities in the community, making it the central point connecting permit-related applications, business dossiers, identity verification, and driver’s-license point-status updates. [Data: Entities (3205); Relationships (9116, 8064, 6634, 6306)]

Its described functions include submission of application materials, receipt of processing notices, and association with electronic identity accounts. These records indicate significant administrative reach, but do not establish specific outcomes or the extent of actual use. [Data: Entities (3205)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit reissuance is handled through an application-linked procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Permit Reissuance Procedure concerns applying for and receiving a reissued permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. Applicants may submit documents through the National Identification Application and receive application notifications there. [Data: Entities (3695, 3205); Relationships (9116)]

The application description also identifies electronic forms for certain permit-related requests, including changes to or reissuance of a smart traffic vehicle operating permit. The records describe administrative functionality, not whether any particular permit application was approved or refused. [Data: Entities (3205)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: International travel service businesses can file dossiers through the application
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnamese businesses licensed to provide international travel services may apply for approval to organize foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism. The described process requires an application dossier to be submitted to the Traffic Police Department, and the businesses may submit that dossier through the National Identification Application. [Data: Entities (2745); Relationships (8064)]

This connects a defined business applicant group and an administrative approval process to the central digital service. The provided information does not indicate that any named business has applied or received approval. [Data: Entities (2745, 3205); Relationships (8064)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The application provides an access route for electronic identity verification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Electronic Identification and Authentication System is accessed through the National Identification Application. It is described as a means of accessing and verifying a test participant’s identity information, including comparing candidate identity details with information in an examination application. [Data: Entities (1752); Relationships (6634)]

This relationship shows the application’s role as an interface to identity-verification functionality. The records do not specify technical safeguards, data-sharing rules, or the system’s availability beyond the stated access relationship. [Data: Entities (1752, 3205); Relationships (6634)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver’s-license point-status updates are linked to electronic identity accounts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a process for recording deducted points on a driver’s license. When the license is represented as a data message, the status may be updated in the electronic identity card and electronic identification account through the National Identification Application. [Data: Entities (1566, 3205); Relationships (6306)]

The application description also refers to updates for deducted or restored points, while the dedicated point-status entity specifically describes deducted-points recording. The records establish a described digital linkage, not a report of any individual driver’s status or a particular update. [Data: Entities (1566, 3205); Relationships (6306)]

v.tieu_de: Priority-Vehicle Signal Permit Withdrawal and Reissuance
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a permit-compliance procedure and the unnamed agencies and organizations that hold relevant permits. When an existing permit to use a signal device on a military-force priority vehicle does not comply with the decree, the permit holders are responsible for withdrawing it and requesting a new permit. The supplied information describes the required process but does not identify any specific holder, permit, or instance of noncompliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but meaningful regulatory importance because it concerns permit compliance for signal devices on military-force priority vehicles, with no specific violation or operational impact documented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit holders are responsible for taking corrective action
phat_hien.giai_thich: The unnamed agencies and organizations that hold existing permits are responsible for withdrawing permits and requesting new ones when required. The relationship records this responsibility directly, without naming any particular agency or organization. [Data: Entities (2898); Relationships (8579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The procedure applies when an existing permit does not comply
phat_hien.giai_thich: Withdrawal and reissuance are described as necessary when a permit to use a signal device on a military-force priority vehicle does not comply with the decree. The information establishes a conditional process, not evidence that any particular permit is currently noncompliant. [Data: Entities (3697)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The corrective process has two stated steps
phat_hien.giai_thich: The permit holder must withdraw the existing permit and request a new one. The supplied description does not specify further steps, deadlines, or decision criteria for the reissuance process. [Data: Entities (3697); Relationships (8579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is narrowly focused on permit administration
phat_hien.giai_thich: The two entities are linked through a single responsibility: agencies and organizations holding permits carry out withdrawal and reissuance when required. No other entities, procedures, or activities are identified in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (2898, 3697); Relationships (8579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific breach or consequence is documented
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe what holders must do if their permits do not comply, but they do not identify a noncompliant permit, a named permit holder, or an enforcement action. Accordingly, the available evidence supports describing a compliance requirement, not asserting that a violation has occurred. [Data: Entities (2898, 3697); Relationships (8579)]

v.tieu_de: Intelligent Traffic Vehicle Permit Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community covers two administrative processes for intelligent traffic vehicle operating permits: replacement or reissuance when a permit is damaged or lost, and revocation when circumstances specified in Article 25, clause 5 apply. Authorized representatives connect to both processes: they may submit replacement or reissuance applications and surrender permits on an owner's behalf. The available information describes procedural responsibilities and a processing timeframe, but does not establish how often these processes occur or whether any party has complied with the requirements.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is limited because the records describe bounded permit-administration procedures and representation authority, without evidence of broader operational impact or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two distinct permit-administration procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community centers on replacement or reissuance of a damaged or lost intelligent traffic vehicle operating permit, and revocation of a permit under specified circumstances. These are separate administrative processes rather than evidence of a single incident or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (2717, 2718)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorized representatives act across both procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe authorized representatives as persons permitted under law to act for an intelligent traffic vehicle owner. Their stated roles span both processes: submitting an application for replacement or reissuance and surrendering a permit subject to revocation on the owner's behalf. [Data: Entities (624); Relationships (2796, 2797)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Replacement and reissuance have a stated processing timeframe
phat_hien.giai_thich: For a damaged permit or a lost permit, the licensing authority processes a replacement or reissuance request within two working days after receiving the application. The information specifies the processing timeframe but does not indicate whether it is consistently met in practice. [Data: Entities (2717); Relationships (2796)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Revocation is tied to specified circumstances and surrender
phat_hien.giai_thich: The revocation procedure applies when a permit falls within circumstances specified in Article 25, clause 5. The owner or an authorized representative must surrender the permit to the competent authority that issued it. The provided records do not describe the circumstances listed in that clause or establish that any particular permit was revoked. [Data: Entities (2718, 624); Relationships (2797)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support procedural analysis, not a compliance finding
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data identifies the relevant procedures, the representative's permitted actions, the issuing authority's processing timeframe for replacement or reissuance, and the surrender requirement associated with revocation. It contains no case-specific applications, decisions, outcomes, or evidence of failure to follow these procedures, so actual compliance or noncompliance cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (2717, 2718, 624); Relationships (2796, 2797)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Foreign-Vehicle Approval Procedure
v.tom_tat: This community consists of an administrative procedure for approving certain foreign-vehicle activities in Vietnam and the relevant provincial and centrally run city People’s Committees. The procedure covers specified tourism and non-tourism cases, as well as changes to existing approval information. Approval documents are sent to the relevant committees to coordinate management. The available information describes an administrative framework, but does not establish compliance outcomes, technical capabilities, or allegations of misconduct. [Data: Entities (226, 3687); Relationships (668)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it governs specified foreign-vehicle activities and involves coordination with local government bodies, while the provided records indicate no broader impact or compliance concerns.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The approval procedure is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community centers on the Approval Procedure for Foreign Vehicles in Vietnam, an administrative process concerning approval for specified activities involving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. Its listed degree is 8, compared with 1 for the relevant provincial and centrally run city People’s Committees, indicating that the procedure is the more connected entity in this small community. [Data: Entities (226, 3687); Relationships (668)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The procedure covers distinct tourism and non-tourism cases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The procedure covers Vietnamese international travel service businesses organizing foreign visitors who bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism. It also covers organizations or individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam for non-tourism purposes. [Data: Entities (226)]

These are the stated scopes of the procedure; the records do not specify approval criteria, processing times, or implementation outcomes. [Data: Entities (226)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Changes to existing approval information are included
phat_hien.giai_thich: The procedure also covers changes to information in an existing approval, so its stated scope extends beyond initial approvals. The available record does not describe which information may be changed or the steps required to request a change. [Data: Entities (226)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Local committees coordinate management of approved activities
phat_hien.giai_thich: Approval documents are sent to the relevant provincial and centrally run city People’s Committees for coordination in managing the approved vehicle activities. This establishes a link between the central procedure and local government bodies in relevant jurisdictions. [Data: Entities (3687); Relationships (668)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe an administrative framework, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information identifies the procedure’s scope and the committees’ coordination role, but does not report whether particular applicants complied with requirements, whether approvals were granted or denied, or whether violations occurred. The records therefore support describing the governance structure, but not drawing conclusions about enforcement effectiveness or legal compliance in practice. [Data: Entities (226, 3687); Relationships (668)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP and Implementation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP, which amends Vietnamese rules on road traffic order and safety. Its provisions address information-sharing involving the road traffic database, procedures for approving certain foreign motor vehicles to enter Vietnam, and transitional treatment of applications received or postmarked before the decree takes effect. Approval documents are also sent to relevant provincial and municipal People's Committees for coordination in management. The records describe regulatory and administrative arrangements but provide no evidence about enforcement outcomes, reputation, or technical capabilities.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because the decree sets national administrative rules for road traffic safety, vehicle-entry approvals, and coordination with local authorities.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree is the community's central legal instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP is described as a Vietnamese government decree amending and supplementing rules concerning road traffic order and safety. It is the central entity connecting the application-transition condition and the provincial and municipal authorities in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (1313); Relationships (641, 5741)]

The records identify several administrative subjects addressed by the decree, but do not provide information about its implementation, enforcement, or practical effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Procedures cover approval for certain foreign motor vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 14 adds Article 33a, which sets out procedures for approving international travel-service businesses and other organizations or individuals to bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam, including right-hand-drive cars. It also addresses procedures for amending information in an existing approval. [Data: Entities (1313)]

The supplied information describes the scope of these procedures but does not specify approval criteria, processing times, or the number of applications affected.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree amends rules on road-safety information sharing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 5 amends Clause 1 of Article 14 concerning connections to and sharing of information involving the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (1313)]

No technical architecture, data-security controls, or participating systems are described in the records, so the operational capabilities and risks of the information-sharing provisions cannot be assessed from this material.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application timing determines transitional treatment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 17 establishes transitional rules for administrative-procedure applications received by a competent authority or postmarked before the decree takes effect. The receipt or postmarking date is identified as the condition for applying the earlier rules. [Data: Entities (1313), (218); Relationships (641)]

The records do not state the decree's effective date or further detail how applications are handled beyond this timing-based distinction.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Local authorities receive approval documents for coordination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree requires approval documents to be sent to the relevant provincial and municipal People's Committees for coordination in management. [Data: Entities (3956), (1313); Relationships (5741)]

This establishes a documented coordination link between the national decree's approval process and relevant local authorities. The supplied records do not specify the committees' additional duties, decision-making powers, or compliance outcomes.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Military Control Force and Law 36/2024/QH15
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Military Control Force and its road-based inspection responsibilities. Article 65 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is described as providing for inspections of military vehicles and checks of internal-regulation and legal compliance. The Minister of National Defence issues regulations governing these activities, including inspections of the force itself. The records describe a legal and operational oversight framework; they do not report inspection outcomes, violations, or other compliance findings.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public and institutional importance because it links military road inspections to statutory provisions and ministerial regulation, but the records provide no evidence of violations or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Military Control Force is the operational center
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Military Control Force is described as responsible for checking military vehicles and inspecting compliance with internal military regulations and road law. Its relationships connect it directly to vehicle inspections and to inspections of both internal regulations and its own legal compliance, making it the central operational entity in this community. [Data: Entities (2990); Relationships (8702, 8040, 8701)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 65 provides a statutory basis for inspection activities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description says Article 65 of Vietnam’s Law 36/2024/QH15 governs patrol and inspection activities concerning road traffic order and safety, including requirements for military vehicles and their drivers to comply with inspections. The relationship record further states that Article 65 provides for the Military Control Force to inspect military vehicles and check internal-regulation and legal compliance on roads. [Data: Entities (2836); Relationships (8423)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Minister of National Defence sets relevant regulations
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Minister of National Defence is described as responsible for issuing driving-licence regulations for military forces performing national-defence duties under Article 62, and as authorized to regulate road-based inspections.
