phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 30 is associated with ambulance-driver penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The ambulance-driver entity description states that Article 30 addresses penalties and driver’s-license point deductions applicable to ambulance drivers. [Data: Entities (165)]

The data does not give the number of points deducted or clarify the specific Article 30 consequences for each of the monitoring-related circumstances described. [Data: Entities (165, 169)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence is narrow in scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community data contains two entities and one relationship, defining a regulatory topic rather than documenting a broader network of people, organizations, or events. [Data: Entities (165, 169); Relationships (520)]

No information is provided about actual compliance levels, enforcement frequency, operational impact, or the identity of any person involved; those matters therefore cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (165, 169); Relationships (520)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Article 36(2): Overhanging-Goods Transport Violations
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Article 36, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and two transport violations it covers: carrying overhanging goods during the day without red warning signals, and doing so at night or in darkness without lights or warning signals. The provision is described as prescribing fines of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for these violations. The records describe the rules and penalties, not specific cases of noncompliance or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (415, 1251, 3248); Relationships (1763, 1765)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low to moderate because the records describe a defined road-transport compliance rule and monetary penalties, but provide no evidence of actual violations, enforcement, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: One provision links two distinct violation conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 36, Clause 2 is the central entity in the community and is linked to both the daytime and nighttime transport violations. The records characterize it as the provision that prescribes fines for each condition. [Data: Entities (415, 1251, 3248); Relationships (1763, 1765)]

This structure indicates that the community concerns two specific warning-equipment requirements for vehicles carrying overhanging goods, rather than a broad set of unrelated transport offenses. [Data: Entities (1251, 3248); Relationships (1763, 1765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty range is 400,000 to 600,000 VND
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 36, Clause 2 entity description states a fine range of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for the stated goods-transport violations. Both relationships connect the article to one of the two described violations as the basis for a fine. [Data: Entities (415); Relationships (1763, 1765)]

The records do not provide additional penalty tiers, enforcement statistics, or information about how the amount is applied in individual cases. [Data: Entities (415); Relationships (1763, 1765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Daytime rule concerns missing red warning signals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The daytime violation is defined as transporting goods that extend beyond the front or rear of a vehicle without red warning signals at the goods’ front and rear ends. Article 36, Clause 2 is identified as prescribing a fine for this condition. [Data: Entities (1251, 415); Relationships (1763)]

The description specifies the relevant condition and warning-signal placement, but does not report an actual incident or establish that any named person or organization committed this violation. [Data: Entities (1251); Relationships (1763)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Nighttime rule concerns missing lights or warning signals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The nighttime violation applies when goods extend beyond the front or rear of a vehicle operating at night or in darkness without lights or warning signals. The relationship record identifies Article 36, Clause 2 as prescribing a fine for this condition. [Data: Entities (3248, 415); Relationships (1765)]

The supplied description does not specify particular operating locations, enforcement actions, or outcomes associated with this violation. [Data: Entities (3248); Relationships (1765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a narrow regulatory scope, not a history of noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community data defines two conditions and links each to the same cited provision. It contains no case records or claims identifying violators, enforcement activity, frequency, or resulting injuries or damage. [Data: Entities (415, 1251, 3248); Relationships (1763, 1765)]

Accordingly, the information supports describing the rule’s stated scope and penalty, but not assessing real-world compliance levels or the practical effectiveness of enforcement.

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Traffic Violations and 4–6 Million VND Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a stated fine range of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND, linked to three described road-traffic violations: certain driving-rule violations, improperly carrying people on a vehicle bed, and allowing people to lie, sit, or cling to the outside of a moving vehicle. The supplied records identify these as penalties under Clause 5 of Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, but provide no information about enforcement outcomes, affected parties, or broader organizational or technical capabilities. [Data: Entities (2195, 4555, 2627, 163); Relationships (7205, 7204, 516)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the records describe a specific monetary penalty tied to multiple road-traffic violations, but provide no evidence about enforcement, scale, or wider impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine range is the community’s central element
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND range is described as the monetary penalty specified in Clause 5 of Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for listed violations. It is connected in the relationship records to all three violation categories represented in this dataset. [Data: Entities (2195); Relationships (7205, 7204, 516)]

The records establish the stated range and its listed applications; they do not provide details about how penalties are assessed or enforced in particular cases. [Data: Entities (2195); Relationships (7205, 7204, 516)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-rule violations are included among the listed offenses
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described driving-rule violations include driving on the wrong side or in the wrong lane, and crossing the fixed median separating roadways. The description refers to drivers of cars and specified four-wheeled motor vehicles. [Data: Entities (4555)]

The relationship record connects this violation category to the 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND fine range. The supplied information does not specify further conditions or case-by-case application. [Data: Entities (4555, 2195); Relationships (7205)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improperly carrying people on a vehicle bed is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The dataset identifies carrying people on a vehicle bed contrary to regulations as a road-traffic violation. [Data: Entities (2627)]

A relationship explicitly states that the 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND fine range applies to this violation. No additional details about the circumstances or enforcement are included. [Data: Entities (2627, 2195); Relationships (7204)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Allowing people outside a moving vehicle is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described violation is allowing someone to lie, sit, or cling to the outside of a vehicle while it is moving. [Data: Entities (163)]

The relationship record links this conduct to the stated 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND fine range. The provided records do not describe specific incidents or outcomes. [Data: Entities (163, 2195); Relationships (516)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is limited to penalty and violation descriptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships document one fine range and three associated violation categories. They do not provide information about enforcement frequency, compliance rates, affected individuals, or the practical impact of the penalty. [Data: Entities (2195, 4555, 2627, 163); Relationships (7205, 7204, 516)]

No organizational, technical-capability, or reputation information is included in these records, so those dimensions cannot be assessed from the available evidence. [Data: Entities (2195, 4555, 2627, 163); Relationships (7205, 7204, 516)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Road-Traffic Towing Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its specified penalties for towing-related conduct by drivers of cars and certain similar vehicles. Article 6 links several towing and pushing violations to fines of VND 800,000–1,000,000, while Article 29 separately provides for a VND 5,000,000–10,000,000 fine when a road-rescue vehicle tows a vehicle ineligible for rescue. The records also identify an Article 6 exception referring to Article 29 and a separate driving-licence point-deduction provision. The material describes legal rules, not evidence of actual violations or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (503, 2115, 355, 3647, 895); Relationships (2376, 1446, 3458)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes concrete traffic-safety penalties and licensing consequences, but the records concern a narrow legal framework and do not establish actual violations or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 is the central rule for specified driver violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the hub of the community: it sets out penalties and driving-licence point deductions for specified violations by drivers of cars, motorized four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles, and similar vehicles. It is connected to both the individual towing-related violations and the applicable fine. [Data: Entities (503); Relationships (2376, 2384, 2387, 2388, 2390)]

The available records describe provisions and penalties; they do not identify any person or organization that committed a violation, nor do they document enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (503, 2115)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified towing and pushing conduct carries a fine of VND 800,000–1,000,000
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated fine for the specified towing-related violations is VND 800,000–1,000,000. The linked conduct includes pushing another vehicle or object with a car, towing an additional trailer, vehicle, or object behind a trailer or semi-trailer, and towing another vehicle or object with a car subject to stated exceptions. [Data: Entities (2115, 4008, 4970, 4973); Relationships (2376, 2381, 2387, 2388)]

An insecure or unsafe connection between a towing vehicle and the vehicle being towed is also identified as a violation subject to the stated fine, with a separately specified Article 29 exception. [Data: Entities (5265, 2115); Relationships (2390, 7108, 1449)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 distinguishes ordinary towing violations from an Article 29 rescue-vehicle rule
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6’s clause 3 penalties do not cover the separately specified violation in Article 29, clause 3a, point b, concerning a road-rescue vehicle towing a vehicle that is not eligible for rescue. The records explicitly connect Article 6’s exception to Article 29. [Data: Entities (503, 355, 3647); Relationships (1446, 1449)]

For that unauthorized towing by a road-rescue vehicle, the stated penalty is VND 5,000,000–10,000,000. This is a different, higher stated fine than the VND 800,000–1,000,000 range associated with the specified Article 6 towing violations. [Data: Entities (3647, 355, 2115); Relationships (3458, 2376)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine provisions cover distinct towing scenarios and exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish towing another vehicle or object with a car from towing an additional trailer, vehicle, or object when already towing a trailer or semi-trailer. Article 6 also identifies exceptions for specified circumstances, including towing a trailer or semi-trailer and towing a disabled specialized vehicle that cannot move under its own power. [Data: Entities (4973, 4970); Relationships (2387, 2388, 7106, 7107)]

Pushing another vehicle or object with a car is listed as a separate violation rather than being folded into the towing descriptions. [Data: Entities (4008); Relationships (2381, 7105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 includes licensing consequences beyond the listed towing fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 is described as addressing both monetary penalties and driving-licence point deductions. In particular, clause 16 provides for a 10-point deduction for violations specified in Article 6, points a of clause 9, clause 10, and point đ of clause 11. The records do not say that this deduction applies to the clause 3 towing violations discussed elsewhere in the community. [Data: Entities (503, 895); Relationships (2365)]

The article description also notes that specified violations may involve confiscation of improperly installed or used priority-signal equipment, confiscation of a vehicle for repeat weaving or swerving, and application of the temporary-detention rule in Article 48. These are described as provisions within Article 6, not as consequences specifically established for the towing violations in this dataset. [Data: Entities (503)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support regulatory importance, not conclusions about actual compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community provides details about the scope of the rules, fine ranges, exceptions, and a licensing consequence. It therefore has relevance to understanding the stated road-traffic penalty framework. [Data: Entities (503, 2115, 355, 895); Relationships (2376, 1446, 2365, 3458)]

No records here identify enforcement cases, rates of compliance, affected parties, technical capabilities, or public reputation. The available evidence consequently does not support claims about how often the rules are breached or what their real-world effects have been. [Data: Entities (503, 2115, 355, 3647)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Businesses and Regulatory Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road transport and transport-support businesses and two specified violations: failing to comply with posted vehicle information and failing to provide passengers with safety and emergency-exit guidance. The supplied records associate both violations with the business category and state fines for them; the passenger-guidance record also gives different fine ranges for individuals and transport business organizations. The information indicates regulatory and compliance relevance, but does not document actual violations by particular businesses, enforcement actions, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (4475, 1964, 2019); Relationships (6916, 6999)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes financial penalties for transport-related regulatory violations, but the records do not identify specific offenders or actual incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport businesses are the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road transport and transport-support businesses form the community's organizing category. The records describe these organizations as subject to fines for the specified violations, making their regulatory obligations the main connection among the entities. [Data: Entities (4475); Relationships (6916, 6999)]

The records address a sector and stated rules rather than naming any individual business or asserting that a particular organization committed an offense. [Data: Entities (4475, 1964, 2019); Relationships (6916, 6999)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to comply with posted vehicle information carries a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One identified violation is failing to comply with information displayed on a vehicle as required by regulations. The relationship record states that organizations engaged in road transport or transport-support services committing this violation are subject to a fine of 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1964, 4475); Relationships (6916)]

The supplied text links this penalty to Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, but provides no details about enforcement or any specific case. [Data: Entities (4475); Relationships (6916)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger safety and emergency-exit guidance is a separate compliance issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The second violation concerns using a commercial passenger vehicle without providing passengers with required traffic-safety and emergency-evacuation guidance. The description identifies this as a requirement associated with passenger transport. [Data: Entities (2019)]

The relationship record applies the violation and its stated fine to organizations conducting transport or transport-support business. It does not report that any identified organization failed to provide the guidance. [Data: Relationships (6999)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The passenger-guidance penalty varies by type of offender
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For failure to provide passenger safety and emergency-exit guidance, the entity record states a fine of 1,000,000–2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for an individual and 2,000,000–4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for a transport business organization. [Data: Entities (2019)]

These stated amounts differ from the 10,000,000–12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng range associated with failure to comply with posted vehicle information. The records therefore distinguish the violations and their respective penalties. [Data: Entities (1964, 2019, 4475); Relationships (6916, 6999)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support compliance awareness, not conclusions about actual conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Together, the records identify two types of transport-related noncompliance and describe penalties applicable to relevant businesses. This makes the information useful for understanding the stated regulatory issues and their potential financial consequences. [Data: Entities (4475, 1964, 2019); Relationships (6916, 6999)]

No supplied record names an offending business, confirms that a violation occurred, or describes an enforcement outcome, passenger injury, or operational impact. The community's significance should therefore be assessed as regulatory in scope, without treating the listed violations as evidence of actual misconduct. [Data: Entities (4475, 1964, 2019); Relationships (6916, 6999)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Traffic Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a stated fine of 18,000,000–20,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to several traffic violations: reversing, making a U-turn, or driving against traffic on an expressway; driving with prohibited drugs or stimulants in the body; and failure to obey traffic-controller instructions. The expressway-violation descriptions also cite a higher fine range of 30,000,000–40,000,000 đồng, creating unresolved ambiguity about which provision applies. The records describe exemptions for priority vehicles performing emergency duties under the cited provision. They document penalty descriptions, not actual violations or enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns serious road-safety violations and substantial fines, while the records show legal descriptions rather than evidence of actual incidents or enforcement.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The 18,000,000–20,000,000 đồng fine is the community’s central link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified fine is connected to five violation categories in the relationship data: reversing, making a U-turn, or driving against traffic on an expressway, driving with prohibited drugs or stimulants in the body, and failing to obey traffic-controller instructions. This makes the fine the main organizing point in the community. [Data: Entities (2154); Relationships (7156, 7155, 6337, 6505, 6957)]

The records describe prescribed penalties; they do not establish that any particular person committed a violation or was fined.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Expressway penalties are described inconsistently
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For making a U-turn, reversing, and driving against traffic on an expressway, the descriptions cite both 18,000,000–20,000,000 đồng and 30,000,000–40,000,000 đồng. The records state that the applicable range cannot be determined from the descriptions alone and depends on which provision governs. [Data: Entities (2949, 4211, 1597)]

This uncertainty is material to interpreting the penalty information. The available data does not resolve the discrepancy or identify which decree or version applies.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency-duty priority vehicles are described as exempt from specified penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect performing emergency duties with exemptions from the specified penalties for making a U-turn, reversing, and driving against traffic on an expressways. The descriptions qualify this as applying to priority vehicles performing emergency duties as prescribed. [Data: Entities (3690); Relationships (8651, 6338, 9580)]

The exception is described for these expressway provisions; the data does not establish that it applies to the other violation categories in this community.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine also covers drug-related driving and disobeying traffic controllers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving on a road while the driver’s body contains narcotics or other stimulants prohibited by law is described as punishable by 18,000,000–20,000,000 đồng under Article 8, Clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The relationship data links this violation to the central fine. [Data: Entities (1691, 2154); Relationships (6505)]

Failure to comply with a traffic controller’s commands or instructions is also linked to the same range under Article 6, Clause 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, for the specified vehicle types. The records do not provide further detail about which vehicle types are covered. [Data: Entities (1997, 2154); Relationships (6957)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal provisions, not observed conduct or enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities characterize violation types and prescribed fines, while the relationships associate those descriptions with penalty amounts or an emergency-duty exception. They contain no identified driver, incident, enforcement action, or outcome. [Data: Entities (2154, 2949, 4211, 1597, 1691); Relationships (7156, 7155, 6337, 6505, 6957)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant as a summary of traffic-rule and penalty information, but the supplied evidence does not support claims about actual compliance, enforcement frequency, or the reputation of any person or organization.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Violations and Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a stated fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 VND, linked to several driving violations and to Article 6, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The listed violations include driving onto an expressway, unsafe vehicle-door opening, and failures to yield at specified roundabouts. The source descriptions distinguish the expressway violation as an Article 7 matter and note an exception for vehicles managing or maintaining the expressway. [Data: Entities (2193, 1646, 517, 5280, 2040); Relationships (6406, 2424, 7021, 7022, 2425)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate public and compliance significance because it describes several traffic violations and a substantial stated fine, but the records provide no evidence of broader operational or societal impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community’s central link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 4,000,000-to-6,000,000 VND penalty is the most connected entity in the provided records, with relationships linking it to the expressway violation, Article 6, Clause 5, and both roundabout-yield violations. This makes the penalty the organizing point for the community. [Data: Entities (2193); Relationships (6406, 2424, 7021, 7022)]

The records establish the stated amount and links to the listed violations, but do not provide information about enforcement frequency, payment, appeals, or additional consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6, Clause 5 provides a legal basis for some listed penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting fines of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 VND for specified violations by drivers of cars and similar vehicles. Its relationship to the fine entity and to unsafe vehicle-door opening directly supports that connection. [Data: Entities (517, 2193, 5280); Relationships (2424, 2425)]

The source material does not establish that every violation in the community falls under this clause; the expressway violation is separately described as an Article 7 violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving onto an expressway is linked to the stated fine, with an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving a covered vehicle onto an expressway is described as a road-traffic violation under Article 7, and the relationship record links it to the 4,000,000-to-6,000,000 VND fine. The entity description states that the prohibition does not apply to vehicles used to manage or maintain the expressway. [Data: Entities (1646, 2193); Relationships (6406)]

This is a distinct legal basis from Article 6, Clause 5 in the supplied descriptions; the records do not provide further detail about the covered vehicle categories or how the exception is applied.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unsafe vehicle-door opening is identified under Article 6, Clause 5
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The unsafe-door-opening violation is defined as opening a vehicle door or leaving it open without ensuring safety. The entity description states that Article 6, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP subjects it to the stated fine, and the relationship records connect the provision to both the violation and the fine. [Data: Entities (5280, 517, 2193); Relationships (2425, 2424)]

The records describe the conduct and penalty but do not specify incident circumstances, injury outcomes, or enforcement data.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two roundabout-yield violations are associated with the same fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify failure to yield to traffic from the left at a signed roundabout-priority intersection and failure to yield to traffic from the right at an unsignalized roundabout intersection. Each is linked to the 4,000,000-to-6,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (2039, 2040, 2193); Relationships (7021, 7022)]

The descriptions distinguish the intersection conditions and direction of approaching traffic. The provided records do not state which specific statutory clause governs these two violations, so no further legal attribution can be made from this data.

v.tieu_de: Road-Transport Safety Violations and Regulated Service Providers
v.tom_tat: This community links journey-monitoring and driver-image service providers, and vehicle-device manufacturers, assemblers, and importers, to road-transport traffic-order and safety violations. The relationships identify both groups as subject to fines specified in Article 26; the supplied description gives a fine range of 40,000,000 to 60,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the specified violations. The records indicate regulatory and financial significance but do not detail particular incidents or the conduct of individual organizations.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to road-transport safety regulation and potentially substantial fines, balanced against the limited evidence about specific violations or affected organizations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on regulated road-transport safety violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violations entity concerns regulations on road-traffic order and safety in road transport and road-transport support services. It is connected to both journey-monitoring and driver-image service providers and vehicle-device manufacturers, assemblers, and importers, making it the regulatory focus of this community. [Data: Entities (4580); Relationships (8133, 10323)]

The records establish a regulatory connection, but do not identify a specific incident, organization, or finding of liability. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580, 5515); Relationships (8133, 10323)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Journey-monitoring and driver-image providers are within the cited enforcement scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The service-provider category covers organizations or units that monitor vehicle journeys and record images of vehicle drivers. The relationship to road-transport traffic-order and safety violations says violations by these providers are subject to fines specified in Article 26. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580); Relationships (8133)]

The records do not specify which particular provider, action, or circumstances would constitute a violation. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580); Relationships (8133)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-device businesses are also linked to Article 26 fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The second regulated group comprises organizations that manufacture, assemble, or import devices installed in cars to record driver images. The relationship records that violations by these organizations are subject to the fines specified in Article 26. [Data: Entities (5515, 4580); Relationships (10323)]

No individual business or specific noncompliant device or practice is identified in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (5515, 4580); Relationships (10323)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine range indicates potential financial consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violations description gives a fine range of 40,000,000 to 60,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the specified road-transport traffic-order and safety violations. [Data: Entities (4580)]

The relationships connect both listed organizational categories to fines specified in Article 26, but the records do not provide a separate amount for each category or describe how a particular fine would be determined. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580, 5515); Relationships (8133, 10323)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes categories and regulatory links, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define two types of organizations and connect them to a violations category, but they do not name particular organizations or report that any specific entity has violated the rules. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580, 5515); Relationships (8133, 10323)]

Accordingly, the information supports identifying the groups’ stated regulatory exposure, but not drawing conclusions about actual compliance, enforcement history, or reputation. [Data: Entities (2792, 4580, 5515); Relationships (8133, 10323)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Đồng Traffic Fine and Covered Violations
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around a stated fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to seven traffic violations. The violations cover expressway conduct, dangerous-goods transport, vehicle inspection, and obeying traffic signals. The information describes penalties and violation types, but does not provide enforcement outcomes or details about affected individuals or organizations. [Data: Entities (2192); Relationships (6730, 6361, 6509, 6883, 6956, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the fine connects several distinct traffic-compliance categories, while the data provides no evidence of actual incidents, enforcement outcomes, or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single monetary penalty is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng is the hub of the community, and the listed relationships connect it to seven specified traffic violations. Its description also associates the penalty with provisions including Article 6, Clause 5, and Article 13, Clause 6, without mapping every provision to an individual violation. [Data: Entities (2192); Relationships (6730, 6361, 6509, 6883, 6956, +more)]

The records describe a regulatory penalty rather than a particular enforcement case. They do not identify drivers, vehicles, dates, or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Four listed violations concern expressway conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalty is linked to failing to maintain a safe distance on an expressway, entering or exiting an expressway contrary to rules, and driving in an emergency stopping lane or on the shoulder. These are presented as separate violations subject to the stated fine. [Data: Entities (1931, 1803, 1611, 2192); Relationships (6883, 6730, 6361)]

The records identify the conduct but provide no incident-level information or evidence about how often these violations occur.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods transport requirements are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Two listed violations concern cars transporting dangerous goods without required hazard labels or identification symbols, and without required warning lights or signals. The relationships state that the central fine applies to both violations. [Data: Entities (5133, 5135, 2192); Relationships (7202, 7203)]

The supplied information describes the missing safety-related equipment or markings, but does not report any specific transport, hazardous material, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle inspection compliance is another covered area
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Operating a vehicle that requires inspection without a valid inspection certificate or sticker—or with one expired for at least a month—is described as subject to the 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 đồng fine. The description includes trailers and semi-trailers. [Data: Entities (1695, 2192); Relationships (6509)]

This record specifies the inspection-related condition and penalty, but does not identify particular vehicles or provide information about inspection or enforcement activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to obey a traffic signal is explicitly linked to the fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The failure-to-obey-a-traffic-signal entity states that the fine is between 4,000,000 and 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and its relationship to the central fine entity confirms the connection. [Data: Entities (1996, 2192); Relationships (6956)]

The community therefore covers both traffic conduct and vehicle or dangerous-goods compliance. The available records do not describe a specific signal violation, its circumstances, or its consequences.

v.tieu_de: Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which is linked to specified road-traffic violations, improper use of roadways or sidewalks, and penalties or remedial measures. The described consequences include fines for false or inaccurate reporting to evade responsibility and, in a specified case, a 22-to-24-month driving-license suspension. The material describes regulatory provisions and violation categories; it does not establish how often violations occur or whether any particular person or organization has violated the rules.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the article’s practical regulatory significance and potentially substantial penalties, while the provided records do not indicate the prevalence of violations or broader community-level effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 is the community’s organizing entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 is described as setting out penalties, including driving-licence point deductions, for specified road-traffic violations and improper use of roadways or sidewalks. It is linked to each of the other listed entities, making it the central subject of this community. [Data: Entities (247); Relationships (791, 792, 793, 794, 795)]

The records describe legal rules and categories of conduct, not particular enforcement events or a documented pattern of non-compliance. The community’s significance is therefore grounded in the scope of the provisions described, rather than evidence of actual incidents. [Data: Entities (247, 4468); Relationships (795)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified violations may carry driving-license suspensions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe driving-license suspension as an additional or supplementary penalty for specified road-traffic violations. They identify possible periods of 10 to 12 months or 22 to 24 months under applicable provisions, and caution that these ranges concern different violations rather than one universal suspension period. [Data: Entities (1717)]

The relationship specifically states that Article 12 provides for a 22-to-24-month suspension in a specified case. The provided information does not identify the exact circumstances of that case, so the duration should not be generalized to all violations covered by Article 12. [Data: Relationships (791); Entities (247, 1717)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Use of roads and sidewalks for non-permitted purposes is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Improper use of roadways or sidewalks is described as using these spaces for purposes not permitted by applicable rules, and the entity record connects this conduct to Article 12. [Data: Entities (2623); Relationships (793)]

A second entity describes misuse of roads or sidewalks as use for purposes other than their intended purposes. Article 12 is also linked to that category as a subject of penalties, but the supplied records do not specify particular examples, fine amounts, or remedial measures for each form of misuse. [Data: Entities (3037); Relationships (794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: False or incomplete reporting to evade responsibility is penalized
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a violation involving failure to report, false reporting, or providing inaccurate information or documents to evade responsibility after being found to have violated road-traffic order and safety laws. [Data: Entities (1846)]

Article 12 is linked to fines for this conduct. The data does not provide the fine amounts or indicate that any particular person has engaged in it. [Data: Relationships (792); Entities (247, 1846)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a regulatory overview, not the scale of real-world impact
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed entities cover Article 12, related violation categories, and described penalties; the relationships connect these subjects directly to the article. This supports treating the community as a compact overview of a traffic-enforcement provision and its associated consequences. [Data: Entities (247, 1717, 2623, 1846, 4468, +more); Relationships (791, 792, 793, 794, 795)]

No supplied record gives violation counts, enforcement frequency, affected populations, or evidence of actual cases. Accordingly, the material supports conclusions about the types of conduct and consequences described, but not claims about prevalence, compliance rates, or aggregate harm. [Data: Entities (247, 4468); Relationships (791, 792, 795)]

v.tieu_de: Push-Cart Road Violation and 100,000–200,000 VND Fine
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of a traffic violation—using a push cart as a mobile stall on a road in a way that obstructs traffic—and a monetary penalty of 100,000–200,000 VND. The relationship states that the decree sets this fine for the violation. The supplied data does not identify further entities, enforcement details, or broader impacts.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the data describes a specific traffic obstruction violation and a limited monetary penalty, with no evidence of broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is specifically defined as obstructing traffic
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described conduct is using a push cart as a mobile stall on a road in a way that obstructs traffic. The record identifies this as a road-traffic violation, but provides no additional details about circumstances or enforcement. [Data: Entities (5354)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is 100,000–200,000 VND
phat_hien.giai_thich: The fine entity specifies a monetary penalty in the range of 100,000–200,000 VND. The data does not state how the amount is determined within that range. [Data: Entities (2140)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree links the fine directly to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship record states that the decree sets the specified fine for using a push cart as a mobile stall on a road and obstructing traffic. This connects the penalty and the violation within the supplied information. [Data: Relationships (7136)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is narrowly focused on one regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: The two entities and their single relationship describe only the specified violation and its associated fine. The records provide no other offenses, penalties, organizations, or individuals to broaden the community's scope. [Data: Entities (2140, 5354); Relationships (7136)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Broader compliance and impact conclusions are not supported
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify a prohibited form of conduct and its stated monetary penalty, but do not provide information about actual incidents, enforcement frequency, compliance rates, or resulting harm. Accordingly, the evidence supports describing the rule and penalty, but not conclusions about prevalence or wider effects. [Data: Entities (2140, 5354); Relationships (7136)]

v.tieu_de: Car Driving and the Inoperative-Horn Violation
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a driver of a car and the traffic violation of driving without an operative horn. The relationship identifies the driver as the person who commits the violation, which the provided description says is punishable under Article 13 by a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND. The records do not describe other entities, broader consequences, or enforcement details.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the community concerns a specific vehicle violation with a stated monetary fine and provides no evidence of broader or more severe impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a specific traffic violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is driving a car without a horn or with a horn that does not work. Its description identifies it as a traffic violation and states that Article 13 provides a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND. [Data: Entities (1578)]

The records provide no further details about the circumstances in which the rule applies or how it is enforced. [Data: Entities (1578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver is directly linked to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies a car driver as the person who commits the inoperative-horn violation. The driver entity includes cars towing trailers or semi-trailers in its description. [Data: Entities (1459, 1578); Relationships (6048)]

This link establishes the described actor and violation, but does not identify a particular driver or incident. [Data: Entities (1459, 1578); Relationships (6048)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A monetary penalty is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation description gives a fine range of 400,000 to 600,000 VND under Article 13. The records do not state how the amount is determined within that range or whether other penalties may apply. [Data: Entities (1578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information is narrowly scoped
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationship cover only the car driver, the inoperative-horn violation, and the link between them. They provide no information about an organization, a particular enforcement action, or a specific case. [Data: Entities (1459, 1578); Relationships (6048)]

Accordingly, the community's documented significance is limited to the described traffic rule and its stated fine. [Data: Entities (1578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No broader capabilities or reputation are documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a vehicle category and a traffic violation, but provide no evidence about technical capabilities beyond the horn requirement, or about any person's or organization's reputation. [Data: Entities (1459, 1578); Relationships (6048)]

Any assessment beyond the stated violation, driver relationship, and fine would exceed the information provided. [Data: Entities (1459, 1578); Relationships (6048)]

v.tieu_de: Road Weight-Limit Violation and 40–50 Million Đồng Fine
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a road-traffic violation—driving a vehicle whose total weight or axle load exceeds the permitted road limit by more than 50%—and the associated fine of 40,000,000 to 50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The relationship records that the violation is subject to this penalty; the violation description also states an exception for vehicles with a valid circulation permit under Clause 5 of Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The data describes a legal penalty, not a specific incident or finding that any person or vehicle violated the rule.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the significance of a severe load-limit violation and substantial specified fine, while the data provides no evidence of an actual incident or broader community activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community links one violation to its specified penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community has a simple structure: the described road-weight-limit violation is directly connected to the fine of 40,000,000 to 50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The relationship states that the violation is subject to that fine. [Data: Entities (1589, 2197); Relationships (6327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation involves exceeding the limit by more than 50%
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation description concerns a vehicle whose total weight or axle load, including cargo and passengers, exceeds the road's permitted load by more than 50%. The data does not describe a particular vehicle, driver, or occurrence. [Data: Entities (1589)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is a monetary range
phat_hien.giai_thich: The specified penalty is a fine ranging from 40,000,000 to 50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The relationship connects this penalty to the described violation, without specifying how a fine within that range is determined. [Data: Entities (2197); Relationships (6327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A valid circulation permit is stated as an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation description states that the penalty applies except when the vehicle has a valid circulation permit. The supplied information does not further define permit requirements or establish whether any particular vehicle holds one. [Data: Entities (1589)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The description identifies a specific regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation description attributes the fine to Clause 5 of Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The data provides this reference as part of the description but does not include the underlying legal text or additional details about enforcement. [Data: Entities (1589, 2197)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial Police Social Order Division and Head
v.tom_tat: The community consists of a provincial-level police division responsible for administrative management of social order and the official who heads it. The division’s description says its head has sanctioning authority, and the sole relationship record confirms the head–division connection. The available information establishes a formal administrative role but does not describe specific actions, outcomes, or broader institutional context.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the division’s stated sanctioning authority and provincial-level remit, tempered by the limited evidence about its activities and wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial administrative police function
phat_hien.giai_thich: The division is described as a provincial-level police division for administrative management of social order. This identifies its stated organizational remit, but the records do not specify the jurisdiction’s boundaries or the division’s particular operations. [Data: Entities (3973)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division head is identified as having sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich: The division’s description expressly includes it among divisions whose heads have sanctioning authority, and the head entity is itself described as an official listed as having that authority. The records do not specify the kinds of sanctions, the procedures for applying them, or any instance in which the authority was exercised. [Data: Entities (3973, 3974)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A direct leadership relationship links the two entities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship record states that the official heads the provincial police administrative management of social order division. This establishes the central organizational link in the community; no other relationships are provided. [Data: Relationships (9802)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a narrow documented structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records identify one division, its head, and their leadership relationship. This supports describing the available network as a simple organizational pair, but does not establish that the division has no other personnel, units, or external connections. [Data: Entities (3973, 3974); Relationships (9802)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance, reputation, and operational performance cannot be assessed
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the division’s remit and the head’s stated authority, but provide no information about legal compliance, allegations, public reputation, technical capabilities, or operational outcomes. These areas therefore remain undetermined from the supplied evidence. [Data: Entities (3973, 3974); Relationships (9802)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Road-Traffic Regulation
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, a broad Vietnamese framework governing road-traffic order and safety. Its connected provisions cover road users, vehicle owners, transport businesses, and vehicle-related service organizations, linking specified violations to fines, driving-licence point deductions, remedial measures, and enforcement powers. The records describe a substantial regulatory and operational footprint, including freight rules and journey-monitoring requirements, but do not establish actual violations or compliance outcomes by any person or organization. [Data: Entities (1282, 1562, 495); Relationships (4991, 5302, 5341)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the decree has broad reach across road users, commercial transport, vehicle services, and enforcement, although the records establish regulatory scope rather than actual violations or harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad framework with extensive regulatory reach
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the community’s central entity, with provisions spanning traffic conduct, transport, vehicle condition, licensing, and enforcement. Its stated scope includes individuals and organizations, including Vietnamese and foreign parties operating in Vietnam. [Data: Entities (1282)]

The decree covers a wide range of road users and activities, including drivers, pedestrians, vehicle owners, transport and rescue operators, inspection services, and driver training and testing. This makes the framework relevant to both individual conduct and organizational operations. [Data: Entities (1282); Relationships (2299, 4991, 5302)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctions combine fines, licence points, and other measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree provides for monetary fines and driving-licence point deductions for specified violations. The point-deduction measure applies according to the relevant provision and does not automatically attach to every violation described in the records. [Data: Entities (1282, 1562); Relationships (4991)]

Other described consequences include vehicle confiscation, temporary deprivation of certain licence or certificate rights, and corrective measures such as remedying vehicle conditions or recovering unlawful gains. These are provisions of the framework, not evidence that a particular sanction was imposed. [Data: Entities (1282, 5381); Relationships (5568, 3899)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Enforcement authority is allocated to designated officials and bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree identifies officials and bodies authorized to impose administrative sanctions. Article 41 allocates penalty authority to specified police units, while Article 43 addresses the powers of specified People’s Public Security officials. [Data: Entities (446, 453); Relationships (2038, 2079)]

The records also identify a head of a Traffic Police Department professional division as having sanctioning authority and describe the director of the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order as authorized to impose fines up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The supplied material describes these authorities but does not document their exercise in any particular case. [Data: Entities (2437, 3802); Relationships (5175, 5341)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework addresses serious and routine road-safety conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Listed provisions cover conduct with potentially significant road-safety consequences. For example, the records associate specified Article 6 violations with fines of 40,000,000–50,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and driving-licence point deductions, while not identifying all conduct to which that range applies. [Data: Entities (3054); Relationships (5250)]

Other examples include improper lane changes on expressways, failure to yield to a priority vehicle, and hazardous U-turns or turns where prohibited. These examples show that the decree also regulates more routine driving conduct; the records do not establish that any of these violations occurred. [Data: Entities (2603, 2064, 4727); Relationships (5204, 5100, 5458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Freight operators face cargo, vehicle, and documentation requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses oversized or overweight cargo transport, including cargo dimensions relative to a valid permit. The listed penalty for exceeding permitted dimensions is a fine of 8,000,000–10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and a driving-licence point deduction, with the number of points not specified in the entity description. [Data: Entities (3506); Relationships (5302)]

Related provisions cover transporting oversized or overweight cargo without required size signage and loads exceeding the capacity stated in a vehicle inspection certificate. The records specify a 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng fine for the signage violation and distinguish overloading fines for individuals and organizations. [Data: Entities (5144, 4516); Relationships (5513, 5429)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monitoring-device operation and data integrity are regulated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify violations involving falsified journey-monitoring data and operating a vehicle with an ineffective journey-monitoring device. They also describe requirements concerning driver-image data, making device function and data integrity part of the compliance framework. [Data: Entities (2083, 3391); Relationships (5106, 5289)]

The supplied report records state that passenger-compartment image-recording provisions have a specified effective date of January 1, 2029. That date is distinct from the other monitoring-related rules; the available information does not provide further implementation detail. [Data: Reports (3-4)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Responsibility extends beyond the driver
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree includes vehicle-owner penalties, including cases where an owner directly commits a specified violation or allows an employee or representative to commit it. The records also indicate that some owner fines differ between individuals and organizations. [Data: Entities (5587, 3715); Relationships (5599, 5335)]

The broader scope includes vehicle manufacturing, assembly, inspection, and testing establishments, as well as driver-training and testing services. This indicates regulatory exposure for organizations and service providers in addition to drivers and owners. [Data: Entities (1282); Relationships (5241, 5485)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A reported inconsistency makes one confiscation limit uncertain
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 is described as authorizing specified officials to confiscate evidence and vehicles, subject to a value ceiling. The Article 43 entity description gives a limit of 30,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (453); Relationships (2079, 3899)]

The confiscation entity, however, reports conflicting limits of 30,000,000 đồng and 45,000,000 VND and says the applicable ceiling cannot be determined from the supplied information. The limit should therefore be verified against authoritative legal text before operational reliance; the records do not establish any particular confiscation action. [Data: Entities (1084, 453); Reports (3-6)]

v.tieu_de: Driver Image-Recording Equipment Penalties and 2028 Effective Date
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a set of administrative penalties for violations of driver image-recording equipment rules and the date those penalties take effect. The penalties concern specified categories of vehicles, and the connected effective-date entity identifies January 1, 2028, as their start date. The data does not specify penalty amounts or further implementation details.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory importance because it describes penalties affecting several vehicle categories, while the available data provides no penalty amounts or broader impact details.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on administrative penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich: The primary subject is administrative penalties for violations of required driver image-recording equipment rules. The entity description identifies the penalties and the relevant equipment requirement but does not state the penalty amounts or specific consequences. [Data: Entities (77)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated scope includes multiple vehicle categories

The provided information does not identify a particular institution or explain the branch’s role beyond this reference. [Data: Entities (670, 5385); Relationships (2891)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe procedures, not demonstrated compliance or misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions outline a document-check process, a provision addressing temporary custody, and a reference involving a receipt and certified registration copy. They do not identify a person or organization accused of wrongdoing, nor do they report whether any party complied with the described requirements.

Accordingly, the community supports an account of procedural connections but not a conclusion about actual legal compliance, enforcement, or adverse conduct. [Data: Entities (5385, 5367, 670); Relationships (10630, 2891)]

v.tieu_de: Article 13 Vehicle Emissions and Noise Penalties
v.tom_tat: This narrowly focused community concerns a vehicle-equipment and environmental-compliance violation addressed by Clause 2 of Article 13. The records describe a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for driving a covered vehicle without effective muffler or smoke-reduction equipment, or with equipment that does not meet emissions or noise standards. The penalty and the violation are directly linked, but the records do not describe enforcement cases, affected parties, or broader institutional relationships.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it describes a specific monetary penalty tied to vehicle emissions and noise compliance, while the available records show only a narrowly scoped provision and violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A defined fine applies to the specified violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 2 of Article 13 is described as setting a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for the covered vehicle-condition violations. The penalty record repeats this range and identifies the provision as part of Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (904, 3632)]

The relationship record connects Clause 2 directly to the vehicle-equipment and environmental-compliance violation, identifying the clause as the source of the fine. [Data: Relationships (3391)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The covered conduct concerns mufflers and smoke-reduction equipment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is described as driving a covered vehicle without an effective muffler or smoke-reduction component, or with such equipment when it fails the applicable environmental standards. [Data: Entities (5428)]

The penalty description likewise identifies the absence or failure of these components as conduct covered by the fine. [Data: Entities (3632)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emissions and noise standards are both in scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records specify that the relevant equipment may fail environmental standards for emissions or for noise; the described violation is therefore not limited to one of those two compliance dimensions. [Data: Entities (3632, 5428)]

The penalty event is linked to this specific violation, rather than to a general category of vehicle offenses. [Data: Relationships (9500)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The graph links the legal provision, penalty, and violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community has a compact structure: Clause 2 of Article 13 is connected to the vehicle violation as the source of its fine, while the penalty entity is also connected to that same violation as the conduct it covers. [Data: Relationships (3391, 9500)]

These records establish the relationship among the provision, the penalty description, and the conduct, but do not provide additional details about how a particular case would be assessed or processed. [Data: Entities (904, 3632, 5428); Relationships (3391, 9500)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information is limited to the provision and covered conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the fine range, the relevant equipment and standards, and the links among these items. They do not identify any individuals, organizations, enforcement actions, or specific incidents associated with the violation. [Data: Entities (904, 3632, 5428); Relationships (3391, 9500)]

Accordingly, the evidence supports a description of the rule and its stated scope, but not conclusions about compliance rates, enforcement outcomes, or broader effects.

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Road-Traffic Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road-traffic violations and administrative penalties under Vietnamese Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 7 is a prominent hub for penalties applying to motorcycle and similar-vehicle operators, including fines and, for specified violations, driving-license point deductions. The supplied records describe several concrete violations and fine ranges, while emphasizing that point deductions depend on the particular conduct and provision. The information shows the scope of the penalty framework but does not establish whether any person or organization complied with it.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the broad relevance of traffic rules and penalties across vehicle types, while the records provide no evidence of a specific incident, widespread noncompliance, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad administrative framework for road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as addressing violations by multiple classes of road users. Article 6 covers drivers of cars and similar vehicles, Article 7 covers motorcycle and similar-vehicle operators, and other provisions address additional traffic rules and vehicle owners. The available descriptions therefore indicate a framework with relevance across varied road users, though they do not quantify its reach or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4433, 1710)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 7 is a central node for motorcycle-related penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 7 sets out fines and driving-license point deductions for operators of motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and similar vehicles. The linked records connect the article to speeding, failure to use headlights, and obstruction of a priority vehicle, as well as to the broader category of fines and point deductions. [Data: Entities (1292, 542, 2263); Relationships (5630, 5632, 5633, 5635)]

The excerpts give some fine ranges but do not identify all conduct associated with every stated amount. In particular, the description for a 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 đồng fine says the specific violations are not identified in the excerpts. [Data: Entities (1292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point deductions are conditional and not fully specified for individual violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving-license point deduction is described as a sanction for specified traffic violations, potentially alongside other penalties. The records caution that many descriptions identify point deduction as addressed or possible without establishing that a deduction applies to the particular conduct or specifying its amount. [Data: Entities (1710); Relationships (6552, 5631, 2548)]

Some point amounts are stated for other specified conduct in the general point-deduction description, including four points for a vehicle owner who directly operates the vehicle and commits a covered violation, two points for specified conduct under Article 29, and three points for conduct under Article 34. The supplied records do not connect those examples to the specific Article 7 violations described elsewhere. [Data: Entities (1710)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examples include speeding and failure to use headlights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records specify a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for driving a motorcycle or similar vehicle from 5 km/h to less than 10 km/h above the speed limit. Article 7 and a Clause 2 fine record are linked to this speeding violation. [Data: Entities (1292, 901, 1576); Relationships (5630, 3388)]

Failure to use headlights between 18:00 and 06:00, or in conditions that restrict visibility, is described as carrying a fine of 200,000 to 400,000 đồng. The records link Article 7 to both this violation and the corresponding fine range. [Data: Entities (2054, 2176); Relationships (5632, 5634, 6544)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Alcohol-related motorcycle violation carries a substantial stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described alcohol-related violation involves operating a motorcycle or similar vehicle above specified blood- or breath-alcohol concentration thresholds. Under Article 7, Clause 8, the stated fine is 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and the description says license points may also be deducted. The records do not specify the number of points for this violation. [Data: Entities (151, 3178); Relationships (490, 491)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle obstruction and other penalties are also represented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to give way to or obstruct a priority vehicle signaling while on duty is described as carrying a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. Article 7 is linked to this violation, and a separate record represents the same fine range. [Data: Entities (2070, 3064); Relationships (5633, 7055)]

The data also references fines of 18,000,000 to 20,000,000 đồng for certain violations, but does not identify the specific conduct associated with that range. It should therefore not be attributed to any particular violation on the basis of these records. [Data: Entities (3059); Relationships (8990)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules and sanctions, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied material identifies penalty provisions, violation categories, and selected fine amounts. It does not identify individual drivers, enforcement actions, adjudications, compliance rates, or resulting injuries or losses. Accordingly, it supports a description of the regulatory and penalty structure, but not a conclusion about actual compliance or the frequency and consequences of violations. [Data: Entities (4433, 1292, 1710)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168 Vehicle-Condition Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle-condition traffic violations under Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 13, with related entities covering unauthorized or altered vehicle documents, registration-number mismatches, sanctions, and penalty ranges. It also includes two cargo-loading violations under Article 21(1), which share a stated fine of 600,000–800,000 VND and driving-license point deductions. The records describe regulatory requirements and sanctions, but do not identify specific offenders or actual incidents. [Data: Entities (5510, 5340, 1284, 5481, 2924); Relationships (10629, 5612, 10677, 7085, 7086)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad relevance to traffic compliance and administrative penalties, while the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or actors.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 is the central regulatory link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 13, is directly connected to vehicle-condition violations and to both unauthorized or altered vehicle documents and vehicle registration mismatches. This makes the article the main regulatory anchor in the community. [Data: Entities (1284, 5510, 5340, 5481); Relationships (5612, 5610, 5611)]

The records characterize Article 13 as providing fines and driving-license point deductions for specified violations. They do not establish that any particular person or vehicle has committed one. [Data: Entities (1284, 2097); Relationships (5609)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized or altered vehicle documents are a defined violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe this violation as using, or placing a vehicle in traffic with, a registration certificate, technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate, or inspection sticker or label that was not issued by a competent authority, or was erased or altered. It is explicitly categorized as a vehicle-condition traffic violation. [Data: Entities (5340, 5510); Relationships (10629)]

Article 13 is linked to a fine of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND for the described document-related violation, and the records also associate it with fines and driver’s-license point deductions. [Data: Relationships (5610, 7328)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration-number mismatches form a separate compliance issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community distinguishes use of a registration certificate whose chassis or engine number does not match the vehicle from the broader category of vehicle-condition violations. The description also covers a towed trailer or semi-trailer. [Data: Entities (5481, 5482, 5510); Relationships (10677)]

The records link Article 13 to a fine of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND for the described mismatch and associate the related registration-number violation with fines and driver’s-license point deductions. [Data: Relationships (5611, 7329)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify multiple penalty bands
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions include a 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND fine for specified Article 13 violations and a 10,000,000–12,000,000 VND fine for certain vehicle-condition offenses. They also describe penalties of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND for individuals and 8,000,000–12,000,000 VND for organizations under a provision. The records do not fully specify how every listed range maps to each offense, so these amounts should not be treated as interchangeable. [Data: Entities (1284, 2237, 2260, 5510); Relationships (7297, 5610, 5611)]

The community also includes references to supplementary sanctions, remedial measures, and driver’s-license point deductions. The number of points deducted is not specified in the provided descriptions. [Data: Entities (2097, 2264, 3626); Relationships (7330, 9497, 5609)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-loading violations are connected but distinct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Loading goods on the cab roof and loading goods so as to unbalance a vehicle are listed as alternative violations under Article 21(1), involving cargo vehicles, tractors, or similar vehicles. The records associate each with a fine of 600,000–800,000 VND and a driving-license point deduction. [Data: Entities (2923, 2924, 2097); Relationships (7085, 7086, 8611)]

These cargo-loading violations sit alongside the Article 13 vehicle-condition material in the broader community, but the supplied descriptions identify Article 21(1), rather than Article 13, as their cited provision. [Data: Entities (2097, 2923, 2924); Relationships (7085, 7086)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is regulatory, not incident-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe violation categories, provisions, and sanctions. They do not name specific drivers, vehicle owners, organizations involved in an incident, or actual enforcement outcomes. Accordingly, the material supports assessing regulatory and compliance significance, but not attributing wrongdoing or measuring the prevalence of these violations. [Data: Entities (5510, 5340, 1284, 5481, 2923); Relationships (10629, 5612, 10677, 7085, 7086)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Article 13 Vehicle-Condition Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its rules for vehicle-condition violations in traffic. The article connects to a general violation category, covered vehicle operators, specified clauses, and Clause 4, which provides penalties for specified violations including non-compliant truck cargo-body dimensions and certain registration-document violations. The data also describes corrective measures to restore or replace equipment and identifies fine ranges for particular violations. [Data: Entities (259, 5581, 945, 1586, 4191); Relationships (874, 866, 869, 868, 9962, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s moderate-to-high importance as a regulatory framework addressing vehicle condition, road-safety requirements, penalties, and corrective measures, rather than evidence of any particular violation or compliance outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 is the community’s central regulatory reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the central entity, linking to the general category of vehicle-condition violations, Clause 4, a specific truck-dimension violation, covered four-wheeled motor-vehicle drivers, and the specified clauses cited in the text. This structure makes the article the organizing reference for the community’s penalties and scope. [Data: Entities (259); Relationships (874, 866, 869, 868, 873)]

The article description says it applies to drivers of cars and certain four-wheeled motor vehicles, sets out fines and driving-licence-point deductions for specified violations, and identifies specified violations and clauses subject to temporary seizure procedures. The data does not provide details about any actual enforcement action or seizure. [Data: Entities (259)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation category covers vehicle-condition requirements in traffic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general violation category concerns vehicles that fail to meet required condition standards while participating in traffic. Its stated scope includes drivers of cars and specified four-wheeled motor vehicles, as well as operators of specialized motorcycles, including those towing trailers. [Data: Entities (5581)]

The category is linked to two corrective measures: restoring equipment to its prescribed technical function, or installing missing equipment or replacing equipment so that it meets technical safety standards and regulations. These are described as measures associated with the violation category; the records do not specify an individual case or say that either measure has been imposed. [Data: Entities (4191, 2705); Relationships (9962, 8007)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 4 specifies penalties for listed vehicle-condition violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 4 is linked to Article 13 and is described as prescribing a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified vehicle-condition violations. The listed examples include driving without valid vehicle registration documentation and violating prescribed truck cargo-bed dimensions. [Data: Entities (945); Relationships (866)]

The records provide the rule and examples but do not establish whether a particular driver committed a violation, received a fine, or satisfied the relevant requirements. [Data: Entities (945, 259)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Truck cargo-body dimensions are a specifically identified violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies driving a truck—including one towing a trailer or semi-trailer—with cargo-body dimensions that do not match the technical specifications recorded in its technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate as a violation. Article 13, Clause 4 is linked to this violation. [Data: Entities (1586, 5161); Relationships (869, 3471)]

The stated fine for this violation is 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND. The record describes the applicable violation and penalty, not an actual truck, operator, or enforcement event. [Data: Entities (1586, 5161, 2581); Relationships (6322)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data distinguishes a broader fine range for certain violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general vehicle-condition category states that certain violations involving cars or specified four-wheeled motor vehicles carry fines of 3,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. This range is distinct from the 2,000,000-to-3,000,000-VND fine described for specified Clause 4 violations, including the truck cargo-body-dimension violation. [Data: Entities (5581, 945, 1586, 5161)]

The records do not enumerate every violation subject to the broader range, so the amount should not be treated as applying to all vehicle-condition violations. [Data: Entities (5581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified portions of Article 13 are separately identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies point a of Clause 4; points a and b of Clause 5; Clause 6; point b of Clause 7; point a of Clause 8; and Clause 9 as specified portions of Article 13. These portions are linked to the article as particular parts cited in the text. [Data: Entities (4721); Relationships (873)]

The data does not describe the substantive rules in each of those portions, so no additional penalties or requirements can be attributed to them from these records alone. [Data: Entities (4721)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Transport Violation and Six-Point Licence Deduction
v.tom_tat: This community describes a road-transport regulations violation committed by a transport-business driver directly operating a vehicle, with relationships linking the violation and driver to a six-point driving-licence deduction. Point c of Clause 8 of Article 26 is identified as the cited provision associated with that penalty. However, the driver entity’s description refers to a two-point deduction, conflicting with the six-point descriptions in the other records; the provided data does not resolve this discrepancy. [Data: Entities (4658, 5112, 4577, 3773); Relationships (10431, 10319, 9637, 10320)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the records describe a specific regulatory violation and licence penalty, but provide little information beyond this narrowly defined enforcement context.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The six-point deduction is the community’s central outcome
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The six-point driving-licence deduction is connected to the transport-business driver and to the specified road-transport violation. The relationship records describe it as the consequence when the violation is committed while directly driving for transport business. [Data: Entities (4658); Relationships (10431, 10319)]
