The records establish a stated penalty mechanism, but do not provide information about its administration, duration, appeal process, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver’s role is defined by direct vehicle operation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The transport-business driver is described as a person engaged in the transport business who directly operates the vehicle involved in a violation. A relationship likewise states that the driver directly commits the specified violation while operating the vehicle. [Data: Entities (5112, 4577); Relationships (10320)]

The records therefore make direct operation a key condition in the described circumstances. They do not identify a particular driver, business, vehicle, or incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation concerns road-transport rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is defined as a breach of regulations governing road traffic order and safety in road transport or road-transport support services. It is linked both to the driver who commits it and to the six-point deduction. [Data: Entities (4577); Relationships (10319, 10320)]

No specific act, date, location, or evidence of an actual violation is provided, so the records support only this general description.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point c of Clause 8 of Article 26 is cited as the relevant provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity for point c of Clause 8 of Article 26 is described as identifying the violation that triggers a driving-licence penalty when committed by a person directly driving a vehicle for transport business. Its relationship to the deduction says that a violation under this point triggers the six-point penalty in the circumstances stated in Clause 14. [Data: Entities (3773); Relationships (9637)]

The provided records do not reproduce the legal text of either clause or provide further jurisdictional context.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records contain an unresolved point-deduction inconsistency
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The transport-business driver entity description says that, under the specified circumstances, the driver is subject to a two-point deduction. In contrast, the six-point deduction entity and its relationships describe a six-point penalty for the specified violation. [Data: Entities (5112, 4658); Relationships (10431, 10319, 9637)]

The supplied information does not explain whether these descriptions concern different circumstances or whether one is inaccurate. The discrepancy should be checked against the applicable source before relying on the penalty amount.

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Article 26 and Road-Transport Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which sets penalties for specified road-transport and transport-support service violations. It is linked to Chapter II, a route-information display violation, failure to number passenger seats or berths, transport-business individuals who directly drive, a driving-licence point deduction under Clause 14, and organizations facing higher fines for repeat specified violations. The records describe regulatory provisions and penalties, not particular incidents or enforcement actions. [Data: Entities (333, 804, 4591, 1366, 1994, +more); Relationships (1365, 1376, 1369, 1370, 1367, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate-to-high because the provisions establish financial and licence-point consequences for road-transport violations, including substantial fines for repeat violations by relevant organizations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the main hub in the supplied records. It is identified as part of Chapter II and is connected to several specific violations, penalties, and affected parties. [Data: Entities (333, 804); Relationships (1365, 1376, 1369, 1370, 1367)]

The article covers road-traffic order and safety rules in road transport and related transport-support services. The available information establishes the scope of the provision, but does not indicate that any person or organization has committed a violation. [Data: Entities (333)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Route-information display violations are addressed in both Articles 20 and 26
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The route-information display violation is described as a failure to display information about a vehicle’s route and is associated with both Article 20 and Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 26’s corresponding provision is identified as point g, clause 4. [Data: Entities (4591, 333); Relationships (1376)]

The records also connect this violation to the circumstance in which a transport-business individual personally drives the vehicle involved. They state that the applicable penalty is under point g, clause 4 of Article 26, but do not give a specific fine amount for this particular circumstance. [Data: Entities (1366, 4591); Relationships (1369, 5837)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Direct-driving transport-business individuals may face a licence-point deduction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 14 of Article 26 provides for a deduction of six points from a driving licence when a person directly drives a vehicle while conducting transport business and commits the specified violation. [Data: Entities (889, 1366); Relationships (1367, 1369, 5837)]

This is a separate stated consequence from a monetary fine. The supplied records do not specify any further licensing outcome or establish that a deduction has been applied in a real case. [Data: Entities (889)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26 covers several distinct operational requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
In addition to route-information display, Article 26 addresses failure to number passenger seats or berths on passenger-carrying motor vehicles. The article specifies fines for this violation, with different fine ranges for individuals and transport-service organizations. [Data: Entities (333, 1994); Relationships (1370)]

The article description also mentions other breaches, including failures to display required route information and use of untrained personnel to transport dangerous goods. These examples indicate that the provision spans multiple operational and safety requirements; the supplied records do not provide details about actual compliance by operators. [Data: Entities (333)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Financial penalties vary by party and may increase for repeat violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain violations, Article 26 prescribes fines of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for individuals and 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 đồng for business organizations. The records do not establish that these ranges apply to every violation covered by the article. [Data: Entities (333); Relationships (1370)]

Organizations conducting road-transport businesses or providing transport-support services may face fines of 80 million to 100 million Vietnamese đồng for repeat violations of specified regulations. Article 26 is explicitly linked to repeat violations by organizations in these sectors, but the data does not identify any particular repeat offender. [Data: Entities (4476); Relationships (1374)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a regulatory framework, not a specific enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe legal provisions, violation categories, and potential penalties. They do not identify a particular vehicle, driver, transport business, enforcement proceeding, or instance of non-compliance. [Data: Entities (333, 4591, 1366, 1994, 4476); Relationships (1369, 1370, 1374, 5837)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance lies in the potential compliance and operational consequences of the rules described, rather than evidence of an active incident or demonstrated misconduct. The supplied material does not provide information on enforcement frequency, technical capabilities, or reputational effects. [Data: Entities (333, 804)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168 Article 13 Vehicle-Compliance Framework
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its rules for vehicle-condition violations, required documentation, fines, and supplementary sanctions. Credit institutions and foreign bank branches are connected to the documentation rules because they may retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate; the article describes acceptable substitute documents in that circumstance. The material also covers violations such as operating without required registration documentation or a license plate, and consequences including document revocation and plate confiscation. The source description notes that a separate Article 13 in Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerns lane-use rules, so the article number alone does not identify a single legal provision. [Data: Entities (256, 1135, 2302, 5509, 3361, +more); Relationships (826, 832, 844, 91, 842, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial practical importance because it links road-traffic compliance rules, financial penalties, and vehicle-document procedures, while the supplied information describes regulations rather than evidence of actual violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 is the regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the central entity in the network, connecting vehicle-condition violations with fines, driving-licence point deductions, and supplementary or remedial measures. Its stated scope primarily concerns cars and certain four-wheeled motor vehicles that fail applicable requirements for participating in traffic. [Data: Entities (256); Relationships (844, 840, 91)]

The source also notes a distinct Article 13 in Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerning lane-use rules when vehicles pass others on roads with multiple same-direction lanes. This creates a potential reference ambiguity: the provision should be identified by its legal instrument as well as its article number. [Data: Entities (256)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition violations include documentation and equipment issues
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community defines a vehicle-condition traffic violation as operating a motor vehicle in traffic without meeting applicable condition requirements. Examples include an incorrect chassis or engine number and a registration certificate not issued by a competent authority; the wider Article 13 description also identifies improperly issued or mismatched registration and inspection documents, certain vehicle modifications, and technical defects. [Data: Entities (5509, 256); Relationships (844)]

One specifically identified offense is operating a car or similar vehicle, including certain towing combinations or four-wheeled transport vehicles, without required registration documentation. The specified fine for that offense is 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (3361)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Credit institutions and foreign bank branches have a defined documentation role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Credit institutions and foreign bank branches may hold a vehicle’s original registration certificate, including where the vehicle is mortgaged or held as collateral. Article 13’s described procedures allow or require the operator, in the relevant circumstances, to carry a certified copy of the registration certificate together with the institution’s or branch’s original or valid receipt; collateral may also require a relevant confirmation document. [Data: Entities (1135, 2302); Relationships (826, 832, 4003)]

This is a documentation exception connected to possession of the original certificate, not evidence that either type of institution has committed a violation. The network also links both institution types to provisions concerning operating without registration documentation, certificate revocation, and temporary document retention. [Data: Relationships (4005, 4012, 4007, 7378, 7384, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalties vary by offense and responsible party
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed administrative fines span multiple ranges and depend on the violation and who is responsible. The supplied material includes 3,000,000–4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for covered vehicle-condition violations, 10,000,000–15,000,000 đồng for specified violations by testing and certification establishments, and different amounts for individual versus organizational vehicle owners under Article 32, Clause 7. Other listed violations carry lower individual and organizational fine ranges. [Data: Entities (41); Relationships (91, 835)]

The description also identifies a 1,000,000–2,000,000 đồng fine for driving with a steering system that fails technical-safety standards, and a 10,000,000–12,000,000 đồng fine for driving a car, trailer, or semi-trailer without a required license plate. These examples show that the penalties are offense-specific rather than a single standard amount. [Data: Entities (256, 1593); Relationships (829)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Supplementary measures can affect vehicle documents and plates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Beyond fines, the framework includes consequences such as driving-licence point deductions, temporary retention of documents, revocation of vehicle registration or inspection documents under specified conditions, and confiscation of a vehicle’s license plate for a particular violation. [Data: Entities (256, 4877, 5474, 5420, 4239); Relationships (842, 838, 840, +more)]

The supplied relationships specify that plate confiscation is tied to the violation identified at point a of clause 8, while revocation of a registration certificate is linked to a specified vehicle-condition violation. The information does not establish how frequently these measures are applied. [Data: Entities (3752, 5420, 5474); Relationships (9635, 10651, 10675)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules have broad compliance significance, but no actual cases are documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community connects statutory requirements to drivers, vehicle owners, financial institutions holding registration documents, and testing or certification establishments subject to specified penalties. This breadth makes the framework relevant to routine vehicle operation, documentation handling, and enforcement. [Data: Entities (256, 1135, 2302, 41); Relationships (826, 832, 91, 840)]

The records describe legal provisions and potential penalties; they do not identify particular offenders, enforcement actions, or evidence of non-compliance by the named categories of entities. Accordingly, the material supports an assessment of regulatory importance, not a finding of actual misconduct. [Data: Entities (256, 41, 1135, 2302)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Traffic and Driver-Training Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and connects vehicle-condition, equipment, and registration requirements with specified traffic fines. A shared fine range of 2,000,000–3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng applies to several distinct violations, while the records also describe separate rules for driver-training facilities and practical instructors, and a 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng penalty for specified conduct under Article 14, Clause 3. The information describes legal requirements and violation categories; it does not establish that any particular person or organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (265, 2158, 1497, 1719); Relationships (918, 7163, 6145, 6577)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it covers multiple road-safety and driver-training compliance areas, although the records describe rules rather than verified violations by specific parties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 14 is the central regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 14 addresses vehicle-condition and equipment requirements for operators of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles in traffic, and is linked to registration-document, horn, and equipment violations. The entity description also identifies licence-plate violations and a 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng fine for specified conduct under Clause 3. [Data: Entities (265); Relationships (911, 917, 918, 920)]

The linked 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng penalties concern specified violations, including registration-document and horn-related conduct; they should not be conflated with the separate Clause 3 range described for Article 14. [Data: Entities (2158, 265); Relationships (7162, 7163, 918)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration-document violations share a stated fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish driving without the required valid vehicle registration documentation from using documentation that has expired or ceased to be valid. Both are linked to Article 14, Clause 2, and each is stated to carry a fine of 2,000,000–3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1696, 5357, 2158); Relationships (912, 6510, 918, 7163)]

A separate entity describes expired or ineffective registration documentation under Article 13, Clause 4, including documentation for a trailer or semi-trailer, with the same stated fine range. [Data: Entities (5362, 2158); Relationships (7164)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng range covers several distinct violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine-range entity groups multiple categories whose applicable penalty depends on the specific provision. The described examples include vehicle-registration violations, use of a non-compliant horn, certain driving-instructor violations, and failure to ensure safety when a car breaks down at a road–rail crossing. [Data: Entities (2158, 1696, 5306, 1719, 1970)]

Relationships also connect this range to a specialized-motorcycle driver’s traffic-rule violation. The range is therefore a common penalty amount across different conduct, not evidence that the violations are identical or that they occurred in any particular case. [Data: Relationships (7160, 6577, 6924, 7162)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-training facilities and instructors have separate compliance duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver-training facility may violate training regulations if it lacks enough practical driving instructors for its planned use of training vehicles; the facility description states that specified violations may draw a fine of 20,000,000–30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1497, 3836); Relationships (6145)]

Separately, a practical driving instructor violates the stated permit requirement by failing to carry a permit for a driving-practice vehicle or carrying an expired permit. The described penalty for that violation is 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (1719, 3836, 2158); Relationships (6577, 6578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Level-crossing breakdowns are treated as a specific safety circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe a violation where a driver fails to take required safety measures when a car breaks down at a road–rail level crossing. The stated fine is 2,000,000–3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and the breakdown is identified as the circumstance in which the safety-related violation arises. [Data: Entities (1970, 694, 2158); Relationships (6924, 2953)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The dataset spans additional equipment and road-rule examples
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Use of a horn that does not meet technical standards for the relevant vehicle type is identified as a traffic violation and linked to Article 14 and the 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng range. [Data: Entities (5306, 2158, 265); Relationships (917, 7162)]

Other entries describe vehicle-condition violations, driving with non-compliant equipment, a specialized-motorcycle driver’s road-rule violation, and illegal parking on a sidewalk. The sidewalk-parking entry gives a distinct fine of 600,000–800,000 đồng and is linked as an example associated with the specialized-motorcycle violation entry. [Data: Entities (5584, 1592, 4431, 2523); Relationships (911, 920, 7782)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a penalty framework, not actual compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe provisions, violation types, and stated penalties. They do not identify a particular driver, facility, enforcement action, or confirmed instance of non-compliance; conclusions about actual violations or the compliance record of specific parties are therefore unsupported by this material. [Data: Entities (265, 1497, 1696, 1719, 1970); Relationships (918, 6145, 6510, 6577, 6924)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Service-Life Violation and Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP
v.tom_tat: This community describes a vehicle service-life violation and its regulatory treatment. Article 13(5)(c) of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is cited as defining the violation, while Article 26(7)(i) is identified as the penalty provision when a transport-business individual directly drives the vehicle. The records establish this legal relationship but do not provide a penalty amount or details of a specific enforcement case.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate-low because the community maps a specific administrative violation and conditional penalty rule, but the supplied records describe no particular case, penalty amount, or broader operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The vehicle service-life violation is the community’s central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a violation of rules governing a vehicle’s permitted service life. The record describes it as referenced in Article 13, point c, clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (5493)]

The relationships connect this violation to both the cited provision and the circumstances under which a separate penalty rule applies, making it the hub of the regulatory mapping. [Data: Relationships (877, 9513, 5833)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13(5)(c) is cited as defining the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 13(5)(c) of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as a provision defining violations of rules on permitted vehicle service life. The relationship record explicitly connects that provision to the violation. [Data: Entities (262); Relationships (877)]

The supplied information identifies the provision but does not reproduce its full text or provide additional interpretation of its requirements. [Data: Entities (262, 5493); Relationships (877)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Direct driving by a transport-business individual is the stated condition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a circumstance in which an individual engaged in transport business directly operates the vehicle involved in the violation. They link that circumstance to the vehicle service-life violation and to the penalty category under Article 26(7)(i). [Data: Entities (1364); Relationships (5833, 5832)]

The records do not identify a specific driver, vehicle, or incident; the condition is presented as a general rule in the regulatory mapping. [Data: Entities (1364, 5493); Relationships (5833, 5832)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26(7)(i) is identified as the applicable penalty rule in the stated circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalty entity is described as the administrative penalty under Article 26, clause 7, point i, applicable when a transport-business individual directly drives the vehicle. The relationship records connect that penalty to both the direct-driving condition and the service-life violation. [Data: Entities (3657); Relationships (9513, 5832)]

Article 26(7)(i) is also identified as the provision specifying this penalty. No penalty amount or further sanction details are included in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (335, 3657); Relationships (1381)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information is a narrow regulatory mapping, not a case record
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships focus on one type of vehicle-related violation, the cited provisions, and a conditional penalty rule. They do not describe an enforcement action or establish that a particular person or organization has committed the violation. [Data: Entities (5493, 3657, 335, 1364, 262); Relationships (9513, 5833, 877, 5832, 1381)]

Accordingly, the community supports identifying the cited legal structure, but not conclusions about actual compliance, the outcome of a case, or the scale of any real-world impact. [Data: Entities (5493, 3657); Relationships (9513, 5833)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Transport-Violation Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its penalties for specified passenger-vehicle conduct, including excess passengers, passenger mistreatment, and attempts to evade inspection. It links several categories of violations to a fine of 3,000,000–5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, while excess-passenger records also describe a per-passenger administrative fine. A separate branch concerns Article 37, Clause 3 and operating without a valid transport permit, which is associated with the same fine range. The records describe legal provisions and violation categories, not specific incidents or identified operators. [Data: Entities (301, 2180, 735, 3358, 419, +more); Relationships (1122, 1112, 98, 7187, 1776, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s significance as a connected set of transport-safety rules and substantial administrative penalties, while the records establish no specific incident, offender, or operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the main hub, connecting the fine range to several passenger-vehicle violation categories. Its described scope includes route-information requirements, cargo limits, passenger capacity, and conduct addressed in Clause 6. [Data: Entities (301, 2180); Relationships (1122, 1112, 1126, 1128, 1130)]

The records describe rules and potential penalties; they do not establish that a particular driver or company committed any violation. [Data: Entities (301); Relationships (1112, 1130)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified Article 20 violations carry a 3–5 million đồng fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 6 of Article 20 is linked to a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified conduct. The connected categories include threatening or insulting passengers, competing for or soliciting passengers, and acts intended to evade detection of overloading or excess passengers. [Data: Entities (301, 2180, 1068, 4945, 3447); Relationships (1122, 1130, 1117, 1126, +more)]

The data also identifies putting passengers off to evade inspection as a penalized act under Clause 6. This describes a prohibited evasion method, not evidence that it occurred in a particular case. [Data: Entities (4009); Relationships (1128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess-passenger penalties are described under more than one provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records associate carrying more passengers than permitted with Article 20, while also describing an administrative fine of 400,000–600,000 Vietnamese đồng per excess passenger, capped at 75,000,000 đồng. The Article 20 relationship notes a stated exception, so the source data does not support treating these amounts as one universal penalty. [Data: Entities (735, 43, 301); Relationships (1112, 98, 99)]

The description of the excess-passenger entity also cites Article 28 and Article 32 as setting other fines or owner penalties. These references indicate that the applicable amount depends on the provision and circumstances; the supplied records do not resolve every boundary between those rules. [Data: Entities (735)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other passenger-vehicle goods and animal categories are linked to the fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich: The fine entity is connected to transporting animals, foul-smelling goods, and other goods that may affect passengers’ health in a passenger vehicle. These are listed violation categories associated with the 3,000,000–5,000,000 đồng fine; the data does not report an actual transport event. [Data: Entities (2180, 5125, 5136, 5141); Relationships (1122, 7188, 7189, 7190)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 37, Clause 3 addresses transport-permit violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate provision, Article 37, Clause 3, is described as applying to drivers of road motor vehicles with foreign registration plates. It identifies operating without a required inter-transport or international road transport permit, or with an expired permit, as a violation. [Data: Entities (419, 3358); Relationships (1776)]

The same 3,000,000–5,000,000 đồng fine entity is linked to operating without a valid transport permit. This connects the permit issue to the wider penalty-focused community, but does not make it an Article 20 violation. [Data: Entities (2180, 3358); Relationships (7187, 1776)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support regulatory significance, not evidence of enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is useful for understanding several transport-safety and compliance topics: passenger capacity, passenger treatment, cargo carried in passenger vehicles, inspection evasion, and permit validity. Its central relationships connect provisions, penalty amounts, and defined violation categories. [Data: Entities (301, 2180, 735, 3358, 419); Relationships (1122, 1112, 1126, 7187, 1776)]

No supplied record identifies a particular violator, enforcement action, resulting harm, or compliance history. Accordingly, the community’s impact rating reflects the breadth and stated seriousness of the regulatory framework rather than a claim of observed misconduct. [Data: Entities (301, 2180, 735, 3358); Relationships (1122, 1112, 7187)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Article 34, Article 47, and Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which addresses specified vehicle, load, dimension, and passenger-limit violations and prescribes penalties and driving-licence point deductions. Article 47 connects to Article 34 by including its violations in rules for handling overlapping provisions. The related records describe the covered vehicle operations and penalties, as well as technical-equipment detection when authorities cannot stop a vehicle immediately. The information concerns legal requirements and enforcement procedures; it does not identify particular drivers, operators, or enforcement cases.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the provisions concern road-safety compliance and enforcement, while the records provide no specific incident or identified actor indicating a higher immediate impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 34 defines the core set of covered traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 34 addresses operating oversized or overweight vehicles, including crawler-tracked vehicles, and violations of vehicle or road weight and dimension limits. It also covers oversized or overweight cargo and carrying more passengers than permitted. [Data: Entities (403)]

The associated violation category summarizes these as specified vehicle-operation violations on public roads, including passenger vehicles. [Data: Entities (3410); Relationships (1708)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalties include driving-licence point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that Article 34 prescribes penalties and driving-licence point deductions for the violations it covers. This makes licence-point consequences part of the described regulatory response, alongside other penalties. [Data: Entities (403, 5019); Relationships (1709)]

The penalty record links those consequences to drivers who commit the specified vehicle-operation violations; it does not provide particular penalty amounts or identify any affected driver. [Data: Entities (5019); Relationships (9304)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 47 provides a cross-reference for overlapping provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47 sets procedures and principles for penalizing vehicle owners and drivers when conduct falls under multiple provisions, including overlapping violations. Its clause 3 specifically identifies Article 34 violations among those covered by its penalty rule. [Data: Entities (465); Relationships (1705)]

This relationship indicates that Article 34's violations are addressed within a broader rule for resolving overlapping provisions; the records do not describe the outcome of any particular case. [Data: Entities (403, 465); Relationships (1705)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes technical-equipment detection procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 47 also covers violations detected using professional technical equipment when authorities cannot stop the vehicle immediately. This is a stated enforcement procedure in the article's description, rather than evidence that a particular device was used in a specific incident. [Data: Entities (465)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is regulatory rather than case- or actor-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect a legal provision, a second provision addressing overlapping rules, a category of vehicle-operation violations, and the associated penalties and licence-point deductions. [Data: Entities (403, 465, 3410, 5019); Relationships (1705, 1708, 1709, 9304)]

The provided information describes the scope and enforcement consequences of the rules but names no individual driver, vehicle operator, organization, or actual enforcement case. Accordingly, it supports assessing the regulatory community's road-safety relevance, but not the compliance or conduct of a specific actor. [Data: Entities (403, 465, 3410, 5019)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Vehicle-Owner Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community is a regulatory-reference network centered on Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which sets penalties for specified vehicle-owner violations and connects to related provisions in Articles 21, 22, and 34. Its records describe monetary fines, possible driving-licence point deductions, and remedial requirements, including for permit-related goods transport and vehicle registration issues. The information indicates substantial relevance to road-traffic compliance, but does not establish that any particular person or organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (372, 322, 47, 1702, 4192); Relationships (1265, 1604, 1611)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad relevance to vehicle-owner compliance and significant stated penalties, while the records provide no evidence of actual violations or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (372, 47, 322); Relationships (104, 1265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is the network’s central penalty provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is the main hub in the supplied relationships, linking to multiple covered violations, penalties, and consequences. Its description says it addresses vehicle owners who violate traffic rules or allow or direct others to do so, with fines and, where applicable, driving-licence point deductions. [Data: Entities (372, 1702); Relationships (1599, 1604, 1610, 1601, 1611)]

The network also links Article 32 to provisions in Articles 21 and 34, as well as to registration-related conduct and operating beyond temporary or restricted permissions. The records do not describe every underlying violation in detail, so the scope of those cited provisions should not be inferred beyond the supplied descriptions. [Data: Relationships (1237, 1593, 1594, 1609, 1610)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22 violations can trigger owner penalties under Article 32
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22 addresses specified oversized or overweight goods transport and carrying more passengers than permitted. The relationship data states that Article 47, clause 3 links specified Article 22 violations to Article 32 penalties when the vehicle owner is also the driver, including the conduct in point b, paragraph 3, of Article 22. [Data: Entities (322); Relationships (1265)]

The graph separately connects Article 22’s point-b violation to conduct by an owner who assigns or permits an employee or representative to commit it. This shows a regulatory link between the underlying transport violation and owner responsibility, rather than evidence that such conduct occurred in a particular case. [Data: Entities (596); Relationships (1267, 105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified owner conduct carries substantial stated fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied record states that the fine under paragraph 14 of Article 32 is VND 28,000,000–30,000,000 for an individual vehicle owner and VND 56,000,000–60,000,000 for an organizational owner. The graph links that fine to Article 32 and to assigning or allowing an employee or representative to commit the specified Article 22 violation. [Data: Entities (47, 596); Relationships (104, 105, 1265)]

These amounts are stated for the specified conduct and should not be generalized to every violation covered by Article 32. The text also links paragraph 14 to Article 34, clause 4(c), but the supplied description does not identify the nature of that underlying violation. [Data: Entities (408); Relationships (1593)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22 specifies a separate fine for permit-inconsistent goods
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22 is linked to a violation involving oversized or overweight goods carried under a valid circulation permit when the goods do not match the type specified in that permit. The stated fine for this conduct is VND 13,000,000 to VND 15,000,000. [Data: Entities (322, 5145, 2238); Relationships (1271, 1270, 7298)]

This is a distinct stated penalty from the paragraph 14 vehicle-owner fine. The records establish the violation description and amount, but do not provide case-level information about enforcement or any individual or organization subject to the fine. [Data: Entities (47, 5145, 2238); Relationships (1265, 1270)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records cover registration and vehicle-use compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is linked to operating a vehicle without valid registration, including use of a vehicle without a registration certificate or with an expired or otherwise invalid document. The description includes an exception where the original certificate is held by a credit institution or foreign bank branch and required supporting documents are carried. [Data: Entities (3365); Relationships (1610)]

Other linked records identify failure to complete registration-certificate and license-plate revocation procedures, and use of vehicles with temporary or restricted permissions beyond the allowed period, route, or area. A clause 8 penalty record states fines of VND 4,000,000–6,000,000 for an individual owner and VND 8,000,000–12,000,000 for an organizational owner for its specified violation. [Data: Entities (1955, 3343, 991); Relationships (3553, 1609, 1601)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional rules address equipment and vehicle restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 32 sets fines for individual and organizational owners of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles who install or use sound or lighting equipment in a way that disrupts road-traffic order and safety. The records identify this conduct as a sanctionable violation but do not state the fine amount in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (929, 1409); Relationships (1599, 3440)]

Article 32, clause 19, is also linked to a remedial requirement to restore a vehicle’s registered brand and paint colour to match its registration certificate in specified cases. The data does not specify which cases beyond identifying this as a requirement under clause 19. [Data: Entities (4192); Relationships (1611)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Transport Violations and Article 26 Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community concerns road-transport regulatory violations and the consequences described for specified violations. It links an administrative fine of 20–40 million Vietnamese dong to journey-monitoring and driver-image-recording service providers and to producers, assemblers, and importers of journey-monitoring equipment. A separate relationship identifies bringing vehicle paint color and identifying signs or markings into compliance as a corrective measure. The records describe regulatory provisions, not evidence that any particular organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (4578, 57, 2793, 4509, 5518); Relationships (126, 10321, 124, 125)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it describes monetary penalties and a corrective compliance measure across several road-transport-related organization types, but does not document actual violations or their effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is centered on road-transport regulatory violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central topic is conduct that breaches regulations governing traffic order and safety in road transport and road-transport support services. The available description says Article 26 provides penalties for specified violations, but does not enumerate the acts covered. This limits conclusions about the precise conduct at issue. [Data: Entities (4578)]

The fine and vehicle-marking corrective action are connected to this violation category in the records, establishing the community’s main regulatory focus. [Data: Relationships (126, 10321)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated administrative fine is 20–40 million Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify an administrative fine ranging from 20 million to 40 million Vietnamese dong for specified violations. The fine is linked to the broader road-transport regulatory-violation category. [Data: Entities (57, 4578); Relationships (126)]

This is a stated penalty range; the data do not establish that the fine was assessed against any specific entity or that a violation occurred.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two categories of organizations are expressly covered by the fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One covered category consists of organizations providing vehicle journey-monitoring or driver-image-recording services. The record states these organizations face the specified fine if they commit one of the covered violations. [Data: Entities (2793, 57); Relationships (124)]

The other category consists of organizations producing, assembling, or importing journey-monitoring equipment for motor vehicles; the same stated fine applies if one of the specified violations is committed. The records identify categories, not individual businesses. [Data: Entities (4509, 57); Relationships (125)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-marking compliance is identified as a corrective measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For specified violations, the stated corrective measure is to bring a vehicle’s paint color and identifying signs or markings into compliance with regulations. This is linked to the road-transport regulatory-violation category. [Data: Entities (5518, 4578); Relationships (10321)]

The provided information does not specify which particular violations trigger this measure or describe any completed corrective action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory exposure, not documented enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions and relationships outline the violation category, a fine range, the types of organizations to which the fine may apply, and a vehicle-marking corrective measure. They do not identify an accused or sanctioned organization, a specific incident, or an enforcement decision. [Data: Entities (4578, 57, 2793, 4509, 5518); Relationships (126, 10321, 124, 125)]

Accordingly, the community supports assessing the scope of the described compliance framework, but not attributing noncompliance or reputational harm to any named organization.

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Vehicle-Owner Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 32 penalty provisions in Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and the fines applied to specified vehicle-owner traffic violations. The linked violations include unauthorized changes to a vehicle’s use, components or structure, and unauthorized installation of lifting equipment. The supplied records describe fines by clause and owner type, but do not identify actual violators, enforcement events, or organizations. [Data: Entities (373, 2272, 5525, 5198, 5218); Relationships (7341, 7338, 7340, 7339, 1615, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the significance of a defined penalty framework with potentially substantial fines, while the supplied records provide no evidence of actual violations or enforcement activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is the regulatory anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as addressing penalties for vehicle owners who violate road-traffic rules. Its links to three specified offenses identify paragraph 16 as covering unauthorized change of vehicle use, unauthorized vehicle component or structural alteration, and unauthorized installation of lifting equipment. [Data: Entities (373); Relationships (1615, 1616, 1617)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fines vary by clause and owner type
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated schedule distinguishes individual vehicle owners from organizational owners and gives different ranges for clauses 11, 14, and 16. For clause 11, the ranges are VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for individuals and VND 20,000,000–24,000,000 for organizations; for clause 14, they are VND 28,000,000–30,000,000 and VND 56,000,000–60,000,000, respectively. [Data: Entities (2272)]

For clause 16, the stated ranges are VND 65,000,000–75,000,000 for individuals and VND 130,000,000–150,000,000 for organizations. The records link the fine schedule to the specified vehicle-owner violations. [Data: Entities (2272); Relationships (7341, 7338, 7340, 7339)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions cover vehicle owners and certain conduct through representatives
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle-owner violations entity covers owners of cars, motorized four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and similar vehicles. It describes liability in relation to owners directly committing specified violations or allowing an employee or representative to commit conduct specified under Article 20, Clause 7 or Article 21, Clause 6(c). [Data: Entities (5525)]

The fines entity is expressly linked to the vehicle-owner traffic violations, connecting the described owner scope to the penalty schedule. [Data: Relationships (7341)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized vehicle modifications are a central violation category
phat_hien.giai_thich: One linked offense concerns unauthorized changes to a vehicle’s frame, engine, brakes, drivetrain, running system, structure, shape, or dimensions, contrary to the manufacturer’s design or an approved design. Article 32, paragraph 16, identifies this type of alteration as punishable, and the fine schedule is linked to it. [Data: Entities (5218, 2272); Relationships (1617, 7340)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Change of use and lifting equipment are also explicitly covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify changing a vehicle’s intended use without authorization as a violation. They also identify unauthorized installation of equipment to raise or lower a vehicle body or container—including on trailers and semi-trailers—as a separate violation. [Data: Entities (5198, 5202)]

Article 32, paragraph 16, identifies both offenses as punishable, and the stated owner-fine schedule is linked to each. The supplied information establishes the regulatory scope and penalties, but does not document particular cases, enforcement outcomes, compliance rates, or the reputation or technical capabilities of any specific owner. [Data: Relationships (1615, 1616, 7338, 7339); Entities (2272)]

v.tieu_de: Article 47 Road-Traffic Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 47, which the provided data says refers to provisions in two Vietnamese legal instruments: Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Its connected entities cover penalty procedures for traffic violations, drivers, passenger and goods transport—particularly by motorcycles, mopeds, and rudimentary vehicles—and safety requirements such as pre-trip checks and secure cargo. The material describes a regulatory framework and relevant violation categories, but does not establish that any specific person or operator has violated the rules or whether compliance has been achieved.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects traffic enforcement with transport safety requirements, although the data provides no evidence of a specific incident or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 47 refers to provisions in two separate legal instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is potentially ambiguous: the data identifies Article 47 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP as addressing sanctioning procedures and specified road-traffic violations, while Article 47 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerns order and safety when certain vehicles transport passengers or goods. The applicable meaning therefore depends on which instrument is being referenced. [Data: Entities (462)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the connected topics: the relationships link Article 47 to both penalty procedures and transport requirements, but do not independently identify which instrument applies in each relationship. [Data: Relationships (2141, 2149, 2159)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework connects drivers to traffic-sanction procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle drivers are directly linked to Article 47 through procedures and principles for sanctioning drivers who violate road-traffic regulations. The entity description also states that drivers are subject to applicable road-traffic rules and enforcement procedures. [Data: Entities (5394); Relationships (2159)]

The data describes potential sanctions and enforcement, not an actual case involving a particular driver. It also mentions that specified violations may lead to vehicle confiscation under Article 35 and that driver images may be recorded by services related to vehicle journey monitoring. [Data: Entities (5394)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overlapping violations have a stated penalty-application process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47(3) is connected to Chapter II of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP and addresses how penalties are applied when the same person's conduct violates multiple provisions of that chapter. The entity description further notes circumstances involving the same person committing overlapping violations or a vehicle owner also being the direct operator. [Data: Entities (462, 803); Relationships (2141)]

This makes the provision relevant to interpreting cases involving multiple applicable rules, but the supplied information does not specify a particular case outcome or penalty amount. [Data: Entities (462)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger and goods transport is a major regulatory focus
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Several entities and relationships connect Article 47 to passenger and goods transport, especially transport using motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and rudimentary vehicles. The described requirements cover the activity and related passenger-capacity, load, and dimensional limits. [Data: Entities (3554, 3556, 4488); Relationships (2149, 2150, 2156)]

The data also identifies carrying more passengers than permitted as a violation addressed by Article 47. These connections indicate a broad safety and compliance focus, but do not show that any transport operator exceeded a limit. [Data: Entities (1872, 3579); Relationships (2147, 2151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pre-trip checks and secure cargo are explicit safety controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The covered passenger and goods transport activity is linked to checking a vehicle's safety condition before it enters road traffic. This is presented as a required check, not as evidence that a particular vehicle passed or failed an inspection. [Data: Entities (3840); Relationships (2154, 9431)]

Cargo must be arranged and secured so it does not endanger road users, obstruct the driver's view, or cover vehicle lights or license plates. The transport description additionally states that loose goods, construction materials, and waste must not spill onto roads or cause noise or dust; for cargo extending beyond a vehicle, the Article 47 description specifies red marking in daylight and lights or other signals in darkness. [Data: Entities (4593, 4488, 462); Relationships (9432)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed violation categories extend beyond passenger capacity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 47 is linked to violations involving road or sidewalk use, vehicle or road load limits, and vehicle or road dimensional limits, in addition to passenger-capacity violations. This breadth connects the provision to both how roads are used and how vehicles or their loads are configured. [Data: Relationships (2157, 2161, 2162, 2147)]

The entity descriptions characterize these as regulatory violation categories; the data does not report actual violations, enforcement activity, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (4582, 5436, 5434, 1872)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Road-Traffic Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Article 32, which the available information associates with several legal instruments and road-traffic topics. Its most prominent cluster concerns Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: owner penalties, driving-licence point deductions, unauthorized vehicle alterations, transport-related violations, and remedial restoration followed by re-inspection. The data also describes Article 32 provisions concerning foreign vehicles and drivers under Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and animal-drawn traffic under Law 36/2024/QH15. The material establishes regulatory scope and specified sanctions, but does not provide evidence about compliance rates, enforcement outcomes, or the technical capabilities of affected parties.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad road-safety and vehicle-compliance significance, including monetary penalties and requirements that can restrict a vehicle’s return to traffic, without evidence here of actual violations or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is the community’s central regulatory node
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is connected to a range of subjects, including traffic violations, vehicle-owner penalties, alteration of vehicles, transport conduct, animal-drawn road use, and restoration and re-inspection. This makes it the organizing legal reference for the community rather than a single entity or incident [Data: Entities (367); Relationships (1555, 1563, 1562, 1543, 1566)].

The entity description cautions that “Article 32” refers to provisions in several instruments, so its meaning depends on the instrument cited. Accordingly, the references should not be treated as one uniform provision without checking the specific legal instrument [Data: Entities (367)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Decree 168 cluster combines penalties with remedial measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied description identifies most references as Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and states that it sets administrative penalties and driving-licence point deductions for vehicle-owner violations. It also describes supplementary sanctions and remedial measures [Data: Entities (367), (3069); Relationships (1546)].

For specified conduct, Clause 19 requires a vehicle to be restored to its original shape and dimensions, returned to a technically safe condition, and re-inspected before it can be used in traffic again. The data links this measure to points in Clauses 11, 14, and 16 [Data: Entities (5490), (3787), (3776), (3782); Relationships (1566, 1552, 1551, 1553, 9640)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized vehicle alterations carry stated financial penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Unauthorized changes to a vehicle’s frame, engine, shape, dimensions, or characteristics are identified as violations covered by Article 32, Clause 8. The data specifically gives fines of 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizational owners for the described alteration violations [Data: Entities (5217), (3429); Relationships (1563, 1548, 9319)].

The broader entity description says Article 32 includes penalties for vehicle owners and supplementary or remedial measures. The records do not establish how often alterations occur or whether any particular owner has been penalized [Data: Entities (367), (4419)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The material specifies monetary sanctions and licence-point consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the violations described under Article 32, Clause 9, the data states fines of 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng for individual vehicle owners and 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizational owners, with driving-licence point deductions also addressed by the provision [Data: Entities (3069); Relationships (1546)].

A separate record states that Clause 2 provides fines of 300,000–400,000 đồng for individuals and 600,000–800,000 đồng for organizations for the covered vehicle-owner violations. These amounts concern distinct described provisions and should not be conflated [Data: Entities (2123); Relationships (1539)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-owner responsibility extends to specified transport conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a transportation-related violation concerning goods carried using transport vehicles, machinery, technical equipment, or cylindrical items. The supplied description says that when the vehicle owner directly operates the vehicle, the penalty is imposed under point đ, Clause 13 of Article 32 [Data: Entities (5118); Relationships (1562)].

More generally, the data describes Article 32 as setting penalties for vehicle owners who commit road-traffic regulation violations. It does not provide case records or information about the frequency or enforcement of these penalties [Data: Entities (4419); Relationships (1555)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records also cover plate compliance and inspection-related conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 8 is described as establishing fines for individual and organizational owners of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles in specified licence-plate circumstances, including operation without a required plate or with a plate that does not match registration or was not issued by a competent authority [Data: Entities (987); Relationships (1528)].

The data also identifies renting or borrowing car components or accessories while a vehicle is undergoing inspection as a violation, with stated fines of 4,000,000–6,000,000 đồng for individuals and 8,000,000–12,000,000 đồng for organizations that own the specified vehicles. The records describe rules and sanctions, not observed conduct [Data: Entities (4123), (3069); Relationships (8996)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other Article 32 references concern foreign vehicles and animal-drawn traffic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 32 entity description says Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP regulates foreign motor vehicles and foreign nationals driving in Vietnam, including operating conditions, customs and immigration procedures, and the period during which those vehicles may participate in traffic [Data: Entities (367)].

It also describes Article 32 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as addressing people guiding animals and operating animal-drawn vehicles on public roads, including requirements to keep to the right, cross safely, avoid obstructing traffic, and stay out of lanes designated for motor vehicles. These are distinct legal topics grouped under the same article number [Data: Entities (367), (2413); Relationships (1543)].

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Clause 19 Corrective Measures
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Clause 19 of Article 32 and two provisions identified as violations that trigger its corrective measures: Clause 9A and Point O, Clause 7 of Article 32. Clause 19 is the central provision, requiring individuals and organizations committing the specified violations to take corrective measures, including installing prescribed rescue equipment and driver- or journey-monitoring devices. The records describe the provisions and their links but do not provide details about jurisdiction, enforcement, or actual compliance outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational significance because it links specified violations to corrective measures involving safety equipment and driver or journey monitoring, while the records provide no evidence of actual violations or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 19 is the community's central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 19 of Article 32 is described as requiring individuals and organizations that commit specified violations to take corrective measures. It is linked to both of the other provisions in the dataset, making it the central entity in this small regulatory community. [Data: Entities (899); Relationships (3382, 3383)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two provisions are identified as triggers for corrective measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 9A of Article 32 is identified as a violation that triggers the measures specified in Clause 19. The relationship record confirms that Clause 19's corrective measures apply to violations under Clause 9A. [Data: Entities (998); Relationships (3382)]

Point O, Clause 7 of Article 32 is likewise described as a violation that triggers Clause 19's measures. [Data: Entities (3789); Relationships (3383)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Corrective measures include equipment and monitoring devices
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of Clause 19 specifies corrective measures that include installing prescribed rescue equipment and driver- or journey-monitoring devices. The records do not specify the devices' technical characteristics, how they are monitored, or the procedures for verifying installation. [Data: Entities (899)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationships establish a shared corrective-measures framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: Both triggering provisions connect to the same Clause 19 provision, indicating that the dataset presents one corrective-measures framework applicable to the violations named in Clause 9A and Point O, Clause 7. The relationships describe the scope of that framework but do not establish that any person or organization has committed a violation. [Data: Relationships (3382, 3383); Entities (899, 998, 3789)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records support a limited compliance assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied entity descriptions identify the provisions and the corrective measures, and the relationships specify which violations trigger them. They do not provide jurisdictional context, enforcement details, compliance status, penalties, or evidence of real-world cases; conclusions on those matters cannot be drawn from these records. [Data: Entities (899, 998, 3789); Relationships (3382, 3383)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Violations and Administrative Sanctioning
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road traffic violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and the administrative procedures used to address them. It connects a broad set of driver and vehicle-owner conduct to enforcement, verification, corrective measures, and supplementary penalties. Covered issues include passenger over-capacity, load and dimension limits, environmental protection, cargo securing, and certain vehicle-monitoring equipment failures; consequences described include penalties, unloading excess cargo, and temporary suspension of inspection-certificate or vehicle-badge use.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it encompasses a broad traffic-safety enforcement framework with verification processes, corrective measures, and penalties that can affect vehicle operators and owners.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad regulatory framework is the community's center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road Traffic Violations is the central subject, covering breaches of rules governing order and safety on roads and linking to administrative sanctioning, owner procedures, verification, and specified penalties. The framework is described as addressing conduct by drivers, vehicle owners, and other individuals or organizations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (4464, 104, 3656); Relationships (285, 9510, 10258)]

The relationships show that administrative sanctioning and vehicle-owner procedures apply to the specified violations. The data describes a regulatory and enforcement community; it does not provide evidence of particular cases, enforcement outcomes, or rates of noncompliance. [Data: Relationships (285, 9510)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violations span several operational and safety-related categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The covered conduct includes carrying more than 50% above a vehicle's permitted passenger capacity, exceeding vehicle or road load or dimension limits, failing to secure transported goods, and environmental-protection violations. These categories connect to the general road-traffic violation framework and to the administrative sanctioning process. [Data: Entities (4464, 3480, 1886, 2030, 1823); Relationships (9377, 282, 280, 283)]

The entity description also lists improper use of roads or sidewalks and other provisions of the decree, including specified articles. The supplied material identifies these as covered conduct but does not quantify their prevalence or specify individual penalty amounts. [Data: Entities (4464)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle owners may be subject to procedures alongside drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework includes procedures and principles for penalizing vehicle owners, as well as drivers, for specified violations. The owner-procedure relationship is directly connected to the general violations category. [Data: Entities (3656, 104); Relationships (9510)]

A person or organization acquiring a vehicle by purchase, transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance may be treated as its owner for penalty purposes under the cited provision. The data describes this rule but does not detail how responsibility is determined in a particular case. [Data: Entities (5366); Relationships (9511)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified violations can trigger temporary supplementary penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain violations, the described supplementary penalty is suspension of the right to use a vehicle's technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate and inspection sticker for one to three months. This consequence is linked to the general road-traffic violations category. [Data: Entities (4831); Relationships (10252)]

Certain violations described in Article 32, including specified passenger-capacity violations, may also lead to suspension of the vehicle badge for one to three months if the vehicle has a badge. The data presents these as conditional penalties rather than consequences that apply to every violation. [Data: Entities (4839, 3480); Relationships (10253, 9378)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess cargo may require a corrective unloading measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a vehicle exceeds its permitted carrying capacity and has not yet left the loading area, the described corrective measure requires unloading the excess cargo. The measure is connected to violations involving load limits. [Data: Entities (2973, 1886); Relationships (6829, 8678)]

This is distinct from the supplementary penalties involving inspection-certificate or badge use: the supplied description characterizes unloading as a corrective measure, with the loading-area condition specified as relevant. [Data: Entities (2973, 4831, 4839); Relationships (6829, 10252, 10253)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Verification and vehicle-monitoring equipment are part of the compliance picture
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework includes a verification process intended to detect conduct that may violate provisions referenced in the decree. The relationship connects verification directly to the broader road-traffic violations category. [Data: Entities (5592, 4464); Relationships (10258)]

The violations description also identifies cases involving tractor-truck and internal-transport vehicle owners who use journey-monitoring equipment that is missing, nonfunctioning, noncompliant, or tampered with. This indicates that equipment status can be relevant to compliance, but the data does not specify the equipment's technical design or the verification methods used. [Data: Entities (4464)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence describes rules, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records set out violation categories, procedures, and possible consequences, including the one-to-three-month suspensions and conditional cargo-unloading measure. They do not provide records of specific offenders, adjudicated cases, penalty amounts, or observed effects. [Data: Entities (4464, 104, 4831, 4839, 2973); Relationships (10252, 10253, 8678)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is grounded in the breadth of the described regulatory and enforcement framework; the supplied information does not establish the frequency or severity of actual violations. [Data: Entities (4464, 104); Relationships (285, 10258)]

v.tieu_de: Clause 19 Vehicle Compliance Measures
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Clause 19 of Article 32 and two corrective measures it requires for specified vehicle non-compliance: correcting the permitted cargo weight on the inspection certificate, and adjusting a non-compliant vehicle body followed by re-inspection before road use. The records describe regulatory requirements but provide no information about specific vehicles, affected parties, enforcement, or whether the measures have been completed. [Data: Entities (898, 3698, 5371); Relationships (3380, 3381)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate compliance significance because it specifies corrective measures for vehicle weight and body non-compliance, but the records do not indicate specific cases, enforcement outcomes, or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 19 is the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 19 of Article 32 is described as setting out additional corrective measures for individuals and organizations when a vehicle’s body or permitted cargo weight does not comply with current regulations. It connects directly to both corrective measures in the community. [Data: Entities (898); Relationships (3380, 3381)]

The records establish the scope of the clause as described, but do not identify the underlying violations in detail or provide information about penalties, enforcement activity, or particular cases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-weight records must be corrected
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One measure requires revising the permitted cargo weight recorded on a vehicle’s technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate when that weight does not comply with current regulations. [Data: Entities (3698); Relationships (3380)]

This links the stated compliance response to the vehicle’s inspection documentation. The records do not specify how the correction is verified or whether any particular certificate has been amended.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-compliant vehicle bodies require adjustment and re-inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 19 requires a vehicle body that fails to meet current regulations to be adjusted and the vehicle inspected again before it is used on the road. [Data: Entities (5371); Relationships (3381)]

The stated sequence connects correction of the vehicle body with a further inspection and a condition on road use. No details are provided about inspection procedures, timelines, or the outcome of any re-inspection.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The measures address two distinct types of non-compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community separates corrective action for permitted cargo weight from corrective action for a vehicle body. The first concerns the weight recorded on an inspection certificate; the second concerns adjustment of the vehicle and re-inspection. [Data: Entities (3698, 5371); Relationships (3380, 3381)]

Together, these measures indicate that Clause 19 addresses both a recorded vehicle parameter and a physical vehicle condition. The source material does not establish how often either type of non-compliance occurs.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe requirements, not implementation or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information identifies Clause 19 and describes the two corrective measures associated with it. It does not name individuals, organizations, vehicles, regulators, or enforcement cases. [Data: Entities (898, 3698, 5371); Relationships (3380, 3381)]

Accordingly, the available evidence supports describing the community’s stated compliance requirements, but not assessing actual compliance rates, enforcement effectiveness, or the consequences of particular violations.

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Driver Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on the MOTOR VEHICLE DRIVER, which is connected to four categories of traffic violations and a monetary fine. The records describe environmental-protection violations, failure to yield to a safely overtaking vehicle, unsafe or unsignaled turning, and license plate violations. They specify fines for failure to yield and license plate violations, but provide no evidence about particular drivers, how often violations occur, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (3100, 1827, 2066, 5422, 5272); Relationships (6751, 7047, 9019, 8989, 9020)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it covers multiple driver duties and significant stated penalties, but the records do not establish violation frequency or actual impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
MOTOR VEHICLE DRIVER is the central node in the supplied relationships: it is linked to each of the four described violation categories and to the monetary fine. The driver definition spans cars, vehicles with trailers, tractors, motorized four-wheel vehicles, motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles, giving the described rules a broad range of vehicle types. [Data: Entities (3100); Relationships (6751, 7047, 9019, 8989, 9020)]

These records describe regulatory relationships, not identified individuals or evidence that any driver has committed a violation. [Data: Entities (3100, 1827, 2066, 5422, 5272)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violations address several distinct driving obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct includes environmental-protection violations while participating in traffic, failure to yield when it is safe to a vehicle seeking to overtake, unsafe or unsignaled turning, and specified license plate violations. Together, these records cover both driving behavior and vehicle identification requirements. [Data: Entities (1827, 2066, 5272, 5422); Relationships (6751, 7047, 9019, 9020)]

The supplied descriptions establish the types of conduct covered, but do not give prevalence figures, enforcement outcomes, or evidence that the violations occurred in a specific case. [Data: Entities (1827, 2066, 5272, 5422)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to yield has a stated fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to yield to an overtaking vehicle is described as failing to give way when doing so is safe. The record identifies the conduct under Article 9, Clause 2, and states that Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (2066, 3056); Relationships (7047, 8989)]

The fine is a stated administrative penalty associated with the specified violation; the records do not indicate that it was imposed on any particular driver. [Data: Entities (3056); Relationships (8989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License plate violations carry the largest stated fine in the records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The license plate provision covers operating a vehicle without the required number of plates, with improperly positioned or fitted plates, illegible or obscured characters, or plates whose characters or physical features have been altered. It also covers materials or devices that interfere with technical enforcement equipment identifying a plate. The stated fine is 20,000,000 to 26,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (5422); Relationships (9020)]

This is the largest specific fine range provided in the supplied records. The material does not state how often these violations occur or whether the stated penalty has been applied in any case. [Data: Entities (5422)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unsafe or unsignaled turning and environmental violations are identified without penalty amounts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The unsafe-turning description covers failing to observe or ensure a safe distance from vehicles behind, failing to slow down, or failing to signal a turn continuously; it excludes following a bend where roads do not intersect at the same level. The relationship identifies the driver as the person operating a covered motor vehicle who commits the described violation. [Data: Entities (5272, 3100); Relationships (9019)]

Environmental-protection traffic violations are described as conduct by a driver of a car, tractor, or similar vehicle that violates environmental-protection regulations while participating in traffic. The supplied records do not specify a penalty amount for either this category or unsafe turning. [Data: Entities (1827, 5272); Relationships (6751, 9019)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle-Owner Road-Traffic Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on penalties for vehicle owners and links those fines to two situations: an owner allowing an employee or representative to commit a referenced traffic violation, and an owner personally committing one. The records provide two fine ranges by owner type but do not clearly map each range to a specific conduct item. One description also cites the legal provision inconsistently, so that reference requires verification. The information concerns regulatory compliance; it does not establish that a violation occurred or provide evidence of actual enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2271, 157, 4564, 5440); Relationships (503, 7337, 504, 10309)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes substantial regulatory fines and owner liability, but the records establish no actual violations, enforcement, or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fines are the community's central regulatory element
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The FINES FOR VEHICLE OWNERS entity is connected to both allowing an employee or representative to commit a referenced violation and personally committing a referenced violation. This makes owner penalties the organizing feature of the community. [Data: Entities (2271, 157, 5440); Relationships (503, 7337)]

The records describe the relevant legal framework and possible penalties, not any specific case or finding of noncompliance. They therefore support an assessment of regulatory relevance, but not a conclusion that a particular owner has violated the rules. [Data: Entities (2271, 157); Relationships (503, 7337)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed fine ranges distinguish individual and organizational owners
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine description gives one range of 20,000,000–26,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for an individual owner and 40,000,000–52,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for an organizational owner. It gives another listed act ranges of 28,000,000–30,000,000 đồng for an individual and 56,000,000–60,000,000 đồng for an organization. [Data: Entities (2271)]

The provided records do not specify which of these two schedules applies to each of the conduct categories in the relationships. Accordingly, the amounts should not be assigned to a particular category without further verification. [Data: Entities (2271); Relationships (503, 7337)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Allowing an employee or representative to violate traffic rules is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
