The records describe a vehicle owner handing over a vehicle to, or otherwise allowing, an employee or representative to operate it when that person commits a specified road-traffic violation. A relationship connects this conduct to the owner-fines entity. [Data: Entities (157, 2271); Relationships (503)]

A separate relationship connects the allowance conduct to the violation referenced in Point d, Clause 3, Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The records do not provide further details about the underlying violation, so its nature should not be inferred. [Data: Entities (4564); Relationships (504)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records also address an owner personally committing a violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity for a vehicle owner directly committing a road-traffic violation describes the owner personally driving while committing the referenced violation. The relationships connect this conduct both to the fines for vehicle owners and to the violation referenced in Point d, Clause 3, Article 22. [Data: Entities (5440, 4564, 2271); Relationships (7337, 10309)]

This establishes that owner-perpetrated conduct is represented separately from allowing an employee or representative to commit a violation. The records do not say that either conduct occurred in a particular incident. [Data: Entities (157, 5440); Relationships (503, 7337)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The legal citation for the allowance conduct needs verification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of allowing an employee or representative to commit a violation cites Clause 2, Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP in one instance and Point b, Clause 2, Article 21 in another. The description itself notes that the applicable citation should be verified. [Data: Entities (157)]

This inconsistency is a material limitation when using the records to determine the precise legal basis. The linked violation entity identifies Point d, Clause 3, Article 22, but the supplied information does not resolve the discrepancy in the allowance description. [Data: Entities (157, 4564); Relationships (504)]

v.tieu_de: Driving-Licence Point Deduction and Article 50
v.tom_tat: This community concerns the administration of driving-licence point deductions for qualifying traffic violations. Clause 1 of Article 50 addresses cases where multiple qualifying violations are sanctioned in the same instance: only the deduction for the violation carrying the highest deduction applies. An authorized official is responsible for notifying the affected person. The records describe the rule and roles but do not establish how often it is applied or whether particular officials or people have complied with it.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it sets a rule affecting licence holders sanctioned for qualifying violations and requires notification, while the records provide no evidence of broader effects or implementation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 50 limits deductions in a single instance
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 1 of Article 50 provides that when multiple qualifying administrative violations are sanctioned in the same instance, points are deducted only for the violation with the highest deduction. This defines how the deduction is determined in that specific situation. [Data: Entities (865); Relationships (3340)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The deduction applies to a penalized licence holder
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the person subject to an administrative penalty as the person whose driving-licence points are deducted for a qualifying violation. The data does not identify any particular person or case. [Data: Entities (3712); Relationships (6518)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An authorized official must give notice
phat_hien.giai_thich: The authorized driving-licence point-deduction official is responsible for notifying the affected person that points have been deducted. The relationship establishes a notification duty, but does not indicate how notice is delivered or whether it occurred in any specific case. [Data: Entities (614, 3712); Relationships (2774)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The sanction is part of a broader administrative framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: Driving-licence point deduction is described as an administrative sanction for qualifying road-traffic violations and may be imposed alongside a fine or another penalty. The description identifies several cited provisions and notes that the sanction can relate to violations by cargo-vehicle drivers. [Data: Entities (1701)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish deduction amounts for some conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description states that the cited provisions do not specify the number of points deducted for the described overweight-towing conduct or for certain other violations. Accordingly, these records support the general framework and the Article 50 rule, but not a specific point amount for those cases. [Data: Entities (1701)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to rules and assigned responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe the deduction mechanism, the multiple-violation rule, the affected person, and the official's notification responsibility. They do not provide case outcomes, implementation rates, compliance findings, or evidence about the practical effects of the system. [Data: Entities (1701, 865, 3712, 614); Relationships (3340, 6518, 2774)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Administrative Violations and Decree 168
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative violations in Vietnam’s road-traffic system and the rules for enforcing them. Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is linked to penalty forms and remedial measures, while civil servants and public employees performing official duties are authorized to document violations. The framework also covers temporary vehicle detention, permit or practice-certificate revocation, and how multiple violations are handled in one proceeding. An amendment to Clause 2 of Article 46 is separately linked to the authority of civil servants and public employees. The records describe legal powers and procedures, not particular violations, enforcement cases, or findings of noncompliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad relevance to road-traffic enforcement and the significant administrative powers described, without evidence of any specific incident or actual harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A legal framework for road-traffic administrative violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity describes administrative violations as breaches of rules governing road-traffic order and safety in Vietnam, subject to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and applicable law. It connects the framework to administrative penalties and remedial measures, making the decree a key part of the community’s enforcement structure. [Data: Entities (127, 360); Relationships (400)]

The information establishes the scope and mechanisms of the framework, but does not identify particular violations, enforcement outcomes, or compliance rates. [Data: Entities (127, 360); Relationships (400)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Civil servants and public employees may document violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Civil servants and public employees are described as authorized to prepare and make records of administrative violations when performing their official duties or assigned tasks. Their role is therefore procedural: the records support documentation of violations under the applicable rules. [Data: Entities (841, 3996); Relationships (401, 414)]

An amendment to Clause 2 of Article 46 is also linked to both groups and described as specifying this authority. The provided information does not establish the actions of any particular official or employee. [Data: Entities (183); Relationships (562, 564)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework provides for penalties and remedial measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as addressing forms of administrative penalties and remedial measures, including revocation of permits and professional practice certificates. The relationships in the data connect Article 3 both to the general forms of penalties and to permit or certificate revocation. [Data: Entities (360, 2361, 4236); Relationships (1468, 1473)]

Administrative violations are also linked to the forms of penalties as enforcement measures. The records describe the types of measures covered, but do not specify a penalty imposed in any particular case. [Data: Entities (127, 2361); Relationships (400, 408)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary detention is described as a preventive measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes temporary detention of vehicles and related documents under Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The entity description characterizes it as a preventive measure available in specified circumstances, and the relationship states that detention is permitted to immediately prevent specified administrative violations. [Data: Entities (4871); Relationships (418)]

The general description of administrative violations notes that stopping conduct or detaining a vehicle may be used where necessary, including when failure to act could cause serious social consequences. This is a description of a legal power, not evidence that detention occurred in a specific instance. [Data: Entities (127, 4871); Relationships (418)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Rules address multiple violations in a single proceeding
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes a proceeding in which one person is sanctioned for multiple administrative violations at the same time. It also states that a monetary fine is imposed for each violation in that proceeding. [Data: Entities (4613, 3068); Relationships (417, 8995)]

For driving-licence point deductions, the central entity description states that when at least two violations in the same instance carry deductions, points are deducted only for the violation with the highest deduction. This describes how overlapping sanctions are treated, rather than an outcome in any individual case. [Data: Entities (127); Relationships (417)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns regulatory authority, not documented misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships concern statutory provisions, authorized roles, and enforcement procedures. They do not identify a specific person who committed a violation, a particular enforcement action, or a finding that an entity failed to comply with the law. [Data: Entities (127, 360, 841, 3996); Relationships (400, 401, 414)]

Accordingly, the significance of this community lies in the scope of the road-traffic administrative framework and the powers it describes. The supplied records do not support conclusions about actual enforcement frequency, public reaction, or the effects of these measures. [Data: Entities (127, 4871); Relationships (408, 418)]

v.tieu_de: Permit and Practice Certificate Remedial Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a procedure for enforcing two remedial measures concerning permits or practice certificates: requiring the return of altered documents and revoking documents that have expired or were not issued by a competent authority. The relationships connect the central procedure to each measure. The material describes document-control and authorization concerns but does not identify a jurisdiction, responsible bodies, or specific cases. [Data: Entities (3882, 4228, 4162); Relationships (9738, 9739)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes measures for addressing altered or invalid credentials, while providing no evidence about their implementation or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A central procedure links the remedial measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The procedure for enforcing remedial measures is the hub of this community and is connected to both the required return of altered permits or practice certificates and the revocation of invalid ones. This structure presents the two actions as parts of a shared enforcement procedure. [Data: Entities (3882); Relationships (9738, 9739)]

The records describe the procedure's scope but do not specify who administers it, how enforcement is initiated, or what steps are involved. [Data: Entities (3882)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Altered documents are subject to a return requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One measure requires the return of permits or practice certificates that have been erased or modified in a way that distorts their contents. The linked relationship confirms that this return requirement is included in the central procedure. [Data: Entities (4162); Relationships (9738)]

The supplied information does not state how alteration is established, who must return the documents, or what consequences apply if they are not returned. [Data: Entities (4162, 3882); Relationships (9738)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Expired or unauthorized documents are subject to revocation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The second measure concerns revoking permits or practice certificates that have expired or were not issued by a competent authority. It is explicitly included in the central enforcement procedure. [Data: Entities (4228); Relationships (9739)]

The records identify the grounds for revocation but do not describe the decision-maker, review process, or whether affected holders have an appeal or other remedy. [Data: Entities (4228, 3882); Relationships (9739)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The measures address distinct document-integrity concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The return requirement addresses documents whose contents have been distorted through erasure or modification, whereas revocation addresses documents that are expired or lack issuance by a competent authority. These are distinct grounds for intervention within the same procedure. [Data: Entities (4162, 4228); Relationships (9738, 9739)]

The source material does not say whether the measures can apply to the same document or whether one must precede the other. [Data: Entities (4162, 4228); Relationships (9738, 9739)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is narrowly scoped, with implementation details unspecified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available records are limited to three entities and two links, all concerning enforcement measures for permits or practice certificates. They provide no named organizations, individuals, jurisdiction, implementation examples, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (3882, 4228, 4162); Relationships (9738, 9739)]

Accordingly, the material supports identifying the measures and their stated grounds, but not assessing how often they are used, how effectively they are enforced, or their effects in practice. [Data: Entities (3882, 4228, 4162); Relationships (9738, 9739)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Driver's License Points and Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the driver's-license point-deduction measure under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and connects it to motorcycle and moped traffic violations, motor-vehicle condition violations, passenger-car violations, and rules about license suspension and remaining points. Related entities describe monetary fines, including a specific fine for motorcycle helmet violations. Together, the records outline how point deductions and fines apply to certain traffic violations, along with procedural limits on deductions. The information is regulatory in scope; the records do not establish enforcement outcomes or compliance by particular drivers.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community's broad relevance to traffic penalties and driver licensing, while the provided records describe rules rather than specific incidents or demonstrated harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver's-license point deduction is the central measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The point-deduction measure is linked to several violation categories, including motorcycle and moped traffic-rule violations, vehicle-condition violations, and passenger-car violations. This makes it the organizing mechanism connecting much of the community's regulatory information. [Data: Entities (1522, 4436, 3099, 5046); Relationships (6193, 6187, 6199)]

The measure is described as an administrative traffic penalty imposed in addition to other applicable penalties when prescribed for a violation. The records therefore present point deduction as one part of a broader sanction framework, not as a substitute for every other penalty. [Data: Entities (1522)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The measure has a defined procedure and limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 50 says an authorized sanctioning person deducts the prescribed points from the applicable part of an integrated driver's license. It distinguishes the non-expiring category for motorcycles and similar vehicles from time-limited categories for cars and specified four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles. [Data: Entities (1522)]

When a driver's remaining points are fewer than the prescribed deduction, all remaining points are deducted. The most recent deduction starts the 12-month period used to determine eligibility for automatic restoration. [Data: Entities (1522, 2374); Relationships (6184)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle and moped violations connect fines with possible point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 7 is described as covering road traffic rule violations by motorcycle and moped drivers, with fines ranging from 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the described violations. The same violation category is linked to driver's-license point deduction. [Data: Entities (4436, 1522, 61); Relationships (6193, 132)]

The records establish that these penalty types are associated with the category, but they do not specify the number of points deducted for every violation within it. The point-deduction entity notes that many cited provisions identify deduction as a possible sanction without stating the particular point amount. [Data: Entities (1522, 4436); Relationships (6193)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Helmet violations have a specific fine and stated exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The helmet-violation category concerns carrying a passenger without a motorcycle helmet or with the helmet strap incorrectly fastened. It is identified as a type of Article 7 motorcycle and moped traffic-rule violation. [Data: Entities (3168, 4436); Relationships (9085)]

The specified fine is 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng. The description lists exceptions for carrying someone who needs emergency medical care, a child under six, or a person being escorted for violating the law. [Data: Entities (2109, 3168); Relationships (7100)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition and passenger-car violations are also within the point-deduction network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records link driver's-license point deduction to specified vehicle-condition violations by motorcycle, moped, and similar-vehicle drivers. One listed vehicle-condition violation is associated with an administrative fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (3099, 61, 1522); Relationships (6187, 131)]

The network also links point deduction to described traffic violations by drivers of passenger cars, vehicles carrying people, and similar vehicles. The provided records do not detail the specific passenger-car conduct or the number of points applicable to it. [Data: Entities (5046, 1522); Relationships (6199)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point deductions are subject to restrictions involving license withdrawal or suspension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The point-deduction description states that points are not deducted when the same case also involves a violation subject to withdrawal of the right to use the license. Separately, a relationship states that points must not be deducted while the license is within a period of suspension of the right to use it. [Data: Entities (1522, 4838); Relationships (6196)]

These records describe restrictions on when point deduction applies; they do not provide information about any specific driver's suspension or the outcome of a particular case. [Data: Entities (1522, 4838); Relationships (6196)]

v.tieu_de: Time-Limited License and Practice Certificate Withdrawals
v.tom_tat: This community concerns time-limited withdrawals of the right to use a driver's license or a professional practice certificate, and the procedure governing both sanctions. The procedure is linked to each sanction and applies to violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. The driver's-license sanction also has a stated interaction with license-point deduction: where both apply, the withdrawal sanction is applied. The records describe a regulatory framework but provide no specific cases or evidence about enforcement outcomes, compliance, or reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes sanctions affecting driving and professional practice, although the records provide only a narrow procedural account and no case-specific impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A shared procedure connects both withdrawal sanctions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The procedure for time-limited withdrawal of licenses and practice certificates is the central entity linking the driver's-license sanction and the practice-certificate sanction. The relationships specify that it governs each type of withdrawal. [Data: Entities (3885, 4895, 4963); Relationships (9740, 9741)]

The described scope is violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. The records establish the procedural connection but do not identify particular proceedings or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (3885)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver's-license withdrawal is a distinct sanction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver's-license measure is described as a time-limited sanction that removes the right to use a driver's license. It is linked to the shared procedure for withdrawal of licenses and practice certificates. [Data: Entities (4895); Relationships (9740)]

The record further states that if a case involves both a violation subject to withdrawal and one subject to license-point deduction, the withdrawal sanction is applied. This describes how the two measures interact in that circumstance, but does not provide details about particular cases or the duration of any withdrawal. [Data: Entities (4895)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Practice-certificate withdrawal applies to professional credentials
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate time-limited sanction removes the right to use a professional practice certificate for violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. The shared procedure is expressly linked to this sanction. [Data: Entities (4963); Relationships (9741)]

The entity description states that the applicable procedure is governed by administrative-violation law. The records do not specify which professions or individual certificate holders are affected. [Data: Entities (4963)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework concerns road-traffic order and safety
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated subject matter of the procedure and practice-certificate sanction is violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. This situates the community within a regulatory and sanctioning context, rather than describing an organization or a specific enforcement operation. [Data: Entities (3885, 4963)]

The provided descriptions do not identify a jurisdiction, particular statutory provisions, or the factual circumstances that trigger either sanction. [Data: Entities (3885, 4895, 4963)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports the framework, not its real-world effects
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe two types of time-limited withdrawal and a procedure linking them, including the stated interaction between driver's-license withdrawal and point deduction. They do not provide named individuals, enforcement statistics, case outcomes, or information about compliance or public reputation. [Data: Entities (3885, 4895, 4963); Relationships (9740, 9741)]

Accordingly, the evidence supports an account of the measures' described scope and procedural relationships, but not conclusions about how frequently they are used or what effects they have in practice. [Data: Entities (3885, 4895, 4963); Relationships (9740, 9741)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Vehicle-Owner Traffic Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle owners—individuals and organizations—and road-traffic violations addressed under Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The records connect owners to fines and specified compliance failures, including vehicle modifications made without required advance declaration and incomplete registration changes. Penalties vary by owner type and violation, with some cited ranges reaching tens of millions of VND. The material describes a regulatory framework, not evidence that any particular owner committed a violation; it provides no specific information about technical capabilities or reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it covers broad categories of vehicle owners and potentially substantial statutory penalties, although the records do not establish actual violations by identified owners.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 provides the community’s regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central topic is road-traffic violations attributed to vehicle owners and addressed under Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The listed vehicle categories include cars, motorized four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles, specialized vehicles, motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles. [Data: Entities (4568, 4467); Relationships (7898, 9328, 7897, 9327)]

The records describe both individual and organizational vehicle owners as subject to the provisions. They also state that coverage includes cases where an owner personally drives and commits a violation, as well as cases where an owner allows an employee or representative to drive in violation of a cited provision. [Data: Entities (4568)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individual owners face several distinct fine levels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records associate individual owners with a number of fine amounts, including VND 4–6 million for specified violations, VND 28–30 million for other specified violations, and VND 20–26 million for a separate category. These are distinct amounts tied to different provisions or violation types, not one general fine range. [Data: Entities (2648, 5520, 3071, 3625); Relationships (7894, 7896, 7901)]

The source material also identifies other individual-owner amounts, including VND 300,000–400,000, VND 800,000–1,000,000, and VND 4–6 million for specified vehicle or violation categories. The records do not provide enough detail here to map every amount to a complete list of circumstances. [Data: Entities (2648)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizational owners have separate, often higher fine amounts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Organizations that own covered vehicles are connected to Article 32 violations and to fine amounts of VND 8–12 million and VND 56–60 million for specified violations. The entity description also lists VND 600,000–800,000 and VND 1,600,000–2,000,000 for separate specified violations. [Data: Entities (3434); Relationships (9326, 8999)]

A separate set of records states that organizations may face VND 40–52 million for a described category, distinct from the higher VND 130–150 million range cited for certain other violations. These amounts should not be treated as one general penalty range. [Data: Entities (5520); Relationships (9329)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle modifications and registration changes are identified compliance issues
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One specified violation is modifying a vehicle without first completing a required procedure with the vehicle registration authority. The records say that both individual and organizational vehicle owners may commit this violation. [Data: Entities (1965); Relationships (6917, 6918)]

Another specified violation is failing to complete the required procedure to change a vehicle registration certificate or license plate. The records connect this failure to both individual and organizational owners, but do not report any particular owner having committed it. [Data: Entities (1957); Relationships (6908, 6909)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Paragraph 9 addresses expired inspection documentation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Paragraph 9 of Article 32 is described as setting fines for owners who allow a vehicle to participate in traffic when a required inspection certificate or sticker has been expired for less than one month. The records connect this provision to both individual and organizational owners. [Data: Entities (3528); Relationships (7895, 9325)]

The provided material identifies the circumstance and the existence of applicable fines, but does not specify the exact Paragraph 9 amounts in the associated entity description. It therefore does not support assigning a particular fine figure to this circumstance. [Data: Entities (3528)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fine amounts vary by provision and should not be conflated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The source records explicitly describe Article 32 penalties as dependent on both the specific violation and whether the owner is an individual or an organization. They distinguish the VND 20–26 million individual and VND 40–52 million organizational amounts from the VND 65–75 million and VND 130–150 million amounts applicable to certain other violations. [Data: Entities (5520); Relationships (7901, 9329)]

Other listed schedules, such as VND 4–6 million for individuals and VND 8–12 million for organizations, likewise refer to specified violations rather than a universal penalty. [Data: Entities (3071); Relationships (7894, 8999)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe penalties and license-point measures but give limited detail on the latter
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An entity describes Article 32 enforcement measures as including monetary fines and driving-license point deductions, and another entity says the article concerns penalties and deduction of driving-license points. [Data: Entities (3625, 4467)]

The supplied records do not state the number of points deducted or the conditions for a deduction. They also contain no case-specific enforcement outcomes, identified offenders, technical capability assessments, or reputation information; conclusions on those matters are not supported by this dataset. [Data: Entities (3625, 4467)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Transport Violations and 3–5 Million Dong Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong associated with several transport-related violations. The records link the penalty to failure to carry a temporary import–re-export road transport declaration, journey-monitoring device violations (including missing, nonfunctioning, or falsified devices), and listed violations by drivers of automobiles and similar vehicles. The data describes the regulatory scope and penalty but does not establish how often violations occur or how enforcement is carried out. [Data: Entities (2179, 1944, 3387, 3398, 2086); Relationships (6896, 6246, 7184, 7185, 7070, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it links a defined monetary penalty to multiple transport compliance obligations and driver categories, while the records provide no evidence of violation prevalence or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single monetary penalty is the community’s central link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong is the central entity, with relationships connecting it to the declaration violation, driver category, and journey-monitoring violations. This structure makes the penalty the common point across several distinct compliance issues. [Data: Entities (2179); Relationships (6896, 6246, 7183, 7184, 7185, +more)]

The records establish the stated fine range and its associations, but do not indicate the frequency of enforcement, the number of affected drivers, or the amount collected.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Declaration-carrying requirement applies to specified drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes failure to carry the required temporary import–re-export road transport declaration as a violation and links it to drivers of automobiles and similar vehicles. A separate relationship states that the specified fine applies to this failure. [Data: Entities (1944, 1540, 2179); Relationships (6245, 6896)]

The records identify the obligation and penalty association but do not provide further details about the circumstances in which the declaration is required.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Journey-monitoring violations cover missing, malfunctioning, or falsified device data
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify three forms of journey-monitoring noncompliance: operating without a required device, operating with a device that does not function as required, and falsifying device data. Each is linked to the 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 dong fine. [Data: Entities (3387, 3398, 2086, 2796, 2179); Relationships (7184, 7185, 7070, 7183)]

The broader journey-monitoring violation description says it concerns commercial transport vehicles, tractor trucks, or internal transport vehicles. The records do not quantify the prevalence of these violations. [Data: Entities (2796, 3387, 3398)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify more than one driver and vehicle scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One entity describes drivers of automobiles and similar vehicles as subject to provisions in Article 38, including drivers of vehicles registered to operate in specified economic zones. Another describes device-related violations involving commercial transport vehicles, tractor trucks, or internal transport vehicles. [Data: Entities (1540, 2796, 3387, 3398)]

These descriptions indicate that the community spans multiple stated vehicle or driver categories; the data does not establish that every category is subject to every listed violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty descriptions cite different decree provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity describes the penalty as prescribed under Article 8, Clause 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for specified violations. The journey-monitoring violation entity separately describes the same fine range under Article 21, Clause 5. [Data: Entities (2179, 2796)]

The supplied records do not explain the relationship between those provisions, so this report cannot determine whether they concern distinct legal bases or reflect an inconsistency in the descriptions.

v.tieu_de: Article 7 and Vietnamese Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Article 7, which is described as setting administrative penalties and driving-licence point deductions for certain road-traffic violations. Its recorded connections link it to point deductions, motorcycle and moped enforcement, and violations by motorcycle drivers. The data also associates Article 7 with removal of phrases and Law No. 118/2025/QH15, but these references appear to involve different legal provisions, leaving an ambiguity that should not be treated as a single, consistent legal identity. [Data: Entities (536, 1570, 4117, 2839, 3155, +more); Relationships (2489, 2510, 2502, 2505, 2513)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns traffic penalties and licence-point deductions, while the records provide no evidence of particular enforcement outcomes or compliance failures.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 7 is the community’s central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 7 is the common entity linked to all five listed relationships, connecting it to point deductions, phrase removal, Law No. 118/2025/QH15, motorcycle and moped enforcement, and motorcycle-driver violations. This makes it the organizing reference for the community, though the relationships do not all appear to describe the same legal instrument. [Data: Entities (536); Relationships (2489, 2510, 2502, 2505, 2513)]

The entity description identifies the central provision primarily as Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and describes it as setting administrative penalties and licence-point deductions for covered traffic violations. [Data: Entities (536)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision concerns penalties for motorcycle-related traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP says it addresses violations by drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, motorbikes, and similar vehicles. It specifies penalties for particular violations, including fines of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng in certain cases. [Data: Entities (536)]

The relationship records likewise connect Article 7 to motorcycle and moped traffic enforcement and to road-traffic rule violations by motorcycle drivers. These records establish the stated regulatory scope, but do not identify particular incidents or enforcement results. [Data: Entities (3155, 4438); Relationships (2505, 2513)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-licence point deductions are a prominent penalty mechanism
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 7 is explicitly linked to driving-licence point deduction as a penalty for covered traffic violations. The entity description says point deductions are addressed across several articles of the decree, including Article 7, and that the provisions cover specified drivers or operators as well as certain vehicle-owner violations under Article 32. [Data: Entities (1570); Relationships (2489)]

The number of points deducted is not specified in the provided description. The records therefore support the existence and general scope of this penalty mechanism, but not the amount of any deduction for a particular violation. [Data: Entities (1570)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records contain conflicting or potentially conflated Article 7 references
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The primary Article 7 entity description identifies Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as the consistent reference, while also noting that some descriptions associate the name with Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP, or Law No. 118/2025/QH15 and that these may refer to different provisions or instruments. [Data: Entities (536)]

A separate entity describes Article 7 of Law No. 118/2025/QH15 as amending and adding provisions of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety, and a relationship asserts that Article 7 is part of that law. Taken together, these records create ambiguity about which Article 7 is meant in that relationship; the available data does not resolve it. [Data: Entities (2839); Relationships (2502)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Phrase removal is a distinct recorded subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One relationship states that Article 7 specifies removal of certain phrases from clauses and articles, and the corresponding entity describes this as an action specified in Article 7. [Data: Entities (4117); Relationships (2510)]

This subject differs from the traffic-penalty description associated with Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The provided records do not specify the phrases, provisions, or instrument involved, so the connection should be treated as a separate or unresolved reference rather than assumed to describe the same Article 7. [Data: Entities (536, 4117); Relationships (2510)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger-Vehicle Traffic Violations and Fines
v.tom_tat: This community concerns traffic rules and penalties involving passenger-carrying vehicles. The driver is linked to violations for failing to follow an approved route or itinerary and for leaving vehicle doors open while moving; the latter is linked to a fine entity. A separate violation concerns prohibited right-side passing and is linked to a fine of 100,000–200,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records describe regulatory penalties, but do not establish actual incidents, enforcement outcomes, or broader effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest public-safety and legal significance because it describes passenger-vehicle traffic violations and monetary penalties, but the records show no evidence of incidents or wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-vehicle drivers are associated with two specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver entity is defined as a person operating a passenger-carrying car or similar vehicle who is subject to applicable traffic rules and penalties. The relationship records connect such a driver to failure to follow an approved route or itinerary and failure to close doors while the vehicle is moving. [Data: Entities (1467); Relationships (6063, 6064)]

These records describe regulatory responsibilities and violation types; they do not identify a particular driver or establish that a violation occurred.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to follow an approved route or itinerary
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The route-related violation concerns a passenger-carrying automobile or similar vehicle operating outside its legally permitted route, schedule, or transport itinerary. Its entity description states that Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP provides a fine of 600,000–800,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1971)]

The driver relationship describes the driver as committing this violation by not following the permitted route, schedule, or itinerary. The supplied relationship records do not separately connect this violation to the fine entity. [Data: Relationships (6064)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Leaving passenger-vehicle doors open while moving
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The door-related violation is defined as failing to close the doors of a passenger-carrying car or similar vehicle while it is moving. Its entity description states that Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets a fine of 600,000–800,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1953)]

The records assign responsibility for the violation to the driver and link the violation to the fine entity. [Data: Relationships (6063, 6904)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibited right-side passing carries a separate stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Prohibited right-side passing is described as passing on the right in circumstances where it is not permitted. The entity description cites Article 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and states a fine of 100,000–200,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (3924)]

The relationship record likewise connects this violation to a fine of 100,000–200,000 Vietnamese đồng. The provided records do not connect this violation specifically to the passenger-carrying driver entity. [Data: Relationships (7110)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine information covers multiple stated amounts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general fine entity describes penalties ranging from 100,000–200,000 Vietnamese đồng and 800,000–1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, and separately specifies 600,000–800,000 Vietnamese đồng for failing to close vehicle doors while moving under Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (2119)]

The relationship records specifically support a 100,000–200,000 đồng fine for prohibited right-side passing and link the door-closure violation to the fine entity. The records do not explain which violation the general 800,000–1,000,000 đồng range applies to, so no such assignment can be made here. [Data: Relationships (7110, 6904)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 50: Licence Points and Road Transport
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around the label “Article 50,” which refers to two distinct provisions in Vietnamese legislation: one concerning driving-licence point deductions and another setting requirements for road transport of live animals and fresh food. The connected entities cover deduction principles and two licence categories, alongside transport activities subject to safety, hygiene, and disease-control requirements. The data describes regulatory scope, not evidence of violations or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (478, 3253, 4959, 1625, 5115); Relationships (2240, 2241, 2238, 2235, 2244, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful compliance importance because it spans driver-licence administration and safety requirements for animal and food transport, although the records identify rules rather than specific violations or harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 50 is a shared label for two distinct legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity description explicitly distinguishes Article 50 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning driving-licence point deductions, from Article 50 of Law 36/2024/QH15, concerning vehicles transporting live animals or fresh food. The shared label therefore connects two regulatory topics but should not be read as evidence that they are one provision or one regulatory scheme. [Data: Entities (478)]

The relationships link the central Article 50 entity to both licence-deduction and transport entities, reflecting this breadth. [Data: Relationships (2240, 2241, 2238, 2244, 2243)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Licence-point rules cover two categories in an integrated licence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies deductions from a non-expiring licence category for point-deductible violations committed while operating a motorcycle or similar vehicle, and deductions from a time-limited category for violations involving a car or specified four-wheel passenger or cargo vehicles. Article 50 is linked to each category. [Data: Entities (3253, 4959); Relationships (2240, 2241)]

These records indicate differentiated licence categories and vehicle contexts. They do not provide the number of points deducted for particular violations or describe any individual case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The deduction framework includes principles and case-handling procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 50 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting out the principles, authority, sequence, and procedures for deducting driving-licence points. The associated principles entity and relationship confirm that point-deduction principles are part of this community’s regulatory scope. [Data: Entities (478, 1625); Relationships (2235)]

The entity description also states that when multiple point-deductible violations are handled in a single case, points are deducted only for the violation carrying the highest deduction. This is a rule summary in the provided data, not evidence that it has been applied in a particular case. [Data: Entities (478)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Live-animal transport is subject to safety and hygiene requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data connects Article 50 with both “TRANSPORTATION OF LIVE ANIMALS” and “TRANSPORT OF LIVE ANIMALS.” The descriptions state that road transport of live animals must comply with road-traffic safety, veterinary hygiene, disease-prevention, and environmental-hygiene requirements. [Data: Entities (5115, 5102); Relationships (2244, 2243)]

The two entity records describe closely related aspects of the same regulated activity. They provide no information about specific operators, shipments, inspections, or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fresh-food transport has a separate set of stated safeguards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fresh-food transport entity describes road transport subject to road-traffic safety, food safety, epidemiological hygiene, disease-prevention, and environmental-hygiene requirements. Article 50 is directly linked to this activity. [Data: Entities (2370, 478); Relationships (2238)]

This places food-safety and hygiene considerations alongside traffic requirements in the community’s scope. The records do not identify particular foods, transporters, or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community’s importance lies in its cross-domain compliance scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Taken together, the linked records cover administrative rules for driver-licence points and operational requirements for transporting animals and fresh food. This makes the community relevant to both driving compliance and transport-related safety and hygiene oversight. [Data: Entities (478, 3253, 4959, 5115, 5102, +more); Relationships (2240, 2241, 2238, 2244, 2243, +more)]

The evidence describes legal requirements and their connections only. It contains no reported breaches, penalties, enforcement actions, or measurable impacts, so the community’s importance should not be interpreted as evidence of current harm.

v.tieu_de: Article 6 Clause 5 Road-Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Clause 5 of Article 6, which establishes a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified driver or vehicle-operator violations. The clause is linked to driving on the wrong side of the road, driving in an incorrect roadway or lane, and crossing the fixed median. The incorrect-roadway-or-lane description separately refers to Article 8, Clause 6, creating a cross-reference difference in the supplied information.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the community describes a specific monetary penalty and several road-traffic violations, while the data provides no broader evidence of impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine provision anchors the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 5 of Article 6 is the central entity, with relationships connecting it to three specified road-traffic violations. Its description sets a fine range of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for drivers or vehicle operators committing listed violations. [Data: Entities (963); Relationships (3517, 3516, 3515)]

The records identify the provision and penalty but do not provide information about enforcement frequency, affected populations, or actual cases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving on the wrong side is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving on the wrong side of the road is described as failing to keep to the right-hand side in the direction of travel, and the description specifies that it applies to motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles. [Data: Entities (1645)]

The relationship data states that Clause 5 includes this violation among those subject to its fine range. [Data: Relationships (3517)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Incorrect roadway or lane use is linked to the penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving in an incorrect roadway or lane is described as driving outside the prescribed roadway or lane, including a lane used for either the same or opposite direction of travel, subject to any stated exception. [Data: Entities (1613)]

The relationship record associates this violation with Clause 5 of Article 6 and its fine range. The entity description, however, identifies the violation as described in Article 8, Clause 6; the supplied data does not explain this difference. [Data: Relationships (3516); Entities (963, 1613)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Crossing the fixed median is another listed violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes crossing the fixed median as driving across the fixed divider between two roadways. [Data: Entities (1159)]

Clause 5 of Article 6 is linked to this violation as one of those subject to the provision's fine range. [Data: Entities (963); Relationships (3515)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is a compact provision-to-violations network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied relationships form a simple structure: Clause 5 of Article 6 connects directly to three violation entities—wrong-side driving, incorrect roadway or lane use, and crossing the fixed median. [Data: Relationships (3517, 3516, 3515)]

The records establish the listed associations and fine range, but do not provide further details about legal interpretation, exceptions beyond those noted in the violation description, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (963, 1613, 1645, 1159)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Violations and 600,000–800,000 VND Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on an administrative fine of 600,000 to 800,000 VND, linked to several traffic violations. The records associate the fine with crossing a fixed median, driving in the wrong roadway section or lane, violations grouped under Clause 3, and operating a passenger transport vehicle without required onboard service staff. The information describes penalties and violation categories, not specific incidents or enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has practical regulatory and road-safety relevance, but the records describe administrative penalties rather than specific incidents, broader consequences, or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 600,000–800,000 VND administrative fine is the most connected entity in the supplied records, with relationships linking it to multiple violation categories. This makes it the organizing point for the community's information about traffic compliance and penalties. [Data: Entities (2221); Relationships (4038, 3457, 6364, 7261)]

The records establish the listed amount and associations, but do not specify how often the fine is imposed or whether any particular case resulted in a penalty. [Data: Entities (2221); Relationships (4038, 3457, 6364, 7261)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Crossing a fixed median is linked to the stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Crossing a fixed median is described as driving a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle across the fixed divider between roadways. A relationship explicitly connects this violation to the 600,000–800,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (1151, 2221); Relationships (4038)]

The supplied information does not describe a specific occurrence or provide additional details about enforcement beyond this stated penalty association. [Data: Entities (1151, 2221); Relationships (4038)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Wrong-roadway or wrong-lane driving is linked to the fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe driving a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle outside its prescribed roadway section or lane, including in a lane for traffic traveling in the opposite direction. The relationship data specifies the 600,000–800,000 VND fine for this violation. [Data: Entities (1614, 2221); Relationships (6364)]

No case-specific information, frequency data, or further penalty consequences are provided. [Data: Entities (1614, 2221); Relationships (6364)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 groups several additional traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Clause 3 category includes clinging to, towing, or pushing another vehicle or object; leading animals; carrying bulky objects; and carrying a passenger standing on the seat or luggage rack, or sitting on the handlebars. The relationship data states that a person operating a vehicle who commits one of the listed violations is subject to the stated fine. [Data: Entities (942, 2221); Relationships (3457)]

The records identify these as covered violation types but do not provide incident details or additional consequences. [Data: Entities (942); Relationships (3457)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger transport operations without required onboard staff are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One described violation is operating a passenger transport vehicle without an onboard service employee when one is legally required. The fine entity description and a direct relationship associate this violation with the 600,000–800,000 VND penalty. [Data: Entities (2221, 3570); Relationships (7261)]

The supplied information does not specify which vehicle types require such staff, the circumstances of any violation, or whether other penalties apply. [Data: Entities (2221, 3570); Relationships (7261)]

v.tieu_de: Unlicensed Paid Passenger Transport and Its Fine
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of a specified passenger-transport violation and its associated fine. The violation concerns using a private, non-commercial passenger car to carry people for payment or under a contract or booking; the stated penalty range is 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 đồng. The data establishes the link between the violation and the fine, but provides no information about particular drivers, enforcement activity, or broader compliance patterns.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited documented scope, though it identifies a specific transport violation and a substantial stated monetary penalty.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is specifically defined
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described violation is using a private car that is not operated as a passenger-transport business to carry people for payment or under a contract or booking. The data presents this as a defined violation, not as an allegation against any identified person or organization. [Data: Entities (5253)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A monetary penalty is attached to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The stated fine is 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 đồng for a driver who uses a non-commercial passenger car for paid or contract-based transport. The penalty entity describes this range, and the relationship record connects it to the specified violation. [Data: Entities (2143, 5253); Relationships (7140)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community’s sole stated consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The only consequence documented in the supplied records is the monetary fine. The data does not specify additional penalties, how the fine is determined within the range, or the procedures for imposing it. [Data: Entities (2143, 5253); Relationships (7140)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rule concerns paid or contract-based passenger transport
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description ties the violation to carrying people for payment or under a contract or booking, rather than merely using a private car to transport passengers. This stated scope distinguishes the conduct covered by the record. [Data: Entities (5253)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No case-specific or broader compliance information is provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe a violation category and its stated fine, but identify no person or business as having committed the violation. They also provide no enforcement, frequency, technical-capability, or reputation information from which to assess actual compliance patterns. [Data: Entities (5253, 2143); Relationships (7140)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Violations and VND 6–8 Million Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 fine linked to several road-traffic violations: speeding by more than 20 km/h, disobeying a traffic signal, and failing to yield to or obstruct a priority vehicle. Motorcycle and motorbike drivers are specifically connected to the fine and the speeding violation. The descriptions emphasize that penalties can differ by vehicle category; the records describe a separate higher fine range for some signal violations and a separate lower range for some speeding categories. The information describes prescribed penalties, not particular incidents or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2214, 1404, 1883, 2069, 3157); Relationships (6824, 5888, 7054, 7244, 6825)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes substantial statutory penalties for several road-safety violations, while providing no evidence of specific incidents or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The VND 6–8 million penalty is the community's central link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity describes a monetary penalty applicable to several listed traffic violations, and it has the highest degree among the provided entities. Relationships connect it to speeding, disobeying a traffic signal, failure to yield to or obstruction of a priority vehicle, and motorcycle and motorbike drivers. [Data: Entities (2214); Relationships (6824, 5888, 7054, 7244)]

These records establish a connected set of penalty descriptions, rather than evidence that any particular driver committed an offense or received a fine. [Data: Entities (2214); Relationships (6824, 5888, 7054, 7244)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Speeding is linked to both the fine and motorcycle drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Exceeding the speed limit by more than 20 km/h is linked to the VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 fine. The description specifies that this range applies to motorcycle, motorbike, or similar-vehicle drivers under Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (1883, 2214, 3157); Relationships (6824, 6825)]

The speeding description also gives a VND 3,000,000–5,000,000 range under Clause 6 of Article 8, explaining that the differing ranges apply to different vehicle categories rather than being one universal penalty. [Data: Entities (1883)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Signal violations have category-dependent fine ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Disobeying a traffic signal is linked to the VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 fine in the relationship records. Its entity description, however, specifies different penalties by vehicle category: VND 18,000,000–20,000,000 under Clause 9 of Article 6 for one applicable category and VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 under Clause 7 of Article 8 for another. [Data: Entities (1404, 2214); Relationships (5888)]

Accordingly, the records present the fine amounts as category-dependent, not as a single penalty range that applies to all signal violations. [Data: Entities (1404)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to yield to or obstruction of a priority vehicle is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described offense involves failing to give way to, or obstructing, a vehicle entitled to priority while it is signaling and performing its assigned duty. The entity description states a fine of VND 6,000,000–8,000,000, and a relationship connects this offense to the central fine entity. [Data: Entities (2069, 2214); Relationships (7054)]

The records describe the offense and its prescribed penalty, but do not provide evidence of a specific incident or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (2069, 2214); Relationships (7054)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle and motorbike drivers are an identified driver category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes an entity for people driving motorcycles, motorbikes, or similar vehicles, described as subject to penalties under Article 7. The relationships connect this driver category to the central fine and connect it directly to the speeding violation. [Data: Entities (3157, 2214, 1883); Relationships (7244, 6825)]

This supports a specific connection between these drivers and the described penalty framework, but the records do not identify individual drivers or establish that any driver has violated the rules. [Data: Entities (3157); Relationships (7244, 6825)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulations, not actual compliance or enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entity descriptions state offense definitions and penalty ranges, and the relationships link certain offenses to the fine. They contain no named individuals, case details, enforcement statistics, or outcomes that would show whether the rules were followed or penalties imposed. [Data: Entities (2214, 1404, 1883, 2069, 3157); Relationships (6824, 5888, 7054, 7244, 6825)]

The community therefore provides information about the stated legal consequences of selected traffic violations, but does not support conclusions about actual compliance levels or the frequency of those violations. [Data: Entities (2214, 1404, 1883, 2069, 3157)]

v.tieu_de: Clause 10 and Article 20 Clauses 8 and 8A
v.tom_tat: This small community links Clause 10 to traffic violations under Article 20, Clauses 8 and 8A of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The described consequence is a six-point deduction from drivers’ licences, in addition to a monetary fine; however, the source descriptions give inconsistent article references for Clause 10, leaving its precise cross-reference unclear. [Data: Entities (871, 5603); Relationships (3346)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the practical significance of a stated driving-licence penalty, tempered by the community’s narrow scope and the unresolved article-reference discrepancy.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 10 is linked to the specified Article 20 violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship record states that Clause 10 specifies a six-point deduction for violations under Clauses 8 and 8A of Article 20. This is the only recorded relationship in the community. [Data: Relationships (3346)]

The related entity description also identifies those violations as traffic violations referenced in Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (5603)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated consequence includes a six-point licence deduction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Clause 10 states that drivers committing the specified violations face supplementary penalties, including the loss of six points from their driving licences. [Data: Entities (871)]

The linked violations under Article 20, Clauses 8 and 8A are likewise described as carrying a six-point deduction. [Data: Entities (5603); Relationships (3346)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The deduction is described as supplementary to a monetary fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 10’s entity description says the six-point loss is a supplementary penalty imposed in addition to a monetary fine. The data does not specify the fine amount or provide further details about how the penalties are applied. [Data: Entities (871)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The article reference for Clause 10 is unclear
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Clause 10 description notes that different descriptions cite Article 13 and Article 20 for the provision, and therefore identifies its article reference as unclear. [Data: Entities (871)]

Although the relationship connects Clause 10 to violations under Article 20, Clauses 8 and 8A, that link does not resolve the stated discrepancy. [Data: Entities (5603); Relationships (3346)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records establish a narrow regulatory connection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community consists of two described entities—Clause 10 and the specified Article 20 violations—and one recorded relationship connecting them. [Data: Entities (871, 5603); Relationships (3346)]

The records do not identify particular drivers, enforcement actions, fine amounts, or outcomes. Accordingly, they support describing the stated penalty and its link to the specified violations, but not assessing actual enforcement or broader effects.

v.tieu_de: Passenger Vehicle Drivers and Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community links passenger vehicle drivers to traffic order and safety violations and to a specific passenger-vehicle overloading violation. The overloading rule applies to carrying more passengers than permitted on a route longer than 300 km, with a stated per-passenger fine and a total cap. The records describe regulatory and financial consequences but provide no information about enforcement outcomes, technical capabilities, or reputation. [Data: Entities (5014, 3577, 3575); Relationships (9446, 9445)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory and financial significance because it concerns penalties for passenger-vehicle drivers, but the supplied records indicate no broader impact or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Drivers connect the community’s violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Passenger vehicle drivers are linked both to the general category of traffic order and safety violations and to the specific overloading violation, making drivers the central connecting entity in this small network. [Data: Entities (3575, 5014, 3577); Relationships (9446, 9445)]

The relationships identify drivers as the people subject to penalties for the general traffic violations and as the people who commit the specified overloading violation. The records do not identify particular drivers or describe individual cases. [Data: Relationships (9446, 9445)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The overloading rule has a defined route-length condition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The passenger vehicle overloading violation is described as carrying more passengers than the vehicle is permitted to carry on a route longer than 300 km. The supplied description does not specify how passenger capacity is determined or provide other conditions for applying the rule. [Data: Entities (3577)]

The relationship assigns this violation to passenger vehicle drivers who carry more passengers than their vehicle is permitted to carry. [Data: Relationships (9445)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated overloading penalty is financially significant
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description states a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong for each excess passenger, capped at 75,000,000 dong in total. These amounts establish a potential financial consequence in the records, but they do not show fines actually imposed or collected. [Data: Entities (3577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broader traffic-order category is also identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic order and safety violations are described as violations of regulations governing traffic order and safety committed by drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles, including those transporting passengers or other people. The description says these violations are addressed under Article 20; it does not provide the text of that article or further legal context. [Data: Entities (5014)]

Passenger vehicle drivers are explicitly linked to this broader category as the people subject to penalties. [Data: Relationships (9446)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records provide limited evidence beyond regulatory scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies driver groups, violation descriptions, and a stated overloading fine, but it does not report enforcement activity, compliance rates, specific incidents, or resulting harms. The community’s demonstrated significance is therefore limited to the regulatory and financial matters described in the records. [Data: Entities (5014, 3577, 3575); Relationships (9446, 9445)]

No technical capabilities or reputational information are provided for these entities in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (5014, 3577, 3575)]

v.tieu_de: Four-Point License Deduction and Passenger-Capacity Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns a four-point driver’s-license deduction and the provisions and violations linked to it. The deduction is connected to a qualifying passenger-capacity violation, including references to Clauses 2 and 4 of Article 20, and to a violation under Point a, Clause 5 of Article 34. The records also describe the deduction as applying in addition to another penalty. One entity description says the Clause 4 case is excluded from a passenger-overcapacity penalty, while a relationship says it is included in the qualifying violation subject to the deduction; the provided information does not resolve that distinction. [Data: Entities (2365, 4012, 946, 5591, 3645); Relationships (7571, 7570, 7573, 3472, 3395)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory importance because it describes a defined license-point sanction and related violations, but the records provide no evidence of broader operational or societal impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The four-point deduction is the central regulatory consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around a sanction that removes four points from a driver's license for specified violations. Its entity description identifies provisions in Article 7 and a violation under Point a, Clause 5 of Article 34 as within the stated scope. [Data: Entities (2365)]

The relationships also connect the deduction to a qualifying passenger-capacity violation and describe it as established by Clause 10 of Article 20. Together, these records make the deduction the primary link among the community's provisions and violations. [Data: Relationships (7571, 3347)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger overcapacity is tied to a qualifying violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The qualifying passenger-capacity violation is described as involving a vehicle carrying more passengers than permitted by more than 50% and up to 100%, under Clauses 2 or 4 of Article 20. The relationship records associate both clauses with the qualifying violation subject to the four-point deduction. [Data: Entities (4012); Relationships (3395, 3472)]

The deduction is explicitly linked to that qualifying violation, making this passenger-capacity case a prominent part of the community's enforcement structure. [Data: Relationships (7571)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify additional provisions and conduct in the sanction’s scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The four-point deduction entity describes its scope as including violations referenced in Clauses 4, 6, 7, and 8 of Article 7, as well as the violation in Point a of Clause 5 of Article 34. The provided data does not describe the conduct covered by all of those Article 7 clauses. [Data: Entities (2365)]

Separately, the Point a, Clause 5 violation is described as resulting in a license deduction under Clause 7, and a relationship directly connects that violation to the four-point deduction. [Data: Entities (5591); Relationships (7573)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The deduction may apply alongside another penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes the four-point deduction as being imposed in addition to the other penalty for a specified violation. This indicates that the point deduction is presented as an additional consequence, rather than as a replacement for that penalty. [Data: Entities (3645); Relationships (7570)]

Clause 10 of Article 20 is also described as providing for points to be deducted in addition to the applicable penalty. The relationship record links that clause to the four-point deduction. [Data: Entities (872); Relationships (3347)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Clause 4 records leave a scope distinction unresolved
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Clause 4 entity describes the specified overcapacity case as excluded from the passenger-overcapacity penalty described in the text. In contrast, the relationship between Clause 4 and the qualifying passenger-capacity violation says that the case is included in the violation subject to the four-point deduction. [Data: Entities (946); Relationships (3472)]

These statements may concern different consequences—the passenger-overcapacity penalty and the license-point deduction—but the records do not explicitly clarify their interaction. The distinction should therefore be retained rather than treated as a definitive contradiction or resolved interpretation. [Data: Entities (946, 2365); Relationships (3472, 7571)]

v.tieu_de: Article 20 Passenger-Transport Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 20 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its administrative penalties for passenger-vehicle and transport-related traffic violations. Linked entities cover badge requirements, passenger pickup and drop-off conduct, unauthorized passengers, unbalanced loading, and fine ranges. The information describes regulatory provisions, not evidence that any particular operator or driver committed a violation. The Article 20 description also distinguishes these rules from a separate Article 20 in Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerning permits for signal devices on priority vehicles.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s importance to passenger-transport compliance and road safety, while the records describe rules and penalties rather than documented violations or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 is the central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 20 is described principally as a provision of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP establishing administrative penalties and driving-licence point deductions for drivers of passenger cars, vehicles carrying people, and similar vehicles who breach traffic-safety or passenger-transport requirements. Its high number of connected relationships reflects its role as the hub linking the specific violation categories and penalties in this community.

The entity description also notes amendments or supplements to certain provisions by Article 7 of Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP. The records do not provide further detail on the changes or their effects. [Data: Entities (299); Relationships (1095, 1103, 1097, 1106, 1105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-vehicle badge compliance carries a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: The badge violation covers operating a passenger vehicle without the required badge, failing to display it, using an expired badge, or using one not issued by a competent authority. Article 20 is linked to this violation, and the associated fine range is 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. These records describe the applicable rule and penalty, not a specific enforcement case. [Data: Entities (3586, 63); Relationships (1095, 136, 137)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger pickup and drop-off conduct is regulated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct includes picking up or dropping off passengers on an expressway, at a location not specified in the transport contract, or at an operator’s premises or another fixed street location. Article 20 relationships identify these as covered violations, with the contract-location entry noting an exception for conduct covered by Clause 8.

The expressway entry states a fine of 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records do not state a penalty amount for each of the other pickup or drop-off situations. [Data: Entities (3738, 3740, 3741); Relationships (1097, 1098, 1099)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Rules address authorized passenger groups and vehicle loading
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 20, Clause 5, identifies transporting people outside the authorized passenger group for certain contract vehicles—including vehicles serving pupils, students, officials, public employees, or workers—as a punishable violation. This makes passenger eligibility one of the compliance topics represented in the community. [Data: Entities (5106); Relationships (1105)]

The records also identify placing luggage or goods so that a vehicle becomes unbalanced as a violation, with a stated fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (5222); Relationships (1106)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records give multiple penalty ranges but limited case-specific detail
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a fine of 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 đồng for the described passenger-vehicle badge violations and an expressway pickup or drop-off fine of 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 đồng. It also records a 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 đồng range for unbalanced loading. [Data: Entities (63, 3738, 5222); Relationships (137, 1097, 1106)]

A separate entity lists a range of 600,000 to 800,000 đồng for one of the covered traffic-regulation violations, but the supplied relationship does not identify which specific violation the range applies to. The data therefore supports noting the range, but not assigning it to a particular conduct category. [Data: Entities (2222, 5034); Relationships (7263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate Article 20 reference must not be conflated with these traffic rules
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Article 20 entity explicitly distinguishes the Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP traffic-penalty provision from Article 20 of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The latter concerns applications for issuing or reissuing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles, including a written request using Form No. 02b of Appendix II for a new permit. These are separate provisions with different subject matter. [Data: Entities (299)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Condition Violations and Equipment Restoration
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a category of vehicle-condition violations involving motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles, and a corrective measure requiring noncompliant equipment to be replaced or its technical function restored. The single recorded relationship links the violation category to that measure. The data describe the regulatory remedy but provide no information about particular cases, organizations, penalties, or compliance outcomes.
