[Data: Entities (4286, 4777); Relationships (10027)]

This limited structure supports describing the community’s subject and setting, but does not establish additional organizations, individuals, or related activities. [Data: Entities (4286, 4777); Relationships (10027)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish broader impact or compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The information defines a traffic violation and its associated location, but provides no evidence about enforcement, penalties, legal compliance by any individual, frequency, or consequences. [Data: Entities (4777, 4286); Relationships (10027)]

Accordingly, the low impact rating reflects the narrow scope of the supplied information, not a finding that the violation is harmless or that no incidents have occurred. [Data: Entities (4777, 4286); Relationships (10027)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Traffic Rules Under Article 21
v.tom_tat: The community centers on “Article 21,” an ambiguous label covering provisions in multiple Vietnamese legal instruments. Its linked records primarily describe road-traffic rules and penalties for goods-transport vehicles, including cargo loading, trailer mass, vehicle badges, and goods handling on expressways. Other linked topics concern permits for priority-vehicle signal devices and restrictions on horn use near medical facilities at night. The available data describes legal requirements and penalties, but does not establish compliance by any particular person or organization, or provide evidence about reputation or technical capabilities. [Data: Entities (306, 4966, 1581, 2129, 2675); Relationships (1161, 1184, 1170, 1173, 1166)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad regulatory importance across traffic safety, goods transport, vehicle permits, and public-nuisance restrictions, rather than evidence of a specific threat or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 21” refers to distinct legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity description cautions that “Article 21” appears in several Vietnamese legal instruments and that the applicable meaning depends on which instrument is cited. It identifies Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for certain road-traffic penalties, Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP for procedures involving permits for signal devices on priority vehicles, and Law 36/2024/QH15 for horn-use rules. [Data: Entities (306)]

Consequently, the shared article number should not be treated as a single, uniform rule. The linked records span different regulatory subjects, so identifying the instrument is necessary to interpret a particular obligation or penalty. [Data: Entities (306); Relationships (1170, 1173)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The largest cluster concerns cargo-vehicle traffic rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Most of the listed relationships connect Article 21 to violations or penalties involving goods-transport vehicles. These include cargo loading height, overloading, trailer towing mass, required badges, and broader road-traffic order and safety violations. [Data: Entities (1878, 712, 4966, 4401, 1581); Relationships (1165, 1149, 1184, 1182, 1161)]

This concentration makes commercial road transport the most prominent subject in the community. The records describe administrative rules and potential sanctions; they do not establish that any particular driver committed a violation. [Data: Entities (306, 4401); Relationships (1182)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Badge-related violations carry stated fines of VND 5–7 million
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify operating a vehicle without a required badge, using an expired badge, or using one not issued by a competent authority as separate violations. The linked relationships state a fine of VND 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 for each of these badge-related cases. [Data: Entities (1581, 3354, 5358, 5356); Relationships (1161, 1176, 1186, 1187)]

The records distinguish the underlying circumstances—missing, expired, or improperly issued badges—rather than treating them as one identical description. They provide no evidence that a specific vehicle or operator was involved. [Data: Entities (3354, 5358, 5356)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo loading and overloading have specified penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 is linked to carrying goods above the permitted loading height, for which the relationship states a fine of VND 2,000,000 to 3,000,000. It is also linked to cargo loads more than 30% and up to 50% above permitted capacity, with a stated fine of VND 3,000,000 to 5,000,000. [Data: Entities (1878, 712); Relationships (1165, 1149)]

The central description also notes that specified overloading violations may require excess loads to be unloaded or oversized goods removed. The available records do not support extending that consequence to every violation in the community. [Data: Entities (306)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Trailer mass and goods handling on expressways are separately addressed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One linked violation concerns towing a trailer or semi-trailer whose total mass exceeds the vehicle’s permitted towing mass by more than 10% and up to 30%. The relationship confirms that Article 21 specifies an applicable fine, but does not state its amount. [Data: Entities (4966); Relationships (1184)]

A separate relationship associates Article 21 with a VND 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 fine for a driver who receives or delivers goods on an expressway. The records identify this as a distinct circumstance and do not provide further details about enforcement or specific cases. [Data: Entities (2129); Relationships (1166)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records include a range of other stated penalty amounts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
In addition to the badge and loading-related amounts, a linked entity records a VND 7,000,000 to 8,000,000 fine for certain goods-transport-driver violations, while the relationship does not identify which individual violations the range applies to. The central description gives an example of VND 800,000 to 1,000,000 for towing a trailer whose total mass exceeds the permitted towing mass by more than 10% and up to 30%. [Data: Entities (2225, 306); Relationships (1167, 1184)]

Because some fine records lack a specific violation or a stated amount, the amounts should be read only in the contexts expressly described in the data. [Data: Entities (2225, 306); Relationships (1167, 1184)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community also covers priority-vehicle permits and nighttime horn restrictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 is linked to the initial procedure for issuing a permit to use a signal device on a priority vehicle; the central description says the relevant Decree 151 provision also concerns reissuing such permits. [Data: Entities (2675, 306); Relationships (1170)]

Separately, the records describe restrictions on horn use between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. in populated areas and near medical facilities, with an exception for priority vehicles. This is a different regulatory topic from cargo-vehicle penalties and illustrates why the cited legal instrument matters. [Data: Entities (2983, 306); Relationships (1173)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Violations and 600,000–800,000 Dong Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a prescribed fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and connects it to prohibited right-side overtaking, carrying oversized luggage or cargo, and specified stopping and parking violations. The records describe regulatory penalties and violation categories, rather than particular enforcement cases or drivers.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory relevance because one specified monetary penalty applies across several traffic violations, but the records provide no evidence of particular cases or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single fine links multiple traffic violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong prescribed for several violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The records connect the fine to prohibited right-side overtaking, oversized luggage or cargo, and specified stopping and parking violations. [Data: Entities (2219, 738, 3923, 5039); Relationships (7251, 3024, 7252)]

The fine description also mentions allowing a person to lie in a hammock while a vehicle is moving and violations listed in Clause 3, Article 7. These are described as part of the fine’s scope, not as evidence that any particular violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2219)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community’s central connection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity is directly linked to each of the three other listed violation entities, making it the organizing point of the provided relationships. The records indicate the penalty associated with each category but do not provide further details about enforcement or affected individuals. [Data: Entities (2219, 738, 3923, 5039); Relationships (7251, 3024, 7252)]

The fine’s stated range is 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong. The data does not specify how the amount within that range is determined for individual cases. [Data: Entities (2219)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized luggage or cargo is one covered violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The oversized-luggage-or-cargo category concerns luggage or goods exceeding a vehicle’s outer dimensions. Its description attributes a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong to Article 20, Clause 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (738, 2219); Relationships (3024)]

This is a description of a prohibited conduct and its stated penalty; the records do not identify an actual vehicle, shipment, or enforcement event. [Data: Entities (738)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibited right-side overtaking is separately identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes prohibited right-side overtaking as passing on the right in a situation where that maneuver is not permitted. It states that the violation is punishable by a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese dong under Clause 3 of Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (3923, 2219); Relationships (7251)]

The description specifies drivers of motorcycles, motorized two-wheelers, and similar vehicles. It does not provide information about how frequently this violation occurs or any particular driver’s conduct. [Data: Entities (3923)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified stopping and parking conduct is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stopping and parking category concerns drivers of specialized motor vehicles and includes stopping or parking in the wrong place, against the direction of traffic, on a fixed median, on a slope without wheel chocks, or where stopping or parking is prohibited. The fine entity states that specified stopping and parking violations are subject to the 600,000-to-800,000-dong penalty. [Data: Entities (5039, 2219); Relationships (7252)]

The records do not establish that every stopping or parking violation carries this penalty; they refer to specified violations and provide examples of the category. [Data: Entities (5039, 2219)]

v.tieu_de: Article 11 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Animal-Related Traffic Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 11 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its traffic rules for people handling or guiding animals and drivers of animal-drawn vehicles. The provision is linked to failures to yield, failures to signal by hand when turning, and failures to obey traffic signals, signs, or road markings. A fine of 150,000 to 250,000 đồng is specified for listed violations, while conduct covered by clause 3 is excluded from the clause 1 penalty; the data does not describe that exception in detail. [Data: Entities (239, 2000, 1887, 2151, 2060); Relationships (730, 731, 732, 570, 6971)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest practical importance because it concerns road-safety rules and monetary penalties for a defined group of road users, but the provided information indicates limited scope and relatively small fines.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 11 is the community’s central legal provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 11 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the hub of the community: it sets out penalties for people handling, leading, or controlling livestock and drivers of animal-drawn vehicles who violate road traffic rules. The provision is also connected to the specific violations and the clause 3 exception represented in the data. [Data: Entities (239); Relationships (730, 731, 732, 570)]

The data describes the provision’s subject and selected penalties, but does not provide the full text of Article 11 or enough detail to assess how it is applied in individual cases. [Data: Entities (239)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules concern people handling animals and drivers of animal-drawn vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated scope covers people who handle or guide animals and people driving animal-drawn vehicles. The relationship record explicitly links this category of road-traffic violation to Article 11. [Data: Entities (188, 239); Relationships (570)]

The supplied information identifies these road users but does not specify how many people or vehicles are affected, or provide information about enforcement frequency. [Data: Entities (188, 239)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data identifies three types of traffic conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violations represented include failing to yield and failing to signal by hand when changing direction; Article 11 is stated to specify a fine for each. [Data: Entities (2060, 2033); Relationships (731, 732)]

A further listed violation is failing to obey traffic lights, signs, or road markings. The data links this conduct to the specified fine, subject to the clause 3 exception described separately. [Data: Entities (2000); Relationships (6971, 6830)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine of 150,000 to 250,000 đồng is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalty amount represented in the data is 150,000 to 250,000 đồng. Article 11’s description identifies that range for specified violations, and the failure-to-obey-traffic-instructions record is explicitly linked to the fine. [Data: Entities (239, 2151, 2000); Relationships (6971)]

The provided records do not establish that this range applies to every violation or circumstance covered by Article 11, so the amount should be understood as the stated penalty for the listed conduct rather than a universal penalty. [Data: Entities (239, 2151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The clause 3 exception is noted but not explained
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 11, clause 1 excludes conduct governed by clause 3, and the data connects that exception to the failure-to-obey-signals, signs, or road-markings violation. [Data: Relationships (730, 6830); Entities (1887, 2000)]

The entity description for the exception does not specify what the clause 3 conduct is. Consequently, the supplied information supports noting that an exclusion exists, but not identifying which particular circumstances qualify. [Data: Entities (1887)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Violations and 400,000–600,000 VND Fine
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around a stated fine of 400,000–600,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to several traffic violations: motorcycle lighting, motorized-bicycle helmet use, and stopping or parking on pedestrian crossings or contrary to specified signs. The pedestrian-crossing violation is also connected to the road areas designated for pedestrian crossings. The records describe penalties and violation categories, but do not identify particular offenders, enforcement outcomes, or broader legal-compliance or reputation information. [Data: Entities (2204, 3170, 4788, 4780, 3184, +more); Relationships (7230, 7237, 7234, 7231, 9475)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest practical importance because it summarizes a specified traffic penalty and several road-safety-related violations, but provides no evidence of specific cases or wider impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single stated fine connects multiple violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a fine of 400,000–600,000 VND, which the records associate with motorcycle-lighting violations, motorized-bicycle helmet violations, and two types of stopping or parking violations. This makes the penalty the organizing link across otherwise distinct traffic conduct. [Data: Entities (2204); Relationships (7230, 7231, 7234, 7237)]

The records establish the stated penalty and its listed associations; they do not show whether a fine was actually imposed in any specific case. [Data: Entities (2204); Relationships (7230, 7231, 7234, 7237)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle lighting is one of the fine-linked violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The lighting violation covers operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle without effective near- or high-beam lights, or with lights that do not meet design standards. The relationship record states that the 400,000–600,000 VND fine applies to this violation. [Data: Entities (3170, 2204); Relationships (7230)]

The supplied information describes the conduct and penalty association, but does not identify affected drivers, vehicles, or enforcement events. [Data: Entities (3170, 2204); Relationships (7230)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two listed violations concern stopping or parking
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One category concerns stopping or parking in the road area designated for pedestrians to cross; another concerns stopping or parking where specified prohibitory signs apply. The records associate the stated fine with both categories. [Data: Entities (4788, 4780, 2204); Relationships (7237, 7234)]

These are presented as separate violation types, and the dataset does not provide case counts or information about where or how frequently they occur. [Data: Entities (4788, 4780); Relationships (7237, 7234)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pedestrian crossings provide context for one parking violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The pedestrian-crossings entity describes road parts designated for pedestrians to cross. It is linked to the violation involving stopping or parking in that designated area, while the fine record separately connects that violation to the 400,000–600,000 VND penalty. [Data: Entities (3609, 4788, 2204); Relationships (9475, 7237)]

This establishes the subject of the violation as a pedestrian crossing, but the records do not describe a specific crossing, obstruction, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (3609, 4788); Relationships (9475)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Helmet-related penalty applies to motorized-bicycle riders
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The helmet violation is described as riding a motorized bicycle without a motorcycle-style helmet or wearing one without correctly fastening its chin strap. The relationship record states that Article 9, Clause 4 specifies a fine of 400,000–600,000 VND for this violation. [Data: Entities (3184, 2204); Relationships (7231)]

The supplied records provide a description of the violation and its stated penalty, but no information about individual compliance, enforcement, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (3184, 2204); Relationships (7231)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Article 18, Clause 4 and Underage Motorcycle Driving
v.tom_tat: This small legal-information community consists of Article 18, clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and an underage motorcycle-driving violation. The provision is described as covering the violation, which concerns a person aged 16 to under 18 operating a motorcycle meeting a stated engine-capacity or electric-motor-power threshold. The records establish the regulatory connection but do not provide penalty amounts, enforcement information, or evidence of any individual’s compliance status. [Data: Entities (289, 5226); Relationships (1049)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the provision’s relevance to legal compliance and a defined category of motorcycle operation, while the available records do not establish penalties, enforcement outcomes, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18, clause 4 is the regulatory anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s central legal reference is Article 18, clause 4, described as a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addressing requirements applicable to motor-vehicle drivers. Its recorded connection to the violation identifies it as the relevant provision for this topic. [Data: Entities (289); Relationships (1049)]

The supplied information does not quote the full provision or specify the applicable sanction, so those details cannot be assessed from these records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is defined by an age range and vehicle thresholds
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation concerns a person aged 16 to under 18 operating a motorcycle with an engine-cylinder capacity of at least 50 cm³ or an electric motor power of at least 4 kW. These are the stated conditions associated with the violation in the entity description. [Data: Entities (5226)]

The description sets out a category, not evidence that any particular person committed the violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship explicitly links the provision to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole recorded relationship states that Article 18, clause 4 covers the specified violation by a person aged 16 to under 18. This provides a direct link between the legal provision and the conduct category, rather than merely a thematic association. [Data: Relationships (1049)]

No additional relationships or entities are provided to identify other relevant provisions, agencies, or affected individuals.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a narrow, clearly bounded scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied community contains two entities and one relationship: a named provision and the underage motorcycle-driving violation it covers. The records therefore support a focused account of the provision’s connection to this specific violation, but not a wider map of the decree or motorcycle regulation. [Data: Entities (289, 5226); Relationships (1049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and enforcement outcomes are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records provide a description of the violation and identify a provision that covers it, but they do not state a penalty amount, enforcement procedure, case outcome, or compliance status for any person. [Data: Entities (289, 5226); Relationships (1049)]

Accordingly, the information supports identifying a legal-compliance topic, but not judging how frequently it occurs or how it is enforced.

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Article 8 Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which establishes administrative penalties for specified road-traffic violations by drivers and operators of specialized motor vehicles. Its linked records cover failure to signal or place a warning sign when forced to park, driving through a road tunnel without low-beam headlights, provisions of Article 8, and fine amounts. The records describe regulatory requirements and penalties; they do not establish that any person committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns enforceable road-safety rules and fines, although the records describe provisions rather than actual violations or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 8 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets administrative penalties for road-traffic violations by drivers or operators of specialized motor vehicles, including specialized motorcycles. The relationships connect it to road-traffic rules, specific conduct, and fine information, making it the organizing provision in this dataset. [Data: Entities (557); Relationships (2593, 2587, 2592, 2603, 2602)]

The records establish the provision’s regulatory scope, but do not provide information about enforcement frequency, compliance rates, or the outcomes of any particular case. [Data: Entities (557)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision addresses warning failures when a vehicle is forced to park
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One violation identified under Article 8, clause 1 is failing to use hazard lights or place a “Caution: Parked Vehicle” sign when a technical failure or other force majeure requires parking partly in a traffic lane or in a prohibited parking area. Article 8 is explicitly linked to this conduct as a traffic violation. [Data: Entities (2035); Relationships (2593)]

The description excludes the separately specified case covered by point b, clause 6 of Article 8. The dataset identifies that exception, but does not provide further details about the circumstances it covers. [Data: Entities (3768); Relationships (7017)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tunnel driving without low-beam headlights is linked to a fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 8 identifies operating a vehicle in a road tunnel without the required low-beam headlights as a violation. The relationship record associates this conduct with a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1669); Relationships (2592)]

This is a description of a prescribed penalty, not evidence that a particular driver committed the violation or received a fine. [Data: Entities (1669); Relationships (2592)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 1 covers specified specialized-motorcycle conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The dataset describes clause 1 of Article 8 as establishing a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for specified conduct by a driver of a specialized motorcycle. Clause 1 is identified as part of Article 8. [Data: Entities (870); Relationships (2587)]

The records provided do not specify which conduct attracts this particular range, so it cannot be assigned to a specific violation based on this dataset alone. [Data: Entities (870)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fine records have differing descriptions and limited linked detail
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A fine entity describes a range of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified reversing-related violations. Separately, a relationship states that Article 8 prescribes that same range for specified violations, and the tunnel-headlight relationship associates it with a specific violation. [Data: Entities (4354); Relationships (2602, 2592)]

The provided records do not connect the reversing-related description directly to a specific Article 8 violation. The dataset therefore supports noting the fine description, but not inferring which reversing conduct it applies to or how it relates to the tunnel-headlight case. [Data: Entities (4354); Relationships (2602, 2592)]

v.tieu_de: Railway Traffic Safety Corridor Parking Violation
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of a railway traffic safety corridor and the traffic-violation category of stopping or parking within it. The sole recorded relationship states that the violation concerns activity within the corridor. v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the safety relevance of the identified traffic violation while accounting for the limited evidence about specific incidents, impacts, or scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a defined railway safety area
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The railway traffic safety corridor is described as the area along a railway designated as its traffic safety corridor. It is one of the two entities in this community. [Data: Entities (4027)]

The data does not specify the corridor’s location, extent, or operating conditions. [Data: Entities (4027)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Stopping or parking in the corridor is identified as a traffic violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stopping-or-parking entity describes conduct within the railway traffic safety corridor as a traffic violation. This establishes the nature of the conduct represented in the community. [Data: Entities (4782)]

The record does not identify a particular occurrence or provide information about a person or vehicle involved. [Data: Entities (4782)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship links the conduct directly to the corridor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole recorded relationship states that the violation concerns stopping or parking within the railway traffic safety corridor. The relationship connects the two entities directly. [Data: Relationships (9831)]

No other entities or relationships are listed, so the available structure is limited to this corridor-and-violation link. [Data: Entities (4782, 4027); Relationships (9831)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The information describes a violation category, not a documented enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description identifies a type of traffic violation, but the supplied records do not describe an enforcement action, adjudication, or penalty. [Data: Entities (4782)]

Accordingly, the data supports characterizing the conduct as a violation category, but not claiming that a specific person committed it or was found liable. [Data: Entities (4782); Relationships (9831)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Potential railway-safety relevance is evident, but actual impact is unreported
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described conduct takes place within an area designated as a railway traffic safety corridor, making the subject relevant to railway-area traffic safety. [Data: Entities (4027, 4782); Relationships (9831)]

The records provide no evidence of disruption, injury, damage, frequency, or broader community effects. The severity of any particular event therefore cannot be determined from this information. [Data: Entities (4027, 4782); Relationships (9831)]

v.tieu_de: Level Road-Railway Intersections and Stopping/Parking Rules
v.tom_tat: This small community links level road-railway intersections with the traffic violation of stopping or parking contrary to railway-crossing rules. Driving without wearing a seat belt is described as a road-traffic violation involving a person driving a car or similar vehicle on the road without wearing a seat belt. The relationship record states that a driver committing this violation is subject to the 800,000–1,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (1700, 2234); Relationships (6517)]

The records establish the stated rule and penalty association, but do not indicate that a particular driver failed to wear a seat belt or received a fine. [Data: Entities (1700); Relationships (6517)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required lighting applies during specified conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to use required lighting is described as not using, or not adequately using, vehicle lights between 6:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., or when weather or other conditions restrict visibility. The relationship record connects this violation to the stated fine range. [Data: Entities (2055, 2234); Relationships (7040)]

This entry identifies both a time window and low-visibility circumstances relevant to the rule. It provides no evidence of a specific lighting violation or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (2055); Relationships (7040)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalty covers specified prohibited overtaking
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed category concerns overtaking on a section displaying a no-overtaking sign applicable to the vehicle type, subject to the exception cited in Article 7, Clause 4. The data links this category to the 800,000–1,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (3515, 2234); Relationships (7289)]

A separate entry covers motorcycle or moped drivers overtaking where overtaking is not permitted, and its relationship record also specifies the same fine range under Article 7, Clause 4. [Data: Entities (3919, 2234); Relationships (7290)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improper vehicle avoidance is another linked violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes improper vehicle avoidance as avoiding another vehicle contrary to traffic regulations. A relationship record lists this violation among those subject to the 800,000–1,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (2624, 2234); Relationships (7288)]

The provided information does not define the circumstances of a particular event or show that anyone committed this violation; it records the category and its penalty association. [Data: Entities (2624); Relationships (7288)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe penalty rules, not observed compliance or enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Across the community, the evidence consists of descriptions of violations and relationships specifying the associated fine range. It does not identify drivers, reported incidents, enforcement actions, payment records, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (2234, 1700, 2055, 3515, 3919, +more); Relationships (6517, 7040, 7288, 7289, 7290)]

Accordingly, the community supports a summary of the listed regulatory associations, but not conclusions about actual compliance levels, enforcement frequency, or the prevalence of these violations.

v.tieu_de: Return of Altered Licenses and Certificates
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a remedial measure requiring altered licenses or practice certificates to be returned when their contents have been falsified. Individuals and organizations responsible for violations must carry out the measure, while authorized decision-makers implement it by forwarding the documents to the issuing authority or official. The available records describe a compliance process and its participants, but do not report specific cases, outcomes, or penalties. [Data: Entities (4200, 2655, 3442, 611, 2899); Relationships (2769, 7937, 9351, 8580, 8581)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it defines a connected remedial process for returning falsified credentials, although the records provide no evidence of particular cases or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The remedial measure is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Return of Altered Licenses and Certificates is the hub connecting the responsible parties, implementing decision-makers, and recipients of the documents. Its description specifies returning licenses or practice certificates that were erased or altered to falsify their contents and forwarding them to the issuer. [Data: Entities (4200); Relationships (2769, 7937, 9351, 8580, 8581)]

The measure has the highest listed degree among the entities, at 8, consistent with its central role in the relationships provided. [Data: Entities (4200, 2655, 611, 3442, 2899, 2900)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individuals and organizations that violate requirements are responsible for the measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Individuals who commit administrative violations are described as responsible for carrying out the required remedial measure when a license or certificate has been altered to make its contents inaccurate. [Data: Entities (2655); Relationships (7937)]

Organizations committing specified administrative violations are likewise required to carry out required remedial measures, including returning altered licenses or certificates; their description also states they must cease the violating conduct. [Data: Entities (3442); Relationships (9351)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorized decision-makers implement and route the measure
phat_hien.giai_thich: Authorized decision-makers implement the remedial measure and forward the altered license or certificate to its issuer. This assigns them a procedural role distinct from the responsibility placed on the individuals or organizations committing violations. [Data: Entities (611); Relationships (2769)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The document is returned to its issuing authority or official
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described process routes altered licenses or practice certificates to the competent authority that issued them. [Data: Entities (2899); Relationships (8580)]

The records also identify the competent official who issued the document as a recipient. They therefore describe two possible issuer destinations—an issuing authority or an issuing official—without specifying which applies in any particular case. [Data: Entities (2900); Relationships (8581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a procedural framework but not its real-world results
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions and relationships outline who is responsible for the remedial measure, who implements it, and where the altered documents are forwarded. [Data: Entities (2655, 611, 3442, 2899, 2900); Relationships (2769, 7937, 9351, 8580, 8581)]

No provided record identifies a specific violation, person, organization, enforcement outcome, or penalty. Accordingly, the evidence supports describing the process, but not assessing its frequency, effectiveness, or effects in particular cases. [Data: Entities (4200, 2655, 611, 3442, 2899, 2900); Relationships (2769, 7937, 9351, 8580, 8581)]

v.tieu_de: Article 20 Passenger-Vehicle Cargo Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on three traffic-safety violations involving goods in passenger vehicles: placing goods in the passenger compartment, securing luggage or cargo unsafely, and allowing luggage or cargo to fall onto the road. The records describe each as subject to the same fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng and connect them to administrative enforcement measures under Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The information concerns stated rules and penalties; it does not establish that a particular violation occurred or describe enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate-low because the records describe specific passenger-vehicle safety violations and a defined fine range, but provide no evidence about actual incidents, prevalence, or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three related cargo-handling violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies three distinct violations: placing goods in the passenger compartment, securing luggage or cargo unsafely, and luggage or cargo falling onto the road. The records link these categories as alternative violations subject to the same fine under Article 20. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937); Relationships (7615, 7614, 8632)]

These are descriptions of regulatory categories, not evidence that any driver or vehicle committed them. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A common fine range is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Each of the three violation descriptions states a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng. The relationships likewise characterize the violations as alternatives subject to the same fine under Article 20. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937); Relationships (7615, 7614, 8632)]

The provided records do not distinguish different fine amounts among these categories or specify other case-specific factors affecting the penalty. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 provides the enforcement framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity describing administrative penalties and driving-license point deductions identifies Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as addressing enforcement measures for drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles. Its relationships connect each of the three cargo-related violations to that framework. [Data: Entities (75); Relationships (164, 163, 162)]

The records do not specify the number of license points deducted, or establish that point deductions apply to each of these particular violations. [Data: Entities (75); Relationships (164, 163, 162)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules cover different stages of cargo handling
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The categories distinguish where goods are placed, how luggage or cargo is secured, and whether it falls onto the road. Together, these descriptions cover separate aspects of carrying goods in a passenger vehicle or similar vehicle. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937)]

This distinction is useful for understanding the scope of the listed violations, but the records do not provide operational guidance, technical standards, or examples of compliant cargo arrangements. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The information describes rules, not observed compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records identify violations, their stated fine range, and their connection to Article 20 enforcement measures. They do not identify people, organizations, vehicles, enforcement actions, or actual incidents. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937, 75); Relationships (164, 163, 162)]

Accordingly, the community supports an assessment of the described regulatory requirements, but not conclusions about compliance levels, safety outcomes, or the frequency of these violations. [Data: Entities (2394, 5270, 2937, 75); Relationships (7615, 7614, 8632)]

v.tieu_de: Driver Identification-Card Violations and Article 20, Clause 5 Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on two traffic violations involving driver identification cards: failing to use the required card and using another driver's card. Cargo-transport vehicle drivers are explicitly associated with both violation types, while the entity descriptions also specify passenger-car contexts for the failure-to-use and another-driver's-card offenses. Article 20, Clause 5 links the specified offenses to a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong. The provided information concerns legal compliance and penalties; it does not establish how often violations occur or indicate broader organizational, technical, or reputational issues.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate compliance significance because it describes multiple driver identification-card violations and an associated monetary penalty, but provides no evidence of their frequency or wider effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to use a driver identification card is a central violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The failure-to-use violation concerns not using a driver identification card to log required information while operating a vehicle. Its description covers cargo-transport business and passenger-car contexts, and the relationships specifically identify cargo-transport vehicle drivers as people who may commit it. [Data: Entities (2051, 717); Relationships (2996)]

Article 20, Clause 5 is linked to this violation and prescribes a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (2253); Relationships (7037)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Using another driver's card is represented as a separate violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data distinguishes use of another driver's identification card from failure to use one's own card. One entity describes the offense in a passenger-car context, while another specifies a cargo-transport vehicle driver using another driver's card for cargo-transport business. [Data: Entities (5322, 5323)]

The cargo-transport driver entity is explicitly associated with the cargo-specific version of this violation. [Data: Entities (717); Relationships (2997)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine applies to both specified violation types
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity specifies a range of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Article 20, Clause 5. Relationships connect that penalty to both failure to use a driver identification card and use of another driver's identification card. [Data: Entities (2253, 2051, 5322); Relationships (7037, 7323)]

The provided records state the penalty range but do not indicate how the amount is determined within that range or whether other consequences apply.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-transport drivers are the explicitly identified affected group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Cargo-transport vehicle drivers are described as drivers of trucks, tractors, and similar vehicles used to transport goods. The relationships identify this group as potential violators in both the failure-to-use case and the cargo-specific use-of-another-driver's-card case. [Data: Entities (717, 2051, 5323); Relationships (2996, 2997)]

The data does not quantify the number of drivers involved or establish actual incidents; it identifies the group and the violations to which it may be subject.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support a narrow compliance assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community's documented links concern driver identification-card conduct, cargo-transport drivers, and a statutory fine. These records support assessing the subject as a traffic-compliance matter, but they do not provide evidence about enforcement levels, violation frequency, organizational involvement, technical capabilities, or reputation. [Data: Entities (2051, 5322, 5323, 717, 2253); Relationships (7037, 2996, 2997, 7323)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Lane-Change Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6, Clause 2 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, described as setting a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified improper lane changes by drivers of cars and similar vehicles. Four linked violation types are covered: changing across more than one adjacent lane, changing without an advance signal, changing where lane changes are unauthorized, and changing without a safe distance. The provision expressly excludes violations specified at Article 6, Clause 5, Point G; the supplied data does not describe that exception in further detail. [Data: Entities (507, 2815, 2819, 2817, 2818, +more); Relationships (2391, 2394, 2395, 2396, 2397)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes a traffic-safety rule and monetary penalty, but the data establishes no actual violations, enforcement, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6, Clause 2 is the community's central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, Clause 2 is described as a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribing a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain improper lane changes by drivers of cars and similar vehicles. It is the hub of the supplied relationships, connecting the rule to four specified violation types and an exception. [Data: Entities (507); Relationships (2391, 2394, 2395, 2396, 2397)]

The supplied information identifies the provision and its stated penalty, but does not establish how frequently it is applied or whether any particular driver or incident is involved.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision covers four distinct lane-change violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The linked conduct includes moving across more than one adjacent lane in a single lane change, changing lanes without an advance signal, changing lanes at an unauthorized location, and changing lanes without maintaining a safe distance from nearby vehicles. Each is connected to Article 6, Clause 2 in the relationship records. [Data: Entities (2815, 2819, 2817, 2818); Relationships (2394, 2395, 2396, 2397)]

These descriptions distinguish the rule's stated categories of improper lane changing; the data does not provide further criteria for determining when a location is unauthorized or what distance is considered safe.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rule limits a lane change to an adjacent lane
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed violation is moving across more than one adjacent lane in a single lane change. Its entity description contrasts this conduct with the rule that each change may move only into an adjacent lane, and the relationship connects that violation to Article 6, Clause 2. [Data: Entities (2815); Relationships (2394)]

The record identifies this as a covered violation but does not specify additional procedural requirements or describe a real-world case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Advance signaling and an authorized location are also specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data separately identifies changing lanes without giving an advance signal and changing lanes where lane changes are not permitted as conduct subject to the fine listed under Article 6, Clause 2. [Data: Entities (2819, 2817); Relationships (2395, 2397)]

These are presented as separate categories in the supplied material. It does not give further details about signal timing, signage, or how permitted locations are designated.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Safe distance is a covered consideration, with an express exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, Clause 2 is linked to lane changes made without a safe distance from vehicles ahead, behind, or alongside. The data does not state a numerical distance threshold. [Data: Entities (2818); Relationships (2396)]

The provision is also described as expressly excluding violations specified at Article 6, Clause 5, Point G. That point is identified as an exception, but the supplied records do not explain its substance or which conduct it covers. [Data: Entities (519); Relationships (2391)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Administrative Violations and Corrective Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety, and the penalties and remedial measures that apply to them. One specified corrective measure requires a vehicle’s body to be adjusted to regulations, the vehicle to be reinspected, and its permitted cargo weight to be revised on its inspection certificate before the vehicle is used on the road. The information describes regulatory measures, not a specific violation or enforcement case. [Data: Entities (130, 76, 2974); Relationships (165, 428)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it concerns road-traffic safety and corrective requirements for vehicles, but the records describe rules rather than a specific incident or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns administrative violations of road-traffic order and safety
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative Violations in Road Traffic are defined as breaches of order and safety in road transportation, with applicable provisions prescribing administrative penalties and corrective or remedial measures. This establishes the community’s central subject as regulatory compliance in road transport. [Data: Entities (130)]

The records provide no specific violation, person, organization, or enforcement event. The findings therefore describe the stated scope of the rules, not evidence that a particular breach occurred. [Data: Entities (130)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalties and remedial measures are linked to the violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative Penalties and Remedial Measures apply to administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety. The relationship between these entities makes the consequences and corrective actions part of the same regulatory framework. [Data: Entities (76, 130); Relationships (165)]

The description attributes the relevant provisions to Article 3 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and says they cover administrative penalties, remedial measures, and revocation of licenses and professional practice certificates. No particular penalty or revocation is stated as having been imposed. [Data: Entities (76)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific vehicle adjustment and reinspection requirement is identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify Mandatory Vehicle Adjustment and Reinspection as a corrective measure associated with administrative violations in road traffic. The relationship states that vehicle adjustment, reinspection, and cargo-weight revision are specified corrective measures for these violations. [Data: Entities (2974, 130); Relationships (428)]

This is a defined compliance action in the provided information; the records do not establish that it was ordered for a particular vehicle or that any vehicle has completed it. [Data: Entities (2974); Relationships (428)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The corrective measure includes multiple steps before road use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified measure requires adjusting the vehicle body to comply with current regulations, having the vehicle inspected again, and revising the permitted cargo weight recorded on its technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate. These are the stated components of the measure. [Data: Entities (2974)]

The description says these actions must occur before the vehicle is used on the road. It does not provide further details about inspection procedures, deadlines, or which authority would carry them out. [Data: Entities (2974)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence describes a regulatory topic, not operational or reputational concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships concern road-traffic violations, administrative measures, and a vehicle-specific corrective requirement. They do not identify organizations or individuals, technical capabilities, reputational allegations, or a particular compliance case. [Data: Entities (130, 76, 2974); Relationships (165, 428)]

Accordingly, the community’s supported significance is its connection to road safety and vehicle compliance requirements; the records do not support conclusions about actual enforcement, rates of noncompliance, or impacts from a specific incident. [Data: Entities (130, 76, 2974)]

v.tieu_de: Goods-Vehicle Overloading Violation and Fine
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a defined goods-vehicle overloading violation and the monetary penalty prescribed for it. The violation concerns a load exceeding the permitted payload recorded in the vehicle’s technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate by more than 100% and up to 150%; the stated fine is 7,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The sole relationship in the data connects that fine to the violation. [Data: Entities (3495, 2224); Relationships (7265)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low-to-moderate because the data describe a specific transport violation and its monetary penalty but provide no evidence of broader community reach or impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A narrowly defined goods-vehicle overloading violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation applies to driving a vehicle transporting goods with a load exceeding the permitted payload stated in its technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate by more than 100% and up to 150%. The description also includes vehicles with trailers or semi-trailers. [Data: Entities (3495)]

The provided information defines the conduct and threshold, but does not identify a particular vehicle, driver, incident, or enforcement action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is 7,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describe a monetary penalty in the range of 7,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the specified overloading violation. [Data: Entities (2224, 3495)]

The relationship record confirms that this fine is prescribed for that violation. [Data: Relationships (7265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is directly linked to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community has one recorded relationship: the fine entity points to the overloading violation, with the relationship description stating that the fine is prescribed for it. This makes the penalty the sole explicitly connected counterpart to the violation in the supplied data. [Data: Relationships (7265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The threshold is tied to a recorded permitted payload
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation description measures excess load against the permitted payload recorded in the vehicle’s technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate. The stated range is more than 100% and up to 150% above that permitted payload. [Data: Entities (3495)]

No further thresholds, exceptions, or related penalties are included in the supplied records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to a rule and its stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records establish a described violation, a stated monetary penalty, and their direct relationship. They do not provide evidence about how often the violation occurs, actual compliance levels, enforcement outcomes, or effects on road safety. [Data: Entities (3495, 2224); Relationships (7265)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance can be assessed only in terms of the specific regulatory conduct and penalty represented here.

v.tieu_de: 600,000–800,000 Đồng Traffic Fine and Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a prescribed fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to several road-traffic violations. These include route-display violations, unsafe conduct involving stopped vehicles, restricted stopping or parking, driving three or more vehicles side by side, carrying too many people in a vehicle cab, and unsafe vehicle-door conduct. Clause 3 of Article 20 is specifically linked to the route-display violation and this fine range. The records describe penalties and violations, but do not establish actual incidents, enforcement outcomes, or compliance rates. [Data: Entities (2220, 5259, 923, 5264, 4783); Relationships (7257, 3432, 7258, 7256, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it connects one stated fine range to multiple traffic-safety and regulatory violations, while the data provides no evidence about actual incidence or enforcement.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single fine range anchors the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng, described as applying to several specified traffic violations. Its relationships connect it to multiple distinct violation categories, making the penalty the organizing point of this community. [Data: Entities (2220); Relationships (7257, 7012, 7258, 6474, 7256, +more)]

The records establish the stated fine and its listed associations, not the number of cases, how often the penalty is imposed, or whether any particular person or organization has violated these rules. [Data: Entities (2220); Relationships (7257, 7012)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Route-display violations are linked to Clause 3 of Article 20
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The route-display violation covers driving without displaying a route or displaying one that differs from the route authorized by the competent authority. The entity description states a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 đồng for this violation. [Data: Entities (5259); Relationships (7257)]

Clause 3 of Article 20 is separately identified as prescribing this fine for the route-display violation. The supplied records do not provide further detail about the broader legal framework or the application of this clause beyond that stated link. [Data: Entities (923); Relationships (3432)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Stopped-vehicle conduct and security are separately covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed violation involves leaving the driver’s position or turning off the engine while stopped, subject to stated exceptions for opening or closing a door, loading or unloading goods, or checking the vehicle. The relationship data links this conduct to the 600,000–800,000 đồng fine. [Data: Entities (5264); Relationships (7258)]

A separate violation concerns leaving the driver’s position while stopped without using the parking brake or another safety measure; its relationship also links it to the same fine range. These are recorded as distinct provisions, and the data does not establish that either conduct occurred in a specific case. [Data: Entities (2029); Relationships (7012)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restricted stopping and parking locations are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed locations include a bus-only lane, a drainage opening, telephone or high-voltage utility access openings, a designated firefighting water-access point, and a pedestrian crossing. The record links stopping or parking in these locations to the 600,000–800,000 đồng fine. [Data: Entities (4783, 2220); Relationships (7256)]

The supplied information identifies the locations and stated penalty but does not describe actual obstruction, resulting harm, or enforcement activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving in a formation of three or more vehicles is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes operating a vehicle in a side-by-side formation of three or more vehicles as a road-traffic violation. It links that violation to the 600,000–800,000 đồng fine. [Data: Entities (1667, 2220); Relationships (6474)]

No further details are provided about the circumstances, frequency, or consequences of this violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess passengers in a vehicle cab are linked to the same penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed violation is carrying more people in a vehicle cab than regulations allow. The entity description states that it is punishable by a fine of 600,000 to 800,000 Vietnamese đồng, and the relationship data connects it to the central fine entity. [Data: Entities (736, 2220); Relationships (3022)]

The records do not specify passenger limits, exceptions, or any particular enforcement case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unsafe vehicle-door conduct is another covered violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity describes opening a vehicle door or leaving it open without ensuring safety as a traffic violation. The relationship data links this conduct to the 600,000–800,000 đồng fine. [Data: Entities (5279, 2220); Relationships (7260)]

The supplied records do not describe an incident or its outcome; they establish only the conduct category and its stated penalty association.

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Registration Documentation and Permitted-Use Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns vehicle-registration documentation and permitted-use rules. Credit institutions and foreign bank branches may retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate; in the specified circumstances, drivers must carry an officially certified or authenticated copy and the institution’s or branch’s original receipt. The data also describes a failure-to-carry violation, a stated fine of 300,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese đồng, and registration or permitted-use violations involving certain vehicle owners and drivers. [Data: Entities (1137, 2303, 5468, 1947, 3444, 3140); Relationships (4020, 7389, 4017, 6898, 9353, 6899)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it links document-retention exceptions to driver obligations and stated fines, while the data does not establish broader or systemic impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration and permitted-use violations form the central issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s central topic is a set of road-traffic violations, including using a vehicle without a valid registration certificate or operating a temporarily registered or restricted vehicle beyond its permitted time, route, or scope. [Data: Entities (5468)]

The violation provisions are connected to both credit institutions and foreign bank branches in cases where they retain the original registration certificate. The relationships indicate that the rules specify supporting documentation for a vehicle to participate in traffic in these circumstances. [Data: Relationships (4020, 7389)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A documentation exception applies when a credit institution holds the original
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Credit institutions may retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate. In the circumstances described, the vehicle’s documentation can include an officially certified or authenticated copy of the certificate and the institution’s original receipt. [Data: Entities (1137)]

The driver-related provision specifies that the certified copy and original receipt must be carried to meet the stated exception when a credit institution holds the original certificate. [Data: Entities (1947); Relationships (4017)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign bank branches are covered by a parallel document arrangement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign bank branches may also hold or retain a vehicle’s original registration certificate. The specified supporting documents are an officially certified or authenticated copy and the branch’s original receipt, for the circumstances described in the decree. [Data: Entities (2303)]

The relationship to the failure-to-carry provision connects this arrangement to drivers’ documentation obligations when the branch holds the original. [Data: Relationships (6898)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to carry required documents has a stated monetary fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described Article 18 violation concerns operating a covered vehicle used for transport business without carrying its registration certificate, or without the specified certified copy and bank receipt when the original is held by a credit institution or foreign bank branch. The stated fine is 300,000 to 400,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1947)]

The data links this violation to motor-vehicle drivers, identifying drivers of covered vehicles as the people who may commit it by not carrying the required documentation. [Data: Relationships (6899)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described driver scope covers specified transport-business vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver entity covers people operating cars, motorized four-wheeled passenger vehicles, motorized four-wheeled cargo vehicles, trailers, semi-trailers, or similar vehicles used for transport business. [Data: Entities (3140)]

That scope is connected to the failure-to-carry violation, which concerns drivers’ possession of the required registration documentation. The provided information does not specify enforcement frequency or how often these violations occur. [Data: Relationships (6899); Entities (1947, 3140)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizations owning motorcycles and similar vehicles are also implicated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Organizations that own motorcycles, mopeds, or similar vehicles may be fined under the decree for the specified registration and permitted-use violations. [Data: Entities (3444)]

Their connection is to the broader category of vehicle registration and permitted-use violations, rather than specifically to the failure-to-carry provision described for covered transport-business vehicles. [Data: Relationships (9353); Entities (5468)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Administrative Penalty Limitation Framework
v.tom_tat: This community concerns how the limitation period for administrative penalties relates to whether a violation is completed or ongoing. Its central concept is Article 4, described as covering the limitation period under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, while a separate road-traffic concept specifies a one-year period for violations concerning road traffic order and safety in road transport. The records describe legal concepts and relationships, not a particular case, organization, or enforcement outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The framework has moderate importance because it addresses the time limits for imposing administrative penalties, including road-traffic violations, but the records identify no specific case or broader operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 4 is the central reference for limitation-period rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect Article 4 to both completed and ongoing administrative violations in the context of determining the limitation period for imposing penalties. This makes the status of the violation a key element of the described framework. [Data: Entities (431, 89, 3312, 1070); Relationships (1885, 1888)]

The Article 4 entity description also cautions that the label refers to provisions in two separate Vietnamese legal instruments, with different subject matter. [Data: Entities (431)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Completed and ongoing violations are distinct statuses
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A completed administrative violation is described as conduct that has ended, while an ongoing administrative violation is conduct that is still being committed or carried out. The records explicitly connect these two statuses as the categories addressed together in Article 4. [Data: Entities (1070, 3312); Relationships (3882)]

The distinction matters to calculating the limitation period, but the supplied information does not provide the detailed rules for identifying the relevant dates in an individual case. [Data: Entities (89, 1070, 3312); Relationships (231, 232)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated road-traffic limitation period is one year
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic-specific entity describes a one-year limitation period for administrative penalties concerning road traffic order and safety in the field of road transport. It states that this period applies to both completed and ongoing violations. [Data: Entities (88); Relationships (227, 229)]

The records provide this period as a rule description; they do not identify a particular violation or establish whether a penalty in any specific matter would be timely. [Data: Entities (88); Relationships (227, 229)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violation status is relevant to limitation-period calculation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general administrative penalty limitation period is described as depending on whether the violation has ended or remains ongoing. The relationships separately connect both statuses to that calculation. [Data: Entities (89, 1070, 3312); Relationships (231, 232)]

The material establishes the relevance of classification but does not spell out the full calculation method or address exceptions, so those details cannot be determined from these records. [Data: Entities (89, 1070, 3312)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Article 4 label could refer to two different legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 4 description distinguishes Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning limitation periods for administrative violations, from Article 4 of Law 36/2024/QH15, concerning the Government’s policy on road traffic order and safety. These are identified as separate provisions with different subject matter. [Data: Entities (431)]

Accordingly, references to “Article 4” should be read in context; the records do not support treating the two provisions as interchangeable. [Data: Entities (431)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a legal framework, not an enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships define violation statuses, limitation-period concepts, and their stated road-traffic application. They do not identify a person or organization subject to a penalty, a specific administrative proceeding, or a finding of legal compliance or non-compliance. [Data: Entities (3312, 1070, 431, 89, 88); Relationships (1885, 1888, 227, 229)]

Therefore, the material supports assessing the framework’s structure and stated scope, but not drawing conclusions about actual enforcement, reputation, or the conduct of any particular party. [Data: Entities (3312, 1070, 431, 89, 88)]

v.tieu_de: Article 21 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Cargo-Vehicle Traffic Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 21 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its links to cargo-vehicle traffic violations and related penalties. The listed violations cover cargo-document requirements, cargo placement and dimensions, and driving-license point deductions. The provided material gives an 800,000–1,000,000 đồng fine range for certain listed violations, but does not specify the point deduction amount or the full penalties for every violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the article’s practical importance for cargo-vehicle safety and regulatory compliance, while the provided records describe rules and penalties rather than a specific incident or entity posing an immediate threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 21 is the community’s central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 is connected to the listed cargo-vehicle violations and to the broader category of cargo-vehicle road-traffic violations, making it the organizing point of this community. Its described scope includes penalties and driving-license point deductions for drivers of trucks, tractors, trailers, and similar vehicles transporting goods. [Data: Entities (308, 713); Relationships (1203, 1211)]

The relationships identify individual violations addressed by the article, including cargo-document failures and improper cargo positioning or dimensions. The records do not provide the complete text of the regulation or establish how it is enforced in practice. [Data: Relationships (1204, 1205, 1206, 1212, 1216, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certain violations carry a stated fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description states that Article 21 sets fines of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain failures involving required cargo-transport documents and for carrying cargo on top of a vehicle bed, beyond its width, or more than 10% of its designed length beyond the front or rear. [Data: Entities (308)]

The relationships confirm that Article 21 specifies fines for several of these violations, including failure to provide access to document software and cargo extending beyond the vehicle bed’s width. The available material does not establish that this same fine range applies to every violation connected to the article. [Data: Relationships (1204, 1205, 1206, 1212, 1216, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo placement and dimensions are key safety-related concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed cargo-related violations include carrying goods on top of a vehicle bed, extending cargo beyond the bed’s width, and extending cargo more than 10% of the vehicle’s designed length beyond its front or rear. These descriptions identify specific loading conditions regulated by Article 21. [Data: Entities (729, 730, 731); Relationships (1204, 1205, 1206)]

The relationship for the overhang violation refers to a stated exception, but the supplied entity description does not explain that exception. Accordingly, the records support identifying the regulated condition, but not determining when the exception applies. [Data: Entities (730); Relationships (1205)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The document rules distinguish several forms of noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify operating a commercial cargo-transport vehicle without the required written document, operating without carrying it, and operating without a device capable of accessing the software that displays it. Article 21 is linked to each of these document-related violations. [Data: Entities (3314, 3315, 3316); Relationships (1216, 1217, 1218)]

A separate violation concerns a driver who has a device capable of accessing the software but fails to provide access to competent authorities when requested. This is distinct in the provided descriptions from operating without such a device. [Data: Entities (1932, 3315); Relationships (1212, 1217)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-license point deductions are identified, but not quantified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 is described as covering driving-license point deductions for certain goods-vehicle violations, and the article is linked to a dedicated point-deduction entity. [Data: Entities (308, 1712); Relationships (1211)]

The provided description specifically says it does not give the number of points deducted for the described overloading violation. The records therefore support noting that point deductions are part of the regulatory framework, but not assigning a deduction amount to a particular violation. [Data: Entities (1712); Relationships (1211)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory scope, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s entities and relationships concern a decree provision, categories of cargo-vehicle violations, and associated fines or license-point consequences. They do not describe a particular driver, enforcement action, accident, or compliance outcome. [Data: Entities (308, 713, 1712); Relationships (1203, 1211)]

The supplied information also does not establish an organization’s technical capabilities or reputation. The findings should therefore be read as a summary of the regulation and the listed violation categories, rather than as evidence about a specific actor or incident. [Data: Entities (308, 713); Relationships (1203)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Administrative Violations and Vehicle Custody
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Law on Handling Administrative Violations and its relationship to temporary custody of vehicles and related documents under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 4 of the decree directs that whether a violation is completed or ongoing be determined under the law, while the law provides a basis for temporary custody. The measure can apply to specified vehicle-driver violations and may be used before a penalty decision. The records describe legal and enforcement procedures, not evidence of a particular incident or misuse.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high impact because it describes legal rules that govern administrative penalties and can authorize temporary custody of vehicles and documents, but the records do not establish a specific enforcement incident or adverse outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law is the central legal authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Law on Handling Administrative Violations is the most connected entity in the community. It supplies the cited legal basis for temporary custody under Article 125 and is also the law to which Article 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP refers when determining whether a violation is completed or ongoing. [Data: Entities (2848, 435, 4865); Relationships (8499, 1899)]

The law’s described scope also includes the limitation period for penalties, authority to extend verification time, and return of altered licenses and certificates. These provisions indicate that its role reaches beyond custody to other stages of administrative enforcement. [Data: Entities (2848)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary custody is a defined enforcement measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Temporary custody of vehicles and related documents is described as a measure under Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It may be used in specified cases to verify facts needed for a penalty decision or to ensure that decision can be enforced. [Data: Entities (4865)]

The relationship data connects this measure to Article 125 of the law, which is cited as the basis for holding a vehicle and related documents before a penalty decision. The records describe a legal authorization and procedure, rather than establishing that custody occurred in any specific case. [Data: Entities (2848, 4865); Relationships (8499)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree incorporates the law’s test for violation status
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns limitation periods and the distinction between completed and ongoing administrative violations. It states that the status of a violation is determined under the Law on Handling Administrative Violations. [Data: Entities (435, 2848); Relationships (1899)]

The law’s description links that distinction to calculation of the limitation period for imposing penalties. This makes classification of a violation relevant to the timing of administrative enforcement, although the supplied records do not provide a specific example or calculation. [Data: Entities (2848, 435)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-driver violations are within the measure’s stated scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes an administrative violation by a vehicle driver as a separate entity, and the relationship data states that temporary custody is permitted to immediately prevent specified driver violations. [Data: Entities (111, 4865); Relationships (354)]

The custody description also says the procedure may apply when a driver cannot present required paperwork during an inspection. It further states that continuing to drive after the deadline for resolving the violation may result in a penalty as though the required documents were absent. These are described as procedural conditions, not findings about any individual driver. [Data: Entities (4865)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes connected penalty and enforcement stages
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records link violation classification, penalty timing, fact verification, temporary custody, and enforcement of a penalty decision. Together, they describe a framework in which legal classification and procedural steps inform how an administrative vehicle case may be handled.
