No specific operator, incident, enforcement outcome, or evidence of repeated conduct is identified in these records. Accordingly, the community’s significance is best assessed as regulatory and informational on the available evidence, rather than as proof of a particular safety event or pattern of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (3464, 5194, 3259); Relationships (9217, 9370)]

v.tieu_de: Motor-Vehicle Road-Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community is a small legal and regulatory classification centered on Motor-Vehicle Road-Traffic Violations, which is linked to two specific categories: Failure to Yield to an Oncoming Vehicle and Improper Avoidance of an Oncoming Vehicle. The descriptions distinguish the circumstances and scope of those categories, but the provided information does not specify penalties, enforcement outcomes, or broader operational impacts.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the community covers a limited set of traffic-violation classifications and provides no evidence about their frequency, penalties, or wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A general traffic-violation category anchors the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor-Vehicle Road-Traffic Violations is the broad category in this community. Its description identifies it as a category of road-traffic-rule violations by drivers of specified motor vehicles, addressed by Article 6 of the decree. [Data: Entities (3143)]

Both other entities are connected to this general category, making it the organizing concept in the supplied records. [Data: Relationships (7837, 7046)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to yield concerns specified road conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to Yield to an Oncoming Vehicle is described as a violation involving failure to yield where required on a narrow or steep road, or at a place with an obstruction. [Data: Entities (2065)]

The relationship record places this category within Motor-Vehicle Road-Traffic Violations. [Data: Relationships (7046)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improper avoidance is a separate classification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Improper Avoidance of an Oncoming Vehicle is described as failure to avoid an oncoming vehicle in accordance with regulations. Its description excludes the separately specified misuse of high-beam headlights. [Data: Entities (2595)]

This category is also identified as one of the road-traffic violations addressed by the decree. [Data: Relationships (7837)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The two specific categories have distinct descriptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions distinguish failure to yield in specified road conditions from improper avoidance under regulations. This supports treating them as separate classifications, while the records do not provide further criteria for how they may be applied in particular cases. [Data: Entities (2065, 2595)]

Both are linked to the same general motor-vehicle violation category. [Data: Relationships (7046, 7837)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is limited to classification, not enforcement or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify violation categories and their relationship to Article 6 of a decree, but provide no penalties, case examples, enforcement statistics, or jurisdictional details. The available material therefore supports describing the taxonomy, but not assessing how often these violations occur or what consequences they carry. [Data: Entities (2065, 2595, 3143); Relationships (7046, 7837)]

v.tieu_de: Alcohol-Test Refusal and Specialized Motorcycle Driver Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on refusal to undergo an alcohol concentration test, described as a road traffic violation involving a driver who does not comply with an on-duty official’s request. The records link that violation to a specified fine of VND 18,000,000 to VND 20,000,000 and identify a specialized motorcycle driver as a possible driver subject to the described rules and penalties. The information establishes a narrow regulatory relationship; it does not provide broader details about enforcement, legal status, technical capabilities, or reputation. [Data: Entities (4050, 2240, 4698); Relationships (7301, 9842)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but concrete regulatory significance because it connects a specified traffic violation and driver category to a substantial stated fine, while providing no evidence of wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Refusal of an alcohol concentration test is the central violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity describes a road traffic violation in which a driver does not comply with an on-duty official’s request to undergo an alcohol concentration test. The records do not provide further circumstances, such as where or how often this violation occurs. [Data: Entities (4050)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific monetary penalty is linked to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The stated fine is VND 18,000,000 to VND 20,000,000, and the relationship record says it applies to a driver who refuses to comply with the test request. This supports the existence of a stated penalty in the supplied data, but the records do not establish its current legal status or provide additional sentencing details. [Data: Entities (2240, 4050); Relationships (7301)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized motorcycle drivers are included in the described context
phat_hien.giai_thich: A specialized motorcycle driver is described as a person who operates a specialized-use motorcycle and is subject to applicable traffic rules, responsibilities, and penalties. The relationship record associates this driver category with the refusal violation; it does not establish that any particular driver committed it. [Data: Entities (4698, 4050); Relationships (9842)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community forms a compact violation–penalty–driver structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records connect the refusal violation to the specified fine and separately connect the violation to the specialized motorcycle driver category. Together, these links outline a concise regulatory relationship among conduct, penalty, and a driver type, rather than a broader network of organizations or individuals. [Data: Entities (4050, 2240, 4698); Relationships (7301, 9842)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to the stated rule and its associations
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records do not describe enforcement outcomes, compliance rates, named drivers, or wider effects. They also provide no information about technical capabilities or reputation; accordingly, no conclusions about those areas can be drawn from this community data. [Data: Entities (4050, 2240, 4698); Relationships (7301, 9842)]

v.tieu_de: Drivers and Phone Use While Driving
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of the driver of a motor vehicle and the violation of using a phone or other electronic device while driving. The relationship identifies the driver as the person who commits the violation while operating a moving vehicle on a road. The cited provision specifies a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 VND; the data provides no information about a particular driver, incident, or enforcement outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is modest because the community describes a road-safety violation with a specified monetary penalty, but contains only two entities and no evidence of a particular incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a driving violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central subject is using a phone or another electronic device while driving, described as a road traffic violation involving use of the device while operating a moving vehicle on a public road. [Data: Entities (5352)]

The graph connects this violation to a driver of a motor vehicle, with no other entities or relationships provided. [Data: Entities (1464, 5352); Relationships (6055)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver is the actor associated with the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver entity is described as a person operating an automobile, a motorized four-wheel passenger or goods vehicle, or a similar vehicle. [Data: Entities (1464)]

The sole relationship states that the violation is committed by a driver operating a moving vehicle on a road. It does not identify an actual driver or assert that a specific person committed the violation. [Data: Relationships (6055)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The cited provision specifies a monetary penalty

This gives it a defined public-sector function within the community, although the records do not provide details about its operational scope or activities in particular cases. [Data: Entities (1323)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Director leads the department and has specified enforcement powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The director is identified as the official who heads and leads the department. The entity description attributes to the director specified administrative sanctions and remedial measures, authority to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations, and the ability to revoke licenses or professional certificates for a fixed period or temporarily suspend activities, citing Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (1378); Relationships (5764)]

These are consequential administrative powers, but the records do not describe any particular exercise of them or establish whether any action was lawful or unlawful.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The department includes a professional division
phat_hien.giai_thich: A professional division is stated to belong to the department, linking the department’s organizational structure to a specialized unit. The provided information does not specify the division’s name, subject-matter remit, or operational responsibilities beyond its association with sanctioning authority. [Data: Entities (3904); Relationships (5767)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A professional-division head is also identified as having sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich: The head of a professional division is described as an official listed in Article 43 as having administrative-sanctioning authority. The relationship data confirms that this official heads a professional division belonging to the department. The records do not specify the full scope, limits, or instances of this authority. [Data: Entities (2429, 3904); Relationships (7675)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal authority, not a compliance or conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The descriptions cite Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and Article 43 as the basis for specified powers attributed to the director and professional-division heads. They provide no case records, audit findings, allegations, or other evidence about how these powers have been applied. Accordingly, the supplied information supports describing the stated legal framework but not drawing conclusions about compliance, misconduct, or actual effects. [Data: Entities (1323, 1378, 2429)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam People’s Public Security and Administrative Sanctions
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Vietnam’s People’s Public Security, a law-enforcement force whose designated officials and units are described as having administrative sanctioning powers under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. District-level police are part of the force, with district-level chiefs and heads identified as sanctioning authorities; police post and station heads are also listed. A related database concerns driver training and road-traffic-law refresher certificates within the People’s Public Security. The information establishes institutional responsibilities and a connection to administrative and data-management functions, but does not provide evidence of specific enforcement actions, compliance outcomes, or misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial institutional importance because it links a law-enforcement force and multiple levels of officials with administrative sanctioning authority and a related driver-training database.

phat_hien.tom_tat: People’s Public Security is the central institution
phat_hien.giai_thich:
People’s Public Security is described as a Vietnamese law-enforcement force whose designated officials and units may impose fines and other administrative penalties under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It is also the central entity linking the district-level police, specified police heads, and the driver-training database in the supplied relationships. [Data: Entities (3688); Relationships (5912, 6118, 9574, 9571)]

This supports the force’s significance as an enforcement and administrative institution. The records do not establish how often these powers are exercised or whether particular actions comply with applicable rules. [Data: Entities (3688)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: District-level police are part of the force
phat_hien.giai_thich:
District-level police are explicitly described as units within the People’s Public Security and as police authorities covered by the decree’s provisions. This connects the central force to a district-level organizational structure. [Data: Entities (1415); Relationships (5912)]

The records identify the district-level chief and the head of a district-level police unit in connection with that structure. They do not provide information about specific districts, personnel, or operational performance. [Data: Entities (814, 2441); Relationships (5909, 3184)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several police leadership roles are identified as sanctioning authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chief of district-level police is identified as an official authorized to impose administrative sanctions, and the head of a district-level police unit is also described as an authority empowered to impose administrative penalties. The records connect these roles to district-level police leadership. [Data: Entities (814, 2441); Relationships (5909, 3184)]

Police post heads and police station heads are separately listed among People’s Public Security officials authorized to impose sanctions under Article 43. The supplied information does not specify the precise scope or limits of each role’s authority beyond these descriptions. [Data: Entities (3812, 3817); Relationships (9571, 9574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a defined administrative enforcement function
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The source descriptions associate designated People’s Public Security officials and units with fines and other penalties for administrative violations under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. This indicates formal administrative enforcement responsibilities within the community. [Data: Entities (3688, 814, 2441)]

These records describe legal authority, not evidence that any particular person or unit has imposed a penalty, nor an assessment of the legality or fairness of any enforcement decision. [Data: Entities (3688, 814, 2441)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-training and refresher-certificate data is a related capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A database managed by the Ministry of Public Security concerns driver training and the awarding of certificates for road-traffic-law refresher instruction within the People’s Public Security. The relationship record links this database-related activity to the force. [Data: Entities (1490, 3688); Relationships (6118)]

This establishes a connection to information management for training and certification. The records do not describe the database’s technical architecture, access controls, data volume, or operational effectiveness. [Data: Entities (1490); Relationships (6118)]

v.tieu_de: Mobile Police Battalion and Commander
v.tom_tat: This community consists of the Mobile Police Battalion and its commander, linked by a leadership relationship. The supplied information identifies the commander as an authority under Article 43, Clause 3, with specified administrative enforcement powers, including fines up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese đồng, limited seizure authority, and specified remedial measures. The records describe legal powers but provide no information on their use, compliance outcomes, or broader reputation. [Data: Entities (3040, 3041); Relationships (8966)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it includes a police unit and a commander with defined administrative enforcement powers, while the data provide no evidence of how those powers have been exercised.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The commander is linked to the battalion through a leadership role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship record states that the Mobile Police Battalion is led by the Mobile Police Battalion Commander, connecting the two entities through an organizational hierarchy. It also associates the commander with applying specified remedial measures. [Data: Relationships (8966)]

The records establish this leadership link but do not describe the battalion’s wider structure, operational activities, or the commander’s identity beyond the role title. [Data: Entities (3040, 3041); Relationships (8966)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The commander has authority to impose administrative fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The commander is identified as an authority under Article 43, Clause 3, and is described as having the power to impose administrative fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (3041)]

The battalion description also places its commander among officials authorized under that clause to impose specified administrative penalties, including fines. The records describe authorization, not any particular fine imposed or violation handled. [Data: Entities (3040, 3041)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Seizure authority is subject to a stated value limit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The commander may seize objects and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. This is a defined limit on the seizure power described in the record. [Data: Entities (3041)]

No information is provided about any actual seizure, the procedures governing one, or enforcement beyond this stated value threshold. [Data: Entities (3041)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified remedial measures are part of the commander’s powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that the commander may apply remedial measures specified in the decree. The battalion-commander relationship also refers to the commander’s authority to apply specified remedial measures. [Data: Entities (3041); Relationships (8966)]

The provided information does not enumerate those measures, so their specific scope or practical effects cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (3041); Relationships (8966)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal authority but not compliance or performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available evidence describes the commander’s statutory enforcement powers and the commander’s leadership relationship with the battalion. It does not report whether the battalion or commander has exercised those powers, nor does it provide findings about legal compliance, misconduct, reputation, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (3040, 3041); Relationships (8966)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is grounded in its stated administrative authority; further conclusions about operational impact or conduct are not supported by the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3040, 3041); Relationships (8966)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 43: Public Security Sanctions and Vehicle Responsibilities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on “Article 43,” which refers to provisions in two different Vietnamese legal instruments. One provision concerns People’s Public Security officials’ administrative penalty authority, including a stated fine limit for on-duty officers; the other concerns responsibilities of vehicle inspection facilities, owners, and operators. The connected entities include Clause 1, the Department of Administrative Police for Social Order and its officials, and vehicle owners and operators. The records describe legal authority and responsibilities, but do not establish whether any entity has complied with or violated the provisions.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects administrative sanctioning powers and vehicle-related responsibilities, while the records provide no evidence of particular enforcement actions or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 43 refers to two distinct legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description distinguishes Article 43 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning the sanctioning authority of the People’s Public Security, from Article 43 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, concerning responsibilities of vehicle inspection facilities, owners, and operators. The shared article number should therefore not be treated as evidence that the provisions address the same subject. [Data: Entities (451)]

The relationships connect the Article 43 entity both to sanctioning officials and to vehicle owners and operators, reflecting this dual scope in the community data. [Data: Relationships (2074, 2067, 2070, 2071)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 1 describes a fine limit for on-duty officers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 1 is linked to Article 43 as the provision specifying officers’ fine-imposing authority. The entity description states that Clause 1 of Article 43 authorizes on-duty People’s Public Security officers to impose fines of up to 7,500,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (856); Relationships (2064)]

The relationship from Clause 1 to People’s Public Security officers also records that fine limit. The records describe an authorized maximum; they do not show that a particular fine was imposed. [Data: Entities (3679); Relationships (3327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department and its senior officials are associated with penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department of Administrative Police for Social Order is described as part of the People’s Public Security and as responsible for administrative policing and maintaining social order. Article 43 is linked to the department’s director as an official authorized to impose penalties. [Data: Entities (1325, 1379); Relationships (2067)]

The department is also connected to its director and to the head of a professional division, with the latter identified as an official empowered to impose administrative penalties. These records describe institutional roles, not evidence of any specific sanctioning decision. [Data: Entities (2430); Relationships (5770, 5771)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: On-duty officers have described sanctioning powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes both a general category of People’s Public Security officers performing official duties and a specific “People’s Public Security Officer on Duty” entity. Article 43 is linked to the on-duty officer category, while Clause 1 is linked to officers’ authority to impose fines up to 7,500,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (3678, 3679, 856); Relationships (2074, 3327)]

The on-duty officer description also mentions warnings and confiscation of violating items or vehicles up to a prescribed value limit. No value for that confiscation limit, nor any individual enforcement event, is provided in the records. [Data: Entities (3678)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle owners and operators are identified as having responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 is linked separately to motor vehicle and specialized motorcycle owners and operators, and the entity descriptions identify them as having responsibilities under Law No. 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (3092, 3093); Relationships (2070, 2071)]

The supplied records do not specify the detailed content of those responsibilities or indicate whether any owner or operator failed to meet them. The connection supports recognizing these groups as subjects of the provision, not drawing conclusions about their conduct. [Data: Entities (451, 3092, 3093)]

v.tieu_de: Department for Administrative Management of Social Order
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Department for Administrative Management of Social Order, its director, and divisions within the department. The supplied records describe the department and designated officials as having authority under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP to impose administrative sanctions; Article 43, Clause 6 specifically authorizes the director to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations. The entities also include specialist divisions covering weapons, explosives, support tools and fireworks, and conditional-business sectors and seals. The records describe legal authority and organizational roles, but do not establish actual enforcement activity or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (1321, 454, 1377, 1421, 1418); Relationships (5758, 5760, 5759, 2088)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial institutional importance because it is associated with administrative sanctioning authority, including the director’s power to confiscate objects and vehicles, alongside specialist public-order responsibilities.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The department is the community’s organizational hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department for Administrative Management of Social Order is linked to its director, a professional division, and two specialist divisions, making it the central organizational entity in the supplied network. The relationships identify these units as belonging to, or leading, the department. [Data: Entities (1321, 3903, 1421, 1418); Relationships (5758, 5763, 5760, 5759, 5757)]

This structure indicates a department with both leadership and specialized functions. The records do not provide staffing levels, operational capacity, or details about how the units coordinate, so those aspects cannot be assessed from the available information.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative sanctioning authority is a key function
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The department is identified as an authority with powers to impose administrative sanctions under Article 43. The description also identifies the director and chiefs of professional or specialist divisions among officials with sanctioning powers. [Data: Entities (1321, 454, 3903)]

This establishes a formal enforcement role in the community’s described scope. The supplied records do not specify the full range of sanctionable conduct, penalty amounts, or how often these powers are exercised.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The director has a specific confiscation power
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43, Clause 6 is described as authorizing the department’s director to confiscate objects and vehicles used in administrative violations. A relationship directly connects that provision to the Director of the Department for Administrative Management of Social Order. [Data: Entities (454, 1377); Relationships (2088)]

The department is also connected to its director in the organizational records, which describe the director as leading the department. The information establishes the stated authority but does not document any particular confiscation, case, or implementation outcome. [Data: Entities (1321, 1377, 1322); Relationships (5758, 5757)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialist divisions cover public-order-related areas
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One specialist division is described as responsible for guidance and management concerning weapons, explosives, support tools, and fireworks. The department-to-division relationship identifies it as a unit within the department. [Data: Entities (1421); Relationships (5760)]

A second specialist division is described as responsible for guidance and management of business sectors subject to security and public-order conditions, as well as seals. These descriptions indicate specialized subject areas, but the records do not detail technical systems, procedures, or the divisions’ specific operational capabilities. [Data: Entities (1418); Relationships (5759)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes legal powers, not performance or compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entity descriptions and relationships identify statutory authority, departmental structure, and areas of responsibility. They do not report specific enforcement actions, adjudicated disputes, violations by the department, or assessments of its legal compliance. [Data: Entities (1321, 454, 1377, 1421, 1418); Relationships (2088, 5758, 5760, 5759)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance can be assessed from the powers and functions described, but its reputation, effectiveness, and actual compliance record cannot be determined from these records alone.

v.tieu_de: Article 43 Amendment and Police Penalty Powers
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the amendment to Article 43 associated with Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP. The amendment is linked to officials across the Mobile Police and traffic-police structures, including unit commanders, the Mobile Police commander, the Traffic Police Department director, and police team leaders, whose described authorities include administrative penalties and, for some roles, remedial measures. Separate relationships connect battalion- and regiment-level units and a police team to their commanders. The records describe legal authority, but provide no evidence about its implementation, compliance outcomes, or alleged misuse.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the amendment’s broad significance for administrative enforcement powers across several police roles, while the records provide no evidence of misuse or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The amendment is the community’s central legal node
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The amendment is the hub of the recorded network, with relationships to six types of officials whose administrative penalty powers are specified or established under Article 43. The entity description characterizes it as an amendment in Article 14 of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP revising Article 43; the records do not provide further legal text or clarify the amendment’s implementation. [Data: Entities (178); Relationships (532, 549, 535, 551, 539, +more)]

Its central position makes the community relevant to understanding the allocation of administrative enforcement authority among the listed roles. The records establish the stated connections, but do not document enforcement activity or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Mobile Police commanders at multiple levels are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The amendment is linked to battalion- and regiment-level Mobile Police unit commanders, as well as the Mobile Police commander. The descriptions attribute administrative penalty powers to these roles, and describe specified remedial measures for the battalion-level commander and Mobile Police commander. [Data: Entities (635, 4061, 3042); Relationships (532, 549, 539)]

The battalion and regiment unit entities are separately linked to their respective commanders. These records establish organizational associations, but do not specify operational procedures or the circumstances in which the powers are exercised. [Data: Entities (634, 4060); Relationships (2828, 9850)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Company-level commander authority includes stated limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The company-level Mobile Police unit commander is described as authorized to issue warnings, impose fines up to 15,000,000 đồng, confiscate items or vehicles within a specified value limit, and apply certain remedial measures. The amendment is linked to this role as specifying its penalty powers. [Data: Entities (1035); Relationships (535)]

The record gives a monetary ceiling for fines but does not state the value limit for confiscated property or enumerate the remedial measures. The available information therefore supports describing the listed powers and stated limit, not a broader interpretation of their scope.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic-police and team leadership roles also have authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The amendment names the Traffic Police Department director and police team leaders among officials with administrative penalty powers. The director’s entity description also mentions remedial measures; the police team leader’s description says the leader is authorized to impose penalties and apply specified remedial measures. [Data: Entities (5027, 3820); Relationships (551, 545)]

A police team is linked to its leader, indicating a recorded organizational relationship. No specific fine limits or detailed list of measures for these roles is included in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3819); Relationships (9689)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network connects legal authority to organizational roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records combine links from the amendment to officials with links between units and their commanders: the battalion-level unit is connected to its commander, the regiment-level unit to its commander, and the police team to its leader. This shows that the described legal powers are associated with both command positions and organizational structures. [Data: Relationships (532, 549, 2828, 9850, 9689)]

The records do not provide names of individual officeholders, staffing details, or evidence about how authority is delegated in practice. The community is therefore best understood as a map of roles and stated powers rather than a profile of particular people.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied evidence is about authority, not compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe an amendment, police roles, organizational links, and administrative penalty powers. They contain no allegations, compliance findings, enforcement statistics, reputation assessments, or technical-capability information. [Data: Entities (178, 4060, 635, 5027, 3042, +more); Relationships (532, 549, 535, 551, 539, +more)]

Accordingly, the records support assessing the community’s institutional and legal significance, but do not support conclusions about whether the powers have been exercised lawfully, effectively, or improperly.

v.tieu_de: Mobile Police Regiment and Its Commander
v.tom_tat: The community consists of a mobile police regiment and the officeholder who commands it. The commander is described as having authority to impose penalties under Article 43, and the sole recorded relationship states that the commander leads the regiment. The data establishes an enforcement-related role but does not describe particular penalties, their use, or the legal-compliance record of either entity.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has potential public significance because the commander is described as authorized to impose penalties, but the supplied data documents only two entities and one relationship.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The commander leads the regiment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The only recorded relationship connects the commander of a mobile police regiment to the Mobile Police Regiment and states that the commander leads it. This makes the command link the defining structural feature of the community. [Data: Relationships (3584)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The commander is associated with penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich: The commander entity is described as an officeholder with authority to impose penalties under Article 43. The data does not specify the circumstances, procedures, or kinds of penalties involved. [Data: Entities (1010)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regiment is identified by its command function
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Mobile Police Regiment is described as a regiment whose commander is listed as having authority to impose penalties. No further information about the regiment's operations, size, or other functions is provided. [Data: Entities (3044)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a narrow organizational structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied community data contains two entities and one relationship, linking the commander to the regiment. It does not identify additional people, organizations, or connections, so the documented network is limited to this command relationship. [Data: Entities (1010, 3044); Relationships (3584)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal compliance and use of authority are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data refers to authority under Article 43, but it provides no information about how that authority is exercised or whether either entity has been subject to a compliance assessment. The record therefore supports identifying the stated authority, but not conclusions about compliant or noncompliant conduct. [Data: Entities (1010, 3044)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial Social-Order Police Division and Its Head
v.tom_tat: The community consists of a provincial-level police division responsible for the administrative management of social order and the head of that division. The recorded relationship identifies the head as the division’s leader, while the head’s description states that Article 43 authorizes the role to impose penalties. The data describe institutional responsibilities but provide no information about specific enforcement actions, compliance history, or misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it combines a provincial police function with a stated penalty-imposing authority, but the records provide little evidence about its activities or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial police division with an administrative social-order remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Division of Police for Administrative Management of Social Order is described as a division within provincial-level police responsible for the administrative management of social order. This establishes its stated institutional function and level of operation. [Data: Entities (1434)]

The records do not detail particular operations or outcomes, so the scope of its practical impact cannot be assessed from this information alone. [Data: Entities (1434)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division and its head are directly linked
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed relationship states that the officeholder leads the corresponding provincial-level division. This makes the division and its head the two connected entities in the community. [Data: Relationships (5939)]

No other organizational, personal, or external connections are provided in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (1434, 2457); Relationships (5939)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The head is described as authorized to impose penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The head’s entity description states that the role is authorized under Article 43 to impose penalties. This indicates a formal enforcement power associated with the position. [Data: Entities (2457)]

The records do not specify which penalties may be imposed, the circumstances for imposing them, or whether the authority has been exercised. [Data: Entities (2457)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Leadership is the only recorded relationship
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole supplied relationship identifies the head as leader of the division, with no additional relationships listed. The available community structure is therefore limited to the division and its leadership link. [Data: Entities (1434, 2457); Relationships (5939)]

This limited structure does not establish how the division interacts with other agencies, individuals, or members of the public.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and reputation cannot be assessed from these records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions state the division’s remit and the head’s stated authority, but include no allegations, findings, or compliance information. Accordingly, these records do not support conclusions about misconduct, legal compliance in practice, or reputation. [Data: Entities (1434, 2457); Relationships (5939)]

Further evidence about decisions, enforcement activity, or oversight would be needed to assess those matters.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam People's Public Security and Mobile Police
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Vietnam’s People’s Public Security, with the Mobile Police as a subordinate force and company- and battalion-level units connected through its command structure. The records describe statutory administrative-penalty powers, including fines, confiscation, and certain remedial measures, as well as road-traffic enforcement and legal-knowledge checks. These materials establish significant public enforcement authority, but do not document specific enforcement outcomes, misconduct, or independent reputation assessments. [Data: Entities (3673, 3039, 1034, 1011); Relationships (8961, 3642, 3587, 8553)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial public-safety and administrative-enforcement responsibilities, while the provided records do not establish harmful conduct or specific adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: People’s Public Security is the community’s institutional center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
People’s Public Security is described as Vietnam’s public security and law-enforcement force, with responsibilities that include road-traffic enforcement and related administrative functions. It is connected to the Mobile Police, officer groups, police teams, enforcement actions, and legal-knowledge checks, making it the broadest institutional hub in the supplied network. [Data: Entities (3673); Relationships (8961, 8553, 3898, 9543, 9544)]

The records describe a formal enforcement role rather than a private or informal network. They do not, however, provide specific enforcement cases or outcomes from which to assess how these powers were exercised in practice. [Data: Entities (3673); Relationships (3898, 9552)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Mobile Police is a subordinate force with defined responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Mobile Police is identified as a force within People’s Public Security. The supplied records state that, within its assigned functions and duties, it may sanction specified administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (3039); Relationships (8961)]

Its internal structure is represented through company- and battalion-level units and their commanders, as well as the Mobile Police commander. This places enforcement authority within a hierarchy rather than attributing all powers to a single role. [Data: Entities (3039, 1034, 1011, 637, 636); Relationships (3642, 3587, 2832)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative-penalty powers vary by official and level
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe different authority limits under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Specified on-duty People’s Public Security officers may issue fines up to 500,000 đồng, while the Mobile Police description identifies a company-level commander limit of 15,000,000 đồng and a Mobile Police commander limit of 75,000,000 đồng. These are role-specific limits, not a single force-wide fine ceiling. [Data: Entities (3673, 3039)]

Depending on the official’s authority under the decree, the described measures also include remedial actions, confiscation of objects or vehicles, temporary revocation of permits or professional certificates, and temporary suspension of activities. [Data: Entities (3039, 1011, 3673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Company-level unit heads have specified sanction and confiscation authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A company-level Mobile Police unit is described as subordinate to the Mobile Police, and its head is identified as a role with administrative-penalty authority. The stated fine limit for the company-level commander is up to 15,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (1034, 2428, 1036, 3039); Relationships (3642, 3641, 3639)]

The company-level unit description specifies that its head may confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 30,000,000 đồng. This is distinct from the separate description of specified on-duty People’s Public Security officers’ confiscation authority for items valued at no more than 15,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (1034, 3673, 1083)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network includes road-safety knowledge checks and enforcement support
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify checking knowledge of laws concerning road-traffic order and safety as a task performed by People’s Public Security officers. Both commissioned and noncommissioned officers are connected to this task. [Data: Entities (2883, 3674, 3676); Relationships (8553, 8554, 8555)]

People’s Public Security is also described as carrying out road-traffic enforcement, with Traffic Police able to coordinate patrol and control operations with other units that may be mobilized and equipped according to their assigned tasks. This indicates a wider operational context, although the supplied records do not give details of particular patrols or deployments. [Data: Entities (3673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish legal powers, not a misconduct or reputation finding
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information focuses on institutional roles, legal authority, and specified enforcement functions. It provides no case-level evidence of misconduct, unlawful enforcement, or adverse outcomes, and it does not contain independent reputation assessments; no such conclusion should be inferred from the existence of sanctioning powers. [Data: Entities (3673, 3039, 1034, 1011); Relationships (8961, 3898)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance here is its documented public-safety and administrative-enforcement remit. Assessing implementation or compliance in practice would require evidence beyond the role and authority descriptions supplied. [Data: Entities (3673, 3039); Relationships (8553, 3898)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial Police Licensing and Suspension Authorities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on license revocation or temporary suspension as an administrative sanction measure, linked to the provincial traffic police division and the provincial administrative management of social order division. Each division’s head is identified as holding sanctioning authority. The traffic division head is also described as responsible for entering related driving-licence point-deduction data when a provincial-level People’s Committee chairperson issues an administrative penalty decision. The records describe administrative roles and powers, but do not establish that a particular sanction was imposed or assess compliance in any specific case. [Data: Entities (2896, 3983, 2467, 3944, 2466); Relationships (8578, 8577, 7708, 7707)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s meaningful regulatory impact through provincial officials’ authority over license-related sanctions, while the records provide no evidence of a specific enforcement action or adverse outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: License revocation or temporary suspension is the central measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s central subject is an administrative sanction described as revoking the right to use a license or professional certificate for a specified period, or temporarily suspending an activity. This identifies a potentially consequential regulatory tool, but the supplied information does not specify a case, affected person, or actual sanction decision. [Data: Entities (2896)]

The measure is linked to both the provincial traffic police division and the provincial administrative management of social order division through descriptions identifying their heads among officials with sanctioning authority. [Data: Relationships (8578, 8577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial traffic police division has a sanctioning role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provincial traffic police division is described as a province-level police division responsible for traffic policing, and its head is included among officials with sanctioning authority. Its relationship to the license revocation or temporary suspension measure connects traffic-policing functions with the stated administrative sanction. [Data: Entities (3983); Relationships (8578)]

The records do not provide details on the scope of an individual decision, procedures, or a specific enforcement outcome; conclusions beyond the stated institutional role would therefore be unsupported. [Data: Entities (3983, 2896); Relationships (8578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic division head has an additional driving-licence data responsibility
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The head of the provincial traffic police division is identified as the division’s leader and as an official with sanctioning authority. [Data: Entities (2467); Relationships (7708, 8578)]

The entity description further states that when the provincial-level People’s Committee chairperson issues an administrative penalty decision, this head is responsible for entering the related driving-licence point-deduction data into the relevant database. This indicates a stated administrative data-entry function associated with that decision process; the records do not describe the database or any particular entry. [Data: Entities (2467)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Social-order administration division is also linked to the sanction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provincial administrative management of social order division is described as a provincial-level police division, and its head is included among the listed sanctioning authorities. The division is linked to license revocation or temporary suspension as one of the measures associated with that authority. [Data: Entities (3944); Relationships (8577)]

Its head is separately identified as leading the division, with a relationship record confirming that leadership connection. No additional duties or specific enforcement actions are described for this official in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (2466); Relationships (7707)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish institutional powers, not a specific compliance or conduct finding
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information describes a sanction measure, the divisions associated with it, and the relevant officials’ stated roles. It contains no case-level facts showing that a license was revoked or an activity suspended, and it provides no evidence of misconduct, procedural compliance, or noncompliance. [Data: Entities (2896, 3983, 2467, 3944, 2466); Relationships (8578, 8577, 7708, 7707)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is best understood as administrative and regulatory: the listed authorities are associated with consequential licensing measures, while the records do not support claims about how those powers were exercised in practice. [Data: Entities (2896, 3983, 3944); Relationships (8578, 8577)]

v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact importance because it links a provincial police division to a leader described as having authority to impose penalties, while the records provide no evidence of specific enforcement actions or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division and its head form a compact leadership structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The two listed entities are the provincial-level Mobile Police Division and its head. The relationship record states that the officeholder leads the division, establishing the central organizational link in this community. [Data: Entities (2465, 3043); Relationships (7706)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The head is described as having penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich: The head's description states that the officeholder is authorized under Article 43 to impose penalties. phat_hien.tom_tat: The division is identified as provincial-level mobile police
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Mobile Police Division is described as a division within provincial-level police. [Data: Entities (3043)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific compliance or enforcement outcomes are documented
phat_hien.giai_thich: Although the head is described as authorized to impose penalties, the data provide no cases, findings, or other outcomes that would establish how the authority is used or whether the division or its leadership has faced compliance concerns. Accordingly, no conclusion about actual compliance or misconduct is supported by the available records. [Data: Entities (2465, 3043); Relationships (7706)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Reputation and technical capabilities are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records identify the division and its leader but contain no information about public reputation, technology, equipment, or specialized technical capabilities. v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it includes a police department and an officeholder authorized to impose penalties, while the records provide no details about the authority’s scope or use.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A three-level administrative structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify the department, a professional division within it, and the head of that division. phat_hien.tom_tat: The division head is associated with penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich: The head of a professional division is described as having authority under Article 43 to impose penalties. The records do not specify which penalties may be imposed, the circumstances in which the authority applies, or whether it has been exercised. [Data: Entities (2431)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The professional division sits within the police department
phat_hien.giai_thich: The professional division is explicitly described as part of the Department of Police for Administrative Management of Social Order. This organizational relationship is also stated directly in the relationship record. [Data: Entities (3905, 1336); Relationships (5785)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The officeholder leads the professional division
phat_hien.giai_thich: The named role is an officeholder who leads a professional division, rather than a separately identified individual. phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and operational details are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the department’s administrative role and the division head’s stated penalty authority, but provide no information about specific cases, enforcement practices, legal compliance outcomes, or public reputation. [Data: Entities (1336, 2431, 3905); Relationships (7676, 5784, 5785)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024/ND-CP Article 43 Penalty Authority
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 43 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and the police departments, professional-unit heads, and other officials it identifies as authorized to impose administrative penalties. The network links the provision to administrative and traffic police functions, provincial and district-level police positions, and the National Population Data Center and its director. The records describe statutory authority and organizational responsibilities; they do not provide evidence about particular enforcement actions, compliance outcomes, or reputational concerns. [Data: Entities (1279, 92, 3207, 1381); Relationships (238, 4929, 4918, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because Article 43 connects administrative penalty authority to numerous police leadership roles and functions, including national, provincial, and district-level bodies.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 43 is the community’s central authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as setting out the authority of the People’s Public Security to impose administrative penalties and identifying officials whose positions confer that authority. It is the central node connecting the listed offices and roles. [Data: Entities (1279); Relationships (238, 4926, 4927, 4928, +more)]

The information supplied establishes the scope of the provision as represented in these records, but does not set out penalty amounts, procedures, appeal mechanisms, or implementation outcomes. [Data: Entities (1279)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative Police Department for Social Order has a prominent role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Administrative Police Department for Social Order is linked to Article 43 through the authority of its professional-unit heads and the inclusion of the National Population Data Center director among authorized officials. The department’s professional units include functions concerning weapons and explosives, and conditional security-and-order businesses and seals. [Data: Entities (92, 1329, 1328); Relationships (238, 239, 240, 241, 242)]

These links indicate that the described authority spans several administrative-policing functions. The records do not specify how often these officials exercise penalty authority or what enforcement results have followed. [Data: Relationships (238, 239, 240, 241)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic Police professional leadership is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 is connected to heads of Traffic Police professional departments, including units responsible for traffic data management and digital transformation, traffic accident investigation and resolution, vehicle registration and inspection, driver licensing, traffic control and escort, and road and railway patrol and control. [Data: Entities (1327, 1332, 1333, 1334); Relationships (4909, 4912, 4913, 4914, 4915, +more)]

The listed responsibilities show that the provision’s described reach includes both operational traffic functions and related administrative or data functions. The records do not describe technical systems, data safeguards, or the departments’ actual enforcement practices. [Data: Entities (1327, 1331, 1332, 1333, 1334)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authority is assigned across multiple levels and units
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify heads of provincial police divisions, including the provincial administrative police division for social order, as well as a district-level police chief and the head of a regiment-level Mobile Police unit as authorized to impose penalties under Article 43. [Data: Entities (3945, 1416, 2450, 2474); Relationships (4918, 4922, 4927, 4931)]

This points to a distributed structure spanning provincial and district-level positions as well as a mobile police unit. It establishes the roles identified in the source data, but does not clarify delegation rules, oversight arrangements, or how authority is divided in individual cases. [Data: Relationships (4918, 4922, 4927, 4931)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The National Population Data Center is linked to penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 is described as including the director of the National Population Data Center among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties. The center is separately identified as a national population-data institution, and a relationship record states that its director leads the center. [Data: Entities (3207, 1381); Relationships (4917, 4929, 5851)]

The supplied information establishes this institutional connection but does not explain the circumstances in which the director may exercise the authority or specify any data-related enforcement capability beyond the center’s population-data role. [Data: Entities (3207, 1381); Relationships (4917, 4929)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal authority, not compliance or performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material provided concerns the roles and organizational relationships associated with Article 43. It contains no claims about unlawful conduct, compliance failures, public reputation, individual enforcement cases, or the effectiveness of the listed offices. [Data: Entities (1279, 92, 3207); Relationships (238, 4929, 4926)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance is supported by the breadth of positions and functions linked to administrative penalty authority, while conclusions about implementation quality or specific impacts would go beyond the available evidence. [Data: Relationships (4911, 4918, 4927, 4928, +more)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial Traffic Police Division and Its Head
v.tom_tat: This community consists of the provincial-level Traffic Police Division and its head, connected by the head’s leadership of the unit. The division organizes road-traffic legal-knowledge tests and has a role in receiving examination applications; its head is described as having specified authority to impose penalties and restore driving-licence points. The records indicate a public-administration and traffic-enforcement function, but provide no information about actual enforcement outcomes, performance, or controversy. [Data: Entities (5029, 2468); Relationships (7709)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it is associated with traffic-law testing and specified enforcement powers, although the records describe only two connected entities and do not establish broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division is the community’s central operational entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Division is a provincial-level police unit and is described as organizing tests on legal knowledge of road-traffic order and safety. Its stated responsibilities give it a direct role in traffic-related administration. [Data: Entities (5029)]

The sole listed relationship connects the division to its head, identifying that official as its leader and linking the unit to the testing function. [Data: Relationships (7709)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The head’s authority combines leadership and specified legal powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The head is described as leading the provincial-level division and overseeing the organization of the legal-knowledge tests. This places the official at the center of the division’s stated testing responsibilities. [Data: Entities (2468); Relationships (7709)]

The entity description also says that, under Article 43, the head is authorized to impose penalties and, in cases covered by Clause 3 of Article 51, to restore driving-licence points. The records do not specify particular cases or outcomes. [Data: Entities (2468)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division participates in examination-application processing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The division may receive examination applications directly. The description also states that commune-level police forward valid applications to it, indicating a described route for applications to reach the provincial unit. [Data: Entities (5029)]

The source material does not provide application volumes, processing timelines, or details about decisions on individual applications; no conclusions about efficiency or access can therefore be drawn from these records. [Data: Entities (5029)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community’s documented functions concern traffic-law administration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The division’s stated testing subject is legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety, while the head’s described powers include imposing penalties and restoring licence points in specified cases. Together, these functions indicate a role spanning testing and certain enforcement-related decisions. [Data: Entities (5029, 2468)]

The relationship record confirms the head’s leadership of the division but does not establish any additional operational or institutional connections. [Data: Relationships (7709)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information supports a limited assessment of conduct and reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provided records describe organizational responsibilities and legal powers, but contain no allegations, findings of misconduct, or reputation assessments. They therefore support describing the community’s stated administrative role, not making a judgment about the conduct or compliance of the division or its head. [Data: Entities (5029, 2468); Relationships (7709)]

The material also does not report technical systems, resources, or enforcement results. Any assessment of operational capability beyond the listed functions would require additional evidence. [Data: Entities (5029, 2468)]

v.tieu_de: Police Station Chief and Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the relationship between a police station and its chief, whose assigned authority includes imposing specified administrative penalties for road-traffic violations. The material also describes a police station located in an export processing zone and states that, in the specified border-gate or export-processing-zone context, the chief may impose fines up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong. The authority is limited to the provisions and duties described.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns an official enforcement role with authority to impose specified administrative penalties, but the stated powers are limited in scope and include a defined fine ceiling.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The chief leads the police station
phat_hien.giai_thich: The police station chief is described as the person who leads the police station referenced in Article 41. This establishes the central organizational link between the enforcement body and the official exercising the specified authority. [Data: Entities (3816, 3815); Relationships (9688)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authority to impose specified road-traffic penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chief is authorized to impose administrative penalties for specified violations involving road-traffic order and safety, within assigned duties and responsibilities. The administrative-penalty entity describes the action as covering violations specified in cited points and clauses of Article 9. [Data: Entities (3816, 84); Relationships (220)]

The supplied material identifies this as a defined enforcement power; it does not establish authority beyond the violations and provisions it names. [Data: Entities (3816, 84)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine ceiling is 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich: Under the description of Article 43, clause 3, the police station chief may impose fines of up to 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong in the specified context. This is a stated upper limit, not an indication that this amount applies to every violation or penalty. [Data: Entities (3816, 3815)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority is bounded by assigned duties and cited provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The chief’s powers are expressly limited to the violations and remedial measures specified in the applicable provisions and to the scope of the chief’s assigned functions, duties, and responsibilities. The community description therefore supports a bounded enforcement role rather than unrestricted sanctioning authority. [Data: Entities (3816, 3815); Relationships (220)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An export processing zone is linked to the police station
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The export processing zone is described as a designated economic zone where a police station may be situated, and the relationship record states that the text describes a police station located in such a zone. [Data: Entities (1913, 3815); Relationships (6847)]

The supplied information does not identify a particular station or export processing zone, or provide details about enforcement activity at a specific location. [Data: Entities (1913); Relationships (6847)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Provincial-Level Police and Sanctioning Authorities
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s provincial-level police and the officials and divisions associated with their administrative sanctioning authority. The provincial police director leads the force and is described as having powers to impose administrative penalties and remedial measures; chiefs of specified administrative-management, traffic, and mobile police divisions also have penalty-imposing authority. The described sanctions include fines, time-limited license or certificate revocation, and suspension of operations. The records give fine ceilings of 37,500,000 and 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong, with one description explaining these as potentially reflecting individual and organizational limits where applicable. The community therefore represents a consequential public-administration and enforcement function, but the supplied data identifies no specific enforcement incident, legal violation, or misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the significant public impact of provincial police administrative enforcement powers, while the records provide no evidence of a specific harmful incident or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial-level police are the community’s organizational center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial-Level Police is the central entity connecting the director, division chiefs, and specialized provincial police departments or divisions. The records describe these officials and units as part of, or associated with, the provincial-level force and its sanctioning framework. [Data: Entities (3989, 3990, 2436, 3976); Relationships (9815, 9816, 7682, 9805, 9810)]

This structure indicates that the relevant authority is distributed across a provincial organization rather than being attributed only to one office-holder. The data describes formal roles and powers, not the operation of any particular provincial force or an individual enforcement case. [Data: Entities (3989, 2434, 3991); Relationships (7680, 7681, 7679, 9799, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provincial police director has broad administrative sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The director is described as leading the provincial-level police force and exercising administrative sanctioning powers under Article 43. Those powers include warnings, fines, specified remedial measures, and confiscation of exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations. [Data: Entities (3990, 1376); Relationships (9815, 5850)]

The description of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP specifically associates the director with fines up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong and specified remedial measures. The records describe statutory authority; they do not establish how frequently or in what cases these powers have been exercised. [Data: Entities (1376, 3990)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fine ceilings differ across the descriptions and require legal-context qualification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records cite fine ceilings of both 37,500,000 and 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong. The Provincial-Level Police description cautions that the figures may arise from different provisions or versions of the rules, while the director description says they can reflect individual and doubled organizational limits where the applicable rules provide for higher organizational fines. [Data: Entities (3989, 3990, 1376)]

Accordingly, the supplied material does not support treating either amount as a universal ceiling for every violation or proceeding. The applicable limit depends on the relevant legal authority and circumstances, as described in the records. [Data: Entities (3989, 3990)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified division chiefs also hold penalty-imposing authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify heads of provincial divisions responsible for administrative management of social order, traffic policing, and mobile policing among officials authorized to impose administrative penalties. They also describe these heads as able to apply remedial measures under the cited authority. [Data: Entities (2433, 2435, 2436, 3991, 3964)]

The associated departments and divisions are linked to Provincial-Level Police, including the provincial Traffic Police Department, the department for administrative management of social order, and the Provincial Mobile Police Division. These links establish their organizational association, not additional powers beyond those described in the entity records. [Data: Entities (3962, 3964, 3980, 3982); Relationships (7681, 9810, 9797, 9799, 9808)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctions include restrictions on licenses and business operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The director’s listed powers include revoking licenses or professional practice certificates for a specified period and suspending specified activities for a specified period. The dataset represents these as distinct sanction types: time-limited license or professional certificate revocation and time-limited suspension of operations. [Data: Entities (3990, 4958, 4962); Relationships (9818, 9819)]

These measures show that the described authority extends beyond monetary penalties to temporary restrictions on professional or operational activity. The records do not specify particular recipients, cases, or the conditions triggering these sanctions. [Data: Entities (3990, 4958, 4962)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe formal authority, not verified conduct or compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material focuses on organizational roles and powers under cited provisions. It contains no specific allegations, enforcement case, finding of legal noncompliance, or evidence about how the authorities have used their powers. [Data: Entities (3989, 3990, 1376, 2436)]

Several entity entries describe closely overlapping titles for provincial police directors and division heads. They are best read as role descriptions in the supplied dataset, rather than as evidence of multiple distinct office-holders or independently verified institutions. [Data: Entities (3990, 1376, 2434, 2436, 3976); Relationships (9815, 5850, 9816, 9805)]

v.tieu_de: Commune-Level Police and Administrative Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on commune-level police and the officials who lead them: the Commune-Level Police Chief and Head of Commune-Level Police. The relationships identify the chief as the leader of the police unit and place the role at the commune administrative level. The supplied descriptions outline administrative enforcement powers for specified road-traffic violations under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, as well as a local role in receiving and forwarding certain examination applications. The records give differing fine limits under different cited provisions, so the applicable limit depends on the governing authority and context.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it connects local police leadership with specified traffic-enforcement powers and an examination-application process, while the records do not establish broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commune-level police leadership is the community's organizing link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Commune-Level Police Chief is described as heading a commune-level police force or unit, and the relationship records explicitly connect the police to its chief. A separate relationship places the chief at the commune administrative level. [Data: Entities (1033, 1031, 1026); Relationships (3621, 3607)]

The Head of Commune-Level Police is also described as leading the local police authority and being authorized to penalize specified violations within assigned jurisdiction. These records indicate closely related leadership roles, but do not establish whether the two titles refer to the same individual or office in every context. [Data: Entities (2440); Relationships (3624)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated enforcement remit concerns specified road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe commune-level police chiefs as having administrative penalty powers for specified road-traffic violations, within their assigned functions and duties. The authorities cited include Articles 41 and 43 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (1033, 1031, 2440); Relationships (3621, 3624)]

The descriptions characterize these as bounded powers rather than an unrestricted enforcement mandate: their application is tied to specified violations and the official's assigned scope. [Data: Entities (1033, 1031, 2440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records state different maximum fine amounts under different authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Commune-Level Police Chief description gives a maximum fine of 37,500,000 đồng in one stated context and cites Article 43, Clause 3 as setting a 2,500,000 đồng maximum in another. It cautions that the applicable limit depends on the governing provision. [Data: Entities (1033)]

The Commune-Level Police description also states a fine limit of up to 37,500,000 đồng within the unit's assigned functions and duties. These descriptions should be read with their stated legal contexts rather than treated as a single universal limit. [Data: Entities (1031)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional measures include seizure, confiscation, and other authorized remedies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chief's described powers include seizing objects or vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 đồng under Article 43, Clause 3, and confiscating exhibits or vehicles where authorized under Clause 4. [Data: Entities (1033)]

The same description also identifies possible temporary revocation of specified permit or professional-certificate rights, suspension of certain activities, and application of authorized remedial measures. The records condition these powers on legal authorization and assigned scope. [Data: Entities (1033); Relationships (3621)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commune-level police have a described role in examination applications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Commune-Level Police description states that offices receive examination applications from people applying through the authority responsible for their place of residence. For valid applications, they provide appointment information according to published schedules and forward applications to the Traffic Police Division no later than one working day after receipt. [Data: Entities (1031)]

This establishes an administrative service function alongside the described traffic-enforcement role; the supplied records do not provide application volumes, processing outcomes, or performance assessments. [Data: Entities (1031)]

v.tieu_de: Police Post Chief and Administrative Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community concerns a police post and the officials associated with it. The Police Post Chief is described as heading the post and having authority to penalize specified road-traffic administrative violations, apply specified remedial measures, and seize objects or vehicles used in violations when the stated value limit is met. A separate entity, Head of Police Post, is also described as leading a police post and having penalty authority; the records do not establish whether this is a distinct official or another name for the chief. The information describes legal powers but does not establish how they are exercised or whether any compliance or misconduct issues exist.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it describes public officials with administrative enforcement and limited seizure powers, but provides no evidence of their actual use or of broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police Post Chief is the central enforcement official
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Police Post Chief is described as heading the Police Post and as authorized, within assigned functions and duties, to impose administrative penalties for specified violations. The relationship records likewise connect the chief to leadership of the post and to enforcement responsibilities. [Data: Entities (3811); Relationships (9683, 9686)]

The records establish a formal role and described authority, not the chief’s identity, conduct in specific cases, or the practical extent of enforcement.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty authority is limited to specified road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Police Post Chief may impose administrative penalties for the specified road-traffic violations referenced in the source material. The violations are described as particular provisions concerning road-traffic order and safety, rather than as an unrestricted power over all violations. [Data: Entities (4725); Relationships (9686)]

The Police Post entry further describes a maximum fine of 2,500,000 Vietnamese dong and specified remedial measures for the chief. These records describe the scope of authority but do not show how often it is used. [Data: Entities (3810, 3811)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Seizure authority has a stated value threshold
phat_hien.giai_thich:
