The authority that previously granted approval is identified as responsible for suspending the activity, while competent Vietnamese authorities handle violation cases. This is a stated enforcement mechanism; the records do not document a specific violation, suspension, or enforcement outcome. [Data: Entities (1067, 4837); Relationships (3877, 3878)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A results report is due within 10 days after program completion
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After the program concludes, a written report of the results of the foreign-vehicle activity must be sent to the authority that issued the permit no later than 10 days afterward. The report follows Form No. 04e in Appendix IV to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (4816, 3912); Relationships (9753)]

The records link program completion to the start of this reporting period for the vehicle-entry arrangements. They establish a deadline and reporting requirement, but do not indicate whether any report has been submitted or whether a deadline has been missed. [Data: Relationships (7446, 9753)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a regulatory framework, not an observed risk event
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s connections focus on approval, travel procedures, reporting, violation handling, and suspension. They show how participants and businesses are governed, but provide no specific incident, identified noncompliant participant, or evidence of actual harm. [Data: Entities (2340, 2357, 5550, 5585, 4837); Relationships (7519, 7560, 10490)]

Accordingly, the community is significant as a cross-border administrative and compliance system, while any assessment of a particular operator’s conduct or reputation would require evidence beyond these records. [Data: Entities (2340, 5550, 1067)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Ministry of Public Security Traffic Governance
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security (MPS), with the Minister of Public Security holding extensive rulemaking responsibilities and the Ministry coordinating traffic governance, police-related licensing, foreign-vehicle administration, and public services. Its stated technical remit includes centrally managed road-traffic databases, connected information systems, an online service portal, and a citizen mobile application. The records describe statutory and administrative responsibilities, not findings of misconduct or evidence assessing how effectively those responsibilities are carried out. [Data: Entities (3019, 3001, 3023, 839); Relationships (8732, 8845, 8889, 4230)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high institutional importance because the Ministry combines national traffic-policy coordination, substantial regulatory authority, and management of extensive traffic and licensing information systems.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry is the central coordinating authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS is described as the Government’s focal agency for unified state management of road-traffic order and safety. It coordinates implementation with other ministries and sectors, leads relevant international cooperation, and assists the Government with negotiating and signing treaties and agreements. [Data: Entities (3019, 4105, 3227); Relationships (8864, 8852, 8750)]

This combination of domestic coordination and international engagement gives the Ministry a broad institutional role. The provided information establishes the scope of its mandate, but does not evaluate the quality or outcomes of its coordination. [Data: Entities (3019, 3006); Relationships (8864, 8852)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Minister has extensive regulatory and procedural authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister of Public Security is the head of the MPS and is assigned responsibilities for prescribing rules across traffic-related areas. These include driver licensing and examinations, vehicle registration plates, examiner qualifications and training, vehicle inspection standards for vehicles managed by the Ministry, accident-investigation procedures, and traffic patrol and violation handling. [Data: Entities (3001, 414, 1608, 1609); Relationships (8732, 1761, 6357, 6359, 6398)]

The Minister also sets rules for traffic command centers and specified monitoring and technical systems, as well as police escorts for domestic delegations and foreign guests. The minister is not identified by name in the supplied material. [Data: Entities (3001); Relationships (8732)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic databases and information sharing are a major technical capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS is responsible for building, centrally managing, operating, maintaining, and upgrading the road-traffic order and safety database and related specialized databases. The described information includes vehicle registration, driver training and testing, licences, violations, accidents, licence-point changes, and certain vehicle journeys and driver images. [Data: Entities (3019, 1243, 1665, 1511, 4511); Relationships (4230, 6473, 6163, 8878)]

The Ministry’s systems are described as connecting with other agencies’ databases to exchange information, including insurance, registration, inspection, accidents, and penalties. This indicates substantial data-management and interagency coordination responsibilities; the records do not specify security controls, retention practices, or system performance. [Data: Entities (3019); Relationships (4230, 6473)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry administers digital channels for public services and notifications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS Public Service Portal is described as a channel for submitting notices, applications, examination applications, and registration dossiers. It also provides access to shared information from the road-traffic database and a means to deliver administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts. [Data: Entities (3023); Relationships (8845)]

The Ministry also manages and operates a citizen mobile traffic application. The supplied descriptions say the application can be used to report relevant changes and, in the broader Ministry remit, to support real-time reporting concerning foreign-vehicle convoy activities. [Data: Entities (839, 4990, 3019); Relationships (3303, 8889)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police forces and their drivers are subject to specialized rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister prescribes aspects of driver training, testing, licensing, and minimum-age requirements for police forces performing security or national-security duties. Police vehicles used for urgent duties are described as priority vehicles that may use priority signal devices in emergencies, with the Ministry directing functional units responsible for specified device management. [Data: Entities (3807, 3803, 2378, 3211); Relationships (8856, 8734, 8733, 7582)]

The source also distinguishes certain police-force inspection, training, licensing, certification, and operator information from specified databases and responsibilities assigned to the Ministries of Transport and Construction. This describes an allocation of administrative scope, not a general exemption from traffic governance. [Data: Entities (3807, 3019); Relationships (8856)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicles and international representatives are within the Ministry’s remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS manages a database concerning foreign motor vehicles driven by foreigners in Vietnam, coordinates relevant procedures with other ministries, and is responsible for inspecting and addressing specified violations involving organizations or individuals arranging such travel. [Data: Entities (2316, 4092, 3019); Relationships (7426, 8860, 1756)]

The Ministry must notify relevant diplomatic, consular, and intergovernmental representative offices about specified violations, accidents, or incidents. The records establish these notification and coordination duties but do not report particular incidents or indicate that any office or individual violated the rules. [Data: Entities (4151, 1363, 1102); Relationships (8867, 3945, 5831)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examiner and driver-testing processes are formally regulated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving examiner training, eligibility, qualifications, and examiner-card issuance are identified as matters governed by requirements prescribed by the Minister. Driving test centers are also subject to national technical regulations. [Data: Entities (1608, 1609, 1607, 4297); Relationships (6357, 6359, 6355, 8869)]

The material also specifies a theoretical legal-knowledge test for certain licence classes: it lasts 26 minutes, has 45 questions, requires a score of at least 41, and includes a disqualifying question whose incorrect answer results in failure. These are stated testing rules; no pass-rate or implementation data is provided. [Data: Entities (4933); Relationships (8884)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a broad legal remit but do not establish compliance outcomes or adverse reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material cites Law 36/2024/QH15, Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, and Ministry instruments including Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA in connection with the Ministry’s responsibilities and traffic rules. It therefore supports describing a formal regulatory framework, rather than determining whether the Ministry or related parties have complied with every requirement. [Data: Entities (3019, 3001, 414, 184, 412); Relationships (1762, 565, 1756, 6613)]

No allegations, enforcement outcomes, independent audits, or reputation assessments are included in the supplied records. Accordingly, the community’s importance rating reflects the scale of its described public authority and information systems, not an inference of wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (3019, 3001, 3023)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police Department and Regulatory Operations
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Traffic Police Department, with the Director, professional divisions, and division heads connected to its operational and enforcement functions. The Department processes specified vehicle-entry and traffic-related applications, administers legal-knowledge examinations and related data systems, issues certain permits, and exercises administrative-sanctioning authority. Its activities also connect foreign diplomatic and consular bodies, central-level agencies, and local People’s Committees. The material describes formal responsibilities and powers, but does not establish how consistently they are carried out or provide evidence of actual compliance outcomes or violations. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2432); Relationships (5861, 9750, 9211, 3058, 9540)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the Department combines national-level permitting, examination, data-management, and enforcement responsibilities with coordination across government and foreign applicants.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A central government department with broad operational responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Department is described as a department of Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security and as a channel for reporting implementation issues to the Ministry. Its remit spans administrative applications, traffic-related permits, examinations, data administration, and enforcement, making it the community’s central institution. [Data: Entities (5026)]

Multiple professional divisions are identified as belonging to the Department, including divisions focused on vehicle registration and inspection, driver training and licensing, traffic patrol and control, and data management and digital transformation. This indicates a functionally differentiated structure, although the supplied information does not detail the divisions’ staffing or operational performance. [Data: Entities (1432, 1420, 1422, 1419); Relationships (9750, 5934, 5914, 5915, 5913)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Director is a key point of authority and accountability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director heads the Department and is assigned responsibility for overseeing implementation of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA, including monitoring, guiding, inspecting, and urging implementation. The Director also organizes research and the application of science and technology and manages legal-knowledge examinations on road traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (1385, 2556, 4173, 2884); Relationships (5861, 5856, 5859, 5857)]

The Director also manages and operates the administrative-violation database and has authority to restore driving-licence points in specified cases. The role is described by office title rather than personal name, so the supplied records do not identify an individual office-holder. [Data: Entities (1385, 2951); Relationships (5858)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application processing connects the Department with foreign applicants and agencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Applications to bring right-hand-drive cars into Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes are submitted to the Department through the Ministry of Public Security public service portal, by post, or directly. For valid and complete applications under the relevant procedure, the Department is described as issuing a written approval or refusal within five working days. [Data: Entities (3256, 5026); Relationships (9211)]

Foreign consular agencies, diplomatic missions, and representative offices of intergovernmental international organizations may provide diplomatic notes or official dispatches explaining the reasons and purposes for vehicle participation in traffic. These records establish procedural links, but do not indicate the number of applications, their outcomes, or any specific applicant’s conduct. [Data: Entities (1101, 2304, 2305, 2730); Relationships (3944, 7390, 7392, 8036)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department holds significant permitting and intergovernmental coordination roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department issues, reissues, and revokes permits for signal devices on eligible priority vehicles registered to central-level ministries, sectors, and agencies, subject to a stated exception for military vehicles on urgent missions. It also issues operating permits for intelligent transport vehicles, except those serving national defense purposes. [Data: Entities (5026, 753, 754, 1272); Relationships (4514, 3058, 3059)]

For specified application approvals, the Department distributes decisions to relevant authorities for coordination, including relevant provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees. This gives its administrative decisions a coordination function beyond the applicant and the Department itself. [Data: Entities (5026, 3671); Relationships (9540)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative-sanctioning powers are substantial but bounded by cited legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, the Department’s Director and heads of professional divisions have specified administrative-sanctioning authority. The Director’s listed powers include fines up to 75 million Vietnamese đồng, confiscation of objects or vehicles involved in violations, temporary permit or certificate revocation, suspension of operations, and designated remedial measures. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2432, 3906)]

The records describe legal authority, not its exercise in particular cases. They provide no case-level evidence of sanctions, procedural errors, or the Department’s overall legal compliance; the authority should therefore not be treated as proof of either misconduct or effective enforcement. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2432)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examination and administrative data systems create technical responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department organizes training and issues examiner cards for legal-knowledge tests on road traffic order and safety. The Director is responsible for research, development, administration, maintenance, and upgrading of examination software, and for managing the related administrative-violation database. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 2884, 2951); Relationships (5857, 5858, 5859)]

Test computers connect over the Ministry’s WAN to a server hosted by the Department; the system supports testing and stores connection and data-editing logs. These details indicate operational dependence on networked systems and recorded activity, but the supplied information does not describe security controls, incidents, access policies, or system reliability. [Data: Entities (5026)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Regulatory procedures include refusal and suspension grounds, with outcomes not documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described amendment to Article 33 under Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP addresses approval procedures for foreign motor vehicles entering Vietnam for tourism and right-hand-drive cars used for non-tourism purposes, as well as grounds for refusal, notification, and suspension. The Department is linked to submission of related dossiers. [Data: Entities (182, 3256); Relationships (560)]

Legal-violation cases, including alleged violations by foreign nationals or breaches of previously approved conditions, are identified as possible grounds for refusal or suspension by the competent authority. The records do not provide particular cases or establish that any applicant or entity has committed a violation. [Data: Entities (2879); Relationships (8545)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community’s importance is institutional; evidence of realized impact is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department’s combination of application review, permit issuance, examination administration, violation-data management, and sanctioning authority supports a high assessment of institutional importance. Its links to national ministries, foreign missions, and local government bodies further indicate a broad administrative reach. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385, 753, 2305, 3671); Relationships (3058, 3059, 7392, 9540)]

However, the supplied records are descriptions of entities, responsibilities, and relationships rather than performance metrics, enforcement case histories, security assessments, or documented public impacts. The rating therefore reflects the scope and significance of the functions described, not a finding of harmful conduct or operational failure. [Data: Entities (5026, 1385); Relationships (5861, 9211, 3058)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Foreign-Vehicle Road Traffic and Tourism
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s regulation of foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers using Vietnamese roads. It connects foreign nationals and visitors, licensed Vietnamese international travel service businesses, organizations and individuals seeking to use right-hand-drive cars, and competent authorities that approve and oversee permitted travel. The framework covers applications, routes and travel periods, immigration and residence requirements, reporting, and responses to violations or incidents. The information describes a broad legal and administrative system, not evidence of misconduct by the entities involved. [Data: Entities (5538, 2326, 5548, 3439, 2652); Relationships (7476, 10693, 3697, 7477, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high operational importance because it concerns nationwide road safety, cross-border vehicle movements, foreign visitors, and multiple layers of Vietnamese authorization and enforcement, though the supplied data does not establish wrongdoing.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vietnam is the regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnam is the central jurisdiction linking the activities and actors in this community. The described rules govern foreign vehicles entering, traveling within, and leaving the country, and cover both tourism-related trips and specified non-tourism use of right-hand-drive vehicles. [Data: Entities (5538, 2319, 3439, 2652); Relationships (7440, 9346, 7931, 7543, +more)]

The legal framework described includes road-traffic rules and penalties, immigration and temporary-residence requirements, and responsibilities assigned to public bodies. Its reach makes the community significant for public administration and traffic safety; the supplied data does not establish a specific incident or adverse outcome. [Data: Entities (5538, 2326); Relationships (7476, 3697, 7453)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Travel businesses organize and report on foreign-vehicle tourism
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Licensed Vietnamese international travel service businesses may arrange tourism trips in which foreign visitors bring foreign-registered vehicles into Vietnam, subject to approval by a competent authority. The businesses also have responsibilities for organizing trips and managing participating visitors and vehicles, including arranging traffic guidance where required. [Data: Entities (5548, 2348, 2338); Relationships (10693, 7477, 7457, 7441, 7514)]

These businesses must report activity results to the permitting authority. They may be refused further approval if they violate previously approved terms, and a proposed schedule or route may be grounds for refusal when it relates to security or political activities. [Data: Entities (5548); Relationships (10696, 10409)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign nationals’ travel and driving are conditional
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign nationals may participate in the described vehicle trips only within the authorized scope, routes, and travel periods, and must comply with Vietnamese traffic and other applicable laws. The rules also address required travel and driving documentation, entry and residence requirements, and, where applicable, travel in a convoy. [Data: Entities (2326, 2325, 2317); Relationships (7476, 7472, 7461, 7453)]

The travel-service business may need to invite and guarantee foreign participants unless they are visa-exempt. A trip may be suspended if participants violate Vietnamese law and have not completed the competent authority’s requirements for resolving the violation. [Data: Entities (2326, 5548); Relationships (7477, 7454)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-tourism use of right-hand-drive cars has a separate approval pathway
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies both organizations and individuals seeking to bring right-hand-drive cars into Vietnamese traffic for purposes other than tourism. Their activities are subject to approval provisions, and the relevant descriptions also require compliance with security and public-order laws. [Data: Entities (3439, 2652, 4260, 4258); Relationships (9346, 7931, 9350, 7936)]

The framework distinguishes this category from tourism trips organized by international travel service businesses. The supplied information establishes that approval requirements apply, but does not provide evidence about the number of applications, approvals, or vehicles involved. [Data: Entities (3439, 2652, 2348); Relationships (9344, 7929, 10693)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorities control routes, timing, and border movements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent Vietnamese authorities grant permission for the described vehicle operations and specify the permitted scope, routes, and times. Foreign vehicles may also be required to use approved international border gates for temporary entry and departure. [Data: Entities (1042, 2735, 1809); Relationships (3697, 8044, 6737, 3696)]

The approval process can take account of the proposed schedule, route, or roads in relation to security or political activities. These controls indicate that decisions about vehicle movement are coordinated with broader public-order considerations. [Data: Entities (4630, 1042); Relationships (10408, 10409, 3697)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violations and incidents can affect travel and vehicle status
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign nationals and drivers are required to comply with Vietnamese law, and the described framework assigns authorities responsibilities for managing violations and traffic accidents. Certain violations can lead to an approved trip being suspended until requirements for resolving the violation are met. [Data: Entities (2326, 2325, 5538); Relationships (7476, 7453, 7454)]

The source description also identifies re-export of a foreign-plated vehicle as a possible consequence for certain violations. If an unforeseen incident prevents departure and cannot be resolved immediately, a foreign national or vehicle may qualify for a limited additional stay of up to 10 days under the stated conditions. [Data: Entities (5456, 5234, 2326); Relationships (10670, 10621, 7475)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes convoy reporting, but no broader technical profile is established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes foreign motor-vehicle convoy activity as monitored and reported in real time through a mobile application. This supports a limited observation about an operational reporting mechanism; it does not establish the application’s technical design, security, or capabilities beyond the stated monitoring and reporting function. [Data: Entities (2314); Relationships (7420)]

The same material describes traffic guidance and identifying logos or flags for convoy vehicles in relevant circumstances. These are operational coordination measures rather than evidence of a broader technology platform. [Data: Entities (2319, 2853, 4089); Relationships (7436, 7461)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied information is regulatory, not reputational evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe legal requirements, administrative responsibilities, approval conditions, and possible consequences. They do not provide substantiated allegations, findings of misconduct, or independent assessments of the reputation of Vietnam’s authorities, travel businesses, drivers, or other participants. The community’s importance should therefore be assessed from the scope of the regulated activity, not inferred adverse conduct. [Data: Entities (5538, 5548, 2326); Relationships (10693, 7476, 10696)]

v.tieu_de: Driving-Licence Point Notifications and Public Service Portal
v.tom_tat: This community describes a citizen-facing process for notifying drivers about deducted or restored licence points and recording restored-point status. The driving-licence point restoration procedure is connected to the Public Service Portal and Traffic Application for electronic notifications, while a separate mobile application is identified as Ministry of Public Security-developed and operated. The information also covers status updates and a distinct notification process for point deductions. Electronic delivery depends on required infrastructure and technical or information conditions, so the data describes available channels rather than confirming universal availability. [Data: Entities (3999, 1704, 4989, 3046, 4196, +more); Relationships (6528, 9820, 6530, 6529, 6525, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has notable public-service importance because it connects a formal driving-licence procedure with citizen notification and status-update channels, although the data does not establish operational reach or adverse impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A formal procedure links restored-point notification and status updates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driving-licence point restoration procedure is described as the process under Clause 3 of Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP for restoring points when a licence has lost all its points. The record states that the procedure includes notifying the licence holder and updating the licence’s restored-point status. [Data: Entities (1704)]

The relationships identify both notification and status updating as steps in that procedure. This makes the process more than a delivery channel: it also encompasses recording that points have been restored. [Data: Relationships (6529, 6525)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Public Service Portal is a central electronic channel
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Public Service Portal is described as an online government platform for submitting applications and required documents, including operating-permit applications. Its record also describes registered accounts as a channel for electronic driving-licence point notifications, subject to necessary infrastructure, technical capabilities, and information conditions. [Data: Entities (3999)]

The relationships connect the portal to the restoration procedure, restored-point notifications, and point-deduction notifications. This makes it a shared channel for both types of point-related notice in the represented community. [Data: Relationships (6528, 9820, 6305)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restoration notices have multiple delivery options
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A restored-point notification is described as a formal notice to the driving-licence holder. It may be delivered directly, by postal service, or electronically through the holder’s registered account on the Public Service Portal or Traffic Application. [Data: Entities (4196)]

The relationships specifically connect restored-point notifications to both the portal and the Traffic Application. The records therefore show a mix of offline and electronic channels, without establishing that every channel is available in every case. [Data: Relationships (9820, 9966)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two mobile application records describe notification capabilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Application is described as a mobile-device application that can provide electronic notifications about restored points and, where the required technical infrastructure is available, may deliver administrative-violation documents. The restoration procedure and restored-point notification are both linked to this application. [Data: Entities (4989); Relationships (6530, 9966)]

Separately, the Mobile Traffic Application is described as developed, managed, and operated by the Ministry of Public Security. Subject to required infrastructure, technical, and information conditions, it enables citizens to receive electronic notices, including notices about deducted points. The data gives these two application records different descriptions and does not establish whether they refer to the same product. [Data: Entities (3046); Relationships (6304)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restored-point status can be updated through recorded channels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driving-licence status update is described as updating information to show that points have been restored. The record identifies publication on the Traffic Police Department’s website and, for licences represented as data messages, updates in the citizen’s electronic identification account as examples of such updates. [Data: Entities (1705)]

The relationship to the restoration procedure establishes that this status update is part of the process. The records do not specify timing, completeness, or the implementation status of these updates. [Data: Relationships (6525)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point-deduction notices are distinct from restoration notices
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The point-deduction notification is described as a formal notice that points have been deducted from a citizen’s driving licence. It may be delivered in writing, by post, or electronically through a registered Public Service Portal account or mobile traffic application account. [Data: Entities (1565)]

The relationships identify the Public Service Portal and Mobile Traffic Application as electronic channels for this notice. This distinguishes the deduction-notice pathway from the restoration procedure while showing that both use digital channels. [Data: Relationships (6305, 6304)]

v.tieu_de: Educational Institutions and Road Safety Education under Decree 151/2024
v.tom_tat: This community centers on educational institutions as the setting for legal education about road traffic order and safety. Article 4 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is linked to the institutions and to lower-secondary students, while institution-student relationships extend the described instruction to primary, lower-secondary, and high-school learners. The material includes age-specific safety content, such as helmet use and safe handling of bicycles, mopeds, and motorcycles; it also states that student compliance may inform conduct assessment. The records describe an education framework, not measured outcomes or evidence of actual compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects a decree-based educational framework with institutions serving multiple student groups on road safety and legal awareness.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Educational institutions are the community's central delivery point
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Educational institutions are described as settings for legal knowledge and education about road traffic order and safety, with responsibility for organizing legal-awareness and information activities for people under their management. Their relationships connect them to multiple student groups and to road safety education, making them the central hub of the community. [Data: Entities (1728); Relationships (6603, 6607, 6602, 6608, 6599)]

The records cover preschools, schools, upper-secondary schools, vocational institutions, and other educational establishments. This indicates a broad institutional scope, but the data does not quantify participation or demonstrate how consistently instruction is delivered. [Data: Entities (1728)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 4 provides the cited regulatory connection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 4 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is identified as a provision concerning legal education on road traffic order and safety in educational institutions. The relationship data links the article to educational institutions and specifies legal education content for lower-secondary students. [Data: Entities (433); Relationships (1892, 1893)]

The available records establish the provision's stated subject and connections, but do not provide further detail about enforcement, institutional compliance, or penalties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described education reaches multiple school-age groups
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships identify primary school students, primary school pupils, lower-secondary students, lower secondary school students, and high-school students as recipients of instruction in educational institutions. The entity descriptions also identify upper-secondary students as a target audience. [Data: Entities (2936, 2934, 3856, 3855, 2484); Relationships (6603, 6607, 6606, 6599, 6601)]

The repeated lower-secondary labels appear in separate records and relationships. Together, these records show that the framework includes several educational stages, though they do not specify the size of each student population or the amount of instruction received.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Instruction includes specific, practical safety content
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For primary school students, the described content includes practical guidance on safely getting on and off bicycles, mopeds, and motorcycles, as well as choosing and properly wearing a helmet. [Data: Entities (3856, 3855); Relationships (6607, 6606)]

For lower-secondary students, the records describe instruction on road traffic laws and signals, including wearing a compliant helmet and fastening its strap correctly. These details show that the stated education includes practical behaviors in addition to legal knowledge. [Data: Entities (2936, 2934, 4304); Relationships (1893, 8627)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student compliance may be considered in conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions for primary and lower-secondary students state that compliance with road traffic laws may be considered when assessing student conduct. This creates a stated connection between road-safety education and conduct assessment for those groups. [Data: Entities (2936, 3856)]

The records do not establish how assessments are carried out, how frequently compliance is evaluated, or whether the described approach has produced changes in student behavior.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes an educational framework, not demonstrated outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships specify institutions, intended student audiences, a decree provision, and examples of instructional content. They do not provide evidence about actual delivery rates, student knowledge, road incidents, or resulting safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (1728, 433, 4304); Relationships (1892, 6608, 8627)]

Accordingly, the community's importance is grounded in the scope and subject of the described education rather than evidence of measured effectiveness or observed compliance.

v.tieu_de: Priority Vehicle Signal-Device Permit Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on an Article 22, clause 3 rule for revoking a priority vehicle’s signal-device permit. Two conditions connect to the rule: the vehicle is damaged beyond repair or has reached the end of its service life. The records describe circumstances requiring revocation, not a specific revocation or an assessment of compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but practical regulatory importance because it specifies when a priority vehicle’s signal-device permit must be revoked, while documenting no actual case or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulatory rule is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity describes revocation of a priority vehicle signal-device permit under Article 22, clause 3. It is linked to two conditions that trigger the revocation requirement. [Data: Entities (4221); Relationships (9732, 9733)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: End of service life is one revocation condition
phat_hien.giai_thich: A priority vehicle reaching the end of its permitted service life is identified as a circumstance requiring revocation of its signal-device permit. The records establish this as a stated condition, but do not identify a particular vehicle or case. [Data: Entities (3871, 4221); Relationships (9733)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Irreparable damage is a separate revocation condition
phat_hien.giai_thich: Damage beyond repair is separately identified as a circumstance requiring revocation of the permit. The available information does not describe any specific vehicle damage or a completed revocation. [Data: Entities (3867, 4221); Relationships (9732)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a rule, not an actual enforcement action
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of the central entity explicitly characterizes the text as conditions for revocation rather than a specific revocation. Accordingly, these records support identifying a regulatory requirement, but not concluding that an authority has acted or that a permit holder is noncompliant. [Data: Entities (4221); Relationships (9732, 9733)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to two triggers and the permit context
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records concern only the priority vehicle’s signal-device permit and the two stated triggers: end of service life and damage beyond repair. They provide no information about enforcement procedures, technical device capabilities, affected parties, or broader reputation and compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (4221, 3871, 3867); Relationships (9732, 9733)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Right-Hand-Drive Vehicle Use and Foreign Drivers
v.tom_tat: This community concerns non-tourism use of right-hand-drive cars on roads in Vietnam and the handling of costs associated with violations or accidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles. It connects individuals and organizations that bring such cars into traffic with the activity itself, while a separate set of relationships links those actors to foreign drivers and assigns them responsibility for related costs. The records describe regulatory and financial responsibilities, but do not establish specific incidents, enforcement outcomes, or the scale of impact.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns road use and responsibility for costs arising from violations or accidents, while the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-tourism use of right-hand-drive cars is the community’s central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The activity is defined as bringing right-hand-drive cars into traffic in Vietnam for purposes other than tourism and is identified as being addressed in Article 35. This places the community within a road-use regulatory context, though the records do not specify the rule’s detailed requirements or enforcement process. [Data: Entities (3258)]

Both individuals and organizations are identified as actors carrying out this activity, connecting the activity to two types of responsible parties. [Data: Entities (2653, 3440); Relationships (7933, 9215)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individuals and organizations are both identified as actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into traffic from organizations doing so. In both descriptions, the relevant use is on Vietnamese roads for purposes other than tourism. [Data: Entities (2653, 3440)]

The relationships explicitly connect individuals and organizations to the non-tourism road-use activity, indicating that the community’s scope includes both personal and organizational involvement. The records do not identify any particular person or organization. [Data: Relationships (7933, 9215)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Responsibility for costs is linked to foreign drivers and vehicle-related violations or accidents
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The foreign-driver entity describes foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam and notes that violations or traffic accidents involving them may give rise to costs that responsible parties must address. [Data: Entities (2308)]

Relationships connect this entity to both individuals and organizations bringing right-hand-drive cars into traffic, with the relationship descriptions stating that the provision assigns responsibility for handling costs arising from violations or accidents involving foreign drivers and foreign motor vehicles. The records do not identify a specific cost amount or case. [Data: Relationships (7400, 7401)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal violations are included as a cost-triggering circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a legal-violations entity describing violations in connection with foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. Its description states that costs arising from these violations must be handled by the responsible parties described in Article 35. [Data: Entities (5597)]

A relationship directly links foreign drivers to violations of law and describes the provision as addressing costs arising from such violations. This supports a connection between the conduct and financial responsibility, but does not establish that any particular party has violated the law. [Data: Relationships (7404)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence indicates regulatory relevance but not an established incident record
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe categories of actors, non-tourism road use, legal violations, and responsibility for costs. They do not provide named cases, dates, enforcement actions, accident details, or measured financial or public-safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (2308, 2653, 3258, 3440, 5597); Relationships (7400, 7401, 7404, 7933, 9215)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant to assessing road-use compliance and potential cost allocation, but the available records are insufficient to determine the frequency, severity, or wider impact of any violations or accidents.

v.tieu_de: Priority-Vehicle Signal-Device Permit Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on revocation of permits for priority-vehicle signal-device use under Article 22, Clause 3 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The provision identifies use contrary to an issued permit and use for an improper purpose as grounds for revocation. Permit issuance is also represented as the authorization against which device use is assessed. The records describe regulatory rules, not a specific permit holder, violation, or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (4222, 324, 5310, 5311, 2765); Relationships (1278, 9980, 9981, 8108)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes regulatory controls on permitted priority-vehicle signal-device use, but provides no evidence of a particular violation or enforcement case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22, Clause 3 provides the regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22, Clause 3 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as specifying circumstances in which a permit to use signal devices on priority vehicles must be revoked. It is directly linked to the revocation concept, making it the stated regulatory basis for the community. [Data: Entities (324, 4222); Relationships (1278)]

The records identify the rule and its subject matter but do not reproduce the full legal text or establish how it has been applied in any particular case. [Data: Entities (324); Relationships (1278)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Use contrary to an issued permit is a revocation ground
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Use of a priority-vehicle signal device in a manner inconsistent with its issued permit is explicitly identified as a circumstance that results in revocation of the permit. [Data: Entities (5310, 4222); Relationships (9980)]

The issuance record describes the permit as the authorization that device use must comply with, linking the permitted use to this revocation ground. No particular device, permit holder, or instance of non-compliant use is identified. [Data: Entities (2765, 5310); Relationships (8108)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improper-purpose use is a separate stated ground
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies use of a priority-vehicle signal device for an improper purpose as a prohibited use and a circumstance leading to revocation of its use permit. [Data: Entities (5311, 4222); Relationships (9981)]

This is presented separately from use contrary to permit terms. The records do not define what purposes qualify as improper or describe any alleged or confirmed instance. [Data: Entities (5310, 5311); Relationships (9980, 9981)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes a permit control and consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect permit issuance, the requirement that device use comply with the authorization, and revocation when specified conditions are met. This indicates a regulatory structure in which the permit defines authorized use and revocation is the stated consequence for the listed circumstances. [Data: Entities (2765, 4222, 324); Relationships (1278, 8108)]

The available information does not describe other stages of administration, such as how permits are assessed, how violations are investigated, or whether there are review procedures. Those details cannot be inferred from this community. [Data: Entities (2765, 4222); Relationships (1278, 8108)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific violation or enforcement outcome is documented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe grounds for permit revocation as general regulatory concepts. They do not identify a named person or organization, a specific permit, an actual device-use incident, or a completed revocation. [Data: Entities (4222, 324, 5310, 5311, 2765); Relationships (1278, 9980, 9981, 8108)]

Accordingly, the data support analysis of the rule’s stated scope, but not conclusions about compliance by any individual or agency, the frequency of violations, or the practical effectiveness of enforcement. [Data: Entities (324, 4222); Relationships (1278, 9980, 9981)]

v.tieu_de: Article 31 Road-Safety Assistance and Vehicle Operations
v.tom_tat: This community links driver assistance and road-user warnings with three vehicle or transport categories: overweight vehicles, oversized or heavy cargo transport, and tracked vehicles. The relationships describe assistance and warnings as being provided when necessary for road safety. The entity descriptions identify Article 31 as the relevant framework; they also state that specified overweight-vehicle violations may result in driving-licence point deductions under a cited decree. The data describes regulatory topics and connections, not specific incidents or operators.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact importance because it concerns road safety and regulated vehicle operations, but the data describes rules and assistance rather than specific incidents or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver assistance and warnings form the community’s hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driver Assistance and Road-User Warnings is connected to each of the three vehicle or transport categories, making it the community’s central coordinating topic. Its description says it covers assistance to drivers and warnings to people and vehicles participating in road traffic, as described in Article 31. [Data: Entities (1444); Relationships (6010, 6012, 6013)]

The relationships qualify this support as being provided when necessary for road safety. The records do not specify particular warning procedures, responsible organizations, or individual events. [Data: Relationships (6010, 6012, 6013)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overweight vehicle operation has a stated licence-point consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Overweight Vehicle Operation concerns using a public road with a vehicle that exceeds the permitted weight limit. Its description identifies it as a vehicle category addressed under Article 31. [Data: Entities (3518)]

The description further states that specified violations may result in a deduction of driving-licence points under the cited decree. It does not identify which specific violations trigger that consequence or provide details of any enforcement case. [Data: Entities (3518)]

Driver assistance and warnings are linked to covered overweight vehicles when necessary for road safety. [Data: Relationships (6012)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized or heavy cargo transport is linked to safety support
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Oversized or Heavy Cargo Transport concerns road transport of exceptionally large or heavy cargo. Its description states that Article 31 provides for assistance, warnings, and safety measures in this context. [Data: Entities (3504)]

The relationship to Driver Assistance and Road-User Warnings specifies that assistance and warnings are provided in connection with such transport when necessary for road safety. No particular cargo, route, operator, or safety incident is identified in the data. [Data: Relationships (6010)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tracked vehicles are another Article 31 category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Tracked Vehicle Operation is described as the operation of tracked vehicles on public roads and as a vehicle category addressed by Article 31. [Data: Entities (4976)]

The records connect this category to driver assistance and warnings when necessary for road safety. They do not provide additional details about the vehicles, applicable procedures, or any specific operation. [Data: Relationships (6013)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a regulatory and safety focus, not incident evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Across the community, the available information concerns Article 31 categories and assistance or warnings associated with road safety. The three links from the central assistance-and-warnings entity establish the structure connecting it to overweight vehicles, oversized or heavy cargo transport, and tracked vehicles. [Data: Entities (1444, 3518, 3504, 4976); Relationships (6010, 6012, 6013)]

The data does not identify particular individuals, organizations, incidents, or demonstrated injuries or losses. Accordingly, the community’s importance is grounded in its subject matter—regulated road use and safety support—rather than evidence of a specific harmful event. [Data: Entities (1444, 3518, 3504, 4976); Relationships (6010, 6012, 6013)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: Foreign Vehicles and Border Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 32 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and its requirements for foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers participating in traffic in Vietnam. The article connects entry and exit processes with customs clearance at the relevant border gate, and with temporary import and re-export procedures for vehicles. The associated descriptions also note applicable visa and traffic-participation periods and a conditional allowance of up to 10 additional days in Vietnam when an unforeseen incident prevents departure. The records describe regulatory requirements but do not assess enforcement, compliance outcomes, or penalties.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the article’s central role in coordinating vehicle, customs, and entry/exit requirements, which makes the community operationally significant without evidence of specific violations or harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is the community’s regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is the central entity, linked to entry into Vietnam, exit from Vietnam, customs clearance, temporary import, and re-export. Its description identifies it as the provision governing foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers participating in traffic in Vietnam, including customs, entry, exit, and permitted-duration requirements. [Data: Entities (370); Relationships (1572, 1574, 1575, 1576, 1577)]

This structure indicates that the provision spans several related stages of a vehicle’s and traveler’s movement rather than addressing only one border procedure. The records establish these regulatory connections but do not specify enforcement practices or compliance rates. [Data: Relationships (1572, 1574, 1575, 1576, 1577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Entry into Vietnam involves immigration periods and border customs
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entry entity describes foreign nationals entering Vietnam under applicable immigration rules, which determine the relevant visa period and the period during which they may participate in traffic. It also states that required customs procedures must be completed as part of entry. [Data: Entities (1816)]

Article 32 specifies that customs procedures must be completed at the entry border gate, and the customs-clearance relationship likewise places those procedures at the border gate when entering Vietnam. [Data: Relationships (1574, 4053)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Exit requirements include customs and a conditional extension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The exit entity describes departure by foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles from Vietnam and says required customs procedures must be completed as part of the process. [Data: Entities (1902)]

It also states that, if an unforeseen incident prevents departure, a foreign national may be permitted to remain for up to 10 additional days, subject to prescribed procedures. Article 32 and the customs-clearance relationship specify that customs procedures are required at the exit border gate. [Data: Entities (1902); Relationships (1575, 4054)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Customs clearance is required at the relevant border gate
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Customs clearance is described as procedures that must be completed at the relevant entry or exit border gate under the decree. Article 32 is directly linked to customs clearance, while separate relationships connect clearance to both entry and exit. [Data: Entities (1168); Relationships (1572, 4053, 4054)]

Together, these records present customs clearance as a requirement at both ends of the cross-border process. They do not provide further procedural steps, documentation details, or consequences for failing to complete clearance. [Data: Relationships (1572, 4053, 4054)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicles are subject to temporary import and re-export procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is linked to both temporary import and re-export, and the corresponding relationships state that these procedures are required for foreign vehicles under customs law. [Data: Entities (4873, 4033); Relationships (1576, 1577)]

The records also explicitly connect temporary import and re-export as procedures required by the decree. They identify the required procedural categories but do not specify timelines, forms, or other implementation details. [Data: Relationships (9837)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework links vehicle participation to permitted periods
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 32 includes permitted-duration requirements for foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers participating in traffic in Vietnam. The entry description separately notes that immigration rules determine the relevant visa period and the period during which foreign nationals may participate in traffic. [Data: Entities (370, 1816)]

These records indicate that the framework concerns both border procedures and the duration of permitted participation. They do not state the ordinary duration limits or establish how those limits apply in individual cases. [Data: Entities (370, 1816)]

v.tieu_de: Intelligent Transport Vehicle License Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community concerns licensing and operating-license revocation for intelligent transport vehicles under Article 25 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The revocation provision is linked to two specified circumstances: a vehicle reaching the end of its service life and a vehicle being prohibited from circulation. The supplied records describe a regulatory framework, not specific enforcement actions or affected vehicles.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational and compliance significance because it describes circumstances that require license revocation, but the data provides no evidence of particular cases or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operating-license revocation is the central topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community centers on the regulatory action of revoking an intelligent transport vehicle’s operating license under specified circumstances in Article 25, Clause 5, of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The entity is connected both to the broader licensing provision and to the circumstances that trigger revocation. [Data: Entities (3376); Relationships (8605, 6710, 9289)]

The records establish a rule described in the supplied data; they do not identify a particular vehicle, license holder, or instance of revocation. [Data: Entities (3376); Relationships (8605, 6710, 9289)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rule sits within intelligent-vehicle operations licensing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The licensing of intelligent transport vehicle operations is addressed in Article 25 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. A relationship explicitly connects that licensing provision to the circumstances in which an operating license is revoked, placing revocation within the broader licensing framework. [Data: Entities (2909, 3376); Relationships (8605)]

The supplied information does not detail application procedures, licensing standards, or other requirements beyond this connection. [Data: Entities (2909, 3376); Relationships (8605)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: End of service life is a stated revocation circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The end of a vehicle’s service life is identified as a circumstance requiring revocation of an intelligent transport vehicle’s operating license under Article 25, Clause 5. This links a vehicle-life-cycle condition directly to the regulatory action. [Data: Entities (1788, 3376); Relationships (6710)]

The records do not specify how service life is determined or provide details about any vehicle to which this circumstance has been applied. [Data: Entities (1788, 3376); Relationships (6710)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibition from circulation is another stated circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies a vehicle not being permitted to circulate as a circumstance requiring its operating license to be revoked under Article 25, Clause 5. This connects a circulation restriction with the licensing consequence described in the community. [Data: Entities (3930, 3376); Relationships (9289)]

No details are provided about the basis for a circulation prohibition, the decision-making process, or an actual case. [Data: Entities (3930, 3376); Relationships (9289)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes rules, not observed enforcement or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships characterize a licensing provision and two circumstances associated with license revocation. They do not report enforcement statistics, affected parties, disputes, safety outcomes, or implementation results. [Data: Entities (2909, 3376, 3930, 1788); Relationships (8605, 6710, 9289)]

Accordingly, the community’s demonstrated importance is regulatory and operational in scope; the supplied records do not support conclusions about how frequently the rule is used or its realized effects. [Data: Entities (2909, 3376, 3930, 1788); Relationships (8605, 6710, 9289)]

v.tieu_de: Intelligent Transport Vehicle Permit Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on revocation of intelligent transport vehicle operating permits. The data identifies two grounds for revocation: permits based on forged documents and permits issued by an authority without proper jurisdiction. Both grounds are linked directly to the revocation action; the records describe regulatory provisions, not specific enforcement cases. [Data: Entities (4226, 3380, 3381); Relationships (9291, 9292)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory significance because it defines two grounds for withdrawing operating permits, while the data provides no evidence of actual cases or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit revocation is the central regulatory action
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community's central entity is the revocation of intelligent transport vehicle operating permits when the permit was granted on either of the stated grounds. The records establish a regulatory consequence, but do not identify any specific permit, vehicle, or enforcement decision. [Data: Entities (4226); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

The available information therefore describes a rule or regulatory action rather than evidence that a revocation has occurred. [Data: Entities (4226); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Forged documents are one stated ground for revocation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A permit issued on the basis of a forged application or supporting documents is identified as a ground for revocation. The relationship record explicitly connects this circumstance to the revocation action. [Data: Entities (3380, 4226); Relationships (9291)]

The data does not establish that any particular applicant submitted forged documents or that a permit was revoked on this basis. [Data: Entities (3380); Relationships (9291)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Lack of jurisdiction is a separate stated ground
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify issuance by an authority lacking proper jurisdiction as another ground for revoking an intelligent transport vehicle operating permit. This basis is linked directly to the revocation action. [Data: Entities (3381, 4226); Relationships (9292)]

No issuing authority or individual permit is named, and the data does not indicate that a specific jurisdictional defect has been found in practice. [Data: Entities (3381); Relationships (9292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The two grounds converge on the same consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community has a clear structure: two distinct types of improper permit issuance—use of forged documents and lack of authority—each connect to the same outcome, permit revocation. [Data: Entities (3380, 3381, 4226); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

This structure distinguishes document-related concerns from jurisdictional concerns while indicating that both are treated as grounds for the same regulatory action. [Data: Entities (3380, 3381, 4226); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to the stated regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the revocation action and its two grounds, but contain no information about enforcement frequency, affected operators, penalties beyond revocation, or outcomes of any cases. [Data: Entities (4226, 3380, 3381); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

Accordingly, the community supports identifying compliance conditions relevant to permit validity, but does not support conclusions about actual misconduct, operational capabilities, or reputational effects of particular entities. [Data: Entities (4226, 3380, 3381); Relationships (9291, 9292)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Order and Safety Law and Amendments
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety and its implementation and amendment framework. Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP amends provisions of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, which implements the law, while Law 118/2025/QH15 directly amends the law. The connected provisions address vehicle categories and operating conditions, driver requirements, rescue eligibility, priority signals, and driving-time limits. The data also specifies staged effective dates for Law 118/2025/QH15 and an expiration date for Article 2 of Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial regulatory importance because it links a national road-safety law, implementation rules, amendments, and provisions affecting vehicle operation and driver requirements.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The road traffic law is the community’s central framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety is described as a Vietnamese law governing road traffic order and safety. It provides a legal basis for connecting and sharing information between the road-safety database and other databases, and for using database information to identify violations. [Data: Entities (2851)]

The law also supplies or establishes a basis for rules on vehicle operation, driver requirements, rescue eligibility, priority signals, school transport, and permitted driving times. These provisions make the law the central reference point for the other legal entities in the community. [Data: Entities (2851); Relationships (3341, 7587, 1711)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework is shaped by implementing and amending instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP implements and details provisions of the law. Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP amends and supplements provisions of Decree 151, making it indirectly connected to the law’s implementation. [Data: Entities (2851, 1295); Relationships (5647, 1400)]

Separately, Article 7 of Law 118/2025/QH15 amends and supplements provisions of the road traffic law. The community therefore contains both an implementation path through decrees and a direct legislative amendment path. [Data: Entities (2822, 537); Relationships (8160, 2515, 2516)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Law 118/2025/QH15 has staged effective dates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Law 118/2025/QH15 generally takes effect on July 1, 2026. The stated exception is point a, Clause 20, Article 7, which takes effect earlier, on January 1, 2026. [Data: Entities (2822, 1739); Relationships (6617)]

These dates are relevant to understanding when the law’s amendments to the road traffic framework apply. The provided information identifies the dates but does not specify the substantive content of the earlier-effective provision. [Data: Entities (2822, 1739)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle categories and operating conditions are linked across the law and decree
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 34 of the law identifies categories of rudimentary vehicles to which operating conditions in Article 26 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP apply. Those conditions include front lighting or reflectors and rear signal lights or reflectors. [Data: Entities (404, 331); Relationships (1711, 1356)]

The law’s description also notes that it defines motor vehicles relevant to intelligent transport vehicle provisions and provides a basis for conditions governing non-motorized vehicle operation. [Data: Entities (2851)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law covers driver obligations and operational limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 56, including Clauses 1 and 2, is cited for requirements applying to people driving cars, certain four-wheeled motor vehicles, and specialized motorcycles; Clause 1 sets conditions a person must meet to drive in traffic. [Data: Entities (2851)]

Clause 1 of Article 64 establishes permitted driving times and is cited in connection with violations of those limits. The provided material identifies these requirements but does not provide specific time limits or penalties. [Data: Entities (2851)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Rescue eligibility and priority-signal rules include defined limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 1 of Article 54 is identified as defining which vehicles are eligible for road rescue. The law also addresses which vehicle groups may be fitted with priority-signal devices, along with licensing and use restrictions. [Data: Entities (867, 2851); Relationships (3341)]

A funeral procession is identified as a category of priority-vehicle convoy but is expressly excluded from the groups eligible to have priority-vehicle signal devices installed under the cited rules. [Data: Entities (2380); Relationships (7587)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP sets a specific expiration date for Article 2
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 28 of Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP addresses entry into force and specifies that Article 2 ceases to have effect on March 1, 2027, subject to stated exceptions. [Data: Entities (1295, 295); Relationships (1059)]

This expiration is distinct from the amendment made by Article 27 of the same decree to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The supplied information establishes these provisions and dates but does not describe the exceptions or the content of Article 2. [Data: Entities (1295, 343); Relationships (1400, 1059)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Safety Education in Vocational and Upper-Secondary Schools
v.tom_tat: The community centers on road traffic law education, described as instruction in traffic order and safety, including legal knowledge and the ability to predict and avoid dangers. The activity is intended for students at vocational education establishments and upper-secondary schools. The vocational institutions also have a stated role in preparing facilities and motorbikes for safe-riding instruction. The records establish the program’s educational scope and institutional links, but do not describe its implementation scale or measured outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it connects road-safety education to two types of educational institutions, while the records provide no evidence about its scale or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road traffic law education is the network’s central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Road traffic law education is the central entity linking the two institution types in the community. It is described as covering legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety, including predicting and avoiding dangers. [Data: Entities (4360); Relationships (10142, 10141)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vocational institutions have a stated instructional-preparation role
phat_hien.giai_thich: Vocational education establishments are intended settings for the education activity. Their managing agencies are directed to prepare facilities and motorbikes for safe-riding instruction, indicating a practical-preparation component in addition to the broader road-safety education provisions. [Data: Entities (5615, 4360); Relationships (10142)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Upper-secondary students are also within the education’s scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify upper-secondary schools as another intended setting for road traffic law education, with their students covered by the decree’s provisions on road traffic order and safety law education. This places both vocational and upper-secondary students within the described scope. [Data: Entities (5291, 4360); Relationships (10141)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The curriculum includes both legal knowledge and hazard awareness
phat_hien.giai_thich: The education activity is not described solely as learning traffic law: its stated content also includes predicting and avoiding dangers. This supports characterizing the activity as combining legal knowledge with attention to road-safety hazards, without establishing how the instruction is delivered or assessed. [Data: Entities (4360)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network connects one education activity to two student settings
phat_hien.giai_thich: The two recorded relationships both originate from road traffic law education and connect it to vocational education establishments and upper-secondary schools. This establishes a shared educational focus across those settings, but the records do not specify participation numbers, implementation status, or educational outcomes. [Data: Relationships (10142, 10141); Entities (5615, 5291, 4360)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Safety Measures and Road Hazards
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Road Traffic Safety Assistance and Measures, described as providing driver assistance and warnings and implementing necessary safety measures for certain large or heavy vehicles. Two relationships identify circumstances in which those measures apply: force majeure road incidents and vehicle operation on damaged or degraded road sections. The information describes safety-related provisions and contexts, but does not establish that any incident occurred or provide details about legal compliance, implementation, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4444, 2298, 5430); Relationships (7368, 10233)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the community concerns road-safety measures for potentially hazardous travel circumstances, while the data provides no evidence of specific incidents, implementation failures, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety assistance is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road Traffic Safety Assistance and Measures is the central subject, described as providing driver assistance and warnings and implementing necessary road-traffic safety measures for certain large or heavy vehicles operating on roads. The two recorded relationships connect this entity to both identified road circumstances. [Data: Entities (4444); Relationships (7368, 10233)]

The data does not specify particular technologies, operating procedures, or whether the described measures are currently in use.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Force majeure incidents are identified as a trigger
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Force Majeure Road Incidents are described as unavoidable incidents affecting road travel and as a circumstance in which road-traffic safety measures may be required. The relationship states that the assistance and measures apply when such an incident occurs. [Data: Entities (2298, 4444); Relationships (7368)]

No specific incident, response, or outcome is documented, so the record supports a stated safety context rather than evidence of an actual event.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Damaged or degraded road sections are another trigger
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle operation on damaged or degraded road sections is identified as a circumstance requiring road-traffic safety measures. The recorded relationship connects this circumstance directly to the assistance and measures entity. [Data: Entities (5430, 4444); Relationships (10233)]

The data does not describe the road sections, the vehicles involved in any particular case, or the precise measures used.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community links safety measures to two distinct road conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships identify two different circumstances for applying safety assistance: force majeure incidents and operation on degraded road sections. Together, these records frame the measures as relevant to both unavoidable travel incidents and road-condition hazards. [Data: Entities (2298, 5430, 4444); Relationships (7368, 10233)]

The records do not establish that these circumstances are exhaustive or provide a priority, frequency, or comparative risk assessment.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance, reputation, and operational effectiveness are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available descriptions identify the purpose and stated contexts of road-safety measures, but contain no information about applicable laws, compliance assessments, organizational reputation, or the effectiveness of implementation. [Data: Entities (4444, 2298, 5430); Relationships (7368, 10233)]

Accordingly, the data supports recognizing the community as safety-related, but not drawing conclusions about whether particular operators comply with requirements or whether the measures prevent harm.

v.tieu_de: Article 17 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP: Priority Vehicle Signal Equipment
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Article 17 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and the installation of priority vehicle signal equipment. The sole recorded relationship states that Clause 2 of Article 17 specifies installation requirements, including motorcycle placements for priority lights, a horn, and a flag. The data describes a technical regulatory provision but does not establish whether any vehicle complies with it or how the requirements are enforced. [Data: Entities (276, 2702); Relationships (991)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has some regulatory and technical importance because it specifies priority-vehicle signal equipment installation, but the data shows no evidence about implementation, enforcement, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 17 is the community's regulatory anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 17 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as a provision addressing signal equipment for priority vehicles, including motorcycle installation requirements. [Data: Entities (276)]

Its recorded connection to the installation activity is direct: Clause 2 specifies how priority signal equipment is to be installed. [Data: Relationships (991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The installation activity is specifically defined
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The installation activity is identified as the activity specified in Clause 2 of Article 17. This links the technical subject directly to the cited provision rather than to a separate organization or operational actor. [Data: Entities (2702); Relationships (991)]

The available records describe requirements, not evidence that a particular vehicle or person has carried out an installation. [Data: Entities (2702, 276); Relationships (991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle priority lights have specified placement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For motorcycles, the description specifies that priority lights are installed on both sides of the crash bar or vehicle body and above the rear pillar. [Data: Entities (2702)]

This is a placement requirement within the recorded installation description; the data does not provide further technical measurements or implementation examples. [Data: Entities (2702)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Horn and flag positions are also specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The installation description places the priority horn at the front of the motorcycle. It places the priority flag at the front on the driver's left side. [Data: Entities (2702)]

These details show that the described requirements cover multiple types of signal equipment, not only lights. [Data: Entities (2702)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish requirements, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and their relationship identify a provision and an installation activity, but provide no records about inspections, enforcement, compliance rates, or violations. [Data: Entities (276, 2702); Relationships (991)]
