Accordingly, the community's importance is grounded in the presence of a specific regulatory and technical requirement; its practical impact cannot be assessed from these records alone. [Data: Entities (276, 2702); Relationships (991)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP Road-Traffic Framework
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, dated November 15, 2024, which implements aspects of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Its connected provisions and procedures cover road-safety education, traffic-safety data, priority-vehicle signaling equipment, intelligent-vehicle licensing, and the participation of foreign vehicles and drivers. The records describe a broad regulatory framework with administrative controls, technical requirements, and enforcement mechanisms; they do not establish how effectively the provisions are implemented in practice. [Data: Entities (1270); Relationships (4483, 4502, 4419, 4387, 4472)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad importance to national road safety, data governance, vehicle operations, and cross-border traffic, rather than evidence of actual noncompliance or harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A central decree with broad road-safety scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is the community’s central entity and is described as a Vietnamese government decree dated November 15, 2024, providing detailed regulations and implementation measures for the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Its subjects span education, safety data, vehicle equipment and operation, and foreign vehicles and drivers. [Data: Entities (1270)]

The relationship records connect the decree to provisions and procedures across these topics, including education, database updates, permit management, intelligent-vehicle licensing, and foreign-vehicle participation. This breadth makes it an important regulatory reference, although the records do not assess real-world outcomes. [Data: Relationships (4483, 4502, 4419, 4413, 4387)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education and traffic-data governance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree provides for road-safety legal education across multiple levels of education, including safe motorbike-riding instruction for students, and assigns responsibilities to education authorities and institutions. [Data: Entities (1270); Relationships (4483)]

Articles 9–15 are described as establishing principles for building, managing, using, connecting, and sharing the road traffic order and safety database. Article 13, clause 1 specifically concerns adding and adjusting database information, and the decree identifies administrative-procedure results and related professional activities as information sources. [Data: Entities (5285, 257, 94, 4095); Relationships (4502, 848, 247, 4469)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The database framework covers sensitive operational and safety information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree’s described database scope includes vehicle registration, ownership, inspection, origin and sales; driver training, licensing and health examinations; insurance; accidents and safety recommendations; administrative violations; transport businesses and vehicle badges; and vehicle journeys and driver images. The provisions also address collecting, updating, accessing, and exchanging information, including information from foreign-vehicle and customs databases. [Data: Entities (1270)]

Article 11 and Article 12 are linked as part of the decree’s database provisions, with Article 12, clause 2 referring to information specified in Article 11, clause 6. These records establish a regulatory design for information flows, but do not show the database’s actual technical architecture, security controls, or operational performance. [Data: Entities (238, 245); Relationships (727, 786, 726)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signaling is governed through standards and permits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree regulates management, installation, and use of signaling equipment on priority vehicles, including technical requirements and procedures for issuing, replacing, reissuing, and revoking permits. Article 21 is associated with new issuance and reissuance procedures, while Article 22 identifies grounds for revocation. [Data: Entities (2960, 2784, 3228, 4083); Relationships (4419, 4408, 4437, 4467, 4476)]

The specified revocation grounds include issuance to an ineligible recipient and expiration of the permit. Appendix I sets out technical requirements, and Form No. 02A is identified as the prescribed form for a new permit application. [Data: Entities (4237, 2763, 1905, 191, 2360); Relationships (8106, 6843, 573, 4389)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency-vehicle signaling has a stated operational rule
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records specifically describe an ambulance responding to an emergency as using a flashing red light and a priority siren. This is presented as a provision of the decree, not as evidence about the behavior of any particular ambulance or operator. [Data: Entities (168); Relationships (524)]

More generally, Article 19 addresses signals and technical requirements for priority-vehicle equipment; the entity description specifies that priority signals may use flashing red, flashing blue, or flashing blue-and-red lights. Appendix I contains relevant technical requirements. [Data: Entities (292, 190); Relationships (1056, 574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent-vehicle licensing and other vehicle-operation controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses licensing the operation of intelligent or smart transport vehicles. The records identify an operating-license application and a permit-granting process, including a required request using the prescribed form. [Data: Entities (2715, 2409, 2907, 3407); Relationships (4406, 4413, 4394, 4445)]

The decree also covers journey-monitoring equipment for specified vehicles, operating conditions for rudimentary vehicles, commercial vehicles transporting students, and safety measures for oversized, overweight, tracked, or exceptionally large or heavy vehicles. These are described as regulated subjects; the records do not provide evidence about specific vehicles or licensing decisions. [Data: Entities (1270, 3411); Relationships (4446)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign and right-hand-drive vehicle participation is subject to controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 32–36 are described as governing foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers in Vietnam, including eligibility, registration and licensing, customs and temporary import/re-export procedures, permitted routes and circulation periods, required documents and insurance, and compliance with Vietnamese traffic laws. The decree is linked to both foreign-vehicle participation and customs procedures. [Data: Entities (1270, 2345, 1171); Relationships (4387, 4056)]

The decree also addresses right-hand-drive vehicles used for non-tourism purposes, including approval arrangements and the handling of violations, as well as changes to previously approved information. The records establish the existence of these regulatory mechanisms, not that a violation has occurred. [Data: Entities (4262, 4183, 3438, 2643, 793); Relationships (4478, 4447, 4397, 3139, 4472)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework applies broadly, but the records do not establish compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is described as applying to domestic and foreign agencies, organizations, and individuals involved in road traffic order and safety matters in Vietnam. This broad stated scope is reflected in separate relationships linking the decree to each group. [Data: Entities (1436, 1437, 1438); Relationships (4371, 4372, 4373)]

The decree also repeals Decree 109/2009/NĐ-CP from the newer decree’s effective date. The available records describe legal provisions, procedures, and regulatory subjects; they do not provide evidence of implementation quality, compliance rates, enforcement results, or reputational assessments. [Data: Entities (1262, 1270); Relationships (4262)]

v.tieu_de: Article 12 Information Collection and Referenced Databases
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a procedure for collecting information under Article 12, clause 9, of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and the databases identified as sources for that collection. The relationship records the databases’ role as information sources. The available data describes the procedure and its statutory references, but does not establish what information is collected in practice, who is affected, or how the information is used.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the importance of a statutory information-collection process while accounting for the limited evidence about its scope, implementation, and effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A defined statutory information-collection procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a process described in Article 12, clause 9, of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. Its description says that information specified in Article 11, clause 13, is collected from databases referenced in Article 12, clause 1. [Data: Entities (2668)]

This establishes a regulatory and procedural context, but the supplied records do not provide the text of the cited provisions or further detail about how the collection is carried out.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Referenced databases serve as information sources
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The second entity represents the databases specified by points a and đ of Article 12, clause 1. The recorded relationship identifies these databases as sources from which information is collected for the Article 12 process. [Data: Entities (1250, 2668); Relationships (4245)]

The records do not name the databases or describe their contents, operators, access controls, or data quality.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is organized around one source-to-process link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available network contains two entities and one relationship: the referenced databases are connected to the information-collection process as its sources. [Data: Entities (1250, 2668); Relationships (4245)]

No additional organizations, individuals, systems, or downstream recipients are identified in the supplied records, so the broader operational network cannot be assessed from this information.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process cross-references separate provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The process description links Article 12, clause 9, to information specified in Article 11, clause 13, and to databases referenced in Article 12, clause 1. [Data: Entities (2668)]

These cross-references indicate that the described procedure depends on provisions beyond the immediate clause, but the supplied data does not specify their full requirements or establish how they are interpreted or implemented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance, capability, and effects are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a statutory process and its database-source relationship, but provide no implementation evidence, compliance findings, technical details, reputation information, or claims about outcomes. [Data: Entities (1250, 2668); Relationships (4245)]

Accordingly, the available information is insufficient to determine whether the process is being applied lawfully in practice, what technical capabilities are involved, or what effects the collection has on individuals or organizations.

v.tieu_de: Appendix II and Signal-Device Use Permits
v.tom_tat: This small community centers on Appendix II to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and the process for issuing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. Appendix II contains related application forms, including Form No. 02a. The available information describes an administrative permitting framework but provides no details about individual applicants, permit decisions, or compliance outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has some administrative and regulatory importance because it concerns permits for signal devices on priority vehicles, but the supplied data indicates no broader effects or specific compliance concerns.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Appendix II is the central documented entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Appendix II is described as an appendix to Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and contains forms relating to applications for permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. It is the sole entity directly linked to the permitting process in the supplied relationship data. [Data: Entities (192); Relationships (579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns a specific permitting process
phat_hien.giai_thich: The second entity identifies the subject as issuance of permits for using signal devices on priority vehicles. The relationship states that Appendix II contains forms related to issuing those permits, establishing the community's procedural focus. [Data: Entities (2778); Relationships (579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Form No. 02a is included among the application forms
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of Appendix II explicitly identifies Form No. 02a as one of the forms it contains. The supplied data does not provide the form's fields, eligibility criteria, or instructions, so no further characteristics can be established. [Data: Entities (192)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The documented relationship is direct and narrowly scoped
phat_hien.giai_thich: The only supplied relationship connects Appendix II to the issuance of signal-device-use permits, describing the appendix as containing related forms. No additional organizations, applicants, authorities, or other process stages are identified in the provided records. [Data: Relationships (579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance outcomes and operational effects are not documented
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe a decree appendix, application forms, and a permitting process, but they do not report whether permits were granted or denied, whether applicants complied with requirements, or how signal devices were used. Accordingly, the supplied information does not support conclusions about actual legal compliance or operational impact. [Data: Entities (192, 2778); Relationships (579)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Education for Elementary School Students
v.tom_tat: This small community links elementary school students with road traffic legal-knowledge education. The education is described as covering commonly encountered traffic rules and why they should be followed. The available records do not identify additional organizations, implementation details, or outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest importance because it concerns road-safety education for elementary school students, but the records describe only two entities and one relationship.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on road traffic education
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central activity is education about road traffic order and safety, including rules commonly encountered by elementary school students. The activity is also described as specified in a decree, though the records provide no further details about that decree. [Data: Entities (4379)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Elementary school students are the intended learners
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify primary-level students as the group expected to learn commonly encountered road traffic rules and why those rules should be followed. [Data: Entities (1754); Relationships (6639)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship emphasizes both rules and obedience
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship between the students and the educational activity specifies that the education covers road traffic rules and the importance of obeying them. This establishes the core connection between the two entities. [Data: Relationships (6639)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network is limited in scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: The provided community consists of two entities—an educational activity and its student audience—connected by one relationship. The records do not identify other participants or related organizations. [Data: Entities (4379, 1754); Relationships (6639)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation and outcomes are not described
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records characterize the educational subject matter and intended learners, but do not specify how or when instruction occurs, who delivers it, or what outcomes have been observed. Accordingly, the community’s practical reach and effectiveness cannot be assessed from the available information. [Data: Entities (4379, 1754); Relationships (6639)]

v.tieu_de: Appendix III and Intelligent Transport Vehicle Operating Licenses
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of Appendix III and the issuance of operating licenses for intelligent transport vehicles. Appendix III is described as an appendix to Decree 151/2024/ND-CP containing forms related to that licensing activity, and the sole recorded relationship links the appendix to the activity. The data establishes an administrative and regulatory-document connection but provides no details about implementation, compliance outcomes, or broader effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited evidenced impact because it concerns licensing documentation, while the data provides no information about implementation, compliance outcomes, or wider consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Appendix III is the central document
phat_hien.giai_thich: Appendix III is described as an appendix attached to Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and as containing forms related to operating licenses for intelligent transport vehicles. It is the primary documented entity in this community. [Data: Entities (193)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The licensing activity is the community’s subject
phat_hien.giai_thich: The second entity is the issuance of operating licenses for intelligent transport vehicles, described as the licensing activity addressed by the forms in Appendix III. The supplied information does not specify license requirements, applicants, or licensing procedures. [Data: Entities (2776, 193)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A direct link connects the forms and licensing
phat_hien.giai_thich: The recorded relationship states that Appendix III contains forms related to the issuance of operating licenses for intelligent transport vehicles. This makes the appendix a documentary component associated with that licensing activity. [Data: Relationships (581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The documented context is regulatory
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description places Appendix III within Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and associates its forms with an operating-license process. The records do not provide the decree’s other provisions or establish how the process is administered in practice. [Data: Entities (193, 2776); Relationships (581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and practical effects are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records identify a document, a licensing activity, and their connection; they do not report compliance findings, enforcement actions, operational capabilities, or impacts. Accordingly, the community’s evidenced importance is limited to this specific documentary and licensing relationship. [Data: Entities (193, 2776); Relationships (581)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 151/2024/ND-CP Article 13 Database Responsibilities
v.tom_tat: This community concerns the database specified in Clause 3 of Article 10 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and the agency responsible for it. Article 13 assigns that agency responsibility for updating the database and synchronizing its information with the road traffic order and safety database. Clause 3 of Article 10 identifies the database at issue. [Data: Entities (4185, 1266, 922, 1249); Relationships (4244, 4357, 3430)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful operational importance because it links a legally specified database and its responsible agency to information updates and synchronization with a road traffic safety database.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A designated agency has end-to-end responsibility for the database
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The responsible agency is described as directly building, managing, operating, exploiting, and using the database specified in Clause 3 of Article 10. The relationship record also assigns it responsibility for updating information in that database. [Data: Entities (4185, 1249); Relationships (4244)]

These duties place database operations and information maintenance with the same designated agency. The provided records do not identify the agency by name or describe its performance. [Data: Entities (4185); Relationships (4244)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 establishes update and synchronization duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 13 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP sets out requirements for updating information in the road traffic order and safety database. Its relationship with the responsible agency specifies duties to update its database and synchronize information with the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (1266, 4185); Relationships (4357)]

The records therefore connect the article’s requirements to operational responsibilities, but do not provide details about update frequency, procedures, or enforcement. [Data: Entities (1266); Relationships (4357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The database is identified through Clause 3 of Article 10
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 10 is described as the provision specifying the database referred to in Article 13. The relationship record connects that clause to the database under Article 10(3). [Data: Entities (922, 1249, 1266); Relationships (3430)]

This creates a clear structural link between the provision identifying the database and Article 13’s update requirements. The supplied information does not state the database’s specific contents or technical design. [Data: Entities (922, 1249, 1266); Relationships (3430, 4357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Information synchronization is a central coordination requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The responsible agency must synchronize information in the database it manages with the road traffic order and safety database. This requirement is stated in the responsible agency’s description and reiterated in the Article 13 relationship. [Data: Entities (4185); Relationships (4357)]

The records establish synchronization as a defined responsibility, but do not specify how the databases exchange information or how consistency is verified. [Data: Entities (4185); Relationships (4357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish governance responsibilities, not evidence of compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity and relationship descriptions identify the responsible agency, the database, the relevant legal provisions, and duties concerning updates and synchronization. [Data: Entities (4185, 1266, 922, 1249); Relationships (4244, 4357, 3430)]

No supplied record documents whether the agency has fulfilled these duties, reports a breach, or describes a technical capability or security incident. Accordingly, the community supports an assessment of assigned responsibilities, but not a conclusion about actual compliance or operational performance.

v.tieu_de: Article 25a and Intelligent Transport Vehicle Licensing
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of Article 25a of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and the licensing of intelligent transport vehicle operations. Article 25a is described as setting out the order and procedures for that licensing process. The provided information identifies a regulatory procedure but does not describe specific applicants, licensing outcomes, compliance issues, or technical capabilities.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest impact because it concerns a defined licensing procedure for intelligent transport vehicle operations, while the available information does not establish its implementation or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 25a is the community's central regulatory reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 25a is described as a provision of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP that sets out the order and procedures for licensing intelligent transport vehicle operations. It is the sole identified legal provision in this community. [Data: Entities (329)]

Its connection to the licensing process is stated directly in the relationship record. [Data: Relationships (1309)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The licensing process is the community's operational subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The licensing process is identified as the procedure for operating intelligent transport vehicles, with its order and procedures addressed in Article 25a. This establishes the process as the practical subject linked to the provision. [Data: Entities (2906, 329); Relationships (1309)]

The records do not specify individual licensing steps, eligibility requirements, timelines, or decision-making bodies.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship is direct and narrowly defined
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The only recorded relationship states that Article 25a sets out the order and procedures for licensing intelligent transport vehicle operations. The supplied network therefore connects one provision to one licensing subject, without identifying additional organizations or people. [Data: Relationships (1309); Entities (329, 2906)]

This supports describing the community as focused on a regulatory procedure rather than a broader network of actors.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a regulatory framework, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describe what Article 25a addresses: the order and procedures for licensing intelligent transport vehicle operations. They do not state whether any operator has applied for or received a license, or whether any entity has complied with the provision. [Data: Entities (329, 2906); Relationships (1309)]

Accordingly, the available information does not support a conclusion about legal compliance, enforcement, or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical and broader impact details are not provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities identify intelligent transport vehicles only in connection with their operation and licensing. They provide no details about vehicle technology, system capabilities, deployment scale, or operational risks. [Data: Entities (2906, 329); Relationships (1309)]

The records also do not describe the effects of the licensing process on operators or the public, so broader consequences cannot be assessed from this information alone.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Localities and Police Agencies under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Localities and their relationship with police agencies serving units and localities, which are identified as subjects to whom Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA applies. Units are also connected through the description of police agencies serving units. The available information describes administrative responsibilities involving road traffic order and safety, funding for a related database, tourist road-travel planning, and jurisdiction-limited sanctioning authority. No specific locality or compliance outcome is identified.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it covers local road-safety responsibilities and related governance provisions, but the data identifies no specific locality, compliance failure, or concrete adverse event.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Localities are the community’s central administrative entities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Localities are described as local administrative areas in Vietnam where responsibilities for road traffic order and safety are carried out. People’s Committees at all levels exercise state management of these matters within their jurisdictions. [Data: Entities (2930)]

The description does not name any particular locality, so the information establishes a general administrative scope rather than a finding about a specific place. [Data: Entities (2930)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police agencies serving localities and units fall within the circular’s stated scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies police of units and localities as agencies to whom Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA applies. The relationship records connect Localities to those police agencies and connect the police-agency category to Units. [Data: Entities (3808, 5237); Relationships (8623, 9682)]

These records describe applicability and organizational relationships; they do not establish how the circular has been implemented or whether any agency has complied or failed to comply. [Data: Entities (3808); Relationships (8623, 9682)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road traffic order and safety responsibilities are a key policy focus
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description states that localities are subject to the relevant circular and that People’s Committees at all levels exercise state management of road traffic order and safety. This makes road-safety governance the principal substantive responsibility documented for the community. [Data: Entities (2930)]

The data does not specify particular enforcement operations, incidents, or outcomes, so it supports describing the policy remit but not assessing operational effectiveness. [Data: Entities (2930)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Database funding and foreign-tourism route planning are additional responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Localities are covered by funding provisions for the road traffic order and safety database. They are also asked to coordinate in researching and developing road-travel programs and routes for foreign tourists. [Data: Entities (2930)]

These provisions indicate that the described role extends beyond local traffic management to include database-related funding and coordination on tourist travel planning. No funding amount, technical capability, or specific program is provided. [Data: Entities (2930)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctioning authority is geographically limited, and specific compliance status is unknown
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description states that each People’s Committee chairperson’s authority to impose sanctions is limited to the boundaries of that person’s local jurisdiction. This establishes a territorial constraint on the authority described. [Data: Entities (2930)]

The records provide no named locality, individual chairperson, sanctions issued, or evidence of legal violations. Accordingly, they support a description of the stated legal framework but not a conclusion about compliance or misconduct. [Data: Entities (2930)]

v.tieu_de: Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police and Decree 151/2024/ND-CP

The supplied information establishes an operational and regulatory connection, but provides no specific compliance assessment, reputational information, or allegations.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it concerns legal provisions governing priority signals on fire engines used for emergency firefighting, while the supplied data describes only two entities and one relationship.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18 provides the regulatory link
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community's sole relationship connects Article 18 of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP to the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police. The relationship states that the article specifies that the force's fire engines deployed on firefighting duties may be equipped with and use priority-vehicle signal devices. [Data: Entities (1267, 2284); Relationships (4358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The police force's defined emergency-response role
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description identifies the Fire Prevention, Firefighting and Rescue Police as responsible for fire prevention, firefighting, and rescue. This gives the regulatory provision a direct connection to emergency-response operations. [Data: Entities (2284)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority signals are associated with firefighting deployment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship expressly conditions the described permission on fire engines being deployed on firefighting duties. The data therefore ties use of the priority-vehicle signal devices to that operational circumstance, rather than describing an unrestricted use. [Data: Relationships (4358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described devices include a light and siren
phat_hien.giai_thich: The police-force entity description says its fire trucks are equipped with priority-vehicle signal devices, including a red flashing light and a priority siren, and says these are specified in the decree. The relationship separately describes Article 18 as allowing fire engines on firefighting duties to be equipped with and use such devices. [Data: Entities (2284, 1267); Relationships (4358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to an institutional and legal connection
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records identify two entities and one relationship concerning the police force's fire engines and a decree provision. They provide no further information about implementation, individual incidents, compliance outcomes, technical specifications beyond the signal types, or reputational claims; conclusions on those matters are therefore not supported by this dataset. [Data: Entities (2284, 1267); Relationships (4358)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Violation-Handling Databases
v.tom_tat: The community consists of a road-traffic-related database for information on administrative violation handling, a broader database concerning road traffic order and safety, and a national database whose general requirements apply to the specialized database. [Data: Entities (1238, 1247, 3194); Relationships (4216, 4217)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public-administration and road-safety importance because it concerns violation-handling information and national database requirements, although the records provide no evidence of operational performance or adverse impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specialized database focuses on road-traffic violation handling
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Database on Administrative Violation Handling in Road Traffic Order and Road Safety is described as containing information about the handling of administrative violations related to road traffic order and safety. The specialized database is linked to the broader Database on Road Traffic Order and Road Safety, which includes information about that violation handling. [Data: Relationships (4216)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The specialized database sits within a broader road-safety information context
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Database on Road Traffic Order and Road Safety is described as concerning road traffic order and safety, with Article 11 addressing information held in it, including administrative-violation handling information. The relationship record connects the specialized violation-handling database to this broader database, but does not specify technical architecture, data exchange processes, or whether the databases are physically or operationally integrated. [Data: Relationships (4216)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: National requirements apply to the road-traffic database
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic-related administrative violation database must satisfy the general requirements prescribed for the National Database on Administrative Violation Handling. phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a limited functional and technical picture
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available descriptions establish that the specialized database contains information about administrative-violation handling and that the broader road-traffic database addresses related information. They do not document software, infrastructure, security controls, data quality, operating capacity, or technical performance. [Data: Entities (1238, 1247); Relationships (4216)]

Accordingly, the database’s stated purpose can be summarized, but its technical capabilities beyond holding or covering the described information cannot be assessed from these records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: No compliance outcome, reputation assessment, or adverse claim is provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that general national requirements apply to the specialized database, but contain no audit findings or other evidence establishing whether those requirements are satisfied. [Data: Relationships (4217)]

The supplied information also contains no claims about misconduct, security incidents, public criticism, or reputational standing. The community’s importance is therefore grounded in its stated administrative and road-safety subject matter, not in any documented adverse event. [Data: Entities (1238, 1247, 3194); Relationships (4216, 4217)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and Vietnam’s Road Traffic Data System
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Decree 151/2024/ND-CP, which establishes rules for road-safety education, government responsibilities, vehicle permits and equipment, foreign vehicles, and the collection and management of road-traffic information. Its most interconnected component is the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety, which receives information from other government databases and is updated through administrative and professional processes. The decree’s broad regulatory scope and its role in coordinating traffic data and agency responsibilities make the community consequential, although the provided material does not establish implementation outcomes or actual compliance. [Data: Entities (1265, 1248, 4097); Relationships (4238, 4327, 4234, 4242)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad national reach across traffic regulation, government implementation, and interconnected road-safety data systems, rather than evidence of a specific adverse event.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree is the community’s central regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/ND-CP connects the community’s main topics: road-safety education, traffic databases, priority-vehicle signals, intelligent-vehicle permits, journey-monitoring data, and foreign vehicles operating in Vietnam. The decree also specifies implementation responsibilities and transitional arrangements, making it the organizing instrument for the other provisions represented here. [Data: Entities (1265); Relationships (4327, 1778, 3156)]

The records describe the decree’s scope and legal structure, but do not establish how effectively its provisions have been implemented or whether particular entities comply with them.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The road-traffic database is a central information hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety is linked directly to the decree’s rules for collecting information. The decree identifies the database as covering information across areas such as vehicle registration and inspection, drivers and licences, training, insurance, and administrative violations. [Data: Entities (1248, 1265); Relationships (4238, 4307, 4308)]

The database is also connected to information sources including the vehicle registration and management database and the National Database on Finance. Its records may be added or adjusted using information from administrative procedures, violation handling, and related professional activities. These links indicate an integrated data-governance structure, but the provided information does not describe specific access controls or security outcomes. [Data: Entities (1246, 3196, 5284); Relationships (4234, 4240, 4242)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Data collection spans operational and personal information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree’s database provisions encompass vehicle records and inspection certificates as well as information related to drivers, including licensing, training, operating time, and health. The database description also identifies driver training, testing, licensing, and road-traffic-law certificates among its contents. [Data: Entities (1265, 1248, 5500, 3096); Relationships (4307, 4351)]

This breadth makes the database relevant to traffic administration and safety oversight. It also means that data handling, sharing, and access are consequential governance considerations; however, the records provided do not document misuse, a breach, or a specific privacy failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Government agencies have assigned implementation and coordination roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree assigns responsibilities to relevant agencies, including bodies involved in managing foreign nationals operating foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam. It also identifies agencies under the Government and their heads as responsible for implementation. [Data: Entities (4097, 145, 2471, 2329); Relationships (4327, 480, 4280, 7488, 482)]

The records further describe agency coordination on traffic congestion, including working with the road management agency to identify causes. This gives the framework an inter-agency dimension, though the supplied information does not assess coordination quality or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4097)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signals and intelligent-vehicle operations are subject to permits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree regulates signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles, including which vehicles may use it, technical requirements, permits, and the authorities responsible for issuing or revoking permits. Articles 17 and 18 are specifically associated with management of the devices and eligible vehicle types. [Data: Entities (1265, 275, 280); Relationships (989, 1020, 988)]

The decree also sets out a permitting process for intelligent traffic vehicle operations. These provisions show regulatory oversight of specialized vehicle technologies and equipment; the supplied records describe rules and procedures, not the number of permits issued or the performance of the technologies. [Data: Entities (2908, 1265); Relationships (4287, 3156)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Journey monitoring and driver-image recording are covered by technical and data rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses the use, sharing, transmission, management, and storage of data from journey-monitoring and driver-image recording devices. It requires driver-image recording equipment for specified categories of vehicles and links the equipment to a national technical regulation. [Data: Entities (1265, 3215); Relationships (4313)]

These requirements extend the framework beyond registration records to information generated during vehicle operation. The records establish that such rules and technical requirements exist, but do not specify retention periods, actual collection volumes, or evidence of non-compliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicles and drivers are covered by dedicated procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree establishes requirements for foreign motor vehicles and foreign nationals driving in Vietnam, including vehicle and driver requirements and approval procedures for certain foreign vehicles entering the country. Relevant agencies are assigned responsibilities for managing foreign nationals who operate foreign motor vehicles in traffic. [Data: Entities (1265, 4097, 2329); Relationships (7488, 4327)]

This creates a specific administrative branch within the wider road-safety framework. The available material describes the requirements and agency roles but does not provide information about particular applications, approvals, or enforcement actions.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transitional rules and a specific insurance penalty connect the framework to enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 37 allows programs approved before the decree took effect to continue under their approval terms and addresses the validity of certain existing permits. Some permit holders are directed to apply for a new permit under Chapter IV. [Data: Entities (420, 805); Relationships (1778, 1777, 3156)]

Separately, Article 19 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong for operating a specialized motorcycle without the legally required compulsory civil-liability insurance certificate. This is a specific penalty described in the records, not evidence that a particular violation occurred. [Data: Entities (290, 3334); Relationships (1053)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Order and Safety Database
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Vietnam’s nationwide Road Traffic Order and Safety Database, a Ministry of Public Security-built and managed system operated and exploited by the Traffic Police Force. It consolidates information on vehicles, drivers, transport businesses, accidents, insurance, and traffic violations, and connects with population, road, business-registration, journey, and other databases. Government agencies and provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees have roles in its management and use. Its national scope, broad data coverage, and inter-agency connections make it a highly consequential public-sector information system; the supplied records describe legal requirements and intended uses, not evidence of noncompliance or misuse. [Data: Entities (4388, 115, 3686, 3008); Relationships (368, 3932, 9108, 10019, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The 8.0 rating reflects the database’s nationwide scope, extensive road-safety and personal-data coverage, and connections enabling use across competent agencies, rather than evidence of wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (4388, 1096, 1040); Relationships (3932, 3651, 9124, 10174)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A nationwide system with central and local government roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Order and Safety Database is described as a nationwide shared information system for state management of road traffic order and safety. It is built and managed by the Ministry of Public Security and operated and exploited by the Traffic Police Force; provincial and centrally governed city People’s Committees also have responsibilities within their assigned authority. [Data: Entities (4388, 3686); Relationships (9569, 9566, 9564)]

The decree’s Article 16 addresses funding for ministries, ministerial-level agencies, and government agencies involved in constructing, operating, using, maintaining, and upgrading the system. This breadth of institutional involvement supports a high assessment of the community’s public-sector importance. [Data: Entities (3008, 4388); Relationships (8756)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Broad coverage of vehicle, driver, and enforcement records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database description lists vehicle and specialized-motorcycle registration, ownership, specifications, inspection and modification records, journeys, and driver operating times. It also covers driver and operator training, tests, licences, certificates, health information, and licence-point history. [Data: Entities (4388); Relationships (9053, 4228, 10047, 6274, +more)]

Its listed contents further include transport-business and vehicle-badge information, insurance and compensation, traffic accidents, and administrative violation outcomes such as fines, sanctions, remedial measures, compliance deadlines, and licence-point management. The breadth of these records makes the system relevant to multiple aspects of road-traffic administration. [Data: Entities (4388, 115, 5095, 4318); Relationships (368, 10182, 10095, 150)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Integration and information sharing expand the system’s reach
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database is intended to connect and share information with the National Population Database, the Road Database, and other relevant databases. The listed relationships also identify specialized databases and the National Database on Business Registration as connected systems or information sources. [Data: Entities (4388, 3198, 4277, 4686, 3195); Relationships (9124, 10019, 10174, 9105, 9368)]

Information may also be collected from road-accident and road-motor-vehicle-journey databases, among other sources specified in the description. This interconnected design increases the system’s operational importance, while the supplied material does not establish the technical implementation or security of those connections. [Data: Entities (4318, 4298, 4388); Relationships (10095, 10047, 3932)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Access is framed for lawful use by competent parties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database is intended for connection, access, extraction, sharing, and use by competent state agencies under applicable rules. State-management agencies and competent agencies and organizations are identified as users, with sharing and use tied to their duties and authority. [Data: Entities (4388, 4755, 1040, 1096); Relationships (10177, 3651, 3932)]

The description says the system is to remain complete, accurate, timely, continuous, stable, and accessible for lawful use by competent agencies, organizations, and individuals. It also expressly excludes information related to national defense and security from access. These are stated operating and access conditions; the records do not demonstrate how compliance is monitored in practice. [Data: Entities (4388)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree specifies data collection, updating, and retention requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 is described as covering collection from national, ministerial, specialized, and other designated databases, including the driver and specialized-motorcycle operator health database. The records also state that information is added or adjusted from specified sources and must be stored in accordance with archival law. [Data: Entities (4388, 2843); Relationships (9108, 9105, 10095, 8496)]

These provisions establish a stated framework for data sourcing, updates, and retention. The supplied information does not include audit results, implementation assessments, or findings that the database has breached these requirements.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative enforcement and transport businesses are represented in the system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The database records administrative handling of road-traffic violations, including applicable penalties, fines, supplementary sanctions, remedial measures, compliance periods, and licence-point management. The administrative violation handling process is directly linked to the database in the supplied relationships. [Data: Entities (115, 71, 4388); Relationships (368, 150)]

Transport-business records may include identifying, licensing, address, operator, and business-type information, as well as vehicle badges. The data also identifies a transport operator field associated with a transport business unit. [Data: Entities (5094, 5095, 5107); Relationships (10181, 10182, 10598)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records show substantial institutional importance, but no adverse reputation evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The system’s nationwide remit, broad administrative coverage, and connections to other databases support a high impact rating based on its importance to road-traffic governance and information sharing. [Data: Entities (4388, 1096, 3686); Relationships (3932, 9569, 9124, +more)]

The supplied records describe the database’s functions, governance, and legal framework. They provide no allegations, incident reports, audit findings, or other evidence establishing misconduct, noncompliance, or reputational damage; no such conclusion is warranted from this material.

v.tieu_de: Decree 151/2024/ND-CP Road-Traffic Safety Data Collection
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Article 12 process for collecting information for the road traffic order and safety database. Article 12 connects that process to information specified in Article 11, including clauses 1–5 and provisions concerning driving tests and license issuance and transport businesses and vehicle badges. A motor vehicle and specialized motorcycle inspection database is identified as a source. The records describe a statutory information flow, but do not establish how it is implemented or its effects. [Data: Entities (237, 244, 2666, 1245); Relationships (725, 785, 722, 782, 783)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes information collection for a road-traffic safety database across several legal provisions and data sources, while the records do not establish implementation or resulting impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 is the hub of the collection process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 concerns collecting information for the road traffic order and safety database, and the records link it directly to the collection process and its information sources. This makes Article 12 the clearest procedural center in the represented community. [Data: Entities (244, 2666); Relationships (785)]

Article 11 supplies information requirements that Article 12 references as part of the collection process. The relationship records therefore describe a connection between legal provisions and a database-oriented process, rather than an independent operational or technical system. [Data: Entities (237, 244); Relationships (725, 785)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clauses 1–5 connect Article 11 to inspection data
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clauses 1–5 of Article 11 are identified as provisions specifying information to be collected for the road traffic order and safety database. Article 11 is also linked to the database on motor vehicle and specialized motorcycle inspection as a source for information specified in those clauses. [Data: Entities (237, 1000, 1245); Relationships (721, 722, 3565)]

The records establish the source relationship, but do not enumerate the specific fields collected or describe the inspection database's technical design. [Data: Entities (1000, 1245); Relationships (722)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 references additional Article 11 provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 is connected to Clause 14 of Article 11, which is described as identifying information collected from the database on driving tests and driver's license issuance. This indicates that the collection framework encompasses information associated with testing and license issuance. [Data: Entities (887); Relationships (782)]

Article 12 is also connected to Clause 16 of Article 11, concerning information from a database on transport business units and vehicle badges. Together, these links show that the represented collection process refers to more than one information category. [Data: Entities (894); Relationships (783)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe an information-collection capability, not its implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The information-collection process is described as gathering information from databases and data categories specified in referenced provisions, with the National Database on Finance named among the sources. The available records thus support a description of the process's intended scope and source categories. [Data: Entities (2666); Relationships (785)]

They do not specify collection frequency, data-transfer mechanisms, security controls, access permissions, or operational performance. The community therefore provides evidence of a defined data-collection framework, but not enough detail to assess its technical execution. [Data: Entities (2666); Relationships (785)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports legal relationships but not a compliance or reputation judgment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships identify provisions of Decree 151/2024/ND-CP and describe how they relate to information collection for the road traffic order and safety database. They do not report whether any organization has complied with the provisions, nor do they document enforcement actions or outcomes. [Data: Entities (237, 244, 2666); Relationships (725, 785)]

The supplied material also contains no reputational assessments or allegations. Accordingly, the records support describing the legal structure and stated information flows, but not conclusions about compliance, misconduct, or public reputation. [Data: Entities (237, 244, 2666); Relationships (725, 785)]

v.tieu_de: Driver Training, Testing, Licensing, and Certification
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative framework covering driver training courses, qualification testing, certificate issuance and reissuance, and driver-license issuance. A training facility provides courses and issues certificates; course completion can be documented through a confirmation, while a designated authority handles certificate exchanges or reissuance. The records describe processes and responsibilities, but provide no evidence about actual compliance, outcomes, scale, or reputation. [Data: Entities (1509, 1493, 1481, 766, 1457); Relationships (6123, 3071, 3074, 6042, 3078, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the broad coverage of driver-training and credentialing processes, while the available records do not establish their scale, outcomes, or any specific compliance concern.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A connected framework spanning training and credentials
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central activity, Driver Training, Testing, Licensing, and Certification, encompasses driver-training courses, certificate issuance and reissuance, qualification testing, and driver-license issuance. The relationships therefore show a framework linking training and assessment with multiple credential-related administrative processes. [Data: Entities (1509); Relationships (6123, 3071, 3074, 6042, 3078)]

The records identify the scope of the processes but do not establish how frequently they occur, how many people they affect, or whether the framework is implemented effectively. [Data: Entities (1509); Relationships (6123, 3071, 3074, 6042, 3078)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Course records include training and completion details
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver-training course may be recorded by identifier and name, with details that can include its training period, practical training distance, completion result, and completion time. This indicates that the course record is described as capable of capturing both participation-related details and completion information. [Data: Entities (1493)]

A separate relationship states that course completion is recorded alongside details of an issued confirmation document. The data describes these recordkeeping elements but does not provide example course records or evidence about the accuracy or retention of such records. [Data: Entities (1492, 1493); Relationships (6120)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A facility connects course delivery with certificate issuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver-training and certificate-issuing facility is described as responsible for providing training and issuing certificates related to road-traffic legal-knowledge training. The relationships specifically link the facility to the driver-training course and identify it as responsible for training and certificate issuance. [Data: Entities (1481, 1493); Relationships (6110, 3073)]

The records identify a functional role, but do not name a particular facility or provide information about its oversight, capacity, performance, or compliance history. [Data: Entities (1481); Relationships (6110, 3073)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Testing is linked to certificate issuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A certificate qualification test is described as determining whether a certificate can be issued, and the test is included among the processes covered by the broader framework. Certificate issuance is also identified as a covered process. [Data: Entities (766, 764, 1509); Relationships (3074, 3078)]

This establishes a stated connection between assessment and credential issuance, but the supplied records do not specify test standards, pass thresholds, appeal procedures, or results for any individual. [Data: Entities (766, 764); Relationships (3074, 3078)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certificate exchanges and reissuances have an assigned authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Certificate exchange or reissuance is included in the framework, and a separately identified authority is described as responsible for carrying out those actions. The process description says that the date and responsible authority are included, while the relationship connects the authority to the reissuance process. [Data: Entities (763, 762); Relationships (3070, 3071)]

The data establishes the existence of an assigned administrative role but does not identify the authority by name or document particular exchanges, reissuances, delays, or disputes. [Data: Entities (762, 763); Relationships (3070)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-license issuance is included, but its procedure is not detailed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driver-license issuance is expressly listed as one of the processes covered by the broader training, testing, licensing, and certification activity. [Data: Entities (1457, 1509); Relationships (6042)]

Beyond that inclusion, the provided records do not describe license eligibility rules, issuing bodies, processing steps, or individual issuance cases. The available evidence therefore supports its place in the framework, not conclusions about how licensing is administered in practice. [Data: Entities (1457); Relationships (6042)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is administrative and does not establish reputation or compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships describe process categories, record details, and assigned functions. They contain no claims or records about violations, legal disputes, adverse outcomes, public reputation, or technical systems. [Data: Entities (1509, 1493, 764, 763, 1481); Relationships (6123, 3071, 3074, 6110, 3070)]

Accordingly, the community can be assessed as a connected administrative process area, but the available information does not support a conclusion that any entity is compliant or noncompliant, or that a specific harm has occurred. [Data: Entities (1509, 1493, 764, 763, 1481); Relationships (6123, 3071, 3074, 6110, 3070)]

v.tieu_de: Applicant Organizations and Priority-Vehicle Signal Permits
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative permitting workflow for agencies or organizations seeking permission to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. The applicant is the central entity, connected to dossier submission, permit issuance or reissuance, and notices about ineligible applications. Insufficient submissions may prompt a request to supplement or complete the application, or a refusal to process it. In emergencies, advance communication with the competent authority is allowed, but the required dossier must still be submitted afterward. The records describe regulatory procedures and requirements, not evidence of noncompliance or misuse.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational and regulatory importance because it governs permits for signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, while the records establish no specific violation or harmful conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The applicant organization is the workflow’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The agency or organization seeking the permit is connected to the main procedural steps: receiving notices about ineligible applications, requesting issuance or reissuance, and submitting the application dossier. Its degree of 9 is the highest among the listed entities, consistent with its central position in the described community. [Data: Entities (196); Relationships (595, 596, 590)]

The records define a regulated application process, but do not identify any particular applicant or establish that an applicant has breached the requirements. [Data: Entities (196)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit issuance and reissuance depend on an application procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The permit issuance or reissuance procedure covers permission to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. The applicant follows this procedure, and submission of the required dossier is identified as a required step. [Data: Entities (3694); Relationships (596, 601)]

The available information describes the process rather than its outcomes; it does not state that any permit was granted, renewed, or denied in a specific case. [Data: Entities (3694); Relationships (596, 601)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dossier submission is a required part of the application
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The application dossier consists of required documents for a permit to use a signal-emitting device on a priority vehicle. The applicant is linked directly to dossier submission, and the dossier submission is in turn linked to the permit procedure. [Data: Entities (200); Relationships (590, 601)]

The records also specify that an applicant who contacts the competent authority in advance during an emergency must submit the required dossier immediately afterward. [Data: Entities (196, 200); Relationships (590)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Insufficient applications may lead to supplementation or refusal
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When an application or its documents are insufficient, the licensing authority may request that the applicant supplement or complete them. This is described as one possible response associated with a notice of an ineligible application. [Data: Entities (4158); Relationships (9224)]

Another possible response is refusal to process an administrative application that does not meet permit requirements; the reason must be stated. The records present these as procedural responses, not as actions taken against a named applicant. [Data: Entities (4057); Relationships (9223)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Notices communicate application deficiencies and procedural outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A notice of an ineligible application concerns an agency’s or organization’s application and identifies that its application or documents do not meet permit requirements, including the reason. Delivery may occur through an available account or a formal administrative response. [Data: Entities (3270, 196); Relationships (595)]

The described notice process is connected to both possible supplementation and refusal to process. The records do not provide details of any actual notice, its recipient, or a specific deficiency. [Data: Entities (3270, 4158, 4057); Relationships (9224, 9223)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam National Identification Application and Public Service Portal
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal, two digital channels connected to a range of administrative procedures. The procedures include smart traffic vehicle licensing and permit changes or reissuance, examination registration, and approvals involving foreign vehicles. The channels also support application notifications and, where specified, identity verification, administrative-violation document delivery, and driver’s-license point-status updates. The supplied data describes services and procedural roles but does not establish whether the systems or users comply with applicable requirements, or provide evidence of reputational issues.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-service importance because national digital platforms connect identity functions to multiple administrative, licensing, examination, and enforcement-related processes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two national digital channels form the community’s hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal are identified as digital channels for submitting covered applications and for receiving documents concerning administrative violations. Their relationship makes them central connecting points across the procedures represented in the community. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209); Relationships (9113)]

Both platforms are described as serving individuals and organizations in interactions with competent authorities. The data supports their broad administrative role, but does not specify platform availability, security performance, or user volumes. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The channels support multiple permit and licensing procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal are each listed as submission channels for smart traffic vehicle operating authorization and for changing or reissuing a vehicle operating permit. The portal is also linked to the smart traffic vehicle operating-permit procedure and new permit issuance, while the application is linked to new issuance and permit-procedure notices. [Data: Entities (4665, 4666, 4663, 3883); Relationships (9132, 9120, 9133, 9121, 9128, +more)]

These connections indicate that the platforms support several stages and types of permit administration. The evidence describes available procedural channels; it does not establish that any particular application was approved or that a permit was issued. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209, 4663, 4665, 4666)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Application tracking and notices are part of the administrative workflow
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The portal is described as enabling applicants to track processing and receive notices, including notices that submissions are incomplete, refused, or ineligible. The National Identification Application is likewise described as a channel for notices about incomplete or refused applications. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209)]

The relationships connect both digital channels to permit-related procedures and to foreign-vehicle approval notices. This evidences a role in communicating application status and deficiencies, though the data does not describe response times or the effectiveness of those notices. [Data: Relationships (9116, 9119, 9127, 9131, 85, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign-vehicle approvals involve businesses and a receiving authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described approval procedure concerns Vietnamese international travel service businesses organizing foreign nationals bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, and cases involving right-hand-drive cars for non-tourism purposes. The procedure also covers changes to previously approved information and review of submitted applications. [Data: Entities (39, 2745)]

International travel service businesses may submit application dossiers through either digital channel, and a receiving agency reviews and processes applications and documents. The data identifies the actors and channels but does not report individual approvals or findings of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (4040, 2745); Relationships (8064, 8065, 87)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Identity verification is linked to examination registration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Examination registration concerns applying for the road traffic law knowledge examination, including submitting a registration dossier and, for online applicants, choosing a testing authority and examination date. Both digital channels are identified as submission routes for registration documents. [Data: Entities (1859); Relationships (6795, 6796)]

The electronic identification and authentication system is accessed through the National Identification Application and may provide candidate identity information for comparison with examination-application details. This indicates an identity-verification function associated with the examination process, without specifying its accuracy or operational outcomes. [Data: Entities (1752); Relationships (6634)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The platforms are associated with enforcement-related digital functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal are described as channels through which administrative-violation documents may be delivered to users’ accounts. The portal also provides public access to information from the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209); Relationships (9113)]

The National Identification Application may also display updates to a driver’s deducted- or restored-points status when a driving licence is represented as a data message. The data establishes these described functions, but does not provide details about specific violations, individuals, or enforcement results. [Data: Entities (1566, 3205); Relationships (6306)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Applicants may act through authorized representatives
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For a smart traffic vehicle permit change or reissuance, an owner or an authorized representative may submit the electronic form or deliver a request to the authority that previously issued the permit. The representative is described as acting on the vehicle owner’s behalf, including in permit-change, reissuance, or surrender matters. [Data: Entities (4666, 623)]

The relationship specifically confirms that a legally authorized representative may submit the change-or-reissuance application. This identifies a delegated route in the procedure; the supplied information does not describe how authorization is verified in individual cases. [Data: Relationships (2794)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP: Traffic Permits and Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP and its changes to Vietnamese road-traffic rules and administrative procedures. The decree is linked to permit issuance, replacement or reissuance, revocation, emergency applications, and transitional withdrawal and reissuance of certain priority-vehicle signal-device permits. It also addresses foreign motor vehicles and transport-related procedures, with specified provisions taking effect on 1 July 2027. The records describe regulatory processes and responsibilities, but do not establish whether any entity has complied with them in practice. [Data: Entities (1297, 2716, 2717, 2718, 1770); Relationships (5650, 5651, 5652, 5653, 5661, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad significance for road-traffic administration and permitting, while the records provide no evidence of actual violations or demonstrated adverse impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree is the community’s central regulatory instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP is described as amending Vietnamese regulations on road traffic, permits, and transport-related procedures. Its provisions cover priority-vehicle signal devices, intelligent traffic vehicles, and foreign motor vehicles operating in Vietnam, making it the central connection among the entities in this community. [Data: Entities (1297)]

The records identify amendments to Articles 20, 22, and 35, alongside additions to permit procedures and provisions on implementation. They do not provide the text or subject matter of every referenced amendment in detail. [Data: Entities (1297, 180, 171, 266); Relationships (559, 527, 924)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent traffic vehicle permits have defined administrative pathways
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree adds Article 25a, which sets out procedures for issuing, replacing or reissuing, and revoking intelligent traffic vehicle operating permits. Issuance is described as taking up to five working days after the authority receives an application; replacement or reissuance is described as taking up to two working days. [Data: Entities (2716, 2717); Relationships (5651, 5652)]

For revocation, the process applies in circumstances specified in Article 25, clause 5, and requires the permit to be surrendered to the competent issuing authority. The records do not specify the underlying revocation circumstances. [Data: Entities (2718); Relationships (5653)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Owners may act through authorized representatives
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define authorized representatives as persons permitted by law to act for an intelligent traffic vehicle owner. They may submit applications to replace or reissue a permit and surrender a permit subject to revocation on the owner’s behalf. [Data: Entities (624); Relationships (2796, 2797)]

This establishes a representative route for the specified administrative steps; the records do not describe additional eligibility checks or the documentation required to prove representation. [Data: Entities (624, 2717, 2718); Relationships (2796, 2797)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency applications include advance consultation
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 8 is associated with an emergency permit application process in which an applicant may consult the competent authority in advance and then submit the required application documents. The provided description does not state a processing deadline or define which circumstances qualify as emergencies. [Data: Entities (1770, 1297); Relationships (5650)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transitional rules address existing signal-device permits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree’s transitional provisions cover administrative-procedure files received by the competent authority or postmarked before the decree takes effect, as well as existing permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. [Data: Entities (1297, 1304); Relationships (5648)]

Where permits for military-force priority vehicles do not comply with the decree, the described procedure requires the holder to withdraw the existing permit and request a new one. The records identify license-holding agencies and organizations as responsible for taking those steps when required. [Data: Entities (3697, 2898); Relationships (5661, 8579)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign-vehicle and transport provisions have a specified future effective date
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18 addresses procedures for approving international travel service businesses that organize foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as procedures for bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnam for non-tourism purposes. The decree’s description also identifies databases concerning foreign motor vehicles driven by foreign nationals in Vietnam and transport businesses and their vehicle insignia. [Data: Entities (1297)]

The specified provisions take effect on 1 July 2027. The records provide this commencement date but do not indicate how implementation will be carried out or whether the relevant databases and procedures are currently operational. [Data: Entities (1741, 3994); Relationships (5649, 5664)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory obligations, not proven compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available information concerns the decree’s rules, administrative processes, deadlines, and assigned procedural responsibilities. It does not report enforcement actions, violations, permit outcomes, or assessments of whether any applicant, permit holder, agency, or organization has complied. Accordingly, legal-compliance conclusions about actual conduct cannot be drawn from these records. [Data: Entities (1297, 2716, 2717, 2718, 3697); Relationships (5651, 5652, 5653, 5661)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Licensing Authority and Vehicle Permit System
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on the Licensing Authority, which receives and reviews applications and decides whether to issue, renew, replace, reissue, or refuse permits. Its processes connect applicants and permit procedures with the Vehicle Registration and Management System, whose data is used to check application information. The records describe defined processing timelines, procedures for incomplete or ineligible submissions, and a separate notification duty concerning specified foreign vehicles. They provide no evidence of misconduct or other adverse claims. [Data: Entities (2904, 5467, 3379, 2835, 2554); Relationships (8602, 8588, 8590, 8421, 7815)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high importance because it combines a central public licensing function with vehicle-data checks and several permit processes, while the records describe no adverse conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Licensing Authority is the community’s operational hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Licensing Authority is described as the competent public authority responsible for receiving, reviewing, and deciding applications for permits and licenses.
