The community also includes related licensing processes for priority-vehicle signal devices and intelligent transport vehicle permits. The records describe regulatory procedures and responsibilities, not evidence of actual violations or adverse conduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-substantial administrative importance because it connects travel approvals, foreign visitors’ permitted stays, incident reporting, and several vehicle-permit processes, while the data provides no evidence of actual noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Competent Licensing Authority is the community’s central decision and coordination point
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority receives applications from Vietnamese international travel service enterprises, decides whether to approve covered arrangements, and receives notices and follow-up reports when approved details change or an incident affects departure. It also sends approval documents to relevant provincial and municipal People’s Committees for coordination and management. [Data: Entities (1052, 4108); Relationships (3817, 3802, 3811)]

The authority’s role is defined by the relevant licensing matter; the entity description says the applicable rules may not name the authority specifically. Accordingly, the records support describing its functions, but do not identify a particular government department. [Data: Entities (1052)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Travel enterprises organize foreign-vehicle tourism and carry defined compliance responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnamese international travel service enterprises may organize tourism trips in which foreign visitors bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam, subject to prior approval. The enterprises submit relevant documents and information to the competent authority. [Data: Entities (5549, 2343); Relationships (7534, 7518, 3817)]

The enterprises are responsible for the accuracy and legality of documents and information concerning foreign nationals and vehicles. They must notify the authority if previously approved details change, and take specified action when an incident delays departure. These are stated obligations; the records do not establish whether any enterprise has breached them. [Data: Entities (5549); Relationships (3817, 7871, 5752)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Changes to travel arrangements and delayed departures trigger notification procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A written notice is required before implementing changes to a route, itinerary, or departure time, and when a foreign visitor or vehicle will depart later than approved or exceed the maximum permitted stay. The notice is sent to the authority that previously granted approval. [Data: Entities (3274, 1318); Relationships (3802, 3791, 3788)]

An incident is defined in this dataset as an unforeseen occurrence affecting departure timing, and delayed departure includes leaving later than approved or exceeding the permitted stay. The authority is to be informed, with a written report submitted after the incident is resolved. [Data: Entities (2631, 1318); Relationships (3792, 5750)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Local police are part of the incident-response chain
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When an incident delays departure, the responsible travel business must promptly contact the police agency in the place where the incident occurs. This places local police alongside the previously approving authority in the described reporting process. [Data: Entities (2929, 5549, 2631); Relationships (8620, 7870, 5751)]

The information describes a notification responsibility, not the police agency’s subsequent actions or the outcome of any incident. No specific incident or enforcement action is recorded. [Data: Entities (2929, 2631); Relationships (8620, 7870)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign travelers’ departure timing is linked to Vietnam’s foreigner-residence framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign travelers may take part in tourism arrangements involving foreign motor vehicles organized by Vietnamese international travel service enterprises. Changes to travelers’ information or departure timing must be reported to the authority that previously approved the arrangements. [Data: Entities (2339, 5549); Relationships (7518, 3791)]

The Law on Entry, Exit, Transit, and Residence of Foreigners in Vietnam is identified as the framework for determining the maximum permitted stay. A departure delay that may exceed that limit can therefore trigger the described notification procedure. [Data: Entities (2846, 1318); Relationships (7515, 5750, 3802)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority also handles specialized vehicle-permit processes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Eligible agencies and organizations may apply for new or replacement permits to use signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles. The competent authority receives these applications and may access supporting documents through a connected shared database, avoiding separate submission where the documents are available there. [Data: Entities (1755, 3875, 1052); Relationships (3790, 3807, 6640)]

The authority’s described functions extend beyond tourism approvals to intelligent transport vehicle operating permits: the authority that issued such a permit receives it and carries out its revocation when required. The records describe the procedure but do not state that a revocation has occurred. [Data: Entities (1052, 4233); Relationships (3812)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence indicates regulatory significance, not demonstrated misconduct or reputational harm
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community covers government approvals, documentation duties, change notices, incident reporting, foreign-stay timing, and vehicle-related permits. These interconnected responsibilities make it relevant to administrative and compliance oversight. [Data: Entities (1052, 5549, 3274, 3875, 4233); Relationships (3817, 3802, 3792, 3807, 3812)]

The supplied records state legal roles and procedures but contain no allegations, findings of noncompliance, enforcement outcomes, or reputation assessments. The community’s impact rating therefore reflects the importance of the regulatory functions described, rather than an inference that the entities have acted improperly. [Data: Entities (1052, 5549, 2631); Relationships (3817, 7871, 3812)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Provincial and Municipal People's Committees
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Provincial and Municipal People’s Committees and their chairpersons, with local functional authorities carrying out management and inspection under the committees’ direction. The committees represent relevant provinces and centrally governed cities and are responsible for coordinating matters involving foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles, including notifying representatives of intergovernmental international organizations about relevant violations, accidents, or vehicle incidents. The information describes administrative responsibilities under the cited decrees, but does not establish implementation outcomes, technical systems, or specific compliance incidents. [Data: Entities (3955, 785, 2927, 4107, 4153); Relationships (3129, 8616, 9793, 9794, 9781)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial administrative importance because it coordinates provincial and municipal oversight of foreign nationals and vehicles, while the supplied data indicates no specific adverse event or implementation failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Committees are the community’s central coordinating bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and Municipal People’s Committees are the central entities in this network. They represent the provinces and centrally governed cities covered by the decree and direct local authorities responsible for managing and inspecting foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles. [Data: Entities (3955, 4107, 2927); Relationships (8616, 9793, 9781)]

Their responsibilities give them a coordinating role across local administration. The records describe this remit but do not identify particular enforcement actions or outcomes. [Data: Entities (3955); Relationships (8616, 9793)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Chairpersons lead the committees and have implementation responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chairpersons of provincial and municipal People’s Committees lead their respective committees. The supplied entity description also assigns them responsibility for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (785, 3955); Relationships (3129)]

The committee description additionally says that chairpersons are responsible for implementing Decrees 238/2026/ND-CP and 168/2024/ND-CP. The data specifies these duties but provides no evidence about whether implementation has been completed or how effectively it is carried out. [Data: Entities (3955, 785)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Local functional authorities carry out management and inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Local functional authorities are described as the government agencies tasked with managing and inspecting foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles. The committees direct these authorities in carrying out that work, establishing a chain of responsibility from the committees to local agencies. [Data: Entities (2927, 3955); Relationships (8616)]

This supports a finding of operational and administrative capacity, but the records do not specify particular agencies, inspection procedures, staffing, or technical tools. [Data: Entities (2927, 3955); Relationships (8616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversight applies across relevant provinces and centrally governed cities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relevant provinces and centrally governed cities are described as the jurisdictions whose People’s Committees may receive approval documents and whose authorities may coordinate management of approved vehicle movements. The committees represent these jurisdictions within the decree’s framework. [Data: Entities (4107, 3955); Relationships (9793)]

A separate entity identifies provinces and cities as the jurisdictions whose People’s Committees are covered by implementation responsibilities. The provided information establishes the geographic-administrative scope in general terms, without listing specific localities. [Data: Entities (3943, 3955); Relationships (9781)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: International-organization representatives are included in incident notifications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The committees are responsible for notifying representatives of intergovernmental international organizations in Vietnam about relevant legal violations, traffic accidents, or vehicle incidents involving foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles. This creates a notification link between local administrative coordination and those representatives. [Data: Entities (4153, 3955); Relationships (9794)]

The records describe a notification responsibility, not evidence that any violation or accident occurred, or that a notification was made in a particular case. [Data: Entities (4153, 3955); Relationships (9794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes administrative duties, not compliance outcomes or technical capabilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information identifies responsible bodies, oversight functions, and notification and coordination duties. It does not report specific breaches, enforcement results, or performance measures, so no conclusion about actual compliance or effectiveness is supported. [Data: Entities (3955, 785, 2927, 4153); Relationships (3129, 8616, 9794)]

Likewise, although the committees receive copies of relevant approval documents to support coordination and management, the records do not describe digital infrastructure, specialized technical systems, or other technological capabilities. [Data: Entities (3955, 4107)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Road-Transport Decree 10/2020 and Its Amendments
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP, a Vietnamese regulation concerning automobile road-transport businesses and business conditions. It was amended and supplemented by Decrees No. 47/2022/NĐ-CP and No. 41/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 38 of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP provides for the repeal of eight specified provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP, linking the original decree, its amendments, and a later repeal mechanism. The information indicates regulatory significance and a need to track changes, but does not describe enforcement, compliance outcomes, or effects on specific businesses. [Data: Entities (1307, 423, 1315, 1314, 988); Relationships (5687, 5688, 1800, 1801, 1802)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it documents amendments and repeals within a Vietnamese regulatory framework for automobile road-transport businesses, while providing no evidence of specific enforcement or harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP is the central regulatory instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP is described as a Vietnamese government decree dated January 17, 2020, concerning the business and business conditions of road transport by automobile. It is the central entity in the supplied relationships: several provisions are identified as parts of it, and later decrees are linked to it through amendments and repeals. [Data: Entities (1307); Relationships (3366, 3512, 3393, 3437, 3392)]

Its centrality makes the decree and its current version important reference points for understanding the other records in this community. The data establishes its subject matter and legislative connections, but does not specify the detailed requirements imposed on transport businesses. [Data: Entities (1307); Relationships (5687, 5688)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 38 of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP establishes a repeal mechanism
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 38 is titled “Effectiveness of implementation,” and clause 2 specifies repeals that take effect from the date the decree comes into force. The supplied relationships connect Article 38 to eight provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP that it repeals. [Data: Entities (423); Relationships (1799, 1800, 1801, 1802, 1803, +more)]

This establishes a formal relationship between the later decree and particular earlier provisions. The provided information does not state the commencement date of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP, so no specific date for the repeals can be determined from these records. [Data: Entities (423, 1307)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Eight specified provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP are identified as repealed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed repealed material comprises Article 12; clauses 2 of Article 13 and Article 14; clause 13 of Article 22; clause 9 of Article 23; clause 3 of Article 26; and clauses 5 and 8 of Article 34. Each is described as repealed under Article 38(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (248, 905, 906, 884, 995); Relationships (800, 1799, 1800, 1801, 1802, +more)]

The listed changes affect multiple parts of the earlier decree rather than a single provision. The records identify which provisions are repealed, but do not provide their text or explain the substantive policy consequences of removing them. [Data: Entities (248, 905, 906, 884, 995, +more); Relationships (800, 1799, 1800, 1801, 1802, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The original decree was amended in 2022 and 2024
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree No. 47/2022/NĐ-CP, dated July 19, 2022, amended and supplemented Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP. Decree No. 41/2024/NĐ-CP, dated April 16, 2024, also amended and supplemented it. [Data: Entities (1315, 1314, 1307); Relationships (5688, 5687)]

These amendments, followed by the specified repeals under Article 38 of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP, show that the regulatory text has undergone multiple changes. The supplied records do not identify which provisions were changed by the 2022 and 2024 amendments or how those changes relate substantively to the later repeals. [Data: Entities (1315, 1314, 423); Relationships (5688, 5687, 1799, 1800, 1801)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Version tracking is relevant for interpreting the regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records connect Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP to two amending decrees and identify eight provisions later repealed through Article 38(2) of Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP. This sequence makes it important to distinguish the original text from its amended and repealed provisions when using the regulation. [Data: Entities (1307, 1315, 1314, 423, 988); Relationships (5687, 5688, 1799, 1800, 1801, +more)]

For decision-makers, checking the applicable version and the status of individual provisions would be a prudent next step before relying on this material. That is a process implication of the recorded amendments and repeals, not evidence that any particular business has failed to comply. [Data: Entities (1307, 423); Relationships (5687, 5688, 1799, 1800, 1801, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish legal changes but not compliance or reputational outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied data describes decrees, provisions, amendments, and repeals. It does not report inspections, enforcement actions, court decisions, business responses, or findings of noncompliance; therefore, no conclusion about the compliance record or conduct of particular transport businesses is supported. [Data: Entities (1307, 423, 1315, 1314); Relationships (5687, 5688, 1799, 1800, 1801)]

Likewise, the information does not assess technical capabilities, public reputation, or operational impact on named organizations. The community's significance in this dataset is its documented regulatory structure and change history, rather than evidence of specific organizational behavior or harm. [Data: Entities (1307, 423, 1315, 1314)]

v.tieu_de: People’s Committees and Decree 151/2024/ND-CP
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the People’s Committees of provinces and centrally run cities and their role in implementing Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. The committees are linked to provinces and centrally run cities as local government bodies, while their chairpersons lead the respective committees and are identified as responsible for implementation. The provided information also places provincial police traffic divisions among the authorities described in Article 23. The community therefore has administrative significance, but the records do not establish specific compliance outcomes or adverse impacts. [Data: Entities (3672, 3938, 784, 760); Relationships (9541, 3125, 3068)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community merits a moderate-to-high impact rating because it concerns decree implementation across provincial and centrally run city governments, although no specific outcomes or harms are documented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: People’s Committees are the community’s central administrative bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The People’s Committees of provinces and centrally run cities are described as local government bodies and the central institutional entity in this network. Their stated role includes receiving notification of approvals to coordinate management. [Data: Entities (3672); Relationships (9541, 3068)]

The network connects these committees to both provinces and centrally run cities, indicating that the described administrative structure covers both types of jurisdictions. The records identify responsibilities but do not describe particular decisions or implementation results. [Data: Entities (3672, 3938, 760); Relationships (9541, 3068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Chairpersons are assigned responsibility for implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chairpersons of provincial and centrally run city People’s Committees are identified as responsible for implementing Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. A relationship record states that they lead their respective committees. [Data: Entities (784, 3672); Relationships (3125)]

This places implementation responsibility with named leadership roles within the local-government structure. The supplied data does not specify what implementation actions have occurred or whether the decree has been fully or effectively implemented. [Data: Entities (784, 3672); Relationships (3125)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The administrative scope includes provinces and centrally run cities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provinces are described as administrative areas whose People’s Committee chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree. The People’s Committees are explicitly linked to provinces as their local government bodies. [Data: Entities (3938, 3672); Relationships (9541)]

Centrally run cities are also within the stated scope: their People’s Committee chairpersons have implementation responsibility, and their committees are described as local government bodies for those cities. [Data: Entities (760, 784, 3672); Relationships (3068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify a role for provincial police traffic divisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provinces entity description states that provincial police traffic divisions are among the authorities described in Article 23. This is the only supplied detail about those divisions’ connection to the decree-related framework. [Data: Entities (3938)]

The records do not specify the divisions’ particular duties, powers, or activities under Article 23. Their inclusion should therefore be treated as a documented scope indicator, not evidence of any specific enforcement action. [Data: Entities (3938)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports administrative significance, not a finding of compliance or misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes government bodies, leadership responsibilities, and decree implementation roles, supporting the assessment that the community has administrative reach across provinces and centrally run cities. [Data: Entities (3672, 3938, 784, 760); Relationships (9541, 3125, 3068)]

No supplied record reports compliance results, violations, enforcement outcomes, or harm. The community’s impact rating therefore reflects the importance and breadth of the described responsibilities rather than a documented adverse event. [Data: Entities (3672, 3938, 784, 760); Relationships (9541, 3125, 3068)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Safety and Environmental Certification
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Technical Safety and Environmental Protection Certification, a process covering technical safety, environmental protection, and vehicle energy consumption. It is linked to importation, assembly, and manufacture of motor vehicles and parts, indicating that the described certification scope spans all three activities. The records describe the process and its scope but do not provide certification outcomes, compliance findings, or information about particular organizations or products.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because the certification process applies across vehicle importation, assembly, and manufacture, but the records provide no evidence of specific compliance outcomes or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certification is the community's central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Technical Safety and Environmental Protection Certification is described as a process for assessing and certifying the technical safety and environmental protection quality of motor vehicles, specialized motor vehicles or motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts. It also covers motor vehicle energy consumption. [Data: Entities (4862)]

The three activity entities in the community each connect to this certification process, making it the central link among them. [Data: Relationships (7826, 2731, 8680)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described scope includes imported vehicles and parts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Importation of motor vehicles and motor vehicle parts is included in the certification framework described in the records. The relationship specifically states that certification applies to vehicles and parts in importation. [Data: Entities (2566, 4862); Relationships (7826)]

The records establish that importation falls within the described scope, but do not state whether any particular import or product has been certified or found compliant.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Assembly is also within the certification scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The assembly activity is described in relation to technical safety quality and environmental protection. Its relationship to the certification process specifies that certification applies to motor vehicles and parts in assembly. [Data: Entities (591, 4862); Relationships (2731)]

No specific assembly facility, product assessment, or certification result is identified in the supplied records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Manufacturing is covered by the same process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The manufacture activity is described in relation to technical safety quality and environmental protection. The corresponding relationship states that certification applies to vehicles and parts in manufacture. [Data: Entities (2976, 4862); Relationships (8680)]

This places manufacturing alongside importation and assembly within the process's described scope; the records do not give details about manufacturers or the results of any assessments.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes regulatory scope, not compliance performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Taken together, the records connect importation, assembly, and manufacture to one certification process, and describe the process's coverage of safety, environmental protection, and vehicle energy consumption. [Data: Entities (4862, 2566, 591, 2976); Relationships (7826, 2731, 8680)]

The supplied information does not report violations, enforcement actions, technical capabilities of particular entities, or outcomes of certification assessments. Therefore, it supports identifying the scope of the process, but not conclusions about actual compliance or reputation.

v.tieu_de: Specialized Motorcycle Road-Traffic Knowledge Certification
v.tom_tat: This community describes a road-traffic legal-knowledge process for operators of specialized motorcycles, linked in the entity descriptions to Article 63 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Its entities cover training, examination, and certificate issuance: the relationships describe training followed by examination and identify the examination as part of certificate issuance. The records establish a regulatory and administrative focus but provide no details about implementation, compliance outcomes, or safety effects. [Data: Entities (1855, 5070, 765); Relationships (3076, 6791)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate public-interest significance because it concerns a statutory knowledge and certification process, but the records provide no evidence of violations, harmful outcomes, or operational scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A process concerning specialized motorcycle operators
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The examination, training, and certificate-issuance entities are each described as relating to road-traffic legal knowledge for operators of specialized motorcycles. The descriptions associate these activities with Article 63 of Law 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (1855, 5070, 765)]

The records do not specify which operators are covered in practice, how the activities are administered, or what consequences follow from completing or not completing them.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training is described as preceding examination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship between examination and training states that the text describes training followed by examination as part of the certification process. This supports a stated sequence from training to examination, without specifying the curriculum, assessment format, or timing. [Data: Relationships (6791)]

The training entity is specifically described as training in road-traffic legal knowledge for specialized motorcycle operators. [Data: Entities (5070)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examination is part of certificate issuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship records that the examination is part of the process for issuing certificates. This links the examination to the certificate-issuance activity, but does not state whether passing is the only condition for receiving a certificate. [Data: Relationships (3076)]

The certificate-issuance entity describes certificates as confirming road-traffic legal knowledge for operators of specialized motorcycles. [Data: Entities (765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe connected stages, not a complete regulatory procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Together, the relationships connect training to examination and examination to certificate issuance, outlining key activities in a certification process. [Data: Relationships (3076, 6791)]

The supplied records do not detail eligibility, responsible authorities, certificate validity, renewal, exemptions, or enforcement. Those aspects therefore cannot be assessed from this community data.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and safety outcomes are not evidenced
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions establish that the process concerns legal knowledge and specialized motorcycle operators, and that it is associated with a cited law. [Data: Entities (1855, 5070, 765)]

No supplied record reports compliance rates, examination results, legal violations, accident trends, or effects on road safety. The community can be identified as regulatory in subject matter, but its actual performance or impact cannot be determined from these records.

v.tieu_de: Article 60 and Driver Licence Upgrade Training
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 60 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and four related descriptions of driver licence upgrade training. Article 60 is connected to training requirements for specified licence categories, including upgrades; the supplied information describes training rules but does not establish whether any person or organization complies with them. [Data: Entities (525, 1498, 1456, 1514, 1499); Relationships (2436, 2438, 2440, 2439)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it concerns statutory driver-training requirements, but the data describe rules and do not indicate a specific compliance issue or harmful activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 60 is the central legal reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 60 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 addresses training required to obtain a driving licence or upgrade to another category. The entity description states that applicants must complete theoretical and practical training under the curriculum for the relevant class, and that matters concerning driver training are to be regulated by the Minister of Construction. [Data: Entities (525)]

The four listed upgrade-training entities are each linked directly to Article 60, making it the organizing reference for this community. [Data: Relationships (2436, 2438, 2440, 2439)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community focuses on licence-category upgrades
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The related entities describe training for people upgrading between licence categories, rather than a specific driver, training provider, or enforcement case. The relationships characterize Article 60 as setting out or specifying upgrade-training requirements. [Data: Entities (1498, 1456, 1514, 1499); Relationships (2436, 2438, 2439, 2440)]

The records do not identify any individual’s training history or state whether a particular upgrade applicant has met the requirements. [Data: Entities (1498, 1456, 1514, 1499); Relationships (2436, 2438, 2439, 2440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several records describe overlapping upgrade-training concepts
phat_hien.giai_thich: The four related entities use similar descriptions of driver training for licence upgrades, and each has a direct relationship to Article 60. This indicates that the community groups multiple formulations of the same broad regulatory topic; the data do not clarify whether each record represents a distinct program or a separate legal obligation. [Data: Entities (1498, 1456, 1514, 1499); Relationships (2436, 2438, 2439, 2440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify particular upgrade categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One entity describes upgrading from category B to C1, C, D1, or D2. Another identifies training for specified classes including C, D1, D2, D, BE, C1E, CE, D1E, D2E, and DE, subject to conditions in Article 60, Clauses 3 and 4. [Data: Entities (1498, 1456)]

A separate entity describes upgrades from C1 to C, D1, or D2 and associates that training with Clause 3 of Article 60. These descriptions specify scope, but the records do not provide the detailed conditions or curricula. [Data: Entities (1514); Relationships (2440)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied information does not establish compliance or enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe statutory training requirements and their relationship to Article 60, but they contain no allegations, inspection results, penalties, or findings about whether any person or organization followed the rules. Accordingly, no conclusion about actual legal compliance or noncompliance is supported. [Data: Entities (525, 1498, 1456, 1514, 1499); Relationships (2436, 2438, 2440, 2439)]

v.tieu_de: Driving Licence Upgrade Training and Class C-to-D Upgrades
v.tom_tat: This community consists of driving-licence upgrade training and three related upgrade paths: class C to class D, D1, and D2. The training is linked to each path, and the entity descriptions identify the upgrades as included under Article 60, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The available information describes the training’s scope and these legal references, but does not establish training outcomes or compliance status. [Data: Entities (1627, 846, 847, 848); Relationships (3313, 3315, 3317)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest, specific importance because it connects licence-upgrade training to three legally referenced upgrade paths, while the supplied records indicate no broader impact or compliance concerns.

phat_hien.tom_tat: One training entity connects the three upgrade paths
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving Licence Upgrade Training is described as training for people seeking to upgrade from class C to class D1, D2, or D. Each of the three upgrade entities has a relationship to this training, making it the community’s central connecting entity. [Data: Entities (1627); Relationships (3313, 3315, 3317)]

The records establish the training’s stated scope but do not describe its provider, delivery method, scale, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (1627)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The class C-to-D path is explicitly represented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Class C to Class D Licence Upgrade is identified as one of the upgrade paths addressed by Article 60, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The relationship record states that the training applies to this upgrade. [Data: Entities (846); Relationships (3313)]

The supplied information does not specify detailed eligibility criteria, procedures, or whether any particular person has completed the training or upgrade. [Data: Entities (846, 1627); Relationships (3313)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The class C-to-D1 path is explicitly represented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Class C to Class D1 Licence Upgrade is described as an upgrade addressed by Article 60, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15, and it is linked to the training as an applicable upgrade. [Data: Entities (847); Relationships (3315)]

No further operational details about this path or its training requirements are provided in the records. [Data: Entities (847, 1627); Relationships (3315)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The class C-to-D2 path is explicitly represented
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Class C to Class D2 Licence Upgrade is likewise identified as covered by Article 60, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Its relationship to the training states that the training applies to the D2 upgrade. [Data: Entities (848); Relationships (3317)]

The records do not provide information about completion, assessment, or outcomes for this upgrade path. [Data: Entities (848, 1627); Relationships (3317)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal references are present, but compliance status is not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions of all three upgrade paths cite Article 60, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. This indicates a stated legal context for the upgrades, but the records do not provide an assessment of whether the training or any related activity complies with applicable requirements. [Data: Entities (846, 847, 848)]

Accordingly, the available data supports describing the community’s stated scope and legal references, not drawing conclusions about regulatory compliance, risk, or effectiveness. [Data: Entities (1627, 846, 847, 848); Relationships (3313, 3315, 3317)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial and Municipal Traffic Police Permit Authority
v.tom_tat: This community centers on provincial and municipal traffic police divisions, including divisions in centrally governed cities. Under Article 23 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, these divisions grant, reissue, and revoke permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles for eligible local bodies, units, and organizations. The data describes a formal administrative role, but does not establish implementation outcomes or compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it includes authorities responsible for administering permits for priority-vehicle signal devices, while the supplied data shows no broader impact or compliance outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic police divisions hold the central administrative role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and municipal traffic police divisions are the community’s central entity and are described as responsible for granting, reissuing, and revoking permits for signal devices on priority vehicles. This makes them the key administrative decision-makers in the process described. [Data: Entities (3960)]

The provided information identifies this authority under Article 23 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP; it does not describe individual decisions or their effects. [Data: Entities (3960)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Centrally governed cities are included in the authority structure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic police divisions covered include those within police forces in centrally governed cities. The relationship establishes that these city divisions are part of the described provincial and municipal traffic-police framework. [Data: Entities (755, 3960); Relationships (3062)]

The entity description also says centrally governed city People’s Committee chairpersons are responsible for implementing the decree. The data does not provide further detail about how that responsibility is carried out. [Data: Entities (755)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Local bodies and organizations are the eligible permit recipients
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Local bodies, units, and organizations in the relevant locality are identified as eligible to receive permits for signal devices on priority vehicles. The relationship connects these potential recipients to the traffic police divisions that administer the permits. [Data: Entities (2925, 3960); Relationships (8612)]

No specific recipient organizations or individual permit applications are identified in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (2925); Relationships (8612)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process includes issuance, renewal, and revocation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The divisions’ stated powers cover granting permits, reissuing them, and revoking them. This indicates that their role spans multiple stages of permit administration rather than being limited to initial issuance. [Data: Entities (3960)]

The available records do not specify application criteria, review timelines, grounds for revocation, or appeal procedures, so these aspects cannot be assessed from the supplied information. [Data: Entities (3960); Relationships (8612)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal responsibilities, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The source describes which authorities are responsible under the decree and which types of entities may receive permits. It provides no evidence about whether the authorities or eligible organizations have complied with the decree, or about enforcement results. [Data: Entities (3960, 755, 2925); Relationships (3062, 8612)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance is supported by its regulatory and administrative function, but the data does not support conclusions about violations, misconduct, or operational effectiveness. [Data: Entities (3960, 755, 2925); Relationships (3062, 8612)]

v.tieu_de: Article 33 Road-Traffic Safety Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 33, described as provisions in both Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP. The linked entities identify passengers and motorcycle drivers as subject to conduct and safety rules, including a prohibition on passengers clinging to, towing, or pushing other vehicles. The material also describes passenger-related fines and restrictions concerning boarding or leaving a passenger vehicle while it is moving. The records concern legal requirements, not documented violations or incidents. [Data: Entities (399, 3552, 3158, 1003); Relationships (1674, 1666, 1673, 3569)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high practical importance because it describes road-safety rules for passengers and drivers, while the records provide no evidence of specific violations or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 33 links related legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 33 is described as referring to provisions in both Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP. The entity description distinguishes the law's rules on drivers, passengers, and carried goods from the decree's administrative penalties for certain passenger conduct. [Data: Entities (399)]

The relationships connect Article 33 to passengers, motorcycle drivers, and the prohibited vehicle interaction, showing that the community covers multiple road-user duties rather than a single isolated behavior. [Data: Relationships (1674, 1666, 1673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger conduct and safety are central
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 33 is linked directly to passengers, and the passenger description says they must follow instructions intended to maintain traffic order and safety. It identifies standing on a motorcycle or its cargo rack and sitting on the handlebars as prohibited conduct. [Data: Entities (3552); Relationships (1674)]

The material also states that passengers must not act in ways that disrupt road traffic order and safety. This makes passenger behavior a central focus of the described rules, alongside the provisions for drivers. [Data: Entities (399, 3552)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passengers may not cling to, tow, or push other vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity describing clinging to, towing, or pushing other vehicles identifies these as prohibited actions for passengers on two- and three-wheeled motorcycles and mopeds participating in road traffic. Article 33 is linked to this prohibition, and a separate relationship connects the prohibited actions to passengers. [Data: Entities (1003); Relationships (1666, 3569)]

This is a specific example of the passenger conduct rules in the community. The provided records describe the prohibition but do not report any particular person committing the conduct. [Data: Entities (1003, 3552)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle drivers are also subject to Article 33 restrictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 33 is linked to motorcycle drivers, with the relationship describing prohibited behaviors for drivers of two-wheeled and three-wheeled motorcycles and motorbikes. The driver entity further describes restrictions on unsafe towing, carrying, or loading practices. [Data: Entities (3158); Relationships (1673)]

The driver description notes an exception referenced in Article 56(1), subject to requirements in Article 56(4). The supplied information does not specify the circumstances of that exception, so its scope cannot be assessed further here. [Data: Entities (3158)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe penalties as well as conduct rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 33 description says the Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP provision sets administrative penalties for passengers who violate traffic order and safety regulations while travelling on passenger vehicles, and provides for confiscation of certain hazardous or prohibited items. [Data: Entities (399)]

The passenger entity gives a fine range of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong for a violation specified in the relevant provision. It also states that allowing someone to board or leave a passenger vehicle while it is moving is a violation. [Data: Entities (3552)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Government Road-Traffic Governance
v.tom_tat: This community comprises the Government of Vietnam, its subordinate government agencies, and the heads responsible for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The Government sets detailed rules for road-traffic order and safety, while agencies implement assigned duties, coordinate on traffic-data systems, and may seek permits for intelligent transport vehicles; agency heads are responsible for implementation. The community has substantial regulatory and administrative reach, although the supplied information does not establish actual compliance outcomes, enforcement effectiveness, or reputational concerns.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad national authority over road-traffic regulation, data governance, licensing, and implementation, rather than evidence of harmful conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A defined government hierarchy directs traffic-safety governance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Government is the national authority responsible for unified state management of road-traffic order and safety. Government agencies are described as subordinate to and operating under the Government, establishing a clear top-level relationship for the community. [Data: Entities (2403, 2404); Relationships (7626)]

The heads of government agencies lead those subordinate bodies and are identified as responsible for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. This connects policy authority with agency-level implementation responsibilities. [Data: Entities (2472); Relationships (7636)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Government has extensive rule-setting responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Government is tasked with issuing detailed regulations across multiple road-traffic matters, including road-safety measures, inspection facilities, vehicle service life, and procedures involving road-traffic authorities. The description also identifies responsibilities concerning driver training and licensing, vehicle plate auctions, and priority-vehicle signaling permits. [Data: Entities (2403)]

These specified responsibilities indicate a broad regulatory remit. The source identifies relevant provisions of Law 36/2024/QH15 and other applicable regulations, but does not provide evidence about implementation results or compliance in practice. [Data: Entities (2403)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic-data governance is a central technical capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Government’s responsibilities include setting rules for the management, collection, use, connection, and sharing of information and data from vehicles, technical equipment, and road-traffic databases. It also regulates the use of technical equipment to detect administrative violations. [Data: Entities (2403)]

Government agencies must coordinate with the Ministry of Public Security to build and manage the road-traffic order and safety database. These descriptions establish data-system responsibilities, but do not specify the systems’ scale, security controls, or operational performance. [Data: Entities (2404)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Agencies have implementation and permit-related duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Government agencies are responsible, within their assigned duties and authority, for implementing Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. Their heads, including heads of agencies attached to the Government, are also assigned responsibility for implementing the decree. [Data: Entities (2404, 2472); Relationships (7636)]

Agencies may own intelligent transport vehicles and prepare and submit application dossiers required for operating permits. The source describes these as permitted activities and responsibilities; it does not indicate how many agencies or vehicles are involved or whether permits have been granted. [Data: Entities (2404)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework governs vehicles, drivers, and road operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Government’s listed responsibilities cover driver training, licensing, testing-center conditions, driving-test permits, motorcycle practice grounds, and the deduction and restoration of driving-licence points. The Government also sets requirements for rudimentary vehicles and their operating conditions. [Data: Entities (2403)]

The described scope extends to vehicle inspection and product or goods recalls, as well as road-traffic procedures and authorities. Together, these duties show that the community’s remit spans multiple stages of vehicle and driver regulation, without establishing specific enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2403)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some responsibilities extend to international arrangements and border procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Government may negotiate and sign international treaties and agreements concerning road-traffic order and safety. This gives the community a stated role in international arrangements within that policy area. [Data: Entities (2403)]

The Government also provides detailed rules for road-traffic procedures concerning the transport of goods within the scope of a smart border gate. The supplied information does not identify particular agreements, border locations, or operational results. [Data: Entities (2403)]

v.tieu_de: Article 62 Driving-License Procedures
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Article 62 of Law 36/2024/QH15, which addresses issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licenses. It is linked to both the administrative procedures covered by the article and an encouraged exchange of qualifying non-expiring licenses issued before July 1, 2012. The available data describes the subject and relationships but does not establish implementation outcomes, compliance issues, or reputational concerns. [Data: Entities (529, 1629, 1894); Relationships (2457, 2458)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited-to-moderate impact as it concerns driving-license administration, but the data provides no evidence of broader consequences or specific risks.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 62 is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 62 is described as a provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 concerning driving-license issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation. Both other entities in the community describe aspects of the article's subject matter, making it the organizing point of the available relationships. [Data: Entities (529); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

The records do not provide the full text of the law or details about how the provision is administered in practice. [Data: Entities (529); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision covers several administrative procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The associated administrative-procedures entity identifies four areas addressed by Article 62: issuing, exchanging, reissuing, and revoking driving licenses. The relationship record directly connects that procedures topic to Article 62. [Data: Entities (1629); Relationships (2457)]

No timelines, eligibility rules, application requirements, or decision-making processes are specified in the supplied records, so those details cannot be assessed from this data. [Data: Entities (1629); Relationships (2457)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Exchange of certain older non-expiring licenses is encouraged
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 62 is described as encouraging the exchange of qualifying non-expiring driving licenses issued before July 1, 2012, for licenses issued under the law. This is a particular exchange policy within the broader licensing subject matter. [Data: Entities (1894); Relationships (2458)]

The records do not state that the exchange is mandatory or provide further information about who qualifies, how exchanges are completed, or how many license holders are affected. [Data: Entities (1894); Relationships (2458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a compact, two-branch structure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied network contains three entities and two relationships. Article 62 links separately to the general administrative procedures and the specific exchange of qualifying older licenses; no relationship between those two topic entities is listed. [Data: Entities (529, 1629, 1894); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

This structure supports identifying Article 62 as the hub of the provided information, but it does not establish whether the records represent every relevant organization, authority, or process connected to the law. [Data: Entities (529, 1629, 1894); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is insufficient to assess compliance or implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available records describe the provision's subject matter and an encouraged license exchange, but provide no information about compliance findings, enforcement actions, implementation results, or disputes. Accordingly, the data does not support a conclusion about legal compliance or operational performance. [Data: Entities (529, 1629, 1894); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

The records also provide no evidence about technical capabilities, organizational reputation, or measurable effects on license holders. These areas remain unassessed rather than established as concerns. [Data: Entities (529, 1629, 1894); Relationships (2457, 2458)]

v.tieu_de: Article 67 Traffic-Control Data Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 67 of Law 36/2024/QH15 and two measures it specifies for detecting legal violations: receiving data from vehicle-weight control facilities and using journey-monitoring and image-recording data. The information describes a legal framework for traffic control and violation detection, including several categories of systems, equipment, and data. The records establish the measures’ stated purpose but do not show how they are implemented or assess their compliance, effectiveness, or effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because Article 67 connects traffic enforcement to multiple technical systems and data types, while the available records do not establish implementation or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 67 is the community’s central legal reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 67 of Law 36/2024/QH15 sets out measures for traffic control and detecting legal violations, and is connected to both activities represented in this community. This makes it the organizing legal reference for the data collection and use described here. [Data: Entities (535); Relationships (2480, 2478)]

The supplied information describes the provision’s scope but does not establish how authorities apply it, whether particular systems are in operation, or whether implementation complies with other legal requirements. [Data: Entities (535)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision encompasses several technical and data categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 67 identifies systems and traffic cameras, technical equipment for inspecting and controlling motor-vehicle loads, vehicle-monitoring data, images of drivers or passenger compartments, and data from vehicle-weight control facilities as resources that may be used for traffic control and violation detection. [Data: Entities (535)]

This breadth indicates that the provision concerns both monitoring infrastructure and information gathered or produced through traffic and vehicle-weight controls. The records do not specify retention periods, access rules, safeguards, or the scale of data collection. [Data: Entities (535)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-weight facility data is identified as an input to violation detection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One activity in the community is receiving data collected by vehicle-weight control facilities for detecting legal violations. Article 67 is explicitly linked to this activity as specifying receipt of that data as a measure for violation detection. [Data: Entities (4039, 535); Relationships (2480)]

The records identify the activity and its stated purpose, but provide no details about which facilities transmit data, what violations are detected, or how the data is processed after receipt. [Data: Entities (4039)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monitoring and image data are described as tools for detecting road-traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate activity involves using data from journey-monitoring devices and devices that record images of drivers or passenger compartments to detect violations of road traffic laws. Article 67 is linked to this activity as specifying the use of those data types for violation detection. [Data: Entities (1234, 535); Relationships (2478)]

The supplied records do not describe the devices’ technical capabilities, the kinds of violations identified, or how images and monitoring data are reviewed or acted upon. [Data: Entities (1234)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence supports a description of purpose, not an assessment of outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Both activities are framed as measures for detecting legal violations, and both are connected to Article 67. This supports characterizing the community as a legal and technical traffic-enforcement framework. [Data: Entities (535, 4039, 1234); Relationships (2480, 2478)]

No supplied record reports enforcement results, operational performance, legal disputes, privacy impacts, or reputational concerns. Accordingly, those matters cannot be assessed from this community’s data alone. [Data: Entities (535, 4039, 1234); Relationships (2480, 2478)]

v.tieu_de: Articles 76 and 79 on Road Safety
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Articles 76 and 79 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Article 79 concerns recommendations on road traffic order and safety in relation to road works, and cites paragraph 1 of Article 76 as the basis for information about risks to road infrastructure. The supplied data describes a regulatory relationship, but does not establish implementation, compliance outcomes, or any specific incident.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest public-impact significance because it concerns responses to road-safety and infrastructure risks, while the data provides no evidence of a specific hazard or implementation outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 79 addresses road-work-related traffic risks
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 79 is described as concerning recommendations on road traffic order and safety in relation to road works. The provision assigns the traffic police authority a role in addressing risks within its management scope or recommending timely action by relevant road managers. [Data: Entities (556)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 76 supplies the cited basis for risk information
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 79 refers to paragraph 1 of Article 76 as the basis for information about risks to road transport infrastructure. This establishes a direct citation relationship between the two provisions in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (553, 556); Relationships (2583)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship is a regulatory cross-reference
phat_hien.giai_thich: The only listed relationship links Article 76 to Article 79 and describes Article 76 as the basis for Article 79's information about road-infrastructure risks. v.tieu_de: Article 89 of Law 36/2024/QH15: Vehicle Transitions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 89 of Law 36/2024/QH15, which addresses transitional matters involving pre-effective-date driving licences and vehicle licence-plate auctions. It links to Article 38 for certain auction cases where confirmation of the winning bid has not been issued, and specifies continued validity for qualifying Class C driving licences that have not been exchanged or reissued.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the provisions’ practical relevance to vehicle licensing and auctions, while the supplied information describes a limited transitional scope and no specific compliance concerns.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 89 is the community’s central transitional provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 89 addresses matters arising before the law took effect, covering both previously issued driving licences and car licence-plate auctions. Its links to the auction rule in Article 38 and the continued-validity rule for Class C licences make it the organizing provision in this set of entities. [Data: Entities (574, 424, 1108); Relationships (1807, 2665)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Auction cases connect Article 89 with Article 38
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 89 refers to point d of clause 1 of Article 38 as an additional rule for certain auction cases where confirmation of the winning bid has not been issued. Article 38 is described as setting out the rights and obligations of people who win vehicle licence-plate auctions. [Data: Entities (574, 424); Relationships (1807)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The auction transition distinguishes confirmation status
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 89 distinguishes between auctions for which confirmation of the winning bid had already been issued and those for which it had not. For the latter cases, the provision refers to point d of clause 1 of Article 38; the supplied information does not specify further outcomes for either category. [Data: Entities (574, 424); Relationships (1807)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Qualifying Class C licences may retain specified validity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described transitional rule allows qualifying Class C driving licences to remain valid for driving trucks and tractors with a load capacity of 3,500 kg or more, as well as vehicles covered by categories B1 and B2. This continued validity applies if the licences have not been exchanged or reissued under the law. [Data: Entities (1108)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community covers two distinct vehicle-related transition areas
phat_hien.giai_thich: The information associates Article 89 with both the treatment of earlier driving licences and the handling of earlier car licence-plate auctions. These are separate subject areas within the same transitional provision; the licence rule is linked directly to Article 89, while the auction rule also draws on Article 38. [Data: Entities (574, 424, 1108); Relationships (1807, 2665)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Use Permit and Traffic Police Coordination
v.tom_tat: This community describes a coordination process for vehicles requiring road-use permits because they are oversized, overweight, or tracked. The permit-issuing agency must immediately notify both the Ministry of Public Security’s traffic police agency and the traffic police agency responsible for the road or road section the vehicle will use. The available records describe administrative responsibilities, but do not identify a specific vehicle movement, incident, or compliance outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational importance because it links permit issuance with traffic-police coordination for specified vehicle movements, while the records show no specific incident or compliance outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The permit-issuing agency is the coordination hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The agency that issues road-use permits for oversized, overweight, or tracked vehicles has the central coordinating role in the described process. It must immediately notify the relevant traffic police agencies when such vehicles travel on a road. [Data: Entities (1189)]

Both recorded relationships originate from the permit-issuing agency, connecting it to the national traffic police agency and the police agency responsible for the relevant route. [Data: Relationships (4089, 4087)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: National-level traffic police are notified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Public Security’s traffic police agency is to be notified about the route of a permitted vehicle. Its stated responsibilities include directing and controlling road traffic and carrying out inspection, control, and enforcement duties. [Data: Entities (1206); Relationships (4089)]

The records establish a notification relationship, but do not specify what action the national agency takes in response to any particular notice. [Data: Relationships (4089)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The route-level traffic police agency has a defined role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate traffic police agency is responsible for maintaining traffic order and safety on the road or road section that the permitted vehicle will travel along. The permit-issuing agency must immediately notify this agency of the vehicle’s movement. [Data: Entities (1188, 1189); Relationships (4087)]

This describes a route-specific notification role; the available information does not identify particular roads, agencies, vehicles, or journeys. [Data: Entities (1188); Relationships (4087)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process links permit issuance with two police jurisdictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described notification process connects the permit-issuing agency to both the Ministry of Public Security’s traffic police agency and the traffic police agency responsible for the vehicle’s route. [Data: Relationships (4089, 4087)]

This structure indicates coordination at national and route levels for the specified permitted movements. The records do not establish whether these agencies exchange information directly with one another. [Data: Entities (1206, 1188, 1189); Relationships (4089, 4087)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe responsibilities, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions specify permit and traffic-management duties, including immediate notification and inspection, control, and enforcement responsibilities. [Data: Entities (1189, 1206, 1188)]

No record in the supplied data identifies a violation, enforcement action, safety incident, or failure to notify. Therefore, the information supports an assessment of the process’s stated roles, but not a conclusion about actual compliance or performance. [Data: Entities (1189, 1206, 1188); Relationships (4089, 4087)]

v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is modest because the records describe a specific vehicle-registration revocation circumstance in designated zones, without evidence of wider impact or implementation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A direct link between the zones and registration expiration
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship record connects Special Economic-Trade Zones with Vehicle Registration Expiration, stating that expiration of vehicle registration in those zones is identified as a revocation circumstance. phat_hien.tom_tat: Expiration is described as a revocation circumstance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Vehicle Registration Expiration entity describes expiration of a vehicle's registration period in specified zones as a circumstance for revoking its registration certificate and license plate. phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated geographic scope is zone-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Special Economic-Trade Zones entity describes zones where vehicle registration periods may expire, potentially triggering the stated revocation circumstance. phat_hien.giai_thich: The record identifies the vehicle registration certificate and license plate as the items subject to revocation in the described circumstance. phat_hien.tom_tat: Broader operational and reputational effects are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe the zones, the expiration circumstance, and their regulatory connection, but provide no information about implementation, affected parties, frequency, technical capabilities, or reputation. v.tieu_de: Road Safety and Transport of Dangerous Goods

phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.giai_thich:

v.tieu_de: Article 29 and the Towing Exception in Law 36/2024/QH15

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship is a cross-reference within the law
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The connection between the two entities is expressly described as a citation: Clause 1 of Article 29 cites Clause 3 of Article 53 as an exception to its towing rule. [Data: Relationships (1450)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions concern vehicle-towing regulation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 29 concerns towing vehicles, trailers, and tractor units towing semi-trailers, and its first clause specifically addresses conditions for a car towing another car or specialized motor vehicle. [Data: Entities (356)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence is narrow and does not establish compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains two provisions and one recorded relationship: Article 29, Clause 3 of Article 53, and the cross-reference between them. [Data: Entities (356, 936); Relationships (1450)]
