It supports an assessment that the community concerns traffic order and safety, but does not establish rates of compliance, the frequency of hazardous events, or the performance of enforcement. [Data: Entities (4502, 4348, 4055, 242, 4023); Relationships (10133, 9847, 738, 9827)]

No specific organization, named individual, technical system, or reputation claim is described in these records. The community’s significance therefore rests on the broad safety role of the rules and relationships documented here, rather than on evidence of particular misconduct or operational capability. [Data: Entities (4502, 4348, 4394)]

v.tieu_de: Law 36/2024 Ferry and Pontoon-Crossing Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the road-traffic activity “Crossing a Ferry or Pontoon Bridge,” described as addressed by Article 23, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Boarding and disembarking from a ferry are linked procedures with different stated movement orders, while pontoon-bridge crossing is also identified as a subject of Article 23. The records describe traffic rules but do not provide evidence about compliance, violations, enforcement, or actual safety outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has practical traffic-safety and legal relevance, but the supplied information is limited to a narrow set of crossing procedures and does not document violations or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A defined traffic procedure is the community’s central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
“Crossing a Ferry or Pontoon Bridge” is the central entity, connecting the ferry boarding and disembarking procedures as well as pontoon-bridge crossing. Its description identifies Article 23, Clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as addressing the road-traffic activity and sets out the stated order for boarding and leaving a ferry. [Data: Entities (1150); Relationships (2859, 4036, 4037)]

This structure indicates a focused community about traffic procedures rather than a broader network of organizations or individuals. The records do not establish how the rule is implemented or whether any party complies with it.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Boarding prioritizes pedestrians before road vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The boarding procedure is linked to the central crossing concept. The supplied description states that pedestrians board first, followed by road vehicles proceeding as directed by the traffic controller. [Data: Entities (655, 1150); Relationships (2859)]

This describes an order of movement and a role for the traffic controller, but the data does not specify enforcement mechanisms, exceptions, or real-world adherence.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Disembarking gives motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles priority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Disembarking from a ferry is identified as one of the ferry-crossing procedures covered by the central provision. The description states that motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles leave before non-motorized vehicles and pedestrians. [Data: Entities (1402, 1150); Relationships (4037)]

The records establish the stated sequence only; they provide no incident data or assessment of the procedure’s safety effectiveness.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pontoon-bridge crossing is included alongside ferry crossing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central activity is connected to “Crossing a Pontoon Bridge,” and the relationship description says the provision addresses pontoon-bridge crossing as well as crossing by ferry. [Data: Entities (1150, 1154); Relationships (4036)]

The pontoon-bridge entity’s description refers to Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15, but the supplied records do not give a separate, detailed sequence of movement for crossing a pontoon bridge.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a limited legal and operational assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships describe a statutory reference and procedures for boarding and disembarking, with a connection to pontoon-bridge crossing. [Data: Entities (1150, 655, 1402, 1154); Relationships (2859, 4036, 4037)]

No records identify regulated parties, enforcement actions, violations, legal interpretations, or observed outcomes. Accordingly, the community’s practical relevance is evident, but the available information is insufficient to assess legal compliance or quantify safety impacts.

v.tieu_de: Failure to Obey Traffic Directions and Traffic Controllers
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the traffic violation Failure to Obey Traffic Directions and its relationship to people who direct or control traffic. The records connect the violation to traffic controllers, traffic-control officers and inspectors, and also to livestock handlers and operators of animal-drawn vehicles as potential violators. They describe monetary penalties and link the rules to road-signal compliance and requirements for priority-vehicle drivers. The material establishes regulatory significance but does not document specific incidents, enforcement outcomes, or reputational claims.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s practical importance to road safety and legal compliance across several road-user groups, while the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or broader harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Failure to Obey Traffic Directions is defined as not complying with commands, directions, orders, or instructions from a traffic controller. It is also explicitly linked to instructions from traffic-control officers and inspectors, making compliance with authorized directions the community’s central theme. [Data: Entities (1998, 4999, 4997, 5051); Relationships (6967, 6966, 6968, 6969)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic controllers have a broad direction-giving role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic-controller description says road users—including drivers, pedestrians, and drivers of priority vehicles—must obey the controller’s commands. It describes directions involving stopping or proceeding, U-turns, ferry boarding order, and movement across pontoon bridges. [Data: Entities (4999)]

The description characterizes controller commands as a distinct, highest-priority form of road direction, while also stating that they are excluded from national technical regulations governing road signals. [Data: Entities (4999)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records associate the violation with multiple road-user categories
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community is not limited to motor-vehicle drivers: the entity description says the violation may apply to drivers and, in some cases, pedestrians. Separate relationships identify livestock handlers and operators of animal-drawn vehicles as people who may commit the violation by failing to obey a traffic controller or traffic-control officer. [Data: Entities (1998, 2919, 3414); Relationships (6960, 6963)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty records contain different amounts that should not be conflated
phat_hien.giai_thich: One description associated with Failure to Obey Traffic Directions specifies a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong. Separately, another entity describes a penalty of VND 4,000,000 to VND 6,000,000 for a driver committing the specified violation while operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle; the relationship links that penalty to the violation. The records do not explain how these amounts relate or resolve the difference. [Data: Entities (1998, 3079); Relationships (6961)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle drivers remain subject to traffic-controller directions
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 27: Priority Vehicles is described as allowing specified priority vehicles to disregard speed limits or traffic lights, or travel against the direction of traffic, subject to restrictions on expressways. The same description states that their drivers must obey traffic controllers and temporary traffic signs. [Data: Entities (347); Relationships (1415)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The material connects controller instructions with signal-compliance rules
phat_hien.giai_thich: Compliance with Road Traffic Signals is identified as the subject of Article 11, and its relationship to Traffic Controller says the article discusses controller instructions in that context. This indicates that the supplied material treats controller directions alongside road-signal compliance, without providing further detail about enforcement or outcomes. [Data: Entities (1075, 4999); Relationships (3887)]

v.tieu_de: Article 23 Ferry and Pontoon Bridge Crossing Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the regulated road-traffic activity of ferry and pontoon bridge crossings under Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15. Its linked entities describe the two crossing types, the ferry and pontoon bridge routes, and fresh-food vehicles as a priority category. The supplied descriptions also specify passenger-occupancy restrictions during ferry movement and single-line traffic rules for certain vehicles crossing pontoon bridges. [Data: Entities (2090, 3826, 3825, 2091, 2371, +more); Relationships (7076, 7072, 7074, 7075, 7073)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it concerns regulated crossing procedures and road-user safety, but the supplied data describes rules rather than any specific incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single regulatory topic links the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Ferry and pontoon bridge crossing is the central activity in the supplied network, and is described as addressed by Article 23 of Law 36/2024/QH15. The related entities represent crossing types, routes, and a vehicle category within the same regulatory context. [Data: Entities (2090); Relationships (7076, 7072, 7074, 7075, 7073)]

The records establish the subject matter and some specific traffic rules, but do not provide information about enforcement, compliance rates, or actual incidents. [Data: Entities (2090, 3826)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules cover both ferry and pontoon bridge crossings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 23’s heading covers ferry and pontoon-bridge crossings, with ferry crossing and pontoon bridge crossing identified as the two types within the broader activity. [Data: Entities (2090, 2091, 3826); Relationships (7073, 7076)]

The network also identifies a ferry and a pontoon bridge as routes used for crossing. These distinctions indicate that the rules apply across two crossing settings, without further detail on location or operating conditions. [Data: Entities (2089, 3825); Relationships (7072, 7075)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fresh-food vehicles are included in the crossing priority order
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicles carrying fresh food are named as a category in the priority order for ferry and pontoon bridge crossings. The supplied records do not specify the full order or the relative priority of other vehicle categories. [Data: Entities (2090, 2371); Relationships (7074)]

This establishes a stated priority category in the regulation, but the data does not describe how that priority is implemented or whether it has resulted in any particular outcome. [Data: Entities (2371); Relationships (7074)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ferry movement includes restrictions on remaining inside vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under Clause 3, people may not remain inside vehicles as they descend onto, travel on, or leave a ferry, except for the driver and specified groups of people. This is a passenger-occupancy rule associated with the broader ferry and pontoon bridge crossing activity. [Data: Entities (2090)]

The supplied description does not identify the specified groups beyond the driver, nor does it provide details about enforcement or compliance. [Data: Entities (2090)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pontoon bridge crossings have traffic-control and lane-order requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road users crossing a pontoon bridge must follow the traffic controller’s instructions. Clause 4 further states that motor vehicles and motorcycles intended for specialized use must cross in a single line in their direction of travel and must not obstruct people or vehicles moving in the opposite direction. [Data: Entities (3826)]

These provisions describe orderly movement and avoidance of obstruction on the crossing. The records do not report specific violations or resulting safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (3826, 2090); Relationships (7076)]

v.tieu_de: Article 76 Road-Safety Incident Response
v.tom_tat: This community describes a response framework for unexpected road situations that cause or may cause disorder or loss of traffic safety, with Article 76 of Law 36/2024/QH15 cited as its context. Individuals who discover a qualifying situation are linked to reporting and, where safety may be threatened, warning actions; the nearest police agency is to be notified promptly. The records establish these stated responsibilities but provide no specific incident, enforcement outcome, technical capability, or reputation information.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to road safety and incident response, balanced against the absence of evidence about a particular event, harm, or compliance outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a potentially safety-critical road situation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is an unexpected road situation that causes or may cause disorder or a loss of traffic safety. Its description cites Article 76 of Law 36/2024/QH15, making the community relevant to both road safety and a stated legal response framework. [Data: Entities (5232)]

The records describe a qualifying category of situation, not a specific incident. They do not establish that any actual disruption, injury, or loss has occurred. [Data: Entities (5232)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Discoverers have reporting and conditional warning responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Individuals who discover a qualifying unexpected situation or road traffic accident are described as being required to take reporting or safety-warning actions under Article 76. The relationship record likewise says discoverers must report and take warning measures when safety may be threatened. [Data: Entities (2656); Relationships (7939)]

The warning duty is conditional in the supplied description: it applies when the situation may threaten safety. The records do not specify how these duties are assessed or document whether anyone has complied with them. [Data: Entities (2553); Relationships (7813, 7939)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Immediate warnings are a protective response when road users may be endangered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes an immediate safety warning as a distinct action associated with the unexpected situation. The relationship states that a warning is required when the situation may endanger people or vehicles participating in road traffic. [Data: Entities (2553); Relationships (7813)]

This indicates a response intended to address possible danger to road users, but the records do not describe warning methods, equipment, or operational procedures. [Data: Entities (2553, 5232); Relationships (7813)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prompt notification of the nearest police agency is part of the response
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The nearest police agency is identified as the agency located nearest to the person or entity discovering an incident. The relationship says it should be notified promptly when such a situation is discovered. [Data: Entities (3225); Relationships (9146)]

This establishes a reporting connection between the qualifying situation and a police agency. No particular agency, notification channel, response time standard, or subsequent police action is identified in the records. [Data: Entities (3225, 5232); Relationships (9146)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records outline responsibilities but not implementation or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Taken together, the records connect the qualifying road situation to discoverers, conditional safety warnings, and prompt police notification. They support an account of stated response responsibilities, rather than evidence that a specific response occurred. [Data: Entities (5232, 2656, 2553, 3225); Relationships (7939, 7813, 9146)]

The supplied material does not identify technical systems, enforcement results, specific incidents, or reputational assessments. Accordingly, the community’s practical effectiveness and any actual compliance cannot be assessed from these records alone. [Data: Entities (5232, 2656, 2553, 3225); Relationships (7939, 7813, 9146)]

v.tieu_de: Article 49 and Goods Transport by Automobile
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 49 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and its requirements for automobiles transporting goods. Article 49 is linked to goods transport by automobile and goods transport by car, while the automobile-transport activity is explicitly connected to road traffic safety. The records describe cargo-securing, covering, load-height, and warning-signal requirements, but provide no information about enforcement, actual compliance, violations, or incidents.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns rules intended to protect road traffic safety during goods transport, although the records describe requirements rather than any specific incident or compliance outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 49 is the central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 49 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 is the community’s primary legal reference, setting road traffic order and safety requirements for automobiles transporting goods. Its direct relationship to goods transport by automobile establishes the regulatory basis for the activity described in this community. [Data: Entities (474); Relationships (2208)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo must be secured or covered
phat_hien.giai_thich: The stated requirements apply to loose cargo, construction materials, and waste: these loads must be secured or covered to prevent spills and reduce noise and dust. This is a specific handling obligation in the supplied description of Article 49, not evidence that any particular transport operator has complied with it. [Data: Entities (474)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A minimum clearance below the vehicle body edge is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Article 49 description states that the load must be kept at least 10 centimeters below the top edge of the vehicle body. This provides a concrete load-height requirement within the broader goods-transport rules. The data do not provide information about inspections or observed load conditions. [Data: Entities (474)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Protruding cargo requires warning signals
phat_hien.giai_thich: When cargo extends beyond the front or rear of a vehicle, drivers must use red warning signals during the day and lights or other signals at night or in darkness. The rule is part of the safety requirements associated with goods transport by automobile. [Data: Entities (474, 2397)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community links goods transport to road traffic safety
phat_hien.giai_thich: The goods-transport-by-automobile activity is explicitly described as subject to safety requirements intended to ensure road traffic safety. This connects the operational subject of the community to a broader public-safety objective, but the records do not identify specific hazards, incidents, enforcement actions, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (2397, 4443); Relationships (7620)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Automobile and car transport are both represented
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data include a goods-transport-by-automobile entity and a goods-transport-by-car entity, with Article 49 linked to each. The car entry describes the activity as including transport of loose cargo, construction materials, or waste; the records do not otherwise explain whether these labels represent distinct vehicle categories or overlapping terminology. [Data: Entities (2397, 2398); Relationships (2208, 2209)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No compliance or reputation evidence is provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe statutory requirements and their stated safety purpose, but they do not name transport operators or provide inspection results, violations, penalties, or evidence of adherence. They also contain no information about the reputation or technical capabilities of particular entities, so no conclusions on those matters are supported. [Data: Entities (474, 2397, 2398, 4443); Relationships (2208, 2209, 7620)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Control and Traffic Diversion
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Road Traffic Control, defined under Article 74 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as direct guidance of road traffic to maintain order, safety, and smooth flow. Its methods include temporary traffic diversion, traffic-signal operation, other road-signal operation, and the use of intelligent traffic-control devices. The Traffic Police Authority is specifically responsible for notifying relevant parties about and implementing temporary traffic-diversion plans under Article 77, Clause 3. The records describe statutory roles and operational functions, but do not provide evidence about implementation outcomes or compliance in particular cases.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high importance because it covers several connected mechanisms for managing road traffic and assigns a specific diversion role to the Traffic Police Authority.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road Traffic Control is the community's organizing framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road Traffic Control is defined as direct guidance of road traffic to maintain order, safety, and smooth flow. The description includes directing traffic, temporarily diverting it, and managing or operating signals and related devices, making this the central activity linking the other operational entities. [Data: Entities (4346); Relationships (10127, 9369, 10129, 8017)]

The description also states that vehicle operators must follow instructions and, as necessary, slow down or stop while control is being conducted in an area. This establishes a stated safety-related duty, but the records do not document specific enforcement actions or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (4346)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary diversion is a defined method of traffic control
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Temporary Traffic Diversion is described as the temporary allocation or redirection of traffic flows as part of Road Traffic Control. The relationship between the two identifies diversion as one method within the broader control activity. [Data: Entities (4888, 4346); Relationships (10127)]

The records do not specify particular roads, diversion plans, durations, or effects on traffic, so the evidence supports the function and connection rather than any assessment of a specific diversion's consequences. [Data: Entities (4888); Relationships (10127)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Traffic Police Authority has a stated role in diversion plans
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under Article 77, Clause 3, the Traffic Police Authority is responsible for notifying relevant parties about temporary traffic-diversion plans and carrying them out. Its relationship to Temporary Traffic Diversion directly connects the authority to implementation and notification responsibilities. [Data: Entities (5025, 4888); Relationships (10503)]

The available information describes this statutory responsibility but does not show how it is performed in any particular situation or identify other parties involved in a specific plan. [Data: Entities (5025)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic-signal operation is one component of the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic Signal System Operation is defined as the management, operation, and use of the traffic signal system to control road traffic. The relationship record identifies managing and operating traffic signals as part of Road Traffic Control. [Data: Entities (5038, 4346); Relationships (10129)]

The evidence establishes this operational function, but does not describe the signal equipment, operating procedures, or technical performance of any system. [Data: Entities (5038)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other road signals provide an additional control method
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Other Road Signal Operation concerns using and operating road signs and other road signals to guide and control traffic. It is explicitly linked to Road Traffic Control as one of its constituent activities. [Data: Entities (3463, 4346); Relationships (9369)]

The records do not identify particular signs, locations, or signal configurations, and therefore support only the general function described. [Data: Entities (3463)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent devices are included, but technical detail is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Intelligent Traffic Control Device Operation is described as the use and operation of intelligent devices that support the direction and control of road traffic. Its relationship to Road Traffic Control establishes that these devices are among the supporting mechanisms in the framework. [Data: Entities (2714, 4346); Relationships (8017)]

No device types, capabilities, deployments, or performance measures are provided. The records therefore indicate a technical category, but do not establish the community's level of technological sophistication. [Data: Entities (2714)]

v.tieu_de: Article 73 of Law 36/2024/QH15
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Article 73 of Law 36/2024/QH15 and three kinds of conduct it addresses: failure by road traffic participants to comply with inspection or control requests, obstruction of people performing official duties, and resistance to those people. The available data describes the provision’s subject matter and links each conduct category to the article; it does not establish that any particular person committed these acts or provide details about penalties or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (550, 1960, 3291, 4176); Relationships (2574, 2576, 2577)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the provision’s relevance to traffic inspections and official duties, while the evidence is limited to its stated subject matter and contains no information about actual violations or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 73 is the community’s organizing provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 73 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is the central entity in this community. Its description identifies prevention of noncompliance with inspection and control requests, and of obstruction or resistance toward people performing official duties, as the provision’s subject matter. [Data: Entities (550)]

The three recorded relationships connect Article 73 to each of these conduct categories, indicating that the community is organized around the provision and the behaviors it addresses. [Data: Relationships (2574, 2576, 2577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Noncompliance with inspection and control requests is one addressed category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes failure to comply with inspection and control requests as conduct addressed by Article 73. It specifies that the relevant requests are made during an inspection or control and concern road traffic participants. [Data: Entities (1960)]

A direct relationship links this category to Article 73, which is described as concerning prevention of such noncompliance. The records do not identify any actual incident or person involved. [Data: Relationships (2574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Obstruction of officials is separately identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Obstruction of people performing official duties appears as a distinct conduct category in the community. The entity description characterizes it as an act addressed by Article 73. [Data: Entities (3291)]

The relationship record links this category to Article 73 and states that the provision concerns preventing obstruction of people performing official duties. No further detail about circumstances, enforcement, or consequences is supplied. [Data: Relationships (2576)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Resistance to people performing official duties is another distinct category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data separately identifies resistance to people performing official duties as an act addressed by Article 73. This is presented as distinct from the category of obstruction, rather than as an account of a specific event. [Data: Entities (4176)]

The relationship record connects resistance to Article 73 and describes the provision as concerning prevention of that conduct. [Data: Relationships (2577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence establishes legal subject matter, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available records describe a legal provision and its association with three types of conduct: failure to comply with inspection or control requests, obstruction, and resistance. They do not state that a violation occurred or identify any individual or organization as responsible. [Data: Entities (550, 1960, 3291, 4176); Relationships (2574, 2576, 2577)]

The supplied information also does not give penalties, procedural requirements, enforcement statistics, or interpretations beyond the brief descriptions. Accordingly, those matters cannot be assessed from this community’s records.

v.tieu_de: Article 72 and Road Traffic Inspection and Control
v.tom_tat: This community describes a legal framework for vehicle inspection and control under Article 72 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Inspection and control follows a vehicle stop and may identify a legal violation, with handling measures addressing such violations. Vehicle operators are entitled to information about the stop grounds, inspection content and results, identified violations, and handling measures. The records describe these rights and processes, but do not establish how they are implemented in practice or provide evidence of particular inspection outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns official road-traffic controls and operator information rights, while the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or implementation outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection and control is the community's central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Inspection and control is described as official checks and control activities involving road traffic participants and vehicles after a vehicle has been stopped. The description also states that participants are required to comply with these activities. [Data: Entities (2680)]

The process connects operators, vehicle stops, potential violations, and subsequent handling measures, making it the organizing concept for the community. The records explain the process at a general level rather than documenting any particular inspection. [Data: Relationships (7969, 7970, 7966, 7661)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 72 establishes the stated information rights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 72 is identified as a provision of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerning the rights and responsibilities of people operating vehicles in road traffic. The relationships specify that it gives operators a right to information about inspection content and results, identified legal violations, and measures for handling a violation. [Data: Entities (547); Relationships (2565, 2567, 2564)]

The supplied material describes these legal entitlements, but does not provide the full text of the provision or evidence about compliance with it in practice.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operators are entitled to information about the stop and inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road traffic vehicle operators are described as having the right to be informed of the grounds for a stop for inspection and control, as well as the inspection's content and results. [Data: Entities (4455); Relationships (10237, 7969)]

A notice concerning stop grounds and inspection results is also represented as communicating this information to operators. The data identify the information to be conveyed but do not specify the format, timing, or procedure for providing the notice. [Data: Entities (3272); Relationships (9227, 9228)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process can identify legal violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that inspection and control may identify a legal violation and that operators have a right to be informed of any violation identified during the process. [Data: Entities (2877, 2680); Relationships (7966, 8542)]

This describes a possible outcome of an inspection, not a finding that any particular operator or vehicle violated the law. No specific violation, case, or enforcement result is included in the supplied data.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Handling measures are linked to identified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Handling measures are described as actions taken to address a legal violation identified during inspection and control. Operators are stated to have a right to be informed of measures taken to handle such a violation. [Data: Entities (2416); Relationships (7661, 7662)]

The records do not identify particular measures or indicate whether measures were applied in any real case, so they support only a description of the framework's stated relationship between violations, responses, and operator notification.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes a legal process, not operational performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships consistently describe a sequence involving a stop, inspection and control, possible identification of a violation, and possible handling measures, alongside operator information rights. [Data: Entities (2680, 5496, 2877, 2416, 3272); Relationships (7970, 7966, 7661, 9228, +more)]

No records provide details about specific officers, agencies, vehicles, inspections, technologies, or compliance outcomes. Accordingly, the material supports analysis of the stated process and rights but does not establish actual enforcement practices or technical capabilities.

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Order and Safety Forces
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Road Traffic Order and Safety Forces, whose stated responsibilities include detecting, preventing, and handling legal violations related to road traffic order and safety. The forces are also the intended recipients of training and capacity-building, while the relationship descriptions say vehicle operators are required to assist and cooperate in the forces’ violation-related work. The records describe an important public-safety mandate but do not establish operational outcomes or compliance levels. [Data: Entities (4392, 5064, 1346, 3852, 2418); Relationships (10189, 9723, 7664, 5799)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it combines road-safety enforcement responsibilities with training and capacity-building, although the records do not indicate outcomes or specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The forces are the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Order and Safety Forces are described as responsible for maintaining order and safety on roads and for detecting, preventing, and handling legal violations. The relationships connect the forces to each of these functions and to their training, making them the organizing entity in this community. [Data: Entities (4392); Relationships (10189, 9723, 7664, 5799)]

These records establish the scope of the stated responsibilities, but do not describe particular enforcement actions or results.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violation detection, prevention, and handling form a broad remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community distinguishes three functions: identifying legal violations, taking steps to stop them, and addressing violations once they occur or continue. Each function is linked to the forces as a responsibility. [Data: Entities (1346, 3852, 2418); Relationships (5799, 9723, 7664)]

Together, these functions indicate a role spanning several stages of addressing violations; the records do not specify procedures, penalties, or the legal standards applied.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training and capacity-building are directed to the forces
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Training, capacity-building, and professional development for road traffic safety forces are identified as a distinct part of the community. The relationship explicitly states that the forces are the intended recipients of this support. [Data: Entities (5064, 4392); Relationships (10189)]

The information establishes that such development is addressed, but does not provide details about curricula, delivery, funding, or demonstrated effectiveness.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle operators are expected to assist and cooperate
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions of the forces’ prevention, handling, and detection responsibilities state that vehicle operators are required to assist and cooperate. This places operator cooperation alongside the forces’ functions in the described framework. [Data: Relationships (9723, 7664, 5799)]

The records do not define the form of required cooperation or describe how the requirement is implemented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe responsibilities, not compliance or performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information identifies the forces’ road-safety duties and their connection to training, while also describing operator cooperation in relation to violation-related work. [Data: Entities (4392, 5064); Relationships (10189, 9723, 7664, 5799)]

It does not provide incident counts, enforcement outcomes, compliance assessments, or evidence of training effectiveness. Accordingly, the community’s importance is supported by its stated functions, while its actual impact cannot be assessed from these records alone.

v.tieu_de: Patrol and Control Force: Road-Traffic Safety and Legal Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Patrol and Control Force, whose stated responsibilities include conducting road-traffic patrol and control, maintaining road-traffic order and safety, and combating crime and legal violations. The connected entities distinguish road-traffic violations from other legal violations and describe crime prevention as part of the force’s remit. The records set out duties and relationships, but do not establish how those duties are performed or provide evidence of particular compliance outcomes or incidents.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety importance because it concerns traffic enforcement, crime prevention, and legal-violation control, while the records provide no evidence of specific harmful incidents or operational outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Patrol and Control Force is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Patrol and Control Force has the highest listed degree among the entities and is the hub of the provided relationships. It is linked to road-traffic patrol and control, road-traffic legal violations, other legal violations, and crime prevention and combating. [Data: Entities (3597); Relationships (9458, 9360, 9457, 4024, 4021)]

The records describe the force’s responsibilities and connections, but do not identify individual personnel, operational locations, or specific enforcement actions. [Data: Entities (3597); Relationships (9458, 9360, 9457, 4024, 4021)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-traffic patrol and control is a core operational function
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The force carries out road-traffic patrol and control, which is described as an activity of the Traffic Police to maintain and enforce road-traffic order and safety. The activity is stated to be conducted in accordance with Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (4546); Relationships (9458)]

The supplied information establishes the stated purpose and legal reference for the activity, but does not document particular patrols, enforcement decisions, or whether procedures were followed in practice. [Data: Entities (4546); Relationships (9458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records distinguish road-traffic violations from other legal violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road-traffic legal violations concern road-traffic order and safety, and the force is required to fight and prevent them. The records connect those violations directly to the broader area of road-traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (4538, 4541); Relationships (9457, 10290)]

Other legal violations are described separately as violations outside the road-traffic order and safety category. The force is also required to combat and prevent these, while vehicle operators are described as having a role in helping detect, prevent, and address them; the Traffic Police may address them as authorized by law. [Data: Entities (3456); Relationships (9360)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Crime prevention is included in the force’s responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community explicitly connects the Patrol and Control Force to a duty to resolutely fight and prevent crime. A separate entity describes crimes and legal violations broadly, including road-traffic and other legal violations, and links that broader category to the force’s responsibilities. [Data: Entities (1140, 1138); Relationships (4024, 4021)]

These records describe a mandate rather than evidence of specific crimes, investigations, or enforcement results. They therefore support the conclusion that crime prevention is within the stated remit, but not an assessment of its effectiveness. [Data: Entities (1140, 1138); Relationships (4024, 4021)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community’s subject matter is public order and safety on roads
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road-traffic order and safety is the stated subject area for the patrol duties and the related category of road-traffic legal violations. This makes the community relevant to road safety and the enforcement of rules governing conduct on roads. [Data: Entities (4541, 4538, 4546); Relationships (9458, 9457, 10290)]

The supplied records do not quantify traffic risk, describe road conditions, or identify affected communities. The community’s significance is therefore grounded in the public-safety functions described, rather than in evidence of a particular local risk or event. [Data: Entities (4541, 4546)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The information describes duties, not verified legal compliance or performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that the force is required to perform patrol and control duties and to combat and prevent various violations. They also identify a legal reference for road-traffic patrol and control. [Data: Entities (3597, 4546, 3456); Relationships (9458, 9360, 9457, 4024, 4021)]

No supplied record reports a finding of compliance or noncompliance, a complaint, a sanction, or an operational outcome. The material supports describing the stated legal and functional responsibilities, but does not support conclusions about actual compliance, misconduct, or effectiveness. [Data: Entities (3597, 4546, 3456); Relationships (9458, 9360, 9457, 4024, 4021)]

v.tieu_de: Article 73 and Official-Duty Noncompliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 73 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and its relationship to obstruction of, resistance to, or noncompliance with official duties. The described conduct is linked to violators and to the application of preventive measures under the law. The supplied information describes a legal framework, not a specific incident or evidence of actual violations. [Data: Entities (549, 212, 3292, 5610); Relationships (618, 2573, 619, 9242)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it connects a statutory provision, specified conduct, violators, and preventive measures, but the data do not establish an actual incident or its consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 73 is the community’s statutory anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 73 is described as a provision of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerning measures to prevent road-traffic participants from obstructing or resisting persons performing official duties, or failing to comply with their inspection and control requests. It is connected both to the specified conduct and to preventive measures. [Data: Entities (549); Relationships (618, 2573)]

The supplied records do not provide the full text of Article 73 or further procedural detail, so the scope of the provision should not be extended beyond these descriptions. [Data: Entities (549); Relationships (618, 2573)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The covered conduct is obstruction or noncompliance with official duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The conduct category includes obstruction of or resistance to people performing official duties, as well as failure to comply with their inspection and control requests. Article 73 is linked to preventing this conduct. [Data: Entities (3292, 549); Relationships (2573)]

The records describe a category of conduct; they do not identify a particular person, event, or instance in which it occurred. [Data: Entities (3292, 549)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Preventive measures are linked to the specified conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Application of Preventive Measures is described as action taken by a person performing official duties under the law when a violator obstructs or fails to comply with an inspection or control request. The relationships connect these measures to both Article 73 and the obstruction or noncompliance category. [Data: Entities (212); Relationships (618, 619)]

The supplied information does not specify what particular measures may be used, how they are carried out, or what safeguards apply. [Data: Entities (212)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violators are defined by conduct covered by Article 47
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The VIOLATORS entity describes people who commit violations covered by Article 47, including obstruction or resistance to inspections and failure to comply with inspection or control requests made by persons performing official duties. The relationship record links this group to the specified obstruction or noncompliance. [Data: Entities (5610, 3292); Relationships (9242)]

The records also state that when one violator’s conduct is covered by different articles in Chapter II, penalties are applied according to the rules stated there; they do not provide those rules or specific penalty amounts. [Data: Entities (5610)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data establish a legal framework, not evidence of enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships describe how Article 73, the specified conduct, preventive measures, and violators are connected. They provide a basis for understanding the topic’s legal and conceptual structure. [Data: Relationships (618, 2573, 619, 9242)]

No enforcement case, compliance record, penalty outcome, or impact on individuals is included in the supplied material. Accordingly, the community’s practical effects cannot be assessed from these records alone. [Data: Entities (549, 212, 3292, 5610); Relationships (618, 2573, 619, 9242)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Command and Control
v.tom_tat: This community centers on ROAD TRAFFIC COMMAND AND CONTROL, described as an Article 74 activity for developing measures to support orderly, safe, and uninterrupted road traffic. The process includes collecting and assessing relevant traffic factors and is carried out through an authorized traffic commander. The records describe an intended public-safety function, but do not provide information about implementation, performance, legal compliance, or specific outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns the organization and safety of road traffic, although the records describe the function rather than any specific operational results or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road traffic command and control is the central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROAD TRAFFIC COMMAND AND CONTROL is the community's central entity. It is connected to the collection and analysis of traffic factors, an authorized person who directs traffic, and the intended outcome of orderly and safe road operations. [Data: Entities (4344, 626, 3422, 5003); Relationships (10125, 2806, 9309)]

The records characterize this activity as a process for developing measures, rather than documenting a particular deployment or traffic event. [Data: Entities (4344)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic factor analysis informs management measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
TRAFFIC FACTOR COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS is described as collecting, analyzing, and assessing factors relevant to road traffic. The relationship record identifies this work as part of the road traffic command and control process and says it informs the development of measures. [Data: Entities (5003); Relationships (10125)]

No specific factors, analytical methods, tools, or resulting measures are identified in the provided records. [Data: Entities (5003, 4344); Relationships (10125)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An authorized person carries out traffic command
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify an AUTHORIZED TRAFFIC COMMANDER as a person with authority to direct road traffic. They further state that road traffic command is carried out through such a person. [Data: Entities (626); Relationships (2806)]

The records do not name an individual or provide details about the scope, appointment, or oversight of this authority. [Data: Entities (626); Relationships (2806)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated objective is orderly, safe, uninterrupted traffic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ORDERLY AND SAFE ROAD TRAFFIC OPERATIONS is the intended outcome associated with the central activity. The relationship record says road traffic command and control develops measures to support orderly, safe, and uninterrupted traffic operations. [Data: Entities (3422, 4344); Relationships (9309)]

This is a stated objective; the supplied information does not establish whether the measures achieve that outcome in practice or provide safety or traffic-flow results. [Data: Entities (3422, 4344); Relationships (9309)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operational effectiveness and compliance are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the activity, its analytical component, its authorized human role, and its intended outcome. They do not provide evidence about actual operations, technical systems, performance metrics, incidents, or public reputation. [Data: Entities (4344, 626, 3422, 5003); Relationships (10125, 2806, 9309)]

Accordingly, the community's importance can be assessed from its stated connection to safe road traffic, but conclusions about effectiveness or compliance would go beyond the available evidence. [Data: Entities (4344, 3422); Relationships (9309)]

v.tieu_de: Traffic Command Center and Connected Road-Safety Systems
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Traffic Command Center system established under Article 75 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. It includes national, provincial, and centrally governed municipal-level centers. Road-security, public-order, and traffic-safety monitoring systems are required to connect to a Traffic Command Center, while the centers are permitted to connect and share data with ministries, sectors, and specified systems and databases. The provided information describes legal roles and technical relationships, but does not establish actual implementation outcomes, compliance performance, or reputational concerns. [Data: Entities (4993, 3007, 4309, 3199, +more); Relationships (8755, 10052, 9809, 8752, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the system’s substantial public-sector importance, given its national and subnational structure and its legally defined links to road-safety monitoring and data-sharing systems.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A legally defined, multi-level command-center system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 75 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 describes the Traffic Command Center system as comprising national-level and provincial- or centrally governed municipal-level centers. The described centers include technical infrastructure, technology equipment systems, and a database. [Data: Entities (4993)]

The national and subnational components are explicitly represented in the relationships: the National Traffic Command Center, provincial centers, city centers, and centers for centrally governed cities are included in the broader system. [Data: Entities (3219, 3981, 840, 758); Relationships (9140, 9809, 3304, 3066)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety monitoring has a required connection to the centers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-security, order, and traffic-safety monitoring system is described as needing to follow proper procedures, ensure continuous operation, and connect to a Traffic Command Center. The relationship data specifically states that this monitoring system must connect to the center. [Data: Entities (4309, 4993); Relationships (10052)]

This establishes a defined operational connection in the described framework. The records do not, however, report whether particular monitoring systems are currently connected or how effectively they operate.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The centers are authorized to exchange data with government bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 75(4) permits Traffic Command Centers to connect to and share data with ministries and sectors, subject to the law’s provisions. Ministries and sectors are also described as responsible for building national and specialized databases and connecting and sharing relevant information with the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (3007, 4993, 3199); Relationships (8755, 8752)]

The description says the participating ministries and sectors agree on the detailed data fields for the exchange. This indicates a defined coordination role, but the supplied records do not specify the actual fields or describe implementation arrangements. [Data: Entities (3007)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Multiple transport systems and databases may interoperate with the centers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships identify several systems with which a Traffic Command Center may connect and share data: journey-monitoring and image-data management, motor-vehicle load control, load-inspection technical equipment, road traffic signals, and intelligent transport system management. [Data: Entities (2790, 3120, 3121, 4453, 2719); Relationships (8132, 9042, 9043, 10236, 8024)]

The provision also refers more generally to specified systems and databases eligible for connection and data sharing. The source material establishes permitted connections, not that every listed connection is active or that the data is exchanged routinely. [Data: Entities (4844, 4993); Relationships (10491)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework links national databases with road-traffic safety information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
National databases are described as being built by ministries and sectors and connected to and shared with the road traffic order and safety database in accordance with law. The relationship between ministries and sectors and national databases assigns those bodies responsibility for building the databases. [Data: Entities (3199, 3007); Relationships (8752)]

This places the Traffic Command Center’s data-sharing role within a broader government information framework. The records do not identify the contents of particular national databases or specify what information is shared in practice.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence supports legal and technical significance, not a finding of misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe statutory responsibilities, system components, required connectivity for monitoring systems, and permitted data-sharing relationships. They contain no claims about legal violations, security incidents, misuse of data, or reputational issues, so no such conclusions are supported by this material. [Data: Entities (4993, 3007, 4309); Relationships (8755, 10052)]

Accordingly, the community’s impact assessment is based on the stated public-sector scope and interconnection structure rather than evidence of adverse conduct or demonstrated operational outcomes.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Urban Transport Regulation and Traffic Camera System
v.tom_tat: The community centers on urban areas subject to transport provisions under Articles 25 and 44, with provincial-level People’s Committees regulating road transport and accessible public passenger transport requirements there. Traffic cameras are installed in urban areas and along traffic routes, while Article 25 enforcement measures and the chairperson’s fine-setting authority form part of the enforcement framework. The records describe regulatory powers and infrastructure, but do not establish how they are implemented or their outcomes. [Data: Entities (5294, 3986, 4991, 3624, 3985); Relationships (9813, 10546, 9495, 9812, 10545)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderately high because the community combines local-government authority over urban transport and accessibility, traffic-camera coverage, and substantial potential fines, although the records do not show actual enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Urban areas are the community’s regulatory focal point
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Urban areas connect the regulatory, enforcement, and monitoring elements in the supplied records: committees regulate transport there, Article 25 penalties apply to specified urban transport violations, and the camera system is installed there. [Data: Entities (5294, 3624, 4991); Relationships (9813, 9495, 10546)]

The urban-area description also states that a vehicle may request to overtake between 22:00 and 05:00 only by using lights. This is a specific operating rule in the records, not evidence about compliance with it. [Data: Entities (5294)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial-level committees have transport and accessibility responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial-level People’s Committees are authorized to regulate road transport activities in urban areas, including the proportion of public passenger transport vehicles equipped with devices to assist people with disabilities. Their relationship to urban areas makes them a central governance body in this community. [Data: Entities (3986); Relationships (9813)]

The records identify the committees’ regulatory remit but do not state what proportions are required, whether particular vehicles meet them, or whether the requirements have been enforced. [Data: Entities (3986)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic cameras provide monitoring infrastructure across urban areas and routes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic camera system is described as installed both along traffic routes and in urban areas. These two relationships indicate coverage across more than one type of location. [Data: Entities (4991, 5036); Relationships (10545, 10546)]

The system is also described as one of the systems to which traffic command centers may connect and with which they may share data. The records do not specify the system’s capabilities beyond this description or document actual data sharing. [Data: Entities (4991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes penalties and licensing consequences for specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 25 entity describes enforcement measures for drivers of environmental sanitation vehicles and waste-carrying cars who violate urban transport regulations. The relationship to urban areas situates these penalties within the community’s urban transport rules. [Data: Entities (3624, 5294); Relationships (9495)]

The supplied description does not give the penalty amounts or specify the driving-license point deductions, so those details cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (3624)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Committee chairpersons may impose fines up to 75 million Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under Article 42, Clause 3, the provincial-level People’s Committee chairperson is authorized to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 Vietnamese dong. The chairperson is identified as the head of a provincial-level People’s Committee, linking this enforcement authority to the local-government structure. [Data: Entities (3985, 3986); Relationships (9812)]

The records establish the stated maximum fine and the chairperson’s authority, but do not document any specific fine, case, or enforcement result. [Data: Entities (3985)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Parking at Road Intersection Edges
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of Vehicle Parking and Road Intersection Edge, connected by a rule prohibiting vehicle parking within five meters of an intersection edge. The entity description associates the restriction with Article 18 of Law 36/2024/QH15; the records describe a legal rule, not a specific parking incident or enforcement action.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but practical regulatory importance because it describes a specific parking restriction near road intersections without evidence of a particular violation or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific restriction links the two entities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship states that vehicle parking is prohibited within five meters of a road intersection edge, making the edge the reference point for the restriction. [Data: Relationships (10025)]

The two entities are connected by this single rule; the records do not describe additional parties, events, or related restrictions. [Data: Entities (5451, 4285); Relationships (10025)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The legal context is identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vehicle Parking description names Article 18 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as the provision that names vehicle parking alongside vehicle stopping and prohibits parking at road intersections and within five meters of their edges. [Data: Entities (5451)]

The description notes that the cited excerpt does not define vehicle parking. The records therefore provide the stated restriction but not a fuller statutory definition. [Data: Entities (5451)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The intersection edge is the measurement boundary
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Intersection Edge is described as the boundary of a road intersection from which the five-meter restricted area is measured. [Data: Entities (4285)]

This clarifies how the relationship frames the restricted distance: it is measured from the edge, rather than from an unspecified point within the intersection. [Data: Entities (4285); Relationships (10025)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a rule, not an incident
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available records establish a prohibition on parking within the specified area, but do not identify a vehicle, location, date, alleged violation, penalty, or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (5451, 4285); Relationships (10025)]

Accordingly, the community supports a description of the regulatory requirement, but not a conclusion that anyone has breached it or that a particular case has occurred. [Data: Entities (5451, 4285); Relationships (10025)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate provision is noted for opening vehicle doors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vehicle Parking description also states that Article 19 permits a vehicle door to be opened in connection with a parked vehicle. [Data: Entities (5451)]

The provided information does not give further conditions or explain how this provision interacts with the five-meter parking restriction, so no broader interpretation is established by these records. [Data: Entities (5451)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Patrol and Operator Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community describes a road-traffic safety framework centered on Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, the patrol and control forces that carry out the relevant activities, and road vehicle operators who must comply with stop and inspection requests. The framework covers detecting, preventing, and handling violations, while also recognizing operators’ right to report violations and to challenge relevant administrative decisions or acts. The material establishes legal responsibilities and procedures but provides no specific technical systems, compliance outcomes, or reputation assessments. [Data: Entities (533, 3598, 4514, 548, 4398); Relationships (2470, 9460, 8548, 2571, 8497)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns legally defined road-safety enforcement powers and obligations affecting patrol forces and road users, although the data indicates no specific incident or adverse outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 65 provides the statutory basis for patrol and control
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 addresses patrol and control activities relating to road traffic order and safety. The activities include detecting, preventing, and handling legal violations, linking the law to the operational work of designated forces. [Data: Entities (533, 4411); Relationships (2470, 2469, 2472)]

The available description also states that forces must comply with the law and with orders and plans issued by competent authorities. This establishes an explicit requirement for lawful, authorized conduct, but the supplied material does not describe how compliance is monitored or report outcomes. [Data: Entities (533, 3598)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Patrol and control forces have enforcement responsibilities and constraints
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Patrol and control forces are responsible for road-traffic order and safety patrols and are authorized to issue vehicle-stop orders and make inspection or control requests while performing their duties. The relationships identify these forces as carrying out the regulated patrol and control activity. [Data: Entities (3598, 4398); Relationships (9459, 9455)]

Their authority is bounded by duties to comply with applicable law, competent authorities’ orders and plans, and governing work principles; they must also accept legal responsibility for their decisions and actions. The activity description further says the forces must respect and protect the lawful rights and interests of agencies, organizations, and individuals. [Data: Entities (3598, 4398)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road vehicle operators have defined duties and procedural rights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road vehicle operators must obey stop orders and requests for inspection or control from patrol and control forces. Their broader responsibilities include observing safety requirements and restrictions applicable to road use, as described in the entity record. [Data: Entities (4514, 548); Relationships (9460, 2571, 2570)]

The framework also recognizes operators’ right to explain, complain, or sue in relation to relevant administrative decisions or acts. These provisions indicate that the material covers both compliance obligations and avenues for contesting certain official actions; it does not provide examples of how those rights are exercised. [Data: Entities (548)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to obey a stop order and fleeing are identified conduct categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data separately identifies failure to obey a signal or order to stop and fleeing after failing to comply as conduct involving a road vehicle operator. The relationship records connect the two categories, describing fleeing as occurring after failure to obey the stop signal or order. [Data: Entities (1995, 2294); Relationships (6955, 7363, 6953)]

These records establish that the conduct is addressed in the community’s road-traffic context, but they do not specify penalties, frequency, causes, or any particular incident. No further conclusions about prevalence or enforcement outcomes are supported by the supplied information. [Data: Entities (1995, 2294)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operators are also described as a channel for reporting violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road vehicle operators may report acts that violate the law, and the data links that right to the Law on Denunciations. The entity description says operators may report legal violations observed during patrol and control activities. [Data: Entities (4514, 2844); Relationships (8548, 8497)]

This reporting role complements the authorities’ responsibility to detect, prevent, and handle violations. The supplied material establishes the reporting pathway in general terms but does not describe submission channels, protections for reporters, or the disposition of reports. [Data: Entities (533, 4411); Relationships (2472, 8547)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described framework includes coordination and cross-border violation reporting
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road-traffic patrol and control may be conducted by designated forces and, when necessary, by other mobilized forces and units in coordination with the Traffic Police. The description also emphasizes protection of the lawful rights and interests of affected agencies, organizations, and individuals. [Data: Entities (4398)]

The legal-violations description additionally includes violations in Vietnam by foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles, and says provincial and municipal authorities are required to report such violations to designated ministries and relevant foreign representative bodies. This indicates a reporting dimension beyond ordinary domestic enforcement, though no specific cases or reporting results are provided. [Data: Entities (2880)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is legal and procedural, not technical or reputational
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe statutory provisions, enforcement duties, operator obligations, reporting rights, and categories of conduct. They do not identify particular enforcement technologies, operational systems, or technical capabilities, so none can be assessed from this material. [Data: Entities (533, 3598, 4514, 4398)]

Likewise, the records contain no claims about public reputation, misconduct by a named force, or observed compliance outcomes. The assessment is therefore limited to the framework as described and should not be read as a finding about real-world performance. [Data: Entities (533, 3598, 548)]

v.tieu_de: Turning Around in Prohibited Road Areas
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the traffic violation of turning a vehicle around in prohibited road areas. Five location entities—pedestrian crossings, bridges, bridge approaches, underpasses, and areas beneath overpasses—are linked to that violation. The supplied descriptions characterize the conduct as restricted under stated traffic rules and note that applicable directions, signs, or traffic arrangements may provide exceptions; the data describes rules, not a particular incident or enforcement outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it concerns traffic-rule compliance and road safety, but the supplied records describe restrictions rather than an actual incident or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: One violation concept links five restricted locations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is the traffic violation of turning a vehicle around in prohibited road areas. It is linked to five locations: pedestrian crossings, bridges, bridge approaches, underpasses, and areas beneath overpasses. [Data: Entities (5169, 3606, 672, 673, 5228); Relationships (9470, 2895, 2899, 10609, 673)]

This structure indicates a focused community about where turning around is restricted, rather than a network of separate organizations or individuals. The supplied records do not identify any specific driver, vehicle, incident, or enforcement action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The central description includes stated exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation description identifies exceptions where a traffic controller directs the maneuver, temporary signs permit it, or traffic arrangements provide a designated turning place. The restriction should therefore be understood in the context of those stated exceptions, rather than as an unconditional prohibition in every circumstance. [Data: Entities (5169)]

The source data does not provide details about how these exceptions are applied in a particular location or case.

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Stopping and Related Road-Safety Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on VEHICLE STOPPING and connects it to stated reasons for a temporary stop—passenger boarding or alighting, goods loading or unloading, and a technical inspection—as well as door handling and safety precautions. The supplied description also states restrictions on stopping near road intersections and a requirement to stop before opening a door. The records describe rules and activities, but do not establish whether any person or vehicle complied with them or whether an incident occurred.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it covers road-use restrictions and safety measures, but the records describe rules rather than a specific violation, incident, or threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: VEHICLE STOPPING is the central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:

[Data: Entities (3557, 2395, 3553, 5497); Relationships (7616, 9433, 9430)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A technical inspection is another stated reason to stop

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe safety precautions when the driver leaves the driving position

phat_hien.tom_tat: Door handling is treated as a specific exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.tom_tat: The description identifies restrictions near road intersections

No particular intersection, vehicle, or alleged violation is identified, so the records support describing the restriction but not asserting that it was breached. [Data: Entities (5497)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Officials and Article 73 Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on persons performing official duties in road-traffic settings. Obstruction or resistance is addressed as a violation under Article 73, while officials are directed to take measures in response to noncompliance or obstruction; the specific measures are not stated. v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it connects official road-traffic powers, participant obligations, and an Article 73 violation, although the records establish no specific incident or harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Officials are the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road users are required to comply with official requests
phat_hien.giai_thich:

The relationship records connect the requests to both the officials who make them and the participants who must comply. [Data: Entities (4407, 2683, 3722); Relationships (7973, 7974)]

This establishes an explicit duty to comply in the described framework, but the supplied information does not specify the full range of requests, exceptions, or procedures for challenging them. [Data: Entities (4407, 2683)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pursuit is linked to an operator fleeing after a stop direction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The pursuit entity describes action by a person performing official duties to prevent and handle a violation after an operator ignores a stop signal or order and flees. Officials are expressly identified as authorized to carry out that pursuit. [Data: Entities (4006, 3722); Relationships (9613)]

The information gives no further detail about pursuit procedures, limitations, or outcomes, so it supports describing the stated authority but not assessing how it is applied in practice. [Data: Entities (4006)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Measures may follow noncompliance, but their details are absent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that persons performing official duties take measures when road traffic participants fail to comply with inspection or control requests or obstruct or resist them. The measures are described as legally prescribed or directed, but their specific nature is not stated. [Data: Entities (3722, 2559); Relationships (7823)]

Accordingly, the community reflects an enforcement response in the text, while leaving its scope and practical consequences unspecified. The available records do not support conclusions about particular sanctions or the proportionality of any measure. [Data: Entities (2559, 3722)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes a framework, not an observed event
phat_hien.giai_thich:

They do not identify a specific incident, named individual, organization, or outcome. [Data: Entities (3722, 4407, 3293, 4006); Relationships (7973, 7974, 9613)]

No technical capabilities, organizational reputation, or particular compliance history are provided. The impact assessment therefore reflects the subject’s institutional and road-safety relevance as described, rather than evidence of actual misconduct or harm. [Data: Entities (3722, 3293, 4407)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Article 6, Clause 4 Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6, Clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which establishes fines for specified road traffic violations by drivers of covered vehicles. The clause is linked to a fine of VND 2,000,000 to VND 3,000,000 and to prohibited left and right turns where traffic signs forbid them. v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the clause’s relevance to road safety and financial penalties, while the records provide no evidence of particular incidents or broader effects.

phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibited left turns are included

The records identify the violation and its connection to the clause, but do not report any particular driver, location, or occurrence. [Data: Entities (3916); Relationships (2420)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibited right turns are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A prohibited right turn is described as turning right where a traffic sign forbids the turn for the type of vehicle being driven. The clause provides a fine for this violation. [Data: Entities (3922, 515); Relationships (2421)]

No individual enforcement action or incident involving a prohibited right turn is documented in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3922); Relationships (2421)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community documents a narrow set of related provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed entities form a compact structure: Article 6, Clause 4 connects the specified fine with the prohibited-left-turn and prohibited-right-turn violations. [Data: Entities (515, 2242, 3916, 3922); Relationships (2419, 2420, 2421)]

The records support describing these specific links, but do not establish the clause’s full list of covered violations, the frequency of infractions, or its wider effects. [Data: Entities (515, 2242, 3916, 3922); Relationships (2419, 2420, 2421)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Invitation and Guarantee Procedures and Visa Exemption
v.tom_tat: This community consists of procedures for inviting and guaranteeing certain foreign nationals connected with foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam, and a visa-exemption category. v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but identifiable administrative importance because it describes the scope of a procedure and an explicit visa-exemption carve-out, with no evidence of broader impact or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Procedures concern foreign nationals associated with foreign motor vehicles

phat_hien.tom_tat: Visa-exempt cases are excluded

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe scope, not implementation or compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available descriptions establish the procedural subject and the visa-exemption carve-out, but provide no evidence about implementation, enforcement, or compliance by any person or organization.
