The provided record does not enumerate the specific prohibited acts, so the exact conduct that would trigger a fine cannot be determined from this data alone. [Data: Entities (5600, 5091)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulated category includes both transport businesses and support services
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relevant organization category is not limited to road carriers: it explicitly includes organizations engaged in road transport business or road-transport support services. [Data: Entities (5091)]

The record does not name any organizations or distinguish among types of support services, so the information supports only a general description of the covered category. [Data: Entities (5091)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes a regulatory rule, not a documented enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship states a conditional consequence: organizations in the specified sectors are subject to the fines when they commit the specified violations. It does not report that any organization has been found in violation or fined. [Data: Relationships (10596)]

Accordingly, the community signals a compliance obligation with potential financial consequences, but the available records provide no basis for assessing actual enforcement frequency, organizational conduct, or reputational impact. [Data: Entities (5091, 5600); Relationships (10596)]

v.tieu_de: Driver Image-Recording Equipment Penalty Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community consists of administrative penalty provisions concerning driver image-recording equipment and a linked effective-date record. The provisions address specified passenger-transport, freight-transport, and internal-transport vehicles; the linked date record states that provisions for specified passenger and freight transport vehicles take effect on January 1, 2028. The data does not identify a jurisdiction, enforcement history, or actual violations. [Data: Entities (1452, 1729); Relationships (6034)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it describes future-dated administrative penalty provisions for certain transport vehicles, but the supplied records provide no evidence of implementation, violations, or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions are the community's central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity describes administrative penalties for violations involving equipment that records images of drivers. The sole relationship connects these penalty provisions to their effective-date record. [Data: Entities (1452); Relationships (6034)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A stated effective date is January 1, 2028
phat_hien.giai_thich: The effective-date record states that the relevant administrative penalty provisions take effect on January 1, 2028. This is a future date relative to the information as presented; the records do not establish whether the provisions have since been amended or implemented. [Data: Entities (1729); Relationships (6034)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described vehicle scope includes several transport categories
phat_hien.giai_thich: The penalty-provisions description refers to specified passenger-transport, freight-transport, and internal-transport vehicles. The effective-date description, however, names specified passenger and freight transport vehicles; the supplied records do not clarify whether or when internal-transport vehicles are covered by that date. [Data: Entities (1452, 1729)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records concern administrative penalties, not documented enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity descriptions identify administrative penalty provisions for violations involving driver image-recording equipment. They do not provide penalty amounts, enforcement procedures, cases, or evidence that any person or organization has violated the provisions. [Data: Entities (1452, 1729)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence is narrow and leaves key context unspecified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The dataset contains two entities and one relationship, linking the penalty provisions to the stated effective date. It supplies no jurisdiction, issuing authority, technical specifications for the equipment, or information on practical compliance or operational impact. [Data: Entities (1452, 1729); Relationships (6034)]

v.tieu_de: Administrative Sanctioning and Vehicle-Document Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Administrative Sanctioning, which is linked to three categories of road-traffic violations: license-plate, temporary vehicle-registration-certificate, and vehicle-registration-certificate violations. The information describes a legal and procedural framework for administrative penalties, but does not identify specific cases, sanctioned parties, penalty amounts, or compliance outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it connects a general administrative-sanctioning framework to three defined traffic-violation categories, while providing no case-specific evidence of harm or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative Sanctioning is the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative Sanctioning is the hub of this community and is connected to each of the three listed vehicle-related violation categories. Its description covers administrative penalties, including those for road-traffic violations, and refers to applicable procedures and principles. [Data: Entities (103); Relationships (274, 276, 278)]

The provided information describes rules and their scope; it does not establish that any particular person or organization was sanctioned. [Data: Entities (103); Relationships (274, 276, 278)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes procedural and timing provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Administrative Sanctioning description references procedures and principles set out in Article 47 and a limitation period for issuing a sanctioning decision addressed in Article 4 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (103)]

It also states that, for road-traffic violations, the governing decree is the one in force when the violation occurred. The data does not provide further details about how these provisions apply in an individual case. [Data: Entities (103)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-plate violations are within the stated penalty scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
License-Plate Violation is explicitly linked to Administrative Sanctioning as a violation subject to the stated penalty rules. Its description says the category is covered by cited provisions of Articles 13, 14, 16, and 32. [Data: Entities (2902); Relationships (274)]

No specific license-plate conduct, case, penalty, or enforcement result is supplied, so the record supports identification of the category but not conclusions about a particular violation. [Data: Entities (2902); Relationships (274)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two registration-certificate violation categories are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community separately identifies Temporary Vehicle-Registration Certificate Violation and Vehicle-Registration Certificate Violation. Both are linked to Administrative Sanctioning as subject to the stated penalty rules. [Data: Entities (4894, 5526); Relationships (276, 278)]

The descriptions refer to cited provisions of Articles 13, 14, 16, and 32, but do not specify conduct, case facts, penalties, or outcomes for either category. [Data: Entities (4894, 5526)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence is regulatory, not case-specific
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the sanctioning framework and its connection to three violation types. They do not identify individuals, vehicle owners, enforcement agencies, or specific sanctioning decisions. [Data: Entities (103, 2902, 4894, 5526); Relationships (274, 276, 278)]

Accordingly, the data supports describing the community’s legal subject matter, but not assessing the compliance history, reputation, technical capabilities, or actual impact of any actor within it. [Data: Entities (103, 2902, 4894, 5526); Relationships (274, 276, 278)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger-Cabin Image-Recording Equipment Penalties
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of a set of administrative penalty provisions concerning equipment that records images of passenger compartments in road-transport vehicles and a separate entity specifying when those provisions take effect. The two are directly linked: the provisions take effect on January 1, 2029. The supplied information does not describe particular violations, penalty amounts, enforcement procedures, or legal compliance by any person or organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it identifies a future effective date for administrative penalties, but provides little detail about their scope or practical consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A narrowly connected, two-entity community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains two entities: the effective-date item and the passenger-cabin image-recording equipment penalty provisions. The only supplied relationship connects them by stating that the provisions take effect on January 1, 2029. [Data: Entities (1730, 3578); Relationships (6611)]

This establishes a focused connection between a legal timing provision and the subject of the penalties, rather than a broader network of named organizations or individuals. [Data: Entities (1730, 3578); Relationships (6611)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions concern administrative penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalty provisions are described as administrative penalties for violations involving equipment that records images of passenger compartments in road-transport vehicles. [Data: Entities (3578)]

The supplied record does not specify the conduct that constitutes a violation, the amount or form of any penalty, or who is responsible for enforcing it. Those details therefore cannot be assessed from this data. [Data: Entities (3578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: January 1, 2029 is the stated effective date
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The effective-date entity states that the provisions on administrative penalties related to passenger-cabin image-recording equipment take effect on January 1, 2029. The relationship record confirms that this date applies to the penalty provisions. [Data: Entities (1730); Relationships (6611)]

The data identifies a future commencement date but does not provide information about any earlier or transitional rules. [Data: Entities (1730, 3578); Relationships (6611)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The scope is tied to equipment in road-transport vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalty provisions are specifically described in relation to equipment that records images of passenger compartments in road-transport vehicles. [Data: Entities (3578)]

The records do not establish whether the provisions cover particular vehicle types, operators, equipment configurations, or uses of recorded images. [Data: Entities (3578)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal and operational implications remain unspecified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The effective-date description says the provisions are subject to the relevant law on passenger-cabin image-recording equipment in road vehicles. [Data: Entities (1730)]

No text of that law, compliance guidance, enforcement activity, or evidence of actual violations is included. Accordingly, the records support identifying the stated legal timing and subject matter, but not conclusions about compliance, implementation, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (1730, 3578); Relationships (6611)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Order and Safety Community
v.tom_tat: This community centers on individuals and organizations subject to Vietnam’s road-traffic order and safety rules. Both groups are connected to knowledge checks, permit procedures for intelligent transport vehicles, and potential administrative penalties; organizations also have a stated role in legal information dissemination. The material describes protections for their lawful rights, several categories of violations and sanctions, and the use of technical equipment or collected results in identifying violators. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 2724, 4364); Relationships (7908, 7915, 8030, 9336, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high impact because the rules apply to both individuals and organizations across road-traffic procedures, permitting, enforcement, and substantial penalties. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 2268); Relationships (7916, 9337, 7331, 7332)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individuals and organizations are the central stakeholders
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around two broad stakeholder groups: individuals and organizations affected by road-traffic order and safety rules. Both may be involved in legal-knowledge checks, intelligent-transport-vehicle permit applications, and enforcement for specified violations. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 2724, 4364); Relationships (7908, 7915, 8030, 9336)]

The descriptions also state that both groups’ lawful rights and interests must be respected during patrols, controls, and accident investigations or resolutions. The rules therefore concern both compliance obligations and protections in enforcement processes. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes rights protections and participation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Individuals and organizations may contribute amendments or supplements to information in the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database. The descriptions also prohibit misuse or abuse of patrol, control, investigation, and resolution processes in ways that infringe their lawful rights and interests. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437)]

These provisions indicate that the community is not described solely in terms of regulated parties: the entities are also identified as participants in updating information and as holders of protected rights. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Knowledge checks and organizational legal dissemination are part of the system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Law Knowledge Check assesses knowledge of laws concerning road-traffic order and safety, and the competent authority assigns personnel to conduct it. The circular is described as applying to individuals and organizations related to these checks. [Data: Entities (4364); Relationships (7915, 9336)]

Organizations also have a stated responsibility to organize legal propaganda and dissemination for people under their management. This places them in a compliance-support role in addition to their potential exposure to penalties. [Data: Entities (3437)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent transport vehicles require a formal permit application
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Owners of intelligent transport vehicles, whether individuals or organizations, must prepare an application dossier and submit it to the competent licensing authority. The procedure allows submission online, by postal service, or in person. [Data: Entities (2724); Relationships (7908, 8030)]

The described process establishes a defined administrative step for these owners; the provided information does not specify approval criteria or processing times. [Data: Entities (2724)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violations can lead to varied administrative consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The source describes multiple fine ranges for individuals, with the applicable amount depending on the particular violation. It also identifies possible additional consequences, including revocation of specified vehicle documents, corrective measures, and surrender of unlawful gains. [Data: Entities (2651, 1126, 4421); Relationships (7916, 3980)]

Organizations may likewise face fines and additional penalties, including document revocation, corrective measures, or surrender of unlawful gains. The available records describe a broad enforcement framework rather than a single penalty applicable to all violations. [Data: Entities (3437, 1126, 4421); Relationships (9337, 3981)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some specified offenses carry particularly high fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Organizing illegal racing is associated with fines of VND 40 million to 50 million for individuals and VND 80 million to 100 million for organizations. These figures demonstrate that the stated consequences differ substantially by offender type and offense. [Data: Entities (2268); Relationships (7331, 7332)]

Other identified areas include unauthorized vehicle-registration-plate transactions and exceeding permitted vehicle payload. The records connect both individuals and organizations to penalties for these conduct categories, but do not provide a single uniform penalty applicable across them. [Data: Entities (2549, 1875, 2651, 3437); Relationships (7808, 7809, 6818, 6819)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Enforcement uses collected results, with consequences for obstruction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Individuals and organizations may provide technical equipment or collected results used to identify administrative violators. The descriptions also state that intentional evasion of or obstruction to sanctioning can affect the period for using collected results, which is recalculated when the conduct ends. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 1847); Relationships (6777, 6778)]

This links technical inputs and evidence handling to the enforcement process, while the records do not specify the equipment types or the detailed recalculation method. [Data: Entities (1847, 2651, 3437)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information describes regulation, not individual compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify duties, procedures, rights protections, and potential penalties for categories of individuals and organizations. They do not identify particular people or organizations as having complied with or violated these rules, so no conclusion about any specific entity’s conduct or compliance status is supported. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 2724, 4421); Relationships (7908, 8030, 7916, 9337)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Violations and Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP
v.tom_tat: This community describes a transitional rule for administrative road-traffic violations: penalties are imposed under the decree in force when the conduct occurred, even when a violation is discovered later or remains under review. The effective date of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP is identified as relevant to determining whether the rule applies. The records establish a procedural connection between violations, timing, and penalty decisions, but do not name the earlier governing decree or provide the effective date.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because its timing rule can affect how administrative road-traffic penalties are determined, though the records provide no evidence of broader harms or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A transitional rule links violations to penalty decisions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central relationship is that an administrative road-traffic violation is subject to a penalty under the decree in force when the conduct occurred. This makes the time of the violation—not simply the later date of its resolution—relevant to the penalty process. [Data: Entities (98, 2586, 1306); Relationships (259, 5685)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The effective date of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP is a timing boundary
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify the decree’s effective date as a factor in deciding whether its transitional rule applies to a violation that occurred and ended before it took effect. The date itself is not supplied, so the records do not establish which calendar-day violations fall on either side of the boundary. [Data: Entities (98, 1735); Relationships (258)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Later discovery or continued review does not change the stated rule
phat_hien.giai_thich: The provision is described as applying when the violation is discovered later or is still under consideration for resolution after the conduct has ended. In those circumstances, the violation remains connected to the decree in force at the time it was committed for purposes of imposing a penalty. [Data: Entities (98, 1400, 2586, 1306); Relationships (257, 259, 5685)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The earlier governing decree is not identified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community specifies that the decree in force when the violation occurred governs the penalty, but the corresponding entity explicitly does not name that decree. Consequently, these records support the timing principle but do not identify the precise earlier instrument applicable to any particular violation. [Data: Entities (1306, 2586); Relationships (5685, 259)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe administrative conduct, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation entity concerns breaches of administrative road-traffic rules and notes that the database records conduct, time, and location. The supplied relationships establish how such violations connect to review and penalty imposition, but they do not provide individual cases, penalty amounts, compliance results, or evidence of broader consequences. [Data: Entities (98, 2586, 1400); Relationships (257, 259)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Ministry of Health Driver Health Databases and Vehicle Standards
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Vietnamese Ministry of Health, which establishes health-related standards and manages health databases for drivers and operators of specialized vehicles. The relationships connect the Ministry to two driver-health database records, specialized motor vehicle operators, and requirements for ambulance signal-device permits. The database includes health information about specialized motorcycle operators, while the Ministry’s broader described responsibilities include driver examinations, alcohol-assessment requirements, and ambulance standards. The records indicate regulatory and public-service significance but provide no evidence of noncompliance, data misuse, or security incidents.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the Ministry’s broad health-regulatory responsibilities and its management of health information for vehicle operators, alongside its role in ambulance-related requirements.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry of Health is the community’s central authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vietnamese Ministry of Health is described as responsible for establishing health standards and examination requirements for drivers and operators of specialized motorcycles and other specialized motor vehicles. Its remit also includes periodic health examinations for professional car drivers and requirements for assessing alcohol concentration and endogenous alcohol in blood. [Data: Entities (3014)]

The Ministry is directly linked to the driver health database, the driver and specialized motorcycle operator health database, and operators of specialized motor vehicles. These relationships make it the central institutional entity in this community. [Data: Relationships (6007, 6030, 8815)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry builds and manages driver-health databases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Two database entities are identified: the Driver and Specialized Motorcycle Operator Health Database and the Driver Health Database. The relationships state that the Ministry builds and manages each database. [Data: Entities (1443, 1449); Relationships (6007, 6030)]

The records describe health information as the databases’ subject matter and identify the databases as sources of information specified in Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. The supplied information does not establish how the databases are secured, who can access them, or whether any misuse has occurred. [Data: Entities (1443, 1449)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized motorcycle operators are represented in the health-data system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Driver and Specialized Motorcycle Operator Health Database is described as containing health information about specialized motorcycle operators, and a relationship directly links those operators to the database. [Data: Entities (1443, 4703); Relationships (6009)]

The operator entity also describes specialized motorcycle operators as participants in road-traffic-law training, testing, and certification. These details indicate that the community concerns both health information and a population subject to training and certification provisions; the records do not specify the volume of people or records involved. [Data: Entities (4703)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Health information also covers operators of specialized motor vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is described as responsible for managing a health database that includes information about operators of specialized motor vehicles. The corresponding relationship connects the Ministry to this population through that database-management responsibility. [Data: Entities (3014, 3418); Relationships (8815)]

This connects the Ministry’s administrative role to health information about people operating specialized vehicles. The supplied records do not detail specific data fields, retention periods, or operational safeguards. [Data: Entities (3418)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ambulance signal-device permits are conditional on health-ministry requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The permit-issuance process covers new or replacement permits to use signal devices on priority vehicles. For ambulances, the entity description says permits are conditional on compliance with applicable ambulance standards and use requirements. [Data: Entities (3876)]

A relationship assigns the relevant ambulance standards and use requirements to the Minister of Health, linking the Ministry’s regulatory role to this permit process. The records do not describe individual permit decisions or indicate noncompliance. [Data: Relationships (8816)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has notable regulatory and public-service importance, with no documented misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe responsibilities spanning driver health standards, examinations, health databases, and ambulance requirements. Taken together, these functions give the community significance for health administration and vehicle-related public services. [Data: Entities (3014, 1443, 3876); Relationships (6007, 8816)]

The supplied data contains no allegations, enforcement actions, or evidence of data breaches or other wrongdoing. Accordingly, the impact assessment reflects the importance and reach of the described functions, not a finding of harmful conduct. [Data: Entities (3014, 1443, 3876); Relationships (6007, 8816)]

v.tieu_de: Onboard Staff and Passenger Instruction Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community links onboard service staff, a passenger traffic-order and safety violation, and the legal provision that sets its penalty. The staff are described as giving safety-related instructions, while Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 33, Clause 1 identifies passenger failure to follow such instructions as punishable by a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese dong. The records describe a general rule and do not identify a specific incident.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it connects onboard safety instructions to a defined legal penalty, but the records describe a limited regulatory topic rather than a specific incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Onboard service staff are the operational center of the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Onboard service staff are described as personnel who provide services aboard passenger-transport vehicles and who may coordinate with police agencies on tasks supporting national security and public order. The description also says passengers must follow their instructions concerning traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (3308)]

Their connection to the passenger violation makes their instructions the operational trigger in this community’s rule structure. [Data: Relationships (9262)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation concerns noncompliance with safety-related instructions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The defined violation is a passenger’s failure to comply with instructions from a driver or onboard service staff while traveling in a vehicle. The stated subject of those instructions is traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (3559)]

The relationship record specifically connects this violation to onboard service staff and confirms the safety- and traffic-order context. [Data: Relationships (9262)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The cited provision sets a monetary fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 33, Clause 1 is described as covering listed traffic-order and safety violations, including failure to follow instructions from a driver or onboard service staff. [Data: Entities (1291)]

For this conduct, the records state a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (3559, 1291); Relationships (5629)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is structured around a rule and its enforcement consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records form a compact chain: onboard service staff give safety-related instructions; a passenger’s failure to comply is the defined violation; and the cited legal provision specifies the fine. [Data: Entities (3308, 3559, 1291); Relationships (9262, 5629)]

This structure makes the community relevant to understanding the stated relationship between onboard conduct and a regulatory penalty. The available records do not describe enforcement processes beyond the specified fine. [Data: Entities (3559, 1291); Relationships (5629)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a general rule, not a particular case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions define staff duties, a category of passenger conduct, and the applicable fine; the relationships connect those concepts. They do not name a passenger, vehicle, enforcement action, or specific event. [Data: Entities (3308, 3559, 1291); Relationships (9262, 5629)]

Accordingly, the material supports an account of the rule and its stated penalty, but not conclusions about how often violations occur or whether a particular person has violated it. [Data: Entities (3559, 1291); Relationships (5629)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP Road-Traffic Amendments
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP, a Vietnamese government decree amending administrative rules and penalties related to road traffic. Its connected provisions include Article 8, which addresses journey-monitoring devices and data in transport vehicles, while Articles 18, 19, and 11 concern further amendments to other regulatory provisions. The decree’s described scope also includes vehicle license-plate violations, sanctioning authority, and transitional rules. The records establish regulatory subject matter but do not report implementation outcomes or compliance by particular operators.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high impact importance because the decree covers multiple areas of road-traffic regulation and administrative enforcement, though the records provide no evidence of implementation outcomes or specific harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree is the community’s central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP is the central entity, described as a Vietnamese government decree amending and supplementing administrative penalties for road-traffic violations and related matters. Its provisions cover several distinct subjects, including license-plate requirements, sanctioning authority, image-recording equipment, and transitional handling of violations. [Data: Entities (1300)]

The connected amendment records reinforce this structure: Articles 8, 18, 19, and 11 are each identified as provisions or changes within the decree. [Data: Relationships (2606, 1019, 1055, 566)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 8 addresses journey-monitoring devices and data
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 8 amends point c of clause 5 of Article 21 concerning journey-monitoring devices and data in transport vehicles. It is explicitly linked to Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP as one of the decree’s provisions. [Data: Entities (558); Relationships (2606)]

The associated conduct is operating a commercial transport car, tractor unit, or internal transport vehicle in traffic without a journey-monitoring device, with a device that is not functioning as required, or while altering device data. The records identify this as conduct addressed by the amendment; they do not specify enforcement outcomes or establish that any named operator committed it. [Data: Entities (3383); Relationships (2607)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree covers vehicle plate violations and enforcement authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree description identifies rules concerning plates that are missing, improperly positioned or formatted, unclear, altered, obscured, or made difficult to identify. It also describes amendments to rules on improper plate placement or formatting and obscured or altered plate information. [Data: Entities (1300)]

The same description states that Article 15 amends Article 44, which sets out the administrative sanctioning authority of road and construction officials. This establishes that the decree addresses both regulated conduct and who has authority to impose administrative sanctions, but the supplied records do not detail particular cases or enforcement results. [Data: Entities (1300)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Articles 18, 19, and 11 form a cluster of additional amendments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18 is described as adding paragraphs 3 and 4 after paragraph 2 of Article 53, and its relationship record connects that amendment to the decree. The decree description further says Article 18 adds rules governing administrative penalties related to image-recording equipment on certain road-transport vehicles. [Data: Entities (279, 1300); Relationships (1019)]

Article 19 concerns supplementation, replacement, and repeal of specified phrases, points, clauses, and articles. Separately, the Article 11 record identifies amendments and supplements to certain points and clauses of Article 32. Both are linked to the decree, indicating that its changes extend beyond the Article 8 journey-monitoring provisions. [Data: Entities (291, 185); Relationships (1055, 566)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records show regulatory scope, not demonstrated compliance or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material describes the decree’s provisions and identifies one category of conduct involving journey-monitoring devices and altered data. It does not identify specific transport operators, enforcement actions, penalty amounts, compliance rates, or the practical effects of the amendments. [Data: Entities (1300, 3383, 558)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance can be assessed from the breadth of the stated regulatory topics, but the records do not support conclusions about the decree’s implementation, the reputation of affected entities, or actual violations by any person or organization. [Data: Entities (1300); Relationships (2606, 2607, 1019, 1055, 566)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Inspection Refusal and Documentation Issues
v.tom_tat: This community centers on inspection refusal and two documented grounds for it: suspected vehicle-document falsification and discrepancies between registration information and the vehicle or license plate presented. The entity description also lists other circumstances in which refusal may be permitted, but the supplied relationships specifically connect refusal to falsification and registration discrepancies. The records describe grounds for an administrative decision, not a finding that any particular owner committed falsification or that a specific vehicle was refused inspection.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest impact because it concerns vehicle inspection decisions and documentation compliance, while the supplied records establish procedural grounds rather than particular cases or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection refusal is the community’s central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich: Inspection refusal is the highest-degree entity in the supplied set and serves as the point connecting the two documented issues: suspected falsification of vehicle documents and discrepancies in vehicle registration information. Its description presents refusal as permitted only in specified circumstances, rather than as an unrestricted action. [Data: Entities (2691, 5386, 5479); Relationships (7991, 7992)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Suspected document falsification is a stated ground for refusal
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe suspected falsification by a vehicle owner of documents or papers relating to a vehicle as a possible ground for refusing inspection. The linked relationship qualifies this by stating that there must be a substantiated basis to suspect falsification. This describes a potential basis for refusal, not proof that falsification occurred in any specific case. [Data: Entities (5386, 2691); Relationships (7991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration-information discrepancies can also justify refusal
phat_hien.giai_thich: A mismatch between information on a vehicle registration certificate and the vehicle’s license plate or the vehicle presented for inspection is identified as a stated ground for refusal. The relationship links that discrepancy directly to inspection refusal. [Data: Entities (5479, 2691); Relationships (7992)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The refusal description includes additional circumstances
phat_hien.giai_thich: Beyond the two issues represented by relationship records, the inspection-refusal entity description lists other circumstances: a request from an authority involved in legal proceedings, an unresolved administrative-violation requirement, and failure to replace a registration certificate after modification certification. These are presented as specified circumstances in which refusal is permitted. [Data: Entities (2691)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish grounds, not case outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information describes when an inspection facility may refuse inspection and identifies possible documentation-related grounds. It does not identify a particular vehicle owner, an actual inspection refusal, an adjudicated violation, or the outcome of any proceeding. Accordingly, the records support a description of the stated procedure, but not conclusions about individual compliance or wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (2691, 5386, 5479); Relationships (7991, 7992)]

v.tieu_de: Drivers and Road-Safety Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on drivers and the regulatory requirements that apply to their work. Drivers are linked to periodic health examinations, professional training and guidance, and experience-related violations involving student transport and double-decker sleeper buses. Organizations have responsibilities for arranging certain remedial measures, which can also cover vehicle service employees. The available records describe rules and specified violations, but do not establish how often violations occur or identify particular offenders. [Data: Entities (1538, 882, 3911, 3692, 5342, +more); Relationships (3360, 6233, 6235, 6243, 6242, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it covers driver conduct and passenger transport, although the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or the prevalence of violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Drivers are the community’s central regulated group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around drivers, who operate vehicles on roads and are subject to traffic rules and applicable training, guidance, health, and administrative requirements. The supplied description includes speed limits, safe-distance rules, seat-belt use, expressway requirements, and helmet standards for motorcycle and motorbike drivers. [Data: Entities (1538)]

These requirements show why the community has broad road-safety relevance. The records describe obligations rather than documenting whether any particular driver complied with or breached them. [Data: Entities (1538)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Health checks and professional guidance are specified compliance measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers are connected to periodic health examinations and professional training and guidance. The relationships describe health examinations as an express requirement and training or guidance as potentially applicable depending on the circumstances. [Data: Relationships (6233, 6235)]

Clause 13 is also linked to these measures as requirements that organizations arrange in specified cases. The records therefore identify both driver-related requirements and organizational duties, without specifying how widely the measures are implemented. [Data: Entities (882, 3692, 3911); Relationships (3362, 3363)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Experience requirements concern sensitive passenger-transport duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Two specified violations involve using drivers who have not met the required years of experience: operating vehicles transporting preschool children or students, and operating double-decker sleeper passenger buses. Drivers are identified as the people whose insufficient experience constitutes these violations. [Data: Entities (5342, 5341); Relationships (6243, 6242)]

These categories indicate that experience requirements are relevant to transport involving students and passengers on sleeper buses. The records do not state the required number of years, name any operator or driver, or establish that either violation occurred in a particular case. [Data: Entities (5342, 5341)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizations and vehicle service employees also fall within the compliance framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The remedial measures described include arranging training and professional guidance for relevant personnel, as well as regular health examinations for drivers and employees serving on vehicles. This makes the framework broader than drivers alone. [Data: Entities (3911, 3692, 5492); Relationships (9752, 9581)]

The records place responsibility for arranging these measures on an organization in specified cases, but do not identify any organization or provide evidence about whether a particular organization has fulfilled its responsibilities. [Data: Entities (3911, 3692); Relationships (3362, 3363)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-transport duties include operational safety steps
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers conducting passenger transport must follow applicable rules and, where required, hold an identification card and carry a transport order or another transport document. Before departure, they must check vehicle safety and inform passengers about road safety and emergency evacuation. [Data: Entities (1538)]

The description also says passenger-transport drivers may be required to coordinate with police agencies in duties supporting national security and public order. This is presented as conditional, not as a universal requirement for every driver or trip. [Data: Entities (1538)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Clause 13 reference is not fully resolved by the records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 13 is described in two regulatory contexts: as a clause of Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning remedial measures for certain road-transport violations, and as Clause 13 of Article 13 concerning driver-license point deductions for specified vehicle-condition violations. The entity description explicitly does not establish whether these are the same provision. [Data: Entities (882)]

Relationships connect Clause 13 with drivers, periodic health examinations, and professional training and guidance. Those links should be read alongside the stated ambiguity; the available data does not justify treating the two regulatory references as identical. [Data: Relationships (3360, 3362, 3363)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Inspection Activity and Regulatory Violations
v.tom_tat: This community consists of the regulated activity of inspecting motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts, and the category of violations concerning regulations for that activity. The activity is described as regulated by Article 40; violations by inspection facilities may result in a monetary penalty. The data does not identify a particular facility, incident, or penalty.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low to moderate because the community concerns regulatory noncompliance with potential monetary penalties, but the data describes a general violation category rather than a specific incident or demonstrated impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community links inspection activity with related violations
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship explicitly connects motor vehicle inspection activity to violations of vehicle inspection regulations, describing the violations as concerning regulations governing that activity. This establishes a direct regulatory connection between the two entities. [Data: Relationships (9033)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection activity is regulated under Article 40
phat_hien.giai_thich: Motor vehicle inspection activity is described as the inspection of motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts. The entity description states that this activity is regulated by Article 40. [Data: Entities (3112)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation category concerns inspection facilities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violations entity describes conduct by inspection facilities that violates regulations governing vehicle inspections. The data identifies the type of regulated party at a general level but does not name any particular facility. [Data: Entities (5601)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monetary penalties are a stated possible consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation category is described as conduct that may result in a monetary penalty. The record does not establish that a penalty was imposed in any particular case. [Data: Entities (5601)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a regulatory category, not a specific case
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records define inspection activity and a related violation category, and connect them through a single relationship. They do not identify a specific inspection, violator, enforcement action, or realized harm, so the community's impact cannot be assessed as an actual incident from these records alone. [Data: Entities (5601, 3112); Relationships (9033)]

v.tieu_de: Competent State Authority and Administrative Violation Resolution
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a competent state authority and the process for resolving an administrative violation related to road traffic order and safety. The authority may require a vehicle owner to complete that resolution. The authority is also described as empowered to issue vehicle registration plates and produce or authorize their production. The supplied information does not establish particular violations, compliance outcomes, or broader reputational or technical impacts. [Data: Entities (122, 1064); Relationships (387)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a limited administrative relationship and do not document specific violations, adverse outcomes, or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority may require resolution of a road-traffic administrative violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship record states that the competent state authority may require a vehicle owner to resolve an administrative violation concerning road traffic order and safety. This establishes the central connection between the two entities in the community. [Data: Relationships (387)]

The record describes an authority and a possible requirement; it does not identify a particular owner, violation, enforcement action, or outcome. [Data: Relationships (387)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The resolution process is defined as an administrative procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative Violation Resolution is described as the process of resolving an administrative violation in the field of road traffic order and safety. The description says a vehicle owner may be required to complete it by a competent state authority. [Data: Entities (122)]

No details are provided about the steps, deadlines, penalties, or criteria involved in the process. [Data: Entities (122)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority also has vehicle-registration-plate responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent state authority is described as empowered by the cited law to issue vehicle registration plates, produce them, or authorize their production. This places its described functions beyond requiring resolution of administrative violations. [Data: Entities (1064)]

The records do not specify the authority’s jurisdiction, operational capacity, or how it carries out these plate-related functions. [Data: Entities (1064)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship identifies a possible obligation for vehicle owners
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description and relationship both indicate that a vehicle owner may be required to complete the violation-resolution process. The wording is conditional and does not establish that every owner, or any named owner, is subject to such a requirement. [Data: Entities (122); Relationships (387)]

No individual cases or evidence of owners’ compliance or noncompliance are included in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (122); Relationships (387)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records do not support conclusions about compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information describes the authority’s stated powers and its connection to an administrative process, but contains no case outcomes, compliance findings, allegations, or reputation assessments. Accordingly, those matters cannot be evaluated from these records. [Data: Entities (122, 1064); Relationships (387)]

The community is narrowly documented as an administrative and regulatory relationship; the records do not establish further impacts beyond the described functions and possible requirement. [Data: Entities (122, 1064); Relationships (387)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Owner and Registration Responsibilities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the MOTOR VEHICLE OWNER, whose responsibilities are linked to both individuals and organizations named on vehicle registration certificates. The registered individual or organization continues to bear owner responsibilities in specified cases until the registration certificate and license plates are recalled. The records describe legal and administrative responsibilities, including responsibilities that may arise after an accident, but do not document a specific violation or incident. [Data: Entities (3126, 4066, 4067); Relationships (9048, 9049)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical and regulatory importance because it connects vehicle ownership to ongoing responsibilities for both individual and organizational registrants, though no specific incident or violation is recorded. [Data: Entities (3126, 4066, 4067); Relationships (9048, 9049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The MOTOR VEHICLE OWNER is the community's central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MOTOR VEHICLE OWNER is the central entity and is described as a person who owns a motor vehicle, including a specialized motor vehicle. Its listed degree is 7, higher than those of the two registration-related entities, consistent with its central role in this community. [Data: Entities (3126, 4066, 4067)]

The description associates ownership with responsibilities under Article 43 and a relevant legal passage, including responsibilities that may arise when a road traffic accident occurs. It also mentions administrative-violation requirements and possible falsification of vehicle documents, but does not state that any particular owner committed a violation or falsification. [Data: Entities (3126)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registered individuals can retain owner responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A REGISTERED INDIVIDUAL is described as an individual listed on a vehicle registration certificate. In specified cases, that individual continues to bear the responsibilities of the vehicle owner until the certificate and license plates are recalled. [Data: Entities (4066); Relationships (9048)]

This relationship makes registration status relevant to identifying who remains responsible under the stated conditions. The records do not specify which cases require recall or provide an example of an individual registrant's conduct. [Data: Entities (4066); Relationships (9048)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registered organizations are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A REGISTERED ORGANIZATION is an organization listed on a vehicle registration certificate. Like a registered individual, it continues to bear the responsibilities of the vehicle owner in specified cases until the registration certificate and license plates are recalled. [Data: Entities (4067); Relationships (9049)]

The community therefore describes responsibilities applying to both individual and organizational registrants. It does not identify any particular organization or indicate that an organization in the data has violated a requirement. [Data: Entities (4067); Relationships (9049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recall of registration documents and plates is a stated boundary
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Both relationships describe continued owner responsibilities as lasting until the registration certificate and license plates are recalled, where recall is required. This establishes a condition associated with the end of those continuing responsibilities in the specified cases. [Data: Relationships (9048, 9049)]

The supplied records do not explain the recall procedure, its timing, or whether recall has occurred for any vehicle. Accordingly, the data supports identifying recall as a relevant condition, but not conclusions about the status of a specific registration. [Data: Entities (4066, 4067); Relationships (9048, 9049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records indicate legal relevance, not documented noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The owner description refers to legal responsibilities, possible accident-related duties, administrative-violation requirements, and possible falsification of vehicle documents. These points show that the community is relevant to vehicle-related legal and administrative compliance. [Data: Entities (3126)]

However, the entries describe responsibilities and possible issues rather than reporting a specific accident, administrative violation, falsified document, or enforcement action. The available information therefore does not support characterizing any entity as noncompliant. [Data: Entities (3126, 4066, 4067); Relationships (9048, 9049)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Businesses and Compliance Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road transport businesses and related support service providers, connected to two specified compliance issues: vehicle color requirements when transporting preschool children or students, and issuing required transport orders or documents to drivers. The entities also describe obligations involving passenger-compartment recording data and potential administrative fines under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The information concerns regulatory exposure; it does not establish that any particular organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (4480, 4495, 4498, 1984); Relationships (10263, 6942, 6943)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns compliance requirements and potential fines for road transport organizations, but the records do not establish actual violations or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road transport businesses are the central regulated group
phat_hien.giai_thich: Road transport businesses are described as organizations conducting commercial road transport by automobile. The entity record identifies several categories of potential administrative violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, including breaches of business regulations or operating conditions and certain equipment, data-management, and driver-document requirements. These are described as potential regulatory consequences, not as confirmed conduct by a particular business. [Data: Entities (4480)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specified color requirement applies to some student-transport vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify a violation involving the use of a road transport business vehicle to carry preschool children or students when it lacks the paint color required by regulations. The relationship states that organizations committing this violation are subject to a fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The data does not identify a specific vehicle or organization that committed the violation. [Data: Entities (4498); Relationships (10263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required driver transport orders and documents are a compliance concern
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed violation concerns failing to issue a required transport order or document to a driver, or issuing one contrary to regulations. Road transport businesses may commit this violation, according to the relationship connecting the violation to that business category. [Data: Entities (1984); Relationships (6942)]

The entity description for road transport businesses lists several organizational fine ranges for specified violations under the decree, but the provided records do not tie a particular range to this document violation. [Data: Entities (4480, 1984)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Support providers are included in the regulatory network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road transport support service providers are described as organizations that provide support services for road transport. Their entity description identifies potential penalties for specified failures involving data collected by passenger-compartment image-recording devices installed in vehicles. [Data: Entities (4495)]

A separate relationship also connects support service providers to the failure-to-issue-required-transport-orders-or-documents violation, stating that organizations conducting transport support services are covered by the listed fine. The records do not provide a specific fine amount for this connection. [Data: Relationships (6943)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Equipment and data-management requirements broaden the compliance scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road transport business description identifies potential violations involving failure to provide, update, transmit, store, or manage data from passenger-compartment image-recording devices, as well as violations involving journey-monitoring devices. It also notes that Article 26, Clauses 4 and 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP specify organizational fines for certain listed violations, including some concerning passenger-compartment recording equipment. [Data: Entities (4480)]

The support-provider description separately identifies potential liability relating to passenger-compartment image-recording data. Together, these records show that the community’s compliance scope includes data and device management, though they do not establish an actual failure by any organization. [Data: Entities (4495)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Support Organizations and Article 26 Violations
v.tom_tat: This community links road transport support service organizations to two categories of potential regulatory violations under Article 26: failure to issue required driver identification cards and specified passenger-vehicle camera-recording violations. The records describe applicable organizational fines, including higher penalties for camera-related violations. They describe legal requirements and possible penalties, not confirmed violations by any organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns regulatory obligations and potentially significant fines for transport organizations, but the records identify no actual violations or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport support organizations are the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: Road transport support service organizations are the shared entity connecting both violation categories: they may be fined for failing to issue driver identification cards and for passenger-transport vehicle camera-recording violations. This makes their compliance obligations the organizing focus of the community. [Data: Entities (4494); Relationships (6940, 9443)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to issue driver identification cards carries stated fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described Article 26 violation is failing to issue drivers the identification cards required by regulations. The stated fine is VND 3,000,000–4,000,000 for individuals and VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 for transport businesses or transport-support-service organizations. [Data: Entities (1983)]

The relationship record specifically indicates that road transport support service organizations may be fined for this violation; it does not establish that any particular organization committed it. [Data: Relationships (6940)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Camera-recording requirements cover several types of noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The camera-related provision applies to passenger-transport cars with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat. The described violations include lacking required equipment to record images of the passenger compartment, equipment failing to record or store data while the vehicle is in traffic, and falsifying the equipment’s data. [Data: Entities (3569)]

The record identifies these as violations under Article 26, Clause 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It describes the scope of the provision, not a finding that a specific vehicle or operator violated it. [Data: Entities (3569)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Camera-related organizational fines are higher than the stated ID-card fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the specified camera-recording violations, the stated fine is VND 5,000,000–6,000,000 for individuals and VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for transport businesses or transport-support-service organizations. [Data: Entities (3569)]

The organization-level range for failure to issue driver identification cards is VND 6,000,000–8,000,000. Thus, the camera provision has the higher stated organizational fine range among the two categories represented here. [Data: Entities (1983, 3569)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish potential regulatory exposure, not actual noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe violations, applicable fine ranges, and the possibility that transport support service organizations may incur those fines. They do not identify a named organization that committed either violation, nor do they provide enforcement decisions or compliance findings. [Data: Entities (1983, 3569, 4494); Relationships (6940, 9443)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Support Businesses and Compliance Violations
v.tom_tat: This community links road-transport support service businesses with two compliance issues: journey-monitoring device violations and the use of untrained drivers or onboard staff. The data describes organizational fines of 10,000,000–12,000,000 VND for specified device-related violations and links the untrained-staff violation to Article 26, Clause 4 fine ranges of 3,000,000–4,000,000 VND for individuals and 6,000,000–8,000,000 VND for organizations. The records describe regulatory requirements and penalties, but do not identify a particular business, an actual violation, or an enforcement outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory and transport-safety significance because it concerns compliance violations and monetary penalties, while the data provides no evidence of a specific incident or affected business.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Support businesses are linked to both compliance issues
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road transport support service businesses are the central organizational entity in the listed relationships. They are linked to journey-monitoring device violations and to the use of untrained drivers or onboard staff, placing both issues within the community’s compliance scope. [Data: Entities (4493, 4484, 5343); Relationships (10265, 10268)]

The records describe categories of businesses and violations rather than naming a business alleged to have committed either violation. [Data: Entities (4493, 4484, 5343); Relationships (10265, 10268)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Journey-monitoring device violations carry specified fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The device-related violation covers commercial road-transport vehicles used without a required journey-monitoring device, with an inactive or non-compliant device, or with falsified device data. The stated fine range is 5,000,000–6,000,000 VND for individuals and 10,000,000–12,000,000 VND for organizations. [Data: Entities (4484)]

The records specifically connect road transport support service businesses to organizational fines for this violation. [Data: Entities (4493); Relationships (10265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Untrained drivers or onboard staff are identified as a separate violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed violation concerns using drivers or onboard service staff in passenger transport by automobile without required training or guidance in passenger-transport operations and traffic safety, where that training is required. [Data: Entities (5343)]

Road transport support service businesses are associated with this violation in the relationship data. The records do not identify a specific business or establish that any particular staff member lacked training. [Data: Relationships (10268)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26, Clause 4 fine ranges are tied to the untrained-staff violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity states ranges of 3,000,000–4,000,000 VND for individuals and 6,000,000–8,000,000 VND for organizations committing the listed violations. [Data: Entities (2275)]

The relationship data connects those Article 26, Clause 4 fines to the use-of-untrained-drivers-and-onboard-staff violation. These ranges are distinct from the higher device-related ranges specified for journey-monitoring device violations. [Data: Relationships (7343); Entities (2275, 4484)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes potential obligations and penalties, not an enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records define violation categories, describe applicable fine ranges, and connect those categories to road transport support service businesses. They do not provide the name of an investigated organization, evidence that a violation occurred, or details of a penalty imposed in a particular case. [Data: Entities (4484, 4493, 5343, 2275); Relationships (10265, 10268, 7343)]

v.tieu_de: Periodic Driver Health Examination Requirements and Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the road-transport violation of failing to arrange periodic health examinations for drivers or ensuring that they cover required content. The violation is linked to the required examinations and to fines of VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for individuals and VND 20,000,000–24,000,000 for transport businesses or transport-support service organizations. The records describe a regulatory requirement and its penalties, not a specific violation, responsible party, or enforcement action.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the regulatory and financial significance of the stated penalties, while the records identify no specific violator, incident, or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The central issue is failure to arrange complete periodic driver examinations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is defined as either not organizing periodic health examinations for drivers or arranging examinations that do not cover all required content. The relationship record connects this violation directly to the examination requirement. [Data: Entities (2007); Relationships (6978)]

The supplied records establish a regulatory compliance issue, but do not identify a particular driver, business, or case in which the requirement was breached. [Data: Entities (2007, 3691); Relationships (6978)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Periodic examinations are the underlying compliance obligation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The examinations must be organized regularly for drivers and must cover all content required by regulations. This makes both their periodic organization and their completeness relevant to compliance. [Data: Entities (3691); Relationships (6978)]

No examination schedule, list of required medical tests, or implementation details are provided, so the records do not support conclusions about how the obligation is administered in practice. [Data: Entities (3691)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed fines vary by liable party type
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the specified failure to arrange complete periodic driver examinations, the stated fine is VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for individuals and VND 20,000,000–24,000,000 for transport businesses or transport-support service organizations. The relationship record associates these amounts with the examination violation. [Data: Entities (2007); Relationships (6977)]

These are described as penalty ranges; the records do not indicate that any fine was imposed or specify how a particular case would be assessed within the range. [Data: Entities (2007, 2270); Relationships (6977)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine record also mentions a separate violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fines entity includes a VND 1,000,000–2,000,000 penalty for failing to guide preschool children or students to sit in designated positions in a vehicle. Its description expressly presents this as a different violation context from the driver-examination penalties. [Data: Entities (2270)]

That separate amount should not be treated as a penalty for failure to organize driver health examinations; the relationship linking the fines to the community concerns the specified examination failure and its associated amounts. [Data: Entities (2270, 2007); Relationships (6977)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules and penalties, not a documented enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe the violation category, the examination obligation, and applicable fine ranges. They do not name a regulated organization or individual, report an inspection, or establish that a violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2007, 3691, 2270); Relationships (6977, 6978)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is supported as a compliance and penalty framework, but its real-world prevalence, enforcement history, and effects cannot be determined from the supplied records. [Data: Entities (2007, 3691, 2270); Relationships (6977, 6978)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger Guidance Violation and 100,000–200,000 đồng Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a traffic-safety violation involving a passenger-vehicle driver who fails to guide passengers into positions permitted inside the vehicle. The violation is linked to a stated fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records describe a regulatory category and its penalty, but do not establish that a particular driver committed the violation or provide further compliance or enforcement information.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a narrowly defined passenger-safety violation with a stated, limited fine and provide no evidence of a specific incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a passenger-positioning violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity describes a traffic-safety violation in which an operator does not instruct passengers to sit, stand, or lie in positions permitted inside the vehicle. The record presents this as a defined violation category, not as evidence that a particular event occurred. [Data: Entities (1977)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is attributed to the passenger-vehicle driver
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship data identifies the passenger-vehicle operator as the person who commits this violation by failing to guide passengers. The driver entity is described as operating a passenger car or similar vehicle, while the available information does not identify any individual driver. [Data: Entities (3587); Relationships (6934)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation is linked to a fine within the stated range of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records do not specify how the fine is determined within that range or provide additional sanctions. [Data: Entities (2138); Relationships (6933)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a compact, direct structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records connect the violation category to two elements: the responsible driver role and the associated fine. This defines the community's structure as a regulatory violation, a type of responsible operator, and a financial penalty, without indicating additional organizations, incidents, or affected parties. [Data: Entities (1977, 3587, 2138); Relationships (6934, 6933)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish a specific compliance case
phat_hien.giai_thich: The provided information describes what the violation consists of and the fine associated with it. It does not identify a driver, vehicle, enforcement action, or instance of noncompliance, so no conclusion about an actual violation or an individual’s compliance status is supported. [Data: Entities (1977, 3587, 2138); Relationships (6934, 6933)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Inspection Facility and Certification
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Inspection Facility, a public-service organization responsible for technical safety and environmental inspections and for certification results. Its inspectors conduct inspections and the facility issues certificates; the network also connects modified-vehicle certification with a requirement to replace the vehicle registration certificate by the next inspection. The provided records describe specified grounds for refusing an inspection and possible fines for listed violations, but do not establish that any violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2689, 3052, 5473, 2690, 4861); Relationships (7984, 7989, 7987, 7981, 7986)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it conducts vehicle inspections and certifications, while the records describe legal responsibilities and penalties but no specific violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Inspection Facility is the network’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Inspection Facility is described as a public-service organization that inspects motor vehicles and specialized motor vehicles for technical safety and environmental protection, and certifies modified vehicles. It is the hub of the listed relationships, linking inspection work, inspectors, certification, registration replacement, and specified refusal grounds. [Data: Entities (2689); Relationships (7984, 7989, 7987, 7981, 7986)]

The facility is responsible for inspection and certification results. The description also states that it may refuse an inspection only in circumstances specified by law. These records indicate defined regulatory responsibilities, not evidence of misconduct. [Data: Entities (2689); Relationships (7984, 7987)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection and certification support vehicle safety oversight
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Technical safety and environmental inspection is the process applied to motor vehicles and specialized motor vehicles. The facility performs these inspections and is responsible for their results, making this function a core part of the community’s public-service role. [Data: Entities (4861, 2689); Relationships (7987)]

The facility also certifies the technical safety and environmental protection of modified vehicles, and is responsible for those certification results. The records establish the scope of these activities but provide no measures of inspection volume, effectiveness, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (3052, 2689); Relationships (7984)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspectors conduct examinations and the facility issues certificates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility’s inspectors carry out vehicle inspections, while the facility issues the resulting inspection certificates. This establishes a division of functions between the individual inspectors performing the work and the facility issuing certificates and bearing responsibility for results. [Data: Entities (2690, 2689); Relationships (7981)]

The provided information does not identify individual inspectors or describe staffing, qualifications, or operational capacity, so those aspects cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (2690)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Modification certification triggers a registration replacement requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After a vehicle receives a modification certificate, its registration certificate must be replaced by the next inspection. This connects modified-vehicle certification to a subsequent registration-related obligation. [Data: Entities (3052, 5473); Relationships (8977)]

Failure to replace the registration certificate after modification certification is listed as a ground on which the Inspection Facility may refuse an inspection. The records state this as a rule; they do not indicate that a particular vehicle or owner failed to comply. [Data: Entities (5473, 2689); Relationships (7989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records specify limited grounds for refusing an inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A request from an authority conducting legal proceedings is identified as a ground on which the Inspection Facility may refuse an inspection. The procedural authority is described as an authority conducting legal proceedings, without further details about any specific proceeding or request. [Data: Entities (3881, 2689); Relationships (7986)]

Failure to replace a registration certificate following modification certification is another stated refusal ground. The facility’s description says refusals may occur only in circumstances specified by law; the supplied records do not establish any actual refusal. [Data: Entities (2689, 5473); Relationships (7989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The facility has stated legal responsibilities and potential financial penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Inspection Facility is described as subject to responsibilities set out in Article 43. Its description further states that a facility committing a listed violation under Article 40 may be fined between 10,000,000 and 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (2689)]

This information indicates a formal compliance framework relevant to the facility’s role. The records do not identify a violation, fine, enforcement action, or adverse compliance finding involving this community. [Data: Entities (2689)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Article 14: Vehicle-Condition Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its treatment of vehicle-condition violations by drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles. The described framework links violations to penalties, driving-license point deductions, and additional remedial measures; the entity description also notes fines of 400,000 to 600,000 VND for certain violations. The records describe legal provisions and potential consequences, but provide no evidence about actual compliance, enforcement frequency, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (1285, 1545, 3620, 4112, 5514); Relationships (5614, 5615, 5616, 9492)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes regulatory consequences for a defined group of road users, while the records provide no evidence of the scale of violations or real-world effects.
