phat_hien.tom_tat: A critical question is an independent failure condition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The test includes one critical question, and an incorrect answer to it results in failure, even if the overall score might otherwise meet the 32-point threshold. [Data: Entities (688)]

The data does not specify the subject of that question or explain how it is distinguished from the other questions. [Data: Entities (688)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information is specific but limited in scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records provide concrete details about the test’s duration, question count, scoring, pass threshold, and critical-question rule, as well as its required status for a C1 licence holder. [Data: Entities (688, 689); Relationships (2941)]

They do not provide evidence about examination outcomes, enforcement, broader legal compliance, or any organization’s reputation or technical capabilities; conclusions on those matters are therefore unsupported by this dataset. [Data: Entities (688, 689); Relationships (2941)]

v.tieu_de: Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and Vietnam Road-Traffic Testing
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, issued by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security to govern road-traffic legal-knowledge examinations, including tests for drivers whose licence points have been fully deducted. The Ministry sets the regulatory framework and manages specialized transport and driver-related databases; provincial and municipal police traffic divisions conduct examinations within its system. The circular also specifies testing procedures, administrative responsibilities, and implementation duties. Its significance lies in its connection of road-safety enforcement, driver licensing, local police administration, and government data management. [Data: Entities (835, 3022, 3992, 4380); Relationships (3282, 3292, 8899, 6078)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and administrative importance because it links driver testing and licensing rules with nationwide police implementation and management of extensive transport-related databases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The circular establishes the community’s regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is the central entity, issued by Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security. It sets rules for the road-traffic legal-knowledge examination, including registration, organization, retesting, assessment requirements, and responsibilities of authorities conducting examinations. [Data: Entities (835, 3022, 4380); Relationships (3282, 3292)]

The examination is specifically required for drivers whose driving-licence points have all been deducted. This places the circular at the intersection of road-safety regulation and a defined driver-restoration process. [Data: Entities (835, 4380); Relationships (3292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry combines rulemaking with operational data responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is identified as the circular’s issuing authority and is responsible under Article 10 for building and managing specialized databases. The listed subject areas include vehicle registration, traffic violations, road accidents, vehicle journeys and driver images, drivers’ operating time, vehicle inspections, driver testing and licensing, and legal-knowledge training certificates. [Data: Entities (3022); Relationships (3282, 6078, 8897, 8905)]

These responsibilities make the Ministry a central administrative and information-management actor in the community. The source establishes the scope of the databases but does not describe their technical safeguards, access controls, or actual use. [Data: Entities (3022); Relationships (6078, 8897, 8905)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial and municipal police divisions support local examination delivery
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and municipal police traffic police divisions are identified as competent authorities for testing knowledge of road-traffic laws. They are part of the Ministry’s police system, linking the national framework to local examination administration. [Data: Entities (3992, 3022); Relationships (8899)]

The circular assigns responsibilities to directors of provincial and centrally governed municipal police, while also setting out requirements for competent authorities conducting examinations. This creates a distributed implementation structure under central regulation. [Data: Entities (835, 3992); Relationships (3282, 3292, 8899)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The circular defines concrete test conditions and passing standards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 addresses assessment content and method, duration, question structure, results, and passing requirements. For the class C legal-knowledge theory test, the stated format is 40 multiple-choice questions in 24 minutes, with a passing score of at least 36, subject to a disqualifying question that must not be answered incorrectly. [Data: Entities (835, 2890); Relationships (3279)]

The circular also sets requirements for examination facilities and equipment under Article 5. These provisions give the testing system operational standards in addition to its administrative framework. [Data: Entities (835); Relationships (3279)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Software maintenance and public study materials are assigned responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 11 assigns the Traffic Police Department’s director responsibility for researching, developing, administering, maintaining, and upgrading software used for the tests, and for reporting this work to Ministry leadership. This indicates that the examination process relies on centrally overseen software, although the source does not specify its architecture or security controls. [Data: Entities (835)]

The circular also requires competent examination authorities to publicly post study materials on the electronic information portal under their management. This establishes a specified channel for making preparation materials available to candidates. [Data: Entities (835)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizations concerned by the circular have implementation and reporting roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The circular assigns implementation responsibilities to organizations concerned by its provisions and allows them to report difficulties or obstacles encountered during implementation. This provides a formal route for raising implementation issues, though the source does not identify particular organizations beyond the general category. [Data: Entities (4106, 835); Relationships (3288)]

The available description also notes that organizations affected by traffic congestion coordinate with the road management agency to identify its causes. This is a related coordination function in the supplied material, but no specific organization or congestion incident is identified. [Data: Entities (4106)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules sit within an evolving regulatory timeline
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA states that point (a) of Article 6, clause 1 was amended and supplemented by Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. The supplied record identifies March 1, 2025, as the effective date of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. [Data: Entities (835, 1731); Relationships (6612)]

The same description says that Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA contains a transitional rule keeping specified testing provisions in effect through June 30, 2027. This indicates that the examination framework is subject to subsequent amendments and transition arrangements; the provided records do not detail the full content of those later instruments. [Data: Entities (835)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Law Knowledge Examination and Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the road traffic law knowledge examination and the competent examination authority that organizes it. Applicants register, select an authority and examination date, and receive schedule information; registered examinees sit the examination and may be notified if its time or location changes. The described process also covers dossier handling, retests, and retention of examination records and surveillance images. The source describes provisions associated with Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, but does not establish whether implementation has been independently assessed. [Data: Entities (4365, 1047, 4065, 4374); Relationships (3771, 9854, 3770)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it links an examination, its administering authority, applicants, and supporting administrative and recordkeeping processes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination is the community’s organizing purpose
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central activity is an examination testing participants’ knowledge of laws governing road traffic order and safety. The provided description says registration and organization are addressed in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, including provisions referenced in Articles 7 and 8. [Data: Entities (4365, 4374)]

Registration, schedule notices, and examinee participation all connect back to this examination, making it the community’s principal operational focus. [Data: Relationships (6787, 9229, 9854, 9858)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The competent authority has a broad administrative role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent examination authority organizes and conducts the examination, handles applicants’ dossiers, announces schedules, and may address retest requests. Applicants select the authority when registering, and for in-person submissions it assigns a staff member to review the dossier and issue an appointment with the examination time and location. [Data: Entities (1047); Relationships (3771, 3772, 3766)]

This makes the authority the main operational intermediary between the examination process and applicants. The supplied information describes its responsibilities but does not independently assess how effectively or consistently they are performed. [Data: Relationships (3771, 3772)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration links applicants to examination arrangements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Applicants submit a dossier in advance, select an examination date and competent authority, and provide contact details in their application. The records describe registration as a process for participation in the road traffic law knowledge examination. [Data: Entities (1851, 1860, 4064, 4065); Relationships (6787, 9853, 3766)]

For in-person dossier submissions, the authority reviews the materials and provides an appointment specifying the time and location. The available information also refers to an online application option, but does not detail the systems or technical controls involved. [Data: Entities (1047); Relationships (3766)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Schedule announcements and change notices support examinees
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority publicly announces the expected examination time and location for the following month. If either changes, it must notify people who registered earlier using contact details supplied in their applications, including by email or text message. [Data: Entities (1047, 1852, 3273, 4065); Relationships (3770, 3765, 6788, 9229)]

These notices connect schedule management to examinee communication. The records specify the notification channels and responsibility but do not provide information about delivery rates or the frequency of schedule changes. [Data: Entities (1852); Relationships (3770, 3765, 6788)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registered examinees are the direct participants
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Registered examinees are the people who have signed up and sit the examination; their applications include contact information used for schedule notices. [Data: Entities (4065); Relationships (9854, 3770)]

A participant who does not pass may register for a retest, either with the authority that administered the earlier examination or with another competent authority. This provides a defined route for a subsequent attempt, although the supplied records do not state pass rates or retest outcomes. [Data: Entities (4365, 1047); Relationships (3771)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process includes substantial records and surveillance retention
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent authority retains a copy of the examination record and must preserve examination-room surveillance-camera images for at least two years. It must also retain registration records and examination minutes, in paper and electronic form, for at least five years. [Data: Entities (1047); Relationships (3771)]

These requirements indicate that the process relies on both physical and electronic records, as well as surveillance imagery. The provided information describes retention duties but does not establish the security, access, or deletion practices used in implementation. [Data: Entities (1047)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes procedures, not an independent compliance or reputation assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records outline examination administration and identify Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and referenced articles as part of the process description. They do not provide audit results, enforcement actions, performance measures, or allegations concerning the authority or other participants. Accordingly, the information supports a description of stated responsibilities, but not a conclusion about actual compliance or reputation. [Data: Entities (4365, 1047)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Examination and Interpreter Access
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Examination and the people and procedures associated with it. Examinees, including foreign nationals and ethnic-minority participants, may use interpreters who assist with the examination and sign or fingerprint the examination record with the examinee. Registration is linked to a requirement for a valid health certificate from a competent medical facility. The records describe examination and access procedures, but do not identify a particular testing authority or medical facility, or provide evidence of misconduct or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (2749, 4376, 1865, 1053, 1850); Relationships (6804, 6806, 3820, 3819)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it connects a road-safety legal examination with registration and language-access procedures, while the records establish no specific adverse conduct or elevated threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination is the community's central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Examination assesses knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety, and its arrangements include registration and administration. Examinees participate in the examination and sign the examination record when it ends. [Data: Entities (4376, 1865); Relationships (6806)]

The examination is connected to several participant types, interpreter arrangements, and a health-certificate requirement for registration. This makes it the central procedural link in the records, although no specific examination date, location, or administering authority is named. [Data: Relationships (6806, 6772, 7412, 6785, 3820)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Interpreters support access for participants needing language assistance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An interpreter may be hired by the competent testing authority or by the test taker to provide language assistance during the examination. The described assistance includes accurately and completely translating questions and explaining or guiding the participant through the procedure. [Data: Entities (2749)]

The interpreter and examinee sign or fingerprint the examination record together. The records establish this as a procedural safeguard and access mechanism; they do not assess interpreter qualifications, translation quality in practice, or the effectiveness of the assistance. [Data: Relationships (6804)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign and ethnic-minority examinees are explicitly included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign nationals and ethnic-minority members are identified as possible examinees in the road traffic legal knowledge examination. Each group may have an interpreter, with the examinee and interpreter signing or fingerprinting the examination record when interpretation is used. [Data: Entities (2311, 1841); Relationships (7411, 6771, 7412, 6772)]

The records also specifically describe foreign participants and ethnic-minority participants unable to read or write Vietnamese as using interpreters hired by the competent testing authority. These descriptions indicate a defined language-access process, but provide no counts or outcomes for participants. [Data: Entities (2337, 1842); Relationships (7511, 6773)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Interpreter arrangements vary by participant description
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general interpreter description allows the interpreter to be hired either by the competent testing authority or by the test taker. In contrast, the entries for foreign test participants and ethnic-minority participants unable to read or write Vietnamese specify an interpreter hired by the competent testing authority. [Data: Entities (2749, 2337, 1842); Relationships (7511, 6773)]

These records describe more than one hiring arrangement, but do not explain how the arrangements are selected or whether they apply under different circumstances. No conclusion about inconsistent implementation can be drawn from the information provided.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration requires a valid health certificate
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An exam registrant must submit a valid health certificate issued by a competent medical facility. The facility is described as authorized to issue a valid certificate in paper or electronic form, and no specific facility is named. [Data: Entities (1053, 1850); Relationships (3819)]

The health-certificate requirement is linked both to registration and to the examination process. The records do not specify the medical criteria, document-verification method, or any actual registrant's health status. [Data: Relationships (3819, 3820)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is procedural and does not establish compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information describes roles and requirements: the examination assesses road-traffic legal knowledge, interpreters may assist certain participants, and registrants submit health certificates. It does not provide inspection findings, examination results, complaints, enforcement actions, or other evidence of whether these procedures were followed in practice. [Data: Entities (4376, 2749, 1053, 1850); Relationships (6804, 3820, 3819)]

Accordingly, the records support identifying the community's relevant process and access provisions, but not a conclusion about legal compliance, operational effectiveness, or reputational standing.

v.tieu_de: Test Participants and Testing Location
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of test participants and the testing location where they take a road traffic law knowledge test. Participants use connected computers to complete the test and are expected to follow examiner instructions and the location’s rules. The data describes an operational relationship but provides no specific information about legal compliance outcomes, technical systems, reputation, or adverse claims.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited documented impact, being confined to a test-taking activity and its location, with no evidence of broader effects or risks.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Participants are the principal actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The participants are described as people who take the road traffic law knowledge test at the testing location. Their role is to log in to the test software and complete the test under the examiner’s instructions. [Data: Entities (4902)]

The available information does not identify individual participants or provide details about their number, backgrounds, or test results. [Data: Entities (4902)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The testing location provides the setting
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The testing location is described as the place where the test is organized and where participants must follow the testing rules. The relationship record connects the participants’ test-taking activity to this location. [Data: Entities (4913); Relationships (10508)]

No address, operator, or other identifying details for the location are supplied, so its wider role cannot be assessed from this data. [Data: Entities (4913)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship is centered on test-taking and rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The recorded relationship states that participants take the test at the testing location and must comply with its rules. This establishes a straightforward operational link between the two entities. [Data: Relationships (10508)]

The data does not describe specific rule requirements or whether any participant has complied with or breached them. [Data: Entities (4902, 4913); Relationships (10508)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Connected computers and test software are mentioned
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Participants are described as using connected computers at the testing location, logging in to test software, and completing the knowledge test. These details indicate that computer-based testing is part of the described process. [Data: Entities (4902)]

No information is provided about the software’s provider, security, network design, or technical capabilities beyond its use for the test. [Data: Entities (4902)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to an administrative testing context
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe participants, a testing location, and the requirement to follow instructions and rules. They do not include claims or evidence of misconduct, disputes, or other adverse incidents. [Data: Entities (4902, 4913); Relationships (10508)]

There is also no supplied information about the entities’ reputation, regulatory standing, or the consequences of the test. The assessment is therefore limited to the documented test-taking arrangement. [Data: Entities (4902, 4913); Relationships (10508)]

v.tieu_de: Ministry of Public Security Agencies and Unit Heads
v.tom_tat: This community describes an implementation structure within Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security: ministry-level agencies have subordinate units, and unit heads lead those units and are assigned responsibility for implementing a circular. The entity descriptions mention Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA for subordinate units and Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA for heads of units, but the records do not establish whether these references concern the same implementation process. The information indicates administrative responsibility, not whether the circulars have been implemented or whether the entities are legally compliant.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it links ministry-level agencies, subordinate units, and responsible officials, while the records provide no evidence of implementation outcomes or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A hierarchical agency-to-unit structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe ministry-level agencies as the parent organizations of units under the Ministry’s agencies. This establishes the organizational structure through which the circular-related responsibilities are situated. [Data: Entities (3031, 5239); Relationships (8949)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unit heads are assigned implementation responsibility
phat_hien.giai_thich: The heads of units under the ministry’s agencies are described as leading those units and being responsible for implementing the circular. This connects the administrative hierarchy to named responsibility at the unit level, but does not show whether implementation has occurred. [Data: Entities (5239, 2477); Relationships (7715)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ministry-level agencies are part of the management chain
phat_hien.giai_thich: A separate relationship states that heads of units lead units that are part of ministry-level agencies. Together with the stated subordination of units to those agencies, this places unit leadership within the ministry-level agency structure. The records do not identify particular agencies or individual officials. [Data: Entities (3031, 2476); Relationships (8949, 7714)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records cite two different circulars
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of ministry-level agencies associates their subordinate units with Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, while the description of heads of units associates their responsibility with Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. The available records do not explain how these two references relate to each other, so they should not be treated as a single instrument or process without further evidence. [Data: Entities (3031, 2476)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and operational outcomes are not established
phat_hien.giai_thich: The descriptions identify organizational roles and assigned responsibilities, but provide no evidence that the circulars have been implemented, that implementation has been audited, or that any entity has complied or failed to comply. The community therefore supports an assessment of administrative structure, but not a conclusion about legal compliance or operational effectiveness. [Data: Entities (5239, 3031, 2476, 2477); Relationships (8949, 7715, 7714)]

v.tieu_de: Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA and the Amended Circular 65 Provision
v.tom_tat: This small regulatory community links Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA to point a, clause 1, Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, which the former provision amended and supplemented. The description of Article 6 of Circular 13 also says it is cited in the transitional rules of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA. The available data identifies these legal references but does not describe their substantive requirements or implementation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has some regulatory significance because it documents an amendment and a transitional-rule citation, but the supplied data does not establish the provisions’ scope or practical effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is the central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is the source entity in the only recorded relationship and has the higher listed degree of the two entities. Its description also connects it to the transitional rules of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA. These details make it the main point of connection in this community. [Data: Entities (497); Relationships (2327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific provision of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA was amended
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship states that Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA amended and supplemented point a, clause 1, Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The data identifies the target provision precisely but does not specify what wording or requirements were changed. [Data: Entities (3753); Relationships (2327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is a narrow, provision-level regulatory linkage
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe two legal provisions and one direct amendment relationship between them. This supports characterizing the community as a focused connection between circular provisions, rather than a broader network of agencies, regulated parties, or enforcement activity. [Data: Entities (497, 3753); Relationships (2327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A transitional-rule citation connects the provision to Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description for Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA says it is cited in the transitional rules of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, including in clause 3 of Article 6 of that circular. Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is mentioned in the description but is not separately listed as an entity or connected by a relationship in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (497)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Practical compliance implications cannot be determined from these records
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data establishes an amendment and a transitional-rule citation, but provides no text of the provisions, information about affected parties, or evidence of compliance outcomes. Accordingly, it supports identifying regulatory relevance but not assessing specific obligations, violations, or operational impact. [Data: Entities (497, 3753); Relationships (2327)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test established under the framework described in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Its connected entities cover registration and eligible participants, competent authorities and officials, testing rooms and locations, and funding. The described process includes identity verification, computer-based testing, secure data handling and camera recording, while providing for interpreters for certain participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese. The test is also connected to road-safety administration through eligibility for drivers whose licence points have all been deducted and funding from specified traffic-violation fines.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high public importance because it links road-safety regulation, licence-related testing, administrative processes, secure testing infrastructure, and public funding.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulated test is the community’s central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity is an examination of knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. The provided description places its registration and organization under Article 7 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, including a registration request using Form No. 01 in the circular’s appendix. This establishes a formal regulatory context, but the data describes the framework rather than independently verifying how it is implemented in practice. [Data: Entities (4367, 3425, 4072); Relationships (9312, 9859)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The test serves a specified licence-points-related group
phat_hien.giai_thich: Drivers whose licence points have all been deducted are identified as eligible to take the test. The relationship records this eligibility as a direct link to the examination, making the test relevant to a defined group of drivers within the road-safety system. The supplied data does not specify the outcome of the test or any subsequent licensing decision. [Data: Entities (1552, 4367); Relationships (6272)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administration involves an authority, officials, and examiners
phat_hien.giai_thich: The competent authority conducts the test and is responsible for ensuring the facilities and equipment used for it are available. Test officials use computers and printers for their duties, while examiners instruct participants, who are required to follow those instructions. These roles indicate an organized administrative process, though the records do not identify particular offices or individuals. [Data: Entities (1048, 4900, 1866); Relationships (3774, 10144, 6807)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Computer-based testing has specified infrastructure and security measures
phat_hien.giai_thich: The test is described as taking place on computers using designated, approved software, with secure data handling and logging. The testing room must have a secure camera-surveillance system that records and stores images; rooms are also described as equipped with computers, a printer, and other required facilities. These provisions show that the process relies on both technical infrastructure and monitoring, without establishing how well those controls operate in practice. [Data: Entities (4367, 4919); Relationships (10148)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Testing locations connect to a centralized departmental server
phat_hien.giai_thich: Testing locations are described as places where participants’ computers connect over the Ministry of Public Security WAN to a server hosted at the Traffic Police Department. This points to a networked testing arrangement with a designated central server location. The records do not provide further details about network capacity, system availability, or cybersecurity performance. [Data: Entities (4914); Relationships (10147)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Participant verification and interpreter arrangements are specified
phat_hien.giai_thich: Participants are to attend at the time and place notified by the competent authority and present an accepted identity document so their details can be checked against their application. Electronic identification information may be used for verification when available. The framework also provides for an interpreter hired by the competent testing authority for foreign participants and ethnic-minority participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese; the foreign-participant entity is specifically linked to the test. [Data: Entities (4367, 2336); Relationships (7510)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified traffic fines contribute to test funding
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community links administrative violations of road traffic order and safety rules to funding for the test. The entity description states that revenue from the resulting fines is one funding source, and the relationship specifies that this revenue is allocated to test organization after payment into the state budget. This documents a public-revenue connection but does not quantify the funding or its share of total costs. [Data: Entities (133, 4367); Relationships (446)]

v.tieu_de: Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA Implementation and Provincial Police
v.tom_tat: This community centers on implementation of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and the police organizations and officials assigned roles in carrying it out. Provincial and centrally governed city police are responsible through their directors, while police units and localities are identified as reporting difficulties or obstacles encountered during implementation. The information establishes administrative responsibilities and a feedback channel, but does not describe implementation outcomes, compliance status, technical capabilities, or reputational issues.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it links implementation responsibilities across provincial and centrally governed city police with a mechanism for reporting obstacles, although no outcomes or risks are documented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation of the circular is the community's organizing focus
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is the carrying out of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, for which designated officials, organizations, and individuals are responsible. The description also states that implementation difficulties may be reported for guidance, making both execution and issue reporting part of the stated process. [Data: Entities (2557)]

The implementation entity connects directly to provincial and centrally governed city police and to police units and localities, indicating that the described process involves multiple police organizational levels. These records establish assigned roles, but do not say whether implementation has been completed or how effective it has been. [Data: Relationships (7819, 7818)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial and centrally governed city police have an assigned implementation role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and centrally governed city police are described as police organizations whose directors are assigned responsibility for implementing the circular. This makes these organizations a key institutional component of the community. [Data: Entities (3948)]

The relationship record specifically links the circular's implementation to these police organizations through the responsibility of their directors. The available information describes an assignment of responsibility, not evidence of compliance or operational results. [Data: Relationships (7819)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police-unit and locality reporting provides a channel for implementation difficulties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Police units and localities are identified as responsible for reporting difficulties or obstacles encountered while implementing the circular. This establishes a feedback mechanism within the implementation process. [Data: Entities (3822)]

Their connection to implementation is explicitly described as reporting difficulties encountered during that work. The records do not identify specific obstacles, the frequency of reports, or any guidance subsequently issued. [Data: Relationships (7818), Entities (2557)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Directors connect the police organizations to implementation responsibility
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Directors of provincial and centrally governed city police are described as officials who lead those organizations and are responsible for implementing the circular. Their role links organizational leadership with the assigned implementation duty. [Data: Entities (1388)]

A separate relationship confirms that these directors lead the police organizations and are responsible for implementation. The data therefore supports a leadership and accountability structure, but does not provide details about individual directors or their actions. [Data: Relationships (5868, 7819)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence establishes responsibilities, not implementation performance or broader risk
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provided records describe the implementation assignment, the police organizations and officials involved, and the reporting of difficulties. They do not state whether any entity has complied or failed to comply, or provide outcomes from the implementation process. [Data: Entities (2557, 3822, 3948, 1388); Relationships (7819, 7818, 5868)]

The records also contain no specific information about technical capabilities, public reputation, or adverse incidents. Accordingly, those dimensions cannot be assessed from the available evidence; the supported conclusion is limited to the community's administrative structure and stated duties. [Data: Entities (2557, 3822, 3948, 1388)]

v.tieu_de: Competent Testing Authority and Road-Traffic Knowledge Examination
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Competent Testing Authority, which organizes and conducts examinations on road-traffic order and safety legal knowledge. Applicants submit complete and valid applications; the authority then schedules registered examinees, provides advance notice of the time and location, and promptly communicates changes. Candidates who fail may apply to retake the examination. The supplied information describes procedural duties and operational resources, but does not establish whether the authority has complied with those duties in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it governs access to a formal road-traffic legal-knowledge examination through a centralized process, while the data shows no specific incident or demonstrated noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority is the community’s operational center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Competent Testing Authority is authorized to organize and conduct the road-traffic legal-knowledge examination and the related road traffic order and safety test. It also receives applications and is connected to the examination’s scheduling and change-notification processes, making it the principal administrative actor in the community. [Data: Entities (1066); Relationships (3873, 3872, 3875, 3860, 3859)]

The records describe the authority’s mandate and duties; they do not identify a specific authority or provide evidence that it has performed those duties correctly or incorrectly.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Valid applications trigger the advance-notice process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After receipt of a complete and valid application, the authority notifies registered candidates of the examination’s time and location at least two working days in advance. The application receipt is therefore the stated trigger for the notice and its lead-time requirement. [Data: Entities (1863, 4036, 1066); Relationships (3864, 6802, 3860)]

The authority may notify registered applicants by email or text message, according to the relationship description. The supplied records specify the process but do not provide examples or delivery records showing whether individual notices were sent on time. [Data: Relationships (3865)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Changes to examination arrangements require prompt communication
phat_hien.giai_thich:
If a previously announced examination time or location changes, the authority must promptly notify registered examinees and provide the updated details. This change notice is distinct from the initial scheduling notice and is an important part of keeping candidates informed. [Data: Entities (1862, 1066); Relationships (3859)]

No specific schedule change or resulting impact on candidates is documented in the supplied data.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process includes applicants, registered candidates, and retakes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A test applicant may submit an application to a competent authority, and a registered applicant is the person scheduled to take the test. These records distinguish the application stage from the later scheduled-candidate stage. [Data: Entities (4899, 4063); Relationships (3875, 9862)]

Candidates who fail may register for a retake, either with the authority that organized the earlier examination or another competent authority. The data establishes the availability of this route, but does not specify retake limits or outcomes. [Data: Entities (692, 4539); Relationships (2949, 2950, 2951)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination registration dossier has a stated health-certificate requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of the road-traffic legal-knowledge examination states that its registration dossier must include a valid driver’s health certificate issued by a competent medical facility. This is a documented requirement associated with examination registration. [Data: Entities (4539)]

The records do not establish how the requirement is assessed in individual applications or whether any applicant has been denied or delayed because of it.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operational resources and examination-day checks are part of the authority’s duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority is described as needing access to facilities and equipment for examinations. On examination day, it checks candidates’ documents and compares identity information with their applications. These duties indicate that its role includes practical examination administration as well as scheduling. [Data: Entities (1066)]

When language assistance is needed, the authority may hire an interpreter for a participant, including a foreign participant who cannot read or write Vietnamese. The records describe this as an available accommodation, not as evidence that a particular interpreter was engaged or that a particular candidate required assistance. [Data: Entities (1066)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe requirements, not verified compliance or technical performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The information sets out administrative duties, including publicly posting schedules and locations on an electronic information portal within the authority’s management scope, notifying candidates, and promptly communicating changes. These details support an assessment of the process design, but do not demonstrate that the portal is operational or that notices and other duties have been fulfilled in practice. [Data: Entities (1066); Relationships (3860, 3859)]

No violations, enforcement actions, security issues, or documented examination outcomes are included in the supplied records. Conclusions about actual legal compliance, system reliability, or adverse effects would therefore go beyond the available evidence.

v.tieu_de: Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA Driver-Test Transition Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA and its transitional provisions for legal-knowledge tests related to restoring driver’s-license points. Article 6 connects the continued application of testing requirements through June 30, 2027, with a specific continuing provision, Clause 5. Its general computer-based testing method has an exception in Clause 8 of Article 7, which Article 2 amends. The records describe a focused set of regulatory provisions; they do not establish enforcement outcomes or wider effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the practical importance of a defined transition in driver’s-license testing rules, while the records provide no evidence of broader impacts or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 is the community’s central transitional provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 is titled “Effectiveness and transitional provisions,” and Clause 3 specifies which testing rules remain applicable during the transition and for how long. The article is connected to the testing requirements and to provisions concerning the testing method and transition period. [Data: Entities (496); Relationships (2323, 2322, 2324)]

The supplied information identifies the transition’s subject as legal-knowledge tests for restoring driver’s-license points. It does not specify how the rules are enforced or describe any resulting compliance problems. [Data: Entities (496)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified testing requirements continue through June 30, 2027
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 6 establishes that the specified testing requirements continue to apply through June 30, 2027. The requirements cover test content, methods, timing, structure, and the results needed to pass. [Data: Entities (4918, 496); Relationships (2324)]

This date provides a defined endpoint for the stated continuation. The records do not identify what rules apply after that date, so no further conclusion about the post-transition regime is supported. [Data: Entities (496); Relationships (2324)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 5 is among the provisions continuing during the transition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 5 of Article 6 is identified as a provision included among the rules that continue to apply through June 30, 2027. It is explicitly linked to Article 6 as one of its clauses. [Data: Entities (964); Relationships (2322)]

The supplied records do not state the substantive content of Clause 5. Its inclusion in the continuing rules can therefore be noted, but its specific effect should not be inferred. [Data: Entities (964, 496); Relationships (2322, 2324)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Computer-based testing has a stated exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6’s general method calls for candidates to take the legal-knowledge test on a computer using testing software, but the general method does not apply in the exception set out in Clause 8 of Article 7. [Data: Entities (990); Relationships (2323)]

The records identify the exception but do not describe which candidates or circumstances qualify for it. Its practical scope cannot be determined from the supplied information. [Data: Entities (990); Relationships (2323)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 2 amends the referenced exception provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 2 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA amends Clause 8 of Article 7, the provision cited as an exception to the general testing method. This links the amendment provision to the testing-method exception addressed by Article 6. [Data: Entities (296, 990); Relationships (1060, 2323)]

The supplied records do not provide the text of the amendment or explain how it changes the exception. Accordingly, the direction or operational effect of the amendment is not established here. [Data: Entities (296, 990); Relationships (1060)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Safety Law Communication and Implementation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road traffic order and safety responsibilities. The state management agency leads and coordinates law communication and dissemination with relevant individuals and agencies, while those groups participate in the activity and have responsibilities for implementing the decree. The activity is identified as specified in Article 5 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. The data describes roles and coordination, but does not establish implementation outcomes or compliance levels. [Data: Entities (4102, 4756, 4098, 4356); Relationships (9886, 9885, 9879, 10138, 9878)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public-safety and legal implementation importance because it coordinates road traffic law communication and decree responsibilities, although the data provides no evidence of outcomes, noncompliance, or specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Relevant individuals have broad implementation and coordination responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Relevant individuals are described as people concerned by the circular and decree who are assigned responsibility for implementing them and may report difficulties or obstacles. They also work with state management agencies on communicating and disseminating road traffic laws and coordinate with road management agencies to identify causes of traffic congestion. [Data: Entities (4102)]

Their relationships with the state management agency and the law communication activity make them a prominent participant group in the community. The records describe assigned functions, not whether those functions have been carried out successfully. [Data: Relationships (9886, 9885)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The state management agency is the coordinating lead
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The state management agency for road traffic order and safety is described as the government body responsible for managing the subject and leading and coordinating legal communication and dissemination. [Data: Entities (4756)]

It coordinates with both relevant individuals and relevant agencies and organizations, and leads the communication and dissemination activity. This positions the agency as the community's central coordinating entity. [Data: Relationships (9886, 9879, 10138)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Relevant agencies and organizations participate in implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Relevant agencies and organizations are described as bodies concerned with road traffic order and safety and the decree. They coordinate with the state management agency on communicating and disseminating laws and are responsible for implementing the decree. [Data: Entities (4098)]

Their recorded links connect them both to the state management agency and to the communication activity, indicating an inter-organizational implementation structure. The data does not identify individual organizations or report their performance. [Data: Relationships (9879, 9878)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Law communication and dissemination is the shared activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road traffic law communication and dissemination is identified as the activity specified in Article 5 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (4356)]

Relevant individuals and agencies participate in this activity in coordination with the state management agency, which is described as leading and coordinating it. This establishes the activity as the principal point of connection among the community's entities. [Data: Relationships (9885, 9878, 10138)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal roles, but not results or compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information describes responsibilities, coordination relationships, and a legal reference for the communication activity. It does not provide evidence about whether the decree has been implemented, whether any entity complied or failed to comply, or what outcomes resulted. [Data: Entities (4102, 4756, 4098, 4356); Relationships (9886, 9879, 10138)]

Accordingly, the community's significance can be assessed in terms of its stated connection to road traffic safety governance, but the records do not support conclusions about effectiveness, technical capabilities, reputation, or specific safety impacts.

v.tieu_de: Circulars 105/2026 and 65/2024: Testing Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community concerns a transitional rule in Clause 3 of Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA and the test-related provisions of Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The newer clause links to three specific provisions of the earlier circular and states that their specified test content and requirements continue to apply through June 30, 2027. The records describe regulatory continuity for testing, but do not establish enforcement outcomes or compliance by any particular party.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it documents a defined period of continuity for test requirements, while the records show no broader operational or enforcement impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is the transitional link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community centers on Clause 3 of Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, which connects the newer circular to provisions in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. Its stated function is to preserve specified earlier test requirements through June 30, 2027.

This makes the clause the key reference point for understanding how the two circulars relate in this dataset. [Data: Entities (938); Relationships (3451, 3449, 3452)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The transition covers three specific provisions of Circular 65/2024
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The transitional clause is linked to Point A, Clause 2; Clause 3; and Point A, Clause 5 of Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The relationship descriptions state that the test requirements in each cited provision continue to apply through June 30, 2027.

The records therefore indicate a defined set of provisions rather than a general extension of every requirement in the earlier circular. [Data: Entities (3755, 939, 3757, 938); Relationships (3451, 3449, 3452)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The cited provisions sit within Article 6 of Circular 65/2024
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is described as covering test content, methods, timing, structure, and passing requirements. The relationships identify the cited points and clause as parts of that article.

This establishes the subject area of the provisions carried forward: test-related requirements. The supplied records do not give the detailed content of each individual test requirement. [Data: Entities (499, 3755, 939, 3757); Relationships (2334, 2332, 2335)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated continuation has a specific end date
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The transitional clause is described as keeping the specified test content and requirements in force through June 30, 2027. The same date appears in the relationship descriptions connecting it to the three cited provisions.

The records thus provide a clear endpoint for the continuation described here, but do not state what rules apply after that date. [Data: Entities (938); Relationships (3451, 3449, 3452)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The dataset supports regulatory continuity, not conclusions about compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available entities and relationships describe how a transitional clause refers to earlier test provisions and the period for which their requirements continue. They do not identify regulated parties, test results, enforcement actions, or instances of compliance or noncompliance.

Accordingly, the community is relevant for tracking the stated regulatory transition, but these records alone do not support conclusions about implementation or real-world outcomes. [Data: Entities (499, 938, 3755, 939, 3757); Relationships (3451, 3449, 3452, 2334, 2332)]

v.tieu_de: Clause 3 Violation and Six-Point License Deduction
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of a violation referenced in Clause 3 of Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and the stated consequence of deducting six points from the violator’s driver’s license. The relationship record connects the specified violation to that penalty. The data does not identify the conduct constituting the violation or provide further details about enforcement.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it describes a concrete driver’s-license penalty, while the underlying conduct and broader context are not provided.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The six-point deduction is the central consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s main entity is a penalty described as deducting six points from a person’s driver’s license. The record links this penalty to committing the violation specified in Clause 3. [Data: Entities (4657); Relationships (10430)]

The data establishes the stated consequence but does not describe other penalties or effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalty is tied to a specific legal reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The referenced conduct is identified as the violation specified in Clause 3 of Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The relationship record presents this violation as the trigger for the six-point deduction. [Data: Entities (5586); Relationships (10430)]

No further legal text or interpretation is supplied in the records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The underlying conduct is not specified in the available data
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation entity points to Clause 3 of Article 14 but does not state what actions constitute the violation. Accordingly, the records support identifying the legal reference and consequence, but not characterizing the conduct itself. [Data: Entities (5586); Relationships (10430)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a simple, directly connected structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied entities comprise the six-point deduction and the violation specified in Clause 3. A single relationship connects them by stating that committing the violation results in the deduction. [Data: Entities (4657, 5586); Relationships (10430)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records provide limited information about implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data describes the consequence as a penalty but does not provide information about how it is applied, who administers it, or any appeal or compliance process. These details therefore cannot be assessed from this community’s records. [Data: Entities (4657, 5586); Relationships (10430)]

v.tieu_de: Non-Compliant Container Transportation and Traffic Fines
v.tom_tat: This small community links the traffic violation of transporting a container that fails applicable technical regulations to the administrative fine prescribed for that violation. The container offense carries a stated fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The broader fine entity also describes different penalties for other violations, which should not be conflated with the container-transportation penalty.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited scope, but it concerns regulatory compliance and a substantial stated monetary penalty for non-compliant container transportation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a specific container-transportation offense
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The offense is carrying a container on a vehicle, including a semi-trailer, when it does not meet applicable technical regulations and standards. It is identified as a traffic violation under Article 21, Clause 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (3250)]

The available information characterizes this as a compliance issue involving vehicle and container standards; it does not describe additional conduct or consequences. [Data: Entities (3250)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine for the container offense is 8–12 million đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description gives a fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for carrying a container that fails applicable technical regulations and standards. [Data: Entities (3250)]

The relationship connects this specific offense to the traffic-fine entity and states that the fine is prescribed for the non-compliant container. [Data: Relationships (9208)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The two entities are linked by the prescribed penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community consists of the non-compliant container transportation offense and the broader traffic violation fine, joined by a relationship specifying that the fine applies to the container offense. [Data: Entities (3250, 5041); Relationships (9208)]

This forms a direct, narrow relationship between a defined violation and its penalty; the supplied data does not identify other connected entities or relationships.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine entity describes penalties for multiple, distinct violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general traffic-fine description includes a 14,000,000 to 16,000,000 đồng range for specified violations committed following a traffic accident, as well as a 400,000 to 600,000 đồng range for listed helmet-related violations. [Data: Entities (5041)]

Those amounts are stated to apply to different violations. They should therefore be distinguished from the 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 đồng penalty specified for non-compliant container transportation. [Data: Entities (3250, 5041); Relationships (9208)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The documented impact is primarily regulatory and financial
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a technical-compliance requirement for container transportation and a monetary penalty for violating it. They do not provide evidence about enforcement frequency, affected parties, accident outcomes, or broader operational effects. [Data: Entities (3250, 5041); Relationships (9208)]

Accordingly, the community's documented significance is limited to the stated offense and penalty; the available information does not establish wider impacts.

v.tieu_de: Overweight Vehicle Operation on Public Roads
v.tom_tat: This small community links the defined violation of operating an overweight vehicle to a public road with a permitted load limit. The described conduct involves exceeding that limit by more than 10% and up to 20%, and is subject to a fine unless a valid travel permit applies. The records define the conduct and its road context but do not identify a particular vehicle, operator, incident, or permit.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a limited, fine-based road-load violation and provide no specific incident or broader operational context.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on a road-load violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is operating an overweight vehicle, described as driving a vehicle whose total weight exceeds the applicable public-road load limit by more than 10% and up to 20%. [Data: Entities (3372)]

The connection to a public road establishes the setting for the violation; the records do not describe a specific occurrence. [Data: Entities (3998); Relationships (9286)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The public road provides the relevant limit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The public road is defined as a road on which vehicles operate and that has a permitted load limit. This limit is the benchmark used in the description of the overweight-vehicle conduct. [Data: Entities (3998), (3372)]

The relationship explicitly states that the violation concerns exceeding the permitted load limit of the road on which the vehicle is operated. [Data: Relationships (9286)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described excess is bounded
phat_hien.giai_thich: The specified range is more than 10% and up to 20% above the public road’s permitted load limit. The records do not describe other excess-weight ranges or associated conduct. [Data: Entities (3372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine is described, with a permit exception
phat_hien.giai_thich: The defined conduct is subject to a fine unless a valid travel permit applies. The records do not provide details about fine amounts, permit requirements, or whether a permit was held in any particular case. [Data: Entities (3372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific operator or incident is identified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied entities and relationship define the violation and its connection to a public road, but do not name a driver, vehicle, road, enforcement action, or actual incident. Accordingly, the records support describing the rule and context, not asserting that a particular party violated it. [Data: Entities (3372), (3998); Relationships (9286)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Tunnel Reversing and Turning Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns reversing or turning around inside a road tunnel, with Article 8, Clause 5 identified as the applicable provision for these maneuvers. The records connect the two individual violations to a combined violation description and state fines of 2,000,000–3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the combined offense; a separate entry describes an 800,000–1,000,000 đồng fine for motorcycles, mopeds, or similar vehicles that turn around in a tunnel. The evidence is limited to descriptions of traffic violations and penalties, with no information about specific incidents, enforcement outcomes, or other community actors. [Data: Entities (5171, 4208, 4212, 565); Relationships (9972, 9974, 2636, 2637)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns specified road-safety violations and financial penalties, but the records describe rules rather than a particular incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on two prohibited tunnel maneuvers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish turning around in a road tunnel from reversing in one, and present both as traffic violations. A combined violation entity groups these maneuvers together. [Data: Entities (5171, 4208, 4212); Relationships (9972, 9974)]

This structure indicates that the community is focused on a narrow set of driving behaviors rather than on a named organization, individual, or specific enforcement case. [Data: Entities (5171, 4208, 4212, 565)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 8, Clause 5 is the central legal reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 8, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is identified as the provision concerning the tunnel maneuvers. The relationships specifically connect that provision to reversing and turning around in a road tunnel. [Data: Entities (565); Relationships (2636, 2637)]

The combined violation description also cites Article 8, Clause 5 and states a fine for the described act. The records do not provide additional details about enforcement procedures or circumstances that could affect application of the provision. [Data: Entities (4212, 565)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records distinguish reversing from turning around
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Reversing in a road tunnel is described as moving a vehicle backward inside the tunnel, while turning around is a separate maneuver. The combined violation entity treats these as the two behaviors it covers. [Data: Entities (4208, 5171, 4212); Relationships (9972, 9974)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the descriptions: the records group the acts for a combined violation entry but also represent them individually. They do not establish that the two maneuvers are identical. [Data: Entities (4208, 5171, 4212); Relationships (9972, 9974)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalties include a general fine and a motorcycle-specific amount
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The combined violation entry states a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for a driver who commits the described act. Article 8, Clause 5 is also described as specifying that fine range for the stated traffic violations. [Data: Entities (4212, 565)]

Separately, the turning-around entry says that when the driver uses a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle, the violation is described under Article 7, Clause 4 and carries a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 đồng. The records provide this separate amount but do not explain how the provisions interact in any particular case. [Data: Entities (5171)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a focused regulatory assessment, not an incident-level conclusion
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe violations, legal references, and fine ranges, and link the individual maneuvers to the combined violation. They do not identify a driver, location, actual occurrence, enforcement action, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (5171, 4208, 4212, 565); Relationships (9972, 9974, 2636, 2637)]

Accordingly, the community’s documented significance is its connection to road-traffic rules and penalties. The available information does not support conclusions about compliance by particular people, technical capabilities, organizational reputation, or real-world incident frequency. [Data: Entities (5171, 4208, 4212, 565)]

v.tieu_de: Drivers and Road-Traffic Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on the DRIVER entity, which has the highest listed degree and connects to requirements and violations involving inspections, accident conduct, forced stops, child passenger safety, and commercial passenger transport. The information describes a broad set of legal and operational obligations, including possible temporary seizure of a vehicle and documents when required papers cannot be produced. It documents regulatory exposure and specified violations, but does not establish that any particular driver committed them. [Data: Entities (1442, 5368, 2012, 2045, 2034); Relationships (6000, 5955, 5958, 5957, 6002)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high impact importance because it links routine driving to multiple safety and compliance requirements, while the records do not show that any specific driver has violated them.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
DRIVER is described as a person operating a range of road vehicles and has a listed degree of 64, substantially higher than the other entities shown. Its connections span document inspections, accident-related duties, forced-stop precautions, child passenger rules, and passenger-transport business arrangements, making it the organizing entity for this regulatory community. [Data: Entities (1442, 5368, 2012, 2045, 2034); Relationships (6000, 5955, 5958, 5957, 6002)]

The entity description also sets out general qualifications and conduct requirements, including holding an applicable valid driving licence, obeying road-traffic rules, and complying with vehicle-specific safety rules. These are stated requirements, not evidence about the compliance record of an individual driver. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Document checks can lead to temporary vehicle and document retention
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver may be asked to present a driving licence, vehicle registration certificate, or other relevant documents during an inspection. The associated relationship states that inability to present required papers may lead to temporary seizure of the vehicle and related documents. [Data: Entities (5388, 5368, 1442); Relationships (6002, 6000)]

The DRIVER description adds that, in the described case, a penalty may be avoided by presenting the documents or qualifying electronic document information within the stated period. The provided records do not specify that this consequence has occurred in any particular case. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Accident duties include stopping and preserving the scene
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes two distinct accident-related violations: failure to stop immediately and failure to preserve the accident scene when the driver’s conduct is directly related to the accident. The relationships identify the driver as the person who commits these violations if the specified conduct occurs. [Data: Entities (2045, 2012, 1442); Relationships (5958, 5955)]

The DRIVER description also notes specified responsibilities when a traffic accident occurs and says provisions may require testing for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants. These descriptions indicate legal and safety relevance but do not establish that any driver failed to meet these duties or was tested. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Forced-stop precautions are a defined safety and compliance concern
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a violation involving failure to use hazard lights or place a required warning sign when a technical failure or force majeure requires stopping in specified locations. The stated fine is 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong, subject to the exception described in the entity record. [Data: Entities (2034); Relationships (5957)]

Separately, the DRIVER description says that in a road tunnel, when a failure or force majeure requires a stop, the driver must move to an emergency stopping position if possible; otherwise the driver must activate hazard lights, place a warning sign or light at a safe distance, and promptly report the situation. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Child passenger rules create specific driver responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify children under 10 years old and shorter than 1.35 meters as a group subject to specified seating and safety-device rules when transported in a car. The relationship connects those requirements to the driver, who transports the children and is subject to the rules. [Data: Entities (823, 1442); Relationships (3208)]

The DRIVER description states that drivers are responsible for the described seating violations, subject to stated exceptions. This establishes a compliance obligation; the records do not identify an actual violation or affected child. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commercial passenger transport involves electronic records and operator support
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The passenger transport business operator is described as providing equipment for accessing electronic contracts and passenger lists, and the relationship connects that equipment to the driver. The DRIVER description says drivers of contract-based passenger transport vehicles must comply with electronic-contract and passenger-list requirements. [Data: Entities (3566, 1442); Relationships (5980)]

This connection indicates an operational dependency between the driver and the transport business operator for accessing the specified materials. The provided records do not describe the technology used beyond access equipment or report any failure to comply. [Data: Entities (3566, 1442); Relationships (5980)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records describe regulatory exposure, not an adverse reputation finding
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships characterize legal duties, possible penalties, and defined traffic violations associated with drivers. They do not identify a specific driver, report an adjudicated case, or provide evidence of repeated or systemic noncompliance; therefore, the information supports an assessment of regulatory relevance rather than a negative reputation conclusion about an individual or group. [Data: Entities (1442, 5368, 2012, 2045, 2034); Relationships (6000, 5955, 5958, 5957)]

v.tieu_de: Safe Following Distance and Vehicle-Ahead Collision
v.tom_tat: This small community links the road-traffic violation of failure to maintain a safe following distance with a collision involving the vehicle ahead. The violation description covers driving too closely, disregarding a minimum-distance sign, or failing to leave a safe gap in a way that causes a collision; it also specifies a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 4. The records describe a potential connection, not a specific collision or enforcement case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A traffic violation is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The main entity is failure to maintain a safe following distance, defined as not keeping the required safe gap from the vehicle immediately ahead. The description includes driving too closely on an expressway and failing to observe a minimum-distance sign. [Data: Entities (1989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation carries a specified fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description states that, under Clause 4, the violation is punishable by a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The supplied records do not provide further details about enforcement or other possible penalties. [Data: Entities (1989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A collision with the vehicle ahead is identified as a possible consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship record connects the collision entity to the following-distance violation and says that failing to maintain a safe distance can result in a collision with the vehicle ahead. This describes a possible consequence; it does not establish that a particular collision occurred. [Data: Entities (1008, 1989); Relationships (3580)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is narrowly structured around one violation and one outcome
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied data contains two entities—the traffic violation and a collision with the vehicle ahead—and one relationship connecting them. This supports treating the community as a focused road-safety topic rather than evidence of a wider network of actors or events. [Data: Entities (1989, 1008); Relationships (3580)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish a specific case or broader impact
phat_hien.giai_thich: The descriptions define the violation, state its fine, and identify a possible collision consequence, but provide no case-specific details such as a driver, location, date, injury, or enforcement action. Accordingly, the available evidence supports assessing the issue’s general road-safety relevance but not the severity of any particular incident. [Data: Entities (1989, 1008); Relationships (3580)]

v.tieu_de: Specialized Vehicle Operators and Decree 168/2024, Article 16
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the specialized vehicle operator, linked to two expressway traffic violations and to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 16.
