Relevant functional authorities are directed to work with families on traffic-law education and safe moped-riding instruction. The educational activities are described as covering both road-traffic regulations and safe moped-riding skills. [Data: Entities (4101, 4535); Relationships (9883, 9881)]

The data identifies coordination and subject matter, but does not specify particular authorities, training methods, technical resources, or evidence of the activities’ effectiveness. [Data: Entities (4101, 4535)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The school is a channel for compliance communication
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Families are instructed to communicate with the school about students’ compliance with road-traffic laws. This gives the school a role in the described information-sharing arrangement, alongside the families’ direct coordination with authorities. [Data: Entities (4619, 4815); Relationships (10403)]

No further school responsibilities, monitoring processes, or records of reported compliance are provided. [Data: Entities (4619); Relationships (10403)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community’s impact is preventive, with outcomes not established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Taken together, the commitment, family responsibilities, authority coordination, and school communication form a preventive framework intended to support lawful and safe student vehicle use. [Data: Entities (4815, 4557, 4101, 4535, 4619); Relationships (10299, 9883, 10403, 10289, 9881)]

The supplied records do not report traffic incidents, violations, sanctions, or measured safety outcomes. They also do not describe technical capabilities or raise concerns about legal compliance by the participating entities; therefore, the framework’s implementation and effectiveness cannot be assessed from this information alone. [Data: Entities (4815, 4557, 4101, 4535, 4619); Relationships (10299, 9883, 10403, 10289, 9881)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 151/2024: Schools and Student Road Safety
v.tom_tat: This community centers on high schools and vocational education institutions and their responsibilities under Decree 151/2024/ND-CP for student road-traffic safety. Article 6 connects both types of institution to guidance on safe motorbike riding. The wider network includes road-safety education, student conduct assessment, and coordination with students’ families and parent representative boards. The information describes assigned responsibilities, but does not establish how consistently they are implemented or what outcomes they produce.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has notable public importance because it connects educational institutions, student conduct, family engagement, and road-safety education, although the data describes responsibilities rather than evidence of implementation or impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A shared regulatory framework for two types of educational institutions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
High schools and vocational education institutions are both identified as responsible for guiding students in safe motorbike-riding skills under the framework described in Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. Their shared role makes these institutions the central operational entities in the community. [Data: Entities (2485, 5616); Relationships (7738, 2340, 2341)]

The records describe institutional duties, not evidence that either type of institution has fulfilled them in practice. [Data: Entities (2485, 5616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 links institutions to practical riding guidance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 is specifically associated with responsibilities for guiding students in safe motorbike-riding skills, and the data identifies both high schools and vocational education institutions as having such responsibilities. [Data: Entities (501, 4605); Relationships (2340, 2341, 7734)]

The source material does not specify the guidance’s format, frequency, or measured effectiveness, so those aspects cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (501, 4605, 2485, 5616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-traffic legal education is part of the institutions’ role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes road-traffic order and safety legal education for students in both high schools and vocational education institutions. The described subject matter includes traffic rules, road signals, vehicle speed, and safe distances. [Data: Entities (4395, 2485, 5616); Relationships (7731, 10191)]

Vocational education institutions are described as incorporating relevant knowledge into teaching programs in ways suited to their fields of study. The records do not provide comparable detail about curriculum design for high schools. [Data: Entities (5616, 2485)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-law compliance is tied to vocational student conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For vocational education institutions, compliance with road-traffic laws is identified as a criterion for assessing and classifying student conduct. The relationship records also connect road-traffic law compliance to student conduct assessment. [Data: Entities (4807, 4357, 5616); Relationships (10464, 10140, 10139)]

This describes a formal assessment criterion, not actual student compliance rates or the consequences of particular assessment results; those are not provided. [Data: Entities (4807, 4357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Family and parent-representative coordination supports compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe institutions organizing students and families to sign commitments to obey traffic laws and safety requirements, reminding students to honor those commitments, and communicating with families about compliance. High schools are also linked to coordination with student parent representative boards. [Data: Entities (2485, 5616, 4808, 4809); Relationships (7735, 7736, 10465, 10466)]

These connections make family communication and reminders part of the described compliance-support structure. The dataset does not indicate how frequently communication occurs or whether it changes behavior. [Data: Entities (4808, 4809, 2485, 5616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vocational students are a defined recipient group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vocational education students are identified as learners enrolled in vocational education institutions who receive education concerning road-traffic order and safety. This establishes a direct connection between the institutions’ educational responsibilities and their students. [Data: Entities (5618, 5616); Relationships (10702, 10191)]

The provided records do not give student population figures, geographic coverage, or information about other student groups’ exposure, limiting assessment of the community’s reach. [Data: Entities (5618, 5616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish responsibilities, not implementation or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information describes legal and institutional duties related to education, riding guidance, conduct assessment, and family coordination. It contains no reported implementation results, compliance measurements, enforcement actions, or safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (2485, 501, 5616, 4395); Relationships (2340, 2341, 10464, 10465, +more)]

Accordingly, the community is important as a framework for student road safety, but the available evidence is insufficient to evaluate operational performance or determine whether the requirements have reduced traffic risk. [Data: Entities (2485, 5616, 4605)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 5: Student Riding Instruction and License Suspension
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on “Article 5,” a label used for provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one unified topic. The connected relationships emphasize safe motorbike-riding instruction and practice for students beginning upper secondary or vocational education, as well as rules on suspending the use of licenses or professional practice certificates. Clause 6 is referenced as an exception to a restriction during suspension, but its specific provisions are not supplied. The entity description also identifies Article 5 provisions concerning road-traffic law dissemination and child passenger safety, rural-road design speed, and an amendment to another article. [Data: Entities (475, 4599, 4812, 4600, 4833, +more); Relationships (2223, 2225, 2226, 2224, 2214)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because its described provisions cover student road safety and consequential administrative restrictions, while the supplied data does not establish violations or specific harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 5” refers to provisions in multiple instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is explicitly described as referring to different provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments, not a single topic. Its identified subjects include student riding instruction, license or certificate suspensions, road-traffic law dissemination and child passenger safety, rural-road design speed, and an amendment to another article. [Data: Entities (475)]

The connected records reflect only some of those subjects, so the community should not be read as one consolidated rule or as a complete account of every provision called Article 5. [Data: Entities (475); Relationships (2223, 2226, 2222)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student safe-riding instruction is a major connected theme
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 5 is linked to guidance on safe motorbike-driving skills for students entering upper secondary or vocational education, and to the students as intended recipients. [Data: Entities (4599, 4812); Relationships (2223, 2225)]

The described instruction covers starting and stopping the engine, using the throttle and brakes, changing gears, and using protective equipment. This indicates a practical road-safety education focus in the represented provision. [Data: Entities (4598)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community includes practical riding activity and educational institutions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Safe motorbike-driving practice is linked to Article 5, with the entity description stating that students undertake the activity in accordance with the cited provisions. [Data: Entities (4600); Relationships (2224)]

The student group is also connected to upper secondary education institutions. The available records establish this educational context but do not specify institutional duties, program delivery arrangements, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (4812, 5288); Relationships (10478)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License and certificate suspensions carry restrictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 5 is linked to the suspension of license or certificate use, described as a temporary removal of the right to use a license or professional practice certificate. [Data: Entities (4833); Relationships (2226)]

During suspension, affected individuals or organizations generally may not apply for a new, replacement, or renewed license or certificate, subject to an exception in Clause 6. The supplied description does not specify the substance of that exception or the procedures for applying the restriction. [Data: Entities (4833, 973); Relationships (2214)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied data does not establish compliance or misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe the subject matter of provisions and the entities connected to them; they do not identify a person or organization accused of violating the rules, nor do they report an enforcement action or compliance assessment. [Data: Entities (475, 4599, 4833); Relationships (2223, 2226)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is grounded in the scope of the described legal and road-safety topics, not in evidence of wrongdoing or a documented adverse incident. [Data: Entities (475, 4599, 4833)]

v.tieu_de: Student Transport Safety and Article 27 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP
v.tom_tat: This community links drivers of commercial vehicles transporting preschool children or students with the safety requirements for those vehicles and Article 27 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP. The described violation involves transporting preschool or primary-school children without age-appropriate seats or seat belts, including in vehicles combining commercial transport with student pickup and drop-off. Article 27 specifies penalties for covered drivers, including a stated fine range of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the described violation. The information establishes a safety and compliance concern, but does not indicate that a specific violation or injury occurred. [Data: Entities (1542, 344, 5276, 3858, 4810); Relationships (1402, 1405, 6256, 9726, 9725)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the importance of protecting children transported in commercial vehicles and the stated regulatory penalties, while the records do not establish an actual violation or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Child-passenger safety is the central concern
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community centers on commercial transport of preschool children or students, with the specified safety concern involving age-appropriate seats or seat belts for preschool and primary-school children. The records describe a regulated violation scenario, not evidence that a particular vehicle was operated unsafely or that a child was harmed. [Data: Entities (1542, 5276, 3858); Relationships (6256, 9726)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 27 establishes penalties for covered drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 27 of Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP addresses penalties and driving-license point deductions for drivers transporting preschool children or students. Its described subsection specifies a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the specified vehicle-safety violation; the available records do not state the number of points deducted. [Data: Entities (344, 1542); Relationships (1402, 1405)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is defined by missing age-appropriate safety equipment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The described violation is operating a commercial vehicle transporting preschool or primary-school children without age-appropriate seats or seat belts. The relationship records connect this violation to the drivers who operate the covered vehicles and to the primary-school students being transported. [Data: Entities (5276, 3858, 1542); Relationships (6256, 9726)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pickup and drop-off transport is part of the covered context
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community includes student pickup and drop-off transport involving vehicles used to transport preschool children or students. The violation description also includes vehicles that combine commercial transport with student pickup and drop-off, linking the transport activity to the safety concern. [Data: Entities (4810, 5276); Relationships (9725)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory exposure, not a confirmed incident
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe who is covered, what safety condition constitutes the specified violation, and the associated penalty provision. They do not identify a particular driver, vehicle, enforcement action, or injury, so the information supports assessment of potential compliance and child-safety significance rather than a claim that an incident occurred. [Data: Entities (1542, 344, 5276, 3858, 4810); Relationships (1402, 1405, 6256, 9726, 9725)]

v.tieu_de: Student Safe-Riding Guidance and Education
v.tom_tat: This community centers on students receiving safe motorbike-riding guidance and motorcycle-riding instruction and assessment, particularly students beginning upper-secondary education or attending vocational institutions. The network connects students with the guidance, the educational settings where instruction is intended to take place, and families assigned a role in guiding students. The described instruction covers practical riding skills, while the broader student provisions also address legal eligibility and safe transport. The information establishes a road-safety and education focus but does not report implementation outcomes, violations, or reputational concerns.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public-safety importance because it concerns student rider training and transport, although the supplied information describes requirements and intended activities rather than demonstrated harms or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Students are the central population served
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Students are the main connecting entity: the guidance and the instruction-and-assessment activity are both directed to them, with specific attention to students beginning upper-secondary education and those attending vocational education institutions. The described purpose includes building practical skills, self-protection, and voluntary compliance with traffic laws. [Data: Entities (4811, 4604, 4606); Relationships (10383, 10390)]

The student description also refers to eligibility requirements before operating a motorcycle and completion of guidance before operating a moped. These are described as applicable requirements; the data does not establish whether individual students have met them. [Data: Entities (4811, 4596); Relationships (10361)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Guidance covers specific practical riding skills
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The safe motorbike-riding skills guidance covers starting a motorbike, adjusting speed appropriately, stopping safely, and recognizing and handling dangerous situations. The first three are represented as skills linked directly to the guidance in the relationship records. [Data: Entities (4604, 38, 4752, 4768); Relationships (84, 10381, 10382)]

The description associates the guidance with Article 5 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and states that responsibilities for providing it are set out in Article 6. This supports a regulatory context, but the records do not provide an assessment of compliance or enforcement. [Data: Entities (4604)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Schools are intended settings for instruction and assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Upper-secondary schools are identified as institutions whose incoming students are among the intended recipients of safe-riding guidance. The separate instruction-and-assessment activity is also described as taking place at educational institutions, with its timing and implementation adapted to practical requirements there. [Data: Entities (5289, 4606); Relationships (10386, 10392)]

The available records describe intended roles and settings rather than naming specific schools or documenting completed training sessions. [Data: Entities (5289, 4606); Relationships (10386, 10392)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Families have a stated supporting role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Families of students are identified as responsible for guiding students in safe motorbike-riding skills. This adds a family-support component alongside the guidance and instruction associated with students and educational institutions. [Data: Entities (2087); Relationships (7071)]

The data does not specify the form, duration, or monitoring of family guidance, so its practical reach cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (2087); Relationships (7071)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Instruction and assessment are distinct but related activities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish safe motorbike-riding skills guidance from safe motorcycle-riding skills instruction and assessment. Both activities target students beginning upper-secondary education or students in vocational education, while the assessment activity is described as adapted to an educational institution’s practical requirements. [Data: Entities (4604, 4606); Relationships (10383, 10390, 10392)]

This structure indicates a training focus with an assessment component, but the supplied information does not describe assessment criteria, results, or whether students must pass an assessment before riding. [Data: Entities (4606)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student transport safety is also within the described scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The student entity description additionally identifies students as passengers in commercial vehicles and in vehicles used for school or preschool pickup and drop-off. It states that cited provisions address requirements for vehicles carrying students, including required paint color, and assigns educational institutions arranging student transportation responsibility for safe pickup and drop-off. [Data: Entities (4811)]

No separate transport-related entities or relationships are included in the supplied network, so this aspect is present in the student description but is less developed than the rider-training connections. [Data: Entities (4811)]

v.tieu_de: School Passenger Transport and Vehicle-Color Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community links school passenger transport with commercial transport drivers and a specific regulatory violation: operating a school-transport vehicle without the required paint color. The drivers are connected both to the transport activity and to the violation. The supplied records establish these relationships but do not provide details about particular drivers, incidents, frequency, or outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns regulated transport of preschool children and students and identifies a related compliance violation, but the records do not establish its scale or any actual harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: School passenger transport is the community's central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
School passenger transport is defined as transporting preschool children or students in commercial passenger vehicles, including vehicles used for pick-up and drop-off. It is connected to commercial transport drivers, making the transport activity the main operational focus of the community. [Data: Entities (4621, 1019); Relationships (3596)]

The records describe the activity and its connection to drivers, but do not specify routes, locations, operators, or the number of students or vehicles involved. [Data: Entities (4621, 1019); Relationships (3596)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commercial transport drivers link the activity to the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Commercial transport drivers are described as drivers of commercial passenger cars, including vehicles used to transport preschool children and students. The records connect these drivers both to school passenger transport and to the paint-color violation. [Data: Entities (1019); Relationships (3596, 3595)]

This makes drivers the connecting entity in the supplied network. The data do not identify any individual driver or establish that a specific person committed a violation. [Data: Entities (1019); Relationships (3595)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The identified violation concerns required vehicle paint color
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a violation defined as operating a commercial vehicle used for school transport without the paint color required by regulation. The relationship record attributes the violation to a driver operating a vehicle used for school transport. [Data: Entities (1584); Relationships (3595)]

The records do not state which regulation applies, whether the violation occurred in a specific case, or what enforcement action or penalty may have followed. [Data: Entities (1584); Relationships (3595)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records connect the violation specifically to student transport
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is not described as a general commercial-vehicle issue alone: its entity description specifically concerns a commercial vehicle transporting preschool children or students. This ties the compliance concern directly to the community's school passenger transport activity. [Data: Entities (1584, 4621)]

The relationship records reinforce the link between school transport and its drivers, and between those drivers and the violation. They do not provide evidence of an accident, injury, or other outcome. [Data: Relationships (3596, 3595)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Available evidence is limited to definitions and two relationships
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information contains three entity records and two relationships: a connection between drivers and school passenger transport, and a connection between drivers and the paint-color violation. It supports describing the community's topic and structure, but not estimating the prevalence of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (4621, 1584, 1019); Relationships (3596, 3595)]

No dates, locations, named organizations, incident counts, enforcement results, or technical details about vehicles are provided. Accordingly, conclusions about specific legal outcomes or operational capabilities cannot be drawn from these records. [Data: Entities (4621, 1584, 1019); Relationships (3596, 3595)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Safety Legal Education for General Education Students
v.tom_tat: This community connects legal education concerning road traffic order and safety, addressed in Article 6 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, with general education students as an explicitly identified recipient group. The records establish this relationship but do not describe how the education is delivered or its outcomes. [Data: Entities (2867, 2383); Relationships (7598)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public relevance because it concerns road-safety legal education for general education students, while the records provide no evidence of implementation scale or measurable effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community centers on legal education about road traffic order and safety
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central subject is education in legal knowledge concerning road traffic order and safety. It is described as addressed in Article 6 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (2867)]

The records identify the subject and legal reference, but do not provide further details about the law's provisions. [Data: Entities (2867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: General education students are identified as recipients
phat_hien.giai_thich:
General education students are explicitly identified as recipients of the legal education. This makes them the specified audience in the community, without establishing additional details about their ages, locations, or number. [Data: Entities (2383); Relationships (7598)]

The relationship connects this student group directly to the road-traffic legal education. [Data: Relationships (7598)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a direct educational relationship
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The sole supplied relationship states that students of general education institutions are explicitly included among the recipients of education on road traffic order and safety. [Data: Relationships (7598)]

This supports a clear link between the educational topic and its intended recipients, but does not indicate whether students are the only recipients.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The subject has public-safety relevance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The education concerns legal knowledge about road traffic order and safety, giving the topic a direct connection to road-safety awareness. The records establish the subject matter, but do not report changes in knowledge, behavior, compliance, or safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (2867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation and impact are not documented in the supplied records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information identifies the educational topic, its statutory reference, the student recipient group, and their relationship. [Data: Entities (2867, 2383); Relationships (7598)]

It does not specify curriculum content, delivery methods, responsible institutions, geographic coverage, participation levels, compliance monitoring, or measured results; therefore, the community's practical reach and effectiveness cannot be assessed from these records.

v.tieu_de: Child Transport Safety Equipment Violation and Fines
v.tom_tat: This community concerns the prohibited transport of preschool children or students in commercial vehicles without required image-recording equipment, child-presence warning and anti-forgetting equipment, or both. Transport business organizations are identified as potentially liable for the violation, and the cited fine provision sets different fine ranges for individuals and transport business organizations. The information describes a specific compliance requirement and its financial penalties; it does not identify particular operators or instances of noncompliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns child-transport safety compliance and specifies financial penalties, but provides no evidence of particular violations or affected operators.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The central issue is a defined child-transport safety violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The prohibited conduct is transporting preschool children or students in a commercial vehicle without equipment to record images of the children, equipment to warn against and prevent children being left behind, or both. This establishes the core compliance issue represented in the community. [Data: Entities (5129)]

The information describes a regulatory prohibition, but does not report a specific incident, vehicle, or operator that committed the violation. [Data: Entities (5129)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two types of safety equipment are specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described requirement covers image-recording equipment and equipment intended to warn against and prevent children being left behind. The violation may involve the absence of either category or both. [Data: Entities (5129)]

The records do not provide technical specifications, installation standards, or details about how compliance is inspected; those matters cannot be assessed from this information. [Data: Entities (5129)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport business organizations are explicitly within scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Transport business organizations are described as organizations that may be fined for using vehicles to transport preschool children or students without the specified equipment. [Data: Entities (5093)]

A relationship record directly links these organizations to the described violation and states they may be fined for committing it. This makes organizational compliance a key part of the community. [Data: Relationships (10597)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine ranges differ for individuals and organizations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine provision sets a range of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for individuals who commit the specified violation, and 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese dong for transport business organizations that commit it. [Data: Entities (2269)]

The provision is also linked specifically to transport business organizations that commit the violation. The records give the stated ranges but do not provide further information about how fines are determined within each range. [Data: Relationships (7335); Entities (2269)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information supports compliance assessment, not claims about actual enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify the prohibited conduct, the organizations that may be fined, and the stated monetary penalties. Together, these details provide a basis for understanding the compliance obligation and its specified financial consequences. [Data: Entities (5129, 5093, 2269); Relationships (10597, 7335)]

No records identify particular businesses, vehicles, enforcement actions, or repeat violations. Accordingly, the material does not establish whether any entity has breached the requirement or whether penalties have been imposed. [Data: Entities (5129, 5093, 2269); Relationships (10597, 7335)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 31 Road-Traffic Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on “Article 31,” which refers to three distinct provisions in Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one unified rule. The records associate it with road-safety measures for certain vehicles, requirements for people and cargo on rudimentary vehicles, and administrative penalties concerning unlawful vehicle manufacture or assembly and license-plate production, purchase, or sale. The material indicates regulatory and public-safety relevance, but does not document actual violations or incidents. [Data: Entities (366, 4446, 3631); Relationships (1508, 1514)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects Article 31’s broad road-safety and enforcement relevance across several legal provisions, while the supplied records establish no actual violation or incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 31” refers to three separate legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is ambiguous without its legal instrument: the supplied description identifies Article 31 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and Law 36/2024/QH15 as addressing different road-traffic matters. The shared article number should therefore not be treated as a single provision with one subject. [Data: Entities (366)]

The described subjects range from safety requirements for certain vehicles to administrative penalties and rules for drivers, passengers, and cargo on rudimentary vehicles. [Data: Entities (366)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: One provision addresses road-safety measures for certain vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 31 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as covering oversized, overweight, tracked, and special-cargo vehicles traveling on roads. Its measures include driver assistance, warnings to other road users, and other necessary safety steps. [Data: Entities (366)]

The relationship records explicitly connect Article 31 with road-traffic safety measures. This establishes a safety-focused regulatory aspect of the community, but does not show whether any particular vehicle or operator complied with or violated the requirements. [Data: Entities (4446); Relationships (1514)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records identify penalties for unlawful vehicle manufacture and assembly
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 31 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as providing administrative penalties for the illegal manufacture or assembly of road motor vehicles. The entity records separately identify both conduct categories. [Data: Entities (366, 2502, 2515)]

The relationships link Article 31 to penalties for illegal assembly and illegal manufacture. These are descriptions of conduct subject to penalties, not evidence that such conduct occurred in a specific case. [Data: Relationships (1505, 1506, 1513)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-plate production, purchase, and sale are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied description of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP identifies unlawful production, purchase, or sale of vehicle license plates as conduct subject to administrative penalties under Article 31. [Data: Entities (366, 2525, 2527, 2540)]

Separate relationships connect Article 31 to each of these three license-plate activities. The data does not identify a person, organization, transaction, or actual enforcement action associated with them. [Data: Relationships (1508, 1510, 1511)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A third provision concerns rudimentary vehicles and their occupants or cargo
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 31 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is described as addressing drivers, passengers, and cargo carried on rudimentary vehicles, including requirements related to lane use and lights. [Data: Entities (366)]

This subject differs from the safety measures for certain specialized vehicles and the administrative-penalty provisions. The records provide no further detail about specific situations, enforcement, or compliance under this provision. [Data: Entities (366)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is legally significant, but the records do not establish actual misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity and relationship records describe statutory subjects, safety measures, and penalties, making the community relevant to road-traffic safety and regulatory compliance. Article 31 is connected to both safety measures and penalties for specified unlawful conduct. [Data: Entities (366, 3631, 4446); Relationships (1513, 1514)]

The supplied material does not identify actual violations, affected parties, enforcement proceedings, or resulting harm. Accordingly, the significance assessed here concerns the scope of the provisions described, not a finding that anyone has breached them. [Data: Entities (366, 3631); Relationships (1505, 1506, 1508, 1510, 1511)]

v.tieu_de: Permitted Operating Speed Determination and Speed-Sign Installation
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a process for determining permitted operating speeds and arranging corresponding speed-sign installation, together with the road sections subject to that process. The relationship identifies those road sections as the focus of the process. The data describes a road-management activity but gives no specific locations, speed limits, implementation status, or compliance information.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the process’s relevance to road operations and its limited documented scope, with no evidence provided about particular locations or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A process links speed decisions with sign installation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity is a process that considers and decides the permitted operating speed for a road section and organizes installation of the corresponding speed signs. The description therefore brings speed determination and signage coordination together in one activity. [Data: Entities (3700)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road sections are the stated focus
phat_hien.giai_thich: The second entity represents road sections for which a permitted operating speed is to be considered and speed signs installed. The relationship confirms that these sections are the subject of the process. [Data: Entities (4307); Relationships (9586)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship describes intended work, not a confirmed outcome
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship says the event involves deciding a permitted speed and arranging sign installation. It does not establish that a speed has already been decided or that signs have been installed. [Data: Relationships (9586)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is narrowly structured
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied data identifies two entities connected by one relationship: the speed-determination and installation process, and the road sections it concerns. No other organizations, people, locations, or related activities are identified in these records. [Data: Entities (3700, 4307); Relationships (9586)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation and compliance details are not provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records do not specify the road sections’ locations, the permitted speeds under consideration, a schedule, completed installation, or any compliance results. The community can therefore be characterized as a described road-management process, but its implementation and effects cannot be assessed from the supplied data. [Data: Entities (3700, 4307); Relationships (9586)]

v.tieu_de: Preschool Road-Safety Education and Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on preschool educational institutions as settings for road-traffic safety education and compliance management. The related entities describe teaching activities, legal education, road-traffic-law instruction, and oversight of compliance, with the oversight responsibility assigned to the Ministry of Education and Training. The information indicates a public-safety and education focus; it does not document specific compliance failures or incidents.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s stated relevance to children’s road safety and institutional compliance, while the supplied records identify no specific incidents or violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Preschool institutions are the community’s central setting
phat_hien.giai_thich: Preschool Educational Institutions are described as serving preschool-age children and as settings for age-appropriate education on traffic laws, traffic order, and road safety. They connect to the teaching, instruction, legal-education, and compliance-management topics in the community. [Data: Entities (3847); Relationships (9310, 8667, 9719, 9718, 9720)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Teaching activities convey road-traffic knowledge
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community includes the organization of teaching activities on legal knowledge and road-traffic order and safety at preschool and general education institutions. A relationship specifies that these activities are to take place at preschool institutions. [Data: Entities (3424); Relationships (9310)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Safety education addresses rules and consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich: Road Traffic Safety Legal Education is described as covering the laws governing traffic order and safety, including the dangers and consequences of failing to follow safety rules. The records identify this education as content for children at preschool institutions. [Data: Entities (4445, 3847); Relationships (9720)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-traffic-law instruction is developed and delivered in institutions
phat_hien.giai_thich: Road Traffic Law Instruction covers the development, integration, and delivery of learning activities about legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety. The data state that this instruction is organized at preschool educational institutions. [Data: Entities (4362); Relationships (9719)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance oversight is part of the institutional framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe management and oversight of compliance with laws on road-traffic order and safety at preschool and other education institutions. The oversight responsibility is assigned to the Ministry of Education and Training, and the related management activities apply to preschool institutions. [Data: Entities (2958, 4358); Relationships (8667, 9718)]

v.tieu_de: Preschool Child Transport Safety and Decree 168/2024
v.tom_tat: This community centers on preschool children as passengers covered by road-traffic safety provisions. Educational institutions are responsible for safe transport procedures and traffic safety, while child supervisors must be instructed and commercial-vehicle drivers transport the children. The records identify three equipment-related noncompliance categories for commercial vehicles: lacking image-recording equipment, lacking warning and anti-forgetting equipment, or lacking both. They describe regulatory obligations and potential violations, not evidence that a violation has occurred.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high impact importance because it concerns the safety of young passengers and specific transport safeguards, although the records do not establish any actual breach or incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Preschool children are the central, vulnerable population
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Preschool children are the central entity in this community and are described as passengers covered by road-traffic safety provisions, including provisions addressing commercial transport and educational-institution pickup and drop-off. The records also identify them as recipients of instruction on road-traffic order and safety. These details make child protection the principal concern represented by the community. [Data: Entities (3846)]

The relationships connect preschool children to the educational institution, commercial-vehicle drivers, and each of the three equipment-related violation categories, underscoring that the safety framework spans institutional arrangements and vehicle operation. [Data: Relationships (6596, 6258, 9712, 9713, 9715)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Educational institutions have transport-safety responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An educational institution is described as responsible for establishing and communicating safe procedures for transporting preschool children and students, and for ensuring road-traffic order and safety during those activities. Its relationship with preschool children specifically links the institution to responsibility for safety when arranging their transportation. [Data: Entities (1727); Relationships (6596)]

This establishes an organizational responsibility in addition to the requirements associated with vehicle equipment. The records do not specify particular procedures beyond requiring that they be established and communicated, so further operational details cannot be assessed from this data.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commercial-vehicle transport is subject to equipment-related safeguards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe commercial vehicles carrying preschool children or students as subject to requirements for image-recording equipment and equipment that warns against and helps prevent children from being left behind. Drivers of commercial vehicles are identified as the people transporting these children. [Data: Entities (1543, 5128, 5131); Relationships (6258)]

These requirements are framed in the data as safeguards relevant to child transport. The records do not describe equipment specifications, inspection processes, or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three distinct noncompliance categories are identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data distinguishes transport without image-recording equipment, transport without warning and anti-forgetting equipment, and transport without either required device. Preschool children are identified as the passengers covered by each category. [Data: Entities (5128, 5131, 5127); Relationships (9713, 9715, 9712)]

These are descriptions of prohibited or noncompliant conditions, not reports that a particular driver or institution engaged in them. The distinction between the individual equipment omissions and the combined omission helps clarify the risk categories represented, but the records provide no incident counts or details of actual cases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Child supervisors are part of the institutional safety process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Child supervisors are described as people responsible for managing children during transportation. The educational institution must instruct them in required procedures for safely transporting preschool children and students. [Data: Entities (818); Relationships (3190)]

This connects institutional responsibility to the people managing children during transit. The records do not identify specific supervisors, describe the content or completion of instruction, or provide evidence about how procedures operate in practice.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory relevance, not a proven breach
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions place these obligations and equipment-related prohibitions within road-traffic safety provisions, including Articles 27 and 46 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. This makes the community relevant to legal compliance and safeguarding young passengers. [Data: Entities (3846, 5128, 5131, 5127)]

No specific incident, enforcement action, penalty, or finding of noncompliance is included in the provided records. Accordingly, the community’s importance reflects the potential consequences of the subject matter and the safeguards described, rather than evidence of misconduct by any named institution or driver.

v.tieu_de: Clause 9 Traffic Penalties and Vehicle Service-Life Violation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on CLAUSE 9, which is described as referring to different provisions depending on the article. Its relationships connect it to operating a vehicle beyond its permitted service life, for which confiscation is specified subject to an exception, and to a traffic fine of VND 18,000,000–20,000,000 for listed violations. The records describe regulatory penalties, but do not establish how frequently they are applied or the broader compliance status of any person or organization. [Data: Entities (992, 3341, 5042); Relationships (3556, 3557)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to traffic enforcement and substantial listed penalties, while the supplied records are limited to a small set of provisions and do not document wider impacts. [Data: Entities (992, 3341, 5042); Relationships (3556, 3557)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: CLAUSE 9 is the community’s central, article-dependent reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
CLAUSE 9 is the hub connecting the two other entities in the supplied relationships. Its description cautions that the label refers to different provisions, so the applicable effect depends on the article in which it appears. [Data: Entities (992); Relationships (3556, 3557)]

The description associates it with penalties under Articles 6, 7, and 18, as well as vehicle confiscation under Article 13. These are distinct article-specific references, not one consistent sanction. [Data: Entities (992)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A service-life violation is associated with confiscation, subject to an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe operating a vehicle beyond its permitted service life as a traffic violation, except for the separately specified case in Article 13, Clause 5, point c. [Data: Entities (3341)]

The relationship states that CLAUSE 9 identifies this violation as subject to confiscation, with that same stated exception. The supplied information does not specify additional circumstances or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Relationships (3556)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A VND 18–20 million fine is linked to listed violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes an entity for a traffic violation fine of VND 18,000,000 to 20,000,000. Its description identifies failure to obey a traffic signal as one of the covered violations. [Data: Entities (5042)]

The relationship connects this fine to CLAUSE 9 and says it is established for listed violations. CLAUSE 9’s description also associates this range with specified driver violations under Article 6 and listed driving-licence violations under Article 18. [Data: Entities (992); Relationships (3557)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described consequences vary across article references
phat_hien.giai_thich:
CLAUSE 9’s description gives a fine of VND 8,000,000–10,000,000 for the described Article 7 violation, a fine of VND 18,000,000–20,000,000 for specified Article 6 and Article 18 violations, and confiscation for specified Article 13 violations. [Data: Entities (992)]

Because the description explicitly distinguishes these article-specific references, the penalties should not be treated as interchangeable or as a single general sanction. The supplied records do not provide the complete underlying legal text. [Data: Entities (992)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory relevance but not actual enforcement or compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships identify a traffic violation, a monetary penalty, and a confiscation consequence, making the community relevant to traffic regulation and enforcement. [Data: Entities (3341, 5042); Relationships (3556, 3557)]

No supplied record identifies a particular driver, enforcement action, payment, confiscation event, or compliance outcome. Accordingly, the data supports describing the provisions and their stated consequences, but not conclusions about real-world application or the compliance of any individual or organization. [Data: Entities (992, 3341, 5042); Relationships (3556, 3557)]

v.tieu_de: Competent Road Management Authority and Vehicle Oversight
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Competent Road Management Authority, which is described as responsible for issuing circulation permits for certain oversized or overweight vehicles and for leading a coordinated process to determine permitted operating speeds and arrange speed signs. The route’s traffic police force participates in that process, alongside a relevant district-level People’s Committee. The records describe administrative responsibilities and relationships, but do not establish whether permits were issued, speed limits were set, or the procedures were followed in any specific case.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it concerns vehicle permitting and coordinated road-speed and signage decisions, while the records show no specific incident or compliance outcome.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority is the community’s central decision-maker
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Competent Road Management Authority is described as the authorized body for issuing circulation permits for vehicles transporting oversized or overweight cargo, and as the lead body in the speed-determination and sign-installation procedure. Its links to both functions make it the central entity in this community. [Data: Entities (1059); Relationships (3829, 3833)]

The records establish assigned responsibilities, not the authority’s performance in a particular case. They do not document a specific decision, permit, or implementation outcome. [Data: Entities (1059, 1352); Relationships (3829, 3833)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Speed decisions and sign installation are coordinated procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described Article 10 procedure has the authority coordinate with the route’s traffic police and the relevant district-level People’s Committee to consider and decide the permitted operating speed and arrange for speed-sign installation in specified cases. This links a speed decision to both inter-agency coordination and a physical road-sign measure. [Data: Entities (1059, 1352); Relationships (3829, 3832, 5810)]

The records do not identify the specified cases, a particular route, or the speed or sign arrangements adopted. They therefore support a description of the procedure, but not a conclusion about a specific road’s operating conditions. [Data: Entities (1352, 5033); Relationships (3829, 5810)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Route traffic police participate in speed coordination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force on the Route is described as participating in coordination with the authority during the process for determining permitted operating speed and arranging signs. Its role in the community is therefore tied to the route-specific speed procedure rather than to permit issuance in the provided records. [Data: Entities (5033); Relationships (3832, 5810)]

No further detail is provided about the force’s actions, enforcement activity, or decisions on a particular route. The available evidence supports its coordination role only. [Data: Entities (5033); Relationships (3832, 5810)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circulation permits apply to specified vehicle categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority is described as issuing circulation permits for vehicles transporting oversized or overweight cargo, including oversized vehicles, overweight vehicles, and tracked vehicles operating on roads. The permit-issuance function is explicitly connected to the authority in the relationship data. [Data: Entities (1059, 5373); Relationships (3833)]

The records do not provide permit criteria, application details, individual permit decisions, or evidence of compliance by any vehicle operator. They establish the stated function and scope, not how it has been applied in practice. [Data: Entities (1059, 5373); Relationships (3833)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community reflects administrative coordination, not a documented incident
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe an institutional process involving the road management authority, route traffic police, speed decisions, signage, and circulation permits. Nothing in the provided records identifies an accident, enforcement case, dispute, or other specific event. [Data: Entities (1059, 1352, 5033, 5373); Relationships (3829, 3832, 3833, 5810)]

Accordingly, the information supports assessing this community as relevant to road administration and vehicle movement, but does not substantiate a finding of unlawful conduct, deficient compliance, or an adverse outcome. [Data: Entities (1059, 1352, 5033, 5373); Relationships (3829, 3832, 3833, 5810)]

v.tieu_de: Traffic Police Force, Road Management, and Safety Programs
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Traffic Police Force, which coordinates with road authorities on traffic safety, speed decisions, and speed-limit signage, and manages traffic command and data systems. It also connects the Force with high-school management bodies to organize safe motorbike-riding instruction for students. The records describe statutory roles and operational relationships, but do not establish outcomes, compliance performance, or reputational assessments.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public importance because it links road-safety administration, traffic data systems, speed management, and student safety instruction, although the records do not establish adverse impacts or implementation outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Traffic Police Force is the community’s central operational actor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force has the highest listed degree among the entities and is connected to road authorities, speed-setting activities, road sections, and student instruction. Its described responsibilities include patrolling and control, operating traffic command and data systems, coordinating speed decisions, and organizing road-safety instruction. [Data: Entities (5032); Relationships (10041, 10049, 10374, 10376, 5805)]

This central position indicates that the Force participates across both infrastructure-related functions and educational activities. The records establish responsibilities and relationships, but do not report how effectively these duties are carried out. [Data: Entities (5032); Relationships (7730, 7727)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic data systems connect the Force with road authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force is described as managing and operating the traffic command center and systems for journey-monitoring data and images of drivers and passenger compartments. Its applications provide electronic access to shared information from the road traffic order and safety database. [Data: Entities (5032)]

The Road Management Authority and Road Administration Authority are each described as connected to or sharing information through relevant systems with the Traffic Police Force. The records do not specify data-access controls, retention practices, cybersecurity measures, or the details of information exchanged, so no conclusion about those matters is supported. [Data: Entities (4292, 4273); Relationships (10041, 10015)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Speed decisions and signage involve coordinated responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For a road section requiring speed-limit signs, the Road Management Authority leads consideration of the permitted operating speed and the organization of sign placement. The Traffic Police Force coordinates on the route, while the authority and Force are both linked to the speed-determination and signposting process. [Data: Entities (4292, 4306, 1349); Relationships (10039, 5804, 10049, 5805)]

The described arrangement assigns complementary roles: the authority leads the process, and the Traffic Police Force participates in coordination. The material identifies a road section in service but supplies no specific location, speed decision, sign-installation status, or safety outcome. [Data: Entities (4306); Relationships (10039, 5804, 10049, 5805)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Road Management Authority has a stated role in unexpected safety situations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Management Authority is described as responsible for managing roads and addressing risks or problems affecting road infrastructure and traffic safety. It should be notified promptly when a qualifying unexpected situation is discovered and must respond within its functions and duties when it detects or receives information about a situation that causes disorder or threatens road safety. [Data: Entities (4292)]

This describes an assigned response role, not evidence that a particular incident occurred or that a response was delayed or inadequate. The records provide no incident examples or performance measures. [Data: Entities (4292)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student motorbike-safety instruction links traffic and education bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force leads or coordinates safe motorbike-riding instruction for students in cooperation with high-school management agencies and authorities. The records distinguish instruction in safe riding from skills instruction for which high-school management authorities prepare facilities and motorbikes. [Data: Entities (5032, 4601, 4602, 2482, 2483); Relationships (10374, 10376, 7730, 7727)]

The relationships show the education bodies coordinating with the Force, and the management authorities preparing resources for the skills instruction. The supplied information does not indicate how many students participate, the curriculum’s results, or whether instruction has been delivered in specific schools. [Data: Entities (4601, 4602, 2482, 2483); Relationships (7725, 7729)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe statutory duties, not verified compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force’s description identifies Law 36/2024/QH15, including Article 65, clause 3, and Article 71, as the basis for specified patrol, control, and data-system responsibilities. The student instruction description also refers to Article 6 of the law. [Data: Entities (5032, 4602)]

These references establish that the supplied material presents the roles as legally assigned; they do not independently verify compliance, enforcement quality, or legal findings concerning any entity. The records also contain no specific allegations, reputation assessments, or outcome data, so those topics cannot be evaluated from this evidence. [Data: Entities (5032, 4602, 4292)]

v.tieu_de: Prohibited Motorcycle Operating Conduct
v.tom_tat: This community is a regulatory grouping centered on prohibited motorcycle operating conduct described as conduct listed in Clause 11 of Article 7. Seven specific behaviors are linked to the umbrella category: changing drivers while moving, driving blindfolded, steering with a foot, driving with both hands off the handlebars, steering while facing backward, sitting to one side, and lying on the seat. The descriptions identify these behaviors as prohibited and describe them as grounds for vehicle confiscation; the records document rules, not actual incidents or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (3917, 798, 3384, 1689, 3385, +more); Relationships (3147, 6495, 9757, 6503, 9756, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s importance to motorcycle safety and compliance because it groups prohibited conduct, including behaviors described as grounds for vehicle confiscation, without evidence of actual incidents or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: An umbrella category organizes the conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity, PROHIBITED MOTORCYCLE OPERATING CONDUCT, describes a set of acts listed in Clause 11 of Article 7, including unsafe ways of controlling or occupying a motorcycle. The other entities are linked to this category as individual prohibited acts, making it the organizing concept in the community. [Data: Entities (3917); Relationships (3147, 6495, 9757, 6503, 9756, +more)]

The records establish a regulatory classification, but do not provide the jurisdiction, the full text of the cited clause, or evidence that any person committed one of these acts. [Data: Entities (3917)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Changing drivers while moving is listed as prohibited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
CHANGING DRIVERS WHILE THE VEHICLE IS MOVING is described as replacing the person operating a vehicle while it is in motion. Its entity description says the act is prohibited and lists it as grounds for vehicle confiscation, and its relationship places it under the umbrella category. [Data: Entities (798, 3917); Relationships (3147)]

This identifies a stated compliance consequence, not evidence that confiscation has occurred in a particular case. [Data: Entities (798)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving while blindfolded is included in the category
phat_hien.giai_thich: DRIVING WHILE BLINDFOLDED is described as operating a vehicle while blindfolded and as an act listed as grounds for vehicle confiscation. The relationship record identifies it as one of the prohibited acts in the umbrella category. [Data: Entities (1676, 3917); Relationships (6495)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operating without hands on the handlebars is prohibited
phat_hien.giai_thich: DRIVING WITH BOTH HANDS OFF refers to operating a vehicle while letting go of both hands. Its description identifies it as grounds for vehicle confiscation, and its relationship links it to the prohibited-conduct category. [Data: Entities (1689, 3917); Relationships (6503)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Using a foot to steer is listed as prohibited conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich: STEERING WITH A FOOT is described as operating a vehicle by using a foot to steer. The entity description says this act is listed as grounds for vehicle confiscation, while the relationship places it within the umbrella category of prohibited motorcycle conduct. [Data: Entities (4765, 3917); Relationships (9757)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Facing backward while steering is included
phat_hien.giai_thich: STEERING WHILE FACING BACKWARD is described as turning to face backward while operating a vehicle. The record identifies this behavior as grounds for vehicle confiscation, and the relationship connects it to the central prohibited-conduct entity. [Data: Entities (4764, 3917); Relationships (9756)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unusual seating positions are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich: Two listed acts concern the operator’s position: OPERATING WHILE SITTING TO ONE SIDE and OPERATING WHILE LYING ON THE SEAT. Both entity descriptions identify the behavior as grounds for vehicle confiscation, and each is linked to the umbrella category as a prohibited act. [Data: Entities (3385, 3384, 3917); Relationships (9295, 9293)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules rather than incidents or enforcement activity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity descriptions and relationships define prohibited behaviors and, for the specific acts, state that they are grounds for vehicle confiscation. They do not identify offenders, dates, enforcement actions, injury statistics, or actual confiscations; therefore, the available information supports assessing this community as a safety and compliance taxonomy, not as evidence of a specific event or pattern of violations. [Data: Entities (3917, 798, 3384, 1689, 3385, +more); Relationships (3147, 6495, 9757, 6503, 9756, +more)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Clause 17 Vehicle-Confiscation Provision
v.tom_tat: This small legal-reference community consists of Clause 17 of Article 32 and Point b of Clause 16 of Article 32. Clause 17 refers to the violation described in Point b, Clause 16, stating that repeating it triggers vehicle confiscation; it also requires confiscation of specified vehicles when owners commit listed violations. The supplied data does not identify the jurisdiction, the underlying violations, or any implementation, compliance, or reputational information.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects a narrowly scoped provision with a potentially consequential vehicle-confiscation penalty, while the supplied data provides little context about its scope or application.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 17 establishes a vehicle-confiscation penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:

The data describes the rule but does not establish whether confiscation has occurred in any particular case or how the requirement is enforced.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The five-meter restricted area is defined by the intersection edge
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The five-meter area is described as extending up to five meters from the edge of a road intersection. Its relationship to the intersection establishes the reference point for the boundary, while a separate relationship connects the area to the stopping and parking prohibition. [Data: Entities (2290); Relationships (7360, 7359)]

This makes the distance-based restriction a distinct part of the community’s traffic rules, rather than a separate location unrelated to intersections. [Data: Entities (2290, 4284); Relationships (7360, 7359)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional intersection restrictions are noted in the entity description
phat_hien.giai_thich:

These details appear in the entity record but are not elaborated through separate relationship records in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (4284)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Education Ministry Road-Safety Education
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Ministry of Education and Training and its responsibilities under Article 7 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The Ministry leads road-traffic law and safety education and compliance management in preschool and general education institutions, coordinating with the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs and other government bodies. Schools deliver instruction to students, whose compliance may be considered in conduct assessments. The Ministry also has specified duties involving upper-secondary and vocational instruction, practical motorbike-riding education, and specialized certificates for eligible tractor operators. The information describes legal responsibilities, not evidence of actual implementation outcomes or compliance performance. [Data: Entities (3011, 2382, 3015, 4104, 539); Relationships (7592, 8784, 8792, 8791, 8798)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-policy importance because it connects a national ministry’s statutory responsibilities with education institutions and students, although the data provide no evidence of implementation outcomes or adverse impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry of Education and Training is the community’s central authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 7 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP assigns the Ministry of Education and Training responsibilities for organizing road-traffic law instruction and managing compliance at preschool and general education institutions. The Ministry is also linked to the development and integration of this subject matter into education, making it the principal coordinating entity in the community. [Data: Entities (3011, 539, 1354, 2954); Relationships (2519, 5813, 8656, 8788)]

These records establish a formal policy and administrative role. They do not establish how effectively the Ministry or institutions have carried out the assigned duties. [Data: Entities (3011, 539); Relationships (2519, 7592)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation depends on coordination across government bodies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is directed to coordinate with relevant ministries and ministerial-level agencies in carrying out its education-related responsibilities. The Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs is separately identified as a partner in developing and integrating road-traffic legal knowledge into curricula. [Data: Entities (3011, 3015, 4104); Relationships (8784, 8792, 8819, 7593)]

This structure distributes curriculum-related work across government bodies rather than placing every responsibility with a single ministry. The data identify the coordination mandate but do not specify the full set of participating agencies or report on coordination results. [Data: Entities (3015, 4104); Relationships (8792, 8819, 5816)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Schools are the primary settings for instruction and compliance management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
General education institutions—including preschool, primary, lower-secondary, and upper-secondary establishments—are covered by requirements to incorporate appropriate road-traffic legal knowledge into teaching and to manage compliance with relevant laws. The Ministry is responsible for organizing related instruction and activities at these institutions. [Data: Entities (2382, 3845, 3011); Relationships (7592, 8788, 5812)]

The records describe schools as delivery and compliance-management settings. They do not provide institution-level data, identify particular schools, or show whether the requirements are being met in practice. [Data: Entities (2382, 3845, 2954); Relationships (7592, 8656)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Students are both recipients of instruction and subjects of conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry organizes road-traffic law instruction for primary, lower-secondary, and upper-secondary students. Compliance with relevant traffic laws is also included among the criteria used to assess students’ conduct. [Data: Entities (3857, 3011); Relationships (8791, 7595)]

This links educational content with student conduct assessment, extending the policy beyond curriculum instruction alone. The data do not describe the assessment method, consequences, or student outcomes. [Data: Entities (3857); Relationships (8791)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry has additional responsibilities for specialized instruction and certificates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry’s described duties extend to developing road-traffic legal-knowledge instruction for upper-secondary education and coordinating practical safe motorbike-riding instruction, including curricula, guidance materials, facilities, and motorcycles. The description also assigns the Ministry responsibility for procedures concerning specialized vehicle-operation certificates for eligible tractor operators. [Data: Entities (3011, 5290, 4979); Relationships (8799, 8798)]

These responsibilities indicate that the community covers more than general classroom teaching. The supplied information describes assigned functions but does not provide details about the number of participants, training completion, or certificate issuance. [Data: Entities (3011, 4979); Relationships (8798)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence establishes legal scope, not operational performance or technical capacity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify the decree provision, responsible bodies, intended educational settings, and assigned activities. They do not report audit findings, violations, enforcement outcomes, curriculum completion rates, or evidence that institutions are complying or failing to comply. [Data: Entities (539, 3011, 2382, 2954); Relationships (2519, 7592, 8656)]

No specific technical systems, specialized equipment beyond the described preparation of facilities and motorcycles for practical instruction, or measured technical capabilities are documented. Accordingly, the community’s importance is grounded in the breadth of its formal responsibilities, not in evidence of demonstrated harm or implementation success. [Data: Entities (3011); Relationships (8788, 8799)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Driver Violations and License Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community consists of two related legal-regulatory concepts: motor vehicle driver violations and driving-license revocation. The relationship states that certain violations listed in Article 18 can result in revocation when a license was improperly issued or is invalid, in addition to other applicable penalties. The data describes a regulatory consequence, but does not identify any particular driver, actual violation, or enforcement action.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is modest because the community describes a potentially significant licensing penalty but contains only a narrow regulatory relationship and no evidence of a specific case or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A narrow community centered on driver regulation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains two entities: motor vehicle driver violations and driving-license revocation. Their single recorded relationship connects a category of violations to a possible licensing consequence. [Data: Entities (3103, 1716); Relationships (6571)]

The records do not identify additional organizations, individuals, or events, so the evidence supports a focused regulatory topic rather than a broader network. [Data: Entities (3103, 1716); Relationships (6571)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18 violations may lead to revocation
phat_hien.giai_thich:

phat_hien.tom_tat: Revocation is tied to license validity or issuance

The revocation description identifies licenses not issued by a competent authority or licenses that are invalid as grounds for revocation, in addition to other applicable penalties. [Data: Entities (1716)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data describes a possible legal consequence, not a documented case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state a general relationship between certain violations and license revocation. They do not name a driver, document an alleged or confirmed violation by an individual, or report an actual revocation. [Data: Entities (3103, 1716); Relationships (6571)]

Accordingly, the community supports analysis of the stated regulatory mechanism but not conclusions about specific enforcement activity or individual compliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other applicable penalties are mentioned but unspecified

The driving-license revocation description says revocation is imposed in addition to other applicable penalties. [Data: Entities (1716)]

No other penalties are named in the available records, so their types, severity, and circumstances cannot be determined from this community's data. [Data: Entities (1716); Relationships (6571)]

v.tieu_de: Article 14: Request to Overtake and Yielding
v.tom_tat: This small community consists of two traffic-related concepts linked by the heading of Article 14: a request to overtake and the duty to yield to that vehicle.
