The fine description cites Articles 6 and 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The records describe penalties and violation categories; they do not identify particular offenders or establish that any violation occurred.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance because it groups penalties for conduct affecting roadway safety, but the records establish no specific incident or offender.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community’s central link
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 VND penalty is the hub connecting the listed violation categories. Relationships link it to unsafe chemical or waste spills, damage to road-traffic equipment, slippery substances on a roadway, illegal obstructions, and the specified alcohol-concentration violation. [Data: Entities (2216, 4741, 1344, 5273, 2524, +more); Relationships (7250, 5797, 7249, 7246, 486)]

This structure presents the violations together as categories associated with the same fine range; it does not show that they were committed by the same person or in one event. [Data: Relationships (7250, 5797, 7249, 7246, 486)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty range and legal references
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity describes a monetary penalty of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 VND for an individual or driver who commits a covered violation. It cites Article 6, Clause 6, and Article 8, Clause 7, of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (2216)]

The relationships specify the fine’s association with the five named violation categories, but the records do not provide additional details about enforcement procedures or other consequences. [Data: Relationships (7250, 5797, 7249, 7246, 486)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several covered violations concern roadway hazards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct includes discharging or spilling chemicals or waste in a way that endangers traffic safety, pouring substances that make a roadway slippery, and illegally placing or leaving obstructions on a roadway. Each is linked to the specified fine range. [Data: Entities (5273, 4741, 2524); Relationships (7250, 7249, 7246)]

These descriptions identify conduct with potential to affect roadway safety. They are categories of violations in the records, not evidence that a particular spill or obstruction occurred. [Data: Entities (5273, 4741, 2524)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Damage to traffic-control equipment is included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One covered category is destroying, damaging, or rendering ineffective road-traffic control or monitoring equipment, including smart devices used to assist traffic command and control. The associated relationship states that individuals committing this violation are subject to the 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (1344, 2216); Relationships (5797)]

The records describe the prohibited conduct and penalty association but do not identify damaged equipment, a responsible party, or an actual incident. [Data: Entities (1344); Relationships (5797)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The alcohol-concentration category has specific thresholds
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The alcohol-related violation concerns a specialized motorcycle operator driving with a blood alcohol concentration above 50 mg and up to 80 mg per 100 ml of blood, or a breath alcohol concentration above 0.25 mg and up to 0.4 mg per liter of breath. [Data: Entities (149)]

The relationship associates this defined violation with the 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 VND fine under the cited provision. The data does not establish that any operator exceeded these thresholds. [Data: Entities (149, 2216); Relationships (486)]

v.tieu_de: Ministerial Construction Inspection Team and Penalty Authority
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Inspection Team Established by the Minister of Construction and several records describing its head or leader. The records connect these role labels to the team and indicate that the head has administrative penalty authority under Articles 41 and 44, including authority to impose fines of up to 75 million Vietnamese dong under Article 44, clause 3. The officials are unnamed, and the supplied information does not describe specific enforcement actions or outcomes. [Data: Entities (2695, 2463, 2448, 2855); Relationships (7704, 7997, 7694)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it is associated with statutory administrative penalty powers, although the records provide no evidence about particular cases or real-world enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The inspection team is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Inspection Team Established by the Minister of Construction is the main organizational entity in the supplied records, with connections to descriptions of its head and leader. Its description associates the team with penalty authority under Article 41 and identifies its head as authorized under Article 44, clause 3. [Data: Entities (2695); Relationships (7704, 7997, 7694)]

The records establish a regulatory enforcement function, but do not provide details about the team’s membership, remit beyond the cited provisions, or specific inspection activity. [Data: Entities (2695)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The team’s head is associated with administrative sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions identify the head of the inspection team as an official with authority to impose administrative penalties. One record associates that authority with Article 41, while another specifies authorization under Article 44, clause 3. [Data: Entities (2463, 2448); Relationships (7704, 7694)]

The records do not name the officeholder or provide information about any individual decision, penalty, or enforcement outcome. [Data: Entities (2463, 2448)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine ceiling is 75 million Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The team’s description states that Article 44, clause 3, allows its head to impose fines of up to 75 million Vietnamese dong. This indicates a defined financial sanctioning capacity associated with the role. [Data: Entities (2695)]

The supplied information does not specify the violations to which this ceiling applies or whether the authority has been exercised in any particular case. [Data: Entities (2695)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Multiple records describe closely corresponding leadership labels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data includes entries titled “Head of the Inspection Team,” “Head of Inspection Team,” and “Leader of the Inspection Team,” each linked or described in relation to the minister-established team. [Data: Entities (2463, 2448, 2855); Relationships (7704, 7997, 7694)]

These labels appear to refer to corresponding leadership roles, but the records do not establish whether they represent one officeholder, distinct positions, or duplicate descriptions. Treating them as confirmed separate people would go beyond the available evidence. [Data: Entities (2463, 2448, 2855)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records indicate regulatory importance but provide limited operational evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The cited authority to impose administrative penalties, including the stated fine ceiling, makes the team and its leadership relevant to understanding construction-related regulatory powers. [Data: Entities (2695, 2463, 2448)]

The supplied records do not provide information about legal compliance in practice, the team’s reputation, technical capabilities, specific targets of inspections, or enforcement results. Accordingly, the community’s practical impact cannot be assessed beyond the authority described in these records. [Data: Entities (2695, 2463, 2448, 2855); Relationships (7704, 7997, 7694)]

v.tieu_de: Specialized Motorcycle Operator Training and Certification
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a road traffic law training, testing, and certification process and the establishments that carry it out. The establishments provide training and conduct testing and certification for specialized motorcycle operators, with their work subject to standards prescribed by the Minister of Construction. The available data describes a focused administrative and qualification function but does not establish whether any particular establishment complies with those standards or indicate the scale of the program. [Data: Entities (4371, 5068); Relationships (10154)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s defined role in operator training and certification, while the available records provide no evidence of broader reach, actual compliance, or adverse impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A focused training, testing, and certification process
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central process covers training specialized motorcycle operators in road traffic law, testing their knowledge, and issuing or reissuing certificates of completion. This establishes the community’s core function as a structured operator qualification process. [Data: Entities (4371)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Establishments carry out the process
phat_hien.giai_thich: Training establishments for specialized motorcycle operators are identified as the providers of training and as the bodies conducting testing and certification. The relationship record directly connects these establishments to the process. [Data: Entities (5068); Relationships (10154)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ministerial standards are part of the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: The establishments are described as subject to standards prescribed by the Minister of Construction. This indicates a stated standards framework, but the records do not identify its specific requirements or demonstrate whether an establishment meets them. [Data: Entities (5068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certification includes issuance and reissuance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The process description explicitly includes issuing or reissuing certificates of completion after training and knowledge testing. The data does not specify certificate validity periods, testing criteria, or the circumstances that prompt reissuance. [Data: Entities (4371)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available network is small and provides limited evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied community contains two entities linked by one relationship: the process and the establishments that carry it out. These records describe roles and a standards condition, but provide no information about the number of establishments, participation levels, outcomes, or actual compliance. [Data: Entities (4371, 5068); Relationships (10154)]

v.tieu_de: Article 12 Road-Traffic Provisions and Enforcement
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on “Article 12,” a label used for provisions in several different Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one unified rule. Its relationships cover road-user speed and safe-distance duties, penalties for road and sidewalk misuse, collection of road-traffic information, and other instrument-specific subjects such as cargo securing and entry into force. The records describe regulatory requirements and penalties, but do not establish actual violations, enforcement outcomes, organizational conduct, or reputational standing. [Data: Entities (243, 3419, 5335, 1076, 1810); Relationships (762, 779, 743, 752, 758)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful public-safety and regulatory importance because it links traffic duties, enforcement penalties, and information collection, although the records provide no evidence of actual incidents or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (243, 3419, 5335, 977); Relationships (762, 779, 743, 754, 757)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 12” refers to multiple distinct legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity description explicitly cautions that Article 12 refers to different provisions depending on the legal instrument. It identifies Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Law 36/2024/QH15, Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, and Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT as having different subjects. [Data: Entities (243)]

Accordingly, the connected topics should not be treated as a single, internally uniform rule. The relationships include traffic safety duties, penalties, information collection, and an “Entry into force” subject, which is specifically associated with the circular. [Data: Relationships (762, 743, 752, 744, 779)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-user speed and safe-distance duties are a central safety theme
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is described as concerning compliance with speed regulations and the required safe distance between vehicles. The relationship records also connect Article 12 to compliance with speed and distance rules. [Data: Entities (243, 1076); Relationships (744)]

Operators of specialized motorcycles are specifically required to observe speed limits and maintain a minimum safe distance from the vehicle ahead. The provided description also states that these operators must follow applicable road-traffic rules when using expressways under Article 25 of the law. [Data: Entities (3419); Relationships (762)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 includes situational driving-safety actions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify observing road conditions and reducing speed as actions required of drivers in circumstances listed in Article 12, clause 3. These are described as safety actions, not as evidence that any particular driver failed to perform them. [Data: Entities (4048, 3283); Relationships (761, 765)]

The broader Article 12 description places clause 3 within provisions concerning road-user safety requirements. The available material does not specify the circumstances in detail, so the scope of those duties should not be expanded beyond the descriptions provided. [Data: Entities (243)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Roadway and sidewalk misuse is treated as penalized conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses using roads, roadways, or sidewalks for purposes other than their intended traffic-related use. The records characterize this as a category of violation subject to penalties. [Data: Entities (5335, 5336, 5338, 4586); Relationships (779, 777, 780, 781, 770)]

The information establishes that these types of use are addressed by the cited provision, but it does not identify a specific instance, responsible party, or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (243, 5333); Relationships (779, 777)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty amounts vary by violation and category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records list fines of VND 500,000 to VND 1,000,000 for individuals and VND 1,000,000 to VND 2,000,000 for organizations for specified violations. They separately identify a VND 35,000,000 to VND 37,000,000 fine for an individual committing one of the violations described in the text. [Data: Entities (2265, 2267, 2190); Relationships (756, 757, 754)]

These amounts are attached to specified violations, and the records do not establish that they apply to every form of roadway or sidewalk misuse. They should therefore be read as distinct penalty references rather than combined into a single general tariff. [Data: Entities (243, 2190, 2265, 2267); Relationships (754, 756, 757, 779)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community also touches traffic-information collection and driver health data
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerns collecting information for the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety. A related record states that information specified in Clause 7 of Article 11 is collected under Article 12. [Data: Entities (243, 977); Relationships (743)]

The specialized-motorcycle operator description adds that operators’ health information may be held in the driver health database. The records do not provide technical details about either database, such as its systems, security controls, or operational practices. [Data: Entities (3419)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other linked subjects are instrument-specific and should remain distinct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship data connect Article 12 to violations involving the securing of transported goods, while the central description says those violations are addressed in connection with Article 47. This is a cross-reference, not evidence that cargo securing is the subject of every Article 12 provision. [Data: Entities (243, 2597); Relationships (758)]

Article 12 of Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT is identified as “Entry into force.” Its presence reinforces that the shared article number alone does not establish that the connected subjects belong to the same legal instrument or have the same function. [Data: Entities (1810, 243); Relationships (752)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal content, not actual compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships characterize legal provisions, duties, penalties, and information categories. They do not identify specific individuals or organizations as having violated the rules, nor do they report enforcement outcomes or concrete traffic incidents. [Data: Entities (243, 3419, 5335, 2190); Relationships (762, 779, 743, 754)]

The material therefore supports assessing the community as relevant to traffic regulation and public safety, but does not support conclusions about actual compliance rates, institutional performance, technical capability beyond the stated database references, or reputational standing.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Administration and Decree 168/2024
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Vietnam Road Administration and the administrative powers associated with Article 44 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The agency’s Director may establish inspection teams and delegations; the Director and designated inspection officials have authority to impose specified administrative penalties and measures. The agency is also identified as a competent authority for certain speed-sign decisions and as an agency connected to shared journey-monitoring data. The information describes regulatory responsibilities and powers, but does not establish particular enforcement actions, compliance outcomes, or reputational concerns.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial public-sector importance through road-administration responsibilities and legally defined inspection and sanctioning powers, without evidence of specific misconduct or harmful outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Vietnam Road Administration is the community’s central authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vietnam Road Administration is described as Vietnam’s national government body responsible for road administration. Its connections to the Director, Article 44, and the inspection bodies make it the organizational center of this community. [Data: Entities (5541); Relationships (5867, 2116, 7996, 7978)]

The supplied information establishes formal responsibilities and authority, not a finding about whether the agency or its officials have complied with the law in practice. No specific enforcement case or compliance outcome is provided. [Data: Entities (5541, 457)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Director combines agency leadership with statutory sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director heads the Vietnam Road Administration and is authorized under Article 44 to impose sanctions and apply specified remedial measures. The Director may also establish inspection teams and delegations, placing the office at the center of the enforcement structure described here. [Data: Entities (1387); Relationships (5867, 2112, 5866, 5865)]

The agency description states that the Director General may impose specified penalties, including fines up to 75,000,000 đồng, and confiscate exhibits or vehicles used in violations where authorized. This ceiling is distinct from the lower fine ceiling described for heads of inspection teams. [Data: Entities (5541, 1387)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection teams have delegated enforcement powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director-established inspection team is identified as an inspection body under the Vietnam Road Administration. Article 44 authorizes the team’s head or leader to impose fines up to 60,000,000 đồng and, where specified, apply remedial measures; the supplied descriptions also identify temporary permit revocation or activity suspension among available measures. [Data: Entities (2694, 2462, 2854, 457); Relationships (7996, 2115, 7703, 7995)]

These records describe the scope of legal authority, rather than proving that a particular team was formed for a specific case or exercised any of these powers. [Data: Entities (2694, 2854); Relationships (5866, 2115)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection delegations and their heads form a parallel enforcement channel
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director may establish an inspection delegation, and Article 44 identifies its head as an official with administrative sanctioning authority. The delegation head may impose fines up to 60,000,000 đồng and apply other measures specified in the Article. [Data: Entities (2687, 2445, 2459); Relationships (5865, 5863, 5864, 2113, 7978)]

The dataset contains similarly named records for the head of the inspection delegation. They all describe a leadership role associated with the delegation and statutory sanctioning authority; the records do not establish that these labels refer to separate individuals. [Data: Entities (2445, 2459); Relationships (7690, 7698)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 44 provides the legal framework for the described powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 44 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is the shared legal basis cited for the Director’s authority and the sanctioning powers of designated inspection officials. The recorded relationships connect it to the Vietnam Road Administration, the Director, the inspection team, and a delegation head. [Data: Entities (457); Relationships (2112, 2113, 2115, 2116)]

The information supports a description of authority granted by the decree, including specified fines and remedial or temporary measures. It does not include the full text of the decree or facts about how these powers have been applied in practice. [Data: Entities (457, 1387, 2694, 2687)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The agency also has road-management and monitoring-related responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vietnam Road Administration is identified as a competent authority for deciding on the placement of speed signs on specified roads within the Ministry of Transport’s management scope. It is also described as an agency with which journey-monitoring data is connected and shared. [Data: Entities (5541)]

These details indicate responsibilities extending beyond administrative penalties, but the supplied records do not specify the technical systems involved, the data’s contents, or how it is used. [Data: Entities (5541)]

v.tieu_de: Operational Speed Signs and the State of Vietnam
v.tom_tat: This community links the regulatory activity of placing operational speed signs with the State of Vietnam. The activity concerns decisions by a competent authority about where to place signs on specified roads, including cases covered by Clause 4 of Article 10. The relationship notes that enterprises are assigned by the State to manage, operate, and exploit certain expressways for which speed-sign decisions fall under the regulation. The supplied data does not identify the enterprises, roads, specific sign decisions, or any compliance or safety outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it connects speed-limit signage decisions on certain roads with state-assigned expressway management, while the available information provides no specific outcomes or evidence of harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulatory activity is the community's central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich: Placement of Operational Speed Signs is described as a regulatory activity in which a competent authority determines where operational speed-limit signs should be placed on specified roads. This identifies the subject as a decision-making process, rather than evidence that particular signs have been installed or that a specific decision has been made. [Data: Entities (3746)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulation's stated scope references Clause 4 of Article 10
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entity description says the activity applies to cases specified in Clause 4 of Article 10. The supplied data does not reproduce that clause or detail which roads or circumstances it covers, so the scope cannot be further specified from this record. [Data: Entities (3746)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The State of Vietnam is linked to expressway management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The State of Vietnam is described as assigning enterprises to manage, operate, and exploit certain expressways. The data does not name those enterprises or identify the particular expressways. [Data: Entities (4759)]

The relationship connects this state-assignment context to the speed-sign regulation, stating that the regulation covers speed-sign decisions for the expressways in question. [Data: Relationships (9630)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship connects public authority and operational responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available relationship indicates that speed-sign decisions covered by the regulation concern expressways managed, operated, and exploited by enterprises assigned by the State. This establishes a link between a regulatory decision process and state-assigned expressway responsibilities, but does not specify how authority or duties are divided among the competent authority, the State, and the enterprises. [Data: Entities (3746, 4759); Relationships (9630)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data does not establish compliance, safety outcomes, or reputational concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the regulatory activity and its connection to state-assigned expressway management, but provide no evidence about whether any entity complied with the regulation, whether signage decisions improved or worsened safety, or whether there are controversies or reputational issues. These matters therefore cannot be assessed from the supplied information. [Data: Entities (3746, 4759); Relationships (9630)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial-Level Chief Inspectors in Vietnam
v.tom_tat: This community consists of the chief inspector of a province or centrally-run city and the provincial-level administrative areas covered by a provision concerning that role. The single recorded relationship links the chief inspector to those areas. The description indicates that the inspector may impose sanctions under a stated condition, but the condition and further details of the provision are not provided.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited but relevant administrative and regulatory importance, while the available information does not establish the provision’s scope or practical effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The chief inspector is the central role
phat_hien.giai_thich: The chief inspector of a province or centrally-run city is the key official represented in this community. The entity description says this official may impose sanctions under a stated condition, but does not specify the condition or the sanctions involved. [Data: Entities (810)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision covers provincial-level administrative areas
phat_hien.giai_thich: The other entity identifies provinces and centrally-run cities as Vietnamese provincial-level administrative areas covered by the provision. The data does not name any individual province or city. [Data: Entities (3942)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationship links the role to its administrative scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: The sole recorded relationship states that the provision concerns chief inspectors serving these provincial-level areas. This establishes an administrative connection between the official role and the areas in scope, without providing further organizational or operational detail. [Data: Relationships (3173)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctioning authority is conditional but underspecified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The chief inspector’s description refers to the possibility of imposing sanctions under a stated condition. The condition, the nature of the sanctions, and the persons or entities subject to them are not identified in the available records, so the authority’s practical reach cannot be assessed. [Data: Entities (810)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a narrow assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community is represented by two entities and one relationship, all focused on the inspector role and the provincial-level areas covered by the provision. No additional records establish implementation, compliance outcomes, technical capabilities, reputation, or broader effects; conclusions on those topics would therefore go beyond the evidence provided. [Data: Entities (810, 3942); Relationships (3173)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and Road Administration Penalty Authority
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 41 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and the officials and inspection teams associated with its administrative penalty powers for road traffic order and safety violations. The decree links the Director General of the Vietnam Road Administration and an inspection team and its head to that authority; the Director General is also described as establishing inspection teams. The records establish a formal enforcement structure, but provide no information about particular enforcement actions, outcomes, or compliance in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial institutional importance because it describes statutory authority to impose administrative penalties in the area of road traffic order and safety, without evidence of specific enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 41 is the legal basis connecting the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as allocating authority to impose administrative penalties for violations concerning road traffic order and safety. It is directly linked to the Director General, an inspection team established by that official, and the team’s head as penalty-authorized roles. [Data: Entities (1278); Relationships (4894, 4899, 4897)]

The supplied records describe the decree’s stated allocation of authority, not whether particular penalties were imposed or whether enforcement complied with applicable procedures.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Director General has a central enforcement and organizational role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director General of the Vietnam Road Administration is described as having authority to impose specified administrative penalties under Article 44, and as being able to establish an inspection team or delegation. The relationships also identify the Director General as the official who established the teams represented in the records. [Data: Entities (1374); Relationships (4894, 5846, 5848)]

This combination of described sanctioning and team-establishment responsibilities places the office at the center of the community’s enforcement structure. The data do not specify the full scope of penalties or identify any individual officeholder.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection teams and their heads are authorized roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 41 lists the inspection team established by the Director General as having penalty-imposing authority, and separately grants that authority to the team’s head. The records also describe the head as authorized to impose specified administrative penalties under Article 44. [Data: Entities (2693, 2461); Relationships (4899, 4897, 7701)]

The relationships distinguish the team from its head while connecting the head to the team. The information supports the existence of these assigned roles, but does not establish the composition, activity, or decisions of any particular team.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records include parallel descriptions of an administration-established team
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Alongside the inspection team established by the Director General, the data list a “Vietnam Road Administration-established inspection team” and a corresponding team head. These entries describe the Director General as establishing the team and identify the person as its head, with the head authorized to impose specified penalties. [Data: Entities (5542, 2469); Relationships (5848, 7710)]

These descriptions closely overlap with the other team and head entries, but the records do not explicitly establish whether they refer to the same team and positions or to separate ones. They should therefore be treated as parallel representations rather than definitively separate operational units.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community represents formal enforcement capability, not evidence of enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe legal and organizational capacity to impose specified administrative penalties in the road traffic order and safety context. That capacity is attributed to the Director General, an established inspection team, and its head. [Data: Entities (1278, 1374, 2693, 2461); Relationships (4894, 4899, 4897)]

No supplied record identifies a specific violation, penalty, enforcement action, or outcome. The data therefore support assessing the community as institutionally significant, but do not support conclusions about actual compliance, enforcement effectiveness, or misconduct.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, Article 44 and Road Management Officials
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 44 of Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and officials it identifies as having authority to impose administrative penalties. The provision is linked to the Director of a Road Management Area and to the head of an inspection team established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration. A Road Management Area is described as a unit under that Administration, and its Director’s stated powers include fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, temporary permit withdrawal or activity suspension where authorized, and specified remedial measures. The supplied information describes legal authority, not its exercise or any compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (1280, 1383, 4290, 2447); Relationships (4939, 4947, 4941, 5853)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful institutional importance because Article 44 assigns administrative enforcement powers to road-management officials, but the records do not establish how those powers have been used or any resulting impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 44 is the legal center of the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 44 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as specifying which officials have authority to impose administrative penalties. Its recorded links identify both the Director of a Road Management Area and the head of a designated inspection team as authorized officials. [Data: Entities (1280); Relationships (4939, 4941, 4947)]

The records establish the provision’s stated enforcement role, but do not describe particular cases, decisions, or outcomes under it. [Data: Entities (1280); Relationships (4939, 4941, 4947)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road Management Area Director has specified sanctioning powers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Director of the Road Management Area is identified as an official authorized under Article 44 to impose administrative penalties. The described powers include fines of up to 37,500,000 đồng, temporary withdrawal of the right to use permits, temporary suspension of activities, and remedial measures specified in Article 3, Clause 3. [Data: Entities (1383, 4290); Relationships (4939, 5853)]

The descriptions frame permit withdrawal and activity suspension as powers available where authorized; they do not indicate that the Director has applied these measures in any specific instance. [Data: Entities (1383, 4290)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Road Management Area is an organizational unit under the Vietnam Road Administration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Management Area is described as an organizational unit under the Vietnam Road Administration, and its Director is described as the official who heads it. This establishes the organizational relationship between the unit and the official associated with Article 44’s penalty authority. [Data: Entities (1383, 4290); Relationships (4947, 5853)]

The records connect the unit to Article 44 because the article identifies its Director as authorized to impose specified administrative penalties. [Data: Entities (4290); Relationships (4947, 5853)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate inspection-team role is also identified as authorized
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 44 is described as granting administrative-penalty authority to the head of an inspection team established by the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration. This is a distinct official role from the Director of a Road Management Area. [Data: Entities (2447); Relationships (4941)]

The supplied records do not specify the inspection-team head’s penalty limits or detail the scope of measures available to that role, so those powers cannot be compared further with the Director’s listed authorities. [Data: Entities (2447); Relationships (4941)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports legal authority, not an assessment of enforcement conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The information provided describes the roles and powers attributed to Article 44, including a stated maximum fine and certain temporary or remedial measures for the Road Management Area Director. [Data: Entities (1280, 1383, 4290, 2447); Relationships (4939, 4941, 4947, 5853)]

It does not provide records of specific enforcement actions, compliance findings, or allegations concerning these entities. Accordingly, the community’s institutional significance is supported, while conclusions about actual conduct or compliance are not established by these records. [Data: Entities (1280, 1383, 4290, 2447); Relationships (4939, 4941, 4947, 5853)]

v.tieu_de: Provincial and Centrally Governed City Inspectorate Authority
v.tom_tat: This community concerns the chief inspector and inspectorates serving provinces or centrally governed cities. The chief inspector is linked to both jurisdictions and is described as the head of the relevant inspectorate. Under the stated condition that no Department of Transport Inspectorate has been established, the provincial or city chief inspector may impose specified, time-limited measures, including revoking permits or professional practice certificates or suspending operations. The data identifies no individual office-holder and documents no specific enforcement action or compliance finding.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s meaningful regulatory authority over permits, professional practice certificates, and operations, balanced against the conditional scope of that authority and the absence of evidence about any specific action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The chief inspector is the community’s central authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Chief Inspector of a Province or Centrally Governed City is the central entity in the network: the relationships connect this office to both provincial and centrally governed city jurisdictions, as well as to the relevant inspectorate. The office is described as authorized to apply specified remedial measures under stated circumstances. [Data: Entities (809); Relationships (3169, 3063, 3170)]

The data refers to an office rather than a named person, so it supports describing the role and its institutional connections, but not identifying who currently holds it. [Data: Entities (809)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority spans two types of administrative jurisdiction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described chief inspector may serve in a province or a centrally governed city. The relationships expressly connect the chief-inspector role with both jurisdiction types, indicating that the community’s described structure is not limited to one of them. [Data: Entities (3937, 756, 809); Relationships (3169, 3063)]

A centrally governed city is described as governed directly by the central government. The provided data does not identify a particular province or city. [Data: Entities (756, 3937)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The remedial powers are conditional and time-limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provincial or centrally governed city chief inspector is described as able, when no Department of Transport Inspectorate has been established, to revoke permits or professional practice certificates for a fixed period, or suspend operations for a fixed period. This indicates consequential regulatory powers, but the condition and stated time limits are important qualifications. [Data: Entities (3965)]

The information describes potential authority; it does not establish that a permit, certificate, or operation has actually been affected. [Data: Entities (3965)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The chief inspector heads the relevant inspectorate
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships identify the chief inspector as the head of the relevant provincial or centrally governed city inspectorate. The inspectorate is therefore part of the institutional structure associated with the office, rather than a separately described enforcement actor with additional powers in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (3966, 809); Relationships (3170)]

The records also connect the provincial or city chief inspector role to both province and centrally governed city settings. [Data: Entities (3965); Relationships (9770, 3064)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data does not establish compliance outcomes or misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe an office, its jurisdictional links, and conditional remedial authority. They do not provide a named office-holder, an account of a particular enforcement decision, or evidence of a legal violation or compliance outcome. Accordingly, the community’s regulatory significance can be assessed, but no conclusion about actual conduct or compliance is supported. [Data: Entities (809, 3965, 3966); Relationships (3169, 3063, 3170)]

v.tieu_de: Confiscation Authority in Vietnam’s Traffic Police
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the administrative confiscation of exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations, with links to specified Traffic Police Department division heads and a provincial chief inspector. The information describes different officials’ authority and identifies a 105,000,000-VND limit for the provincial chief inspector, while also noting a 75,000,000-VND limit elsewhere without explaining how the two limits apply. The material indicates a defined administrative enforcement function, but does not provide case examples or further detail on the circumstances governing each official’s authority. [Data: Entities (1085, 3961, 2451, 2454, 2456); Relationships (3903, 3904, 3905, 3908, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to administrative enforcement and asset confiscation, while the supplied information is limited to the stated authority and does not describe actual enforcement cases or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Confiscation is the community’s central administrative sanction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is the confiscation of exhibits and vehicles used in an administrative violation, described as an administrative penalty authorized for specified transport-sector officials under Article 44, Clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (1085)]

The sanction connects to the provincial chief inspector and three named Traffic Police Department division-head roles, making it the organizing point for the community’s relationships. The supplied information describes authority to impose the sanction, not specific instances of its use. [Data: Relationships (3903, 3904, 3905, 3908)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial chief inspector has a stated value limit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provincial chief inspector is described as able to confiscate exhibits and vehicles when their value does not exceed 105,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, subject to specified circumstances. The relationship record likewise connects this official to the confiscation sanction within a specified value limit and circumstances. [Data: Entities (3961); Relationships (3908)]

The provided material does not detail those circumstances or identify any enforcement action by a provincial chief inspector. Accordingly, the evidence establishes a described scope of authority, but not how it has been applied in practice. [Data: Entities (3961); Relationships (3908)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three Traffic Police Department division heads are included among authorized officials
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed roles include the heads of the divisions responsible for propaganda, investigation, and traffic accident resolution; training, testing, and driver-licence management; and vehicle registration and inspection. The relationships identify each of these role-holders among officials authorized to confiscate exhibits and vehicles involved in administrative violations. [Data: Entities (2451, 2454, 2456); Relationships (3903, 3904, 3905)]

The descriptions do not specify value limits or detailed conditions for these three division heads. The evidence therefore supports their inclusion among authorized officials, but does not establish that their authority is identical in scope to that of the provincial chief inspector. [Data: Entities (2451, 2454, 2456); Relationships (3903, 3904, 3905)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two division-head roles are explicitly linked to their divisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies a professional division for guidance on propaganda, investigation, and traffic accident resolution, and a division for guidance, training, testing, and driver-licence management. Each division is connected to a corresponding head role. [Data: Entities (1426, 1431, 2451, 2454); Relationships (5919, 5931)]

These links clarify the organizational context of two authorized roles. Although the vehicle-registration-and-inspection head is also listed as authorized, the supplied relationships do not identify a corresponding division entity for that role. [Data: Entities (2456); Relationships (3905, 5919, 5931)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated confiscation value limits are not fully reconciled
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central sanction description gives two value limits—75,000,000 and 105,000,000 Vietnamese đồng—and explicitly says the descriptions do not explain how they differ. It states that the applicable limit depends on the relevant provision or official’s authority. [Data: Entities (1085)]

The provincial chief inspector’s description specifies a ceiling of 105,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, but the supplied information does not assign the 75,000,000-VND limit to a particular official or provision. This unresolved distinction limits what can be concluded about the precise scope of each role’s authority. [Data: Entities (1085, 3961); Relationships (3908)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger-Vehicle Traffic Violations and Badge Revocation
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a driver of a passenger vehicle and a traffic-safety violation involving allowing passengers to board or alight while the vehicle is moving. The driver is linked to the violation and to a possible vehicle-badge revocation when the badge is expired or was not issued by a competent authority. The records describe a specific regulatory enforcement scenario, but do not establish how often it occurs or whether any particular driver has been penalized.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is limited to moderate because the records describe a specific traffic-safety violation and a conditional administrative consequence, without evidence of broader activity or realized harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driver is the community's central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich: The driver of a passenger vehicle has the highest listed entity degree and is linked to both the described conduct and the traffic-safety violation. This makes the driver the connecting point in the community's regulatory relationships. [Data: Entities (1466); Relationships (513, 6061, 6062)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The conduct concerns passenger boarding or alighting while moving
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify allowing passengers to board or leave a passenger vehicle while it is moving as the specific conduct at issue. The relationship states that this violation is attributed to the driver. [Data: Entities (162, 1466); Relationships (513)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is framed as a public-order and traffic-safety matter
phat_hien.giai_thich: A separate entity describes the matter as a violation of public-order and traffic-safety regulations, and the relationship identifies the driver as the person who commits the described violation. The supplied information does not specify additional circumstances, such as where or when the conduct occurred. [Data: Entities (5573, 1466); Relationships (6062)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Badge revocation is conditional
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records state that a driver committing a violation specified in Clause 7 may have a vehicle badge revoked when that badge has expired or was not issued by a competent authority. This describes a possible consequence under stated conditions, not a confirmed revocation in an individual case. [Data: Entities (5370, 1466); Relationships (6061)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes a narrow regulatory scenario
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records cover one category of driver, one described passenger-safety violation, a broader traffic-safety classification, and a conditional badge consequence. They provide no evidence about particular cases, enforcement frequency, outcomes, or the broader reach of the provision, so the community's demonstrated impact should be assessed cautiously. [Data: Entities (1466, 162, 5370, 5573); Relationships (513, 6061, 6062)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Return and Special Commercial Economic Zones
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a remedial measure, Required Return of Vehicles, and the Special Commercial Economic Zone to which a vehicle may be directed. The relationship describes an administrative mechanism, but no specific zone, vehicle, authority, jurisdiction, or implementation details are identified. The available information does not establish whether the measure is being applied or whether any compliance issue has occurred.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited evidenced impact because it describes a potentially consequential administrative measure but provides no specific zone, case, implementation details, or documented compliance issue.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required return is described as a remedial measure
phat_hien.giai_thich: Required Return of Vehicles is defined as a remedial measure requiring a vehicle to return to a special commercial economic zone or an international border-gate economic zone. The description establishes the nature of the measure but does not specify the circumstances in which it would be imposed. [Data: Entities (4163)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The economic zone is the stated destination
phat_hien.giai_thich: The Special Commercial Economic Zone is described as a type of economic zone referenced in the decree, and vehicles may be registered to operate there. The record does not identify a particular zone or provide its location or operator. [Data: Entities (4678)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The two entities are directly linked
phat_hien.giai_thich: The relationship records that a required return may direct a vehicle to a special commercial economic zone. This links the remedial measure to the zone as a possible destination, without establishing that any specific vehicle has been ordered to return. [Data: Relationships (9940)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available description permits more than one destination type
phat_hien.giai_thich: The measure’s entity description names both a special commercial economic zone and an international border-gate economic zone as possible destinations. The recorded relationship, however, specifically describes return to a special commercial economic zone; the supplied information does not elaborate on how the destination is selected. [Data: Entities (4163); Relationships (9940)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific compliance case or operational details are provided
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe a measure and a category of economic zone, but identify no individual vehicle, responsible authority, enforcement action, or outcome. They therefore do not support conclusions about actual compliance, violations, legal disputes, or the measure’s practical effects. [Data: Entities (4163, 4678); Relationships (9940)]

v.tieu_de: Article 44 and the Specialized Inspectorate
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 44, described primarily as a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning administrative sanctioning authority. Its relationships connect the article to the Specialized Inspectorate, specialized inspectors, and personnel assigned to specialized inspection duties. The supplied descriptions assign these officials powers while on duty, including certain sanctions, remedial measures, and confiscation authority; one description attributes Article 44 to a different law, creating an unresolved numbering or source discrepancy. The information indicates regulatory and administrative significance, but provides no evidence of misconduct or of particular enforcement actions.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it concerns officials’ administrative sanctioning and enforcement powers, while the data provide no evidence of misuse or specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 44 is the community’s legal and relational center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 44 is primarily described as a provision of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning who may impose administrative penalties. Its direct relationships identify the Specialized Inspectorate, specialized inspectors, persons assigned to specialized inspection duties, and a specialized inspector as relevant to those powers. [Data: Entities (455); Relationships (2103, 2100, 2104, 2102)]

The entity description also notes a conflicting association with Law 36/2024/QH15 and road traffic order and safety. The provided information does not resolve whether this is a source or numbering discrepancy, so the Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP attribution is best treated as the primary description rather than as an independently verified conclusion. [Data: Entities (455)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Specialized Inspectorate provides the institutional framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Specialized Inspectorate is described as the authority under which specialized inspectors and assigned personnel conduct inspection work. Article 44 is linked to the inspectorate’s sanctioning role, while relationships connect the inspectorate to inspectors and personnel carrying out specialized duties. [Data: Entities (4688); Relationships (2103, 10439, 9609, 9608, 8002)]

This structure indicates an administrative chain connecting the legal provision to an inspection authority and its personnel. The supplied records describe roles and powers, but do not identify particular cases, operational outcomes, or evidence of noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctioning powers are tied to official inspection duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions specify that specialized inspectors and persons assigned to specialized inspection duties may exercise sanctioning authority while performing their official functions. The relationships likewise connect Article 44 to those groups’ authority and link assigned personnel to the Specialized Inspectorate. [Data: Entities (3718, 4689); Relationships (2100, 2104, 9609, 9610)]

The records therefore frame these powers as duty-bound rather than general authority outside inspection work. They do not provide details about procedures, appeals, or how the powers have been applied in practice.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records specify a limited fine amount for certain personnel
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions state that specialized inspectors and personnel assigned to specialized inspection duties may impose fines of up to 500,000 Vietnamese đồng under Article 44, clause 1. The relationship records associate both groups with the Article’s sanctioning authority. [Data: Entities (4689, 3716); Relationships (2104, 2100)]

This stated amount is specific to the described personnel and clause. The supplied material does not establish whether other officials have different fine limits, or provide additional details about the scope of offenses to which this limit applies.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Confiscation and remedial measures are part of the described authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describe authority for specialized inspectors or a specialized inspector on official duty to confiscate qualifying objects or vehicles used in administrative violations, subject to a stated value limit. A separate description says Article 44, clause 2 grants the Chief Inspector of the Department of Transport power to confiscate items or means in connection with these powers. [Data: Entities (4687, 4688); Relationships (2102)]

Inspectors are also described as authorized to apply remedial measures specified in the decree. The records do not state the value limit or enumerate those remedial measures, so their precise extent cannot be assessed from this information. [Data: Entities (2697, 4688)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No evidence of enforcement outcomes or wrongdoing is provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe legal roles and powers, including penalties, remedial measures, and confiscation, but contain no account of a particular inspection, sanction, confiscation, or alleged abuse. The relationships are about authority and organizational roles rather than documented enforcement events. [Data: Entities (455, 4688, 3718, 4689, 4687); Relationships (2103, 10439, 2100, 2104, 2102)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is grounded in the administrative powers described, not in any demonstrated harmful conduct. The provided information is insufficient to assess actual compliance, implementation, or the consequences of particular decisions.

v.tieu_de: Article 38 Decree 168/2024/ND-CP Vehicle Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 38 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND. The provision connects that penalty to three described vehicle-related violations: using an unauthorized control badge, driving without a valid control badge, and failing to meet urban vehicle sanitation requirements. The records describe regulatory requirements and penalties, but do not establish that any specific driver committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes a specific legal provision and monetary penalties for several vehicle-operation violations, while providing no evidence of actual cases or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 38 is the community’s central legal provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 38 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as specifying fines for drivers of vehicles registered to operate in designated economic zones. It is directly linked to the stated fine and to the two control-badge violations, making it the central node in the community’s regulatory structure. [Data: Entities (422); Relationships (1795, 1798, 1794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The specified penalty is 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND for the covered violations. Article 38 is linked to this penalty, and the penalty is separately linked to each of the three listed violation types. The records do not provide information about enforcement frequency or actual fines imposed. [Data: Entities (2213); Relationships (1795, 7243, 6507, 6952)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized control badges are a listed violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: Using a control badge not issued by a competent authority is described as a punishable violation under Article 38. The stated fine applies to this conduct; the source material does not indicate that any particular driver used such a badge. [Data: Entities (5361); Relationships (1798, 7243)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving without a valid prescribed badge is also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community distinguishes driving without the prescribed control badge from using an unauthorized one. The former category includes operating a covered vehicle without the badge or with an expired badge, and it is linked to Article 38 and the same fine range. [Data: Entities (1693, 2213); Relationships (1794, 6507)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Urban vehicle sanitation requirements form a separate violation category
phat_hien.giai_thich: Operating a vehicle in an urban area without meeting the required sanitation standards for circulation is included among the conduct carrying the specified fine. The records link this violation to the penalty, but do not identify particular sanitation standards or document any specific instance of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (1993, 2213); Relationships (6952)]

v.tieu_de: Department of Transport and Its Inspectorate
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Department of Transport, its associated Department of Transport Inspectorate, and the Chief Inspector who heads the inspectorate and exercises enforcement powers. The described powers include fines, temporary restrictions on permits or operations, confiscation within a stated value limit, and remedial measures. The inspectorate’s establishment is described as conditional, and the Chief Inspector is also linked to the sanctioning authority of the Specialized Transport Inspectorate.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has notable public impact because it describes government transport-enforcement authority capable of imposing financial penalties and restricting permits or operations, although the records do not establish that these powers were exercised.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Department and inspectorate form the community’s institutional core
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department of Transport is described as a provincial or municipal government department, with the Department of Transport Inspectorate identified as its associated inspection body. The relationship record further states that the inspectorate belongs to the department, while noting that its establishment may be uncertain under the applicable provision. [Data: Entities (1337, 1338); Relationships (5786)]

This places the community within a government transport-administration context. The records describe institutional roles and powers, not particular enforcement actions or findings of noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Chief Inspector is the central enforcement official
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Chief Inspector is described as heading the Department of Transport Inspectorate and as an official of the Department of Transport. A separate relationship identifies the Chief Inspector as exercising the sanctioning authority of the Specialized Transport Inspectorate. [Data: Entities (811); Relationships (3177, 3179)]

The role therefore connects the department’s inspectorate structure to the enforcement powers described in the records. The information identifies the office and its authority, but does not name an officeholder or show that any specific power has been used.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Available sanctions can restrict permits or operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Chief Inspector may revoke, for a fixed period, the right to use permits or professional certificates, or suspend operations for a fixed period. These are administrative measures that can directly affect the ability to conduct transport-related activity. [Data: Entities (811, 1338)]

The records describe these as authorized sanctions under the cited provisions. They do not specify the circumstances of a particular case, the duration of any actual restriction, or whether a sanction has been imposed.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records specify financial and confiscation limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department of Transport’s Chief Inspector is described as authorized to impose fines of up to 37,500,000 Vietnamese đồng. The Chief Inspector may also confiscate exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1337, 811)]

These stated limits indicate the scope of the enforcement authority described in the source material. The records do not provide examples of fines or confiscations, nor do they establish how frequently these powers are applied.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The inspectorate’s establishment is conditional in the described provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department of Transport Inspectorate is associated with the Department of Transport, but the records say its establishment may depend on circumstances in the applicable provision and identify a situation in which it has not been established. [Data: Entities (1338, 1337); Relationships (5786)]

This qualification matters when interpreting the institutional structure: the records do not establish that every Department of Transport has an operating inspectorate. They describe the Chief Inspector’s authority in connection with the relevant provisions, rather than confirming the inspectorate’s status in any particular locality.

v.tieu_de: Cargo-Transport Traffic Violations and Administrative Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community describes a regulatory framework connecting a cargo-transport road-traffic violation to an administrative penalty under Article 21 and to withdrawal of certain vehicle badges. An authorized official decides whether to impose the penalty, with a stated exception for certain paperwork violations when documents or integrated information are presented within the appointed period. The records describe rules and possible consequences, not a specific violation or enforcement case. [Data: Entities (80, 716, 618, 5642); Relationships (185, 186, 2995)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns enforceable road-safety requirements and potential penalties, but the records describe a narrow regulatory framework rather than a specific incident or broader pattern. [Data: Entities (80, 716); Relationships (186, 2995)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative penalties are the framework's central consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An administrative penalty is described as a sanction imposed by an authorized official for covered violations of road-traffic, public-order, or traffic-safety regulations. The stated scope includes environmental-protection rules, vehicle-condition requirements, dangerous-goods transport regulations, and specified offenses under cited provisions. [Data: Entities (80)]

The penalty is distinct from additional consequences that may apply to the same violation, including driver’s-license point deductions, vehicle-registration certificate revocation, or remedial measures. The data establish potential regulatory consequences, not that any particular person or organization has received them. [Data: Entities (80)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-transport violations are expressly linked to an administrative penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The cargo-transport road-traffic violation is defined as a breach of road-order and safety regulations by a driver operating a truck, tractor, or similar vehicle used to transport goods. [Data: Entities (716)]

The relationship record states that the specified violation is subject to an administrative penalty under Article 21. It does not provide details about a particular driver, incident, penalty amount, or enforcement outcome. [Data: Relationships (186)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An authorized official has a decision-making role, with a paperwork exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authorized official is empowered under the cited rules to decide whether to impose an administrative penalty for a paperwork violation. The relationship record further states that the specified penalty is not issued for that paperwork violation when the required documents or their integrated information are presented within the appointed period. [Data: Entities (618); Relationships (185)]

The entity description also says the official may temporarily seize a vehicle and related documents to prevent an administrative violation. The records do not specify how often this authority is used or identify any particular official or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (618)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certain vehicle-badge violations can lead to badge withdrawal
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver who commits the specified violation is subject to withdrawal of a vehicle badge that has expired or was not issued by a competent authority. The relationship connects this consequence to the cargo-transport road-traffic violation, while the entity description identifies the relevant provision as Article 21. [Data: Entities (5642); Relationships (2995)]

This is a described regulatory consequence rather than evidence that a badge was withdrawn in a specific case. The available records do not state the duration or further operational effects of withdrawal. [Data: Entities (5642); Relationships (2995)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records outline rules, not a documented enforcement case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community consists of descriptions of a violation category, possible administrative and badge-related consequences, and an official’s authority. The supplied relationships connect those regulatory concepts but do not identify an individual, vehicle, organization, date, or completed enforcement action. [Data: Entities (80, 716, 618, 5642); Relationships (185, 186, 2995)]

Accordingly, the information supports assessing the framework’s potential compliance and enforcement significance, but not determining whether a violation occurred or whether a penalty or badge withdrawal was actually imposed. [Data: Entities (80, 716, 5642); Relationships (186, 2995)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Violation and Odometer Correction
v.tom_tat: This small community links a road-traffic rule violation attributed to a vehicle owner with a remedial odometer-reading correction. The relationship states that when the specified violation involves a falsified odometer reading, the displayed mileage must be corrected. The data provides no further case, enforcement, or outcome details.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the records describe a specific traffic-compliance issue and remedy, but provide no evidence of broader scale, enforcement, or realized impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community centers on a category of road-traffic rule violation committed by a vehicle owner, described as addressed in Article 32 of a decree. The supplied information does not identify a particular owner or case. [Data: Entities (4552)]
