[Data: Entities (444, 79, 4015); Relationships (1983, 1997, 1987, 1996)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 41 has two distinct legal meanings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data cautions that “Article 41” refers to provisions in two instruments and that they should not be conflated. Article 41 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns which officials may impose administrative penalties for specified road-traffic violations; Article 41 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 concerns technical safety and environmental protection requirements for covered vehicles and parts. [Data: Entities (444)]

The relationships reflect both branches: Article 41 connects to police sanctioning authority and also to quality inspection, production, importation, and assembly requirements. This dual structure is central to interpreting the community accurately. [Data: Relationships (1983, 1997, 1987, 1996, 1977)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decree assigns enforcement powers to several police roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The enforcement network includes commune-level police chiefs, police post chiefs, police station chiefs, and chiefs of police stations at border gates or in export-processing zones. Their authority is described as applying to specified road-traffic violations and being bounded by their assigned functions and duties. [Data: Entities (1033, 663, 3816, 3811, 953); Relationships (1983, 1978, 1995, 1994, 1981)]

Article 41 is also linked to road inspectors and personnel assigned specialized road-inspection duties, likewise acting within their assigned remit. The framework therefore describes a distributed authorization structure rather than authority vested in a single office. [Data: Relationships (1999, 1990); Entities (4282, 3719)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctioning authority is limited to specified violations and assigned duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records characterize the powers as applying to particular road-traffic order and safety violations referenced in specified provisions, rather than as unrestricted authority over all violations. Article 41(4) is associated with named police roles, while other clauses and points of the cited provisions identify covered offenses. [Data: Entities (953, 4725, 3794, 980); Relationships (1981, 1993, 1991, 1992, 1980)]

The administrative-penalty framework is described as setting out penalties, remedial measures, and the officials authorized to prepare violation records and impose penalties. The available data does not provide a complete offense-by-offense schedule, so the precise applicable sanction cannot be determined from this community alone. [Data: Entities (79); Relationships (216, 176)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described measures include fines, seizure, and other remedies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain officials, the records describe authority to issue warnings or fines and apply authorized remedial measures. They also describe seizure of objects or vehicles used in administrative violations when their value does not exceed 5,000,000 đồng, subject to the cited authority. [Data: Entities (1033, 663, 3811, 4633); Relationships (3636, 2880, 9685)]

The specific scope depends on role and legal provision. For example, the border-gate or export-processing-zone station chief is described as having authority to impose fines up to 2,500,000 đồng under Article 43, Clause 3, as well as the specified seizure power. [Data: Entities (663); Relationships (1978, 2880)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The commune-level fine limits are presented with differing figures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The commune-level police chief description cites a maximum fine of 37,500,000 đồng in one context and a maximum of 2,500,000 đồng under Article 43, Clause 3 in another. The same record says the applicable limit depends on the governing provision, so these figures should not be treated as a single, interchangeable ceiling. [Data: Entities (1033)]

A separate commune-level police description also cites fines up to 37,500,000 đồng and refers to confiscation authority under Article 43, Clause 4. The supplied records do not resolve which ceiling applies to any particular violation; that requires identifying the governing authority and provision. [Data: Entities (1031, 1033); Relationships (3621, 3636)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The law branch addresses vehicle safety and environmental quality
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 41 description identifies technical safety and environmental protection requirements for motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor-vehicle parts during importation, manufacture, and assembly. The associated relationships connect the provision to quality inspection and each of these stages. [Data: Entities (444, 4015, 3898, 590, 2565); Relationships (1997, 1987, 1996, 1977)]

The records establish that these are regulatory requirements and inspection-related subjects, but they do not specify technical test methods, standards, inspection results, or the capabilities of particular manufacturers or inspectors. [Data: Entities (4015, 444)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified display and research contexts are described as exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies scientific research and research serving production as exceptions to the stated inspection requirements for specified parts. It also describes vehicles displayed or introduced at trade fairs and commercial exhibitions as exempt from the requirements described in the provision. [Data: Entities (4624, 4174, 4980, 1015, 4981); Relationships (2000, 1998, 2001, 1982, 2002)]

These exceptions are described in relation to the vehicle-quality branch of Article 41; they should not be confused with the decree’s separate rules on administrative sanctioning. The data does not elaborate on the conditions or procedures for applying the exceptions. [Data: Entities (444); Relationships (1982, 2000, 2002)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal authority, not institutional conduct or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community data documents relationships among legal provisions, police roles, administrative penalties, and vehicle inspection requirements. It does not provide case outcomes, enforcement statistics, evidence of compliance or noncompliance, allegations of misconduct, or public-reputation assessments. [Data: Entities (444, 79, 4015); Relationships (1983, 1997, 216)]

Accordingly, the community is significant as a regulatory framework, but the supplied information does not support conclusions about how consistently the rules are enforced or whether the entities have caused particular harms. [Data: Entities (79, 1031, 444)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Dangerous-Goods Transport Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 23 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as described in the data, which connects dangerous-goods transportation violations to penalties and possible driver’s-license point deductions. It also identifies a fine of 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for transporting dangerous goods without a valid permit, with an expired permit, or contrary to permit conditions, subject to a stated exception. A related but distinct set of Article 20 records concerns specified violations by drivers of passenger-carrying vehicles and a two-point deduction. The material describes legal provisions and possible sanctions, not actual violations by identified drivers or operators.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the community concerns consequential traffic-safety enforcement measures, but the data establishes legal provisions rather than actual violations or their real-world scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 23 is the central link for dangerous-goods enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
In the relationships provided, Article 23 connects the dangerous-goods transportation violation to penalties and driver’s-license point deductions. The entity description specifies that this is Article 23 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which lists violations and sanctions for specified conduct by car drivers transporting dangerous goods. [Data: Entities (325, 5574); Relationships (1284, 1287, 1289, 9502)]

The entity named “Article 23” is not unique across the cited legal instruments: the data also describes Article 23 provisions in Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and Law No. 36/2024/QH15. Accordingly, conclusions about dangerous-goods penalties apply to the Decree 168 provision, not automatically to every provision called Article 23. [Data: Entities (325)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit-related dangerous-goods violations carry a specified fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described violation covers transporting dangerous goods without a valid permit, with an expired permit, or contrary to permit conditions. The stated fine is 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, subject to the exception cited in Article 20, clause 6, point a. [Data: Entities (5206, 2141, 305); Relationships (7137, 1146)]

The source material describes this as a prescribed administrative consequence; it does not identify a particular transporter, establish that a violation occurred, or indicate that a fine was imposed in any case. [Data: Entities (5206, 2141)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point deductions are possible, but should not be assumed for every violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records associate Article 23 with deduction of points from the license of an operator who commits a specified violation, and connect such deductions to dangerous-goods transportation violations. The description does not establish that every violation covered by the relevant provisions results in a deduction. [Data: Entities (1527, 325, 5574); Relationships (1284, 6210)]

The data separately specifies a two-point deduction for certain violations listed under Article 20. That amount should not be generalized to Article 23’s dangerous-goods provisions, for which the supplied descriptions do not state a specific number of points. [Data: Entities (5179, 4728, 325); Relationships (6265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20 forms a related but distinct enforcement strand
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes drivers of passenger-carrying vehicles, specified traffic violations under Article 20, and a two-point driver’s-license deduction for the listed violations. The relationships connect these drivers to the specified violations and to the two-point consequence. [Data: Entities (1546, 4728, 5179); Relationships (6264, 6265)]

These Article 20 records provide context for the exception referenced in the dangerous-goods fine, but they do not establish that every passenger-vehicle violation is a dangerous-goods violation or that the two-point deduction applies to the Article 23 conduct. [Data: Entities (305, 325, 5179); Relationships (1146, 6265)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The information supports regulatory significance, not a finding of actual noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe penalties, fine amounts, permit-related conduct, and possible license-point consequences. They therefore indicate that compliance with dangerous-goods transportation rules can have financial and licensing implications for drivers or vehicle operators. [Data: Entities (3634, 5206, 2141, 5574); Relationships (9502, 7137, 6210)]

No case-specific evidence is supplied about an actual driver, operator, enforcement action, injury, or pattern of violations. The community’s significance should therefore be understood as regulatory and potential, rather than as evidence of demonstrated misconduct or an established operational incident. [Data: Entities (325, 5206, 5574)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Vehicle Inspection and Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 40 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and a stated administrative fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 VND. Article 40 is linked to vehicle inspection noncompliance, motor vehicle components, and specialized motorcycle inspection activities; the fine is also linked to oversized-cargo transport and specified motorcycle road-traffic violations. The information describes regulatory scope and penalties, but does not establish enforcement outcomes, technical capabilities, or the identity or conduct of particular organizations or individuals. [Data: Entities (438, 2228, 3261, 3501, 3177, +more); Relationships (1945, 7268, 7269, 7267, 1948, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns vehicle inspection and road-traffic compliance with a substantial stated fine, but provides no evidence of specific enforcement outcomes or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40 establishes the inspection-regulation framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting penalties for violations of rules governing inspections of motor vehicles, specialized-use motorcycles, and motor vehicle components or parts. It is therefore the principal regulatory reference point in this community. [Data: Entities (438); Relationships (1946, 1948, 1949)]

The supplied information describes the regulation’s subject matter and penalty relationships, but does not provide a broader account of the decree, its administration, or actual compliance rates. [Data: Entities (438); Relationships (1945, 1948)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 VND
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central penalty entity specifies an administrative fine ranging from 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese dong. Article 40(1) is linked to this amount for an individual committing the described violation. [Data: Entities (2228); Relationships (1945)]

The fine is also linked in the relationship records to vehicle-inspection noncompliance, oversized-cargo transport, and specified motorcycle road-traffic violations. The records do not explain how these different violation categories relate to one another or provide additional details about circumstances affecting the amount. [Data: Relationships (7268, 7269, 7267)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection noncompliance concerns procedures and technical standards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Noncompliance with vehicle inspection rules is described as failing to follow applicable procedures and technical standards when certifying or inspecting motor vehicles, specialized-use motorcycles, or vehicle parts. Article 40(1) is linked to this noncompliance as a violation subject to a penalty. [Data: Entities (3261); Relationships (1948, 7268)]

A separate relationship connects motor vehicle certification to the described noncompliance, specifically identifying failure to follow procedures and standards during certification. The data do not identify a particular inspection provider, vehicle, or instance of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (3097, 3261); Relationships (9017)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40 includes components and specialized motorcycle inspections
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor vehicle components are explicitly included in Article 40’s inspection-related subject matter. The article is also linked to violations of rules governing specialized motorcycle inspection activities. [Data: Entities (3098, 4701); Relationships (1946, 1949)]

These links indicate that the regulatory scope described is not limited to inspection of whole motor vehicles. However, the records provide no technical specifications, testing methods, or details about the inspections themselves. [Data: Entities (438, 3098, 4701); Relationships (1946, 1949)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is linked to separate road-traffic violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records link the 8,000,000-to-10,000,000 VND fine to oversized-cargo transport, described as carrying goods beyond a size limit specified in a circulation permit, and to specified motorcycle conduct. [Data: Entities (2228, 3501, 3177); Relationships (7269, 7267)]

The motorcycle conduct described includes weaving or swerving on a road, or dragging a kickstand or another object while moving. These are presented as fine-linked violations, but the provided information does not give enforcement examples or clarify their relationship to Article 40’s inspection provisions. [Data: Entities (3177); Relationships (7267)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam People’s Public Security and Mobile Police
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s People’s Public Security, with Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP describing administrative sanctioning powers across the force. The Mobile Police, district-level police, and social-order departments are connected to that framework, with authority assigned to officials at different levels and, in some cases, limited by fine or confiscation thresholds. The records also associate the force with road-traffic enforcement, legal-knowledge checks, and driver-training and certification databases. These materials establish significant institutional and enforcement importance, but do not document actual compliance outcomes, misconduct, or reputational assessments.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community rates highly for impact because it encompasses a national law-enforcement force and multiple subordinate units and officials with defined administrative enforcement powers.

phat_hien.tom_tat: People’s Public Security is the community’s institutional center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
People’s Public Security is described as Vietnam’s public security and law-enforcement force, and multiple entities—including the Mobile Police, district-level police, and social-order departments—are connected to it as units or authorities within its sanctioning structure. This makes it the principal organizational hub in the supplied network. [Data: Entities (3673, 3688, 3039); Relationships (8961, 2073, 5911, 5765, 5772)]

The records describe formal functions and statutory powers rather than operational performance. They therefore support a finding of institutional significance, but not conclusions about the force’s effectiveness or its conduct in particular cases. [Data: Entities (3673, 3688); Relationships (2073, 9545, 9546)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 43 defines a broad, tiered administrative-sanctioning framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is identified as the provision governing the sanctioning authority of People’s Public Security personnel and units. The records associate it with officers on duty, district-level police chiefs, department directors, police-team leaders, and Mobile Police commanders at several organizational levels. [Data: Entities (451, 454, 3679, 1415); Relationships (2073, 2074, 5911, 545, 2065)]

The described powers include imposing fines and, for designated officials, confiscating objects or vehicles, applying remedial measures, temporarily revoking permits or certificates, or suspending operations. The records specify that these powers depend on the official’s role and applicable limits; they do not establish that every official holds every listed power. [Data: Entities (3673, 3039, 1323, 1011); Relationships (2086, 2088, 2073)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Mobile Police have distinct powers at multiple command levels
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Mobile Police are described as a unit within People’s Public Security and as having authority to sanction specified road-traffic order and safety violations when acting within assigned functions. Their commanders and subordinate unit leaders are separately identified in the sanctioning framework. [Data: Entities (3039, 1011, 3041, 1034, 4060); Relationships (8961, 8962, 538, 532, 535)]

The supplied descriptions give examples of differentiated limits: a company-level commander may impose fines up to 15,000,000 đồng, a battalion commander up to 2,500,000 đồng, and the Mobile Police commander up to 75,000,000 đồng. They also describe value limits for confiscation in some roles. These figures are reported as stated in the supplied records, whose references to legal instruments should be checked against authoritative current texts before operational use. [Data: Entities (3039, 1034, 3041); Relationships (8962, 2831, 7674, 8966)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Social-order departments form a specialized enforcement branch
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department for Administrative Management of Social Order and the Department of Administrative Police for Social Order are linked to People’s Public Security. The records identify directors and professional-division heads as officials with sanctioning authority under Article 43. [Data: Entities (1321, 1323, 1325, 1377, 1379); Relationships (5761, 5765, 5772, 5762, 5773)]

The department descriptions include powers such as imposing specified sanctions and, for designated directors, confiscating exhibits or vehicles and applying specified remedial measures. Specialist divisions are also identified, including divisions concerned with conditional-business sectors and seals, and with weapons, explosives, support tools, and fireworks. [Data: Entities (1323, 1418, 1421); Relationships (5759, 5760, 5764, 5763)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network connects enforcement to road-traffic education and records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions associate People’s Public Security with road-traffic enforcement and with legal-knowledge checks concerning road-traffic order and safety. Commissioned and noncommissioned officers are specifically connected to the checking task. [Data: Entities (3673, 2883, 3674, 3676); Relationships (8553, 8554, 8555)]

The records also identify driver training and road-traffic law refresher certification as activities within People’s Public Security and describe a related database managed by the Ministry of Public Security. This points to an administrative and information-management role in addition to enforcement, but the supplied data do not specify the database’s contents, access controls, or security arrangements. [Data: Entities (3673, 1490); Relationships (6118)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A listed 2026 amendment is linked to the sanctioning framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The network includes an entity describing Article 14 of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP as amending Article 43, and relationships connect that amendment to People’s Public Security, the Mobile Police, and several command roles. [Data: Entities (178); Relationships (541, 538, 532, 539, 535)]

Because the supplied records do not provide the amendment text or establish its publication, commencement, or current legal status, the amendment should be treated here only as a recorded legal reference—not as independently verified confirmation of the rules currently in force. [Data: Entities (178); Relationships (541, 538)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data describe legal authority, not proven compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records focus on statutory responsibilities, organizational roles, and administrative penalty powers. They do not provide case outcomes, audits, allegations, disciplinary findings, or other evidence sufficient to assess whether the entities comply with the law in practice or how they are regarded publicly. [Data: Entities (3673, 3688, 3039, 1323); Relationships (2073, 8961, 5765)]

There is also a potential interpretive ambiguity: the entity record for “Article 43” expressly distinguishes Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning sanctioning authority, from Article 43 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15, concerning vehicle inspection responsibilities. References to Article 43 should therefore be read with the instrument specified. [Data: Entities (451); Relationships (2073, 2071, 2070)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Cargo-Vehicle Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 21 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and its rules for cargo-vehicle traffic violations, including overloading, cargo compliance, and container transport. The article connects specific conduct to fines and, through Clause 13 and Clause 9, a six-point driving-license deduction. Article 28 forms a related but distinct strand covering motorized four-wheel passenger and cargo vehicles and license-point deductions. The records describe legal provisions and penalties; they do not establish enforcement outcomes or the compliance record of any particular driver or operator. [Data: Entities (307, 349, 883, 994, 732); Relationships (1191, 3365, 1424, 1188, 1199)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high impact because it brings together regulatory provisions that prescribe fines and license-point deductions for multiple road-traffic violations, though the records do not show enforcement or actual harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 21 is the central framework for cargo-vehicle violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 is described as setting penalties and driving-license point deductions for specified road-traffic order and safety violations involving cargo-carrying vehicles, including trucks and tractors with trailers or semi-trailers. Its connections to specific clauses and violation types make it the organizing provision in this community. [Data: Entities (307, 2591); Relationships (1191, 1190, 1192, 1188, 1198)]

The records identify several covered conduct categories, but do not provide a complete account of every provision or sanction in Article 21. The community therefore supports an overview of the framework, not a comprehensive interpretation of the decree. [Data: Entities (307, 994, 978); Relationships (1191, 1192)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overloading above the permitted payload carries a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes an overloading violation in which a truck, tractor, or similar goods-transport vehicle carries more than 50% and up to 100% above the permitted payload recorded in its inspection certificate. Article 21 is linked to this violation and to a fine of 5,000,000 to 7,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (732, 711, 2210); Relationships (1188, 3015, 2990)]

The records also link the specified overloading conduct to the imposition of fines and driving-license point deductions under Article 21. They do not establish how frequently the violation occurs or whether a particular operator has committed it. [Data: Relationships (3016)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 13 links specified conduct to a six-point deduction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 13 of Article 21 provides for a six-point driving-license deduction when a driver commits conduct specified in Clause 9. The records connect Clause 13 to both Clause 9 and the six-point deduction, and indicate that an administrative penalty also applies. [Data: Entities (883, 994, 4659, 85); Relationships (3365, 3560, 3364, 221)]

The available description of Clause 9 does not identify the conduct it covers. Consequently, the records support the existence of this deduction mechanism but do not support specifying which particular act triggers it. [Data: Entities (994, 883); Relationships (3364, 3365)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Container-securing violations have a higher stated fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a violation involving a container carried without a locking mechanism or allowed to shift during transport. Clause 10 of Article 21 is linked to this conduct, and the stated fine is 18,000,000 to 22,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (873, 5122); Relationships (1190, 3348)]

This is a separate violation from transporting oversized container-shaped equipment that is not a container. Article 21 is linked to the oversized-cargo violation, but the provided records do not state its fine amount. [Data: Entities (3503); Relationships (1199)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 21 covers additional cargo and towing-related violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct also includes transporting cargo that does not match information in the trailer or semi-trailer inspection certificate, carrying oversized container-shaped equipment, and towing a trailer or semi-trailer more than 150% above the permitted towing weight recorded in the vehicle’s certificate. Article 21 is linked to each of these categories. [Data: Entities (3262, 3503, 4967); Relationships (1198, 1199, 1200)]

The records identify these as subject to penalties, but do not provide a specific amount for each of them. In particular, the towing relationship says Clause 8 specifies a fine without giving the amount in the supplied data. [Data: Relationships (1200); Entities (3262, 3503, 4967)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 28 provides a related, distinct license-point framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 28 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns operators of motorized four-wheel passenger and cargo vehicles. Its Clause 4 provides a six-point deduction for conduct specified in Clause 3, linking a separate article to the same six-point penalty found in the Article 21 provisions. [Data: Entities (349, 927, 948, 4659); Relationships (1421, 1422, 1424, 3438, 3475)]

The records also associate Article 28 with a two-point deduction for conduct referenced in Clause 2, but do not describe that conduct. The Article 28 material should therefore be distinguished from Article 21’s cargo-vehicle provisions rather than treated as a description of the same violations. [Data: Entities (5185, 349); Relationships (1425)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Administrative Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative violations of road traffic order and safety and the penalties and remedial measures associated with them. The central violation category connects to supplementary sanctions—including confiscation, time-limited suspension, and temporary loss of permit or certificate rights—and to corrective actions involving obstructed signs, vehicle identification, and vehicle documentation. The information describes a regulatory framework, including Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, but does not document specific violations, affected parties, enforcement outcomes, or compliance rates. [Data: Entities (131, 4821, 1095, 3526, 4961); Relationships (437, 430, 436, 439, 10481, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it covers a broad set of road-safety sanctions and corrective requirements, while the records provide no evidence of specific cases or actual harm. [Data: Entities (131); Relationships (437, 430, 436, 433, 439)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Central regulatory category and scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative violations of road traffic order and safety are the hub of this community. The described category includes administrative-rule breaches in road transport and matters such as vehicle plates and markings, vehicle information, paint color, and identifying signs. It is also described as a subject of a specialized database managed by the Ministry of Public Security. [Data: Entities (131)]

The category description identifies Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as the basis for applicable administrative penalties and, where relevant, remedial measures. The records establish the regulatory scope but do not identify any particular person or organization that has violated these rules. [Data: Entities (131)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Supplementary penalties depend on the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that one or more supplementary administrative penalties may be imposed alongside other applicable penalties, depending on the nature and severity of a violation. This makes the penalty framework conditional rather than evidence that a particular sanction has been imposed in any case. [Data: Entities (4821); Relationships (437)]

The community also links the central violation category to time-limited suspension of activities and temporary deprivation of the right to use a permit or professional practice certificate. Both are described as possible supplementary sanctions, not as automatic consequences. [Data: Entities (4961, 4868); Relationships (10481, 438, 372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Confiscation is distinguished from the principal penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Confiscation of items connected with a violation or of vehicles used to commit it is described as a supplementary penalty that may apply to road-traffic violations. The relationship records qualify this by stating that confiscation applies when it is not imposed as the principal penalty. [Data: Entities (1095, 3860); Relationships (430, 3929)]

Accordingly, the records describe a possible enforcement measure and its relationship to the principal administrative penalty; they do not show that any property or vehicle has actually been confiscated. [Data: Entities (1095, 3860)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Corrective measures address obstructed road signs and traffic lights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One identified remedial measure requires removing objects that obstruct the visibility of road signs or traffic lights. The measure is linked to paragraph 3 of Article 3 and to the central category of road-traffic administrative violations. [Data: Entities (3526, 2971); Relationships (436, 434, 8677)]

This indicates that the framework includes corrective action intended to address an obstruction, in addition to penalties. The records do not describe a specific obstruction, its location, or whether removal has been ordered or completed. [Data: Entities (2971); Relationships (434, 8677)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle identification and documentation can require correction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The remedial measures include mandatory compliance with vehicle identification requirements. The described requirements cover number plates, lettering or digits on plates, information displayed on vehicle sides and doors, paint color, and identifying signs. [Data: Entities (2965, 131); Relationships (433)]

The records also identify procedures involving changing or revoking vehicle registration documents and issuing new documents, registration and license-plate documents, and technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificates. These are presented as applicable remedial procedures, not as actions documented in a specific case. [Data: Entities (5460); Relationships (439)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Paragraph 3 groups remedial measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Paragraph 3 of Article 3 is represented as listing remedial measures applicable to road-traffic administrative violations. The relationships specifically connect it to the mandatory removal of objects obscuring road signs or traffic lights, placing that measure within the described remedial framework. [Data: Entities (3526, 2971); Relationships (436, 8677)]

The records also separately link the central violation category to vehicle-identification compliance and vehicle-document procedures. They do not provide the complete text of paragraph 3, so the specific measures described here should not be treated as an exhaustive list. [Data: Entities (2965, 5460); Relationships (433, 439)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence is limited to rules, not observed compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information describes violation categories, possible penalties, and remedial measures. It does not identify specific alleged or confirmed incidents, enforcement actions, affected individuals or organizations, or outcomes; therefore, it cannot establish the frequency or severity of actual noncompliance. [Data: Entities (131, 118, 4821); Relationships (437, 430, 436)]

No technical capabilities or reputation assessments are provided for actors in this community. The available material supports an assessment of regulatory significance, but not conclusions about particular actors’ conduct or standing. [Data: Entities (131, 4821, 1095)]

v.tieu_de: Article 6, Clause 3 Road Traffic Violations
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around Article 6, Clause 3 Road Traffic Violations, which links improper use of high beams, continuous horn use or engine revving, and use of an air horn. The high-beam violation is further connected to four specified road situations, while priority vehicles carrying out prescribed duties are described as excepted from the specified restrictions. The records give different fine ranges for improper high-beam use and for the clause overall; they do not explain how those amounts relate. [Data: Entities (512, 2621, 5318, 1112, 3872); Relationships (2414, 2412, 2416, 2415)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate public-safety importance because it concerns common driving conduct and specified penalties, but the records describe rules rather than actual violations or their scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The clause is the community’s organizing entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, Clause 3 connects three described categories of conduct: improper high-beam use, continuous horn use or engine revving, and use of an air horn. The relationships make the clause the central point linking these traffic violations. [Data: Entities (512, 2621, 5318, 1112); Relationships (2414, 2412, 2416)]

The records also associate priority vehicles carrying out prescribed duties with an exception to the specified restrictions. This is presented as an exception, not as a general exemption for other drivers. [Data: Entities (3872); Relationships (2415)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: High-beam restrictions cover four stated road situations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe improper high-beam use when encountering pedestrians crossing, driving through a residential area with functioning street lighting, meeting oncoming traffic, and turning at an intersection. These situations are separately connected to the high-beam violation. [Data: Entities (1786, 1670, 2984, 5173, 2621); Relationships (6708, 6475, 7865, 7867)]

For meeting oncoming traffic, the description specifies an exception when a divider capable of preventing glare is present. No comparable exception is stated in the provided records for the other listed situations. [Data: Entities (2984); Relationships (7865)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records state different fine ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The improper-high-beam entity describes a fine of 200,000 to 400,000 VND for covered vehicle operators. The Article 6, Clause 3 entity gives a stated fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the clause’s covered violations. [Data: Entities (2621, 512)]

These descriptions provide different amounts, but the records do not explain whether the amounts apply to different circumstances, whether one supersedes the other, or how they should be reconciled. The discrepancy therefore remains unresolved within the supplied information. [Data: Entities (2621, 512)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed restrictions address visibility and driver conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich: The high-beam situations include encountering crossing pedestrians and meeting oncoming traffic, as well as driving in an illuminated residential area and turning at an intersection. The records establish these as prohibited contexts for high-beam use, but do not provide data on resulting incidents or injuries. [Data: Entities (1786, 2984, 1670, 5173); Relationships (6708, 7865, 6475, 7867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Noise-related conduct is included under the same clause
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Continuous horn sounding or repeatedly revving an engine is identified as a violation covered by Article 6, Clause 3. Use of an air horn is also listed as a covered violation. [Data: Entities (1112, 5318, 512); Relationships (2412, 2416)]

The supplied descriptions do not specify separate fine amounts for these two behaviors; the clause-level entity provides a single stated range for the covered violations. [Data: Entities (512, 1112, 5318)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The information concerns rules, not documented enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe prohibited conduct, specified driving contexts, an exception, and stated fines. They do not provide records of actual offenses, enforcement actions, affected people, or the frequency of violations, so the community’s real-world incidence cannot be assessed from this data alone. [Data: Entities (2621, 512, 5318, 1112, 3872); Relationships (2414, 2412, 2416, 2415)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024 Traffic Penalties and Article 38
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 38 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and related Vietnamese road-traffic penalty provisions. Its relationships connect drivers and vehicles registered in specified economic zones to monetary fines, badge withdrawal, and corrective return measures; other connected provisions cover driving-time and rest-period violations, journey-monitoring requirements, and driver’s-license point deductions. The supplied material describes legal rules rather than particular violations, enforcement outcomes, or the compliance record of any person or organization. Article 38 is also used for a separate provision of Law 36/2024/QH15 on vehicle license-plate auction winners’ rights and obligations, which should not be conflated with the decree’s traffic rules.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high practical importance because it describes a range of financial, licensing, and corrective consequences under traffic regulations, although no actual violations or enforcement outcomes are documented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 38 is the central regulatory node, but the article number is ambiguous
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The main cluster concerns Article 38 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which addresses penalties for drivers or operators of vehicles registered to operate in specified economic zones. It is linked to the stated fine range, an import-re-export declaration violation, and provisions cited as grounds for withdrawing a vehicle badge. [Data: Entities (421); Relationships (1785, 1784, 1788, 1789)]

The same entity description also identifies Article 38 of Law 36/2024/QH15, concerning the rights and obligations of vehicle license-plate auction winners. These are distinct legal provisions sharing an article number; the supplied relationships principally describe the decree’s traffic-penalty framework. [Data: Entities (421)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules prescribe multiple monetary penalties, including a 3–5 million VND range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 3,000,000-to-5,000,000 VND fine is associated with specified violations by drivers of cars and similar vehicles registered in the relevant economic zones. The connected records also identify driving beyond the permitted time, failure to observe the required rest period, and specified journey-monitoring violations among conduct carrying that fine. [Data: Entities (2181, 1541, 1603, 2006, 3323); Relationships (1785, 6247, 6345, 6976, 7191, +more)]

A separate violation—failure to carry the prescribed temporary import-and-re-export declaration—is described as carrying a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND under Article 38, Clause 1. The records therefore distinguish this amount from the 3–5 million VND range. [Data: Entities (1943, 2181); Relationships (1784)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Economic-zone registration determines which drivers and vehicles fall within the described rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 38 is linked to drivers of cars and similar vehicles registered to operate in special trade economic zones and international border-gate economic zones. The material describes these zones as categories, not as specific identified locations. [Data: Entities (2736, 1541, 4682, 4683); Relationships (1786, 1791, 6248, 6249)]

The rules are thus presented as applying to a defined vehicle-registration context rather than to all drivers without qualification. The available information does not identify particular drivers, vehicles, or economic zones. [Data: Entities (2736, 1541, 4682)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Consequences include badge withdrawal and corrective return of vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 38 description states that certain repeat violations can lead to confiscation and that specified provisions can be grounds for withdrawal of a vehicle badge. The relationship records specifically connect Article 38 with points b of Clauses 1 and 2 as grounds for badge withdrawal. [Data: Entities (421, 3762, 3766); Relationships (1788, 1789)]

A separate corrective measure requires a vehicle involved in specified violations to return to the economic zone where it is registered to operate. The records identify both special trade-economic zones and international border-gate economic zones in connection with this measure. [Data: Entities (1128, 4684); Relationships (3988, 3989)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-time, rest-period, and journey-monitoring rules form a related compliance cluster
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The connected provisions describe driving beyond the permitted time under Article 64 of the Road Traffic Order and Safety Law, as well as failure to observe the required rest period between continuous driving periods. The supplied relationships associate both violations with a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 VND. [Data: Entities (1603, 2006, 4393, 2181); Relationships (6345, 6976, 6346, 6057)]

Journey-monitoring-related conduct in the records includes operating a passenger-transport vehicle without a required device, operating it with a nonfunctioning device, and falsifying journey-monitoring data. The listed fine range is linked to these violations, though the material does not establish that any specific driver committed them. [Data: Entities (2085, 3323, 3324, 2181); Relationships (7191, 7192, 7069)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver’s-license point deductions are a separate, consequential part of the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe two- and four-point deductions for specified road-traffic violations, including provisions under Article 6 of the decree. Drivers of cars and similar vehicles are linked to specified violations and a two-point deduction; another relationship connects specified violations to a four-point deduction. [Data: Entities (4724, 5181, 2364, 1541); Relationships (6250, 6251, 10449, 7569)]

Clause 21 is also described as providing for point deductions when a vehicle owner directly drives and commits specified violations. These point-deduction provisions broaden the potential consequences beyond monetary fines, but the supplied records do not document deductions imposed in actual cases. [Data: Entities (919, 4561, 5181); Relationships (3408, 3409, 10305)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The material supports analysis of legal exposure, not an assessment of actual compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe statutory provisions, violation categories, and stated penalties. They do not identify a particular subject’s violation history, an enforcement action, or an adjudicated outcome; accordingly, they do not support conclusions about the compliance or reputation of a driver, business, or authority. [Data: Entities (421, 2181, 4724); Relationships (1785, 1786, 7569)]

The information is sufficient to show that the framework spans fines, license-point deductions, badge withdrawal, and corrective vehicle-return measures. It does not establish how frequently these measures are applied or their effects in specific cases. [Data: Entities (1128, 2364, 421); Relationships (1788, 3988, 7569)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Traffic Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and road-traffic violations connected to them. Article 6, Clause 5 is linked to failure to yield and to two specific road-entry situations, alongside a fine of 4,000,000–6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. Article 9 is linked to a broader failure-to-yield violation and a fine of 100,000–200,000 Vietnamese đồng, and separately identifies obstruction of a priority vehicle as a violation. The records describe different vehicle categories for the cited provisions but do not fully resolve how the linked violation scenarios map to those categories.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns road-safety compliance and monetary penalties, while the records document regulations rather than actual incidents or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree provisions organize the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify Article 6, Clause 5 and Article 9 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as the principal legal provisions. Their links to violations and fines make this a regulatory community focused on road-traffic compliance. [Data: Entities (518, 581); Relationships (2430, 2717, 2718)]

Article 6, Clause 5 is described as prescribing fines for specified violations by drivers of cars and similar motor vehicles. Article 9 is described as covering drivers or operators of bicycles, motorized bicycles, and other rudimentary vehicles. [Data: Entities (518, 581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to slow down or yield is the central violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The broad violation is described as occurring when a bicycle, motorized-bicycle, or other rudimentary-vehicle driver enters a priority road from a non-priority road, or a main road from a branch or side road, without slowing down or stopping to yield. It connects the two specific road-entry situations in the records. [Data: Entities (2043, 1793, 1794); Relationships (6717, 6718)]

The violation is linked both to Article 6, Clause 5 and to Article 9, as well as to penalty records associated with those provisions. This makes it the main connecting conduct in the dataset. [Data: Relationships (2430, 7026)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two specific road-entry situations are identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish entering a main road from a side road without yielding from entering a priority road from a non-priority road without yielding. Each is described as a specific form of the broader failure-to-yield violation. [Data: Entities (1793, 1794); Relationships (6717, 6718)]

Both situations are also linked to Article 6, Clause 5 as conduct subject to a fine. The supplied descriptions do not give additional details about circumstances, enforcement, or how these situations are assessed in practice. [Data: Relationships (2428, 2429)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records associate Article 6, Clause 5 with a higher fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, Clause 5 is described as setting a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified traffic violations by drivers of cars and similar motor vehicles. The corresponding fine entity and relationship associate that range with the clause and its listed violations. [Data: Entities (518, 5005); Relationships (2431)]

The clause is linked to the broad failure-to-yield violation and to both specific road-entry situations. However, the records do not specify the vehicle category for each of those linked scenarios, so the clause’s stated vehicle scope should be kept in view when interpreting the links. [Data: Relationships (2430, 2428, 2429)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 9 records a lower fine for the described rudimentary-vehicle conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 9, Clause 1 is described as setting a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain violations by bicycle, motorized-bicycle, and other rudimentary-vehicle drivers. The failure-to-yield description specifically associates this range with the conduct it defines. [Data: Entities (2043, 581, 2137); Relationships (7026, 2717)]

The dataset therefore includes both this lower fine range and the higher range linked to Article 6, Clause 5. Because the provisions’ descriptions refer to different vehicle categories, the records do not establish that one amount applies universally to every instance of failure to yield. [Data: Entities (518, 581, 2137); Relationships (2430, 7026)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 9 also identifies obstruction of a priority vehicle
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Obstructing a priority vehicle is identified as a road-traffic violation under Article 9, Clause 2. The relationship records indicate that Article 9 makes this conduct subject to a fine. [Data: Entities (3288, 581); Relationships (2718)]

No specific fine amount for this violation is provided in the supplied records. The community data also contains no incident, enforcement, or outcome details for obstruction of a priority vehicle. [Data: Entities (3288, 581); Relationships (2718)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024: Driver-Image Data Falsification Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 26, Clause 10 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and a fine of 40,000,000 to 60,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The provision connects the penalty to falsification of data from driver image-recording devices by two categories of organizations: device manufacturers, assemblers, and importers, and journey-monitoring or driver image-recording service providers. The supplied records describe a specific regulatory penalty and covered conduct; they do not establish that any organization has committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it defines a substantial stated penalty and identifies regulated organizations and conduct, while the records provide no evidence of an actual violation or enforcement event.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A defined monetary penalty anchors the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central measure is an administrative fine ranging from 40,000,000 to 60,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records link this fine to Article 26, Clause 10 and to the listed violation involving driver image-recording data. [Data: Entities (62, 336); Relationships (133)]

The data specifies the penalty amount but does not provide information about how fines are calculated within that range, enforcement outcomes, or whether any penalty has been imposed.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two organizational categories are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provision applies to manufacturers, assemblers, and importers of driver image-recording devices when they commit the specified violation. These organizations are explicitly linked to the stated fine. [Data: Entities (1451, 62); Relationships (134, 6033)]

Journey-monitoring and driver image-recording service providers are also identified as subject to the same fine if they falsify the relevant information or data. [Data: Entities (2791, 62); Relationships (135, 7066)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The specified violation is falsification of device data
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define the violation as altering or falsifying information or data from a device installed in a motor vehicle to record images of its driver. [Data: Entities (2080)]

The listed manufacturers, assemblers, and importers, as well as the covered service providers, are connected to this violation and the stated penalty. The information supplied does not describe detection methods, intent requirements, or other elements for determining whether conduct qualifies as falsification. [Data: Relationships (6033, 7066, 134, 135)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26, Clause 10 provides the regulatory basis
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 26, Clause 10 is described as a provision of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP covering penalties for specified road-transport violations. It is linked directly to the fine for the covered violation. [Data: Entities (336, 62); Relationships (133)]

The records establish the provision and penalty relationship but do not provide additional details about the decree's broader scope or other sanctions.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records indicate compliance relevance, not proven misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies organizations and data-related conduct that fall within the stated penalty framework, making accurate handling of driver image-recording data a relevant compliance consideration for the listed categories. This observation follows from the provision's stated coverage of falsification and its associated fine. [Data: Entities (1451, 2791, 2080, 62); Relationships (134, 135, 6033, 7066)]

No specific organization, incident, investigation, or enforcement action is identified in the supplied records. Accordingly, the data does not support a conclusion that any covered entity has violated the provision.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic-Law Knowledge Examination
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the road-traffic-law knowledge examination and the procedures and institutions connected to it. The examination is linked to re-examination for candidates who do not pass, application submission through the People's Public Security Force, identity verification, health certification, public posting of schedules and locations by provincial or municipal police, a specified paper-based format modeled on the A1 motorcycle licence test, and signing the examination record. The supplied information describes administrative requirements and processes; it does not establish violations or other adverse conduct. [Data: Entities (4571, 4032, 3675, 691, 617); Relationships (9836, 9560, 2948, 9800, 41, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects a formal legal-knowledge examination with public-security institutions and several defined candidate-administration procedures, while the data identifies no specific adverse impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination is the community's central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic-law knowledge examination is described as covering legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety. Its circular sets out registration, scheduling, administration, candidate identification, interpretation arrangements, and recordkeeping, making it the hub for the other entities and procedures in this community. [Data: Entities (4571)]

The examination has the highest stated degree among the listed entities, and the relationships consistently connect other processes or institutions to it. [Data: Entities (4571); Relationships (9836, 9560, 2948, 9800, 41, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A further attempt is available after an unsuccessful examination
phat_hien.giai_thich: The re-examination is described as another attempt at the same examination for a candidate who did not pass. It is subject to stated application requirements, although the provided data does not specify those requirements in detail. [Data: Entities (4032); Relationships (9836)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Applications can be submitted through the People's Public Security Force
phat_hien.giai_thich: The People's Public Security Force is identified as Vietnam’s public security force, and applications through the force are listed as one channel for submitting examination applications and registration. The data does not describe this as the only application route. [Data: Entities (3675, 4571); Relationships (9560)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Candidate identity is checked before the examination
phat_hien.giai_thich: The competent testing authority verifies a candidate’s identity before the examination by comparing identification information with the application. The described verification may use identity documents or available electronic identity information. [Data: Entities (691); Relationships (2948)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Health certification is part of the application requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich: An authorized medical facility is defined as a facility authorized to issue a valid health certificate required as part of an examination application. The provided data does not give further details about the certificate’s criteria or how it is assessed. [Data: Entities (617); Relationships (2779)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial or municipal police may publish examination logistics
phat_hien.giai_thich: The examination schedule and location may be publicly posted on an electronic portal within the management scope of the provincial or municipal police. This establishes a described public-information role for those authorities, without specifying which portal or the timing of publication. [Data: Entities (3967); Relationships (9800)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data describes examination format and recordkeeping procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For a specified group of candidates from ethnic minorities, the A1 motorcycle licence test is cited as a model for a paper-based multiple-choice question-and-answer format. The information provided does not identify the candidates or provide additional details about how this format is administered. [Data: Entities (18); Relationships (41)]

At the conclusion of the examination, the candidate signs or fingerprints the examination record; an interpreter also signs or fingerprints it when applicable. These procedures form part of the community’s documented administration and recordkeeping arrangements. [Data: Entities (1857, 4571); Relationships (6792)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Road Traffic Sanctions and Inspection-Procedure Requirements
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road-traffic sanctions and the prohibition on imposing requirements contrary to prescribed vehicle-inspection procedures. Its records link Article 32 sanctions to individual violators, connect unlawful inspection-procedure requirements to individuals who impose them and to individuals or organizations who may be affected, and specify a fine of VND 8,000,000–10,000,000 for the described individual violation. The information describes regulatory provisions and affected parties, not specific enforcement cases or outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns financial penalties, possible withdrawal of vehicle documents, and inspection procedures affecting individuals and organizations, although no specific cases or actual impacts are documented.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 links road-traffic violations to sanctions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is described as covering penalties and driving-license point deductions for vehicle owners’ road-traffic violations, including withdrawal of specified altered, forged, or improperly issued vehicle documents. The relationship record specifically links the provision to individual violators and says penalties and document withdrawal apply to listed violations. [Data: Entities (374, 2650); Relationships (1622)]

The described violations span several areas, including roadways or sidewalks, environmental protection, passenger capacity, vehicle or road limits, cargo securing, and driver training or tests. The supplied data identifies possible sanctions but does not document any particular violation or enforcement outcome. [Data: Entities (2650, 374)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unlawful inspection-procedure requirements are a distinct violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a violation defined as imposing requirements on individuals or organizations that contravene prescribed vehicle-inspection processes or procedures. A relationship connects this violation to an individual who imposes such requirements, identifying the conduct as the described violation. [Data: Entities (5240); Relationships (7907)]

The records distinguish the person imposing the unlawful requirement from those who may be subjected to it: affected individuals and affected organizations are both linked to the inspection-procedure violation. The data does not specify particular inspection bodies, affected parties, or incidents. [Data: Entities (141, 140, 5240); Relationships (460, 461)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The specified individual fine is VND 8,000,000–10,000,000
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify a fine of VND 8,000,000–10,000,000 for an individual committing the specified violation. The relationship data links this fine both to individual violators and directly to unlawful inspection-procedure requirements. [Data: Entities (2246, 2650, 5240); Relationships (7316, 7317)]

The supplied information states the amount and the connection to an individual violation, but does not establish how often the fine is imposed, whether it is mandatory in every case, or whether other sanctions apply to this specific inspection-procedure violation. [Data: Entities (2246, 5240); Relationships (7317)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individuals and organizations are identified as potentially affected
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Both affected individuals and affected organizations are expressly identified as parties to whom unlawful vehicle-inspection requirements may be made. This means the described procedural issue is not limited to individual vehicle users; organizations are also within the stated affected group. [Data: Entities (140, 141); Relationships (460, 461)]

The records do not name any affected person or organization, quantify the scope of potential impact, or describe practical consequences beyond the connection to unlawful requirements. [Data: Entities (140, 141, 5240); Relationships (460, 461)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory scope, not documented cases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships describe sanctions, a prohibited inspection-procedure practice, a stated fine, and categories of affected parties. They do not identify a particular enforcement action, adjudication, compliance record, or operational actor. [Data: Entities (374, 5240, 2650, 2246, 140, +more); Relationships (1622, 7907, 7316, 7317, 460, +more)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant for understanding the stated regulatory and potential impact landscape, but the data provided does not support conclusions about actual prevalence, compliance, or realized harm. [Data: Entities (374, 5240, 2650, 2246); Relationships (1622, 7907, 7316, 7317)]

v.tieu_de: VND 2–3 Million Traffic Penalty and Decree 168
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND, linked to several distinct traffic and transport violations. Article 28 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is specifically connected to unauthorized transport-badge use by certain four-wheeled commercial vehicles. The records describe regulatory penalties and violation types, but provide no information about technical capabilities or reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it connects a defined monetary penalty to multiple traffic and commercial-transport compliance violations, with no evidence here of broader operational or reputational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine is the community’s central link
phat_hien.giai_thich: The 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND fine is the central entity, connected to vehicle-condition violations, passenger conduct that threatens or infringes another person’s health, and unauthorized transport-badge use. This structure indicates that the same fine range is associated with distinct types of conduct rather than one single offense. [Data: Entities (2159, 5213, 4944, 5377); Relationships (7167, 7165, 7166)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 28 addresses transport-badge compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 28 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is linked both to the stated fine and to unauthorized transport-badge use. The records describe the provision as applying to four-wheeled passenger or goods vehicles used for transport without a valid, properly issued regulatory badge. [Data: Entities (353, 5213, 2159); Relationships (1429, 1431)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized badge use includes several specified cases
phat_hien.giai_thich: The unauthorized-badge offense covers operating a four-wheeled motor passenger or goods vehicle for commercial transport without the required badge, with an expired badge, or with a badge not issued by a competent authority. The relationships identify this offense as subject to the 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 VND fine and connect it to Article 28. [Data: Entities (5213, 353, 2159); Relationships (7166, 1431, 1429)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine also applies to passenger conduct affecting health
phat_hien.giai_thich: A separate listed violation concerns a passenger threatening or infringing the health of another passenger, the driver, or onboard service staff. The records link this conduct to the same fine range, distinguishing it from the commercial transport-badge violation. [Data: Entities (4944, 2159); Relationships (7165)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition violations are another distinct application
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community also connects the fine to a vehicle-condition violation described as failure to meet traffic-participation requirements for motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles. This is a separate compliance category from the four-wheeled commercial-transport badge rules. [Data: Entities (5377, 2159); Relationships (7167)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Violations and the 800,000–1,000,000 Dong Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a specified fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese dong and the violations associated with it. The records connect the fine to child-passenger safety violations—including seating a young child in the driver’s row in specified circumstances and failing to use an appropriate child safety device—and to speeding 5 to under 10 km/h above the limit when committed by a specialized motorcycle driver. The data describes penalties and prohibited conduct, but does not establish that any violation occurred or provide information about enforcement, frequency, or broader impact. [Data: Entities (2232, 820, 4730, 2052, 817); Relationships (7283, 7038, 3189, 3194, 10297)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s documented relevance to traffic safety and monetary penalties, while the records provide no evidence of actual violations, enforcement scale, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single fine links several specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 800,000–1,000,000 Vietnamese dong fine is the central connecting entity. The records associate it with specified child-passenger safety conduct, the corresponding provision in Clause 3 of Article 6, and speeding by a specialized motorcycle driver. [Data: Entities (2232, 937); Relationships (3448, 7038, 3189, 7283)]

The entity description also says the fine applies to one violation covered by Article 21, but the supplied records do not identify that violation. The data establishes a stated penalty framework, not that any person was fined or that a violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2232)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Child-passenger safety violations cover two forms of conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The child-passenger safety violation category includes both carrying a child under 10 years old and under 1.35 meters tall in the driver’s row in specified circumstances, and failing to use an appropriate child safety device. [Data: Entities (820, 817, 2052); Relationships (3188, 3194)]

The records connect each of these forms of conduct to the 800,000–1,000,000 dong fine through Clause 3. [Data: Relationships (7038, 3189, 3448)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The child-seating restriction has a stated exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described prohibited conduct is carrying a child under 10 and under 1.35 meters tall in the same row as the driver. The description explicitly excludes a car with only one row of seats from this restriction. [Data: Entities (817)]

This conduct is identified as part of the broader child-passenger safety violation category and is linked to the specified fine. [Data: Relationships (3188, 3189)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Failure to use an appropriate child safety device is separately identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify failure to use an appropriate child safety device as prohibited conduct and as one of the violations included in the child-passenger safety category. [Data: Entities (2052, 820); Relationships (3194)]

The stated penalty connection is to the fine prescribed in Clause 3 of Article 6. The supplied information does not specify device types or additional circumstances. [Data: Entities (937, 2232); Relationships (7038, 3448)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specialized-motorcycle speeding violation is linked to the same fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe speeding as driving at least 5 km/h but less than 10 km/h above the prescribed limit. They identify this conduct as a road-traffic rule violation covered for a specialized motorcycle driver. [Data: Entities (4730, 4551); Relationships (10297)]

The fine entity is directly linked to this speeding violation when committed by a specialized motorcycle driver. The data does not establish that a particular driver committed it or provide further details about the circumstances. [Data: Entities (2232); Relationships (7283)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Driving-Time and Rest Requirements
v.tom_tat: This community concerns Vietnamese road-traffic rules governing driving time and required breaks or rest periods for transport-vehicle drivers. Article 64, Clause 1 of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety supplies the driving-time limits, while Article 21, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is linked to violations involving excess driving time and missed breaks or rest periods. The listed decree provision also specifies fines of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng; one record additionally mentions driving-licence point penalties. The data includes closely related descriptions and differently rendered names for provisions and violations.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects transport-driver time and rest requirements with legal penalties, although the records do not establish the scale or frequency of violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A legal framework links driving-time limits to punishable violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 64, Clause 1 of the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety establishes permitted driving-time limits, and the data links those limits to violations for exceeding them. Article 21, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is identified as making excess driving time a punishable violation. [Data: Entities (314, 532, 1877); Relationships (1232, 2464)]

This structure connects a rule defining the permitted limit to a provision identifying noncompliance as punishable. The records describe the legal relationship, but do not provide information about enforcement or how often the violation occurs. [Data: Relationships (1232, 2464)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess driving time appears under two closely related descriptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe both “Exceeding Prescribed Driving Time” and “Exceeding the Permitted Driving Time.” Each is associated with Article 64, Clause 1, and the decree provision is linked to each as a punishable violation. [Data: Entities (1877, 1879, 532); Relationships (1232, 1235, 2464, 2465)]

The descriptions are closely aligned, but the supplied data does not establish whether they are formally identical offenses or distinct entries. They should therefore be treated as related descriptions rather than conclusively merged. [Data: Entities (1877, 1879); Relationships (2464, 2465)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required breaks and rest periods are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is linked to failure to observe required breaks between continuous driving periods as a punishable violation. A separate record associates the NĐ-CP rendering of the decree provision with failure to observe required rest periods. [Data: Entities (2004, 2005); Relationships (1233, 1236)]

The data thus places both break-related and rest-period-related noncompliance within the community of transport-driver rules. It does not provide the specific duration of required breaks or rest periods. [Data: Entities (2004, 2005); Relationships (1233, 1236)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed fine range is 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The record for Article 21, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP states fines of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong for specified violations by goods-transport-vehicle drivers, alongside driving-licence point penalties. A second record, using the NĐ-CP spelling, states the same fine range for specified goods-transport-driver violations but does not mention licence points in its description. [Data: Entities (314, 315)]

The records do not specify which individual violation receives which fine within the range, or the number of licence points affected. [Data: Entities (314, 315)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provision names and violation labels vary across records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree appears in the data as both “168/2024/ND-CP” and “168/2024/NĐ-CP.” The records associate these renderings with related provisions and violations, including excess driving time and failures to observe breaks or rest periods. [Data: Entities (314, 315, 1877, 1879, 2004); Relationships (1232, 1233, 1235, 1236, +more)]

These variations matter when interpreting the dataset: the records support a common subject area, but do not explicitly state that every differently named entry is legally or administratively interchangeable. [Data: Entities (314, 315, 1877, 1879, 2004)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/ND-CP: Vehicle Document-Carrying Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the requirement for motorcycle, moped, or similar-vehicle transport operators to carry required vehicle registration documents. Article 18(2) of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is linked to the violation and specifies a fine of 200,000 to 300,000 Vietnamese đồng. The data also describes that fine as applying to a covered insurance-document violation, but provides no separate insurance-violation entity or relationship. The records describe a regulatory rule, not evidence of a particular operator violating it.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low to moderate because the community describes a specific traffic-compliance penalty, with no evidence of an actual violation or broader operational impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns a specific document-carrying violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central violation is failure by a motorcycle, moped, or similar-vehicle transport-business operator to carry the vehicle registration certificate or prescribed substitute documents. The records characterize this as a defined traffic violation, rather than documenting a specific incident or operator's conduct. [Data: Entities (1949, 3156); Relationships (6902)]

The available information is limited to the stated document requirement and its penalty context; it does not establish how frequently the violation occurs or whether any particular party has been cited.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18(2) connects the violation to its penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18(2) is described as the provision defining the penalty for failure to carry the required vehicle registration documents. Its relationship to the violation identifies the provision as the legal basis represented in this community. [Data: Entities (285, 1949); Relationships (1040)]

The broader Article 18 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is separately described as setting penalties and license-point deductions for driver-requirement violations. The provided records do not specify any license-point deduction for this particular document-carrying violation. [Data: Entities (281)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is 200,000 to 300,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify a fine of 200,000 to 300,000 Vietnamese đồng for the specified failure to carry vehicle registration documents, and connect that amount to Article 18(2). [Data: Entities (2171); Relationships (6900, 1041)]

The fine is a defined monetary consequence in the described rule. The data does not provide information about enforcement rates, payment outcomes, or other sanctions for an individual case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described operator group is transport-business drivers of small vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relevant operator is described as a person operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle for transport business, subject to the document-carrying requirement. [Data: Entities (3156, 1949); Relationships (6902)]

The records do not identify any specific driver, transport business, vehicle, or location. Accordingly, they support analysis of the rule's stated scope, but not conclusions about an identified person or organization's compliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The fine entity mentions an additional insurance-document violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
