The fine entity's description says the 200,000-to-300,000-đồng range also applies to covered cases of failing to carry a valid compulsory civil liability insurance certificate while operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle for transport business. [Data: Entities (2171)]

However, the relationship records connect the fine to the registration-document violation, and the dataset does not provide a separate insurance-violation entity or supporting relationship. The insurance detail is therefore present in the fine description, but is not elaborated elsewhere in this community. [Data: Relationships (6900, 1041)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/ND-CP: Articles 42–46 and Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety in road transport and the provisions of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP addressing enforcement authority. Articles 42, 43, and 44 specify positions authorized to impose penalties, while Article 46 addresses who may make violation records and refers to those three articles. The records describe a legal framework and allocation of authority, not particular officials, enforcement actions, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (461, 132, 608, 448, 452); Relationships (443, 2105, 441, 442, 440, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it describes legal authority for documenting and penalizing road-traffic violations, but the records provide no evidence of specific enforcement outcomes or misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 46 is the central link between violation records and enforcement authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 46 concerns who is authorized to make administrative violation records for road-traffic order and safety violations in road transport. It is linked both to the violation category and to the separate concept of record-making authority. [Data: Entities (461, 609, 132); Relationships (443, 445, 2138)]

Article 46 also refers to Articles 42, 43, and 44, which specify positions authorized to impose penalties. This makes Article 46 a procedural connection between recording violations and the related penalty-authority provisions; the data does not specify the names or duties of individual officials. [Data: Relationships (2057, 2075, 2105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns administrative violations in road transport
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation category is described as covering administrative violations addressed by Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, including violations for which the decree specifies authority to make records and impose penalties. It is the shared subject of Article 46, Articles 42–44, and both authority concepts in the network. [Data: Entities (132); Relationships (443, 440, 441, 442, 444)]

The records establish a legal and administrative scope, but do not identify particular violations, affected parties, cases, or outcomes. The significance evidenced here is the framework’s application to this category of road-transport violations. [Data: Entities (132); Relationships (443, 444, 445)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Articles 42, 43, and 44 govern penalty-imposing authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Each of Articles 42, 43, and 44 is described as specifying positions authorized to impose penalties for the relevant road-traffic violations. Each is also linked to the broader concept of authority to impose administrative penalties. [Data: Entities (448, 452, 456, 608); Relationships (440, 441, 442, 2058, 2076, +more)]

Article 46 refers to all three provisions when addressing record-making authority. The network therefore presents these articles as related parts of the enforcement framework, while not providing the specific positions or the limits of their powers. [Data: Relationships (2057, 2075, 2105)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recording violations and imposing penalties are distinct authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data distinguishes authority to prepare administrative violation records from authority to impose administrative penalties. Article 46 addresses the former, while Articles 42–44 specify positions authorized for the latter. [Data: Entities (609, 608, 461, 448, 452); Relationships (2138, 2058, 2076, 2106)]

Both authorities apply to the same road-traffic violation category, but the records do not say that every person authorized to make a record may also impose a penalty. The distinction is important when interpreting the allocation of powers described in the network. [Data: Relationships (444, 445, 2138, 2058, 2076)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports analysis of legal structure, not compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities and relationships describe provisions of a decree and the legal concepts those provisions address. They do not identify organizations or individual officials, report particular enforcement conduct, or provide evidence of compliance, violations by authorities, technical capabilities, or reputational assessments. [Data: Entities (461, 132, 608, 609); Relationships (443, 444, 445, 2138)]

Accordingly, the community’s supported significance is its description of the formal division of record-making and penalty-imposing authority. Any assessment of how the framework is implemented would require evidence beyond these records. [Data: Entities (448, 452, 456, 461); Relationships (2057, 2075, 2105)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle License-Plate Violations and Clause 8 Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle license-plate violations described under Clause 8 of Article 13. Three categories—missing or incorrectly positioned plates, illegible or altered characters, and bent, covered, or otherwise modified plates—are linked to the violation category, which carries a stated fine of 20,000,000 to 26,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records describe the violations and penalty but do not establish enforcement activity, compliance rates, or broader effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the community describes a defined set of vehicle-related violations with a substantial stated fine, but provides no evidence of enforcement scale or wider consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single violation category connects the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle License-Plate Violations is the central entity: the three described violation types and the fine are each linked to it. This structure presents a consolidated regulatory category rather than evidence of separate organizations or actors. [Data: Entities (5425, 2166, 2552, 3034, 638); Relationships (7174, 8955, 7811, 2835)]

The records describe the listed conduct as covered by Clause 8 of Article 13. They do not provide further information about the law’s jurisdiction, current status, or practical enforcement. [Data: Entities (5425); Relationships (8955, 7811, 2835)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is 20,000,000 to 26,000,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified monetary penalty is connected directly to the vehicle license-plate violations and is described as the fine set by Clause 8 for the listed conduct. [Data: Entities (2166, 5425); Relationships (7174)]

The data gives a range, not an individual fine amount or information about how the amount is determined in particular cases. It also does not report actual assessments, collections, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2166); Relationships (7174)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Missing or incorrectly positioned plates are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed category is driving a covered vehicle without all required license plates, or with plates placed incorrectly or failing to meet required specifications. It is explicitly linked to the central violation category. [Data: Entities (3034, 5425); Relationships (8955)]

The description covers automobiles, trailers and semitrailers, and specified four-wheel motor vehicles as part of the broader provision. The records do not quantify how often this violation occurs. [Data: Entities (5425, 3034)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Illegible or non-paint-altered characters are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed violations include plates with unclear letters or numbers and characters or numbers altered using materials other than paint. This category is linked to Vehicle License-Plate Violations. [Data: Entities (2552, 5425); Relationships (7811)]

The supplied information describes the conduct but does not provide examples of materials, detection methods, or evidence about how frequently this category is encountered. [Data: Entities (2552, 5425); Relationships (7811)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Bending, covering, or modifying a plate is also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Another listed category includes bending or obscuring a license plate, or changing its characters, colors, shape, or dimensions. The relationship record identifies these actions as part of the central violation category. [Data: Entities (638, 5425); Relationships (2835)]

Taken together, the records distinguish this conduct from missing or incorrectly positioned plates and from illegible or non-paint-altered characters. They do not provide information about intent or the circumstances of any specific violation. [Data: Entities (638, 3034, 2552, 5425); Relationships (8955, 7811, 2835)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger Helmet Violation and Exceptions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the traffic violation of transporting a passenger without a properly worn motorcycle helmet. The described penalty is a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong, with three stated exceptions: emergency transport of a patient, carrying a child under six, and escorting a person for a legal violation. Each exception is directly linked to the central violation in the provided relationships. [Data: Entities (5123, 5120, 1839, 1777); Relationships (6768, 6697, 10600)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to traffic-law compliance and a specified financial penalty, while the provided information is limited to one violation and its exceptions.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Central rule concerns a passenger’s helmet
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity describes a traffic violation involving a motorized-bicycle driver carrying a passenger who is not wearing a motorcycle helmet or whose helmet’s chin strap is not correctly fastened. The description identifies these as the circumstances associated with the violation. [Data: Entities (5123)]

The community’s other entities and all three relationships concern exceptions to the penalty for this violation, making it the organizing subject of the available information. [Data: Entities (5123, 5120, 1839, 1777); Relationships (6768, 6697, 10600)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified fine for the violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation description states a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese dong. The source provides no further information about how the amount is determined or whether other consequences apply. [Data: Entities (5123)]

The listed exceptions are described as exceptions to this helmet-related penalty; the records do not provide additional procedural details about applying them. [Data: Entities (5123, 5120, 1839, 1777); Relationships (6768, 6697, 10600)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency patient transport is an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities identify emergency transport of a patient as an exception to the helmet-related penalty. The description specifies that this applies when a driver is transporting a sick person for emergency care. [Data: Entities (1777)]

A relationship explicitly connects this exception to the central passenger-helmet violation. The provided records do not define what qualifies as emergency care beyond that description. [Data: Relationships (6697)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Carrying a child under six is an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data state that the helmet-related penalty does not apply when the passenger being carried is a child under six years old. [Data: Entities (5120)]

This exception is directly linked to the central violation in the relationship data. No other age-related conditions or details are specified. [Data: Relationships (10600)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Escorting a person for a legal violation is an exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify escorting a person accused of a legal violation as an exception to the penalty for carrying a passenger without a properly worn helmet. The entity description phrases the circumstance as escorting a person for having committed a legal violation. [Data: Entities (1839)]

The relationship confirms the connection to the central helmet-related penalty. The provided information does not clarify the circumstances or procedures required for this exception. [Data: Relationships (6768)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024/ND-CP Article 12, Clause 14 Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Clause 14 of Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and its treatment of insulting, threatening, obstructing, or resisting people performing official duties to ensure road traffic order and safety. The clause is linked to a fine of 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 dong for individuals who commit the specified violations. The records describe a focused regulatory provision and its associated conduct and penalty; they do not provide information about enforcement or particular cases. [Data: Entities (246, 888, 2189, 3302); Relationships (787, 3370, 3369, 7201)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes a specific traffic-related legal provision and substantial individual fines, while providing no evidence of enforcement activity or broader consequences.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 14 is the community's central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 14 is identified as part of Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, making the clause the central link between the broader article, the prohibited conduct, and the stated penalty. [Data: Entities (888, 246); Relationships (787)]

The supplied description of Article 12 says it addresses penalties and driver’s-license-point deductions for certain road-traffic violations and other uses of roads and sidewalks. The data does not specify that the fine discussed here involves a particular point deduction. [Data: Entities (246)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provision specifies official-duty-related prohibited conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 14 identifies insulting, threatening, obstructing, or resisting people performing official duties to ensure road traffic order and safety as violations. The dataset links this conduct directly to the clause. [Data: Entities (3302); Relationships (3370)]

The records describe the conduct as a category of violation; they do not identify any individual, incident, or organization involved in such conduct. [Data: Entities (3302)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A substantial monetary penalty is associated with the specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated fine is 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 dong for individuals who commit the specified violations. Clause 14 is linked to this penalty, and the records also connect the fine directly to official-duty obstruction or resistance. [Data: Entities (2189, 888, 3302); Relationships (3369, 7201)]

The supplied information does not describe how the fine is calculated within the range or provide examples of penalties imposed. [Data: Entities (2189)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationships form a clear provision-to-conduct-to-penalty structure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships establish a straightforward regulatory chain: Clause 14 belongs to Article 12, identifies the prohibited conduct, and prescribes the stated fine; the fine is also explicitly associated with that conduct. [Data: Relationships (787, 3370, 3369, 7201)]

This structure makes the community relevant to understanding the stated rule and its penalty, but the records do not provide additional procedural details or interpretive guidance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is limited to descriptions of the legal rule
phat_hien.giai_thich:

They do not report whether verification succeeded, whether a decision was issued, or whether a penalty was ultimately imposed. [Data: Entities (1928, 5530); Relationships (6881)]

Accordingly, the data supports describing the procedure but not drawing conclusions about any individual case or its outcome. [Data: Entities (1928, 5530); Relationships (6881)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community's documented scope is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied data includes only the deadline-extension entity, the person-verification entity, and their connecting relationship. The stated connection is limited to allowing verification before a penalty decision deadline. [Data: Entities (1928, 5530); Relationships (6881)]

No additional entities or details establish broader operational, technical, reputational, or compliance effects. The records therefore support a narrow assessment of this procedural topic only. [Data: Entities (1928, 5530); Relationships (6881)]

v.tieu_de: Traffic Police Guidance and Investigation Division
v.tom_tat: The community consists of the Division of Guidance, Propaganda, Investigation and Traffic Accident Resolution and the unnamed head of that division. The division is described as a professional unit under the Traffic Police Department, and the relationship identifies the unnamed role as its head. The head is also described as having sanctioning authority in a decree, but the provided information does not specify the scope or use of that authority. [Data: Entities (1427, 2452); Relationships (5921)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The division’s place within the Traffic Police Department and its chief’s stated sanctioning authority indicate institutional importance, while the limited information provides no basis for assessing broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Division of Guidance, Propaganda, Investigation and Traffic Accident Resolution is the principal organizational entity in this community. It is described as a professional division under the Traffic Police Department. [Data: Entities (1427)]

The only listed relationship connects this division to its head, making the division the organizational center of the available information. [Data: Relationships (5921)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division is situated within the Traffic Police Department
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The division’s description places it under the Traffic Police Department. This establishes an organizational affiliation, but the supplied information does not describe the department’s wider structure or the division’s reporting arrangements beyond its head. [Data: Entities (1427)]

No additional entities or relationships are provided to establish further institutional links. [Data: Entities (1427, 2452); Relationships (5921)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An unnamed chief heads the division
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The division is described as headed by a division chief, and the related entity represents that role rather than naming an individual. The relationship explicitly identifies the role as the head of the professional division. [Data: Entities (1427, 2452); Relationships (5921)]

The records provide no personal identity or biographical details for the person occupying the position. [Data: Entities (2452)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The chief is described as having sanctioning authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description for the division head says that the unnamed chief is identified in a decree as having sanctioning authority. This signals a formal authority associated with the role, but the provided record does not specify its scope, legal basis beyond the reference to a decree, or how it has been exercised. [Data: Entities (2452)]

Accordingly, the available information supports noting the stated authority but not drawing conclusions about particular sanctions, enforcement actions, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (2452)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The division’s named remit is broad, but operational details are absent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The division’s title refers to guidance, propaganda, investigation, and traffic-accident resolution. The record describes it as a professional division but does not explain the activities, procedures, technical capabilities, or outcomes associated with those areas. [Data: Entities (1427)]

No claims, incidents, or reputation-related information are included, so these matters cannot be assessed from the supplied records. [Data: Entities (1427, 2452); Relationships (5921)]

v.tieu_de: Article 32 Driving-License Point Deduction Clauses
v.tom_tat: This community consists of Clause 21 of Article 32 and the two provisions it references, Clauses 5 and 6. Clause 21 describes driving-license point deductions for specified violations and references those clauses as defining relevant conduct in the stated circumstances. The supplied information does not identify the conduct in Clauses 5 and 6 or provide details about enforcement, affected parties, or the broader legal context.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low-to-moderate because the provisions describe a potential driving-license points consequence, while the supplied records provide limited detail about the underlying conduct or practical impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 21 is the community's central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 21 of Article 32 is the hub of the supplied community: it is described as stating that individuals or organizations committing specified violations may also have driving-license points deducted, and it is the source of both listed relationships. [Data: Entities (920); Relationships (3410, 3411)]

The records describe a legal consequence, but do not establish that any particular person or organization has violated the provision or received a deduction. [Data: Entities (920)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clauses 5 and 6 are referenced as the underlying conduct provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 21 references Clause 5 and Clause 6 as specifying conduct that can form a basis for the point deduction in the circumstances described. [Data: Relationships (3410, 3411)]

The supplied descriptions explicitly omit the specific conduct stated in Clauses 5 and 6. Their substantive scope therefore cannot be assessed from these records alone. [Data: Entities (959, 972)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated consequence concerns driving-license points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The consequence expressly described for the specified violations is that driving-license points may also be deducted. The wording indicates a possible consequence, rather than documenting that a deduction has occurred in any particular case. [Data: Entities (920)]

No information is supplied about the number of points, procedures, decision-makers, or other consequences, so those aspects cannot be determined from this community's records. [Data: Entities (920)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The relationships form a narrow, clause-to-clause structure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains three entities and two relationships: Clause 21 points to Clause 5 and Clause 6, with no other entities or links listed in the supplied data. [Data: Entities (920, 959, 972); Relationships (3410, 3411)]

This structure supports treating Clause 21 as the connecting provision, but does not establish how these clauses relate to any larger statute, regulatory system, or enforcement process.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records are insufficient to assess compliance or enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material describes provisions and their cross-references, not specific cases, regulated parties, enforcement actions, or compliance outcomes. It therefore does not support conclusions about whether the clauses are being followed or how often point deductions are applied. [Data: Entities (920, 959, 972); Relationships (3410, 3411)]

The missing descriptions of the conduct in Clauses 5 and 6 also limit assessment of the substantive legal scope and potential effects of the provisions. [Data: Entities (959, 972)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Ministry of Public Security and Traffic Police Governance
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security (MPS), which coordinates national road-traffic governance and operates extensive regulatory, administrative, and information-system functions. The Traffic Police Department operates under the MPS and handles specified applications, examinations, permits, and enforcement-related tasks; the Minister sets rules, while police forces, other ministries, foreign representatives, and local authorities connect to particular responsibilities. The community also includes public-service and mobile channels for applications and licence-point notifications. The records establish substantial institutional importance and technical responsibilities, but do not document operational performance, security outcomes, specific enforcement cases, or general compliance results. [Data: Reports (2-393, 2-396, 2-404); Entities (3019, 5026, 3001); Relationships (8893, 8732, 8845)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the MPS’s broad national authority, interconnected traffic-administration systems, and consequential licensing and enforcement functions, rather than evidence of harmful conduct or operational failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The MPS is the community’s central coordinating authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS is identified as the Government’s focal agency for unified state management of road-traffic order and safety. It coordinates implementation with other ministries and sectors and leads relevant international cooperation, giving it a broad institutional role. [Data: Reports (2-393); Entities (3019, 4105); Relationships (8864, 8852)]

The Traffic Police Department operates under the MPS and serves as a channel for specified applications and reports. This places the Department’s operational activities within the Ministry’s wider governance structure. [Data: Reports (2-396); Entities (5026); Relationships (8893)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Minister and Department exercise extensive but legally defined authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister of Public Security is assigned rulemaking responsibilities across driver licensing and examinations, vehicle registration, accident investigation, traffic patrol, and specified monitoring and traffic-command systems. The supplied records identify the office, not the individual holding it. [Data: Reports (2-393); Entities (3001); Relationships (8732)]

The Traffic Police Department’s Director and professional-division heads have specified administrative-sanctioning powers under Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The Director’s listed powers include fines up to 75 million Vietnamese đồng and certain confiscation, suspension, temporary-revocation, and remedial measures. These are descriptions of legal authority, not evidence that particular sanctions have been imposed. [Data: Reports (2-396); Entities (5026, 1385, 2432); Relationships (8893)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Department handles operational procedures, permits, and examinations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Department receives and reviews specified applications, including requests concerning right-hand-drive vehicles used for non-tourism purposes. For valid and complete applications under the described procedure, it is to issue written approval or refusal within five working days and may distribute decisions to relevant authorities for coordination. [Data: Reports (2-396); Entities (5026); Relationships (8893)]

The Department also organizes legal-knowledge testing, issues examiner cards, and manages examination software and a related administrative-violation database. It issues, reissues, and revokes certain priority-vehicle signal-device permits and issues operating permits for specified intelligent transport vehicles, subject to stated exceptions. [Data: Reports (2-396); Entities (5026, 753, 1272); Relationships (8893, 3057, 4513)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic data systems and networked testing form a significant technical capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS is responsible for building, centrally managing, operating, maintaining, and upgrading road-traffic and related specialized databases. The described data includes vehicle registration, driver training and testing, licences, violations, accidents, and licence-point changes; the Ministry’s systems are also described as exchanging information with other agencies. [Data: Reports (2-393); Entities (3019, 1243); Relationships (4230)]

At the Department, test computers connect over the Ministry’s WAN to a Department-hosted server, and the testing system stores connection and data-editing logs. These details establish networked operational dependencies, but the supplied information does not describe cybersecurity controls, incidents, access policies, or system reliability. [Data: Reports (2-396); Entities (5026)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Digital public services support applications and licence-point notifications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MPS Public Service Portal accepts specified notices, applications, and examination dossiers, provides access to shared road-traffic database information, and can deliver administrative-violation decisions and related documents to users’ registered accounts. [Data: Reports (2-393); Entities (3023); Relationships (8845)]

The licence-point restoration process includes notifying the licence holder and updating restored-point status. Notices may be delivered directly, by post, or electronically through a registered portal or Traffic Application account; the records make electronic delivery conditional on necessary infrastructure and technical or information conditions. A separate MPS-developed mobile application is also identified as a channel for point-deduction notifications, and the records do not establish whether the application descriptions refer to the same product. [Data: Reports (2-404); Entities (1704, 3046, 4196, 4990); Relationships (6526, 8847, 8888)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The MPS coordinates with other government bodies and foreign representatives
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry coordinates with relevant ministries and sectors on traffic governance and international cooperation. Its responsibilities also include maintaining a database concerning foreign motor vehicles driven in Vietnam and coordinating specified procedures and responses to violations, accidents, or incidents. [Data: Reports (2-393); Entities (3019, 2316, 4105); Relationships (8864, 7426)]

Foreign consular agencies and representative offices of intergovernmental international organizations are connected to specified vehicle-related procedures and notification duties. The records describe these administrative relationships, not particular incidents or wrongdoing by those offices, applicants, or other parties. [Data: Reports (2-396, 2-393); Entities (1101, 4151); Relationships (8867, 3943)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish formal responsibilities, not compliance or reputation outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material describes statutory mandates, procedures, and administrative powers, including responsibilities assigned under cited laws, decrees, and ministerial instruments. It does not provide case histories, audit findings, enforcement outcomes, or evidence of how consistently the responsibilities are carried out. [Data: Reports (2-393, 2-396); Entities (3019, 3001, 5026)]

Accordingly, the community’s high rating reflects the scale and significance of its public authority and information systems. It should not be interpreted as a finding of misconduct, effective enforcement, legal compliance, or operational failure. [Data: Reports (2-393, 2-396); Entities (3019, 5026)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Framework: Law and Decree 151/2024
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on Vietnam’s Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety and Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, which details implementation across education, traffic-safety data, vehicle operation, priority-vehicle signaling, and foreign-vehicle participation. The framework is connected to later amendments, notably Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP and Law 118/2025/QH15, and includes specific border procedures under Article 32. Its provisions establish broad administrative and technical controls, but the available records do not show how they are implemented or whether entities comply in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because this is a broad national road-safety framework affecting public agencies, road users, vehicle operations, safety data, and cross-border traffic, although its real-world outcomes are not established by the records.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad, interconnected national regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as implementing the Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety. Their connected subject areas include road-safety education, database governance, vehicle operation, priority signals, and participation by foreign vehicles and drivers. [Data: Entities (1270, 2851); Relationships (4410, 4376, 4419)]

The decree is described as applying to domestic and foreign agencies, organizations, and individuals involved in road traffic order and safety matters in Vietnam. This breadth makes the framework consequential across public administration and road use, though the records do not assess its practical effects. [Data: Reports (2-410)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework is subject to amendments and staged effective dates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 184/2025/NĐ-CP is connected to Decree 151 through amendments and supplements, while Law 118/2025/QH15 directly amends provisions of the road-traffic law. The community therefore reflects both implementation through decrees and a separate legislative amendment route. [Data: Entities (1295, 2851); Relationships (4366); Reports (2-419)]

The supplied material states that Law 118/2025/QH15 generally takes effect on July 1, 2026, with a specified provision taking effect on January 1, 2026. It also says Article 2 of Decree 184 ceases to have effect on March 1, 2027, subject to exceptions whose details are not provided. [Data: Reports (2-419)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education is assigned to educational settings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151 provides for road-traffic legal education across educational levels and assigns related responsibilities to education authorities and institutions. The described content includes safe motorbike-riding instruction for students; vocational establishments are also linked to the decree’s education provisions. [Data: Entities (1270, 1728, 5615); Relationships (4376, 4511)]

These records establish that education is part of the regulatory design, not whether instruction has been delivered, its quality, or its effect on safety behavior. [Data: Reports (2-410)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic-safety data provisions describe extensive information flows
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Articles 9–15 are described as governing the creation, management, use, connection, and sharing of the road traffic order and safety database. The listed information categories include vehicle and driver records, insurance, accidents, violations, transport businesses, journeys, and driver images; Article 13, clause 1 addresses adding and adjusting database information. [Data: Entities (1270, 5285, 238); Relationships (4502, 727)]

The records describe a regulatory scope for data collection and exchange, including links to other and customs databases. They do not establish the database’s actual technical architecture, security controls, privacy safeguards, operational performance, or how information is used in practice. [Data: Reports (2-410)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signaling is subject to technical and permit controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree covers management, installation, and use of priority-vehicle signaling equipment, including technical requirements and permit issuance, replacement, reissuance, and revocation. Appendix I is described as setting technical requirements, and Form No. 02A is identified as an application form for a new permit. [Data: Entities (2960, 191, 2360, 4237); Relationships (4419, 4389, 4476)]

Revocation grounds include an ineligible recipient or an expired permit; the records also describe revocation where equipment is damaged beyond repair or has reached the end of its service life. These are stated regulatory conditions, not evidence that a particular permit was revoked. [Data: Entities (4221, 4222, 1905); Relationships (4473, 4474, 4380)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle operation and licensing provisions define administrative controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses licensing operations of intelligent or smart transport vehicles, including application and permit processes, and identifies specified grounds for operating-license revocation, such as a forged application or issuance by an authority lacking proper jurisdiction. [Data: Entities (2909, 3376, 4226, 3381); Relationships (4414, 4440, 4444)]

Other regulated subjects include rudimentary vehicles, journey-monitoring equipment, student transport, and safety measures for overweight, tracked, or exceptionally large or heavy vehicles. The material describes categories and controls but does not document individual licensing decisions, violations, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (1270, 3518, 4976); Relationships (4454, 4496)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign vehicle participation is linked to border and customs procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 governs foreign motor vehicles and foreign drivers participating in traffic in Vietnam, connecting entry and exit with customs clearance and temporary import and re-export procedures. The records also describe permitted periods of participation as related to immigration and visa periods. [Data: Entities (370, 1816, 1902); Relationships (1572, 1574, 1575, 1576, +more)]

The described exit provisions allow a foreign national to remain for up to 10 additional days if an unforeseen incident prevents departure, subject to prescribed procedures. The records do not specify ordinary duration limits, detailed procedural requirements, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Reports (2-424)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Right-hand-drive vehicle use and violations are addressed by regulation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree addresses organizations and individuals bringing right-hand-drive cars into Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes, as well as procedures for handling violations involving previously approved arrangements. These links show that the framework includes approval and violation-handling mechanisms. [Data: Entities (3440, 2653, 4183, 4262); Relationships (4449, 4399, 4472, 4478)]

The presence of these provisions does not establish that a violation occurred or that any organization or individual failed to comply. [Data: Reports (2-410)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Compliance and performance evidence is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material describes legal provisions, administrative procedures, technical requirements, and regulatory subjects. It does not provide compliance rates, implementation quality, enforcement results, operational database details, or reputational assessments of the entities involved. [Data: Reports (2-410, 2-419, 2-424)]

Accordingly, the framework’s potential importance is supported by its scope, but conclusions about effectiveness or actual safety outcomes cannot be drawn from these records alone. [Data: Entities (1270, 2851); Reports (2-410)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam National Defence, Road Safety and Foreign-Vehicle Management
v.tom_tat: This community links Vietnam’s Ministry of National Defence and military functions with national road-safety rules and the administration of foreign nationals driving foreign vehicles in Vietnam. The Ministry connects military driver regulation, vehicle inspections, signal-device permits, specialized databases, and border procedures to a broader network of ministries and agencies. Decrees No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP and No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP provide regulatory and procedural links, including vehicle requirements, intelligent-transport permits, foreign-vehicle approvals, and information sharing. The records establish broad public responsibilities and administrative capabilities, but do not establish implementation outcomes, actual compliance, or adverse conduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public impact because it connects national defence, road-safety regulation, border operations, and multi-ministry management of foreign vehicles, although the records do not show adverse conduct or implementation outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry of National Defence is a central institutional hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is associated with military transport and driver regulation, road-traffic responsibilities, specialized information management, and border procedures. Its links to the Minister, military forces, road-safety provisions, and other ministries make it a central coordinating authority in this community. [Data: Entities (3017, 3018); Relationships (8711, 8731, 8775, 8808, 8802)]

The records describe assigned functions rather than measured results. They do not show how effectively these responsibilities are carried out or establish particular compliance outcomes. [Data: Reports (2-479)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Military driving and vehicle oversight combines regulation and inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister of National Defense is described as setting rules for military driver training, testing, age requirements, and licences. The Ministry’s responsibilities also include vehicle registration and inspection procedures and technical-safety and environmental-quality certification for vehicles within its remit. [Data: Entities (3000, 3018, 2988); Relationships (8709, 8731, 8698, 3081)]

The community records identify military road inspections and oversight of the military control force, but do not report inspection findings, violation rates, or specific instances of misconduct. [Data: Reports (2-479); Entities (3017, 2990, 2991); Relationships (8701, 8702, 8704)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency vehicle signal permissions have a defined defence remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is among the authorities responsible for issuing, reissuing, or revoking permits for signal-emitting equipment on priority vehicles within its management area. The records describe an administrative division in which matters managed by National Defence are excluded from the stated responsibilities of the Ministry of Public Security. [Data: Entities (3017, 2775, 4224); Relationships (8120, 8839, 8711)]

Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP provides that permits for vehicles assigned emergency duties expire when the relevant emergency ends. The supplied information does not identify permit holders or establish that any particular permit was issued, revoked, or used. [Data: Entities (1308); Reports (2-486)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign-vehicle management depends on cross-ministry coordination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Management of foreign nationals driving foreign motor vehicles in Vietnam involves the Ministries of National Defence, Culture, Sports and Tourism, Foreign Affairs, and Finance. Decree No. 236/2026/NĐ-CP is linked to sending approval documents to ministries for coordination, while the approval procedure covers tourism and specified non-tourism cases, including right-hand-drive vehicles. [Data: Entities (2955, 1313, 226, 3010, 3013); Relationships (5735, 5736, 5737, 667, 8657)]

Local People’s Committees and foreign representative agencies also appear in the described coordination framework. These records establish administrative roles and information flows, not the outcomes of particular applications or evidence of failures in coordination. [Data: Reports (2-482); Entities (3013); Relationships (7504, 7502)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety rules cover specified vehicle technologies and categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree No. 151/2024/NĐ-CP covers journey-monitoring devices for specified commercial vehicles, driver-image recording for specified vehicle types, operating permits for intelligent-transport vehicles, and conditions for rudimentary vehicles. It also includes identifying-sign and exterior-colour requirements for vehicles transporting preschool children and pupils. [Data: Entities (1308); Reports (2-486)]

These provisions indicate a regulatory framework for particular vehicle types and uses. The records do not provide technical specifications, installation rates, licensing decisions, or evidence of real-world compliance. [Data: Entities (1308); Reports (2-486)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized databases are an important information-management capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of National Defence is described as managing specialized information on vehicle registration and inspection, driver training and licensing, road accidents, and administrative violations. Its database responsibilities connect defence transport administration with the wider road-traffic information environment. [Data: Entities (3017, 3018, 134); Relationships (447)]

The Ministry of Finance is separately responsible for databases concerning imported and exported vehicles, vehicle-sale documents, registration fees, and customs information. The records describe these data-management responsibilities but do not specify system architecture, security controls, or technical performance. [Data: Entities (3012); Reports (2-479, 2-482)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Border and temporary-import procedures link transport management to border operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
At border gates under its management, the Ministry of National Defence is described as organizing entry and exit inspections, conducting border procedures, and issuing or modifying visas and temporary-residence certificates. It also coordinates with other state agencies on vehicles completing temporary-import and re-export procedures. [Data: Entities (3017); Reports (2-479)]

The Ministry’s coordination with the Ministry of Finance on temporary import and re-export of foreign motor vehicles connects these border functions with the broader framework for foreign vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam. No particular vehicle, border incident, or procedural outcome is identified. [Data: Entities (3012, 3017); Relationships (8802, 5698)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish adverse reputation or verified compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information describes legal responsibilities, regulatory procedures, coordination arrangements, and database duties. It does not provide allegations, sanctions, verified violations, or praise that would support a conclusion about the reputation of the ministries or other entities. [Data: Reports (2-479, 2-482, 2-486)]

Likewise, the existence of rules and oversight responsibilities does not establish whether organizations or vehicle operators comply with them in practice. Assessing implementation, effectiveness, or compliance would require evidence beyond the records provided. [Data: Entities (1308, 1313, 3017); Reports (2-479, 2-482, 2-486)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Traffic Safety and Pedestrian Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road traffic and the rules governing pedestrians, vehicle operators, and groups needing particular consideration, including children, pregnant women, older or frail people, and people with disabilities. Article 30 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 is a key connection for participation rules, while Article 10 is associated with specified pedestrian fines and, in a separate decree, road-traffic database development. The records describe legal duties and safety measures, but do not establish whether any person or entity complies with them in practice. [Data: Entities (4313, 232, 364, 3619, 5432); Relationships (9484, 1493, 693, 681)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety importance because it connects rules for everyday road users, crossing protections, and penalties, although the records describe regulations rather than documented incidents or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pedestrians and vehicle operators are linked by shared safety duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Pedestrians are expected to follow traffic rules and use sidewalks, shoulders, pedestrian-only paths, and designated crossings where available. Vehicle operators, in turn, must observe conditions and slow down or stop when necessary; at flashing yellow signals they must yield to pedestrians when required. [Data: Entities (3619, 5432); Relationships (9490, 10659)]

These reciprocal obligations make pedestrian–vehicle interaction a central safety theme in the community. The records describe required conduct, not evidence about how frequently it is followed or the rate of traffic incidents. [Data: Entities (3619, 5432); Relationships (10018, 9490)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 30 organizes rules for pedestrians and groups with additional support needs
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 30 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 is associated with pedestrian rules and the participation in road traffic of children, pregnant women, older or frail people, people with disabilities, and people lacking civil act capacity. The data distinguishes this law provision from Article 30 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which concerns penalties and licence-point deductions for ambulance drivers. [Data: Entities (364, 3619, 822, 3663, 3841); Relationships (1493, 1485, 1495)]

This shared article number refers to different subjects depending on the legal instrument; the records do not support treating the two provisions as one rule. [Data: Entities (364)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Crossing protections combine designated infrastructure, driver precautions, and assistance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Pedestrians are directed to use designated crossings where available, including pedestrian overpasses and tunnels. The crossing-area records also state that overtaking is prohibited in the designated area and that vehicle operators must observe, slow down, or stop when pedestrians or wheelchair users are crossing. [Data: Entities (4276, 3607, 3611, 3617); Relationships (9471, 9477, 9480, 10018, 9474)]

The records identify children under seven, pregnant women, elderly or frail people, people with disabilities, and people lacking civil act capacity as groups who may need assistance crossing. They also specify that children under seven must be accompanied by an adult. [Data: Entities (825, 3841, 1749, 3663, 3660); Relationships (3212, 3213, 6783, 6628, 9522)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Pedestrian violations are subject to specified administrative fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 10 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP lists pedestrian violations and specifies fines of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong for the covered conduct. Examples in the records include crossing at an unauthorized place, crossing a median barrier, crossing without a required hand signal, and walking outside the designated part of the road. [Data: Entities (232, 3615, 5622, 1153, 1161); Relationships (693, 684, 683, 685, 696)]

A separate listed violation—carrying bulky objects that obstruct traffic—is associated with a fine of 400,000 to 600,000 VND. These are descriptions of specified penalties; the records do not establish that a particular pedestrian committed a violation or received a fine. [Data: Entities (728, 2576); Relationships (3014, 7829)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 10 has multiple legal meanings in the supplied records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description states that Article 10 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerns pedestrian administrative penalties, while Article 10 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 sets out general rules for road users. Article 10 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP instead concerns development of databases on road-traffic order and safety and specialized databases. [Data: Entities (232); Relationships (693, 681, 682)]

This is an important interpretation caveat: an Article 10 reference alone does not identify which subject or instrument is meant. The database provisions are present in the community, but no implementation status or technical details are provided. [Data: Entities (232, 1098, 1099); Relationships (681, 682)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-operator rules extend beyond pedestrian crossings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe operators’ duties to observe traffic conditions, adjust speed, or stop when necessary, including at flashing yellow signals and in designated settings such as school, hospital, market, and road-construction areas. They also mention safe following distances, with greater distance required in adverse conditions. [Data: Entities (5432, 5494, 4275, 4620, 2495); Relationships (10659, 10017, 10404, 7749, 6360)]

Other provisions address penalties or consequences for particular operator categories and conduct, including specialized motorcycle operation and overloaded or over-dimensioned vehicles. The information is regulatory in scope and does not indicate the compliance record of any operator. [Data: Entities (4702, 5432, 4313); Relationships (10056)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education and passenger protections are part of the wider framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road-traffic legal education is described as teaching safety and legal knowledge, especially to children and students, including helmet use and awareness of accident risks and responses. The records connect children with this education and identify lower-secondary educational institutions as settings for it. [Data: Entities (4375, 822, 2935); Relationships (3201, 8629)]

The broader road-traffic description also includes seat-belt requirements for drivers and passengers where seats are equipped, alongside rules for safe conduct and following distance. These provisions show that the community covers more than pedestrian crossings, though no evidence is provided about educational outcomes or actual seat-belt use. [Data: Entities (4313, 3590); Relationships (9452)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Road-Traffic Article 11 Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on “Article 11,” a label that refers to provisions in multiple Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one uniform rule. The records connect it to penalties for traffic violations by people handling animals or driving animal-drawn vehicles, including a specified fine for leaving an animal-drawn vehicle without a handler. They also describe vehicle registration and import/export information collected for a road-traffic database. The records establish regulatory subject matter but do not identify specific organizations or individuals as noncompliant.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it spans road-safety penalties and vehicle-registration and import/export records, while the data does not establish specific noncompliance or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 11” refers to provisions in multiple instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity description identifies Article 11 provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments, including Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT, Law 36/2024/QH15, Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP. The applicable subject therefore depends on which instrument is meant; these provisions should not be treated as one rule. [Data: Entities (235)]

The records distinguish road-safety subjects, vehicle database information, administrative penalties, and amendments to another article. They provide no information establishing whether any person or organization complied with, or violated, a particular provision. [Data: Entities (235)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic penalties concern animal handlers and animal-drawn vehicle drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe Article 11 as addressing road-traffic violations by people who control or guide animals and people who operate animal-drawn vehicles. The relationship records connect these road-user categories to the violation category and to Article 11’s penalties. [Data: Entities (187, 5555, 5556); Relationships (568, 569, 718, 719)]

This identifies the categories of conduct and road users covered, but does not report particular incidents or identify any specific person as having committed a violation. [Data: Entities (187, 5555, 5556); Relationships (568, 569, 718, 719)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific fine applies to an animal-drawn vehicle without a handler
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed violation is allowing an animal to pull a vehicle without anyone controlling it. The entity description states a fine of 150,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese đồng for this conduct, and the relationship links the violation to Article 11. [Data: Entities (156); Relationships (501)]

The supplied information gives the fine range but does not provide further details about enforcement, frequency, or any case in which the fine was imposed. [Data: Entities (156); Relationships (501)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle import and export records include traceability details
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 11 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP says the road-traffic order and safety database includes information about vehicle origins and imports or exports. The relationship records identify importing and exporting organizations and enterprises, customs-declaration issuing authorities, and import/export border gates as information included in those records. [Data: Entities (235, 2567, 1170, 2560); Relationships (712, 706, 711)]

No particular business, issuing authority, or border gate is named in the supplied data. These entries describe types of recorded information, not evidence of wrongdoing by an identified party. [Data: Entities (2567, 1170, 2560)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The database also covers vehicle registration and management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 11 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as covering information about the registration and management of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles. A relationship explicitly connects this activity to Article 11. [Data: Entities (235, 3095); Relationships (714)]

The records do not specify the systems, agencies, or operational practices used to maintain this information, so no further assessment of technical capability or data handling can be supported. [Data: Entities (235, 3095); Relationships (714)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a regulatory overview, not a compliance or reputation judgment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe legal topics, covered road-user categories, a fine range, and categories of information recorded in a database. They do not provide claims about an identified entity’s legal history, reputation, or actual compliance conduct. [Data: Entities (156, 187, 235, 2567, 3095); Relationships (501, 568, 712, 714, 718)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is grounded in the scope of the described traffic rules and recordkeeping provisions; the supplied data does not establish a specific threat, adverse reputation, or actual violation. [Data: Entities (235, 5555, 5556); Relationships (568, 718, 719)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Foreign Vehicle Approval and State Authorities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s foreign vehicle entry and use approval process and the competent state authorities that administer relevant requirements. The process covers arrangements for foreign visitors to bring vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as certain right-hand-drive vehicle use for non-tourism purposes. Authorities may require unresolved legal violations, traffic accidents, or vehicle-related incidents to be settled; unresolved matters and continued violations after suspension may affect approval. Vietnamese international travel businesses are identified as potential organizers for tourism-related vehicle entry. The records describe administrative and legal conditions, but do not establish particular applicants’ compliance, technical capabilities, or reputational standing.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful regulatory impact because state authorities can require resolution of violations and incidents and unresolved matters may affect approval or continuation of an activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Competent state authorities are the central oversight entities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent state authorities are described as government bodies with legal authority over the relevant matters, including driving tests and legal violations or traffic accidents involving foreign visitors or foreign motor vehicles. They may require outstanding matters to be resolved, and an authority that previously issued an approval may suspend the related activity until a violation is settled. [Data: Entities (1063)]

Their connections to unresolved accidents, legal violations, incidents caused by foreign vehicles, and continued violations after suspension make them the central oversight node in the supplied relationships. [Data: Relationships (3850, 3849, 3847, 3844)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The approval process covers defined foreign-vehicle use cases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The approval process concerns arrangements for foreign visitors to bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism, as well as an organization or individual bringing a right-hand-drive car into Vietnamese traffic for non-tourism purposes. The process may result in approval or refusal under the conditions described in Decree 151/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (2342)]

The records connect the process to unresolved prior legal violations and traffic accidents or vehicle-related incidents as potential grounds for refusal. They do not establish how any particular application was decided. [Data: Relationships (7528, 7529)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unresolved violations can affect approval
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Prior legal violations involving foreign visitors are relevant when requirements imposed by a competent authority have not been fully fulfilled by the applicant. The approval process lists such unresolved violations as a potential ground for refusing approval. [Data: Entities (3861), Relationships (3849, 7528)]

This describes a condition in the process, not evidence that a named visitor or applicant has committed a violation or that an application has actually been refused.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unresolved accidents and vehicle incidents are also relevant
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify prior traffic accidents involving foreign visitors or foreign vehicles for which authority requirements remain unfulfilled. Those unresolved requirements are connected to the approval process as a potential ground for refusal. [Data: Entities (3862), Relationships (3850, 7529)]

Incidents caused by foreign motor vehicles are separately identified as matters that authorities may require to be resolved, and unresolved incidents may affect approval. The records do not provide details about specific incidents, their severity, or their outcomes. [Data: Entities (2634), Relationships (3847)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vietnamese international travel businesses may organize tourism-related vehicle entry
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnamese international travel businesses are described as businesses that provide international travel services and may organize foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism. Their role is linked to the foreign vehicle entry and use approval process. [Data: Entities (5547), Relationships (7532)]

The supplied information establishes a potential organizing role, but does not identify any particular business or provide evidence about its compliance, operational capacity, or conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Continued violations after suspension are a stated refusal ground
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Continued conduct that had previously been suspended, even after a competent authority requested that the matter be resolved, is identified as a ground for refusing approval. [Data: Entities (1109), Relationships (3844)]

The records also state that an authority that previously issued an approval may suspend the related activity until the violation has been settled. Together, these provisions show that unresolved matters can have consequences beyond an initial approval decision, though no specific suspension or applicant is documented here. [Data: Entities (1063)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is regulatory, not a profile of technical capability or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe the approval process, authority responsibilities, potential refusal grounds, and the possible organizing role of travel businesses. They do not provide evidence about the technical capabilities, reputation, or actual legal-compliance status of any named business or individual. [Data: Entities (1063, 2342, 5547); Relationships (7528, 7529, 7532)]

Accordingly, the community’s documented significance is administrative and regulatory; stronger conclusions about specific actors or outcomes are not supported by these records.

v.tieu_de: Receiving Authority Permit and Application Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Receiving Authority and two administrative processes: permit issuance or reissuance for signal devices on priority vehicles, and application review and approval associated with international travel-service businesses proposing foreign visitors’ motor vehicles in Vietnam. The authority reviews submissions, communicates ineligibility in writing, and makes decisions on complete applications within two working days; for the permit procedure, direct handling also requires entry of permit information into a management database. The records describe procedural requirements, but do not establish actual compliance, application outcomes, or enforcement activity. [Data: Entities (3693, 4041, 221, 2746, 5645, +more); Relationships (9583, 9584, 9582, 9839, 650, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it defines time-bound administrative decisions and eligibility processes relevant to permit applicants and international travel-service businesses, while the records show no specific adverse event or compliance failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Receiving Authority is the central administrative actor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Receiving Authority connects the permit issuance and reissuance procedure with the application review and approval procedure. Its stated functions include reviewing documents, notifying applicants about incomplete submissions or ineligibility, accepting qualifying applications, and issuing permits or decisions. [Data: Entities (4041, 3693, 221); Relationships (9583, 650, 9838)]

This central role makes the authority the main point through which the described applicants and procedures interact. The records describe its assigned functions, not whether it has carried them out correctly in any particular case. [Data: Entities (4041); Relationships (9583, 650, 8068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The procedures specify a two-working-day decision timeline
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the permit procedure, the review period begins when the authority receives a complete and valid application, and the procedure provides for review within two working days. The receipt event is explicitly identified as the trigger for that period. [Data: Entities (3693, 4038); Relationships (9582, 9838)]

The separate application review and approval procedure also specifies an approval decision within two working days after complete documents are received. Together, these provisions establish clear processing expectations, but the records do not indicate actual processing times or whether deadlines were met. [Data: Entities (221, 4041); Relationships (650, 9838)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit issuance concerns signal devices on priority vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Permit Issuance and Reissuance Procedure governs applications to issue or reissue permits for using signal devices on priority vehicles. The Receiving Authority reviews such applications and issues or reissues permits under this procedure. [Data: Entities (3693, 4041); Relationships (9583)]

Where an application is handled directly, the permit information must be entered into a management database. This is a stated recordkeeping requirement; the available information does not describe the database’s technical design, security, or operational performance. [Data: Entities (3693)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ineligible permit applicants are to receive written reasons
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The permit procedure provides for a written explanation when eligibility conditions are not met, and the Receiving Authority is described as issuing a written response that explains why an applicant does not qualify. [Data: Entities (5645, 4041); Relationships (9584, 9839)]

This requirement provides an explicit communication step for negative eligibility decisions. The records do not provide examples of notices, appeal mechanisms, or information about how often applicants are found ineligible. [Data: Entities (5645, 4041); Relationships (9584, 9839)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: International travel-service businesses may apply for approval
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community also includes Vietnamese international travel-service businesses that may seek approval to organize foreign visitors bringing foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam for tourism. These businesses may submit applications under the review and approval procedure, with the Receiving Authority reviewing them and potentially issuing approval. [Data: Entities (2746, 221, 4041); Relationships (649, 8068, 650)]

This connects the administrative process to travel-service activity involving foreign visitors and vehicles. The supplied records establish that businesses may apply, but do not identify any specific business, application, approval, or resulting trip. [Data: Entities (2746); Relationships (649, 8068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe procedural rules, not demonstrated compliance or technical capacity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available information sets out responsibilities, decision timing, eligibility communications, and a database-entry requirement for directly handled permit applications. It does not report audit findings, violations, disputes, actual decision outcomes, or evidence that the stated procedures are being followed in practice. [Data: Entities (3693, 4041, 5645, 221); Relationships (9582, 9584, 9839, 650)]

Likewise, the database reference supports only the existence of a management-recording requirement; it does not establish broader technical capabilities such as system architecture or cybersecurity controls. No reputation-related claims are included in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3693)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Licensing Authority, Decree 236 and Digital Permit Channels
v.tom_tat: This community links Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP and the Licensing Authority with Vietnam’s National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal, applicants, permit procedures, and the Vehicle Registration and Management System. Together, the records describe administrative pathways for priority-vehicle signaling devices, intelligent traffic vehicle permits, and specified foreign vehicles, including application review, data checks, notices, decisions, and defined deadlines. The digital platforms are described as channels for submissions and status communications, with additional identity-verification and enforcement-document functions. The information establishes regulatory responsibilities and stated processes, not actual compliance, performance, security, or adverse conduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial public importance because it connects national road-traffic rules, licensing decisions, digital government channels, vehicle-registration data, and specified immigration notifications, while the records provide no evidence of actual misconduct or operational failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A national regulatory and administrative network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP is the central regulatory instrument described in this community, amending rules and procedures involving priority-vehicle signal devices, intelligent traffic vehicles, and foreign motor vehicles. The Licensing Authority is the operational hub, receiving and reviewing applications and deciding whether to issue, replace, renew, reissue, or revoke permits where applicable. [Data: Entities (1297, 2904); Relationships (5655)]

The decree is connected to both digital application channels, while the authority is connected to applicants, permit procedures, notices, and vehicle-registration checks. This structure makes the community relevant to public administration and road-traffic regulation, but the records do not establish how the rules are implemented in individual cases. [Data: Relationships (5657, 5658, 8584, 8585, 8602)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Digital channels support applications and administrative notices
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The National Identification Application and National Public Service Portal are described as channels through which individuals, organizations, vehicle owners, and authorized representatives may submit applications and follow-up documents. The Licensing Authority may also use their accounts to send notices about incomplete, deficient, or ineligible submissions. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209); Relationships (8584, 8585, 5657, 5658)]

The records further associate the platforms with delivery of administrative-violation documents; the Portal is also described as providing public access to information from the road traffic order and safety database. These are stated service functions, not evidence about service availability, user volumes, security controls, or the outcomes of any specific case. [Data: Entities (3205, 3209); Relationships (9113)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit workflows include review, deadlines, and reasoned outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community describes distinct permit procedures with stated timelines. New permits for signaling devices on priority vehicles are to be issued within one working day after receipt of a complete application, while intelligent traffic vehicle operating permits are described as issued within five working days after receipt. [Data: Entities (3230, 3378, 2716); Relationships (8586, 8589, 8018)]

A separate description states that vehicle-registration data comparison for an intelligent-vehicle application occurs within seven working days, and replacement or reissuance of an intelligent traffic vehicle permit is described as taking up to two working days. These timelines relate to different steps or procedures and should not be treated as a single universal deadline. [Data: Entities (3379, 5475, 2717); Relationships (8603, 8590, 8599)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-registration data is used in intelligent-vehicle permit review
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For intelligent transport vehicle operating-permit applications, the Licensing Authority reviews the submitted information and compares it with vehicle registration data held in the Vehicle Registration and Management System. The application description identifies vehicle quality or inspection-exemption information, registration data, and vehicle-owner documents among the required materials. [Data: Entities (220, 2722, 5467); Relationships (644, 8602, 8026)]

This establishes a data-dependent administrative process, but the supplied records do not describe the system’s security, accuracy, access controls, or wider technical capabilities. It would therefore be unsupported to infer either a security weakness or a particular level of technical assurance. [Data: Entities (5467); Relationships (8602, 8603)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Deficiency handling and refusals are part of the prescribed process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When application materials do not meet requirements, the Licensing Authority may notify the applicant, request supplementation or completion, or refuse to process the procedure; the described notice is to state the reason. For an operating-permit application that does not qualify, the authority is described as providing a written refusal explaining the reasons. [Data: Entities (3271, 3270, 4157, 3382); Relationships (8588, 8591, 8594, 8596, 651)]

These provisions indicate procedural routes for deficient applications and reasoned decisions. The records do not provide examples, counts, or audits of actual notices and refusals, so they do not demonstrate how consistently these steps occur in practice. [Data: Reports (2-460); Relationships (8587, 8591, 8596)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified foreign-vehicle cases require coordination with immigration management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Licensing Authority’s remit includes licensing certain foreign vehicles participating in traffic in Vietnam, including foreign-registered right-hand-drive cars and vehicles brought into Vietnam by foreign visitors for tourism. Article 55 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 is identified as setting requirements for these categories and requiring immediate notification to the Immigration Management Authority in specified circumstances. [Data: Entities (2904, 2835, 2554); Relationships (8421, 7815)]

The decree also describes procedures concerning international travel service businesses organizing foreign visitors’ vehicles and right-hand-drive cars used for non-tourism purposes. The relevant provisions are stated to take effect on 1 July 2027; the records do not establish implementation progress or the number or outcomes of cases. [Data: Entities (1297); Reports (2-472)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Representative and in-person routes supplement digital submission
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For specified permit changes or reissuance, an owner may act through an authorized representative, and the decree’s procedures also describe representatives submitting applications or surrendering permits on an owner’s behalf. The records establish a delegated route but do not describe how authorization is verified in individual cases. [Data: Entities (2717, 2718); Reports (2-472)]

Qualifying applications may also be submitted in person. The authority is described as accepting eligible documents and preparing a receipt with an expected result date, including in the priority-vehicle signal-device permit workflow. These are described procedural options; their frequency and actual processing performance are not provided. [Data: Entities (25, 2769, 217); Relationships (53, 8111, 636)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports public significance, not a finding of adverse conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records map responsibilities across the decree, Licensing Authority, digital channels, applicants, permit procedures, registration data, and immigration notification. They therefore support the community’s importance as a connected public-administration and road-traffic system. [Data: Reports (2-460, 2-467, 2-472)]

The supplied information describes rules, functions, and prescribed steps; it does not provide compliance audits, actual permit outcomes, security assessments, performance measurements, allegations, or reputational evidence. Conclusions about effectiveness, compliance in practice, or adverse impact beyond the significance of the functions described would exceed the available evidence. [Data: Reports (2-460, 2-467, 2-472)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Foreign-Vehicle Traffic and Oversight
v.tom_tat: This community describes Vietnam’s regulatory and administrative framework for foreign nationals and foreign motor vehicles using Vietnamese roads. Vietnam is the jurisdictional hub, connecting foreign drivers and vehicles, licensed international travel-service businesses, competent authorities, and provincial and city People’s Committees.
