phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe monetary and supplementary penalties, with limits on what can be inferred
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The FINE entity describes a monetary penalty of 5,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 3 for covered violations, including specified vehicle-condition violations committed by a driver. It also says that, for certain violations, a fine is imposed alongside deprivation of the right to use a motor vehicle inspector certificate. Article 40 is linked generally to fines and to the inspection-regulation violations. [Data: Entities (2095, 4232); Relationships (1937, 7083, 9984)]

The supplied records do not establish that the Clause 3 fine range applies to every violation discussed here, including the false-document conduct described under Clause 5. The range should therefore not be treated as a universal penalty for all conduct in this community.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspector-certificate deprivation is described as an additional penalty for specified conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe deprivation of the right to use a motor vehicle inspector certificate for one to three months as an additional penalty. The relationship linking this consequence to violations of motor vehicle inspection regulations states that it applies under Clause 6 when an act specified in Clause 1 is committed, in addition to a fine. [Data: Entities (4232, 5598); Relationships (9984, 1941)]

This penalty is tied in the supplied information to specified conduct and should not be generalized to every party or violation covered by Article 40. No record identifies an individual inspector whose certificate rights were actually deprived.

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Ownership Changes and Registration Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community describes the registration obligations that arise when a vehicle changes ownership and the violation and monetary fine associated with failing to complete the required procedures. The ownership change links to registration and license-plate requirements; failure to comply is connected to obtaining an updated registration certificate and plate and to a fine under Clause 7 of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The data describes an administrative road-traffic compliance issue, without providing fine amounts or evidence of broader impacts. [Data: Entities (1958, 5462, 789, 2780, 3057); Relationships (3133, 3134, 6910, 6911)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects a defined vehicle-registration compliance issue with a stated monetary penalty, while the provided information does not indicate impacts beyond this administrative and road-traffic context.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Change of ownership is the compliance trigger
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community centers on a vehicle transfer to a new owner. The description states that registration following the change must meet specified conditions and complete the required procedures for an updated certificate and license plate. [Data: Entities (789); Relationships (3133, 3134)]

This makes the ownership change the circumstance connecting the registration process to the potential violation. [Data: Relationships (3133, 3134)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration and license-plate procedures are the required action
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relevant administrative process concerns issuing or revoking registration certificates and license plates for motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles used in road traffic. The ownership-change description specifically links that process to registration requirements after a transfer. [Data: Entities (5462, 789); Relationships (3134)]

A separate entity identifies issuance of the vehicle registration certificate and license plate as the procedure that must be completed. [Data: Entities (2780)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation is failure to complete the required procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation is defined as failing to complete the required procedures for issuing a registration certificate and license plate after a change of owner. The relationship data explicitly connects the failure to both the ownership change and the issuance procedure. [Data: Entities (1958, 2780); Relationships (3133, 6910)]

The supplied information identifies this as a road-traffic violation but does not provide further details about enforcement practices or case outcomes. [Data: Entities (1958)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A monetary fine is specified, but no amounts are provided
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data states that Clause 7 of Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP prescribes a monetary fine for vehicle owners who fail to complete the registration and license-plate procedures after ownership changes. [Data: Entities (3057); Relationships (6911)]

It also states that the amounts differ for individuals and organizations, but the actual amounts are not included in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3057)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The documented impact is limited to administrative compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records concern vehicle ownership, registration documentation, license plates, and a monetary penalty. They do not provide evidence about the prevalence of noncompliance, broader public-safety effects, or impacts beyond the described road-traffic and administrative context. [Data: Entities (1958, 5462, 789, 3057); Relationships (3133, 3134, 6910, 6911)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Driver-Training Violations and Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 39, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its described penalties for certain driver-training violations. The provision is linked to interference with driver-training monitoring data and to a fine of 20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng; that fine is also associated with training outside the prescribed curriculum. The records describe regulatory provisions and potential violations, not evidence that a particular establishment committed them or that a penalty was imposed.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns defined penalties and monitoring integrity in driver training, but the records do not establish actual violations or enforcement.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 39, Clause 5 is the community’s regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 39, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting out fines for certain violations of regulations governing driver training and driving tests. It is linked both to the specified monetary penalty and to interference with driver-training monitoring data, making it the central regulatory entity in the available records. [Data: Entities (430); Relationships (1883, 1884)]

The information does not identify a specific training establishment, an enforcement action, or an instance in which the provision was applied. [Data: Entities (430); Relationships (1883, 1884)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Interference with monitoring data is identified as punishable conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define the violation as using technical measures, external equipment, or other means to interfere with monitoring equipment and falsify recorded theoretical study time or practical instruction time and distance. Article 39, Clause 5 is stated to describe this conduct as punishable. [Data: Entities (2728, 430); Relationships (1884)]

This concerns the integrity of recorded training and monitoring information; the records do not establish that any person or organization actually interfered with such data. [Data: Entities (2728); Relationships (1884)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine ranges from 20 million to 30 million đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A fine of 20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng is identified for violations described in Article 39, Clause 5, including training that does not follow prescribed content, programs, or curricula. The provision-to-fine relationship is explicit in the records. [Data: Entities (2168, 430); Relationships (1883)]

The fine is presented as a statutory penalty associated with listed violations, not as a fine shown to have been assessed in a particular case. [Data: Entities (2168); Relationships (1883, 7176)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training outside the prescribed curriculum is linked to the stated penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe this violation as a driver-training establishment providing instruction that does not comply with required content, programs, or curricula. They state a fine of 20,000,000 to 30,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for this conduct. [Data: Entities (5072, 2168)]

The relationship data links the fine to training outside the prescribed curriculum. No specific establishment, occurrence, or enforcement outcome is named. [Data: Relationships (7176)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence describes regulatory exposure, not actual noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe a legal provision, two categories of conduct, and a monetary penalty. They establish how these items are connected in the supplied data, but do not identify an investigated party or report an actual violation. [Data: Entities (430, 2728, 5072, 2168); Relationships (1883, 1884, 7176)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant to assessing driver-training compliance and monitoring controls, while any conclusion about real-world misconduct or enforcement would go beyond the evidence provided.

v.tieu_de: Car-Driving Tests, Candidates, Routes, and Examiners
v.tom_tat: This community describes a car-driving test conducted by candidates in road traffic on a designated route. Driving test examiners may supervise the vehicle’s steering. The available data also describes examiner documentation, qualifications, training, and examiner cards as matters prescribed or organized by the Minister of Transport. No claims about misconduct, reputational concerns, or specific compliance outcomes are provided.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has modest practical importance because it concerns a supervised driving examination in road traffic, while the data provides no evidence of an adverse incident or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The test links candidates, a designated route, and an examination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The car-driving test is described as an examination conducted in a test vehicle on a designated route under supervision. Candidates are identified as the people taking that examination, making them the central participants in the community. [Data: Entities (702, 703, 704); Relationships (2979, 2980)]

The relationships establish a compact operational structure: the test involves candidates and takes place on the designated route. [Data: Relationships (2979, 2980, 2981)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Candidates participate in road traffic using the designated route
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Candidates must use a designated test route while participating in road traffic, according to the entity descriptions and relationship data. This situates the examination in a traffic environment rather than describing it as a purely classroom or off-road assessment. [Data: Entities (703, 704); Relationships (2981)]

The data does not specify the route’s location, length, traffic conditions, or how routes are selected, so those details cannot be assessed from this community record. [Data: Entities (704); Relationships (2981)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examiners may supervise the test vehicle’s steering
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving test examiners conduct car-driving tests and may supervise a vehicle’s steering while candidates participate in road traffic. The relationship record specifically connects examiners to candidates through this supervisory role. [Data: Entities (1656, 703); Relationships (2982)]

The records do not describe the exact supervision procedure, examiner-to-candidate ratios, or any incidents. Accordingly, the data establishes a supervisory function but does not support conclusions about how it is carried out in practice. [Data: Entities (1656); Relationships (2982)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examiner standards and documentation are described as regulated responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The examiner description states that examiners must carry documents specified in Article 56(1). It also says the Minister of Transport prescribes examiner qualifications and standards, organizes their training, and provides for issuance of examiner cards. [Data: Entities (1656)]

These details indicate that the source describes formal requirements and administrative responsibilities. It does not provide the contents of Article 56(1), the standards themselves, or evidence of whether any particular examiner complies with them. [Data: Entities (1656)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available evidence is procedural and contains no adverse claims
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the test, its participants, route, and examiner roles. They contain no claims about legal violations, safety incidents, technical systems, organizational reputation, or misconduct. This absence limits the assessment to the community’s stated examination process rather than any unreported outcomes. [Data: Entities (702, 703, 704, 1656); Relationships (2979, 2980, 2981, 2982)]

v.tieu_de: Driver-Training Vehicle Compliance and Clause 2 of Article 39
v.tom_tat: This community concerns driver-training facilities, a specified vehicle-use violation, and Clause 2 of Article 39, which sets a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the listed violations. The relationships connect the clause to both the facilities and the violation, and identify the violation as attributable to facilities. The data describes a regulatory requirement but does not establish that any particular facility has committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate regulatory and safety relevance because it links a specific driver-training vehicle requirement to a monetary penalty, but the data describes a narrow rule and provides no evidence of an actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 2 establishes a specified fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 2 of Article 39 is described as specifying a fine of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese dong for driver-training facilities that commit the listed violations. This gives the community a concrete regulatory and financial dimension, though the supplied information does not identify a particular enforcement action or facility. [Data: Entities (913); Relationships (3401, 3402)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The vehicle-use violation concerns learner safeguards
phat_hien.giai_thich: The identified violation is using a training vehicle without a rain-and-sun canopy or without a securely attached seat in the vehicle bed for a learner. The data establishes these as the specific conditions relevant to the rule, but does not report an injury or other consequence. [Data: Entities (5329, 1534)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-training facilities are the regulated party
phat_hien.giai_thich: Driver-training facilities are the category of organizations associated with the stated vehicle-use violation. Clause 2 is linked to these facilities as the subject of fines for the specified conduct. [Data: Entities (1534, 913); Relationships (3401, 6221)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community forms a focused rule–party–conduct structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The three entities connect the legal provision, the regulated facilities, and the noncompliant vehicle use: the clause sets fines for facilities, the clause specifies a fine for the vehicle-use violation, and the violation is attributed to facilities. This describes a narrow compliance framework rather than a broad network of organizations or events. [Data: Relationships (3401, 3402, 6221)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data does not establish actual noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe the violation and the penalty associated with it, but name no specific facility and do not state that any facility has used a noncompliant vehicle. Accordingly, the information supports identifying a compliance requirement and potential fine, not concluding that a violation occurred. [Data: Entities (1534, 913, 5329); Relationships (3401, 3402, 6221)]

v.tieu_de: Driving Training Establishments and Article 39 Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community describes regulatory requirements and potential violations involving driving training establishments, vehicles, instructors, course records, and facilities. Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and its Clause 3 connect several specified training and testing violations to fines of 5,000,000–10,000,000 VND, while the records also identify a 20,000,000–30,000,000 VND penalty for certain covered violations. The material concerns general regulatory categories and does not identify a particular school as having committed a violation. [Data: Entities (1672, 426, 931, 2207, 2169); Relationships (1860, 1856, 6483, 6482, 7177)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it covers driver-training safety and regulatory compliance, but the supplied records describe general rules and violations rather than an identified establishment’s conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Regulatory framework links training violations to Article 39
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP addresses penalties for driver-training and driving-test violations, and Clause 3 specifies a fine of 5,000,000–10,000,000 VND for listed violations. The relationships explicitly connect the article and clause to that fine range. [Data: Entities (426, 931, 2207); Relationships (1860, 1856, 3443)]

The records establish a compliance framework, not evidence that any named or identifiable driving school has breached it. [Data: Entities (1672, 426)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle safety and instructor supervision are central concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The establishment is associated with a violation for using a training vehicle that lacks an auxiliary brake or has an ineffective one; the stated penalty for that violation is 5,000,000–10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (5314, 2206); Relationships (6485, 7239)]

The records also describe a violation for failing to provide required instructor supervision during practical driving or assigning an instructor who does not meet required standards. These provisions concern safeguards during learner driving, but the data does not document an actual incident or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (1537, 1672); Relationships (6224)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-class authorization is a distinct compliance requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driving training establishment may violate the rules by enrolling students in, or providing training for, a license class it is not authorized to teach. This requirement makes the establishment’s permitted scope of instruction a key compliance issue. [Data: Entities (1672, 5203); Relationships (6483)]

The relationship data associates unauthorized license-class enrollment or training with a fine of 20,000,000–30,000,000 VND. The records also describe the 5,000,000–10,000,000 VND range under Clause 3 for listed violations, so the supplied material presents different penalty mappings; it does not provide enough detail to reconcile their scope. [Data: Entities (2169, 2207, 931, 5203); Relationships (7177, 3443, 6483)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle permits and required markings are part of operational compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed vehicle-related violations include using a practice vehicle without a valid or unexpired permit, failing to display the required “Tập lái” sign, and failing to display the establishment’s name and phone number as required. [Data: Entities (5309, 1968, 1966); Relationships (6484, 6479, 6478)]

The relationships connect the permit and display violations to the 5,000,000–10,000,000 VND fine. These are specified regulatory consequences, not claims that any particular establishment’s vehicles lack permits or markings. [Data: Entities (2207, 5309, 1968, 1966); Relationships (7240, 6922, 6921)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recordkeeping and facility standards extend beyond vehicle operation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driving training facility is required to retain records for each training course, and failure to retain records or retaining them incompletely is identified as a violation. The relationship data associates this recordkeeping violation with a fine of 5,000,000–10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1675, 1671, 2048, 2206); Relationships (6476, 6477, 6494, 7033)]

The material also identifies inadequate classroom facilities or teaching equipment as a violation category. Together, these requirements show that the compliance scope includes course administration and learning facilities as well as vehicles and instruction. [Data: Entities (2015, 1672); Relationships (6480)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty descriptions have overlapping scopes that merit verification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a 5,000,000–10,000,000 VND range under Clause 3 and associate it with several listed matters, including permit and vehicle-marking violations. They separately associate a 20,000,000–30,000,000 VND fine with covered violations and specifically link that range to unauthorized license-class enrollment or training. [Data: Entities (2207, 931, 2169, 5203); Relationships (1860, 7240, 6922, 7177)]

Because the supplied descriptions do not fully explain how these penalty mappings interact, the applicable range for a particular fact pattern should not be inferred from this dataset alone. The data supports identifying the two stated ranges and the linked categories, but not resolving any legal ambiguity. [Data: Entities (2207, 2206, 2169); Relationships (3443, 7177, 7239)]

v.tieu_de: Driver Training Establishments and Article 39 Sanctions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on driver training establishments and the regulatory violations and sanctions associated with them under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The records connect establishments to possible violations involving licensed training locations, records, learner completion and certificates, training vehicles, and disclosure of required information. Listed consequences include fines of different amounts and a possible one-to-three-month suspension of admissions. These records describe rules and potential penalties; they do not establish that any particular establishment committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful regulatory and public-facing importance because the cited rules address training quality, learner certification, and substantial penalties, but the records identify no actual violations or specific establishments.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulatory community centered on driver training establishments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The core entities are driver training establishments, described as organizations or facilities providing driver training and subject to specified sanctions under Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The relationships connect establishments with covered violations and corresponding fine categories, indicating that the dataset primarily represents a regulatory framework rather than a set of named operators or enforcement cases. [Data: Entities (1494, 1673); Relationships (6112, 6126, 6487)]

The records do not name individual establishments or show their licensing status, compliance history, or operational performance. Accordingly, they support analysis of the rules’ potential significance, not conclusions about the conduct of any particular operator. [Data: Entities (1494, 1673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Licensed training locations and recordkeeping are compliance concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Training drivers at a location not listed on an establishment’s driver-training license is identified as a violation. A relationship specifically links this conduct to driver training establishments, and another links the unlicensed-location violation to a fine range of VND 10 million to VND 20 million. [Data: Entities (5254, 2134); Relationships (6131, 7130)]

The establishment description also identifies failures to retain required records, or keeping incomplete records for two or more training courses, as covered violations. This points to both operational authorization and documentation as areas regulated by the cited framework; the data does not report whether any operator has failed these requirements. [Data: Entities (1494)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improper course completion recognition or certificate issuance can affect learners
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify improperly recognizing a learner’s course completion or issuing a primary-level or training certificate contrary to regulations as a violation by a driver training establishment. A learner is explicitly connected to this violation, making the issue relevant to the integrity of training outcomes and credentials. [Data: Entities (2617, 2858); Relationships (6127, 7862)]

The establishment description associates this conduct with a VND 20 million to VND 30 million fine under Clause 5. This is a stated potential penalty, not evidence that improper recognition or issuance occurred in a specific case. [Data: Entities (1494, 54)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes multiple fine ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes a VND 10 million to VND 20 million fine for covered violations under Article 39, Clause 4, and links that range to driver training establishments and unlicensed-location training. [Data: Entities (2134, 5254); Relationships (6126, 7130)]

A separate VND 20 million to VND 30 million fine is associated with specified Clause 5 violations by training establishments. The records also identify a VND 3 million to VND 5 million fine under Article 39(2), but do not provide enough detail here to specify which conduct it covers. These are regulatory penalty descriptions, not recorded fines imposed on named operators. [Data: Entities (54, 56, 2575); Relationships (117, 6488)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training resources and information disclosure are regulated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving training establishments may be fined VND 20 million to VND 30 million for failing to provide enough practice vehicles to meet actual training demand or using vehicles of the wrong class for practical instruction. This connects regulatory exposure to training capacity and the suitability of practical-training vehicles. [Data: Entities (1673)]

The records also identify failure to publicly disclose recruitment rules, training-management rules, and tuition fees as a violation associated with establishments. They do not indicate whether any establishment failed to disclose these items or specify a penalty for this disclosure violation in the provided relationship. [Data: Entities (2021); Relationships (6486)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Suspension of admissions is a possible non-monetary sanction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The dataset describes an additional administrative sanction requiring an establishment to stop accepting admissions for one to three months. A relationship connects this sanction to driving training establishments that commit specified violations. [Data: Entities (4829); Relationships (6490)]

This sanction could interrupt intake at an affected establishment, but the records do not identify an actual suspension, its cause, or an affected operator. The evidence therefore establishes the existence of a potential regulatory consequence, not a realized disruption. [Data: Entities (4829); Relationships (6490)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Records include refresher-training certificate information, but not technical capability assessments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data associates information about road-traffic-law refresher training for specialized-motorcycle operators with driver-training establishment records. This indicates that the described recordkeeping scope includes certificate information for that training. [Data: Entities (4366); Relationships (6128)]

No evidence is provided about establishments’ technology, systems, equipment beyond the stated practice-vehicle requirements, or ability to deliver training effectively. The community’s technical capabilities and actual compliance therefore cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (1494, 1673, 4366)]

v.tieu_de: Practical Driving Learners, Instructors, and Violations
v.tom_tat: This community describes a practical driving arrangement centered on a learner, an instructor, and a lesson in which the instructor supervises the learner's steering. It also records that a learner commits a driving-related violation during practice and that an instructor who allows a specified violation may be subject to the applicable penalty. The information indicates a road-safety and regulatory-compliance concern, but does not establish the scale or broader consequences of any incident. [Data: Entities (1620, 1615, 1720, 3837, 3835); Relationships (6365, 6376, 6579)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the records describe a driving violation and potential instructor penalty in a supervised lesson, but provide no evidence of wider or recurring impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The learner is the central actor in the recorded violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The learner is described as practicing under an instructor's guidance and as committing a violation while practicing. The relationship records connect the learner directly to the driving-related violation. [Data: Entities (1620, 1720); Relationships (6376)]

The violation is described as one of the regulations referred to in Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, committed during practical driving. The records do not specify the conduct involved or the outcome of the violation. [Data: Entities (1720)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Instructor supervision is a stated part of practical driving
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driving instructor is described as teaching practical driving and supervising learners. During practical driving, the instructor is to sit beside the learner and supervise steering. [Data: Entities (1615); Relationships (6365)]

The instructor's presence is also tied specifically to a practical driving lesson, where the same supervision requirement is stated. The information establishes the described supervisory role but does not indicate whether it was fulfilled in the reported violation. [Data: Entities (3837); Relationships (6367)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records associate instructor permission with potential penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The practical driving instructor entry states that an instructor who allows a learner to commit a specified driving-related violation is subject to the penalty applicable to that violation. A relationship likewise links the violation to an instructor who allows it and is subject to the applicable penalty. [Data: Entities (3835, 1720); Relationships (6579)]

This describes a potential consequence tied to the specified circumstances; the records do not identify an actual penalty imposed, its amount, or a finding about any particular instructor.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The incident is situated within a practical lesson and instruction activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The practical driving lesson is defined as a setting where a learner practices driving and an instructor is required to sit beside the learner to supervise steering. The learner is separately linked to practicing during that lesson. [Data: Entities (3837); Relationships (6367, 6379)]

The learner's practice is also connected to the broader activity of practical driving instruction, and the instructor is described as teaching the learner. Together, these records frame the violation as occurring in a teaching and practice context, without providing further incident details. [Data: Entities (3834); Relationships (6377, 6378)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a focused safety and compliance concern, not a broader risk assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records combine a learner's driving-related violation with an instructor's stated supervisory role and a provision for an applicable penalty when an instructor allows a specified violation. These facts make safe supervision and compliance the principal concerns evidenced in this community. [Data: Entities (1615, 1620, 1720, 3835); Relationships (6365, 6376, 6579)]

No information is provided about injury, damage, recurrence, enforcement outcomes, or the prevalence of such violations. The community's impact should therefore be understood as limited to the documented training and regulatory context rather than evidence of a wider pattern.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Driver Training and Decree 168 Article 39
v.tom_tat: This community centers on driving instructors, learner drivers, and the regulated activities and settings of driver training and testing. Instructors supervise learners in practice yards and on public roads, and practical instruction is tied to an authorized route. The records describe badge and training-contract obligations, identify related violations, and specify fines for certain violations under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, Article 39. They describe regulatory requirements rather than actual compliance outcomes, and provide no reputation assessments.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because its rules govern supervised driving practice and testing in traffic settings, with specified fines for some compliance violations.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving instructors are the community’s central operational actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records place instructors at the center of practical driver training: they teach and supervise learner drivers, sit beside them to assist, and are associated with practice in yards and on public roads. [Data: Entities (1619, 2859, 1650); Relationships (6372, 6370, 6374)]

Practical instructors are also required to follow the route specified in the training vehicle’s permit. These duties establish a structured supervisory role, but the records do not state whether any particular instructor complied or failed to comply. [Data: Entities (1619, 628); Relationships (2808)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Learner practice is subject to badge and supervision requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Learner drivers are described as practicing in a training vehicle under an instructor’s supervision and as being required to display and wear a learner-driver badge. The records connect learners to practice in driving yards and on public traffic roads. [Data: Entities (2859, 1650, 4001); Relationships (6408, 8509)]

Practicing without the required learner badge is identified as a violation involving both the instructor who allows it and the learner who practices without displaying or wearing the badge. The supplied records do not specify a fine for this learner-badge violation. [Data: Entities (3839); Relationships (6373, 8508)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Instructor badge violations have a specified monetary penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Teaching without wearing the prescribed driving-instructor badge is identified as a violation by an instructor. Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as setting a fine of 2,000,000–3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for this violation. [Data: Entities (4855, 1276, 2163); Relationships (6375, 7172, 4892)]

This penalty is specifically associated with the instructor-badge violation in the supplied records; it should not be generalized to other violations described in the community.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training contracts carry learner-specific signing and termination duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Learner drivers are required to sign their own driver-training contracts and contract terminations. Contract-related violations include failing to sign or terminate as required, or having someone other than the learner sign the contract. [Data: Entities (2859, 5066, 5067, 1115); Relationships (8510, 3962, 3963)]

The records associate the specified contract-related violations with fines of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for driver-training establishments. They do not provide details about particular establishments or actual enforcement cases. [Data: Entities (2274, 1115); Relationships (3961)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Practice is organized around designated routes and approved settings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Car-driving learners are described as practicing in a training vehicle on a designated route while participating in road traffic, under the supervision of an instructor or driving-test examiner. The authorized route is specified in the training vehicle’s permit. [Data: Entities (700, 701, 705, 628); Relationships (2976, 2975, 2978, 2808)]

A driving practice yard is described as a place for supervised exercises and may also host driving examinations, including motorcycle tests, if it meets required facility and technical standards. The records state this conditional requirement but do not provide technical specifications or assess any particular yard. [Data: Entities (1650)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulatory material covers training and testing, but not actual compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driver training and testing are identified as activities covered by the regulations referenced in Article 39, which concerns listed violations by instructors in this context. The records therefore provide a regulatory framework for some duties and penalties, rather than evidence about how widely violations occur. [Data: Entities (1491, 1276); Relationships (6119, 4891)]

The supplied information describes legal obligations and penalty amounts but does not report enforcement cases, observed compliance rates, or reputation assessments for the people or establishments involved. No conclusion about actual conduct or reputation is supported by these records.

v.tieu_de: Driving Tests, Testing Centers, and Licensing Authorities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the regulated driving-test process: eligible applicants complete a driver-training program, take a test at a testing center, and may qualify for a license if successful. Testing centers are subject to technical and operational requirements and must share results and monitoring data with relevant authorities. The network also covers transitional arrangements for some driving learners, license-category rules, and limited circumstances in which people taking a driving test may be carried in a cargo truck bed. The information describes a safety- and compliance-relevant administrative system, but does not identify specific violations or misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial practical importance because it governs driver testing, licensing, and oversight related to road traffic safety, although the supplied data identifies no specific violations or harmful conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The driving test is the community’s central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driving test connects applicants and participants with training prerequisites, testing centers, licensing rules, and the authorities that receive test results and monitoring data. This makes it the principal operational hub in the community. [Data: Entities (1652); Relationships (6081, 6413, 6412, 6159, 3455)]

The test’s content is described as matched to the relevant license class and driver-training curriculum, and the process is monitored. A satisfactory result makes a participant eligible to receive a license; the data does not establish that every successful participant automatically receives one. [Data: Entities (1652, 1660); Relationships (6412, 6179, 6180)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training and eligibility govern access to testing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated route to registration requires completion of the driver-training program and meeting prescribed age and health requirements. The eligible-applicant entity is specifically described as a person who has completed training and meets those requirements. [Data: Entities (1756, 1503, 1652); Relationships (6153, 6154, 6413)]

The data also identifies driving learners who began training before, or were training when, Law No. 36/2024/QH15 takes effect and have not yet tested or received a license. Those learners may be tested or licensed under the described transitional provisions, subject to applicable eligibility and licensing rules. [Data: Entities (1621); Relationships (6381, 6380)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Testing centers have technical and operational obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver testing center provides test services and may host driver examinations. It must meet conditions prescribed by the Government, comply with national technical standards, and use information-technology equipment. These requirements indicate that the testing function depends on both facilities and technical systems. [Data: Entities (1478); Relationships (6081, 6045)]

The center is also required to promptly share test results and monitoring data with the driver training, testing, and licensing authority and the road traffic order and safety authority. The supplied information states that specified violations may be fined, but it does not identify any actual violation or penalty imposed on a particular center. [Data: Entities (1478, 1508, 4387); Relationships (6080, 6084)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorities receive data for oversight and administer licensing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver training, testing, and licensing authority receives test results and monitoring data to oversee testing, while the road traffic order and safety authority also receives those materials for its oversight role. The community therefore includes a defined flow of test information from centers and tests to authorities. [Data: Entities (1508, 4387); Relationships (6159, 6415, 6080, 6084)]

Licensing responsibilities are represented by the driver examination and licensing authority and the driver training, testing, and licensing authority. The data links these authorities to the issuance process, while Article 62 is described as covering issuance, exchange, reissuance, and revocation procedures. [Data: Entities (1447, 1508, 1521, 1631); Relationships (6023, 6158)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License categories and test outcomes shape issuance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 89 specifies the license-category rules that apply when eligible learners are tested and licensed. The test is thus connected not only to whether a participant succeeds, but also to the category under which a license may be granted. [Data: Entities (941, 1631); Relationships (3455, 3454)]

The supplied descriptions state that a satisfactory test result makes a person eligible for a license and that passing is a condition associated with issuance. They do not provide individual test results, license decisions, or details about how category rules apply to particular people. [Data: Entities (1652, 1660); Relationships (6179, 6180)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-truck-bed provisions include specific driving-related circumstances
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes the rule that carrying people in a cargo truck bed is permitted only in specified circumstances. One listed circumstance is transporting people taking a driving test in a test vehicle. [Data: Entities (744, 1652); Relationships (3037)]

Other listed circumstances include carrying people practicing driving in a training vehicle and workers performing road maintenance or repair. The data describes these as permitted circumstances; it does not provide further conditions or evidence of a particular incident. [Data: Entities (744, 1649, 4288); Relationships (3036, 3038)]

v.tieu_de: Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, described as setting sanctions and driver’s-license-point deductions for certain road-traffic conduct. Its connected entities include operating overloaded or oversize vehicles, driving tracked vehicles on roads, and fines of 8–10 million VND and 40–50 million VND. The data also contains an inconsistency: the 40–50 million VND penalty is described as applying to driving test centers, but relationships connect it to Article 34 and road-traffic violations. The records establish regulatory subject matter and stated penalties, but do not document enforcement, actual incidents, or broader compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (402, 2198, 3368, 3370, 1585); Relationships (1702, 1700, 1703, 1704, 1698, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects Article 34’s central role in a set of road-safety rules and its substantial stated penalties, while the data provides no evidence of actual violations, enforcement, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 34 is the community’s central regulatory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as covering sanctions and driver’s-license-point deductions for vehicles exceeding permitted dimensions or weight, tracked vehicles on roads, and passenger cars in specified categories. Its relationships connect it to the covered conduct, a clause specifying a particular penalty, and the stated 40–50 million VND fine. [Data: Entities (402); Relationships (1702, 1700, 1703, 1698, 1704)]

This makes the article the organizing reference in the available records. The data describes the provision’s scope but does not establish how often it is applied or how it is enforced. [Data: Entities (402); Relationships (1700, 1701, 1703, 1704)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overloaded and oversize vehicle operation are covered conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify operating an overloaded vehicle and operating an oversize vehicle as violations addressed by Article 34. The descriptions define these respectively as exceeding permitted weight and exceeding permitted dimensions. [Data: Entities (3368, 3370); Relationships (1703, 1704)]

The 40–50 million VND fine is also linked by relationships to both types of operation. However, the records do not clarify whether that amount applies to every instance or under what conditions it is imposed. [Data: Entities (2198, 3368, 3370); Relationships (7207, 7208)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tracked vehicles on roads are included in the provision’s scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving or circulating a tracked vehicle on a road is identified as conduct addressed by Article 34. The associated description also says the article includes passenger cars within its scope, though the available records do not specify the relevant categories or circumstances. [Data: Entities (1585, 402); Relationships (1700)]

A relationship connects driving a tracked vehicle on a road with the stated 40–50 million VND fine. The records do not provide additional details about exceptions, enforcement procedures, or license-point consequences for this conduct. [Data: Entities (1585, 2198); Relationships (6321)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 specifies a separate 8–10 million VND penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 34 is described as specifying a fine of 8–10 million Vietnamese dong for listed road-traffic violations. Its relationship to the corresponding penalty entity confirms that this amount is associated with the clause. [Data: Entities (930, 2570); Relationships (1698, 3442)]

The penalty description notes an exception for a valid circulation permit, but the records do not identify the precise conduct to which the exception applies or provide further details about its operation. [Data: Entities (2570)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The 40–50 million VND fine has conflicting descriptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description for the 40–50 million VND fine says it is an administrative penalty prescribed for driving test centers committing specified violations covered by Article 34. In contrast, relationships connect that same fine to Article 34 and to road-traffic conduct, including tracked-vehicle operation and overloaded or oversize vehicle operation. [Data: Entities (2198); Relationships (1702, 6321, 7207, 7208)]

This discrepancy leaves the fine’s intended scope unclear in the supplied records. It should not be treated as definitively applicable to a particular driver or violation without resolving the conflict against the underlying legal text. [Data: Entities (2198); Relationships (1702, 6321, 7207, 7208)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support legal-scope analysis, not conclusions about actual compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe a legal provision, conduct it addresses, and monetary penalties. They provide no records of specific drivers, driving test centers, enforcement actions, observed violations, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (402, 2198, 3368, 3370, 1585); Relationships (1700, 1702, 1703, 1704, 1701)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant to understanding stated regulatory obligations and penalties, but the supplied data alone cannot establish the prevalence of noncompliance, the provision’s practical effectiveness, or the reputation of the entities involved. [Data: Entities (402, 2198); Relationships (1698, 1702)]

v.tieu_de: Article 26 Corrective Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Clause 13 of Article 26, which requires corrective measures in addition to any applicable penalties for specified violations. The provision is linked to three referenced categories: point a and point h of Clause 7, and Clause 11. The supplied records describe the legal structure but do not identify the underlying conduct, jurisdiction, or any actual violations or enforcement.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate informational importance as a provision connecting three violation categories to corrective measures, but the records provide no evidence of actual violations, enforcement, or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 13 is the community's central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 13 of Article 26 is the hub of the supplied relationships: each of the three referenced categories connects to it, and its description states that specified violations require corrective measures in addition to any applicable penalties. [Data: Entities (885); Relationships (3367, 3353, 3368)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two referenced categories fall under point 7 of Clause 7
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records identify point a and point h of Clause 7 as separate categories of violation that trigger the corrective measures described in Clause 13. The supplied information does not explain what conduct either category covers. [Data: Entities (3751, 3785); Relationships (3367, 3368)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 11 is also connected to the corrective-measure provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: Clause 11 of Article 26 is described as a referenced category of violation, and the relationship record states that Clause 13 applies corrective measures to violations specified in Clause 11. No further details about the category or its requirements are provided. [Data: Entities (877); Relationships (3353)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Corrective measures are additional to applicable penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of Clause 13 distinguishes corrective measures from applicable penalties by stating that individuals and organizations committing the specified violations must undertake corrective measures in addition to any applicable penalties. The records do not specify the measures or penalties. [Data: Entities (885)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish legal links, not actual cases or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied material describes a provision and its links to three violation categories, but contains no record of a person or organization committing a violation, an enforcement action, or a legal outcome. Accordingly, the community's documented significance is limited to the stated structure of the rule. [Data: Entities (885, 3751, 3785, 877); Relationships (3367, 3353, 3368)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Regulation and Decree 168/2024/ND-CP
v.tom_tat: This community centers on individuals and organizations subject to Vietnam’s road-traffic order and safety framework, with agencies and provincial or centrally governed city traffic police performing administrative, educational, and permitting roles. Decree 168/2024/ND-CP, particularly Article 32, connects covered violations to fines and possible vehicle-document revocation; other provisions address corrective measures and return of unlawful gains. The network also covers database updates, legal-knowledge checks, public legal dissemination, intelligent-transport vehicle permits, and technical evidence used to identify violators. The records describe legal rules and roles rather than documenting specific incidents or actual violations. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 1274, 142, 5030); Relationships (4884, 4885, 4212, 4214, 9341)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high public and administrative importance because it covers traffic-law compliance, enforcement, and permitting for individuals and organizations, although the records do not establish specific incidents or actual harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Individuals and organizations are both regulated and protected
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Individuals and organizations are central subjects of the framework: both may contribute information to the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database, be involved in road-traffic law knowledge checks, and face penalties for specified violations. The entities’ descriptions also state that their lawful rights and interests must be respected during patrols, controls, accident investigations, and resolutions. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437); Relationships (4212, 4214, 7915, 9336)]

The material therefore describes a dual-purpose system: it assigns compliance duties and enforcement consequences while also setting out protections against misuse or abuse of enforcement processes. It does not report whether any particular person or organization experienced a rights violation. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework provides a broad range of penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described consequences vary by offense and can include administrative fines, corrective measures, revocation of specified vehicle documents, and surrender of unlawful gains. Article 32 is identified as setting penalties for vehicle owners and providing for revocation of certain altered, forged, or improperly issued registration and inspection documents. [Data: Entities (1274, 4201, 1126, 5516); Relationships (4884, 4885, 4888, 7914, 9335)]

The records give examples of differing fine levels, including VND 40–50 million for individuals and VND 80–100 million for organizations that organize illegal racing. They also describe penalties for unauthorized roadway or sidewalk use, vehicle overloading, and illegal registration-plate transactions; applicable amounts depend on the specific violation and subject. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 2268, 1875, 2549); Relationships (7331, 7332, 6818, 6819, 7808)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 32 is a key link between violations and vehicle-owner consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32 is connected to both individuals and organizations and is described as addressing vehicle owners who violate road-traffic regulations. Its stated consequences include specified fines, driving-license point deductions, and possible revocation of certain vehicle-registration and inspection documents. [Data: Entities (1274, 5516); Relationships (4884, 4885, 4887, 4888)]

The network associates Article 32 with road-traffic regulation violations, but does not provide case records or evidence that any particular owner has been penalized. The information supports an account of the provision’s scope, not a conclusion about enforcement frequency or compliance rates. [Data: Entities (1274, 4548); Relationships (4887)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permitting and technical evidence are part of the administrative system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Owners of intelligent transport vehicles, including individuals and organizations, are described as having to prepare one application dossier and submit it to the competent licensing authority online, by post, or in person. The records do not identify the authority for every such application. [Data: Entities (2724, 2651, 3437); Relationships (7908, 8030)]

Separately, individuals and organizations may provide technical equipment or collected technical results used to identify administrative violators. The evidence-use period can expire if no sanctioning decision is issued by the deadline; intentional evasion or obstruction affects how that period is calculated. [Data: Entities (1007, 1909, 1847); Relationships (3578, 3579, 3577, 6777, 6778)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic police divisions have defined permit responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic police division within provincial- and centrally governed city-level police is authorized to issue, reissue, and revoke permits for signaling equipment on priority vehicles for covered agencies and organizations. The division is linked to both provincial police and centrally governed city police in the records. [Data: Entities (5030, 3972, 757); Relationships (9341, 9801, 3065)]

This establishes a specific administrative role within the wider regulatory community. The provided information describes permit authority, but does not document individual permit decisions or the operational use of signaling equipment. [Data: Entities (5030)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal education and database maintenance support implementation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Agencies, organizations, and people’s armed forces units are described as responsible for organizing legal propaganda and dissemination for people under their management. The framework also includes checks of legal knowledge concerning road-traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (142, 3437, 3665, 2876, 4364); Relationships (463, 465, 8540, 9333, 9530)]

Agencies, individuals, and organizations may contribute amendments or supplements to the Road Traffic Order and Safety Database. Changes or detection of incomplete or inaccurate records are identified as reasons to update it, indicating an information-maintenance function alongside education and enforcement. [Data: Entities (1237, 2665, 2651, 3437, 142); Relationships (4212, 4214, 4213, 462)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory risks, not evidence of actual misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes descriptions of prohibited conduct such as illegal plate transactions, illegal racing, and illegal manufacture or assembly of road motor vehicles, along with possible fines or return of unlawful gains. These are presented as legal categories and consequences, not as reports that named or identifiable entities committed the conduct. [Data: Entities (2549, 2546, 2514, 2268, 4201); Relationships (7807, 7808, 7768, 7331, 7332)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance arises from the breadth of the regulatory and enforcement framework and the population it covers. The supplied records do not establish actual incident counts, enforcement outcomes, or reputational assessments of particular individuals or organizations. [Data: Entities (2651, 3437, 1274)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Inspection Facility and Regulatory Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the inspection facility, which conducts technical safety and environmental inspections, certifies modified vehicles, and issues inspection certificates through its inspectors. Its relationships connect vehicle owners and competent authorities to inspection refusal rules, and also describe registration updates and potential penalties for facility violations. The records outline a regulatory framework with public-safety and compliance significance; they do not document specific incidents or establish that any violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2689, 3126, 1064, 5601); Relationships (7987, 7984, 7982, 7990)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it governs vehicle inspections and certification, while the records describe rules and responsibilities rather than specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The inspection facility is the community’s central operational entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility is described as a public-service organization that inspects motor vehicles and specialized motor vehicles for technical safety and environmental protection, certifies modified vehicles, and issues inspection certificates. It is also responsible for the results of its inspections and certifications. [Data: Entities (2689); Relationships (7984, 7987, 7981)]

These functions make the facility the principal link between inspection activity, inspectors, owners, and the regulatory rules governing inspection outcomes. The records describe its statutory responsibilities but do not identify a particular facility or document its actual performance. [Data: Entities (2689, 2690, 4861); Relationships (7981, 7987)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection and certification address technical and environmental standards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The inspection process is described as assessing technical safety and environmental protection for motor vehicles and specialized motor vehicles. Inspectors carry out the inspections, while the facility issues the resulting certificates and is responsible for the results. [Data: Entities (4861, 2689, 2690); Relationships (7981, 7987)]

The facility also certifies modified vehicles for technical safety and environmental protection. These records indicate an important technical and public-service role, but do not specify inspection methods, equipment, staffing levels, or performance outcomes. [Data: Entities (3052, 2689); Relationships (7984)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection refusal is limited to specified circumstances
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility may refuse an inspection only in circumstances specified by law. The listed grounds include a request from a procedural authority, an unresolved required administrative-violation resolution, discrepancies in vehicle registration information, failure to replace a registration certificate after modification certification, and suspected falsification of vehicle documents. [Data: Entities (2691, 122, 5479, 5473, 5386); Relationships (7982, 7986, 388, 7989, 7992, +more)]

The records therefore describe refusal as a rule-bound decision rather than an unrestricted facility discretion. Suspected falsification is identified as a possible ground for refusal, not as proof that an owner has falsified documents. [Data: Entities (2691, 5386); Relationships (7991, 9052)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Owner obligations connect administrative enforcement to inspection access
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A competent state authority may require a vehicle owner to resolve an administrative violation concerning road traffic order and safety. If the required resolution remains incomplete, the inspection facility may refuse to inspect the vehicle. [Data: Entities (3126, 122, 1064); Relationships (387, 388, 7985)]

The records also identify suspected falsification of vehicle documents as a possible owner-related reason for refusal. They describe the relevant legal conditions, but provide no evidence that a particular owner failed to resolve a violation or falsified documents. [Data: Entities (3126, 5386, 2691); Relationships (9052, 7991, 7985)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Modified-vehicle certification triggers a registration-document requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility certifies the technical safety and environmental protection of modified vehicles. After a vehicle receives a modification certificate, its registration certificate must be replaced by the next inspection. [Data: Entities (3052, 5473, 2689); Relationships (7984, 8977)]

Failure to complete that replacement is specified as a ground on which the facility may refuse an inspection. This links modification certification to a subsequent registration obligation and inspection eligibility. [Data: Entities (5473, 2691); Relationships (7989, 8977, 7982)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework provides for penalties for inspection-rule violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that an inspection facility may be fined for listed violations of regulations governing vehicle inspection activity. The facility description gives a fine range of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for a listed violation under Article 40. [Data: Entities (2689, 5601, 3112); Relationships (7990, 9033)]

This establishes a described enforcement mechanism for facility conduct, but the supplied information does not identify a facility that committed a violation, a penalty that was imposed, or a specific enforcement proceeding. [Data: Entities (2689, 5601); Relationships (7990, 9033)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registered individuals and organizations may retain owner responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that an organization or individual named on a vehicle registration certificate continues to bear the responsibilities of the vehicle owner in specified cases until the registration certificate and license plates are recalled. [Data: Entities (4067, 4066, 3126); Relationships (9049, 9048)]

This provision extends the owner-responsibility relationship to the registered party during the stated period. The records do not identify any specific registered organization or individual, or indicate that a recall is pending in a particular case. [Data: Entities (4067, 4066); Relationships (9049, 9048)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Regulation Violations and Corrective Measures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road transport regulation violations, with administrative penalties and required corrective installations linked to the violation category. The corrective measures cover seat belts, driver image-recording devices, journey-monitoring devices, and seats for preschool children and primary school students. The records describe regulatory requirements, but do not establish that a particular person or organization committed a violation or failed to comply.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s importance to road safety and its combination of penalties with specified corrective measures, while the records provide no case-specific evidence of violations or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road transport violations are the community’s central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road Transport Regulation Violations is the central entity, with the highest listed degree (7) among the entities. Its description concerns violations of rules on road traffic order and safety in road transport and support services, including conduct specified in Article 26, paragraphs 4 and 7. [Data: Entities (4491)]

The relationships connect this violation category to administrative penalties and several corrective installations, making it the organizing subject of the community. [Data: Relationships (161, 8675, 6032, 3195, 8135, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violations may entail administrative penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes administrative penalties as sanctions for specified road transport and traffic violations, including those described in Article 31. It also states that these penalties apply in addition to corrective measures or deductions from a driver’s license points. [Data: Entities (74)]

A relationship directly links administrative penalties to the road transport violation category and describes responsible individuals or organizations as subject to penalties as well as remedial measures. The records do not specify penalty amounts or establish that any particular person or organization has been sanctioned. [Data: Relationships (161)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Corrective installations supplement penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community describes remedial installation as a required response for specified violations, in addition to any penalty. The listed measures include compliant journey-monitoring devices, driver image-recording devices, seat belts, and seats for preschool children and primary school students. [Data: Entities (2969); Relationships (8675)]

This structure indicates that the described response is not limited to sanctions: the requirements also call for specified vehicle-related corrections. The records do not provide deadlines, inspection procedures, or details about how compliance is verified. [Data: Entities (2969); Relationships (8675)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several device requirements are linked to specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationships identify installation of a compliant driver image-recording device and a compliant journey-monitoring device as corrective measures for specified road transport violations. [Data: Relationships (6032, 8135)]

The corresponding entities describe these as required installations on a vehicle. The data does not specify device models, technical standards, or which individual violations trigger each requirement. [Data: Entities (1450, 2795)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Seat belts and child seats are also corrective measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records link specified road transport violations to installation of seat belts and suitable seats for preschool children and primary school students. [Data: Relationships (10266, 3195)]

The entity descriptions characterize these as required corrective actions involving vehicle safety equipment. No further technical specifications or evidence of installation status is provided. [Data: Entities (4627, 821)]

v.tieu_de: Article 26 Road-Transport Compliance
v.tom_tat: The community centers on Article 26 of Decree No. 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which establishes penalties and corrective measures for road-transport and transport-support-service violations. Its connected provisions and violation categories cover passenger-service practices, vehicle loading, dangerous-goods transport, and vehicle-data management; consequences described include monetary fines, vehicle-insignia suspension, driver’s-license point deductions, and remedial compliance duties. The records describe a regulatory framework, not specific companies or documented real-world violations. [Data: Entities (330, 4492, 2975, 5402, 886); Relationships (1316, 1332, 1354, 1315, 1339)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial regulatory importance because Article 26 spans multiple transport activities and provides financial, operational, and corrective consequences, although the records do not identify actual violations or their scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 26 is the framework’s central provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 26 is described as setting administrative penalties and remedial measures for violations of road-traffic order and safety in road transport and supporting services. Its relationships connect it to a wide range of covered conduct, affected organizations, penalties, and corrective actions. [Data: Entities (330, 4425, 4472); Relationships (1339, 1340, 1335, 1324, 1332)]

The provision also has amendments or supplements associated with Article 9. The records establish that certain points and clauses are amended, but do not specify the full content or practical effect of those changes. [Data: Entities (172, 330); Relationships (528)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules reach both transport organizations and individuals
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described scope includes individuals and organizations engaged in road transport or transport-support services; in specified circumstances, it also covers a transport-business individual who directly drives a vehicle and commits a violation. [Data: Entities (330, 5090, 4474); Relationships (1350, 1341)]

The records distinguish penalties for individuals and organizations in some cases, and identify passenger road-transport businesses as a covered organizational category. They do not provide a complete account of every regulated party or every penalty amount. [Data: Entities (3563, 2278, 2279, 2572); Relationships (1334, 1325, 1326, 1327)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-transport contract and service practices are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 26-related records identify conduct involving contract passenger transport, including selling tickets or collecting fares beyond a signed contract, confirming bookings beyond contract terms, and setting fixed routes or schedules for multiple customers. These are described as violations subject to fines. [Data: Entities (4635, 1082, 4637); Relationships (1348, 1317, 1349)]

The broader Article 26 description also lists using drivers without required experience for certain passenger or student transport vehicles, and using vehicles whose service life does not match the registered business type. These provisions indicate that the framework addresses service operations as well as vehicle and personnel suitability. [Data: Entities (330)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overloading thresholds are specifically differentiated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish loading a vehicle above its permitted payload by more than 10% and up to 50%, with a different threshold for liquid tankers, from overloading by more than 50% and up to 100%. Article 26 is linked to these loading violations and to fines for individuals and organizations. [Data: Entities (2921, 3491, 3490, 3492); Relationships (1331, 1333, 7344, 7345, 8608)]

The supplied information does not state the full fine schedule for each loading threshold, so the specific amounts cannot be established from these records. [Data: Entities (2921, 3491, 3490, 3492)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle monitoring and image data are compliance obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework addresses failures to provide, update, transmit, store, or manage data collected by prescribed vehicle devices, including driver-image recording equipment. For the specified driver-image data-management violation, the records state fines of VND 5,000,000–6,000,000 for an individual and VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for a transport or transport-support organization. [Data: Entities (1991, 4482, 2975, 330); Relationships (3534, 3536, 6951, 1332)]

For certain violations under specified points and clauses, the required corrective action is to provide, update, transmit, store, and manage the relevant vehicle data. This makes data handling both a basis for penalties and a stated remediation requirement. [Data: Entities (5608, 2975); Relationships (1332, 8679)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional consequences extend beyond monetary fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain specified violations, the records describe an additional one-to-three-month suspension of the right to use a vehicle insignia, if one has been issued. Article 26 is linked to this consequence, but the data does not enumerate every violation that triggers it. [Data: Entities (4492, 5402); Relationships (1354, 10267)]

Article 26 also includes a provision under which a transport-business individual who directly operates a vehicle may receive a two-point driver’s-license deduction for the specified violations. Certain corrective measures include issuing a driver identification card and providing professional training or guidance or periodic health examinations for drivers and onboard service staff. [Data: Entities (886, 2760, 330); Relationships (1315, 1330)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods transport has personnel and escort requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify failure to assign an escort when required for dangerous-goods transport as a violation subject to a fine. They also describe using a driver or cargo escort without required dangerous-goods training as a violation, with stated fines of VND 3,000,000–4,000,000 for an individual and VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 for an organization. [Data: Entities (1935, 5344); Relationships (1321, 6886, 10595)]

These requirements show that the regulatory community includes operational safeguards related to personnel and transport procedures, in addition to vehicle condition and data management. The provided records do not report actual incidents or noncompliance by any named operator. [Data: Entities (1935, 5344, 330)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available records describe regulatory exposure, not actual conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe legal provisions, violation categories, regulated parties, fines, and corrective measures. They do not identify a particular transport company or individual as having committed a violation, nor do they provide evidence of enforcement actions or reputational outcomes. [Data: Entities (330, 4492, 5090, 2248); Relationships (1339, 1324, 1350)]

“Clause 7” is also described as context-dependent across multiple articles, although the Article 26 relationship specifically associates it with penalties for road-transport violations, including driver-image data failures. Conclusions about Clause 7 should therefore be limited to the article-specific context shown in the records. [Data: Entities (976, 1991, 4482); Relationships (1316, 3534, 3536)]

v.tieu_de: Administrative Violations and Decree 168/2024 Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative violations and the procedures and authorities used to detect and address them under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its relationships cover preventive seizure of vehicles and related documents, formal penalty decisions, confiscation, licence-related sanctions, and rules for determining when violations occurred or ended. The data describes a regulatory enforcement framework, not evidence that any particular person or organization violated the law. [Data: Entities (110, 4885, 82, 434, 470); Relationships (352, 207, 316, 314, 318)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad importance to administrative enforcement, including vehicle-related preventive measures, penalties, and technical detection, while the data does not establish a specific incident or unlawful conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative violations are the central organizing concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative Violation is the network’s main hub, connected to sanctioning, penalty decisions, time limits, preventive measures, confiscation, and detection. This structure indicates that the community describes a connected enforcement process rather than a single case or individual. [Data: Entities (110); Relationships (207, 314, 316, 339, 352)]

The entity definition describes violations broadly as conduct by individuals or organizations that breaches administrative law or applicable regulations, and notes that violations may be completed or ongoing. The supplied data does not identify a particular violator or establish that a violation actually occurred. [Data: Entities (110)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary seizure is a preventive measure that can precede a decision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 48 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is associated with temporary seizure of vehicles and documents in specified circumstances. The stated purpose is to immediately prevent a violation, and the measure may be used before a penalty decision is issued. [Data: Entities (4885, 470, 4883); Relationships (318, 212, 8105)]

The network also represents temporary seizure of a vehicle and temporary detention of related documents as distinct but related measures. The available descriptions do not establish that seizure is automatic; they make its application dependent on the relevant legal conditions and authorized person. [Data: Entities (4882, 4869, 4883); Relationships (349, 347, 10497)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty decisions and other sanctions are separate stages or consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data links an administrative violation to an administrative penalty decision and to the broader processes of sanctioning and imposing a penalty. It also states that a vehicle or related documents may be held before a decision, and that custody may help ensure enforcement after a decision takes effect. [Data: Entities (82, 125, 2762, 2768); Relationships (207, 212, 213)]
