Other described consequences include temporary deprivation of the right to use a driving licence or practice certificate, point deductions, and—where authorized—confiscation of objects or vehicles. These are described as measures available under applicable provisions, not as outcomes in a specific case. [Data: Entities (110, 1091, 1086, 4866); Relationships (330, 329, 351, 393)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework distinguishes completed and ongoing violations and uses timing rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 4 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP addresses limitation periods and distinguishes completed violations from ongoing ones. The supplied description says that, for an ongoing violation, discovery is relevant to determining which decree applies when imposing a penalty. [Data: Entities (434, 1399, 2589); Relationships (316, 336, 5886)]

For violations detected using specified technical equipment, Clause 3 of Article 4 connects the recording time with determining when the violation is considered to have ended. These details make the timing of discovery and recording relevant to the framework described in the data. [Data: Entities (932, 4046); Relationships (1894, 3445, 344)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical equipment and outside data providers are part of detection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions state that administrative violations may be detected using professional technical equipment and that recording may also involve equipment provided by an individual or organization. The network includes both individuals and organizations that may provide technical-equipment data for detecting violations. [Data: Entities (110, 4046, 1235, 1236); Relationships (344, 332, 333)]

The supplied information describes a detection and recording mechanism, but it does not specify the equipment’s technical capabilities, accuracy, deployment scale, or any particular data provider. Those matters therefore cannot be assessed from this record set.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authority and licence-related consequences depend on the applicable provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data assigns relevant actions to competent sanctioning authorities and describes temporary deprivation of a licence or practice certificate as a possible administrative penalty. If the document was not seized earlier, the violator may be required to present it; the description also links presentation to the start of a fixed-term deprivation in the stated circumstances. [Data: Entities (1060, 4884, 3849, 4866); Relationships (325, 393, 9721)]

For an integrated driving licence covering categories with different validity periods, the data says an unaffected category may remain available or be issued or renewed while another category is suspended. This is a specific qualification in the described framework, not evidence about any particular licence holder. [Data: Entities (2713); Relationships (3834)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated enforcement measures have defined scope and limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Temporary seizure is tied to specified categories of violations, including cited provisions in Articles 7 and 16; the data also identifies operating a vehicle while under 16 as a circumstance that may lead to temporary seizure. These examples describe specified legal grounds rather than a general power applying to every violation. [Data: Entities (136, 5602, 3345); Relationships (450, 10502, 9279)]

The confiscation description identifies a value limit of 1,000,000 đồng for the provision represented by the Confiscation of Objects and Vehicles entity. The broader entity description cautions that applicable measures and authority depend on the specific violation and legal provision, so the stated limit should not be generalized beyond its described context. [Data: Entities (1091, 110, 1086); Relationships (330, 329)]

v.tieu_de: Administrative Sanction and License Deprivation
v.tom_tat: This community describes a procedural relationship between an administrative violation sanctioning decision and a time-limited deprivation of the right to use a license or professional practice certificate. In the stated circumstances, the decision takes effect as the deprivation period’s start, and the rule applies when the competent authority has temporarily held the license or certificate. The records describe a general rule, not a specific case or individual.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate-low because the rule concerns consequential restrictions on professional or licensed activity, but the records provide no evidence of a particular case, affected party, or actual sanction.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The sanctioning decision is the procedural anchor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The administrative violation sanctioning decision is linked to the deprivation, the start of its period, and the temporary holding of the relevant license or certificate, making it the central entity in this community. [Data: Entities (126); Relationships (396, 397, 398)]

The records describe the decision’s role under stated circumstances; they do not establish that a particular decision was issued or identify a specific violation. [Data: Entities (126); Relationships (396, 397, 398)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The decision’s effective date starts the deprivation period
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Where the stated rule applies, the effective date of the sanctioning decision determines when the time-limited deprivation period begins. [Data: Entities (126, 4751); Relationships (397)]

This makes the decision’s effective date relevant to calculating the period, but the records do not specify the length of any deprivation. [Data: Entities (4751); Relationships (397)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The consequence is a time-limited restriction on license use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The deprivation is described as an administrative penalty that removes an individual’s or organization’s right to use a license or professional practice certificate for a limited period. [Data: Entities (1340)]

The relationship records connect this penalty to the sanctioning decision and identify a start event for the period. They do not indicate that any named person or organization is currently subject to it. [Data: Relationships (396, 5793)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary holding is a stated condition for applying the rule
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The rule applies in the described circumstances when the competent sanctioning authority has temporarily held the license or certificate at the time it issues the decision. [Data: Entities (4872); Relationships (398)]

The temporary holding is described as an action involving a license or certificate belonging to an individual or organization accused of a violation; the records do not provide details about an accusation or authority in a particular case. [Data: Entities (4872)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The start event and deprivation period are explicitly linked
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The start of the deprivation period is defined as the point when the time-limited restriction begins, and the relationship record states that this start event marks the beginning of the deprivation. [Data: Entities (4751, 1340); Relationships (5793)]

Together with the decision’s effective-date rule, this establishes a procedural sequence in the stated circumstances: temporary holding, issuance and effectiveness of the decision, and commencement of the deprivation period. The records do not provide further procedural steps. [Data: Relationships (397, 398, 5793)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP and Road-Traffic Sanctioning
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP and its relationship to administrative sanctioning of road-traffic violations. The decree is described as amending rules on license plates, journey-monitoring devices, image-recording equipment, sanctioning authority, and other provisions. Its transitional rules connect the handling of earlier violations to the decree in force when the conduct occurred, including cases discovered or still under review later. The records establish regulatory and enforcement significance, but provide no evidence about actual compliance rates, enforcement outcomes, or the reputation of any individuals or organizations.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad relevance to road-traffic enforcement and administrative penalties, while the supplied records do not establish actual violations, enforcement outcomes, or wider impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP is the community’s central regulatory instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is connected to multiple provisions and topics, including amendments to Articles 13, 21, 32, 44, and 53, as well as additions, replacements, and repeals described in Article 19. This makes it the main organizing entity in the supplied regulatory material. [Data: Entities (1300, 291, 185, 279); Relationships (1055, 566, 1019, 2606)]

The records describe amendments concerning road-traffic penalties and the authority of road and construction officials to impose administrative sanctions. They do not provide enforcement statistics or establish how these powers have been applied in practice. [Data: Entities (1300)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transitional rules make the timing of a violation central to penalty decisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied description states that an administrative road-traffic violation is generally sanctioned under the decree in force when the conduct occurred. Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP’s Article 21 is associated with that rule for certain earlier violations. [Data: Entities (98, 1300, 1306); Relationships (256, 271, 5685)]

The transitional rule is relevant when a violation ended before the decree took effect but is discovered later or remains under consideration. The data identifies this timing issue but does not specify the effective date of the decree itself. [Data: Entities (98, 1400, 1735); Relationships (257, 258)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative sanctioning encompasses several document and plate violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative sanctioning is linked to violations involving vehicle registration certificates, temporary vehicle registration certificates, and license plates. These are identified as categories covered by the stated penalty rules. [Data: Entities (103, 2902, 4894, 5526); Relationships (274, 276, 278)]

The decree description specifically notes plate-related issues such as missing, improperly positioned or formatted, unclear, altered, obscured, or otherwise difficult-to-identify plates. The records describe the scope of the rules, not the prevalence of these violations or the penalties imposed in particular cases. [Data: Entities (1300); Relationships (274)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Journey-monitoring requirements address device functionality and data integrity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 8 amendment is linked to conduct involving commercial transport cars, tractor units, or internal transport vehicles operated without a journey-monitoring device, with a device that is not functioning as required, or with altered device data. [Data: Entities (558, 3383); Relationships (2606, 2607)]

This establishes that the described provisions address both the presence and operation of monitoring equipment and the integrity of its data. The supplied records do not indicate how often such conduct occurs or whether any specific operator has violated the rules. [Data: Entities (3383)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Image-recording equipment penalties have staged effective dates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that penalties related to driver image-recording equipment for specified passenger and freight transport vehicles take effect on January 1, 2028. The driver-equipment provisions are linked to the decree and to that effective date. [Data: Entities (1452, 1729, 1300); Relationships (5679, 6034)]

Penalties related to passenger-cabin image-recording equipment are stated to take effect on January 1, 2029, subject to the relevant law on such equipment in road vehicles. These dates distinguish the implementation timing of the two types of equipment-related penalty provisions. [Data: Entities (1730, 3578); Relationships (5680, 6611)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a regulatory framework, not demonstrated compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships primarily describe legal provisions, violation categories, sanctioning processes, and effective dates. They include a general description of administrative sanctioning and its procedural context, including a limitation period and the decree applicable when a violation occurred. [Data: Entities (103, 98, 1300); Relationships (254, 271)]

No supplied record identifies a particular person or organization as having violated these rules, gives enforcement outcomes, or assesses the reputation of an affected party. Accordingly, the information supports analysis of regulatory scope and timing, but not conclusions about actual compliance or misconduct.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Safety Regulation: Drivers and Ministry of Health
v.tom_tat: This community centers on drivers and the Ministry of Health’s role in health standards, examinations, and health-information databases for drivers and specialized-vehicle operators. The connected records describe road-safety duties, training and periodic health examinations, passenger-transport requirements, and specified violations, including passenger noncompliance and use of under-experienced drivers in certain services. The material indicates a broad regulatory and public-safety footprint, but describes rules and responsibilities rather than evidence of actual violations or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (1538, 3014, 882, 3308, 3559); Relationships (6230, 6233, 6243, 6242, 9262)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it covers driver conduct, passenger transport, health oversight, and related enforcement provisions, without evidence here of actual incidents. [Data: Entities (1538, 3014, 3559, 5342, 5341); Relationships (6233, 6243, 6242, 8816)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Drivers are the central focus of a broad road-safety framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver entity has the highest listed degree and its description covers road-traffic compliance, including speed and safe-distance rules, seat belts, expressway rules, and helmet use for motorcycle and motorbike operators. It also describes requirements for passenger-transport drivers, such as checking vehicle safety before departure and informing passengers about safety and emergency evacuation. [Data: Entities (1538)]

The relationships connect drivers to training, periodic health examinations, health databases, and violations involving insufficient experience in particular passenger-transport roles. Together, these records show that the community addresses both day-to-day safe conduct and qualifications or oversight for specific duties. [Data: Relationships (6235, 6233, 6029, 6243, 6242)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry of Health oversees driver health requirements and related information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Health is described as responsible for establishing health standards and examination requirements for drivers and operators of specialized vehicles, regulating periodic examinations for professional car drivers, and managing health databases. The records also assign it responsibilities concerning alcohol-concentration assessment and ambulance standards and use. [Data: Entities (3014)]

Two database entities are named: the Driver Health Database and the Driver and Specialized Motorcycle Operator Health Database. Their descriptions and relationships associate driver health information with Ministry of Health management; the supplied records do not establish whether the two named databases are separate systems or overlapping references. [Data: Entities (1443, 1449); Relationships (6029, 6030, 6006, 6007)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training and periodic examinations apply to drivers and vehicle-service personnel
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Professional training or guidance may be required for drivers, while periodic health examinations are expressly identified for drivers. The descriptions characterize training and examinations as remedial measures organizations may be required to arrange in specified circumstances. [Data: Entities (1538, 3911, 3692); Relationships (6235, 6233, 3360, 3363, 3362)]

Onboard service staff are also connected to professional training and periodic health examinations, and vehicle service employees are linked to those requirements. This indicates that the framework extends beyond drivers to some personnel serving passengers or working aboard vehicles. [Data: Entities (3308, 5492); Relationships (3361, 9265, 9263, 9752, 9581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 13 is associated with remedial measures, but its references are ambiguous
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Clause 13 entity is described in two regulatory contexts: as a clause of Article 26 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning remedial measures for certain road-transport violations, and as Clause 13 of Article 13 concerning driver-license point deductions for specified vehicle-condition violations. The entity description explicitly says the available information does not establish whether these are the same provision. [Data: Entities (882)]

Relationships link Clause 13 to training or periodic health examinations for drivers and onboard service staff, and to organizational arrangements for those measures. The context ambiguity should therefore be retained when interpreting the clause rather than treating the references as definitively identical. [Data: Relationships (3360, 3361, 3362, 3363)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger compliance with onboard safety instructions is subject to a stated fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define a violation as a passenger failing to follow a driver’s or onboard service staff’s instructions concerning traffic order and safety. The stated penalty is a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese dong under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 33, Clause 1. [Data: Entities (3559, 1291); Relationships (9262, 5629)]

This provision connects onboard staff’s safety-instruction role with passenger conduct and a specified enforcement consequence. The supplied data establishes the rule and fine range, but does not report how often the violation occurs or how it is enforced. [Data: Entities (3308, 3559, 1291); Relationships (9262, 5629)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Experience requirements address higher-risk passenger-transport assignments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify violations involving use of drivers who lack the required years of experience to transport preschool children or students, and use of under-experienced drivers for double-decker sleeper passenger buses. Drivers are directly linked to both specified violations. [Data: Entities (5342, 5341); Relationships (6243, 6242)]

The driver description also states that drivers transporting preschool children or students must receive instruction in required pickup and drop-off safety procedures, with educational institutions and transport operators bearing related responsibilities. This points to controls addressing driver experience and child-passenger handling, without providing evidence that a particular operator breached them. [Data: Entities (1538, 5342); Relationships (6243)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized-vehicle operators and ambulance permits form a related regulatory branch
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Health is responsible for health information covering operators of specialized motor vehicles, and the named health database also includes specialized motorcycle operators. Specialized motorcycle operators are described as participants in training, testing, and certification under the relevant road-traffic-law provision. [Data: Entities (3014, 1443, 4703, 3418); Relationships (8815, 6009, 6007)]

The records also connect the Ministry to priority-vehicle signal-device permit issuance, specifying that ambulance permits depend on compliance with applicable ambulance standards and use requirements. These relationships broaden the community beyond ordinary drivers to specialized operators and emergency-vehicle administration. [Data: Entities (3014, 3876); Relationships (8816)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes regulatory duties, not demonstrated noncompliance or harm
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material consists of descriptions of legal requirements, administrative responsibilities, databases, and defined violations. It identifies potential penalties and specified under-experience violations, but provides no case records, counts, enforcement outcomes, or evidence of injuries or other actual consequences. [Data: Entities (1538, 3559, 5342, 5341, 1291); Relationships (5629, 6243, 6242)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance is grounded in the scope of the road-safety and health-oversight framework described, rather than in evidence of a particular breach or incident. [Data: Entities (1538, 3014, 882); Relationships (6230, 6233, 8816)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger Transport Safety and Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on passengers and the safety and compliance rules governing road passenger transport. Its relationships connect passenger duties—such as wearing compliant helmets and occupying permitted positions—with driver responsibilities, contract passenger lists and records, boarding and alighting at road stopping or parking points, and potential fines for transport businesses and support providers. The information describes requirements and specified violations, but does not establish that a particular person or business committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns passenger safety and transport compliance, with specified responsibilities and penalties, but the records do not document a particular incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger safety duties are central to the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Passengers are described as people carried in vehicles, including passenger-transport vehicles and motorcycles or motorbikes; for contract services, their names must appear on the passenger list. The passenger-related rules also address instructions before departure and permitted positions inside vehicles. [Data: Entities (3589)]

The relationships identify two specific safety requirements: passengers must wear and correctly fasten compliant helmets when riding motorcycles or motorbikes, and passenger-vehicle drivers must guide passengers to occupy prescribed positions. [Data: Relationships (7724, 9447)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Contract passenger services require appropriate records and passengers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe unauthorized or improper passenger transport as carrying people who are not listed or who do not belong to the group prescribed for the relevant contract service. A separate entry describes noncompliant contract transport in terms of missing or deficient contracts, passenger lists, or access to electronic versions. [Data: Entities (5204, 3263); Relationships (9451, 9218)]

The rules therefore connect passenger eligibility with service documentation. The provided information describes the requirements and violation categories, rather than showing that a specific transport service failed to comply. [Data: Entities (5204, 3263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some contract services are defined for designated passenger groups
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The designated groups identified in the records include preschool children, pupils, students, officials, public employees, and workers. The relationship between these groups and unauthorized or improper passenger transport indicates that the specified-group rule applies to the contract-transport context. [Data: Entities (1341); Relationships (5794)]

This requirement is relevant to assessing whether passengers belong on a particular contract service; the records do not identify a specific service, passenger, or instance of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (1341, 5204); Relationships (5794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport businesses and support providers may face fines for specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Transport businesses and transport support service providers are identified as organizations that may be fined for specified road-transport violations. The relationships connect these organizations to unauthorized or improper passenger transport and to noncompliant contract passenger transport. [Data: Entities (5098); Relationships (10599, 9219)]

The wording indicates potential regulatory exposure, not a finding that any particular organization has been fined or committed a violation. [Data: Entities (5098); Relationships (10599, 9219)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Drivers have a defined duty to guide passengers into permitted positions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a violation in which a vehicle operator fails to instruct passengers to sit, stand, or lie in positions prescribed for the vehicle. The driver is identified as the person responsible for guiding passengers, linking the duty to the operator of a passenger vehicle. [Data: Entities (1977, 3587); Relationships (9447, 6934)]

The stated penalty for this violation is a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese đồng. This is a specified penalty in the data, not evidence that a fine was imposed in a particular case. [Data: Entities (2138); Relationships (6933)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Boarding and alighting are associated with road stopping or parking points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Passenger boarding and alighting is described as taking place at a road stopping or parking point, defined as a location where vehicles stop or park, including for passengers getting on or off. [Data: Entities (4518, 3558); Relationships (9435)]

Passengers are directly linked to the activity and to the stopping or parking point, making these locations part of the community’s transport-safety context. The records do not identify a particular location or report an incident there. [Data: Relationships (9434, 9449)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules and violation categories, not a documented case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships set out passenger obligations, driver duties, contract-service documentation requirements, and specified potential penalties. They provide a framework for understanding compliance responsibilities across passengers, operators, and transport businesses. [Data: Entities (3589, 3263, 1977, 5098); Relationships (9218, 9447, 10599)]

No provided record identifies a named business or driver as having violated these rules, or describes a specific enforcement action. The community’s significance is therefore grounded in the safety and compliance issues covered by the rules, rather than evidence of a particular event. [Data: Entities (5204, 1977, 2138); Relationships (9451, 6933)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Violations and Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative enforcement framework for road-traffic violations, with road traffic administrative violations at its center. The records connect those violations to administrative sanctions and remedial measures, and identify Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as addressing vehicle-condition violations by motorcycle, moped, and similar-vehicle drivers, including penalties and driving-licence point deductions. The framework also covers organizations and several categories of vehicle operators. The information establishes legal and enforcement relevance, but does not provide evidence about specific cases, compliance outcomes, technical capabilities, or reputation. [Data: Entities (4341, 4112, 107, 1285, 5514); Relationships (9895, 303, 302, 5616, 5614)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes traffic-safety enforcement and consequences for both individuals and organizations, while providing no evidence of a particular incident or elevated threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-traffic administrative violations are the framework’s central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define a road traffic administrative violation as an administrative breach involving road-traffic order or safety, and state that a competent state agency may be responsible for resolving it. This concept is the hub connecting sanctions, remedial measures, and covered operators. [Data: Entities (4341); Relationships (9895, 303, 9044, 9983, 9320)]

The material describes a regulatory process, not a report of a particular violation or enforcement case. It does not identify specific offenders, agency actions, or case outcomes. [Data: Entities (4341, 3430)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Administrative sanctions and remedial measures are distinct consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative sanctions are described as principal penalties for administrative violations, while remedial measures are presented alongside sanctions and may be applied to drivers committing specified violations. This indicates that the framework distinguishes punishment from measures intended to remedy consequences. [Data: Entities (107, 4112); Relationships (303, 302, 9895)]

The records do not specify a complete list of sanctions or remedial actions for every violation, so the particular consequences cannot be generalized beyond those described. [Data: Entities (107, 4112)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 14 focuses on vehicle-condition violations by two-wheeled vehicle drivers
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 14 is connected to vehicle-condition violations involving drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles while participating in traffic. The associated records identify penalties, licence-point deductions, and remedial measures as possible consequences. [Data: Entities (1285, 1545, 5514, 3620); Relationships (5616, 5614, 6263, 9492, 5615)]

This is a defined category within the broader traffic-violation framework; the supplied material does not establish how frequently such violations occur or how the provision is applied in practice. [Data: Entities (1285, 5514)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A specific fine range is associated with certain vehicle-condition violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle-condition violations entity states that certain violations by drivers of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicle types are subject to fines of 400,000 to 600,000 VND. The record qualifies this amount as applying to certain violations, rather than establishing that it applies to every violation in the category. [Data: Entities (5514)]

The records also connect these violations to penalties and driving-licence point deductions, but do not provide the point amounts or a violation-by-violation penalty schedule. [Data: Entities (3620); Relationships (9492, 5614)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework covers individuals and organizations, as well as multiple operator categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records refer to people and organizations that commit road-traffic violations. They also identify motor vehicle operators, specialized-use motorcycle operators, and specialized-use motorcycle owners in connection with unresolved administrative-violation requirements. [Data: Entities (3124, 4717, 4718, 3430); Relationships (9044, 10120, 10121, 9320)]

The organization-violator description specifically concerns an organization that has not completed the competent state agency’s requirements for resolving the violation. The supplied records do not describe any named organization or individual, or establish that any particular party is non-compliant. [Data: Entities (3430); Relationships (9320)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Licence and professional-certificate revocation is identified as an available enforcement measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Revocation of licenses and professional certificates is identified among measures associated with administrative violations. The records do not specify the conditions, duration, or cases in which revocation applies, so its presence should not be read as a consequence for every traffic violation. [Data: Entities (4230); Relationships (9983)]

The motor vehicle operator description separately refers to applicable, time-limited licence-category deprivation, but does not provide further procedural details. [Data: Entities (3124)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports legal significance but not assessments of technical capability or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied records describe legal provisions, violation categories, penalties, remedial measures, and affected groups. They contain no concrete information about technical systems or capabilities, public reputation, or actual enforcement results; those dimensions therefore cannot be assessed from this material. [Data: Entities (4341, 4112, 107, 1285, 5514)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Owners and Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community describes a regulatory framework centered on vehicle owners and road-traffic violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It links violations to authorized enforcement, administrative records, resolution deadlines, and penalty decisions, while also covering owner-specific rules for required documents, license-plate retention, and intelligent-transport-vehicle permits. The records describe procedures and potential consequences, not evidence that a particular person or organization violated the rules or that a penalty was imposed. [Data: Entities (5439, 4560, 621, 120, 3637); Relationships (10304, 10221, 2789, 379, 9503)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects vehicle-owner obligations with enforcement and several related regulatory procedures, but the data describes rules rather than specific incidents or actual noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle owners are central to the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The VEHICLE OWNER is the community’s principal hub, connected to violations, administrative records, resolution requirements, penalties, plate rules, and intelligent-transport permits. This structure makes the owner the main point of reference for understanding the described obligations and procedures. [Data: Entities (5439); Relationships (10304, 10221, 382, 9953, 8572)]

The records distinguish between an owner’s possible responsibility and a driver’s conduct. They do not establish that any particular owner committed a violation; responsibility depends on the circumstances described in the applicable procedure. [Data: Entities (5439, 4560); Relationships (10304, 10221)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Enforcement follows a documented process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described process connects an authorized person’s enforcement role with an administrative violation record, a deadline to resolve the case, and a penalty decision. The record may be prepared against an owner when the owner is responsible and absent from the scene; if the owner is absent, the driver may sign as a witness. [Data: Entities (621, 120, 1253, 3637); Relationships (2789, 379, 378, 382)]

The framework also states that the violator must resolve the case or comply with the penalty decision by the applicable deadline. These are procedural requirements in the supplied descriptions, not evidence that a deadline has been missed in a specific case. [Data: Entities (4182, 5049, 3637); Relationships (10302, 9952, 9505, 4248)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules distinguish owner and driver responsibility
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes circumstances in which an owner may be recorded as responsible, including when the owner is present and has committed the violation, or when an owner-responsible violation is handled while the owner is absent. Article 47 is identified as a procedure for recording and sanctioning relevant violations, including cases where the owner is present. [Data: Entities (4560, 463, 120); Relationships (10304, 382, 2170, 2168)]

A specific qualification applies to required documents: a driver may face a penalty for not carrying them, while the owner is not penalized if the required documents or qualifying electronic information are presented within the stated resolution period. [Data: Entities (3643, 5439); Relationships (9507, 2787)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violations may carry additional inspection-related consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described road-traffic regulatory violations include conduct such as using a vehicle whose cargo box or permitted load capacity does not comply with current regulations. The data states that specified violations may also result in suspension of the right to use the vehicle’s technical-safety and environmental-protection inspection certificate and sticker for one to three months. [Data: Entities (4423, 4840, 4240); Relationships (10218, 9985)]

These are potential sanctions associated with specified violations; the records do not identify a vehicle to which such a sanction has actually been applied. [Data: Entities (4423, 4840); Relationships (10218, 9985)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-plate retention is a separate owner entitlement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An owner may retain a license plate for up to five years in described circumstances, including when a vehicle reaches the end of its service life, becomes unusable, or changes ownership. The plate may be registered to another vehicle owned by the same person or organization, subject to the stated rules. [Data: Entities (2894, 5396, 5080, 5439); Relationships (8572, 10640, 10589, 8569)]

The retention period has a defined endpoint: after five years, the registration authority withdraws the plate and returns it to the plate pool for possible issuance to another organization or individual. [Data: Entities (2894); Relationships (8572)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Intelligent-transport vehicles have permit and revocation procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework allows a vehicle owner or legally authorized person to apply to replace a damaged intelligent-transport-vehicle operating permit or reissue one that has been lost. The competent authority considers the application within two working days and gives a reasoned written response if requirements are not met. [Data: Entities (4139, 2913, 5439, 621); Relationships (9922, 2788, 8606)]

If an operating license or permit is revoked, the owner is responsible for surrendering it to the issuing authority. The records describe administrative capabilities and duties, not the technical operation or performance of the vehicles themselves. [Data: Entities (2721, 5439, 621); Relationships (8025, 2785)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A cooperative can be treated as the vehicle owner in a specified arrangement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes an arrangement in which an unnamed cooperative registers a transport business using a member’s vehicle. For purposes of penalties under the stated rule, the cooperative is treated as the vehicle owner. [Data: Entities (1122, 1124); Relationships (3977, 3974)]

This attribution is limited to the described arrangement and penalty context; the records do not identify the cooperative or member, or establish that either is involved in a particular violation. [Data: Entities (1122, 1124); Relationships (3977, 3974)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Decree 168/2024 Road-Traffic Sanctioning
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative enforcement framework for road-traffic violations under Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The violator and administrative violation case or proceeding sit at the center, while an authorized sanctioning official handles detection results, records, sanction decisions, and notices. Missed deadlines can trigger notifications to vehicle, inspection, or driving-license agencies. The material also describes opportunities to present documents during the resolution period, temporary deprivation of license or certificate use, file-retention duties, penalties, and a corrective measure involving removal of disruptive sound or lighting equipment. The records describe procedures and responsibilities; they do not establish that a particular person violated the rules or that any sanction was actually imposed.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high institutional importance because it links violation processing, sanctions, and multiple agency notifications, although the records describe rules rather than a specific incident or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violator is the central subject of the enforcement process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Multiple records connect the violator to the obligation to resolve a road-traffic case or comply with an imposed sanction, and to the possibility of notices when required deadlines are missed. These links make the responsible person the central subject of the process, but do not establish that any particular person is culpable. [Data: Entities (5609, 4422, 112, 4608); Relationships (10217, 357, 10395, 4951)]

The proceeding also provides a period in which a violator may present required documents or qualifying information from an electronic identification account. [Data: Entities (119, 5609); Relationships (376)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authorized sanctioning official is the operational hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authorized official is assigned multiple procedural roles: receiving technical detection results, preparing a violation record, issuing a sanction decision, notifying parties, and sending agency notices when deadlines are missed. This concentration of duties makes the official a key point of control in the described enforcement workflow. [Data: Entities (625, 5076, 5560); Relationships (2802, 2805, 2798, 355, 2801)]

The records also assign this official responsibility for preparing and retaining a case file when handling a license or practice certificate whose use has been temporarily suspended. [Data: Entities (625, 4045, 4867); Relationships (2800, 9841)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Missed deadlines can lead to notifications across relevant agencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a case remains unresolved or a sanction decision is not complied with by the deadline, the authorized official is described as notifying relevant agencies. The agency notified depends on the circumstances specified in the records. [Data: Entities (625, 112, 4608); Relationships (355, 2801)]

The listed recipients include the driving-license issuing agency for an identified violator, the vehicle inspection agency for a vehicle subject to inspection, and the vehicle registration agency. The records describe notification duties, not the agencies’ subsequent actions. [Data: Entities (1708, 5404, 5459); Relationships (2799, 2803, 2804)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes document-submission provisions during case resolution
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The administrative violation proceeding includes a specified resolution period during which a driver may present required documents or qualifying information from an electronic identification account. This is a procedural opportunity described in the records, not evidence that documents were presented in any particular case. [Data: Entities (119, 5609); Relationships (376)]

A commercial transport driver is specifically linked to the ability to present required documents or qualifying electronic information within that period. The provided data does not elaborate on additional requirements or exceptions for this driver category. [Data: Entities (1018, 119); Relationships (373)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License deprivation has timing and recordkeeping requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a provision identified as Article 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning time-limited deprivation of the right to use licenses and practice certificates. A related entity addresses how the start date of that deprivation period is determined. [Data: Entities (477, 1353, 4867); Relationships (2231, 5811)]

Where an affected license or certificate is kept and returned, the described procedure includes preparing a record and retaining the administrative-violation case file. These are procedural requirements in the supplied text; no specific license suspension or recordkeeping event is documented. [Data: Entities (4045, 625); Relationships (2800, 9841)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules encompass penalties and a specified corrective measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data links road-traffic regulations violations with the imposition of penalties on individuals or organizations committing the specified violations. It also identifies Article 32, Clause 19 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP as relevant to potential sanctions for a vehicle owner or operator and the person who committed the violation. [Data: Entities (4422, 2594); Relationships (7836)]

A separate relationship describes removal of sound or lighting equipment installed on a vehicle when it disrupts road-traffic order or safety. This is presented as a corrective measure associated with specified violations, not as evidence that the equipment was found or removed in an actual case. [Data: Entities (4121, 4422); Relationships (9905)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Operators and Decree 168/2024 Road-Traffic Sanctions
v.tom_tat: This community is a road-traffic regulatory framework centered on vehicle operators and the procedures for sanctioning violations under Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. Its connections cover a broad range of operator conduct, including unsafe passenger transport, unauthorized priority signals, obstructive convoy driving, vehicle equipment and environmental standards, and post-accident duties. The records specify different penalty ranges for particular violations and describe a limited case in which an operator may be treated as the registered vehicle owner. The information establishes the scope of the regulatory framework, not that any particular operator has committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public and regulatory importance because it connects a wide range of road-safety, accident-response, and environmental requirements for vehicle operators to administrative sanctions.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle operators are the network’s central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle Operator is the central entity, with the highest listed degree (47), and the relationships connect it to the sanctioning procedure, penalties, and multiple categories of road conduct. The entity definition spans operators of passenger and cargo vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, and other vehicle types, while emphasizing that applicable duties and sanctions depend on the vehicle and provision involved. [Data: Entities (5431); Relationships (10284, 2558, 10628, 3035, 10296)]

This centrality indicates a broad regulatory scope, but the records describe rules and potential sanctions rather than identifying any particular operator or documenting an actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework links violations to administrative sanctioning procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road-Traffic Administrative Sanctioning Procedure is described as setting procedures and principles for sanctioning vehicle owners and drivers who violate road-traffic safety and order regulations, under Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. The procedure is linked to environmental-protection and cargo-securement violations as well as to the central operator entity. [Data: Entities (4528, 1826, 2596); Relationships (10284, 6750, 7838)]

The records indicate that the framework covers more than driving conduct alone, but do not provide details about enforcement frequency, specific cases, or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified unsafe passenger practices carry monetary penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed violations include allowing people to cling to a moving vehicle, carrying passengers illegally in a vehicle bed, and carrying passengers on a vehicle roof. The records associate these practices with a fine of VND 4,000,000 to VND 6,000,000. [Data: Entities (164, 740, 743, 2191); Relationships (519, 518, 3028, 3027, 3035)]

These provisions address passenger safety through sanctions tied to specific conduct. The information does not establish how often these violations occur or whether any operator has been penalized.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Accident-response duties are a distinct compliance concern
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe post-accident duties that can include stopping, preserving the scene, assisting injured people, remaining at the scene, and promptly reporting the accident. Failure to fulfill specified duties is linked to a fine of VND 16,000,000 to VND 18,000,000. [Data: Entities (1974, 2153, 4550, 5431); Relationships (6930, 6929, 10296)]

The broader operator description also says that an operator who causes an accident may be required to provide identifying and accident information to the competent authority. These records describe obligations and penalties, not a specific accident or finding of liability. [Data: Entities (5431); Relationships (10296)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions address priority signals and obstructive convoy driving
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Using or installing a signal device reserved for priority vehicles without priority rights is identified as a violation, with a stated fine of VND 4,000,000 to VND 6,000,000. [Data: Entities (5331, 2120); Relationships (10628, 7111)]

Driving a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle in an obstructive convoy without authorization is separately described, with a stated fine of VND 8,000,000 to VND 10,000,000. Both categories are linked to vehicle operators, but the data does not show actual incidents or enforcement actions. [Data: Entities (1121, 5431); Relationships (3973)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle equipment and environmental compliance are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle without a muffler or smoke-reduction component, and operating with equipment that fails emissions or noise standards, as covered violations. The specified equipment and environmental violations are linked to fines of VND 2,000,000 to VND 3,000,000. [Data: Entities (2241, 3352, 3356, 5395, 5429); Relationships (7303, 7304, 7305, 7306, 10639)]

The framework also includes broader environmental-protection and road-use concerns, such as oversized, overloaded, and tracked vehicles. The supplied records describe these categories but do not give a penalty amount for each one. [Data: Entities (3509, 3488, 4978, 1826); Relationships (9392, 9382, 10531, 6750)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operator and registered-owner responsibilities may overlap in a specified case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that, for applying penalties, an operator may be treated as the vehicle owner when the operator is the spouse of the person named on the vehicle registration certificate. This is presented as a limited circumstance, not a general rule that operators and registered holders are interchangeable. [Data: Entities (5431, 4068); Relationships (9855)]

The same operator description cautions that responsibilities and sanctions depend on vehicle type, conduct, and the applicable provision. This qualification is important when interpreting the range of violations and penalties represented in the community. [Data: Entities (5431)]

v.tieu_de: Road Transport Businesses and Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road transport businesses and their potential exposure to administrative penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The connected issues span vehicle equipment and data, driver health and qualifications, required identification and transport documents, and vehicle color requirements when transporting preschool children or students. Road-transport support organizations and businesses are also linked to several of these compliance areas. The records describe potential violations and fines; they do not establish that any particular organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (4480, 4498, 2007, 1983, 4494); Relationships (10263, 6979, 10262, 9442, 6943)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high impact because it covers multiple regulatory controls relevant to transport operations, passenger safety, and monitoring, but the records describe potential violations rather than confirmed noncompliance. [Data: Entities (4480, 2007, 4484, 3569); Relationships (10262, 10264, 9442, 6979)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road transport businesses are the central regulated group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road transport businesses are the community’s main hub, connected to violations involving vehicle color, driver health examinations, identification cards, journey-monitoring devices, staff training, passenger-compartment cameras, and required transport orders or documents. This breadth indicates that the cited rules cover both operational processes and equipment used in commercial road transport. [Data: Entities (4480); Relationships (10263, 6979, 6939, 10262, 10264, +more)]

The entity description attributes these potential administrative penalties to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and notes that the applicable organizational fine depends on the specific violation. The records do not identify particular businesses or report that any violation has occurred. [Data: Entities (4480)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monitoring devices and passenger-compartment recording are prominent compliance areas
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The journey-monitoring device violation includes operating a commercial transport vehicle without a required device, with an inactive or non-compliant device, or with falsified device data. The stated fines are VND 5,000,000–6,000,000 for individuals and VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for organizations; road transport businesses and support-service businesses are linked to this violation. [Data: Entities (4484, 4493); Relationships (10262, 10265)]

Separate provisions address passenger-transport cars with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat. The described violations include missing image-recording equipment, equipment that fails to record or store data while the vehicle is in traffic, and falsified data; the stated organizational fine is VND 10,000,000–12,000,000. [Data: Entities (3569, 4480, 4494); Relationships (9442, 9443)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver health, training, and identification requirements form a distinct compliance cluster
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe potential penalties for failing to organize periodic driver health examinations or conducting examinations that omit required content. The stated fines are VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for individuals and VND 20,000,000–24,000,000 for transport businesses or transport-support service organizations; the required examinations are described as regular and comprehensive. [Data: Entities (2007, 3691, 2270); Relationships (6979, 6980, 6978, 6977)]

Road transport businesses and support-service organizations are also linked to failure to issue required driver identification cards. The stated organizational fine for transport businesses or transport-support-service organizations is VND 6,000,000–8,000,000, while the individual fine is VND 3,000,000–4,000,000. The data additionally identifies use of drivers or onboard passenger-service staff without required operational and traffic-safety training as a violation, but does not specify its fine in that entity description. [Data: Entities (1983, 5343, 2275); Relationships (6939, 6940, 10264, 10268, 7343)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required transport orders and documents are another operational control
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate violation concerns failing to issue a required transport order or document to a driver, or issuing it contrary to regulations. The records connect this issue to road transport businesses and transport-support service providers, indicating that documentation responsibilities are represented among the community’s compliance topics. [Data: Entities (1984); Relationships (6942, 6943)]

The supplied information does not state a specific fine for this documentation violation. It therefore supports identifying the compliance requirement and the connected organization types, but not assigning a penalty amount. [Data: Entities (1984); Relationships (6942, 6943)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Support-service organizations share exposure to several listed requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road transport support-service organizations are connected to potential violations involving driver health examinations, driver identification cards, and passenger-compartment recording equipment. Their described fines vary by violation: the entity record gives VND 6,000,000–8,000,000 for certain breaches and VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for specified passenger-compartment recording-equipment violations. [Data: Entities (4494, 4495); Relationships (6980, 6940, 9443)]

The records also identify road transport support-service businesses as potentially subject to fines for journey-monitoring device violations and connect support-service providers to the required transport-order/document issue. The applicable penalty depends on the particular violation; the materials do not establish actual noncompliance by any support organization. [Data: Entities (4493, 4495); Relationships (10265, 6943)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student-transport vehicle color is a specific, narrowly described issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a violation involving a road transport business vehicle used to carry preschool children or students without the paint color required by regulations. The relationship record states that a road transport business whose organization commits this violation is subject to a fine of VND 8,000,000–12,000,000. [Data: Entities (4498); Relationships (10263)]

This is a specific vehicle-condition requirement within a broader set of transport rules; the supplied records do not state that a particular vehicle or business has breached it. [Data: Entities (4498, 4480); Relationships (10263)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fine amounts vary by violation and regulated party
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The penalties in the records are not uniform: for example, organizational fines are stated as VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 for certain journey-monitoring and passenger-compartment recording violations, while the vehicle-color violation is linked to VND 8,000,000–12,000,000 for a road transport business. The health-examination violation carries a stated organizational range of VND 20,000,000–24,000,000. [Data: Entities (4484, 3569, 2007, 4494); Relationships (10262, 9442, 10263, 6979)]

The source descriptions repeatedly qualify amounts by violation and by whether the party is an individual, transport business, or support-service organization. These figures should therefore be read as the listed penalties for the specified contexts, not as one general fine applicable to the whole community. [Data: Entities (4480, 2007, 1983, 4484, 3569)]

v.tieu_de: Article 48 Vehicle Inspection and Detention Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 48, which the supplied description associates with provisions in both Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Law 36/2024/QH15. The relationships chiefly describe the Decree’s enforcement framework: vehicle inspection and missing-document cases can lead to administrative records and temporary vehicle detention, with authorized officials acting under cited legal provisions. The framework also addresses replacement transport costs and links inspection procedures to inspection facilities, manufacturers, and electronic document information. The data establishes regulatory and operational significance, but does not document particular enforcement incidents, misconduct, or reputational concerns. [Data: Entities (469, 5403, 2011, 4891, 121); Relationships (2200, 2191, 2199, 2195, 384)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the framework’s material effects on vehicle inspections, enforcement, and transport operations, while the supplied data documents rules and procedures rather than specific harmful incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 48 is the central legal reference, with two distinct statutory contexts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description identifies two Vietnamese legal provisions called Article 48: one in Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP concerning temporary impoundment or custody of vehicles and related documents, and another in Law 36/2024/QH15 concerning requirements for certain motorized four-wheeled passenger and goods vehicles. The latter includes displaying the transport operator’s name and telephone number and, for passenger transport, fares. [Data: Entities (469)]

The relationship network primarily concerns the Decree’s vehicle-enforcement and inspection procedures. It connects Article 48 with inspection, failure to present required documents, detention, replacement transport, and temporary retention. The supplied information therefore supports treating the enforcement procedure as the community’s main operational focus, while keeping the separate Law 36/2024/QH15 requirements distinct. [Data: Relationships (2200, 2191, 2199, 2195, 2197)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection and document production are key decision points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle inspection is described as examining a vehicle for technical safety and environmental protection. Depending on applicable rules, drivers or operators may need to present a driving licence, vehicle registration, and technical inspection documents; the information may be supplied on paper or through an electronic identification account. [Data: Entities (5403)]

Article 48 is linked to cases in which required documents cannot be presented during inspection, and the failure-to-present entity includes failure to provide documents or their electronic information by the deadline for resolving the violation. These records establish a procedural connection between inspection, document production, and enforcement, but do not specify how often such cases occur. [Data: Entities (2011); Relationships (2200, 2191, 6991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary detention is an available enforcement measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions state that Article 48 addresses circumstances in which an authorized person may impound a vehicle before a penalty decision is issued, including specified document-related situations and violations. Article 48 is directly linked to both temporary vehicle detention and temporary retention of vehicles and documents. [Data: Entities (469, 4891, 4878); Relationships (2199, 2197)]

The data links Article 48, Clause 1 to Article 125 of the Law on Handling Administrative Violations, including cited provisions in Clause 2, Clause 8, and Point b of Clause 1. It therefore identifies a legal basis for the measure, but does not establish whether any particular detention was lawful or improperly applied. [Data: Entities (473, 251, 253, 254); Relationships (809, 813, 814, 815)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework connects driver and owner violations with official records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Administrative violation recording is described as preparation of a record for a driver who fails to present required documents and a corresponding record for the vehicle owner for relevant violations under Article 32 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The relationships connect this recording process both to failure to present documents and to temporary vehicle detention. [Data: Entities (121); Relationships (384, 385)]

A competent authority official is identified as the person who prepares the records and carries out detention under the stated rules. The community also lists multiple Article 32 clauses and subparagraphs as provisions associated with violations eligible for temporary impoundment; these are legal references, not evidence that a specific person committed a violation. [Data: Entities (1045, 388, 391, 393, 387); Relationships (383, 1655, 1658, 1660, 1661, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Detention may impose transport and relocation costs
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a detained vehicle was carrying people or goods, the described process may involve arranging another vehicle to transport them. Article 48 is linked to this replacement transport arrangement, and the entity description states that the vehicle owner bears the associated costs. [Data: Entities (4138, 469); Relationships (2195, 9920)]

This establishes a practical consequence of detention beyond the vehicle’s temporary removal from use: arranging alternative transport may create costs for the owner. The supplied data does not quantify those costs or describe their actual economic impact in any case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection processes include administrative and technical dependencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle-inspection description states that processing may be withheld when a relevant data lookup identifies an unresolved traffic violation, and may proceed after the administrative matter is resolved and the relevant authority is notified. It also describes circumstances in which a vehicle holding a required certificate may be exempt from inspection during a transfer. [Data: Entities (5403); Relationships (10584, 6991)]

The network identifies a vehicle registration inspection facility as authorized to inspect vehicles and issue technical safety and environmental protection certificates, and a vehicle manufacturer as a possible issuer of a factory inspection certificate relevant to an exemption. The description also identifies inspection of certain People’s Public Security vehicles as a subject of a specialized Ministry of Public Security database. These details indicate procedural and technical infrastructure, but do not establish its capacity, performance, or security. [Data: Entities (5480, 5426, 5403); Relationships (10645, 10643)]

v.tieu_de: Driving Against Traffic and Its Exceptions
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the road-traffic violation of driving against the direction of traffic. It covers travel against the permitted direction on a one-way street and travel contrary to a prohibitory road sign, while specifying an exception for priority vehicles performing emergency duties under stated circumstances. The supplied records do not describe particular incidents, enforcement outcomes, or organizations. [Data: Entities (1596, 3870, 4294, 3311); Relationships (6333, 6334, 6335)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has limited scope but some public-safety significance because it defines prohibited wrong-way travel and a conditional emergency-vehicle exception.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single traffic violation anchors the community
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity is driving against the direction of traffic, defined as a violation involving travel against the direction of a one-way street or on a road marked as prohibiting travel in that direction. The listed relationships connect this violation to the two road contexts and to an emergency-duty exclusion. [Data: Entities (1596); Relationships (6333, 6334, 6335)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: One-way streets are an expressly covered context
phat_hien.giai_thich: Driving against the permitted direction on a one-way street is included in the specified violation. The records define a one-way street as a road on which travel is restricted to one direction. [Data: Entities (3311, 1596); Relationships (6333)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibitory signs define another covered context
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation also includes driving against the direction indicated by a prohibitory sign. The associated entity describes a road bearing a sign that prohibits travel against the permitted direction. [Data: Entities (4294, 1596); Relationships (6335)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An emergency-duty exception is specified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The text excludes priority vehicles performing emergency duties from the specified violation in the stated circumstances. The entity description likewise frames the exclusion as conditional; the records do not provide further details about those conditions. [Data: Entities (3870, 1596); Relationships (6334)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records define a narrow regulatory topic
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information concerns the definition and scope of one road-traffic violation, including two covered road situations and one conditional exclusion. It contains no information about particular cases, penalties, enforcement, or the reputation or capabilities of any organization, so conclusions on those matters are not supported by these records. [Data: Entities (1596, 3870, 4294, 3311); Relationships (6333, 6334, 6335)]

v.tieu_de: Article 24 Transport Violations and Driver Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community concerns Article 24 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and its treatment of automobile drivers who violate fresh-food or live-animal transport regulations. The relationships connect both violation types to penalties and to driver’s license point deductions. The supplied records describe regulatory consequences, but do not establish that any particular driver committed a violation or provide information about enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it links two transport-regulation violations to penalties and driver’s license point deductions, while providing no evidence of specific cases or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver’s license point deductions are a central consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The deduction of driver’s license points is connected to both live-animal and fresh-food transport violations under Article 24. This makes the point-deduction provision a shared consequence across the two violation categories in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (1316); Relationships (5747, 5746)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fresh-food transport violations are subject to penalties and point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe an automobile driver’s violation of fresh-food transport rules as covered by Article 24. They connect this violation both to penalties for automobile drivers and to driver’s license point deductions. [Data: Entities (5563, 1316, 4612); Relationships (5746, 10399)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Live-animal transport violations are subject to penalties and point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied data identifies violations of live-animal transport rules by automobile drivers as covered by Article 24. The violation is linked to both penalties and deductions of driver’s license points. [Data: Entities (5567, 1316, 4612); Relationships (5747, 10400)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes regulatory consequences, not particular enforcement cases
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships characterize the violations and the penalties or point deductions associated with them. They do not identify a specific driver, describe an individual enforcement action, or indicate how often these rules are applied. [Data: Entities (5563, 5567, 4612, 1316); Relationships (10399, 10400, 5746, 5747)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not establish compliance or broader impact
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information gives no evidence about whether drivers or transport operators comply with the rules, the scale of any violations, or outcomes for animals or food. The community’s documented significance is therefore limited to the regulatory framework and the stated consequences for covered violations. [Data: Entities (5563, 5567, 4612, 1316); Relationships (5746, 5747, 10399, 10400)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Relocation to Detention Location
v.tom_tat: This community describes a vehicle-relocation process involving an authorized detention official and, when direct relocation cannot be arranged, a third-party individual or organization. The central process concerns moving vehicles to a designated detention location under specified circumstances, including noncompliance or failure to meet safety or environmental standards. The records establish procedural roles but do not assess whether any particular relocation occurred or whether the process was legally compliant in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational and regulatory importance because it describes a vehicle detention and relocation process with authorized officials and third-party alternatives, but provides no evidence of specific incidents or broader impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle relocation is the central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community centers on relocating a violating vehicle to a designated detention location. The entity description identifies circumstances including an absent or noncompliant operator or owner, failure to meet conditions for driving, and failure to meet applicable safety or environmental standards. [Data: Entities (5488)]

The relationships connect both the authorized official and potential hired movers to this relocation process, making it the hub of the community. [Data: Relationships (2771, 7746, 7748)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorized officials arrange relocation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An authorized detention official is described as a person empowered to detain a vehicle and arrange its relocation. The relationship record specifies that the official arranges movement to the detention location in circumstances identified in Article 48. [Data: Entities (612); Relationships (2771)]

The supplied information describes the official’s role but does not establish how authorization is granted, how decisions are reviewed, or whether any individual action complied with applicable requirements.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Hiring a third party is a fallback option
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The official may hire a third party when unable to arrange relocation directly. This makes third-party hiring a contingent part of the process rather than the stated primary arrangement. [Data: Entities (2494); Relationships (2770)]

The records define the arrangement at a general level and do not provide details about procurement, payment, oversight, or performance standards.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Both individuals and organizations may move vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies two possible third-party mover categories: a hired individual and a hired organization. Each may be hired to carry out relocation, and each is linked to the central vehicle-relocation process. [Data: Entities (2492, 2493); Relationships (7745, 7747, 7746, 7748)]

No specific individual or organization is named, and the records do not describe their qualifications, operating practices, or track record.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a procedure, not documented outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity and relationship descriptions outline roles, possible circumstances for relocation, and a third-party fallback. They do not identify a specific detained vehicle, a completed relocation, a dispute, or an adverse outcome. [Data: Entities (5488, 2494, 2493, 612, 2492); Relationships (2770, 2771, 7745, 7746, 7747, +more)]

Accordingly, the material supports describing the community’s procedural structure, but not conclusions about actual enforcement frequency, legal compliance, or effects on vehicle owners.

v.tieu_de: Driver’s License Point Restoration and Administration
v.tom_tat: This community concerns the driver’s-license point restoration process described under Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its central process connects the license holder with restoration to 12 points, notification by an authorized person, and an automatic update to the road-traffic administrative-violations database. The data also cover restoration while use rights are suspended and a separate exchange or reissuance process for specified circumstances. [Data: Entities (1523, 1519, 3276, 1518, 1526, +more); Relationships (6177, 6203, 6178, 6202, 4218, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it describes a formal licensing process involving drivers, notifications, and administrative data updates, but the provided records indicate no specific violation or threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restoration is governed by defined timing and point-balance conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described rule provides for automatic restoration of a license’s point balance to 12 when the license has not had all its points deducted and no points have been deducted for 12 months since the most recent deduction. The process is identified as governed by Article 51 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (1523)]

This makes the restoration process conditional rather than an unrestricted reset. The records describe the rule but do not provide further operational details about how the qualifying period is verified. [Data: Entities (1523)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The license holder is the central recipient of the process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver’s-license holder is the person whose points are restored, linking the individual directly to the restoration procedure. [Data: Entities (1519); Relationships (6177)]

After the point data have been restored to 12, an authorized person is to inform the holder immediately. The records establish this notification step but do not identify the authorized person or describe the notification channel. [Data: Entities (1519, 3276); Relationships (6203, 6178)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rule also covers licenses under suspension of use rights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described automatic restoration rule applies even when the license is subject to suspension of the right to use it. This connects point restoration with a distinct licensing status and indicates that suspension does not, by itself, exclude the stated restoration mechanism. [Data: Entities (1523, 1526); Relationships (6202)]

The provided information does not state that restoration ends or changes the suspension; it only specifies that restoration may occur while the suspension is in effect. [Data: Entities (1523, 1526); Relationships (6202)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restored point data are automatically updated in an administrative database
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When points are automatically restored to 12, the driver’s-license point data are also automatically updated in the Database on Administrative Violations in Road Traffic Order and Safety. This establishes a data link between the restoration process and the administrative record system. [Data: Entities (1239, 1523); Relationships (4218)]

The records support the existence of this automatic update but do not specify the database’s technical architecture, access controls, or processing timelines beyond the stated automatic update. [Data: Entities (1239, 1523); Relationships (4218)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Exchange or reissuance is a separate provision for specified circumstances
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community also includes a process by which eligible license holders may exchange or obtain a reissued license in specified circumstances. A change to information recorded on the license is one stated circumstance. [Data: Entities (1518, 1519, 786); Relationships (6176, 3130)]

This process is related to license-holder administration but is distinct from point restoration in the supplied records. The data do not enumerate all circumstances for exchange or reissuance. [Data: Entities (1518, 1519, 786); Relationships (6176, 3130)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Registration and Road-Traffic Violation Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle registration and its links to road-traffic violation resolution, administrative penalties, data lookups, and driver’s-license procedures. A violation identified in a lookup can block registration and other specified procedures until the relevant matter is resolved, while separate rules address registration and auction-winning plates after vehicle transfers.
