The records describe a regulatory process with significant procedural consequences, but do not establish actual compliance outcomes or particular violations by named individuals. [Data: Entities (5458, 114, 4197, 90, 5082); Relationships (362, 9968, 7006, 9969, 10593)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the broad procedural importance of vehicle registration and the potential for violation records to affect registration, inspection, and driver’s-license services, without evidence of specific real-world harm or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle registration is the community’s central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle registration is described as recording vehicles with the relevant regulatory authority and associating license plates with them in a registration and management system. The description includes motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles recorded in a specialized database managed by the Ministry of Public Security, and excludes military vehicles. [Data: Entities (5458, 4076)]

The network’s relationships reinforce registration’s central role: it connects to violation-case resolution, restrictions triggered by data lookups, and transactions involving auction-winning plates. [Data: Relationships (362, 9968, 10593)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unresolved violations can delay vehicle registration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Registration for a vehicle identified as involved in a road-traffic violation is not resolved until the required violation case has been completed and the relevant authority notified. The relationship data likewise connects administrative violation case resolution to the registration process. [Data: Entities (5458, 114); Relationships (362)]

The described rule makes completion of the case a procedural condition for registration; the records do not establish how often delays occur or provide outcomes for individual cases. [Data: Entities (5458, 114)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Missed deadlines are linked to administrative penalties and procedural restrictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to resolve a violation by the deadline includes not addressing the matter by the appointment deadline in the violation record or authority’s notice, or not complying with a penalty decision by its deadline. The administrative penalty procedure sets out principles and processes for imposing penalties on vehicle owners and operators for specified road-traffic violations. [Data: Entities (2026, 90, 3638); Relationships (235, 7005)]

A competent penalty authority is described as authorized to impose penalties and issue a notice concerning resolution. The records connect that authority to both the penalty procedure and the setting of a resolution deadline. [Data: Entities (1055, 114, 90); Relationships (234, 358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Data lookups can trigger restrictions on vehicle and driver’s-license services
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a relevant data lookup identifies a violating vehicle or violator, the described restrictions include not processing the vehicle’s inspection and registration and not issuing, exchanging, or reissuing the violator’s driver’s license. [Data: Entities (4197, 5557, 1560); Relationships (9969, 6283)]

The relationship between missed deadlines and these restrictions is also represented in the network. These records describe a procedural mechanism, not evidence that any particular person or vehicle was subject to it. [Data: Entities (2026, 4197); Relationships (7006)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Auction-winning plates have specific rules for vehicle transactions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe transfer, exchange, gift, or inheritance of a vehicle with an auction-winning plate as a transaction for which registration is addressed afterward. They also connect the transaction to procedures for managing, revoking, and issuing vehicle registration and auction-winning plates. [Data: Entities (5082, 2959, 4241, 2779); Relationships (10593, 8669, 9986, 8122)]

The entity description states that a vehicle transferred, exchanged, gifted, or inherited together with its auction-winning plate is an exception to the general rule of recall after the five-year retention period. It also says the winning bidder generally must complete the procedure to attach the plate to a vehicle within 12 months of receiving confirmation. [Data: Entities (5082, 5458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration is also described as a vehicle-verification and violation-detection mechanism
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle-registration description says registration serves to verify vehicle information and detect violations. It further states that vehicle control software or engines must not be altered to manipulate inspection results. [Data: Entities (5458)]

These statements indicate that the described framework includes verification and inspection-related controls, but the provided records do not specify technical system architecture, detection performance, or instances of attempted manipulation. [Data: Entities (5458)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Road-Traffic Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION, a broad category of administrative breaches under cited provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its connected entities describe consequences and corrective actions, including applicable penalties, license-point deductions, possible driving-privilege suspension, confiscation of license plates and plate-altering devices, and vehicle remediation followed by reinspection. The records also identify cargo-vehicle violations and the specific case of carrying a qualifying child passenger in the same row as the driver. Point deductions and other sanctions are described as provision-dependent, and one record expressly notes uncertainty about the applicable deduction amount. [Data: Entities (4456, 2, 194, 1651, 721); Relationships (4, 584, 10244, 6411, 3917, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it covers varied traffic conduct and potentially significant administrative sanctions, though the records do not establish actual incidents or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Broad scope of covered road-traffic conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION covers administrative breaches involving road order and safety across bicycles and similar vehicles, motorcycles and mopeds, and automobiles and similar vehicles. The description cites Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, including Articles 9 and 32, and gives examples such as registration-document irregularities, failure to establish vehicle origin, and specified conduct by a vehicle owner driving directly. [Data: Entities (4456)]

The records describe possible administrative consequences, including fines, vehicle confiscation, driving-license point deductions, and required corrective measures. They do not provide case-specific evidence that any violation occurred or that a particular sanction was imposed. [Data: Entities (4456); Relationships (584)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctions are attached to the central violation category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship data links ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION to an applicable penalty, indicating that the specified conduct is subject to a sanction. A separate relationship states that certain violations may also require correction of a vehicle’s cargo body and permitted carrying capacity before it returns to the road. [Data: Entities (194, 5489); Relationships (584, 10244)]

The description of APPLICABLE PENALTY says the penalty is imposed in addition to a license-point deduction, but it also notes that the source descriptions differ on whether the deduction is four or ten points. Accordingly, the point amount for that general penalty description cannot be treated as settled by these records. [Data: Entities (194)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ten-point deductions apply to specified provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a ten-point deduction under Clause 13 of Article 21 for specified violations, and state that the deduction applies in addition to any other applicable penalty. The relationship data associates this deduction with cargo-vehicle violations identified in points a and b of Clause 8 and Clause 11, and with TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 21. [Data: Entities (2, 5048, 721); Relationships (2, 3, 5)]

A separate relationship says that when a vehicle owner directly commits the specified violation while driving, ten points are deducted from that owner’s license in addition to the applicable penalty. These are provision-specific descriptions and should not be generalized to every violation in the broader category. [Data: Relationships (4)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some violations may suspend driving privileges or involve plate-related confiscation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Committing the violation specified in Clause 12 may result in a 10-to-12-month loss of the right to use a driving license. The relationship connects this potential suspension to ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION. [Data: Entities (1651); Relationships (6411)]

For specified violations, the records also describe an additional sanction involving seizure of license plates and devices used to alter them. The provided data does not identify the exact circumstances beyond describing these as specified violations. [Data: Entities (1089); Relationships (3917)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-vehicle cases include remediation and reinspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
CARGO-VEHICLE TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS concern drivers of trucks, tractors, and similar goods-transport vehicles, including vehicles towing trailers or semi-trailers. Drivers committing the described violations are subject to a penalty, and the records separately link specified cargo-vehicle provisions to a ten-point deduction. [Data: Entities (721); Relationships (3, 3006)]

Where a vehicle’s cargo body and permitted carrying capacity require correction, the vehicle must be remediated before being used on the road and reinspected after adjustment. These records establish a corrective process but do not specify how frequently it applies or report outcomes. [Data: Entities (5489, 5487); Relationships (10244, 10679)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Child-passenger and post-accident conduct are identified examples
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One described violation involves carrying a child under 10 years old and under 1.35 metres tall in the same row of seats as the driver, except in a car with only one row of seats. The CHILD PASSENGER entity and its relationship to ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION identify this as a specific safety-related case within the broader category. [Data: Entities (4456, 816); Relationships (3187)]

The central entity also describes conduct after a traffic accident: failing to stop, preserve the scene, assist injured people, remain at the scene, or promptly report to authorities. The information is descriptive of covered conduct and does not indicate that a particular accident or failure occurred. [Data: Entities (4456)]

v.tieu_de: Administrative Sanctioning and Road-Use Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Administrative Sanctioning Procedure described in Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It connects an authorized competent person and the process for issuing sanctioning decisions with several categories of road-traffic violations, including road use, vehicle or road load and dimension limits, and environmental protection. The network also describes corrective actions for cargo-related violations, such as securing cargo, closing cargo-box doors, unloading goods from a cab roof, and using a container locking mechanism. The data describes a regulatory and enforcement framework; it does not establish particular violations, penalties imposed, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (106, 4581, 1057, 2767); Relationships (297, 293, 300, 299, 295)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful operational importance because it links an administrative enforcement process to multiple road-safety and environmental violation categories and prescribed corrective measures, but the data gives no specific enforcement outcomes or incidents. [Data: Entities (106, 4581); Relationships (297, 300, 295)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A central procedure connects the violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Administrative Sanctioning Procedure is the network’s central entity, with the highest listed degree, and is linked to road-use and vehicle-load violations as well as load-limit, dimension-limit, and environmental-protection violations. The description identifies Article 47 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP as the source for the procedure and its penalty principles. [Data: Entities (106, 4581, 5437, 5435, 1831); Relationships (297, 300, 299, 295)]

These links indicate a framework spanning several kinds of regulated conduct. They do not show that any particular person or vehicle committed a violation or that a sanction was actually imposed.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A competent person handles records and sanctions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The procedure assigns a role to a competent person, who may prepare an administrative violation record and proceed with sanctions. The network separately links that person to issuance of a sanctioning decision, identifying decision issuance as an authorized step in the process. [Data: Entities (1057, 2767); Relationships (293, 3825)]

The procedure description also states that when a vehicle owner is absent during handling, the vehicle’s driver may sign the violation record as a witness. This describes a procedural contingency, not evidence that it occurred in a specific case. [Data: Entities (106)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation scope includes road use, loads, dimensions, and environmental protection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The broad Road-Use and Vehicle-Load Violations category covers use of roads or sidewalks for other purposes, environmental protection, carrying more people than permitted, vehicle or road load and dimension limits, and securing transported goods. It is linked to the administrative procedure as conduct subject to the stated penalty process. [Data: Entities (4581); Relationships (297)]

The network also separately identifies vehicle or road load-limit violations, vehicle or road dimension-limit violations, and environmental-protection violations as categories covered by that procedure. The records describe the scope of regulated conduct but do not provide individual penalty amounts or case outcomes. [Data: Entities (5437, 5435, 1831); Relationships (300, 299, 295)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-related corrective measures are prominent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed corrective measures include securing transported goods, unloading goods carried on a vehicle’s cab roof, latching and securing rear and side cargo-box doors, and using the prescribed container locking mechanism. These measures are linked to the broader road-use and vehicle-load violation category. [Data: Entities (4629, 5255, 2293, 5348); Relationships (10324, 10325, 7361, 10326)]

The network additionally links specified Article 21 conduct to these same kinds of corrective actions. It therefore presents cargo handling as a recurring element of the described corrective framework, without specifying the circumstances or frequency of any actual violation. [Data: Entities (311); Relationships (1227, 1226, 1228, 1229)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 21 and Article 12 references provide narrower rule groupings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 21 Violations are defined as conduct described in specified clauses of Article 21 for which the text prescribes corrective measures. The listed links connect that category to securing cargo, fixing cargo-box doors, unloading cab-roof goods, and using a container locking mechanism. [Data: Entities (311); Relationships (1227, 1226, 1228, 1229)]

Cargo-Securing Violations are separately described as breaches of rules referenced in Article 12, and the associated relationship specifies securing cargo according to regulations as the corrective action. [Data: Entities (714, 4629); Relationships (2991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules, not demonstrated compliance or enforcement results
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The available descriptions and links specify procedural roles, violation categories, a decision-making step, and corrective actions. They do not identify particular people, vehicles, enforcement cases, penalties actually issued, or whether corrective actions were completed. [Data: Entities (106, 1057, 2767, 4581); Relationships (293, 3825, 297)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is best understood as the breadth and structure of the described administrative framework, rather than evidence of a specific compliance failure, operational capability, or reputational issue.

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Drivers and Road-Traffic Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the vehicle driver, linked to multiple road-traffic violations, enforcement requests by on-duty officials, and associated sanctions. The records cover alcohol- and drug-test refusals, cargo-vehicle violations, improper priority-signal use, and carrying a passenger using an umbrella. They describe fines and an eight-point license deduction, while noting that the applicable penalties depend on circumstances and that the cited drug-test fine ranges conflict. [Data: Entities (5392, 4054, 3306, 4053, 1747); Relationships (9846, 9260, 9845, 3005, 6623)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects broad driver categories to enforcement and potentially substantial sanctions, although the records describe rules rather than the scale of any actual incident. [Data: Entities (5392, 4054, 4053, 1747, 2183); Relationships (9846, 9845, 6623, 7194)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle drivers form the community's central hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The vehicle-driver entity is connected to a range of violations and penalties, including test refusals, cargo-vehicle conduct, improper use of priority signals, and carrying a passenger using an umbrella. The entity description covers drivers of several vehicle types, including cars, motorcycles, trucks, bicycles, and other rudimentary vehicles. [Data: Entities (5392, 3182, 3471, 645); Relationships (9846, 9845, 3005, 10620, 3012)]

This structure makes the driver the common subject of the community's regulatory material; it does not establish that any specific driver committed a violation. [Data: Relationships (9846, 9845, 3005, 6623, 6500)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Officials are linked to alcohol- and drug-testing enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An on-duty official may request or, where authorized, require a driver to undergo alcohol testing or testing for drugs and other prohibited stimulants. The relationships connect officials to drivers and to both alcohol-test and drug-test refusal violations. [Data: Entities (3306, 5392, 4054, 4053); Relationships (9260, 9257, 9256, 9846, 9845)]

The records describe legal enforcement relationships, but do not identify a particular official, driver, test encounter, or outcome. [Data: Entities (3306, 5392); Relationships (9260, 9257, 9256)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Alcohol-test refusal carries cited fines with contextual variation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Refusal to comply with an official's alcohol-test request is described as a road-traffic violation. The entity record gives fine ranges of 400,000–600,000 VND and 30,000,000–40,000,000 VND, and says the applicable amount may depend on vehicle category or regulatory context. [Data: Entities (4054); Relationships (9846, 9257)]

The material therefore signals potentially substantial financial consequences but does not provide enough detail to determine which range applies in a particular case. The driver is the person associated with the refusal violation. [Data: Entities (4054, 5392); Relationships (9846, 9260)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The drug-test refusal fine information is inconsistent
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The drug-test refusal description identifies refusal of an on-duty official's request for testing as a traffic violation, but cites two conflicting fine ranges: 30,000,000–40,000,000 VND and 8,000,000–10,000,000 VND. The record explicitly states that the applicable fine cannot be determined from the supplied information. [Data: Entities (4053); Relationships (9845, 9256)]

This discrepancy limits the reliability of any attempt to state a single penalty based on these records alone. The described violation involves a vehicle driver and a request from an official acting in the course of duty. [Data: Entities (4053, 3306, 5392); Relationships (9845, 9256)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Cargo-vehicle conduct is linked to an eight-point license deduction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The cargo-vehicle violation concerns road-traffic order and safety rules and is associated with drivers of trucks, tractors with trailers or semi-trailers, or similar vehicles transporting goods. The specific conduct referred to in Clause 7 is not specified in the entity description. [Data: Entities (720, 4543, 5392); Relationships (3005, 3004)]

The records state that committing the specified Clause 7 act results in an eight-point deduction from the driver's license. Because the underlying conduct is not detailed here, the records do not establish which particular cargo-vehicle behavior triggers that deduction. [Data: Entities (1747, 720); Relationships (6623, 3003)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other listed violations include alcohol-threshold and road-use offenses
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving above the stated alcohol thresholds—more than 80 milligrams per 100 milliliters of blood or 0.4 milligrams per liter of breath—is described as a violation under Clause 11 of Article 6, with a stated fine of 30,000,000–40,000,000 VND. [Data: Entities (1683, 878, 2183); Relationships (3354, 3355, 6500, 7194)]

The records also describe unauthorized or improper use of priority signals as punishable by a fine of 600,000–800,000 VND, and carrying a passenger using an umbrella as punishable by 200,000–400,000 VND. These are presented as separate violations, not as evidence that an incident occurred. [Data: Entities (5214, 726, 3572); Relationships (10620, 3012, 3011)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Registration Authority and Traffic Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Vehicle Registration Authority and its coordination with the competent sanctioning official, vehicle inspection authority, and driving-license issuing authority. It describes a process in which unresolved traffic violation data is checked before vehicle registration or inspection, and the sanctioning official notifies relevant agencies after a case is resolved. The community also covers registration-document changes, recalled license plates returning to a pool for possible reissue, and the administration of driving licenses. The records describe administrative responsibilities and procedures, but do not provide evidence of misconduct or specific operational failures.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects vehicle registration and inspection processes with violation-case checks, official notifications, and plate and license administration.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle Registration Authority is the central administrative hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vehicle Registration Authority is responsible for vehicle registration and related administrative matters, including registration certificates and license plates. Its relationships span violation checks, official notifications, changes to registration documents and plates, and the return and reissue of recalled plates, making it the most connected entity in this community. [Data: Entities (5469); Relationships (3840, 9253, 10625, 9856, 3142)]

The records establish an administrative role and broad procedural connections; they do not document the authority’s performance, compliance history, or any specific adverse event. [Data: Entities (5469); Relationships (3840, 9253, 10625)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violation checks are described as a precondition for registration and inspection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Before registering a vehicle, the Vehicle Registration Authority must check relevant data concerning vehicles and people with reported violations, including unresolved cases. The Vehicle Inspection Authority must conduct a corresponding check before an inspection. [Data: Entities (5260, 5469, 5406); Relationships (10625, 10624)]

These checks connect unresolved administrative traffic cases to two separate vehicle-related processes. The records describe the checks as procedural requirements but do not specify the data systems used, how checks are performed, or what happens in every case where an unresolved violation is found. [Data: Entities (5260); Relationships (10625, 10624)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Case resolution triggers notices to relevant agencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Once a violation case is resolved, the competent sanctioning official must promptly notify relevant agencies. The listed recipients include the Vehicle Registration Authority, Vehicle Inspection Authority, and Driving License Issuing Authority. [Data: Entities (1061, 3301, 5469, 5406, 1633); Relationships (3836, 3840, 3839, 3835, 9253)]

The official notification may be written or electronically transmitted, and the records describe it as the means by which agencies are informed of a resolved case. This indicates a defined coordination link among the sanctioning official and the three administrative authorities, without specifying notification timelines beyond “promptly” or the agencies’ internal handling procedures. [Data: Entities (3301); Relationships (3836, 9253, 9252, 6388)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violation notices can set a deadline for resolving a case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An authorized sanctioning official may issue a violation notice that specifies a deadline for resolving the case. The community also defines an unresolved administrative traffic violation case as one that remains unresolved after the stated deadline to attend to the case or comply with the penalty decision has passed. [Data: Entities (1061, 5260, 5559); Relationships (3841)]

The unresolved-case status is relevant to registration and inspection because both authorities are instructed to check related violation data before proceeding with their respective functions. The records do not establish that every unresolved case automatically prevents registration or inspection. [Data: Entities (5260, 5469, 5406); Relationships (10625, 10624)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recalled plates may return to circulation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Vehicle Registration Authority withdraws a license plate after its five-year retention period and returns it to the plate pool for possible reissue. A recalled plate may then be registered and issued to another organization or individual, including individuals other than the former owner. [Data: Entities (5469, 4069, 3452); Relationships (9856, 9357)]

The records therefore describe both the administrative return of plates to a pool and a subsequent registration-and-issuance process. They do not provide details about plate availability, selection criteria, or the identity of any recipient. [Data: Entities (4069, 3452); Relationships (9856, 9357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration documents and plates can require changes when their form structure changes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A change by the Vehicle Registration Authority to the form or structure of registration certificates or license plates is identified as a circumstance that may require those documents or plates to be changed. [Data: Entities (5469, 795); Relationships (3142)]

This links the authority’s administrative decisions about document or plate formats to a potential need for replacement or modification. The records do not specify the scope, timing, or practical implementation of such changes. [Data: Entities (795, 5469); Relationships (3142)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driving-license administration is linked to the issuing authority and case notifications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Driving License Issuing Authority is responsible for issuing, exchanging, or reissuing driving licenses and receives notice from the competent sanctioning official after a violation case is resolved. Driving-license administration may proceed according to the rules after resolution and notification. [Data: Entities (1061, 1633, 1628); Relationships (3835, 6388, 6387)]

This establishes a procedural connection between case resolution, agency notification, and license issuance or reissuance. The records do not describe particular license decisions or establish that notification alone determines the outcome of an application. [Data: Entities (1633, 1628); Relationships (6388, 6387)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police Department and Public Security Ministry
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Traffic Police Department (Cục Cảnh sát giao thông), which operates under the Ministry of Public Security and connects national policy to local police implementation. Its responsibilities include licensing-related administration, traffic-law testing, and coordination of implementation reports. The network also includes circulars and their implementing bodies, alongside digital channels used for dossiers and driving-licence point-restoration updates. The records indicate substantial public-administration and road-safety significance, but do not establish adverse conduct or a specific threat.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad importance to national traffic regulation, enforcement, licensing procedures, and public-facing digital services, rather than evidence of misconduct or imminent harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Traffic Police Department is the operational hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Department is subordinate to the Ministry of Public Security and serves as a central channel for implementation-related reporting from police units and local authorities. This places it between national-level guidance and local execution of traffic-related rules. [Data: Entities (1216, 683, 1177); Relationships (2922, 4063, 2920)]

The Department also has operational responsibilities for receiving dossiers, issuing, reissuing, or revoking permits for eligible priority vehicles, and guiding traffic-law tests. These functions give it a significant administrative role across the community. [Data: Entities (1216); Relationships (2940, 4169)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry provides regulatory oversight and implementation guidance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Public Security is identified as the parent authority for the Traffic Police Department and as the recipient of reports about difficulties encountered during implementation of relevant circulars. The records describe the Ministry as providing guidance in response to such reports. [Data: Entities (683, 1177); Relationships (2922, 2920, 2927, 2928)]

This reporting structure links central authority with police units, local authorities, individuals, and organizations concerned with implementation. The material describes an administrative feedback and guidance process, not an assessment of how effectively it operates in practice. [Data: Relationships (2919, 2930, 4063, 4064)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circulars define responsibilities across the implementation network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is described as amending wording and repealing certain appendices and forms in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, while also setting out implementation responsibilities and a process for reporting difficulties. [Data: Entities (4952, 683); Relationships (2927)]

The listed responsibilities extend to provincial and municipal police directors, heads of ministry-level units, and concerned individuals and organizations. Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is also associated with reporting implementation difficulties through the Traffic Police Department. [Data: Entities (4953, 1180, 5191, 1173, 4956); Relationships (4058, 4065, 4077, 10524, 10525)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Licensing and traffic-law testing are core technical and administrative capabilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department develops the theoretical question set used to test knowledge of road traffic law and is responsible for consistent guidance at designated testing locations. The records also describe its director as authorized under the cited provision to impose fines up to 75,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (1216, 2875, 2888); Relationships (4169)]

A simulation-based legal-knowledge test assesses traffic-situation handling through computer simulations. The described test has 10 questions, lasts no more than 10 minutes, and requires at least 35 points out of 50 to pass. [Data: Entities (4651, 4650); Relationships (2926, 10427)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Digital channels support applications and driving-licence point updates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The National Identification Application is identified as an online channel for submitting dossiers to the Traffic Police Department. It also displays restored driving-licence point status in an electronic identification account when the licence is represented as a data message. [Data: Entities (5680); Relationships (4182, 9961)]

The records describe additional electronic channels for communicating restoration status: the Department’s electronic information page, citizens’ registered Public Service Portal accounts, and a mobile traffic application. The restoration procedure is tied to the conditions described under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (1216, 4189, 5679, 1214); Relationships (4177, 4162, 9960)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network has broad public-administration importance, with limited evidence about reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community links a national ministry, its Traffic Police Department, local police agencies, regulatory instruments, testing functions, and public-facing digital services. Taken together, these documented roles indicate importance to traffic administration and road-safety procedures across multiple levels of government. [Data: Entities (683, 1216, 4952, 1177, 5680); Relationships (2922, 2927, 4063, 4182)]

The supplied records describe official mandates, procedures, and channels; they do not provide substantiated claims about misconduct, public reputation, or operational outcomes. Accordingly, the assessment reflects institutional scope and potential public impact, not a finding of wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (1216, 683, 4952); Relationships (2922, 2927)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 and Vietnam Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: The community is organized around Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, a broad administrative framework for road-traffic order and safety. It connects traffic violations and sanctions—including fines, licence-point measures, and corrective actions—to enforcement authorities such as four police forces, People’s Public Security officials, People’s Committees, and specialized inspectors. The records establish substantial legal and administrative significance, including selected fine limits and violation-specific penalties, but do not document actual enforcement outcomes, compliance rates, misconduct, reputation, or technical capabilities. [Data: Reports (2-853, 2-859, 2-860, 2-861); Entities (3235, 1204, 1179, 5662); Relationships (4127, 4073, 4143, 9196)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the decree’s broad effect on road-traffic regulation and its allocation of sanctioning powers across multiple public authorities, not evidence of adverse conduct or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 168/2024 is the community’s central legal framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree provides administrative penalties for road-traffic order and safety violations and covers drivers, vehicle owners, and other responsible parties. Its provisions address a wide range of vehicle types and matters including driver eligibility, vehicle condition, inspection, training, testing, and environmental violations. [Data: Entities (3235); Reports (2-853)]

The surrounding records link the decree to specific articles, violation categories, penalty provisions, and authorities. This makes it the central organizing entity in the community, while the available material describes the law’s scope rather than how often or consistently it is enforced. [Data: Relationships (4127, 4073, 9189, 9188, 9196); Reports (2-853)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Multiple police forces have specified traffic-penalty authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 41, Clause 3 is described as authorizing the Mobile Police, rapid-response police, Order Police, and police responsible for administrative management of social order to penalize specified road-traffic violations within their assigned functions and duties. The records connect all four forces to the same statutory provision. [Data: Entities (1204, 1208, 1210, 1209, 5662); Relationships (4127, 4143, 4152, 4148)]

The described authority is limited to specified violations and assigned remits; the data does not support treating it as authority over every traffic violation. Article 11, Clauses 1 and 2 are identified as defining relevant violations, but their substantive text is not supplied here. [Data: Reports (2-859); Relationships (10704, 8140, 8144)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe fine-setting powers for several police roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Mobile Police entry states that a commander may impose fines up to 75,000,000 đồng and that a head of a battalion-level Mobile Police unit may impose fines up to 22,500,000 đồng. The supplied material also identifies a station chief, team leader, and head of a police post as having authority to impose fines up to 22,500,000 đồng under Article 43, Clause 3. [Data: Entities (1204, 4957, 5164, 5167, 5675); Relationships (4127, 9175, 9177, 9180, 9195)]

These are described statutory limits, not evidence that any official imposed a fine. The records do not provide comparable limits for all the listed police forces or a complete account of the circumstances and procedures governing each role’s authority. [Data: Reports (2-859, 2-860); Entities (1204, 1179, 4957)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctions cover fines, licence points, and corrective or restrictive measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is described as providing fines, driving-licence point deductions and restoration procedures, and other sanctions and remedial measures. Examples include a stated fine of 8,000,000–10,000,000 đồng for driving while prohibited substances are present, and corrective replacement of specified non-compliant equipment with equipment meeting technical safety standards. [Data: Entities (3235, 1677, 4136); Relationships (6498, 9165); Reports (2-853)]

Other provisions address temporary deprivation of licence or professional-practice-certificate use, and the records state that continuing covered activities during that period is treated as conducting them without the required licence or certificate. These are descriptions of legal consequences, not records of particular cases. [Data: Entities (1079); Relationships (3891); Reports (2-853)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework allocates authority beyond the police
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify Article 42 as concerning penalty-imposing authority of chairpersons of People’s Committees at different administrative levels, and Article 44 as addressing specialized inspectors and certain construction-related officials. They also describe an inspection-team head’s authority to temporarily revoke permit-use rights or suspend operations. [Data: Entities (5676, 5668, 5165, 686); Relationships (9196, 9193, 9178, 2937); Reports (2-853)]

The decree’s described institutional reach therefore includes multiple public bodies and official roles. The supplied records are selective, however, and do not establish a complete organizational chart or comprehensive account of every authority involved. [Data: Entities (3235, 5676, 5668); Reports (2-853, 2-860)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Violation-specific provisions illustrate financial and operational consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a vehicle-owner violation linked to Article 32, Clause 9, with stated fines of 4–6 million đồng for individuals and 8–12 million đồng for organizations. The data identifies the conduct as a category involving an owner assigning or allowing another person to drive in breach of cited provisions; it does not identify an actual offender or incident. [Data: Entities (5533, 5660, 5666); Relationships (10683, 10684, 10685); Reports (2-861)]

Other examples include a 400,000–600,000 đồng fine for operating a motorcycle or similar vehicle without an effective or standards-compliant braking system, and a 10,000,000–15,000,000 đồng fine for noncompliant testing or certification. These examples demonstrate varied statutory exposure, but do not establish the frequency or practical impact of such violations. [Data: Entities (3353, 3266); Relationships (9162, 9160); Reports (2-853)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has high public-administrative importance, but evidence of outcomes is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree’s broad subject matter and the participation of police, People’s Committees, and specialized officials support a high assessment of its potential importance to public administration and road-traffic regulation. The community also links national public-security roles to sanctioning authority and provincial-level police to specified remedial measures. [Data: Entities (3235, 1179, 2388, 5676); Relationships (4073, 7605, 9196); Reports (2-853, 2-860)]

The records do not document actual enforcement incidents, compliance rates, legal challenges, misconduct allegations, or public-reputation assessments. They also provide no information about technical systems or equipment used by the forces, so neither operational effectiveness nor technical capability can be assessed from this material. [Data: Reports (2-859, 2-860, 2-853); Entities (1204, 1179, 1208, 1210, 1209)]

v.tieu_de: Clause 8 Article 21 Goods-Transport Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Clause 8 of Article 21 and a fine of 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The clause is linked to violations involving goods-transport vehicle safety and unsafe cargo securement, while the same fine range is linked to transporting a container with its roof cut off contrary to regulations. The records describe specified transport-related penalties but do not establish how often violations occur or whether any particular party has committed them.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it links a defined monetary penalty to multiple goods-transport safety violations, although the records provide no evidence about enforcement frequency or actual incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 8 is the central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 8 of Article 21 is described as prescribing penalties for specified violations involving goods-transport vehicles, including failure to secure cargo safely when required. Its recorded relationships connect it to the fine, cargo securement, and goods-vehicle traffic-order violations. [Data: Entities (986); Relationships (3547, 3548, 3549)]

This makes the clause the community's principal link between the penalty amount and the described conduct. The records do not provide additional details about the clause's broader legal context or its enforcement. [Data: Entities (986); Relationships (3547, 3548, 3549)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The monetary penalty is explicitly identified as 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and is associated with Clause 8 of Article 21. [Data: Entities (2230, 986); Relationships (3547)]

The same fine range is also associated with the violation involving transport of a container whose roof has been cut off contrary to regulations. [Data: Entities (2230, 2544); Relationships (7276)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unsafe cargo securement is a specifically identified violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe an unsafe cargo securement violation as transporting cargo that must be secured without doing so, or securing it in a way that fails safety requirements. [Data: Entities (5262)]

Clause 8 is recorded as prescribing a fine for this conduct, and the entity description gives the range as 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (986, 5262, 2230); Relationships (3549)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transporting a container with its roof cut off is linked to the fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate described violation concerns carrying a container on a vehicle, including a semi-trailer, after its roof has been cut off contrary to regulations. [Data: Entities (2544)]

The relationship data links this violation to the 8,000,000-to-12,000,000 Vietnamese đồng fine. The supplied records do not specify further circumstances or establish that any particular transport operator engaged in this conduct. [Data: Entities (2544, 2230); Relationships (7276)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns road traffic order and safety for goods vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One entity describes a road traffic order and safety violation by a truck, tractor, or similar vehicle used to transport goods. [Data: Entities (4402)]

Clause 8 is linked to penalties for certain violations by vehicles transporting goods. This establishes a connection between the clause and goods-vehicle traffic requirements, but the records do not enumerate all covered violations or describe actual safety outcomes. [Data: Entities (986, 4402); Relationships (3548)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Safety Decree 151 and Transport Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, which governs multiple aspects of road traffic order and safety in Vietnam, and connects it to the Ministry of Transport, the Vietnam Road Administration, related agencies, public-service processes, and road-traffic databases. Its scope includes vehicle-monitoring data and its sharing, speed and priority-vehicle rules, approval procedures for certain foreign-vehicle activities, and traffic-safety education. Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT complements the framework with operating-speed and safe-distance requirements. The records describe regulatory responsibilities and systems, but do not establish whether any entity is compliant or noncompliant in practice.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is high because the community describes nationwide rules, administrative powers, and interconnected vehicle and traffic-safety data systems, although the records identify no specific breach or adverse incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 151 is the community’s central regulatory instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is the main connecting entity: it governs vehicle-related activities and administrative procedures in Vietnam and is linked to government agencies, databases, public-service channels, education, and foreign-vehicle activities. This broad reach makes the decree important to road-safety administration and regulated transport activity across the country. [Data: Entities (3234, 5613); Relationships (9158, 4193, 2935, 4109, 4164)]

The decree also addresses amendments and repeals specified phrases and provisions of Decree No. 10/2020/NĐ-CP. The supplied information describes the legal framework and responsibilities, not evidence of implementation outcomes or compliance by particular parties. [Data: Entities (3234)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport authorities have defined management and enforcement roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Transport builds and manages the vehicle-inspection database, assigns expressways to designated agencies, and is identified as a recipient of vehicle-monitoring data. The Vietnam Road Administration manages assigned road infrastructure, determines speed-limit sign placement on expressways under its management, and also receives monitoring data. [Data: Entities (1221, 685); Relationships (2933, 2932, 4190, 4193, 2935)]

The decree identifies the Director of the Vietnam Road Administration and Regional Road Management Zone directors among officials with sanctioning authority. It also provides for the Administration’s Director to establish an inspection team. These powers indicate an administrative enforcement structure, but the records do not report any particular inspection, sanction, or enforcement outcome. [Data: Entities (1220, 2390, 5669, 5166); Relationships (4187, 4196, 4189, 4191)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety databases and monitoring data form a connected information system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road traffic order and safety database receives information from multiple sources, including vehicle-inspection, driver-licensing, and driver-time-management databases. The decree describes information included in the database, such as vehicle-owner and compulsory civil-liability insurance details. [Data: Entities (1197, 1199, 1196, 1195); Relationships (4108, 4106, 4105, 4107)]

Separately, the decree provides for vehicle journey-monitoring data to be received by the Ministry of Transport and Vietnam Road Administration and shared with provincial and centrally governed city Departments of Transport and other relevant authorities in accordance with law. This establishes significant data-handling and sharing responsibilities; the records do not specify security controls, retention periods, or any incident involving the data. [Data: Entities (3234, 685, 1221, 4846, 1174); Relationships (2935, 4193, 9156, 4059)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circular 38 sets operating-speed and safe-distance requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT covers road design speeds and the operating speeds and safe distances of motor vehicles and specialized motorcycles. It states principles for complying with those requirements and sets a maximum speed of 40 km/h for specialized motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles on roads other than expressways. [Data: Entities (4954, 4714); Relationships (2936, 10446)]

The circular excludes priority vehicles performing duties under law from its stated scope. It also provides that, when a referenced normative document is amended, supplemented, or replaced, the corresponding updated document applies. These provisions describe the applicable rule structure, rather than observed driving behavior or compliance. [Data: Entities (4954)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Special procedures apply to specified foreign-vehicle activities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151 addresses approval and dossier requirements for tourism trips in which foreigners bring foreign motor vehicles into Vietnam. It identifies Vietnamese international travel-service businesses as applicants or organizers in this process and the National Public Service Portal as an online submission route for dossiers. [Data: Entities (1722, 1435, 1215, 3234); Relationships (6581, 5942, 5941, 4164)]

The decree also covers participation in Vietnamese traffic using a right-hand-drive car for a purpose other than tourism, with approval and dossier requirements. The provided records establish that these activities are regulated, but do not indicate whether any application was submitted, approved, denied, or found noncompliant. [Data: Entities (4921, 3234); Relationships (9157, 10516)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education is included in the regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree provides for education about road traffic law and safety in educational institutions. For lower secondary school students, the specified content includes traffic-law knowledge and the safe operation of bicycles and electric bicycles. [Data: Entities (3234, 1200, 2498); Relationships (4113, 4112, 7751)]

This connects the decree’s administrative and vehicle-related provisions with a preventive educational component. The records identify the required subject matter and audience, but do not provide information about curriculum delivery, participation, or educational outcomes. [Data: Entities (3234, 1200, 2498); Relationships (4112, 7751)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signals and permits are governed by specific rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Decree 151 sets technical requirements for signal-emitting devices on priority vehicles, including flashing blue lights for specified duties such as disaster response and recovery. It also specifies documentation for new or replacement permits and provides for permit revocation in stated circumstances, including conversion of a vehicle to another use or liquidation. [Data: Entities (3234, 1395); Relationships (5881)]

These provisions establish controls over signal-device use and associated permits. The records do not identify individual permit holders, particular revocations, or misuse of such devices. [Data: Entities (3234)]

v.tieu_de: Priority-Vehicle Permits and Emergency Response
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the issuance and reissuance of permits for priority-vehicle signal devices, linked to the authority that processes applications and to rules for installing and using the equipment. Its stated scope spans epidemic response, rescue and relief, disaster response, ambulance emergency duty, and dike protection. Article 27 of Law 36/2024/QH15 identifies several such missions as entitled to priority, while Article 18 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP addresses equipment installation and use. The information describes a regulatory and operational framework, but does not establish compliance outcomes, actual deployment, or misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety importance because it connects permit administration and priority-vehicle signalling with multiple emergency and disaster-response duties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit issuance is the administrative hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s most connected entity is the process for issuing or reissuing priority-vehicle signal-device permits. It covers applications for new or replacement permits, and the competent permit-issuing authority is described as processing applications and issuing the relevant documents [Data: Entities (2755, 1056); Relationships (3822)].

The process is linked to multiple qualifying missions, including epidemic response, rescue and relief, disaster response, ambulance emergency duty, and dyke protection. This makes permit administration a central point connecting emergency assignments with authorization to use signal devices [Data: Relationships (6761, 8090, 5880, 523, 6585)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework links legal priority to specified missions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 27 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is described as a provision on priority vehicles, with Clause 2 specifying which vehicles may proceed first at an intersection. The listed relationships connect that provision to epidemic response, rescue and relief, disaster response, and dike-protection missions [Data: Entities (345); Relationships (1409, 1411, 1407, 1406)].

The supplied information therefore presents priority as tied to defined duties rather than as a general attribute of all vehicles. It does not provide further detail about enforcement, eligibility decisions, or how the provision is applied in individual cases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Equipment installation and use are separately addressed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Installation and use of priority-vehicle signal equipment is identified as an activity addressed by Article 18 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. The description identifies flashing blue lights as an example of the signalling equipment available to qualifying priority vehicles [Data: Entities (2699, 1835)].

Relationships connect equipment use with epidemic response, natural-disaster response, rescue and relief duty, and dike-protection duty. This indicates that the framework covers both permit administration and the operational use of signal equipment for specified missions [Data: Relationships (6760, 8004, 8005, 5817)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Epidemic response is a prominent qualifying use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Epidemic response is described as work addressing epidemics, outbreaks, and related incidents. Vehicles assigned to this work may be designated as priority vehicles and eligible to use priority-vehicle signalling equipment, including flashing blue lights [Data: Entities (1835)].

The network connects epidemic response both to the permit process and to equipment installation and use; it also links epidemic response to the broader category of rescue and disaster or epidemic response. An epidemic is separately identified as an incident associated with this response work [Data: Relationships (6761, 6760, 6763, 6758)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Rescue and disaster-related duties form a broad operational category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Rescue and relief operations are described as emergency duties involving rescue, relief, and incident remediation, and are identified as qualifying uses of priority-vehicle signal devices. The description notes that these duties may be performed by vehicles generally, including military vehicles [Data: Entities (4171)].

The community also groups rescue, natural-disaster response, epidemic response, and incident remediation under a broader category of response duties. These links connect the broad category to rescue and relief duty, natural-disaster response, and remediation of incidents arising from disasters or epidemics [Data: Entities (4164, 3222, 2633); Relationships (9941, 9142, 7875)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional listed missions include ambulance and dike-protection duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Ambulance emergency duty is explicitly linked to the permit process as a qualifying case. Dike-protection duty is likewise linked to permit issuance and to installation and use of priority-vehicle signal equipment [Data: Entities (167, 1355); Relationships (523, 6585, 5817)].

The records also include separate labels for dyke-protection duty and dike-protection mission, both connected to the permit or statutory-priority framework. These entries show that the stated scope extends beyond epidemic, rescue, and disaster response to other specified emergency or protective assignments [Data: Entities (1724, 1357); Relationships (1406)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes authorization, not demonstrated compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe permit requirements, an authority responsible for processing applications, and categories of duties eligible for priority-vehicle signalling. They do not provide case-level permit decisions, inspection results, or evidence that a particular vehicle or organization complied with the framework [Data: Entities (2755, 1056, 2699); Relationships (3822)].

No reputation assessments or allegations are included in the supplied records. Accordingly, the community can be characterized as a public-safety and administrative framework, but its real-world compliance performance and reputational standing cannot be assessed from this information.

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Police Authorities and Fines up to 75 Million đồng
v.tom_tat: This community centers on an administrative fine of up to 75,000,000 đồng and the officials described as authorized to impose it under clause 7 of Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The identified officials are the directors of the Traffic Police Department and the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order, and the commander of the Mobile Police. The administrative-management department is also linked to its director. The records describe legal authority, not actual enforcement cases or findings of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (3733, 1217, 5187, 1218, 1219); Relationships (4183, 4185, 4186, 9623)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has meaningful institutional impact because it concerns senior police officials authorized to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng, although the records do not establish how often that authority is used.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A substantial administrative fine is the community’s central subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is an administrative penalty action allowing specified officials to impose a fine of up to 75,000,000 đồng. This amount indicates a potentially significant enforcement consequence, but the records do not identify the conduct to which the fine applies or show that any fine was actually imposed. [Data: Entities (3733)]

The relationships connect this fine authority to the directors of the Traffic Police Department and the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order, as well as the Mobile Police commander. [Data: Relationships (4185, 4186, 9623)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three senior police roles are described as authorized to impose the fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records identify the director of the Traffic Police Department, the director of the Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order, and the commander of the Mobile Police as officials authorized to impose fines up to the stated ceiling. [Data: Entities (5187, 1218, 1219); Relationships (4185, 4186, 9623)]

This indicates that the described authority is associated with multiple police roles rather than a single official. The records do not specify delegation arrangements, the circumstances in which each role may act, or the procedures for imposing a penalty.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The administrative-management department is linked to its director
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Police Department for Administrative Management of Social Order is identified as the organization whose director is among the officials authorized to impose the fine. A separate relationship states that the named Cục trưởng is the director of that department. [Data: Entities (1217, 1219); Relationships (4183, 4186)]

Together, these records connect an organizational entity, its director, and the fine authority. They do not describe the department’s broader responsibilities or any specific enforcement activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Traffic Police Department director is connected directly to the fine authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The director of the Traffic Police Department is described as authorized under clause 7 of Article 43 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP to impose fines of up to 75,000,000 đồng. [Data: Entities (1218); Relationships (4185)]

The evidence supports this stated authorization and maximum amount only. It does not provide details about applicable violations, decision-making conditions, or the use of this authority in particular cases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish stated authority, not evidence of compliance or enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions characterize the fine as an administrative penalty action and identify officials authorized to impose it under a cited provision. They do not report actual penalty decisions, enforcement frequency, appeals, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (3733, 5187, 1218, 1219); Relationships (4185, 4186, 9623)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant as a description of formal enforcement capacity, but these records alone do not support conclusions about misconduct, improper use of authority, or the practical impact of enforcement.

v.tieu_de: Decree 236/2026 and Priority-Vehicle Permits
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnamese Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP, which amends provisions concerning road-traffic administration, including the nationwide road traffic order and safety database and the allocation of authority over permits for priority-vehicle warning-signal equipment. Provincial and centrally governed municipal Traffic Police Divisions issue, reissue, and revoke permits for eligible vehicles belonging to agencies and organizations, subject to stated exceptions. Emergency-duty military vehicles are excluded from those permit procedures. The available records describe the legal framework and institutional relationships, but do not establish how the rules are implemented or whether entities comply with them.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial administrative importance because the decree addresses nationwide traffic-safety administration and assigns permit responsibilities, although the evidence concerns a specific regulatory area rather than demonstrated operational outcomes [Data: Entities (3236); Relationships (9198, 8646, 9199)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Decree 236/2026/NĐ-CP is the community's central legal instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is described as amending Vietnamese road-traffic administration provisions. Article 1 concerns the nationwide road traffic order and safety database, while Article 10 revises provisions on authorities responsible for permits for priority-vehicle warning-signal equipment [Data: Entities (3236)].

The relationships in the dataset specifically connect the decree to the Article 23 amendment and the assignment of permit responsibilities. The records establish the stated scope of the amendments, but do not provide evidence about their implementation or effects [Data: Relationships (9198, 9199)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial and municipal Traffic Police Divisions hold the described permit duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree assigns Traffic Police Divisions of provincial and centrally governed municipal police responsibility for issuing, reissuing, and revoking permits for eligible priority vehicles. This makes those divisions the principal administrative actors in the permit relationships represented here [Data: Entities (3728); Relationships (9198)].

The divisions are identified as part of the corresponding provincial and municipal police forces, linking the operational permit role to those broader police bodies [Data: Entities (1181); Relationships (4079)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit responsibilities apply to eligible agency and organization vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Agencies and organizations are identified as holders of eligible priority vehicles subject to the Traffic Police Divisions’ permit responsibilities. The described duties include issuing, reissuing, and revoking permits, with exceptions stated in the decree’s provisions [Data: Entities (1194, 3728); Relationships (4104, 9198)].

The available information does not enumerate all eligibility criteria or describe particular agencies, organizations, or vehicles. The scope should therefore be understood as the categories stated in the records, not as a complete account of every permit case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency-duty military vehicles are excluded from these permit procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Military forces are connected to the decree through an exclusion for vehicles performing emergency duties. The provincial and municipal Traffic Police Divisions’ described permit responsibilities do not cover those vehicles under the cited provisions [Data: Entities (2944, 3728); Relationships (8646, 8647)].

This is a specific exception in the described permit framework; the records do not provide further detail about military vehicle authorization or other possible procedures.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The amendment and institutional relationships define the community’s structure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The decree is linked to the amendment of Article 23, which revises Clauses 1 and 2 concerning the authorities responsible for permits for priority-vehicle signal equipment. That amendment supplies the legal connection between the central instrument and the administrative duties assigned to provincial and municipal Traffic Police Divisions [Data: Entities (4849); Relationships (9199, 9198)].

Overall, the recorded structure runs from the decree and its amendment to the police divisions, with agencies and organizations as the covered vehicle holders and emergency-duty military vehicles as an exception. The records describe legal responsibilities, not evidence of compliance, enforcement performance, technical capability beyond the database provision, or public reputation [Data: Relationships (9198, 8646, 8647, 4104)].

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Department of Transport Inspectorate and Enforcement Authority
v.tom_tat: This community describes an administrative enforcement structure centered on the Department of Transport Inspectorate, which is part of the Department of Transport. Inspectorate officials may prepare records for specified road-traffic order and safety violations within the inspectorate’s management area. Where the inspectorate has not been established, the chief inspector of a province or centrally governed city has a stated fine-imposing authority of up to 52,500,000 đồng, subject to the provision’s conditions. The records describe legal roles and powers, not specific enforcement actions or allegations of misconduct. [Data: Entities (4923, 826, 1182, 5531, 5189, +more); Relationships (3216, 4080, 10492, 3217, 4081)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high administrative significance because it describes officials’ authority to document road-traffic violations and a chief inspector’s conditional power to impose substantial fines, but it provides no evidence of particular enforcement events or misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Inspectorate is the community’s organizational center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Department of Transport Inspectorate is described as a department-level body responsible for inspection and oversight within its area of management. The Department of Transport is identified as its parent department, making the Inspectorate the central organizational link in this community. [Data: Entities (4923, 4845); Relationships (10492)]

The description notes that the Inspectorate may not have been established in some cases. The data therefore presents its existence as conditional, rather than asserting that an Inspectorate operates in every jurisdiction covered. [Data: Entities (4923); Relationships (3216)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspectorate officials may document specified traffic violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Officials of the Department of Transport Inspectorate are authorized, while performing official duties, to prepare records of violations within the Inspectorate’s management area. This is a stated documentation authority; the data does not say that these officials impose fines themselves. [Data: Entities (1182, 4923); Relationships (4080)]

The specified category is administrative violations involving road-traffic order and safety. The authority is bounded by the Inspectorate’s management area, and the records do not identify particular violations, individuals, or enforcement incidents. [Data: Entities (5531, 1182); Relationships (4081)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Chief inspectors have a conditional fine-imposing role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The chief inspector of a province or centrally governed city is described as able to impose fines of up to 52,500,000 đồng under stated conditions. The relationship data specifies one relevant condition: this authority applies in cases where the Department of Transport Inspectorate has not been established. [Data: Entities (826, 5189, 4923); Relationships (3216, 3217)]

This role is distinct from the authority assigned to Inspectorate officials to prepare violation records. The supplied information does not set out all conditions attached to the fine limit, so the amount should be understood as a stated maximum under conditions, not as a routine or automatic penalty. [Data: Entities (826, 1182); Relationships (3216, 4081)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework is tied to provincial and centrally governed city jurisdictions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes provincial and centrally governed city jurisdictions as the administrative settings for the chief inspector’s office. The relationship records connect the chief inspector to those jurisdictions and separately connect the office’s conditional authority to the possible absence of a Department of Transport Inspectorate. [Data: Entities (5189, 826, 4923); Relationships (3217, 3216)]

The information supports a jurisdictional description of the roles, but does not identify specific provinces or cities, or establish how frequently the Inspectorate is absent. [Data: Entities (5189, 4923); Relationships (3216, 3217)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes statutory capacity, not actual conduct or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records characterize institutional responsibilities and legal powers: oversight, preparation of violation records, and a conditional fine-imposing authority. They do not document individual enforcement decisions, outcomes, compliance rates, technical systems, or alleged wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (4923, 826, 1182, 5531); Relationships (3216, 4081)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is administrative and regulatory. The available information supports assessing the potential importance of these roles, but not drawing conclusions about their practical use, effectiveness, or reputation. [Data: Entities (4923, 826, 1182); Relationships (4080, 3216, 4081)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Safety and Student-Transport Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety and related provisions on driving-time limits, rest periods, and student-transport vehicle managers. Article 64, Clause 1 is associated with the driving-time limit and rest-period rules, while Article 20, Clause 6 is linked to penalties for exceeding driving time and failing to take required rest. The law also sets the manager requirement for certain vehicles transporting preschool and primary-school students. The records describe regulatory requirements and violation categories, not evidence that any specific violation occurred. [Data: Entities (2940, 2801, 2805, 3335, 5659, +more); Relationships (8142, 8151, 8642, 8150, 8141, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns road-safety rules, penalties, and safeguards for student transport, although the records do not establish actual violations or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The road-safety law is the community’s central framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vietnam’s Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety is the primary legal framework represented here. Its stated scope includes operating speed and safe distance, driving time and rest periods, and the required number of managers on vehicles transporting preschool and primary-school students. [Data: Entities (2940)]

The relationships connect this law to both the driving-time provisions and the student-transport manager requirement, making it the principal link among the regulatory topics in the community. [Data: Relationships (8142, 8642)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 64, Clause 1 supplies a driving-time limit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 1 of Article 64 is identified as the source of the prescribed driving-time limit. The violation category “driving beyond the prescribed time” is directly associated with that provision. [Data: Entities (2801, 2942); Relationships (8143)]

This establishes a regulatory connection between a defined limit and a corresponding violation category; the records do not specify the limit’s duration or describe a particular driver or incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Required rest between consecutive driving periods is addressed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a violation category for failing to observe the required rest period between two consecutive periods of driving. Article 64, Clause 1 is associated with rules on driving time and rest periods, and Article 20, Clause 6 is linked to a fine for this rest-period violation. [Data: Entities (2801, 2809, 2805); Relationships (8141, 8149)]

The available records establish the existence of the requirement and its connection to a penalty provision, but do not state the required rest duration or document any actual breach.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20, Clause 6 is linked to penalties for driving-time violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 6 of Article 20 is described as prescribing fines of 3,000,000 to 5,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations. The relationship records associate it with both driving beyond the prescribed time and failure to observe required rest periods. [Data: Entities (2805); Relationships (8150, 8149)]

Article 20 is described as covering administrative penalties and driver’s-license points for automobile drivers and similar vehicles. The data supports a penalty framework, but does not indicate whether a penalty was imposed in a specific case. [Data: Entities (5659); Relationships (8151)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student-transport vehicles have a manager requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The law’s Clause 3 of Article 46 is identified as requiring a specified number of managers on vehicles transporting preschool and primary-school students. The associated violation category covers commercial student-transport vehicles, including vehicles combining transport with student pick-up and drop-off, operating without the required manager or with too few managers. [Data: Entities (2940, 3335); Relationships (8642)]

This requirement is a distinct child-safety component of the community’s regulatory scope. The records describe the rule and violation category, not an identified operator or an actual instance of noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules and violation categories, not demonstrated misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities identify legal provisions, penalty rules, and types of conduct that constitute violations. None of the supplied records names a person or organization as having committed one of those violations, or describes an enforcement action or road-safety incident. [Data: Entities (2940, 2801, 2805, 3335, 5659); Relationships (8142, 8150, 8642)]

Accordingly, the community is significant as a compliance and safety framework, but the supplied evidence does not support treating any violation as having actually occurred.

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Driving-License Point Restoration Tests
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s driving-license point-restoration process and the theoretical and simulated legal-knowledge tests used within it. Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA specifies requirements for the class B theory test, while point restoration for automobile licences generally requires passing both the theory and simulated tests. The network also describes separate test criteria for category A or B1 licences, retake and result-retention rules, and the Ministry of Public Security’s role in approving simulated scenarios. These entities are connected to driver legal-compliance management and motor vehicle licensing.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderately high because the community describes a formal, safety-related licensing and compliance system that governs test requirements and restoration of driving privileges.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point restoration is a structured compliance process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driving-license point restoration is presented as part of driver legal-compliance management. The process addresses drivers whose licence points have been fully deducted, with requirements that vary by licence category. [Data: Entities (1715, 1455, 2373); Relationships (6039, 6565)]

For automobile licences, the supplied description requires passing both the theoretical legal-knowledge test and the simulated legal-knowledge test. The theoretical test is a prerequisite for proceeding to the simulated test. [Data: Entities (1715, 2889, 4648); Relationships (6566, 6569, 8565)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA sets class B theory-test criteria
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is described as a Vietnamese circular dated 12 November 2024 regulating legal-knowledge examinations for drivers seeking point restoration.
