Article 6, clause 3 specifies the class B theory test’s duration, structure, and passing criteria. [Data: Entities (4955, 511); Relationships (8567, 2410, 2411)]

For the class B test, the described format is 20 minutes and 30 multiple-choice questions, including one disqualifying question. A score of at least 27 is required, and an incorrect answer to the disqualifying question results in failure. [Data: Entities (2889, 4955)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Theoretical test requirements differ by licence category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes a separate theoretical legal-knowledge test for holders of category A or B1 licences. Its stated format is 19 minutes and 25 multiple-choice questions, including one critical question; the passing threshold is 23, and an incorrect answer to the critical question results in failure. [Data: Entities (4934, 1706); Relationships (6534)]

The class B criteria in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA are different: 20 minutes, 30 questions, and a passing score of at least 27, with a disqualifying question. The records therefore indicate category-specific test specifications rather than one uniform format. [Data: Entities (2889, 4934, 4955)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The simulated test is a distinct required stage for automobile restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The simulated legal-knowledge test assesses road-traffic rules, order, and safety through computer-based traffic situations. For automobile-license point restoration, it is required in addition to passing the theory test. [Data: Entities (4648, 4647, 4649, 1715); Relationships (6569, 10425)]

The Ministry of Public Security is identified as the authority that approves and issues the simulated traffic scenarios used in the test. The records establish this role but do not provide further detail about how scenarios are developed or administered. [Data: Entities (3021); Relationships (8896)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Test sequence gates access to the simulated examination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A participant who fails the theoretical test may not proceed to the simulated test; passing the theory test allows the participant to take the next stage. This makes the theory result a procedural gate in the automobile restoration pathway. [Data: Relationships (8565, 6982); Entities (2889, 4648, 2008)]

The data also states that a passing theoretical result is retained for one year if the participant fails the simulated test. This rule preserves the theory result during that period rather than requiring the participant to repeat that test immediately. [Data: Entities (4937); Relationships (8566, 10426)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Retake rules provide a defined route after failure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Participants who fail an examination may register to retake it after seven working days from the end of the previous examination. The retake rule is linked to both the theoretical and simulated tests. [Data: Entities (4198); Relationships (8564, 9970, 6981)]

Failure of the theory test also prevents access to the simulated test, so the retake opportunity applies within a sequenced process rather than allowing candidates to bypass the theory requirement. [Data: Relationships (8565, 6982, 8564)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process serves both restoration and driver licensing
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The theoretical legal-knowledge test is described as supporting motor vehicle driver licensing and licence issuance, as well as being used in point-restoration circumstances. The question set is associated with the licensing examination process. [Data: Entities (4934, 3102); Relationships (9022)]

This connection places the test community within both the restoration framework and the broader examination system for drivers. The supplied records do not quantify how many drivers take the tests or how often points are restored. [Data: Entities (1715, 4934, 3102); Relationships (6566, 9022)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A named amendment action concerns Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA materials
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies an action named “THAY THẾ CỤM TỪ, BÃI BỎ PHỤ LỤC VÀ BIỂU MẪU,” described as replacing wording and repealing appendices and forms in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. [Data: Entities (4924, 4955); Relationships (10518)]

The records do not specify the full wording of the changes or their operational effect on the test criteria, so no further conclusion about those effects is supported here.

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Driving-Licence Points and Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community concerns driver’s-licence point deductions, restoration procedures, and penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its central process links a knowledge examination and a 12-month condition to restoration of points, with examination results synchronized to an administrative-violations database and restoration notifications sent to drivers. A related enforcement branch covers vehicle-condition violations under Article 13 and specified fines under Article 6.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high importance because it connects traffic penalties and licence-point restoration to examination, administrative data synchronization, and driver notification processes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Point restoration is the community’s central process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The restoration procedure is the main hub linking the examination, point deductions, the driver receiving restored points, and the administrative database. The described outcome is restoration of the licence to 12 points, followed by automatic updating [Data: Entities (3734, 2810, 5168, 1198, 3245); Relationships (8155, 9624, 4110, 9205, 6800)].

The procedure’s stated conditions include that the driver has not lost all points and has had no further deduction during the 12 months following the most recent deduction. The description also requires passing the knowledge examination [Data: Entities (3734); Relationships (9624, 8155)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination is tied to point restoration, with distinct triggers described
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic-law knowledge examination is identified as a prerequisite for point restoration, and passing it is described as necessary to restore points to 12 [Data: Entities (2810, 3734); Relationships (8155)].

The records also say that having all licence points deducted triggers a requirement to take and pass the examination. Separately, the restoration-procedure description says the driver must not have had all points deducted. These descriptions present distinct conditions; the supplied information does not explain how they are reconciled [Data: Entities (2372, 2810, 3734); Relationships (7576, 8155)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Examination results are synchronized with administrative records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After a driver passes the examination, the result is entered into examination software and synchronized with the administrative-violation handling database for road-traffic order and safety. The data links this synchronization process to the restoration procedure and automatic updating of licence points [Data: Entities (1861, 1198, 3734); Relationships (6799, 6800)].

This establishes a described technical capability for recording examination outcomes and exchanging related administrative data. The supplied records do not specify the software’s architecture, security controls, or operational performance [Data: Entities (1861, 1198); Relationships (6799, 6800)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restoration notifications are automated
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The administrative-violations database is described as automatically sending information to a person after their licence points have been restored. A separate notification entity represents the notice of restoration, and the relationships identify the driver as its recipient [Data: Entities (1198, 4951, 3245); Relationships (4110, 4111, 9206)].

The records establish an automated notification step but do not state the delivery channel, timing beyond the database’s automatic action, or whether the recipient must acknowledge the notice [Data: Entities (1198, 4951); Relationships (4111, 9206)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 13 links vehicle-condition violations to point deductions and penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 13 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as addressing penalties and licence-point deductions for specified vehicle-condition violations. The relationships connect those violations to both point deductions and penalties under Article 13 [Data: Entities (5658, 5535, 5168, 5650); Relationships (10607, 10606, 10687, 10703)].

The records do not enumerate the vehicle-condition violations or specify the associated penalty amounts, so the scope and severity of individual sanctions cannot be assessed from this information alone [Data: Entities (5658, 5535, 5650); Relationships (10607, 10687, 10703)].

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6 includes a specified fine for misuse of a priority signal device
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 4 of Article 6 is described as setting a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the listed violation involving improper or unauthorized use of a priority signal device. The clause is linked to Article 6, the driver subject to the fine, and the fine amount [Data: Entities (2804, 5663, 3732, 3242); Relationships (8148, 8146, 8147)].

Article 6 is also described more broadly as addressing penalties and licence-point deductions for specified road-traffic violations by drivers of cars and similar vehicles. The supplied information does not establish that the particular priority-signal-device fine itself entails a point deduction [Data: Entities (5663, 5168); Relationships (10608, 8148)].

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Law Knowledge Examination Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the road traffic law knowledge examination and the competent authorities responsible for organizing it. The connected process includes applications, scheduling and change notices, examinees and retests, interpreter support, and administrative records. The supplied data describe formal duties and procedures, including advance notice and record-retention requirements, but do not establish whether those requirements are consistently met or identify any violations. [Data: Entities (1066, 4365, 1047, 2749, 4065); Relationships (3867, 3771, 3866, 3861, 3770)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high importance because it organizes a public-facing road-safety legal examination and connects authorities, applicants, accessibility support, and records, while the data identify no specific breach or incident.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Competent authorities are the administrative hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent testing authority is described as responsible for organizing and conducting the examination, handling applications, and ensuring examination facilities and equipment are available. The competent examination authority is also described as administering or overseeing the examination and handling registration, scheduling, and retest requests. [Data: Entities (1066, 1047); Relationships (3867, 3771, 3772, 3766)]

The data use two authority labels with overlapping responsibilities, but do not explicitly state whether they refer to the same institution. Their functions place the authorities at the center of the process, connecting the examination to applicants, registered examinees, notices, and interpreters. [Data: Relationships (3861, 3866, 3875, 3860)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination has a defined registration and retest pathway
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The examination assesses knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. The described procedure allows people to register and permits candidates who do not pass to request or register for a retest, either through the authority that conducted the earlier examination or another competent authority. [Data: Entities (4365, 4539, 692); Relationships (2949, 2950, 6787)]

Registration involves submitting an application or dossier and selecting an authority; the examination-registration description also identifies a valid health certificate from a competent medical facility as a required document. These are stated procedural requirements, not evidence that any particular applicant has met them. [Data: Entities (1047, 1850, 1053); Relationships (3772, 3820, 3819)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Scheduling and change notices are central service obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The authority publicly announces examination schedules, including expected times and locations for the following month. After receiving a complete and valid application, the competent testing authority must notify registered candidates of the examination time and location at least two working days in advance. [Data: Entities (1066, 1047, 1863); Relationships (3860, 3864, 6802)]

If an announced time or location changes, the authority is described as promptly notifying registered examinees, using contact information supplied in their applications, such as email or phone details. The records specify these obligations but do not report actual notice performance or service delays. [Data: Entities (1852, 1862, 4065); Relationships (3859, 3866, 3770, 3765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recordkeeping and examination oversight are specified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent examination authority retains a copy of the examination record and is described as preserving surveillance-camera images for at least two years, along with registration records and examination minutes in paper and electronic form for at least five years. These requirements provide a documented basis for examination administration and later review. [Data: Entities (1047); Relationships (3771)]

At the examination’s conclusion, participants sign or fingerprint the examination record; an interpreter does so as well when applicable. The authority is also described as providing the examinee with a copy of the record. The available data state these procedural controls but do not establish the quality of implementation or the existence of any compliance issue. [Data: Entities (4365, 2749, 1865); Relationships (3767, 6806, 6804)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Interpreter support addresses language-access needs
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An interpreter may be hired by the competent testing authority or the test taker to assist during the examination. The described assistance includes accurately and completely translating questions and explaining or guiding the participant through the testing procedure. [Data: Entities (2749, 1066); Relationships (3861, 6804)]

The community specifically includes foreign examinees and ethnic-minority participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese as groups that may use interpretation. The interpreter and examinee sign or fingerprint the examination record, linking language assistance to the formal examination process. [Data: Entities (2311, 1841, 1842, 2337); Relationships (7411, 6771, 6773, 7511)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Applicants and registered examinees are linked to communication duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records distinguish people applying or registering from registered examinees who will sit for the test. Registered examinees provide contact information in their applications and are entitled to receive examination time-and-location notices through those details or other means provided in the application. [Data: Entities (4065, 4899, 1851, 4063); Relationships (9854, 3865, 6786, 6803)]

This structure makes applicant-provided information part of the scheduling and change-notification process. The data describe the communication channel and recipients, but do not quantify the number of examinees or describe actual notification outcomes. [Data: Entities (4065, 1852, 1862); Relationships (3865, 3859, 6788)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is procedural and public-facing, with limited evidence of adverse events
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe a regulated administrative service for assessing road traffic legal knowledge, rather than a reported incident or allegation. The examination is connected to road traffic order and safety, and authorities have specified responsibilities for organizing it and informing participants. [Data: Entities (4365, 4376, 1066); Relationships (3867, 3872, 3773)]

The supplied records support the importance of the process and its operational requirements, including facilities, equipment, notices, and records. They contain no specific claim of misconduct, legal breach, examination failure, or technical incident; therefore, the community’s significance should not be read as evidence of wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (1066, 1047); Relationships (3771, 3860, 3864)]

v.tieu_de: Competent Authority and Vietnam Road-Traffic Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the COMPETENT AUTHORITY, a generic legal role rather than one specifically named agency. Its relationships span vehicle and permit administration, road-safety examinations and inspections, public notices, and handling of retained documents. Applicants can use specified channels—including postal service and the National Identity Application—for some procedures, while motor-vehicle emissions-certificate violations carry stated fines. The records describe an extensive administrative framework but do not identify a particular authority or establish misconduct by any entity. [Data: Entities (1043, 1753, 3830, 3106, 3206); Relationships (3704, 3730, 3745, 3738, 585)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad importance to road-traffic governance, licensing, examinations, and vehicle compliance, rather than evidence of wrongdoing or a specific threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The competent authority is the central but generic administrative role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The COMPETENT AUTHORITY is described as a public body or government agency designated by the relevant law and subject matter; it does not name one specific agency. Its responsibilities can include vehicle documents, permits, inspections, licences, and other road-traffic functions, so the exact institution depends on the governing provision. [Data: Entities (1043)]

Its network position reflects this breadth: relationships connect it with application procedures, tests, inspections, public notices, and document handling. This indicates regulatory and administrative importance, but the records do not establish that all these functions belong to one real-world organization. [Data: Relationships (3704, 3730, 3711, 3712, 3745, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permits for priority-vehicle signaling devices involve multiple application routes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Agencies and organizations seeking permits submit application dossiers to the competent authority, including for new issuance and reissuance. The data also describes applicant agencies and organizations submitting required supporting documents for permit reissuance. [Data: Entities (195, 143, 4080, 203, 207); Relationships (472, 585, 604, 613, 614)]

For the stated reissuance procedure, postal service and the National Identity Application are identified as submission channels, alongside direct submission to the designated authority. The records establish these procedural options, but do not provide processing outcomes or indicate whether any particular application was approved. [Data: Entities (3830, 3206, 4080); Relationships (9697, 9123, 3730)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Public portals support examination and test transparency
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The ELECTRONIC INFORMATION PORTAL is used to publish proposed examination dates and schedules, including date, time, and location, and provides access to road-traffic order and safety study materials. The competent authority is linked to responsibility for announcements and the portal. [Data: Entities (1753); Relationships (3704, 6636, 6637, 3727)]

The records also describe monthly examination scheduling, with expected times and locations for the following month announced before the 25th of the current month. These mechanisms provide public-facing procedural information; the data does not assess portal availability, security, or actual publication performance. [Data: Entities (3082, 3997, 2869); Relationships (6636, 3728, 3727)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety knowledge examinations and checks are recurring functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent authority is responsible for organizing road-traffic law knowledge tests and publicly announcing their dates. The records state that tests are to be held at least twice per week and that the authority must provide necessary facilities and equipment. [Data: Entities (4368, 3995, 2868); Relationships (3738, 3727, 3710)]

A separate legal-knowledge examination is described as monthly, with registrants able to choose and register for an available date. Assigned officials receive applications and conduct the check, linking administrative staffing to delivery of the examination process. [Data: Entities (2869, 1858, 592, 1856); Relationships (6793, 2732, 3706)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection scheduling and vehicle certification are part of the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent authority is associated with checking and publicly announcing expected inspection schedules and locations. The records describe monthly inspections and a public notice for the following month, with inspection registrants able to select a date. [Data: Entities (3083, 3997, 2692); Relationships (3712, 3728, 9009, 7993)]

Vehicle inspectors are described as certified professionals who inspect vehicles and components, while the competent authority issues the relevant certificate. The information indicates a division between inspection work and certificate issuance, without identifying specific inspectors or agencies. [Data: Entities (5413, 1043); Relationships (3753)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emissions-certificate violations have specified financial penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation described is operating a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle without an emissions inspection certificate, with an expired certificate, or with a certificate not issued by a competent authority. The records state fines of 200,000 to 300,000 Vietnamese đồng for individual owners and 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for organizational owners. [Data: Entities (3106, 2641, 3431); Relationships (3713, 7881, 9024)]

These are stated penalties associated with the violation, not evidence that any named individual or organization committed it. The records provide no case-level enforcement data or information on compliance rates.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Document transfer procedures include an exception for suspected crime
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Where a person who temporarily retained a licence or professional certificate lacks authority to recover it, the document is to be transferred to the issuing authority or another competent authority for legal handling. The procedure also requires notification to the affected individual or organization. [Data: Entities (5077, 3277); Relationships (3745, 9231)]

The ordinary transfer procedure does not apply in the described way when the case shows signs of a crime. This is a procedural exception in the supplied records, not an allegation that a crime occurred in this community. [Data: Entities (750, 5077); Relationships (3048, 3745)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The authority’s remit includes additional traffic-management decisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description assigns competent authorities a range of possible functions, including authorizing people to ride in a cargo-truck bed during a procession and deciding whether maximum operating-speed signs should be placed for particular periods. The associated relationships specifically record these authorization and sign-placement roles. [Data: Entities (1043, 3525, 3744); Relationships (3715, 3720)]

The breadth of these functions reinforces the community’s significance to traffic administration, but the source describes powers generically and does not identify a particular authority, decision, procession, or road where they were exercised.

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test Administration
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test and the processes, people, and infrastructure used to administer it. Participants—including foreign participants who need an interpreter and drivers whose licence points have all been deducted—take the test at designated locations under the direction of officials and examiners. The described framework covers registration, identity checks, computer-based testing, secure handling and monitoring, and specified public funding; testing-location computers connect over the Ministry of Public Security WAN to a server hosted at the Traffic Police Department. The records describe regulatory and operational requirements, but do not independently establish how consistently they are implemented.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderately high importance because it connects road-safety law, licence-point consequences, and a government-administered testing system, while the records provide no evidence of misconduct or operational failure.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulated test is the community’s central function
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Law Knowledge Test is the hub linking participants, test officials, examiners, testing rooms and locations, registration, and the competent authority. The records describe its purpose as assessing knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety and identify Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, Article 7, as addressing registration and organization. [Data: Entities (4367, 3425); Relationships (10145, 10144, 6807, 9859, 3774)]

This makes the community relevant to the administration of road-safety rules. The available material sets out a process and responsibilities; it does not provide performance results or independent evidence that the requirements are being met in practice. [Data: Entities (4367, 3425)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Eligibility includes drivers who have lost all licence points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers whose licence points have all been deducted are expressly identified as eligible to take the test. Their relationship to the test links the assessment to a consequence of the licence-point system, although the records do not specify what happens after a participant passes or fails. [Data: Entities (1552, 4367); Relationships (6272)]

The test is therefore significant to a defined group of drivers affected by point deductions, but the supplied information does not establish the number of eligible drivers or the test’s effect on their licensing status. [Data: Entities (1552, 4367); Relationships (6272)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Computer-based testing depends on connected locations and specified safeguards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Participants take the test on computers using designated, approved software. The description calls for secure data handling and logging, and for a secure camera-surveillance system in the testing room that records and stores images. [Data: Entities (4367, 4919, 4902); Relationships (10145, 10148)]

Testing-location computers connect over the Ministry of Public Security WAN to a server hosted at the Traffic Police Department. This indicates a networked technical setup, but the records do not describe its security architecture, resilience, independent testing, or operational history. [Data: Entities (4914); Relationships (10147)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Identity checks and registration form part of test administration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Participants attend at the time and place notified by the competent authority and present an accepted identity document so their details can be checked against their application; electronic identification information may be used when available. The registration dossier includes a request using Form No. 01 in the circular’s appendix. [Data: Entities (4367, 4072); Relationships (9859)]

These described steps connect registration with participant verification. The supplied records do not identify the accepted documents in detail or explain the handling and retention of identity data. [Data: Entities (4367)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Officials, examiners, and facilities support the testing process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent authority conducts the test and is responsible for ensuring that the facilities and equipment used for testing are available. Test officials use computers and printers, while examiners instruct participants, who are required to follow their instructions and the testing-location rules. [Data: Entities (1048, 4900, 1866, 4913); Relationships (3774, 10144, 6807, 10508)]

Testing rooms are described as having computers, a printer, and other equipment required for testing. These records indicate assigned administrative and facility responsibilities, but do not provide staffing levels, inspection findings, or evidence about the condition of particular locations. [Data: Entities (4919, 1048)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The described process includes accommodations for some participants
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Foreign participants and ethnic-minority participants who cannot read or write Vietnamese use an interpreter hired by the competent testing authority. A foreign test participant who cannot read or write Vietnamese is separately identified as taking the examination with an interpreter. [Data: Entities (4367, 2336); Relationships (7510)]

This describes an accommodation within the test process. The records do not provide information about interpreter availability, qualification standards, or how frequently this arrangement is used. [Data: Entities (4367, 2336)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified public revenues fund test organization
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The test’s organization is funded from specified public revenues. In particular, revenue from fines for administrative violations of road traffic order and safety rules is allocated to fund the test’s organization after being paid into the state budget. [Data: Entities (4367, 133); Relationships (446)]

This establishes a stated funding connection between traffic-rule violations and test administration, but the records do not quantify the revenue, the total cost of the test, or the share supplied by these fines. [Data: Entities (4367, 133); Relationships (446)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Legal-Knowledge Testing Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security and the circulars that govern legal-knowledge tests for road-traffic safety, including tests required to restore fully deducted driving-license points. Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA establishes the core test and implementation framework; Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA amends part of it, and Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA provides further amendments and transitional rules. The framework connects national ministry responsibilities with traffic-police testing authorities, test takers, test software, and specialized databases. The supplied records describe formal procedures and technical capabilities, but provide no evidence of violations, enforcement failures, or adverse reputation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial public-administration importance through nationwide traffic-safety testing, license-point restoration, police implementation, and management of specialized transport-related databases.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A ministry-led regulatory framework governs the testing system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Public Security of Vietnam is identified as the issuing authority for Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, which establishes requirements for testing drivers’ legal knowledge of road-traffic order and safety. The circular assigns responsibilities to competent authorities and sets out test organization, registration, and implementation provisions. [Data: Entities (835, 3022); Relationships (3282, 3281, 3292, 3277)]

The framework is amended by Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA and Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA, both associated with the Ministry. The supplied information supports a coordinated regulatory structure, but does not establish whether implementation has been independently audited or whether any entity has breached the rules. [Data: Entities (831, 832); Relationships (3246, 3252, 3242)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The rules establish a route to restore driving-license points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers whose license points have all been deducted must pass a road-traffic legal-knowledge test as part of the point-restoration process. The test is therefore linked to both traffic-law knowledge and an administrative consequence for drivers. [Data: Entities (835, 1564, 4380); Relationships (3293, 6302, 3292)]

A person who fails may register for a retest after seven working days have elapsed from the end of the previous examination. The records describe this process but provide no figures on test volumes, pass rates, or resulting changes in road safety. [Data: Entities (2871, 2870); Relationships (8522)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulations specify test formats and scoring thresholds
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The theoretical A1 test is described as a 19-minute, 25-question multiple-choice examination, with a passing score of at least 21 and failure if the disqualifying question is answered incorrectly. The C1 test is described as a 22-minute, 35-question examination, requiring at least 32 correct answers and a correct response to its critical question. [Data: Entities (4935, 688); Relationships (3296, 3279, 2942)]

The supplied records also describe a class C test lasting 24 minutes, containing 40 questions and requiring at least 36 correct answers, subject to its disqualifying-question rule. These examples show that test requirements vary by licence category; they do not indicate how well the tests predict safe driving. [Data: Entities (2890)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A sequence of amendments includes transitional and future effective dates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA amended a provision in Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, and the supplied information gives March 1, 2025 as Circular 13’s effective date. Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA provides that specified provisions from the earlier circulars continue through June 30, 2027. [Data: Entities (832, 1106, 1731); Relationships (3246, 3247, 3230, 3231)]

The records state that Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA takes effect on July 1, 2026, subject to an exception, and separately identify July 1, 2027 as the effective date for specified amended and supplemented test provisions. These dates are presented as applying to different provisions or circumstances; the supplied text does not provide enough detail to reconcile every transition case. [Data: Entities (831, 1742, 2799); Relationships (3237, 3238, 3232, 3233)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police authorities have operational and software responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework assigns the Traffic Police Department’s director responsibility for developing, administering, maintaining, and upgrading software used for tests, as well as reporting that work to Ministry leadership. Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA also assigns the director responsibility for directing, inspecting, and urging implementation. [Data: Entities (835, 831); Relationships (3237)]

Provincial or municipal police traffic divisions are identified as competent testing authorities. The records further specify that when testing computers lack the required WAN connection, the authorized inspection authority uses secure information-storage equipment to retain test-taker information for administering the test. [Data: Entities (616, 3992, 4905); Relationships (2776, 2777, 2778, 8899)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry manages extensive specialized databases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is responsible for building and managing specialized databases covering vehicle registration, traffic violations, road accidents, vehicle journeys and driver images, drivers’ operating time, vehicle inspections, driver testing and licensing, and legal-knowledge training certificates. The listed scope links the testing regime to broader public-sector traffic and transport information management. [Data: Entities (3022, 1476, 4510, 3689); Relationships (6078, 8905, 8897)]

The supplied records establish the stated database responsibilities, but do not specify data-retention periods, access controls, security audits, or evidence of misuse. No conclusions about privacy or cybersecurity performance can be drawn from this information alone. [Data: Entities (3022); Relationships (6078, 8905, 8897)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework includes a distinct testing accommodation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Eligible ethnic-minority test takers who cannot read or write Vietnamese, previously held an A1 motorcycle license, and have exhausted its points may take a separately administered test using oral questions and answers and a paper-based multiple-choice method similar to the A1 licensing examination. An interpreter may be provided by the authority or hired by the test taker. [Data: Entities (1757, 4381, 19); Relationships (6641, 42)]

This is a specific access provision described in the records; they do not provide evidence on how often it is used or whether it meets all test takers’ needs.

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Safety Law Implementation Network
v.tom_tat: This community centers on implementing Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and communicating laws on road traffic order and safety. Responsibility is distributed among relevant individuals, police units and localities, provincial and centrally governed city police, and units under Ministry of Public Security agencies. A state management agency leads and coordinates legal communication with relevant individuals and organizations. The network is important for coordinating public-sector implementation, but the supplied records do not establish compliance outcomes, operational effectiveness, or technical capability. [Data: Entities (2557, 4102, 4756, 3948, 5239); Relationships (7820, 9886, 10138, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it coordinates implementation responsibilities across police and government bodies for road-traffic safety laws, although the records provide no evidence of outcomes or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Implementation responsibility is distributed across agencies and officials
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The implementation of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is linked to relevant individuals, provincial and centrally governed city police, units under Ministry agencies, and police units and localities. This indicates a multi-level implementation structure rather than responsibility resting with a single actor. [Data: Entities (2557, 4102, 3948, 5239, 3822); Relationships (7820, 7819, 7822, 7818)]

The records assign implementation duties to directors of the provincial and city police organizations and to heads of units under Ministry agencies. They also describe police units and localities as reporting difficulties encountered during implementation. [Data: Entities (3948, 5239, 1388, 2477, 3822); Relationships (7819, 7822, 7818, 5868, 7715)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Relevant individuals connect implementation with feedback and outreach
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Relevant individuals are assigned responsibility for implementing the circular and may report difficulties or obstacles. Their role therefore includes both carrying out provisions and conveying implementation challenges. [Data: Entities (4102, 2557); Relationships (7820)]

The records also connect these individuals to the state management agency and to road-traffic law communication and dissemination, indicating that they participate in outreach coordinated by that agency. [Data: Entities (4102, 4756, 4356); Relationships (9886, 9885)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The state management agency leads legal communication and dissemination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The state management agency for road traffic order and safety is described as responsible for managing that subject area and leading and coordinating communication and dissemination of relevant laws. [Data: Entities (4756, 4356); Relationships (10138)]

Relevant individuals and relevant agencies and organizations are both linked to this communication activity through coordination with the agency. This makes the agency a central coordinating node in the outreach portion of the community. [Data: Entities (4102, 4098, 4756, 4356); Relationships (9886, 9879, 9885, 9878)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Relevant agencies and organizations broaden the coordination network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Relevant agencies and organizations are described as concerned with road traffic order and safety and with the decree, and as responsible for implementing the decree. The supplied records do not identify these organizations individually. [Data: Entities (4098)]

They are connected to the state management agency for coordinated communication and dissemination of laws, and to the communication activity itself. This provides a coordination link beyond the police and Ministry-related implementation actors. [Data: Entities (4098, 4756, 4356); Relationships (9879, 9878)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ministry-level units have a defined organizational chain
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Units under the Ministry’s agencies are described as organizational units within Ministry of Public Security agencies, with their heads assigned implementation responsibility. The records also identify ministry-level agencies as the parent agencies for those units. [Data: Entities (5239, 3031, 2477); Relationships (8949, 7715)]

This creates a documented chain from ministry-level agencies to subordinate units and their heads, alongside the units’ connection to implementation of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. [Data: Relationships (8949, 7715, 7822)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes responsibilities, not verified performance or capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records specify legal communication, implementation assignments, coordination, and reporting of difficulties. They do not provide evidence about whether the actors complied, how effectively implementation proceeded, or what results were achieved. [Data: Entities (2557, 4102, 4756, 3822); Relationships (7820, 7818, 10138)]

Likewise, no technical systems, tools, or technical capabilities are described in the supplied data. The community’s importance can therefore be assessed from its assigned public-sector remit and network structure, but not from measured operational performance or technical capacity. [Data: Entities (2557, 4102, 4756, 4098)]

v.tieu_de: Driver’s-License Point Restoration Tests
v.tom_tat: This community describes the legal-knowledge testing process associated with restoring points on a driver’s license. The restoration test is benchmarked to the theoretical driving test for the relevant license class, including its duration, questions, and passing score. A passing result qualifies the candidate for point restoration, while a failed candidate may retake the test after seven working days. Article 6, paragraph 3 is identified as specifying requirements for test timing, questions, and results. The records describe administrative procedures but do not establish actual compliance, test-system capabilities, or broader enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (1572, 4931, 524, 3592, 4199, +more); Relationships (6315, 6314, 6313, 2435, 8526, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it links driver-license point restoration to standardized legal-knowledge testing, but the records indicate no wider operational impact or compliance concerns.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The theoretical driving test is the central benchmark
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The theoretical driving test serves as the reference point for requirements in the related legal-knowledge and point-restoration tests. For the corresponding license class, the restoration test’s duration, questions, and passing score correspond to those of the theoretical driving test; separate records also specify alignment on duration and questions and equivalence of passing scores. [Data: Entities (4931, 1572, 2886); Relationships (6315, 8526, 8560)]

This alignment makes the theoretical test the organizing standard across the community’s testing procedures. The records describe the benchmark but do not provide the specific durations, question counts, or passing scores. [Data: Entities (4931, 2872, 2886); Relationships (6315, 8526, 8560)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passing the legal-knowledge test is linked to point restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community connects successful completion of a legal-knowledge test with restoration of driver’s-license points: passing the restoration test qualifies a candidate to have points restored. [Data: Entities (1571, 1572); Relationships (6313)]

A passing result is defined in relation to the required passing score for the corresponding theoretical driving test and license category. The records establish this procedural condition, but do not specify how many points are restored or the broader consequences for a driver’s license. [Data: Entities (2886, 3592, 4931); Relationships (8560, 8559)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 6, paragraph 3 is associated with passing-result requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6, paragraph 3 is described as a provision of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA concerning the timing, questions, and results of legal-knowledge tests. Its recorded relationship to the passing-result entity specifies the score condition under which a result is recognized as passing. [Data: Entities (524, 3592); Relationships (2435)]

The records identify this provision and its stated connection to the passing condition, but do not provide the full text of the circular or evidence about how the requirements are implemented in practice. [Data: Entities (524); Relationships (2435)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Candidates who fail may retake the test after seven working days
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Candidates who do not pass the point-restoration test may register to take it again after seven working days from the end of the previous test. This establishes a specific waiting period in the described retake procedure. [Data: Entities (4199, 1572); Relationships (6314)]

The records do not specify additional retake limits, exceptions, or other eligibility conditions, so those details cannot be inferred from this community data. [Data: Entities (4199); Relationships (6314)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records define a procedural framework, not evidence of compliance or technical performance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities describe the purpose and general format of the restoration test, including that it is generally computer-based and multiple-choice, and identify requirements related to test content, timing, passing results, and retakes. [Data: Entities (1572, 2872, 524, 3592, 4199)]

These descriptions do not document whether any particular test was administered in accordance with the requirements, nor do they provide evidence about system security, reliability, operational capacity, or candidate outcomes. Accordingly, no conclusion about actual legal compliance or technical capability is supported by the supplied records. [Data: Entities (1572, 524, 3592); Relationships (2435, 6314, 6315)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Test and Registration
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Test and its registration process. Registration requires an application dossier, while the test involves participants, a testing officer, and a venue where participants follow applicable rules. The test description refers to Article 7, and registration is described as being conducted under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. [Data: Entities (4377, 4903, 4901, 4917, 4070, +more); Relationships (10159, 10160, 10158, 10161, 9857, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it organizes a regulated test related to road traffic rules and safety, while the provided data describes routine procedures and no specific incidents or harms.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The test is the community's central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Test assesses knowledge of road traffic rules and safety. Its time and location are publicly announced by the competent testing authority, and Article 7 is described as governing its registration, organization, and participant conduct. [Data: Entities (4377)]

The test connects to the registration process, participants, testing officer, and venue, making it the hub of the described community. [Data: Relationships (10159, 10160, 10158, 10161)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration requires an application dossier
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Test Registration is described as the process for applying to take the road traffic legal knowledge test and as being conducted under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. The entity description states that an application for registration is required. [Data: Entities (4903)]

Submitting a registration dossier is explicitly part of the registration process, linking the dossier submission to Test Registration. The data does not specify additional documents, deadlines, or eligibility criteria. [Data: Entities (4070); Relationships (9857)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Participants complete the test under officer instructions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A test participant logs into testing software, completes the test according to the examiner’s instructions, and follows the rules at the testing venue. [Data: Entities (4901)]

The testing officer instructs participants on completing the test, and the participant is described as following those instructions. These records establish the operational roles but do not provide further detail about the software or the officer’s authority. [Data: Entities (4917); Relationships (10160, 10507)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The testing venue is part of the rules-based process
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The test is organized at a testing venue, where participants must comply with applicable rules. The venue is therefore a practical component of test administration, alongside registration and participant instruction. [Data: Entities (4920); Relationships (10161)]

The provided information does not identify a specific venue or describe its security, accessibility, or technical facilities. The venue’s supported role is limited to hosting the test and being subject to applicable rules. [Data: Entities (4377, 4920)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is procedural, with limited evidence about broader impacts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a structured process: registration, dossier submission, testing, participant instructions, and venue rules. The stated subject matter—road traffic rules and safety—gives the test public-safety relevance. [Data: Entities (4377, 4903, 4070); Relationships (9857, 10159, 10161)]

The dataset does not report noncompliance, disputes, security incidents, or adverse outcomes. Accordingly, the community’s importance is grounded in its regulatory and road-safety function rather than evidence of a specific threat or operational failure. [Data: Entities (4377, 4903, 4901, 4917, 4920)]

v.tieu_de: Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA Driver-Test Transition Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA and its transitional provisions for legal-knowledge testing related to restoring driver’s-license points. The provisions connect to testing rules in Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA and Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA, with specified requirements continuing through June 30, 2027. The material also identifies a computer-based testing rule and an exception, but provides no evidence about implementation or compliance in practice. [Data: Entities (496, 938, 499, 497); Relationships (2321, 2326, 3451, 2323)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s meaningful regulatory importance for driver’s-license point-restoration testing, while its scope is limited to the cited provisions and transition period.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is the central transition instrument
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is described as addressing effectiveness and transitional provisions. Its Clause 3 is part of that article and establishes continued application of specified testing requirements through June 30, 2027. [Data: Entities (496, 938); Relationships (2321, 2324)]

This makes the article and its third clause the main hub linking the newer circular to earlier testing provisions. The supplied information describes the rules, but does not establish how they are implemented or whether any entity has complied with them.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Earlier testing requirements remain in force during a defined transition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA identifies provisions of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA whose test requirements continue to apply through June 30, 2027. The referenced provisions include Clause 3 and points in Clauses 2 and 5 of Article 6. [Data: Entities (938, 939, 3755, 3757); Relationships (3449, 3451, 3452)]

Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is described as setting out test content, methods, timing, structure, and passing requirements. These are the subject areas carried into the transition; the data does not specify the detailed substantive requirements themselves. [Data: Entities (499, 4918); Relationships (2336)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The transition bridges multiple circulars
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The transition clause in Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA cites provisions in Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA as continuing to apply through June 30, 2027. Article 6 of Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA is also described as amending and supplementing point a, clause 1 of Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA. [Data: Entities (497, 3753, 938); Relationships (2326, 2327)]

Together, these links show a sequence in which the 2025 circular amended an earlier testing provision and the 2026 circular’s transition rules refer to provisions from the earlier instruments. The available records do not provide a comprehensive account of every amendment or the full consolidated text.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The subject matter is testing for driver’s-license point restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA connects its amendments to legal-knowledge tests for restoring driver’s-license points. It further states that Article 1 amends the provision governing test content, method, duration, and passing requirements. [Data: Entities (496)]

Article 6 of Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA is identified as containing test-related provisions, and the connected testing-requirements entity summarizes those areas as content, methods, timing, structure, and results required to pass. [Data: Entities (499, 4918); Relationships (2336)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The general computer-testing method has a stated exception
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 6 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is linked to Clause 8 of Article 7 as an exception to the general requirement that candidates take the legal-knowledge test on a computer using testing software. [Data: Entities (990); Relationships (2323)]

Article 2 of Circular 105/2026/TT-BCA is described as amending Clause 8 of Article 7. The supplied information does not detail the circumstances covered by the exception, so its scope cannot be determined from these records alone. [Data: Entities (296); Relationships (1060)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes regulatory provisions, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify circulars, articles, clauses, testing requirements, amendment links, and a transition end date. They do not identify regulated parties’ conduct, enforcement actions, violations, or actual testing outcomes. [Data: Entities (496, 499, 497, 4918); Relationships (2321, 2326, 2336)]

Accordingly, this community supports analysis of the structure and stated timing of the rules, but not a conclusion about legal compliance, operational effectiveness, or reputation.

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Legal Knowledge Test and Provincial Police
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the computer-based legal knowledge test on road traffic order and safety. Candidates take the examination, while provincial and municipal police e-portals publish test times and locations, and the police forces manage those portals. Registration requires document submission, and police directors are responsible for implementing Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. The available information does not specify actual test or document-submission times and locations. [Data: Entities (2873, 3957, 3958, 4904, 1390, +more); Relationships (8534, 8535, 2952, 9795, 5877)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate administrative importance because it connects a regulated examination and candidate registration with police-managed public information channels, while the records describe no broader adverse impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The examination is the community’s central activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The legal knowledge test on road traffic order and safety is a theoretical examination assessing candidates’ knowledge of laws concerning road traffic order and safety. Under Circular 65/2024/TT-BCA, candidates take it on a computer using dedicated multiple-choice examination software. [Data: Entities (2873)]

The test connects the other identified entities: candidates take it, registration and document submission are for it, and police e-portals announce information about its times and locations. [Data: Relationships (2952, 8534, 8535)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Candidates take a computer-based multiple-choice test
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Candidates are identified as the people taking the theoretical examination, and the relationship record specifies that they take the computer-based multiple-choice test. This establishes a defined delivery format, but the supplied records do not describe the software’s technical features beyond its use for the examination. [Data: Entities (693, 2873); Relationships (2952)]

The examination is described as assessing knowledge of road traffic order and safety laws. The records do not provide candidate numbers, pass rates, or other outcomes from which to assess the test’s reach or effectiveness. [Data: Entities (2873, 693); Relationships (2952)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration requires documents, but logistical details are unspecified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The registration process includes submitting the required documents, and the test description says applicants may select a test date and competent testing authority before being notified of the expected time and place. [Data: Entities (2873, 4904); Relationships (8535)]

The available information does not give the actual time or location for the examination or for submitting documents. Those missing details limit what can be concluded about the practical arrangements available to applicants. [Data: Entities (2873, 4904)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police e-portals provide public examination scheduling information
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial or municipal police authorities manage electronic information portals on which examination times and locations are publicly announced. Commune-level police use that published information when arranging appointments. [Data: Entities (3958, 3957); Relationships (8534, 9795)]

This makes the portals an information link between the examination process and police appointment arrangements. The records establish their stated function, but do not provide information about portal availability, security, accessibility, or technical performance. [Data: Entities (3958); Relationships (8534, 9795)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Provincial and municipal police have an implementation role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Provincial and municipal police are described as forces operating in provinces and centrally governed cities, and their directors are responsible for implementing Circular 13/2025/TT-BCA. [Data: Entities (3957, 1390); Relationships (5877)]

The forces also manage the e-portals that publish examination schedules and locations, connecting their administrative role to the public information process. The provided records do not specify further implementation measures or assess compliance with the circular. [Data: Entities (3957, 3958); Relationships (9795, 5877, 8534)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Examination Results and License Agencies
v.tom_tat: This community describes how road-traffic-law examination results are communicated to driver’s-license authorities. The competent knowledge-testing authority is responsible for notifying relevant agencies; when data connection and sharing are not established, results are sent to the authorized official’s agency and the driver’s-license management agency. The process supports the work of an official authorized to deduct license points, but the described procedure depends on a non-connected data-sharing context. [Data: Entities (1864, 1050, 619, 1233, 1561, +more); Relationships (3779, 2781, 2782, 6284, 4210, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate operational importance because it links examination-result notification to driver’s-license management and point deduction, while the described process also highlights a dependency on whether electronic data sharing is established. [Data: Entities (1233, 1864, 613); Relationships (3779, 4210, 6284, 2772)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The testing authority is responsible for notifying agencies
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The competent knowledge-testing authority checks people’s knowledge of road-traffic order and safety laws and is responsible for notifying relevant agencies of examination results when data are not connected and shared. This places the authority at the center of the described result-notification process. [Data: Entities (1050, 1864); Relationships (3779)]

The relationships identify two agency recipients: the agency of the authorized point-deduction official and the driver’s-license management agency. [Data: Entities (619, 1561); Relationships (2781, 3778)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Manual or separate notification applies when data are not connected
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The notification procedure is specifically described as applying when data connection and sharing have not been established. The data do not establish whether this is the current arrangement in any particular jurisdiction, only that the process applies under that condition. [Data: Entities (1233, 1864); Relationships (4210)]

The data-connection-and-sharing entity describes electronic exchange as dependent on infrastructure, technical capabilities, and information conditions, and notes that arrangements may not yet be established. This indicates a stated dependency, but provides no details about system performance or implementation status. [Data: Entities (1233)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Results go to both point-deduction and license-management functions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When data are not connected and shared, examination results are sent to the agency associated with the official authorized to deduct points from a driver’s license. [Data: Entities (619, 613); Relationships (2781, 2782, 2772)]

The driver’s-license management agency is also identified as a recipient of the examination-result notification in this condition. The records describe distinct recipient functions but do not specify how the agencies coordinate or whether they use the same records system. [Data: Entities (1561, 1864); Relationships (6284, 3778)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An authorized official is linked to the point-deduction agency
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a person authorized to deduct points from a driver’s license and an agency identified as that official’s agency. This provides the organizational link between examination results and the point-deduction function. [Data: Entities (613, 619); Relationships (2772)]

The agency is described as receiving examination results when data are not connected and shared. The available records do not describe the official’s individual identity, specific cases, or the criteria for deducting points. [Data: Entities (619); Relationships (2781, 2782)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe an administrative process, not a compliance or performance assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provided information defines responsible authorities, recipient agencies, and a conditional notification procedure. It does not report legal violations, disputes, examination outcomes, processing delays, or evidence of non-compliance by any entity. [Data: Entities (1050, 619, 1561, 1864); Relationships (3779, 2781, 6284)]

Likewise, although electronic connection and sharing are described as dependent on technical and infrastructure conditions, no specific technical systems, security controls, reliability measures, or implementation details are supplied. The evidence therefore supports describing a procedural dependency, not making a technical-capability or reputation judgment. [Data: Entities (1233)]

v.tieu_de: Passenger Transport Contract Violations and Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP
v.tom_tat: This community centers on passenger-transport contract violations and their connection to Article 20, Clause 5 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The identified violations cover passenger lists, transport contracts, permitted passenger categories, electronic contract information, and passenger-compartment recording devices. The data associates several violations with fines of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, while noting an exception for a specified international-route case. The records describe regulatory requirements and violation types, not specific operators or confirmed incidents.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it links multiple passenger-transport compliance requirements to stated financial penalties, but the records do not identify actual offenders or incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 20, Clause 5 is the central penalty reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 20, Clause 5 is linked to the broader Article 20 penalty provision, which addresses specified violations by passenger-car drivers and similar vehicles. The clause is described as setting fines of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified passenger-transport violations. The available description cautions that it does not fully specify which violations are covered or whether the clause itself imposes a driver’s-license point deduction. [Data: Entities (303, 302); Relationships (1132)]

The relationships also associate the clause with specific violations, including carrying unlisted passengers, image-recording-device violations, and noncompliant or inaccessible electronic contract information. [Data: Relationships (1137, 1142, 1140, 1141)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violation category covers contract and passenger-list compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community’s central violation category includes failures to carry a passenger list or transport contract, carrying people not listed, and transporting people outside permitted categories. These are presented as regulatory violation types rather than reports that a particular driver committed them. [Data: Entities (3568)]

Individual relationships identify carrying unlisted passengers, failure to carry a passenger list, failure to carry a transport contract, and having a noncompliant contract as components of the broader category. [Data: Relationships (3046, 6891, 6897, 9222)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-list requirements apply to several identified violation types
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data distinguishes carrying a passenger whose name is absent from the required list from failing to have or carry the required list at all. Both are associated with passenger transport under contract, and carrying unlisted passengers is explicitly linked to the broader passenger-transport contract violation category. [Data: Entities (749, 1940, 724); Relationships (3046, 6891, 1133)]

For international fixed-route passenger transport, the described violation concerns operating without a transport order or required passenger list, or carrying a passenger not named on the list, subject to a stated exception. [Data: Entities (2741)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Electronic contracts introduce information-access and integrity requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The identified electronic-contract violations include using a contract without equipment that allows access to the contract and passenger list, or having equipment but being unable to access those records. [Data: Entities (3403); Relationships (1141)]

The records also identify contracts that fail to comply with regulations and unauthorized changes to a signed electronic contract or its passenger list. These are linked to the stated fine range under Article 20, Clause 5. [Data: Entities (3265); Relationships (1140)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger categories and international-route cases have specific scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One violation concerns carrying people outside categories permitted by regulation, with examples including services for preschool children, pupils, students, public officials, civil servants, public employees, or workers. The broader violation category is linked to this restriction. [Data: Entities (5156); Relationships (9441)]

The international fixed-route provision describes missing transport orders or passenger lists and unlisted passengers, but the stated Article 20, Clause 5 penalty is subject to an exception cited as Article 37, Clause 1, Point B. The records do not provide further detail on the scope of that exception. [Data: Entities (2741, 418); Relationships (1135, 1774)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle image-recording is a separate compliance dimension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies a passenger-car image-recording violation for vehicles with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat. The described conditions include lacking a passenger-compartment recording device, having an inoperative device while in traffic, or altering device data. [Data: Entities (3581)]

This violation is associated with Article 20, Clause 5 and the stated fine range of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. This indicates a technical compliance requirement in the regulatory framework, but does not establish the capabilities or conduct of any particular operator or device. [Data: Relationships (1142); Entities (303, 3581)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory scope, not actual enforcement or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The entities and relationships describe legal provisions, types of violations, and stated penalties. They do not identify a named transport company, driver accused of a violation, enforcement action, or confirmed incident; therefore, the information does not support conclusions about an individual operator’s compliance or reputation. [Data: Entities (3568, 302, 303, 3580); Relationships (1136)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Expressway Safety and Specialized Vehicle Operator Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the operator of a specialized motor vehicle and connects two road-safety areas: lighting when encountering a pedestrian crossing the road, and stopping on an expressway during a technical incident or other unavoidable circumstance. The records describe requirements for low beams, hazard lights, warning devices, and notifying the highway management authority when a disabled vehicle cannot be moved to the emergency stopping lane. They also identify violations involving inadequate warnings and unauthorized stopping or parking. [Data: Entities (3412, 1774, 2053, 5507, 2057); Relationships (8407, 7743, 7839)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high public-safety importance because its provisions address pedestrian visibility and measures to warn approaching traffic about stopped vehicles on expressways. [Data: Entities (2828, 3608, 1774, 1924); Relationships (8407, 6872, 6873)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized motor vehicle operator is the central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The operator is linked to lighting requirements around pedestrians, responsibility for signaling stopped vehicles, and improper expressway stopping or parking. These connections make the operator the common point across the community's pedestrian-safety and expressway-stopping topics. [Data: Entities (3412); Relationships (7043, 8407, 7039, 7839, 9305)]

The entity description also states that the operator may be subject to penalties for specified road traffic violations; the records do not provide penalty amounts or further enforcement details. [Data: Entities (3412)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Lighting rules address encounters with pedestrians
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Law 36/2024/QH15, Article 20(2), is described as requiring drivers and specialized motor vehicle operators to switch off high beams and use low beams when encountering a pedestrian crossing the road. The pedestrian is the circumstance that triggers this lighting requirement. [Data: Entities (2828, 3608); Relationships (8407, 9305)]

The records establish the stated rule but do not provide additional details about its enforcement or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The emergency stopping lane is reserved for necessary stops
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The emergency stopping lane is described as a lane alongside an expressway, running in the direction of traffic, intended for vehicles that must stop because of a technical problem or another unavoidable circumstance. Driving in that lane is identified as a traffic violation, distinguishing its emergency-stop purpose from ordinary travel. [Data: Entities (1774, 4860); Relationships (6692)]

The records connect this lane to both a vehicle unable to enter it and a violation involving failure to use hazard lights while stopped there. [Data: Relationships (6691, 6693)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A vehicle unable to reach the emergency lane has specified warning steps
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a disabled vehicle cannot be moved into the emergency stopping lane, the described procedure requires the driver to activate hazard lights, place a warning sign or light at least 150 meters behind the vehicle, and promptly notify the relevant authorities. [Data: Entities (5507)]

The highway management authority is specifically identified as the authority the driver must promptly notify in this situation. [Data: Entities (2488, 5507); Relationships (7743)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Warning failures are identified for vehicles stopped on expressways
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One identified violation is failing to use hazard lights when a technical problem or force majeure requires a stop in the emergency stopping lane. The operator is described as responsible for signaling in that situation. [Data: Entities (2053, 4860); Relationships (7039, 6691, 6692)]

A separate violation concerns failing to use hazard lights and place a warning sign or light at least 150 meters behind a vehicle stopped in an expressway traffic lane due to a technical problem or other unavoidable circumstance. [Data: Entities (2057, 1924, 4860); Relationships (7043, 6872, 6873)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized expressway stopping or parking is also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify stopping or parking a vehicle in an unauthorized place on an expressway as a violation and connect that violation to the specialized motor vehicle operator as the person who may commit it. [Data: Entities (2598, 3412); Relationships (7839)]

This issue is distinct from emergency stopping: the records describe the emergency stopping lane as reserved for necessary stops, while unauthorized expressway stopping or parking is separately categorized as a violation. [Data: Entities (1774, 2598, 4860)]

v.tieu_de: Healthcare Facilities and Road-Accident Response
v.tom_tat: The community centers on healthcare facilities that provide initial emergency care to people injured in road traffic accidents. The facilities are also responsible for promptly notifying the nearest police authority and arranging blood testing of the vehicle operator; when they cannot conduct the tests, they must preserve and transfer the sample to a testing facility. The connected entities cover the victim, emergency care, accident reporting, blood testing, and sample transfer. [Data: Entities (2479, 4335, 2673, 3226, 654); Relationships (7720, 7717, 7718, 2858, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high operational importance because it links emergency treatment with prompt police notification and blood-testing procedures after road traffic accidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Healthcare facilities are the central operational hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Healthcare facilities connect the main functions and participants in this community: they provide initial emergency care, arrange blood testing, notify the nearest police authority, and manage sample transfer when testing is unavailable on site. Their listed degree is 9, and the relationships show connections to the victim, testing facility, police authority, emergency care, and reporting and testing processes. [Data: Entities (2479); Relationships (7720, 7721, 2858, 7718, 7717, +more)]

This central role makes healthcare facilities the key coordination point in the described road-accident response workflow. The data specifies responsibilities, but does not report whether any particular facility has complied with them. [Data: Entities (2479); Relationships (54, 2855, 7721)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Initial emergency care is provided to the injured person
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A road traffic accident victim is defined as a person injured in an accident who receives initial emergency care at a healthcare facility. The facilities’ provision of this care is explicitly represented as a relationship in the network. [Data: Entities (4335, 2673, 2479); Relationships (7720, 7717)]

This establishes treatment of the injured person as a core part of the community’s role. The supplied information does not specify treatment protocols, outcomes, or the severity of any injuries. [Data: Entities (4335, 2673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prompt accident reporting connects facilities to police
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Healthcare facilities must promptly report accident information to the nearest police authority when providing initial emergency care to a road traffic accident victim. Accident information reporting is separately described as prompt reporting by a healthcare facility to that authority. [Data: Entities (3226, 26, 2479); Relationships (7718, 54)]

The data identifies a reporting responsibility and its recipient, but does not provide details about the information reported, a specific accident, or whether a report was made in any particular case. [Data: Entities (26, 3226); Relationships (54, 7718)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Facilities are responsible for arranging operator blood tests
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes blood testing of a vehicle operator for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants after a road traffic accident. Healthcare facilities are responsible for arranging this testing. [Data: Entities (654, 2479); Relationships (2858)]

The records describe the testing purpose and facility responsibility, but do not state any test result or indicate that a particular operator was tested. [Data: Entities (654); Relationships (2858)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sample transfer provides a fallback when on-site testing is unavailable
phat_hien.giai_thich:
If a healthcare facility cannot conduct the required tests, it must preserve the blood sample and send it to a testing facility capable of conducting them.
