The network represents both the facility-to-testing-facility responsibility and the transfer of the sample. [Data: Entities (653, 4912, 2479); Relationships (2855, 7721, 2856)]

This fallback makes preservation and transfer part of the described testing workflow when the initial-care facility lacks testing capability. The supplied records do not specify transfer timing, handling standards, or whether a particular sample was transferred. [Data: Entities (653, 4912); Relationships (2855, 2856)]

v.tieu_de: Expressway Traffic Rules and Violations
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around the EXPRESSWAY as a central setting for traffic rules, exceptions, and violations. Its associated records cover safe following distance, entry and exit, emergency stopping lanes and shoulders, pedestrian access, lane changes, specialized-vehicle speed, and animal-drawn vehicles. A connected set of records addresses specialized vehicle operators and penalties under Article 16 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, including withdrawal of certain vehicle documents. The material describes regulatory requirements and consequences; it does not provide evidence about an organization’s reputation or operational capabilities. [Data: Entities (1920, 4713, 1286, 1989, 4692); Relationships (6855, 6854, 6362, 6863, 6869, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial importance to expressway road safety and traffic regulation, while the records describe rules and penalties rather than evidence of broader harm or misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The expressway is the community’s central regulatory setting
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The EXPRESSWAY is described as a high-speed road with lanes, entry and exit points, shoulders, and emergency stopping lanes. Its rules cover speed, lane use and changes, stopping and parking, and prohibitions including driving against traffic, reversing, and U-turns, subject to stated exceptions. [Data: Entities (1920)]

The relationship records connect the expressway to multiple distinct rules and violations, making it the organizing entity for this community rather than merely a location for one incident. [Data: Relationships (6855, 6854, 6362, 6863, 6869, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several connected violations concern safe driving and expressway access
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify failure to maintain a safe following distance, failure to follow entry or exit rules, driving in an emergency stopping lane or on a shoulder, and unsafe lane changes as expressway-related violations. [Data: Entities (1989, 1612, 1972, 5268); Relationships (6855, 6854, 6362, 6869)]

The safe-distance record covers driving too closely on an expressway, failing to observe a minimum-distance sign, or failing to maintain a gap in a way that causes a collision. The lane-change description specifies that changes must be made one adjacent lane at a time and with safe distances from nearby vehicles. [Data: Entities (1989, 5268)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some violations carry specified monetary penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to maintain a safe following distance is stated to be punishable by a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The record associates this violation with the expressway safe-distance requirement. [Data: Entities (1989); Relationships (6855)]

Driving a specialized motor vehicle onto an expressway when its designed speed is below the prescribed minimum is stated to carry a fine of 14,000,000 to 16,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, with an exception for vehicles or equipment used to manage or maintain expressways. Separately, entering with an animal or animal-drawn vehicle is stated to carry a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (4692, 1801); Relationships (6865, 6727)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized vehicle operators are linked to multiple compliance obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A specialized vehicle operator is defined as a person operating a specialized vehicle, including any towed trailer. The relationships connect such operators to safe-distance, expressway entry or exit, and emergency-lane or shoulder violations. [Data: Entities (4713); Relationships (6947, 6926, 6363)]

Article 16 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as setting penalties for specialized vehicle operators who violate vehicle-condition requirements. One stated administrative consequence is withdrawal of vehicle registration or inspection documents that were improperly issued or do not match the vehicle. [Data: Entities (1286, 5643); Relationships (5617, 10445)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Management and maintenance activities have explicit exceptions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The general expressway description says vehicles may enter only when permitted, giving vehicles used for expressway management or maintenance as an example; it also excludes pedestrians except those performing such work. [Data: Entities (1920)]

The relationships expressly connect management and maintenance vehicles and workers to these exceptions. The low-speed specialized motor-vehicle violation also has a stated exception for vehicles or equipment used to manage or maintain expressways. [Data: Entities (1921, 1922, 4692); Relationships (6852, 6853, 6865)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records distinguish unavoidable stopping from ordinary violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
OTHER UNAVOIDABLE CIRCUMSTANCE is defined as an unavoidable event, other than technical failure, that forces or may require a driver to stop or park on an expressway or in a road tunnel. Its relationship to the expressway identifies it as a circumstance that may require stopping or parking there. [Data: Entities (3476); Relationships (6862)]

The expressway description separately states that stopping or parking is restricted outside designated areas. The records therefore distinguish a defined unavoidable circumstance from the general restrictions, but do not provide further detail about how an exception is assessed in an individual case. [Data: Entities (1920, 3476); Relationships (6862)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A collision with the vehicle ahead is linked to following-distance failure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies collision with the vehicle ahead as an outcome that can occur when a driver fails to maintain a safe distance from the vehicle in front. The relationship explicitly connects that collision to the safe-following-distance violation. [Data: Entities (1008, 1989); Relationships (3580)]

The safe-distance violation description includes failure to maintain a safe gap in a way that causes a collision. This establishes a road-safety consequence in the supplied records, but does not quantify collision frequency or severity. [Data: Entities (1989, 1008); Relationships (3580)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence is regulatory, not a profile of an organization or its reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied entities and relationships describe road rules, violation categories, exceptions, penalties, and consequences involving expressways and specialized vehicle operators. They do not identify an organization, public reputation, or technical capabilities beyond the vehicle and roadway characteristics specified in the records. [Data: Entities (1920, 4713, 1286, 1989, 4692); Relationships (6855, 5617, 10445)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road-Traffic Accidents and Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on TRAFFIC ACCIDENT and connects it to specified road-traffic violations, penalties, and an investigation-and-resolution process. The listed conduct includes speeding, unsafe vehicle maneuvers, unsafe door opening, prohibited-direction driving, and failures involving lane use or safe distance. The records also describe duties for drivers involved in an accident and several fines, while making clear that penalties depend on the particular violation and provision. The information concerns regulatory compliance and road safety; it does not establish actual incidents, enforcement outcomes, or compliance by any particular driver.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it covers multiple accident-causing violations, driver responsibilities, financial penalties, and investigation procedures, without evidence of specific incidents or actors.

phat_hien.tom_tat: TRAFFIC ACCIDENT is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
TRAFFIC ACCIDENT is the hub connecting the listed violations, penalty concepts, and the investigation-and-resolution process. Its description frames an accident as potentially resulting from specified unsafe driving or other violations and notes that accident information is addressed by the cited provision. [Data: Entities (4982); Relationships (10247, 10234, 10532, 7032, 7173)]

The entity description cites Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, but the records do not establish how the decree has been applied in any particular case. [Data: Entities (4982)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community covers a range of accident-causing driving conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify several distinct ways a violation may cause an accident: speeding; driving against prohibited or one-way traffic; unsafe opening of a vehicle door; and failing to slow or stop when required for safety. These are presented as possible violation categories, not evidence that any specific event occurred. [Data: Entities (4729, 1595, 5271, 5267); Relationships (10451, 6332, 10534, 10533)]

Other listed conduct includes improper stopping, parking, turning, reversing, overtaking, or lane changes, as well as incorrect road or lane use and inadequate following distance. [Data: Entities (5281, 5647); Relationships (10535, 10536)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some provisions are expressly conditional on an accident
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROAD TRAFFIC VIOLATION CAUSING AN ACCIDENT is described as an offense specified in Article 6, Clause 12, that results in a traffic accident. The relationship likewise links that violation to the accident outcome. [Data: Entities (4459); Relationships (10247)]

The records also describe a road-traffic safety violation in goods transport by truck, tractor, or a similar vehicle, with a fine stated for specified violations when they cause an accident. The records do not specify the full set of underlying conduct for this category. [Data: Entities (4450); Relationships (10234, 8991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Drivers involved in an accident have specified scene-related duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The TRAFFIC ACCIDENT description states that a driver who causes an accident may be required to stop, preserve the scene, assist injured people, remain at the scene, or promptly report the accident to an authority. [Data: Entities (4982)]

A separate entity describes failure to stop immediately, preserve the scene, or help an injured person as a specified violation, subject to an exception in the text. The records do not spell out that exception, so its scope cannot be assessed here. [Data: Entities (2047); Relationships (7032)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe multiple fine ranges, not one universal accident penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A 20,000,000–22,000,000 VND fine is described for a driver who commits one of the listed traffic-rule violations and causes an accident. A separate 30,000,000–35,000,000 VND fine is associated with specified road-traffic violations that cause an accident. [Data: Entities (2164, 3063); Relationships (7173, 8992, 8991)]

The central accident description also cites 10,000,000–14,000,000 VND, 14,000,000–16,000,000 VND, and 50,000,000–70,000,000 VND amounts for different violations or provisions, and explicitly cautions that these are not a single penalty applying to every accident. [Data: Entities (4982)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Investigation and resolution are part of the regulatory context
phat_hien.giai_thich:
TRAFFIC ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION AND RESOLUTION is described as a process through which violations may be verified and detected. Its relationship to TRAFFIC ACCIDENT identifies investigation and resolution as a means of checking specified violations. [Data: Entities (4983); Relationships (10532)]

This indicates an investigative dimension in the community’s regulatory framework, but the supplied records do not describe investigation results, agencies involved, or the outcome of any case. [Data: Entities (4983, 4982); Relationships (10532)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Yielding Violations and Clause 5 Article 8 Fines
v.tom_tat: This community groups two road-traffic violations: failing to yield to non-motorized vehicles in their designated lane and failing to yield to pedestrians or wheelchair users at marked crossings. Both are described as examples of turning without yielding the right of way, and both are associated with a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 5 of Article 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The records describe rules and penalties, not specific incidents or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (2067, 2061, 5176, 2257); Relationships (7050, 7049, 7044, 7045)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to road safety and specified monetary penalties, while the records provide no evidence of particular incidents, scale, or realized harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two distinct yielding violations are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies one violation involving failure to yield to non-motorized vehicles traveling in a designated lane and another involving failure to yield to pedestrians or wheelchair users at a marked pedestrian crossing. These descriptions identify the road users and circumstances covered by each violation. [Data: Entities (2067, 2061)]

The records connect both violations to a shared right-of-way concept, rather than describing them as unrelated penalties. [Data: Relationships (7050, 7045)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Both violations are linked to turning without yielding
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Turning without yielding the right of way is represented as a broader category, with the two specific failure-to-yield situations given as examples. [Data: Entities (5176); Relationships (7050, 7045)]

The available text does not establish that these are the only circumstances covered by the broader category; it identifies them as examples. [Data: Entities (5176)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A common fine range applies to both specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed penalty for each of the two specific violations is 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng under Clause 5 of Article 8 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (2067, 2061, 2257); Relationships (7049, 7044)]

The fine entity describes this range as applying to the specified road-traffic violations; the records do not provide information about additional sanctions or enforcement procedures. [Data: Entities (2257)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-motorized traffic receives explicit right-of-way protection
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed violation concerns a driver, particularly when turning, failing to yield to non-motorized vehicles traveling in a lane designated for them. This identifies both the protected road users and the designated-lane condition in the description. [Data: Entities (2067)]

The relationship data explicitly links this violation to turning without yielding and to the stated fine. [Data: Relationships (7050, 7049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Marked crossings and accessibility are explicitly addressed
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The crossing-related violation covers failure to yield to pedestrians or wheelchair users with a disability crossing at a marked pedestrian crossing. [Data: Entities (2061)]

This violation is linked both to the fine range and to the broader turning-without-yielding category. The data does not describe specific cases, frequency, or outcomes. [Data: Relationships (7044, 7045)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 31: Vehicle Penalties and Road Safety
v.tom_tat: This community centers on “Article 31,” which refers to provisions in three Vietnamese legal instruments and therefore has more than one subject. The relationships emphasize Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: Article 31 addresses penalties for illegal vehicle manufacture or assembly and illegal production, purchase, or sale of license plates, with confiscation identified as an additional penalty for relevant vehicles and plates. The data also links Article 31 to road-traffic safety measures, while its description identifies separate provisions concerning oversized or special-cargo vehicles and rudimentary vehicles. The records describe legal requirements and penalties, not actual violations or enforcement cases.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the provision’s material vehicle-safety and administrative-penalty subjects, while the data documents legal rules rather than actual violations or realized harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: “Article 31” refers to distinct legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description cautions that Article 31 appears in three Vietnamese legal instruments and that its subject depends on which instrument is cited. It identifies provisions in Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and Law 36/2024/QH15, so treating every reference to Article 31 as addressing the same conduct would be misleading. [Data: Entities (366)]

The relationships in this community connect Article 31 to both penalties for unlawful vehicle and license-plate activity and road-safety measures. The legal-instrument distinction is therefore important when interpreting the network’s otherwise broad references. [Data: Relationships (1507, 1509, 1514)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Illegal vehicle manufacture and assembly are subject to substantial fines
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 31 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as imposing administrative penalties for illegal manufacture or assembly of road motor vehicles. The stated fine range is 40,000,000–50,000,000 đồng for individuals and 80,000,000–100,000,000 đồng for organizations. [Data: Entities (2517); Relationships (1507)]

The network separately identifies illegal manufacture and illegal assembly as prohibited conduct addressed by Article 31. These records describe the applicable penalty framework; they do not establish that any person or organization committed such conduct. [Data: Entities (2502, 2515); Relationships (1505, 1506)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unlawful license-plate activity covers production, purchase, and sale
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community groups illegal production, purchase, or sale of vehicle license plates as prohibited conduct subject to penalties under Article 31 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Separate records also identify each of the three activities, making the scope broader than plate production alone. [Data: Entities (2526, 2525, 2527, 2540); Relationships (1509, 1508, 1510, 1511)]

The provided records do not state specific fine amounts for these license-plate violations. They support the existence of penalties, but not a particular penalty range or evidence of actual offending. [Data: Entities (2526); Relationships (1509)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Confiscation is identified as an additional penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate entity describes confiscation of license plates and vehicles as an additional penalty involving items illegally produced or assembled. The linked relationships specify that illegally produced or assembled vehicles may be confiscated and that illegally produced plates may be confiscated. [Data: Entities (1090); Relationships (3918, 3919)]

These links associate confiscation with the unlawful conduct described in the community, but the records do not provide details about a particular confiscation or enforcement action. [Data: Relationships (3918, 3919)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety provisions are another part of the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 31 is linked to road-traffic safety measures for certain vehicles traveling on roads. The Article 31 entity description specifies that Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerns oversized, overweight, tracked, and special-cargo vehicles, including driver assistance, warnings to other road users, and necessary safety measures. [Data: Entities (366, 4446); Relationships (1514)]

This safety topic is distinct from the penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The community thus combines regulatory material on safe road movement with administrative rules addressing unlawful vehicle and license-plate activity. [Data: Entities (366); Relationships (1507, 1509, 1514)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulation, not an observed violation network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships characterize legal provisions, categories of prohibited conduct, penalties, and safety measures. They do not identify alleged offenders, affected victims, specific incidents, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Entities (366, 2517, 2526); Relationships (1507, 1509, 1514)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant to understanding legal-compliance obligations and potential consequences, but the supplied evidence does not support a claim that violations have occurred or that harm has been realized.

v.tieu_de: Road Tunnel Emergency Stops and Operator Duties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on emergency stops in road tunnels and the duties of specialized motor vehicle operators. Technical failure or force majeure may make a stop necessary; the driver is expected to move the vehicle to a designated stopping position if possible, give a warning, and promptly notify the tunnel management agency or responsible traffic police. The surrounding records also cover tunnel traffic rules, a speeding violation linked to a stated fine, and lighting requirements. The information indicates a public-safety and regulatory focus, but does not establish incident frequency, actual harm, or broader organizational capabilities. [Data: Entities (1773, 4693, 4500, 1776, 4501); Relationships (6687, 6686, 6696, 6821, 10051)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns emergency safety procedures and legal duties in road tunnels, while the records do not show actual incidents or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency stops are the community's central safety issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
An emergency stop in a road tunnel may be required because of technical failure or another force majeure circumstance. If the vehicle cannot be moved to an emergency stopping area, the driver must signal and promptly report the situation. [Data: Entities (1773, 4857, 2297); Relationships (6688, 6683, 6685)]

The emergency-stop entity is closely connected to both the tunnel and the specialized motor vehicle operator, making the event and the operator's response the community's central concern. The records describe required precautions, but do not report a particular stop or collision. [Data: Relationships (6685, 6687)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operators have duties to relocate, warn, and report
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When stopping is necessary, the specialized motor vehicle operator must move the vehicle to an emergency stopping position if possible. That position is described as a designated location within the tunnel. [Data: Entities (1776, 4693); Relationships (6696, 6695)]

The records also state that a driver facing an emergency stop must promptly notify the road tunnel management agency or responsible traffic police. The operator is expected to follow the emergency safety and reporting procedures; no evidence is provided about compliance in any specific case. [Data: Entities (4501, 4693); Relationships (6686, 6687)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Warning requirements address stopped vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies failure to give a warning when stopped in a road tunnel as a violation involving failure to activate hazard lights or place a warning sign or warning light behind the vehicle when an emergency or other unavoidable circumstance requires a stop. [Data: Entities (1975)]

A relationship links this warning issue to technical failure, which may force a driver to stop in a tunnel. The records describe the required warning response but do not specify a penalty for this particular violation. [Data: Relationships (6932)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tunnel rules cover stopping and other traffic conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road tunnel is described as a location where road users should proceed cautiously and slow down or stop when necessary for safety. The entity description identifies gathering three or more vehicles, improper stopping or parking, reversing, and turning around or making a U-turn as tunnel traffic violations addressed by cited provisions. [Data: Entities (4500)]

These rules place emergency-stop procedures within a broader tunnel-safety framework. The records do not provide details about enforcement activity or the prevalence of the listed violations. [Data: Entities (4500, 1773)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A speeding violation is linked to a monetary fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify exceeding the speed limit by 10–20 km/h as a road traffic violation committed by a vehicle operator, and link that conduct to a fine of 1,000,000–2,000,000 VND. [Data: Entities (1882, 2128, 4693); Relationships (6822, 6821)]

The fine entity also describes other provisions for which the same penalty range may apply and cautions that the relevant provision depends on the conduct involved. The available information does not establish that a particular operator has been fined. [Data: Entities (2128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional operator obligations include appropriate headlight use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Specialized motor vehicle operators must switch off high-beam headlights and use low beams on road sections through densely populated areas when the operating lighting system is present. [Data: Entities (4693, 4308); Relationships (10051)]

This is a separate operator obligation from the tunnel emergency procedures. The records provide no evidence about an operator's actual lighting practices or any resulting incident. [Data: Relationships (10051)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence supports regulatory and safety relevance, not a record of actual harm
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe emergency conditions, operator responsibilities, tunnel rules, and a specified fine, giving the community clear relevance to road safety and regulatory compliance. [Data: Entities (1773, 4693, 4500, 2128); Relationships (6687, 6686, 6821)]

The provided records do not identify actual crashes, injuries, enforcement outcomes, or the frequency of these events. They also provide no basis for assessing reputation or broader technical capabilities beyond the described vehicle malfunction and lighting-system conditions. [Data: Entities (4857, 4308)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168 Road-Traffic Penalties and Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on monetary fines under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and connects them to road-traffic violations by drivers, specialized-motorcycle operators, organizations, driver-training and testing activities, and vehicle inspection. The described sanctions include fines, vehicle license-plate confiscation, and temporary suspension of certain license or certificate rights. The data outlines regulatory penalties and compliance areas; it does not establish how often violations occur or whether any named person or organization has committed them. [Data: Entities (3053, 1469, 5580, 3436, 5595); Relationships (8986, 8979, 8987, 8001, 3925)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad coverage of road safety and regulatory compliance, with financial and supplementary sanctions, while the data provides no evidence of actual violation prevalence or real-world outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Monetary fines are the community’s central enforcement mechanism
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Monetary Fine is the most connected entity in the provided data and links penalties to a range of driver, vehicle, organizational, inspection, and training-related violations. This makes financial penalties the central organizing feature of the community. [Data: Entities (3053); Relationships (6069, 8986, 8979, 8987, 8983, +more)]

The fine entity describes amounts varying by violation and responsible party, including examples ranging from 800,000–1,000,000 đồng to 20,000,000–30,000,000 đồng. These are described as prescribed penalties, not evidence that any particular fine was actually imposed. [Data: Entities (3053)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition violations can carry an additional license-plate penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Operators who violate vehicle-condition or eligibility requirements are described as subject to a fine as well as supplementary penalties. The data specifically links this violation to confiscation of the vehicle’s license plate, indicating that the consequences may extend beyond a monetary charge. [Data: Entities (5580, 1093); Relationships (8986, 3925)]

The description places the vehicle-condition violation under Article 14 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and identifies plate confiscation as an additional penalty for specified provisions. The supplied records do not provide details about implementation or the duration of any such penalty. [Data: Entities (5580, 1093)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized-motorcycle operators are subject to several specified traffic rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data identifies specialized-motorcycle drivers, including operators towing trailers, as potentially subject to penalties for vehicle-condition violations and certain lane-change conduct. The listed lane-change issues include changing lanes where prohibited or without advance signaling on an expressway, and changing lanes without a safe distance from nearby vehicles. [Data: Entities (1469, 5580, 5258, 2820); Relationships (6071, 6070, 6068)]

These records describe categories of conduct and applicable penalties; they do not identify a specific driver or document an actual incident. [Data: Entities (1469); Relationships (6069, 6070, 6068)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework addresses multiple forms of driver conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The covered conduct includes stopping, parking, or making a U-turn contrary to regulations, as well as specified road-traffic violations by drivers of cars and similar vehicles. For the stopping, parking, or U-turn violation that causes congestion, the relationship record specifies a fine of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (2543, 4465); Relationships (7803, 8983)]

Specified violations referenced in Article 6, paragraphs 11, 13, and 14 are also linked to withdrawal of the right to use a driving license for 22 to 24 months. The supplied information does not identify the underlying circumstances of individual cases. [Data: Entities (1718, 4465); Relationships (6576)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizations and driver-training or testing activities face compliance obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Organizational violators are described as organizations breaching road-traffic rules or rules governing driver training and driving tests. The data links these organizations and training or testing violations to monetary fines, with possible additional sanctions for certain violations. [Data: Entities (3436, 5595); Relationships (8979, 8987)]

One concrete example is failure by a driving-test center to retain required records, or to retain complete records, for two or more test sessions; this violation is linked to a prescribed fine. The records establish a regulatory requirement but do not show that a particular center failed to comply. [Data: Entities (2027); Relationships (7010)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-inspection violations may affect operating-certificate rights
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Inspection-related regulatory violations are linked to both monetary fines and a possible suspension of the right to use a certificate of eligibility for motor-vehicle inspection operations. The described suspension period is one to three months and applies to specified violations by individuals or organizations. [Data: Entities (2696, 4832); Relationships (8000, 8001)]

This indicates that the described enforcement framework includes consequences for the ability to conduct inspection activities, in addition to financial penalties. The data does not specify which inspection violations trigger the suspension beyond referring to specified provisions. [Data: Entities (4832); Relationships (8001)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a broad penalty framework, not measured enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Across the community, the records connect conduct and regulated parties to fines and supplementary sanctions, including plate confiscation and suspension of driving-license or inspection-certificate rights. This supports assessing the framework as significant in scope, but not estimating the frequency or effectiveness of enforcement. [Data: Entities (3053, 1093, 1718, 4832); Relationships (3924, 6576, 8001)]

No data provided here identifies actual cases, enforcement totals, named violators, or operational technical capabilities. Accordingly, the information supports a description of the stated rules and potential penalties, not conclusions about specific compliance performance or observed harm.

v.tieu_de: Highway Stopping Violations and 12–14 Million VND Fine
v.tom_tat: This community centers on highway stopping and parking rules, including unauthorized stopping or parking and failures to signal or warn when an emergency stop is necessary. Clause 7 of Article 6 is linked to a fine of 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND for the specified conduct. The relationships connect the violations and highway context to the penalty, with an emergency stopping lane or area identified for one of the signal-related violations. [Data: Entities (2031, 2142, 2056, 2490, 2614); Relationships (7013, 7138, 7041, 7139, 3541)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high impact because it concerns highway safety compliance and links several specified stopping or warning violations to a substantial stated monetary penalty.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A common fine links several highway violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine of 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND is connected to failure to signal an emergency stop, failure to warn of a stopped vehicle, and improper highway stopping or parking. It is also associated with the broader category of highway stopping and warning-signal violations. [Data: Entities (2142, 2031, 2056, 2490, 2614); Relationships (7013, 7041, 7138, 7139)]

The data presents this as the penalty for the specified conduct; it does not establish that every stopping or parking violation carries this fine. [Data: Entities (2142, 983); Relationships (3541, 7138, 7139)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency stops require hazard signaling
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One identified violation concerns stopping in a highway emergency stopping lane or area without activating hazard lights when a technical problem or another unavoidable circumstance requires the stop. The emergency stopping lane or area is explicitly linked to this violation. [Data: Entities (2031, 1775); Relationships (6694, 7014)]

The listed failure to signal is connected to the 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND fine. [Data: Entities (2142); Relationships (7013)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Stopped vehicles on highway lanes require warning measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes a violation involving an emergency stop on part of a highway traffic lane without hazard lights and a warning sign or warning lamp placed at least 150 meters behind the vehicle. [Data: Entities (2056, 2487)]

This failure to warn is linked to the same 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND fine as the other specified violations. [Data: Entities (2142); Relationships (7041, 7042)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized highway stopping or parking is covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Improper stopping or parking is defined as stopping or parking on a highway in a location not permitted by the rules. The highway is the setting identified for this conduct. [Data: Entities (2614, 2487); Relationships (7742)]

The listed improper stopping or parking conduct is connected to the stated fine. The records do not provide further detail about which locations are permitted or any exceptions. [Data: Entities (2142, 2614); Relationships (7139)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The provisions organize the specified violations and penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 7 of Article 6 is described as establishing the 12,000,000 to 14,000,000 VND fine for specified highway stopping and parking violations, and is linked to the broader highway traffic stopping and warning-signal category. [Data: Entities (983, 2142, 2490); Relationships (3541, 3542)]

The information supplied is focused on the rule descriptions, conduct, and penalty. It does not identify an enforcing authority, provide procedural details, or offer evidence about actual compliance or enforcement outcomes.

v.tieu_de: Forced Vehicle Stop and Emergency Parking
v.tom_tat: This community describes a regulatory concept centered on a forced vehicle stop: a technical failure or other force majeure may require a vehicle to stop partly in a traffic lane or in a prohibited parking place. A related entity describes forced parking in those same types of locations. The records define circumstances and locations covered, but do not document a specific incident, enforcement outcome, or vehicle operator. [Data: Entities (2300, 4858, 2299, 5010, 3921); Relationships (7371, 7372, 7370, 7369)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has some traffic-safety relevance because it concerns forced stops in lanes or prohibited parking locations, but the records describe a general circumstance rather than a specific event or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Forced vehicle stop is the central concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around FORCED VEHICLE STOP, defined as a stop required by technical failure or another force majeure, potentially in a traffic lane or a place where stopping or parking is prohibited. Its relationships connect it to the triggering circumstance and both location types, making it the hub of the supplied records. [Data: Entities (2300); Relationships (7371, 7372, 7370)]

The records describe a general regulatory situation; they do not identify a particular vehicle, driver, incident, or resulting injury. [Data: Entities (2300, 4858); Relationships (7371)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical failure or force majeure is the stated trigger
phat_hien.giai_thich:
TECHNICAL FAILURE OR OTHER FORCE MAJEURE is described as an unavoidable circumstance that makes it necessary for a driver to stop and park, including in circumstances covered by the regulation. It is linked both to the forced vehicle stop and to forced parking partly in a lane or prohibited area. [Data: Entities (4858, 2299); Relationships (7371, 7369)]

The material does not specify particular failure types or other examples of force majeure, nor does it establish how frequently such circumstances occur. [Data: Entities (4858)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A traffic lane is one location covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic lane is defined as the portion of the road used for vehicle traffic. The forced-stop description and relationship indicate that the regulation covers a stop that occupies part of such a lane. [Data: Entities (5010, 2300); Relationships (7372)]

Because the defined location is used for vehicle traffic, a forced stop there has potential relevance to road movement. The records do not describe an actual obstruction, traffic disruption, or collision. [Data: Entities (5010, 2300); Relationships (7372)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prohibited parking places are also within scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
PROHIBITED PARKING PLACE denotes a location where parking is not permitted. The forced vehicle stop is linked to this location, and its description specifies that the vehicle may be forced to stop there because of technical failure or other force majeure. [Data: Entities (3921, 2300, 4858); Relationships (7370, 7371)]

The records establish that such locations are included in the described regulatory circumstance; they do not identify a specific place or state what legal consequences apply to an individual stop. [Data: Entities (3921, 2300)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Forced parking is a related but separately represented concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
FORCED PARKING PARTLY IN A TRAFFIC LANE OR IN A PROHIBITED AREA is separately defined as parking required by technical failure or other force majeure. Its relationship to the force-majeure entity connects it to the same triggering circumstance as the central forced-stop concept. [Data: Entities (2299, 4858); Relationships (7369)]

The supplied records do not explain any legal distinction between a forced stop and forced parking. They support treating these as related descriptions, without inferring additional rules, exemptions, or obligations. [Data: Entities (2300, 2299, 4858); Relationships (7371, 7369)]

v.tieu_de: Drivers and Road-Traffic Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around DRIVER, a broad legal and operational entity linked to traffic violations, accident duties, document inspections, penalties, and passenger-safety requirements. Related records describe tunnel maneuvers, forced stops, overweight vehicles, and child passengers, alongside administrative consequences such as fines, licence-point deductions, and possible vehicle and document seizure. A transport business operator is also connected through provision of access to electronic contracts and passenger lists. The material describes rules and penalties; it does not establish that any particular driver committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s broad relevance to road safety and regulatory compliance, while the records describe legal rules rather than evidence of specific misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: DRIVER is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
DRIVER is defined broadly to include people operating road vehicles and is connected to numerous requirements and violations, including accident-scene duties, document inspections, tunnel maneuvers, and load limits. Its high degree and many direct relationships make it the network’s organizing entity. [Data: Entities (1442); Relationships (5998, 5986, 6000, 5958, 5997)]

The description also covers licensing and health conditions, observance of traffic rules, vehicle and passenger safety, and specified records that may contain driver and journey information. These are descriptions of applicable obligations and records, not evidence about an identified individual. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tunnel reversing and turning are separately represented violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify reversing and turning around inside a road tunnel as violations, and group them under a combined reversing-or-turning entity. Article 8, Clause 5 is linked to both individual maneuver entities. [Data: Entities (4208, 4212, 5171, 565); Relationships (9972, 9974, 2636, 2637)]

The descriptions specify a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the stated Article 8, Clause 5 conduct, while the turning-around record separately describes a fine of 800,000 to 1,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for motorcycle, moped, or similar-vehicle drivers. The amounts are presented with different stated scopes and should not be treated as interchangeable. [Data: Entities (5171, 4212, 565)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Accident response duties include stopping and preserving the scene
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The network links drivers to duties to stop immediately after a road accident and preserve the scene when their conduct is directly related to it. Failure to meet either duty is represented as a traffic violation. [Data: Entities (2045, 2012); Relationships (5958, 5955)]

The driver description further notes specified responsibilities following an accident and that provisions may require testing for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants. The records establish these as regulatory provisions, not that an accident or test occurred in a particular case. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Document checks can have administrative consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A driver may be required to present a driving licence, vehicle registration, or other relevant documents during an inspection. The network connects the inspection to the driver and describes possible temporary retention of the vehicle and related documents if required papers cannot be produced. [Data: Entities (5368, 5388); Relationships (6002, 6000)]

The driver description says that, in the described case, a penalty may be avoided by presenting documents or qualifying electronic document information within the stated period. This indicates a procedural qualification, rather than an unconditional consequence for every document issue. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road safety rules address forced stops and load limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a forced-stop violation involving failure to use hazard lights or place a required warning sign, with a stated fine of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng, subject to a specified exception. The driver is identified as the person who may commit this violation. [Data: Entities (2034); Relationships (5957)]

A separate rule concerns operating a vehicle that exceeds a public road’s permitted load limit by more than 10% and up to 20%, unless a valid travel permit applies. The relationship links the overweight operation to the road whose permitted load limit is exceeded. [Data: Entities (3372, 3998); Relationships (5976, 9286)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger and goods transport have specific compliance requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers transporting goods are described as having to arrange and secure loads safely and signal when a load extends beyond the vehicle’s front or rear. Drivers transporting children under 10 years old and shorter than 1.35 meters are subject to seating and safety-device rules. [Data: Entities (1442, 823); Relationships (3208)]

For contract-based passenger transport, the driver description refers to electronic-contract and passenger-list requirements. The linked passenger transport business operator provides equipment for the driver to access those materials; the records do not specify the equipment’s technical design or broader capabilities. [Data: Entities (1442, 3566); Relationships (5980)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalties vary by conduct and include licence-point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community contains several distinct penalty types: monetary fines, a six-point driver’s-licence deduction for the conduct specified in Clause 3, and possible vehicle and document retention during an inspection. The records link the six-point deduction to the referenced Clause 3 conduct but do not identify that conduct in detail here. [Data: Entities (4657, 5586, 5368); Relationships (5993, 10430, 6000)]

A general fine record gives 14,000,000 to 16,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for one set of specified violations following an accident and 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng for listed helmet violations; it explicitly distinguishes these amounts as applying to different violations. [Data: Entities (5041)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory significance, not reputation or actual compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describe statutory provisions, driver obligations, violation categories, and stated consequences. They do not identify a particular driver, document an actual enforcement case, or provide evidence that any named person or operator complied with or breached the rules. [Data: Entities (1442, 565, 5041); Relationships (5998, 6002, 5997)]

Accordingly, the community’s significance is its broad connection to road safety and legal compliance. The supplied material does not provide a basis for assessing an individual’s reputation or for attributing real-world technical capabilities beyond the stated provision of access equipment for electronic contracts and passenger lists. [Data: Entities (1442, 3566); Relationships (5980)]

v.tieu_de: Road Segments Outside Populated Areas and Class IV–VI Roads
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road segments outside populated areas, with Class IV, V, and VI roads identified as included categories. The supplied descriptions associate these roads with potentially adverse driving conditions and traffic-safety risks, including sharp or successive curves, steep gradients, and limited visibility. Populated areas provide the geographic distinction and are separately associated with restrictions on horn use from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., except for priority vehicles. The records describe classifications and potential risks, but do not report specific incidents or compliance outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the records identify potentially significant road-safety hazards across several road classes but provide no evidence of specific incidents or actual harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Roads outside populated areas are the community's central category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around road sections located outside populated areas. The relationship record defines the road segments by that location, while the entity description identifies them as sections including Class IV, V, and VI roads and other roads meeting the referenced technical classification. [Data: Entities (4311); Relationships (9694)]

This category is the hub connecting the geographic distinction with the three named road classes. [Data: Relationships (9694, 3323, 3324, 3325)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Potential driving hazards are explicitly identified
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of roads outside populated areas notes adverse conditions and potential traffic-safety risks, specifically sharp or successive curves, steep gradients, and limited visibility. These conditions indicate possible safety concerns, but the records do not state that a collision or other incident occurred. [Data: Entities (4311)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Class IV, Class V, and Class VI roads are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Each of the three road classes is explicitly linked to the broader category of road segments outside populated areas. The descriptions characterize these classes as among the roads that may have adverse conditions and traffic-safety risks. [Data: Entities (853, 854, 855, 4311); Relationships (3323, 3324, 3325)]

The data establishes inclusion in the described category, but does not provide class-specific hazard measurements, locations, or comparative risk levels. [Data: Entities (853, 854, 855); Relationships (3323, 3324, 3325)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Populated areas serve as the geographic reference point
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Populated areas are described as densely inhabited zones used to distinguish the road segments in this community from roads within those areas. The relationship record likewise specifies that the described segments are located outside populated areas. [Data: Entities (3827, 4311); Relationships (9694)]

This establishes a geographic distinction in the records, but does not identify specific populated areas or road locations. [Data: Entities (3827, 4311); Relationships (9694)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A separate horn-use restriction is noted for populated areas
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The populated-areas description states that horn use is restricted between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m., except by priority vehicles. This is the only explicit behavioral restriction in the supplied records. [Data: Entities (3827)]

The records do not specify enforcement, compliance, penalties, or how this restriction relates operationally to the roads outside populated areas. [Data: Entities (3827, 4311); Relationships (9694)]

v.tieu_de: Preschool and Student Transport Safety
v.tom_tat: This community centers on preschool children and the safety rules governing their transport, including commercial transport and pickup and drop-off services. It links children to drivers, educational institutions, child supervisors, transport operators, required vehicle equipment, and provisions in Decree No. 168/2024/ND-CP. The records describe requirements concerning trained personnel, age-appropriate seats or seat belts, image-recording and child-presence warning equipment, and vehicle paint coloring, alongside specified fines and legal education on road-traffic safety. [Data: Entities (3846, 344, 334, 1727, 2867); Relationships (9716, 9714, 9717, 6596, 8519)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety importance because it concerns the protection of young passengers and sets responsibilities and penalties for multiple transport and education actors.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Preschool children are the community’s central and most exposed population
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Preschool children connect to the transport activities, responsible institutions, drivers, safety violations, and road-safety education represented in the records. This makes their safety the organizing concern of the community rather than an incidental issue. [Data: Entities (3846); Relationships (9710, 9711, 6596, 8519, 9714)]

The records specifically cover children traveling in commercial vehicles and vehicles used by educational institutions for pickup and drop-off. They also identify preschool children as recipients of instruction in road-traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (3846, 2867); Relationships (9710, 9711, 8519)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Educational institutions have explicit safety and coordination responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Educational institutions are described as responsible for ensuring road-traffic order and safety during transportation and for establishing and communicating safe transport procedures. The records also state that institutions must instruct child supervisors in those procedures. [Data: Entities (1727, 818); Relationships (6596, 3190)]

These responsibilities place institutions within the practical safety chain for student transport, alongside drivers and transport operators. The provided information establishes these duties but does not indicate whether any particular institution has complied or failed to comply. [Data: Entities (1727, 818)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver and onboard-manager training is tied to specified penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify as an unsafe practice conducting automobile transport business with a driver or onboard vehicle manager who has not received guidance on safe procedures for picking up and dropping off preschool children or students. Article 26, clause 4, is identified as the provision establishing penalties for this practice. [Data: Entities (5275, 334, 3309); Relationships (1379, 9266)]

The stated fine range is 3,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese dong for individuals and 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese dong for organizations. The records connect transport and support-service operators to this organizational penalty. [Data: Entities (5275, 5089); Relationships (10594)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle equipment and child-seating requirements address distinct safety risks
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described prohibited conduct includes transporting children in commercial vehicles without equipment to record images of them, equipment to warn against and prevent children being left behind, or both. The records distinguish these requirements and also describe a violation involving the absence of both devices. [Data: Entities (5129, 5128, 5131, 5127); Relationships (9714, 9713, 9715, 9712)]

A separate violation concerns commercial vehicles transporting preschool or primary-school children without age-appropriate seats or seat belts. Article 27 is linked to this vehicle-safety violation and to the covered drivers. [Data: Entities (5276, 344, 1542, 3858); Relationships (9717, 6256, 1405)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records specify financial penalties for equipment-related violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For the specified violation involving transport without the required image-recording or child-presence warning and anti-forgetting equipment, the records state fines of 4,000,000 to 6,000,000 Vietnamese dong for individuals and 8,000,000 to 12,000,000 Vietnamese dong for transport business organizations. [Data: Entities (2269, 5093, 5129); Relationships (10597, 7335)]

Article 27 is also described as specifying a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese dong for certain violations by drivers transporting preschool children or students. The supplied records do not specify which individual violations this fine range applies to beyond the cited subsection’s description, so it should not be assumed to apply to every equipment or seating violation. [Data: Entities (344); Relationships (1402, 1405)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle identification and paint-color compliance are part of the regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of the provisions covering preschool and student transport includes vehicle identification requirements, including required paint coloring. A separate entity defines operating a commercial vehicle used for school transport without the required paint color as a violation committed by a driver. [Data: Entities (3846, 1584)]

The records establish that paint-color compliance is addressed, but they do not provide a penalty amount or further details about the required color. [Data: Entities (1584)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety education extends beyond transport personnel
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Legal education on road-traffic order and safety is identified as addressing Article 6 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. The records explicitly include preschool children and students of general education institutions among its recipients. [Data: Entities (2867, 3846, 2383); Relationships (8519, 7598)]

This education component complements the operational requirements imposed on institutions, drivers, and transport operators. The provided information identifies its intended recipients but does not describe curriculum, delivery, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (2867, 1727, 1542)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Education and Safe Moped-Riding Guidance
v.tom_tat: The community combines road-traffic legal-education activities for students and vocational education learners with practical safe-moped-riding guidance for students beginning upper-secondary school. The guidance specifies four riding exercises, while compliance with road-traffic laws is also used as a criterion in student conduct assessments. The records describe educational scope and content but do not establish implementation outcomes or measured safety effects. [Data: Entities (4594, 4378, 5292, 5617); Relationships (10359, 10162, 10163)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it addresses road-safety education and conduct assessment for student populations, although the records provide no evidence of outcomes or safety impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two complementary strands of road-safety education
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes legal education on road-traffic order and safety as well as practical instruction in safe moped-riding skills. These are related educational activities, but the records describe them as separate programs rather than specifying a direct operational link between them. [Data: Entities (4378, 4594)]

The legal-education activities apply to several learner groups, while the riding guidance is directed at students beginning upper-secondary school and includes practical exercises. [Data: Entities (4378, 4594); Relationships (10359, 10162, 10163)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Upper-secondary students are a central audience
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Upper-secondary students are included in road-traffic legal-education activities, and students beginning upper-secondary school are the stated audience for the safe-moped-riding guidance. This makes them the clearest population connecting the two strands of the community. [Data: Entities (5292, 4594, 4378); Relationships (10359, 10162)]

The records establish intended coverage, not how many students participate or whether the instruction changes riding behavior. [Data: Entities (4594, 5292, 4378); Relationships (10359, 10162)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vocational education learners are included in legal instruction
phat_hien.giai_thich: Learners in vocational education institutions are included in teaching activities about road-traffic laws. The provided records do not connect this group to the safe-moped-riding exercises, so their documented role is specifically within the legal-education strand. [Data: Entities (4378, 5617); Relationships (10163)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The riding guidance specifies four practical patterns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The safe-moped-riding guidance includes four exercises: figure-eight riding, straight-line riding, riding over a rough road, and riding through a marked obstacle course. These are described as components of the guidance, not as evidence of a particular certification or proficiency threshold. [Data: Entities (4594, 2092, 4805, 4588, 4250); Relationships (7077, 10358, 10356, 9990)]

The exercise set indicates that the guidance covers several defined riding patterns, but the records do not provide details about assessment procedures, training duration, or results. [Data: Entities (4594, 2092, 4805, 4588, 4250)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Legal compliance is linked to conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic legal-education description states that students’ compliance with road-traffic laws is used as a criterion for assessing conduct. This establishes a documented connection between the educational topic and student conduct assessment. [Data: Entities (4378, 5292)]

The available information does not specify how compliance is observed, what standards are applied, or what consequences follow from an assessment. [Data: Entities (4378, 5292)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Road-Safety Education and the Ministry of Education and Training
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Ministry of Education and Training and its responsibilities for incorporating road-traffic law and safety into education. The Ministry coordinates with other government bodies, including the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs, while educational institutions deliver instruction and manage compliance in school settings. The stated scope includes preschool through upper-secondary education, student conduct assessment, and selected vocational and tractor-operator matters. The data describes statutory responsibilities, not evidence of implementation outcomes or actual compliance rates. [Data: Entities (3011, 3015, 3847, 2382); Relationships (8790, 8792, 8784, 8791)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the Ministry’s broad, formal influence over road-safety education and compliance management across educational settings, rather than evidence of adverse conduct or implementation results.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry is the community’s central coordinating authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Education and Training is connected to the community’s principal activities: developing and integrating road-safety legal content, organizing instruction, overseeing compliance, and coordinating with other ministries. Its central role is established in the description of Article 7 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and reflected in numerous relationships. [Data: Entities (3011, 539); Relationships (2519, 8787, 5813, 8666, 8793)]

The network therefore represents a government-led education and compliance framework. The available records describe assigned duties; they do not establish how consistently those duties are carried out or the results achieved. [Data: Entities (3011, 539); Relationships (8790, 7592, 8795)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inter-ministerial coordination supports curriculum development
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is required to coordinate with relevant ministries and ministerial-level agencies in carrying out its education-related responsibilities. The described work includes developing and incorporating knowledge of road-traffic law into educational curricula. [Data: Entities (3011, 4104); Relationships (8792, 5816)]

The Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs is specifically identified as a partner in developing and integrating road-traffic legal knowledge into curricula. The records also describe coordination concerning vocational institutions and practical safe motorbike-riding instruction, including work with the Ministry of Public Security. [Data: Entities (3015, 3011); Relationships (8784, 8819)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Schools are the primary settings for instruction and compliance management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Preschool and general education institutions are described as settings where road-traffic legal knowledge and safety instruction are incorporated into teaching, and where compliance with relevant laws is managed. The Ministry is assigned responsibility for organizing instruction and overseeing this work across those settings. [Data: Entities (3847, 2382, 3845); Relationships (8790, 7592, 8788, 8666)]

This structure links central policy responsibilities to educational institutions as delivery and oversight environments. The records specify the intended arrangement but do not provide institution-level evidence about enforcement, compliance rates, or educational outcomes. [Data: Entities (3011, 2958); Relationships (7591, 7596, 9718)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The curriculum is intended to cover practical safety and legal consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For preschool children, the described education is age-appropriate and includes safety while walking and travelling in road vehicles, as well as awareness of the dangers and consequences of failing to follow traffic-safety rules. The associated activities are to take place within preschool institutions. [Data: Entities (3847, 4445); Relationships (9720, 9310)]

More broadly, the framework calls for road-traffic legal knowledge and safety content to be developed and integrated into teaching at preschool and general education institutions. The records support the planned subject matter and delivery setting, but do not specify particular teaching materials or measure their effectiveness. [Data: Entities (1354, 4362, 3845); Relationships (5815, 5812, 8795)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student instruction is linked to conduct assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry organizes road-traffic law instruction for primary, lower-secondary, and upper-secondary students. Compliance with relevant traffic laws is also among the criteria used to assess and rank students’ conduct. [Data: Entities (3011, 3857); Relationships (8791, 7595)]

This connects educational content with student conduct assessment, extending the framework beyond classroom instruction. The data does not describe assessment procedures, consequences for students, or actual student compliance. [Data: Entities (3857); Relationships (8791, 7595)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Responsibilities extend to vocational education and specified operator certification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry’s described remit includes developing road-traffic legal instruction for upper-secondary and vocational education, with coordination involving the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs for vocational institutions. The Ministry also works with other authorities on curricula and guidance for practical safe motorbike-riding instruction. [Data: Entities (3011, 3015, 5290); Relationships (8784, 8799)]

Separately, the Minister of Education and Training regulates procedures for specialized vehicle-operation certificates for tractor operators holding specified driving licences. This is a defined administrative responsibility; the records do not provide information about certificate volumes or individual operators. [Data: Entities (3011, 4979); Relationships (8798)]

v.tieu_de: Road Vehicle Stopping and Parking Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on stopping and parking rules under Article 18 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. The rules apply to road vehicle drivers, require signaling when entering or leaving a stopping or parking position, and prohibit stopping or parking in specified locations or where it obstructs road users or obscures signs and signals. A technical incident or other force majeure circumstance may require an exception, subject to warning measures. [Data: Entities (4770, 4506, 4643); Relationships (10279, 10278, 10458)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and traffic-management importance because its rules apply to drivers and address potentially hazardous stopping and parking behavior.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A driver-focused regulatory framework
phat_hien.giai_thich: Stopping and parking is the central subject, and the stated restrictions apply to road vehicle drivers. The description identifies Article 18 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15 as the applicable provision; the records describe rules, not evidence of actual compliance or enforcement. [Data: Entities (4770, 4506); Relationships (10279)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Signals are required during stopping and parking maneuvers
phat_hien.giai_thich: Drivers must signal when entering or leaving a stopping or parking position. The signal is intended to notify other road vehicle drivers, linking the maneuver to communication with surrounding road users. [Data: Entities (4643, 1804, 3465); Relationships (10278, 6731, 9371)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restrictions address obstruction and visibility
phat_hien.giai_thich: The provision prohibits stopping or parking where it would obscure road signs or traffic signals. These restrictions are described as safeguards against obstructing road users or endangering people or traffic. [Data: Entities (4770, 3281, 3282); Relationships (9233, 9234)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specific locations are identified as no-stopping or no-parking areas
phat_hien.giai_thich: Stopping and parking are prohibited at office or organization gates with vehicle access roads, including within five meters on either side. The records also identify the area beneath overpasses as prohibited, except where stopping or parking is specifically permitted. [Data: Entities (146, 5224); Relationships (483, 10459)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency circumstances have specified warning requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich: A technical incident or other force majeure circumstance may require a vehicle to stop or park partly on the roadway or in a prohibited place. In that situation, the driver must use hazard lights or place a warning sign behind the vehicle. The data describe this as a conditional exception with warning measures, not as a general permission to park in prohibited locations. [Data: Entities (4770, 4859); Relationships (10458)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe obligations but not operational outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The supplied information establishes the relevant duties and prohibitions, including signaling, avoiding obstruction, and observing location restrictions. It does not provide information about violations, enforcement actions, collision rates, penalties, or the record of any particular driver or organization; conclusions on those matters are therefore not supported. [Data: Entities (4770, 4506); Relationships (10279, 10278, 483, 9233, 9234)]

v.tieu_de: Student Road-Traffic Safety Education
v.tom_tat: This community centers on students beginning upper-secondary or vocational education and the schools and vocational education institutions responsible for road-traffic education and safe-riding guidance. Families, relevant authorities, and student parent representative boards are connected to the program through instruction, signed safety commitments, reminders, and communication about compliance. The framework also links traffic-law compliance to student conduct assessments and addresses safe student transportation. The supplied records describe educational and compliance responsibilities, but do not establish how consistently they are implemented or measure their outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and institutional importance because it connects student training, family involvement, and educational oversight, although the records describe responsibilities rather than demonstrated outcomes or specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Schools and vocational institutions anchor the framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
High schools and vocational education institutions are assigned central roles in educating students about road-traffic laws and guiding them in safe motorbike riding. Vocational institutions are also described as incorporating relevant knowledge into teaching and assessing students’ conduct partly by their compliance with traffic laws. [Data: Entities (2485, 5616); Relationships (7737, 10477, 10140)]

The links between students and these institutions make education, practical guidance, and compliance monitoring parts of a connected framework. The records specify duties, but do not show whether any particular institution has fulfilled them. [Data: Relationships (7738, 10387, 10464)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Practical riding instruction covers foundational safety skills
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described guidance is intended for students beginning upper-secondary or vocational education. Its stated content includes starting and stopping a motorbike safely, adjusting speed, using vehicle controls and protective equipment, and recognizing or handling dangerous situations. [Data: Entities (4604, 4597, 4598, 38); Relationships (10381, 10382, 84)]

Other guidance described in the records includes mounting and dismounting safely, traffic culture, operator responsibilities, and helping people injured in traffic accidents. These are program topics in the supplied descriptions, not evidence that students have completed training or acquired a particular level of skill. [Data: Entities (4597, 4985); Relationships (10365)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Families and authorities share a supporting role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Students’ families are expected to help ensure compliance with road-traffic safety laws, coordinate with relevant authorities on education and safe moped-riding instruction, and avoid allowing students to operate vehicles unless legally eligible. Families are also expected to remind students about their commitments and communicate with schools about compliance. [Data: Entities (4815, 4101); Relationships (10467, 9882, 9883, 10403)]

This creates a coordination network that extends beyond educational institutions to families and authorities. The records describe the expected collaboration but do not identify specific authorities, individual families, or the results of their involvement. [Data: Relationships (7071, 10289, 10403)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Signed commitments and conduct assessments formalize compliance expectations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Students and their families are described as signing a road-traffic safety commitment, including requirements related to students operating vehicles only when legally eligible. Schools and vocational institutions organize or support these commitments and remind students to honor them. [Data: Entities (4557, 4815, 5616); Relationships (10298, 10299, 10300, 7732)]

Vocational institutions are also directed to include traffic-law compliance among the criteria for assessing and classifying student conduct. The records establish this as an assessment criterion, but provide no assessment results or information about sanctions for noncompliance. [Data: Entities (4807, 4357); Relationships (10140, 10139, 10464)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Student transportation is another safety dimension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of STUDENTS identifies them not only as learners receiving safety instruction but also as passengers in commercial vehicles and vehicles used for school or preschool pickup and drop-off. It notes that cited provisions address vehicle requirements and safe pickup and drop-off, and assigns educational institutions arranging student transportation responsibility for safe pickup and drop-off. [Data: Entities (4811)]

This broadens the community’s safety scope from students’ own riding behavior to their safety as passengers. The supplied records do not provide detailed vehicle specifications or evidence about particular transportation arrangements. [Data: Entities (4811)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied legal references require careful distinction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records associate safe-riding guidance for students with Article 5 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP and identify Article 6 of that decree as addressing responsibilities of high schools and vocational education institutions. [Data: Entities (475, 501); Relationships (2222, 2223, 2340, 2341)]

The entity description for ARTICLE 5 explicitly notes that the label refers to different provisions across multiple legal instruments, including provisions on license or certificate suspensions and other subjects. Accordingly, the shared label alone should not be treated as evidence that those separate provisions govern the student-training program. [Data: Entities (475); Relationships (2226, 2214)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe a framework, not verified compliance or impact
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community data set out intended recipients, institutional duties, instructional topics, family responsibilities, and compliance-related assessment criteria. Together these features indicate a structured approach to student road-traffic safety education. [Data: Entities (4811, 5616, 2485, 4557); Relationships (10477, 7737, 10467, 10140)]

No supplied record reports training completion rates, observed changes in student behavior, traffic incidents, enforcement actions, or institutional audit results. The community’s importance is therefore supported by the scope of its stated responsibilities, while its real-world effectiveness cannot be assessed from this evidence alone.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police and Road-Safety Governance
v.tom_tat: The community centers on the Traffic Police Force and its coordination with road-management authorities and district-level People’s Committees. Its functions span traffic-data systems, speed-setting and sign installation, administrative enforcement, and student motorbike-safety instruction. The supplied records describe statutory responsibilities and operational relationships, but do not establish whether any entity has complied with or breached its obligations. [Data: Entities (5032, 1413, 4292, 1059); Relationships (10041, 5906, 5905)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-service impact because its entities coordinate road-safety decisions, traffic-data operations, enforcement, and student instruction, although the records provide no evidence of misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic Police Force is the community’s central operational actor
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Force has the highest listed entity degree in this community and is associated with several central activities, including speed-setting coordination, student instruction, and management of traffic information systems. [Data: Entities (5032); Relationships (10041, 10049, 10374, 10376, 7730)]

The entity description identifies it under Article 65, clause 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 as carrying out patrol and control activities to maintain road traffic order and safety. It also describes responsibilities for managing and operating the traffic command center and specified traffic databases and systems. [Data: Entities (5032)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Speed decisions and sign installation require inter-agency coordination
phat_hien.giai_thich:
