v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the broad importance of the community’s listed military, security, investigative, and emergency functions, while the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency Military Duties is the community’s central organizing entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Emergency Military Duties is the hub of the community, with connections to a range of operational and security functions. The records describe it as urgent duties performed by military vehicles and identify operational, security, investigative, and counterterrorism missions among the specified scope. [Data: Entities (1767)]

Its links include escorting people, arrests, searches, counterterrorism, other investigative activities, command roles, military control, urgent communications, and convoy protection. This breadth indicates that the community covers multiple types of activity, rather than a single narrowly defined task. [Data: Relationships (6663, 6669, 677, 3994, 6667, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The listed duties include custody-related operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Arrest is described as taking a person into custody, and the entity record says it may be carried out by procuracy-force vehicles on emergency duty. Arrest operations are also linked to Emergency Military Duties as one of the listed duties. [Data: Entities (230); Relationships (677)]

Search is likewise described as an operation that may be performed by procuracy-force vehicles while on emergency duty, and the relationship records include searches among the listed duties. These records establish that arrest and search fall within the described scope; they do not provide information about specific cases, procedures, or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4626); Relationships (6669)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Escorting suspects, defendants, or prisoners is an expressly listed function
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a duty specifically described as escorting suspects, defendants, or prisoners, and this duty is connected to Emergency Military Duties. [Data: Entities (1840); Relationships (6663)]

The relationship records separately identify suspects, defendants, and prisoners as people who may be escorted. The entity record for suspects also refers to arrest or escort, but the provided relationships specifically establish escort links for these groups. [Data: Entities (4827); Relationships (6770, 6769, 5748)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Investigative and counterterrorism activities are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Counterterrorism is described as participation in efforts to prevent or combat terrorism, including police duties focused on countering terrorist threats. It is linked to Emergency Military Duties as an included function. [Data: Entities (1131); Relationships (3994)]

The records also include Other Investigative Activities, defined as police investigative operations other than traffic-accident investigations and distinct from arrests or searches. This establishes investigative work as a separate component of the community’s described scope, without indicating any specific investigation or threat. [Data: Entities (3453); Relationships (6667)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The scope spans command, protection, control, and communications roles
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Several listed duties concern command or coordination: commanding firefighting operations, commanding combat operations, and commanding a marching column. Each is linked to Emergency Military Duties. [Data: Entities (1014, 1013, 1012); Relationships (3590, 3589, 3588)]

Other linked functions include military control, urgent communications, and convoy protection. Collectively, these records show that the described duties extend beyond direct custody or investigative operations to include supporting, protective, and command responsibilities. [Data: Entities (2989, 5300, 1120); Relationships (6664, 6670, 3972)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records do not support a legal-compliance or incident assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material describes duties and their connections but does not identify a jurisdiction, statute, policy text, responsible organization, or process for reviewing compliance. It therefore supports describing the listed scope, but not concluding whether the duties or their implementation comply with applicable law. [Data: Entities (1767, 230, 4626, 1131); Relationships (677, 6669, 3994)]

No specific deployments, outcomes, allegations, or technical specifications are provided. The records consequently do not establish how frequently these functions are performed, what equipment or capabilities are used, or whether any particular operation caused harm. [Data: Entities (1767, 1840, 3453); Relationships (6663, 6667)]

v.tieu_de: Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and Driver Training Facilities
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 39 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, which sets administrative penalties for specified driver-training and driving-test violations. The article is linked to driver training facilities and to provisions within its clauses; the provided information also identifies certain provisions for which traffic police may impose penalties under Article 41. The data describes a regulatory framework and potential fines, but does not establish that any entity committed a violation or indicate its actual compliance status.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns administrative penalties and enforcement affecting driver instructors and training facilities, while the data shows no specific violation or actual enforcement action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 39 is the community's central regulatory entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 39 is the main entity in the community and is described as setting administrative penalties for violations involving driver training and driving tests. Its connections to driver training facilities and to multiple provisions within the article show how the framework is organized. [Data: Entities (427); Relationships (1867, 1871, 1872, 1873, 1874, +more)]

The article description identifies specified conduct by driving instructors and refers to other covered violations, but the supplied information does not provide the full text or all details of every provision. [Data: Entities (427)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified instructor conduct carries fines of VND 2–3 million
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The description of Article 39 states that driving instructors may be fined VND 2,000,000 to VND 3,000,000 for failing to follow the permitted training route or failing to sit beside and assist a learner during practical training. These are stated as penalties for specified conduct, not evidence that an instructor has committed either violation. [Data: Entities (427)]

The same description mentions a screen-display violation but does not specify its details or penalty in the supplied material, so no further conclusion about it can be drawn here. [Data: Entities (427)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver training facilities face higher fine bands for specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Driver training facilities are described as driving schools and other organizations that provide driver training. Under Article 39, the description gives a fine range of VND 10,000,000–20,000,000 for specified Clause 4 violations and VND 20,000,000–30,000,000 for specified Clause 5 violations. [Data: Entities (1496)]

The relationship between the facilities and Article 39 confirms that the article names these organizations among entities subject to fines for specified violations. The data does not identify any particular facility or establish that a fine has been imposed. [Data: Relationships (1867)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community maps multiple provisions within Article 39
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The connected provisions include points in Clauses 1, 3, 4, and 5, a point in Clause 2, and Clauses 7 and 8. The relationships identify these as provisions within Article 39, indicating that the community represents several parts of the article rather than only one penalty provision. [Data: Entities (3792, 3748, 989, 982, 3793, +more); Relationships (1871, 1872, 1873, 1874, 1875, +more)]

The provided descriptions do not give the substantive text of most of these provisions. Their individual requirements or penalties therefore cannot be inferred from their labels alone. [Data: Entities (3792, 3748, 989, 982, 3793, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some listed provisions are identified for traffic-police enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions identify specified provisions of Article 39 as among those for which traffic police may impose administrative penalties under Clause 2 of Article 41. The listed groups include provisions from Clauses 1, 3, 4, and 5, as well as Clause 7, Clause 8, and a point in Clause 2. [Data: Entities (3792, 3748, 989, 982, 3797, +more)]

This establishes a stated enforcement connection, but the supplied information does not describe any enforcement event, investigation, or penalty imposed on a particular person or organization. [Data: Entities (3792, 3748, 989, 982, 3797, +more)]

v.tieu_de: Police, Procuracy, and Military Priority-Vehicle Duties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the POLICE FORCE and legally defined emergency duties, with the PROCURACY FORCE and MILITARY FORCE also connected to urgent missions. Its records describe the use and installation of priority-vehicle signals, including flashing blue and red lights, sirens, and, for military vehicles, a military flag. Police-related duties span arrests, searches, rescue and relief, escorts, security protection, urgent communications, and crowd dispersal. The material describes legal rules and assigned functions, but does not establish whether any specific operation complied with them or document misconduct.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s substantial operational and legal importance across police, procuracy, and military emergency vehicle duties, not evidence of wrongdoing.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police vehicles are the community’s central operational entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The POLICE FORCE has the broadest set of described connections, linking emergency duty and signal installation with multiple operational assignments. The relationships identify police vehicles as performing rescue and relief, crowd dispersal, hostage rescue, escorts, arrests and searches, security protection, and urgent communications. [Data: Entities (3806); Relationships (6648, 9671, 9674, 9673, 571)]

This makes the police force the principal hub in the provided network. The records describe duties and relationships, rather than reporting on a particular incident or evaluating the conduct of a specific officer or unit. [Data: Entities (3806); Relationships (7750, 6767, 678, 9675, 9677)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency duty is the legal and operational link across forces
phat_hien.giai_thich:
EMERGENCY DUTY is described as a legally defined urgent official mission involving vehicles of the military, police, or procuracy forces. Examples include arrests, searches, investigative activities, and other assigned urgent tasks; vehicles performing such duties are treated as priority vehicles under the described signal rules. [Data: Entities (1759); Relationships (6648, 6651, 6645)]

The network connects emergency duty to police, procuracy, and military vehicles, indicating that the priority-vehicle framework is not limited to one force. A separate entry describes emergency duties more generally and notes that applicable provisions may also concern oversized or overweight vehicles, but does not specify the circumstances or outcomes of any particular trip. [Data: Entities (1758); Relationships (6648, 6651, 6645)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signals are a key regulatory focus
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The signal-installation rule specifies a red light on the driver’s left and a blue light on the driver’s right. The records connect this rule to police vehicles used for emergency duties and to procuracy-force vehicles used for such duties. [Data: Entities (3877); Relationships (9671, 9735)]

The descriptions also associate emergency-duty vehicles with flashing blue and red lights and a priority siren. These are descriptions of prescribed signals and their use; the provided data does not verify installation on any particular vehicle or establish whether a specific use was lawful. [Data: Entities (1759, 3887, 3806); Relationships (6648, 6651)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Police assignments include public-order and protective operations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The police-related duties include dispersing crowds causing public-order disturbances and operations against protests or riots. The records also describe security-protection tasks, hostage rescue, and escorting suspects, defendants, or prisoners. [Data: Entities (4003, 189, 4632, 2496, 1838); Relationships (9673, 571, 9675, 7750, 6767)]

These entries indicate a broad range of described police capabilities, including public-order, protective, and custodial functions. They do not provide details about a particular protest, crowd, use of force, or operational outcome, so no conclusion about the conduct or impact of any specific operation is supported. [Data: Entities (4003, 189); Relationships (9673, 571)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Procuracy-force vehicles are included in emergency signal rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The PROCURACY FORCE is described as a Vietnamese law-enforcement body whose vehicles may carry out urgent duties such as arrests, searches, and other investigative activities. Its emergency-duty vehicles are linked to the priority-signal framework, including blue and red lights and a priority siren. [Data: Entities (3887); Relationships (6651, 9735)]

The network separately connects EMERGENCY DUTY with PROCURACY FORCES and identifies other investigative activity as an emergency-duty assignment. Together, these records establish a described role in urgent investigations and signal use, without providing information about a specific case or actual compliance. [Data: Entities (3888, 3454, 1759); Relationships (6651, 6652, 6647)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Military emergency vehicles have a distinct signal description
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The MILITARY FORCE is described as using legally prescribed priority signals during urgent missions or other emergency duties. Its listed signals include flashing blue and red lights, a priority siren, and a military flag. [Data: Entities (2994); Relationships (6645, 8708)]

The URGENT MISSION entry further specifies a flashing red light, a priority siren, and a military flag for a military-force vehicle. The supplied records do not explain the relationship between this wording and the broader description of blue and red lights, so the distinction should not be resolved beyond what each entry states. [Data: Entities (5302, 2994); Relationships (8708, 6645)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other police duties include rescue, escort, and communications
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Police vehicles are described as performing rescue and relief duties in response to road traffic accidents, and as being used for hostage rescue and the escort of suspects, defendants, and prisoners. [Data: Entities (4167, 2496, 1838); Relationships (9674, 7750, 6767)]

The records also identify urgent communications performed by police communications vehicles and traffic-police escort activity to which the priority-signal installation rule applies. These connections show that the described vehicle framework covers support and escort functions as well as direct emergency response. [Data: Entities (5299, 5056); Relationships (9677, 9737)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes rules and duties, not verified compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material consists of entity descriptions and relationships about legal definitions, signal requirements, and assigned duties. It contains no specific allegations, enforcement findings, incident reports, or evidence assessing the reputation of the forces. [Data: Entities (1759, 3877, 3806, 3887, 2994); Relationships (6648, 9671, 6651, 6645)]

Accordingly, the community’s importance can be assessed from the breadth of its described responsibilities and the cross-force signal framework, but the records do not support a conclusion about actual compliance, effectiveness, or misconduct. [Data: Entities (1759, 1758, 3806); Relationships (6648, 6645, 6651)]

v.tieu_de: Driving-License Points, Driving Prohibition, and Restoration
v.tom_tat: This community describes a driving-license points process centered on the license holder. Exhaustion of all points triggers a prohibition on driving under that license; after at least six months, the holder may take a road-traffic rules and safety legal-knowledge examination, and passing it qualifies the holder to regain the full 12 points. The restoration description also identifies a separate route when points have not been exhausted and no further deductions occur for 12 months after the most recent deduction. [Data: Entities (1707, 4187, 3931, 4397, 1900, +more); Relationships (6535, 9454, 6537, 9959, 6536, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate because the community describes rules that affect whether a license holder may drive and how points can be restored, but provides no evidence of a specific violation or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Exhausting all license points triggers a driving prohibition
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The exhaustion event is defined as the deduction of all points from a driving license, and the stated consequence is that the holder may not drive in road traffic under that license. The relationship records explicitly connect point exhaustion with the prohibition. [Data: Entities (1900, 3931, 1707); Relationships (6535, 6837, 6537)]

The provided information describes a restriction tied to the license whose points are exhausted; it does not state that the person is barred from all forms of travel or describe additional penalties. [Data: Entities (1707, 3931, 1900)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: An examination offers a route to restore all 12 points
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A holder whose points have been exhausted may take the road-traffic order and safety legal-knowledge examination after at least six months. Passing with a satisfactory result qualifies the holder to have the full 12 points restored. [Data: Entities (4397, 3595, 4187); Relationships (6536, 9454, 9959)]

The examination is described as being organized by the Traffic Police under the cited law. The supplied data does not identify the law or provide further details about the examination’s administration or content. [Data: Entities (4397)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The restoration description identifies two routes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The restoration entity describes one route for a license that has not lost all its points: no further points must be deducted for 12 months after the most recent deduction. It also describes restoration after the driver passes the legal-knowledge examination, with the applicable route depending on the relevant provision. [Data: Entities (4187)]

The relationships focus on the examination route, while the two-route description is provided in the entity record. The data does not specify which provisions apply in particular cases. [Data: Entities (4187); Relationships (9454, 9959)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The license holder is the central affected party
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The holder connects the key stages: the exhaustion event concerns deductions from that person’s license, the driving prohibition applies to that holder, and the holder may take the examination after the stated waiting period. [Data: Entities (1707, 1900, 3931, 4397); Relationships (6535, 6537, 6536)]

Accordingly, the community describes a sequence of conditions and consequences affecting an individual’s authorization to drive under the relevant license. It does not provide information about particular drivers or actual cases. [Data: Entities (1707, 1900, 3931); Relationships (6535, 6837)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns regulatory process, not documented misconduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied records describe point deductions, a driving restriction, an examination, and routes to restore points. They do not include claims about specific individuals, organizations, violations, or compliance outcomes. [Data: Entities (1707, 4187, 3931, 4397, 1900, +more); Relationships (6535, 9454, 6537, 9959, 6536, +more)]

The information therefore supports assessing the process’s potential importance to driving eligibility and road-traffic safety, but does not support conclusions about reputation, enforcement effectiveness, or the prevalence of point exhaustion. [Data: Entities (1707, 4187, 3931, 4397, 1900, +more)]

v.tieu_de: Ministry of National Defense Priority-Vehicle Signal Equipment
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the Ministry of National Defense’s functional units, which the Ministry directs to manage, install, and use signal-emitting equipment on vehicles assigned to qualifying priority duties. The records define the activities and their connections but provide no technical specifications, compliance information, or operational outcomes. [Data: Entities (2379, 5332, 2956, 2703); Relationships (7586, 7584, 7583)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate institutional importance because it concerns Ministry-directed management, installation, and use of signal equipment on priority vehicles, while the records provide little detail about its scale or effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Ministry functional units are the community’s organizing entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of National Defense directs its functional units in relation to priority-vehicle signal equipment. Those units are linked to all three described activities: use, management, and installation. [Data: Entities (2379); Relationships (7586, 7584, 7583)]

This structure makes the functional units the central connection among the activities in the available records. The records do not identify individual units or describe how responsibilities are allocated among them. [Data: Entities (2379); Relationships (7586, 7584, 7583)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community covers the use of equipment during priority duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Use of priority-vehicle signal equipment is defined as installing and using signal-emitting equipment on vehicles assigned to qualifying priority duties. The definition includes operating the equipment while those vehicles carry out their priority functions. [Data: Entities (5332)]

The Ministry directs its functional units to use the equipment, linking this defined activity to the central government entity in the community. The records do not specify the equipment’s signals, operational procedures, or the vehicles’ particular duties. [Data: Relationships (7586); Entities (2379, 5332)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Management is identified as a distinct activity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records separately identify management of priority-vehicle signal equipment as an activity involving equipment used on priority vehicles. The Ministry directs its functional units to manage that equipment. [Data: Entities (2956, 2379); Relationships (7584)]

No further management processes, oversight arrangements, or performance measures are described, so the scope of this responsibility cannot be specified from the available information. [Data: Entities (2956); Relationships (7584)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Installation is identified separately from management and use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Installation of priority-vehicle signal equipment is listed as its own activity, and the Ministry directs its functional units to perform it. [Data: Entities (2703, 2379); Relationships (7583)]

The records do not explain installation requirements, technical standards, or which vehicles receive equipment. Accordingly, they establish the existence of an installation responsibility but not its detailed procedures or extent. [Data: Entities (2703); Relationships (7583)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The available information establishes responsibilities, not compliance or outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity descriptions and relationships establish Ministry direction over use, management, and installation, and define use in connection with qualifying priority duties. They do not provide information about legal or regulatory compliance, technical capabilities beyond the equipment’s signal-emitting function, or the results of these activities. [Data: Entities (2379, 5332, 2956, 2703); Relationships (7586, 7584, 7583)]

The records therefore support describing the community’s stated responsibilities, but do not support conclusions about whether the activities are compliant, effective, controversial, or associated with particular impacts. [Data: Entities (2379, 5332, 2956, 2703); Relationships (7586, 7584, 7583)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Law 36/2024/QH15, Article 68 and Traffic Police Functions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 68 of Vietnam’s Law 36/2024/QH15 and its connection to two traffic-police functions: directing road traffic and responding to road traffic accidents. The provision is described as authorizing a scene’s direct traffic-police commander to mobilize civilians, vehicles, and equipment in urgent circumstances to protect national security, maintain social order and safety, or prevent ongoing or imminent harm. The records establish these legal and operational connections but do not describe a specific invocation, incident, or compliance outcome.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns emergency legal authority and public-safety functions, while the records provide no evidence of a specific exercise, misuse, or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 68 is the community’s central entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 68 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is the hub of the recorded community, with links to both road-traffic direction and road-traffic accident response. Its described subject is emergency mobilization of civilians, vehicles, and equipment by the direct commander of traffic police at a scene when necessary for specified protective purposes. [Data: Entities (2837); Relationships (8426, 8427)]

The records describe the provision’s authorization and stated purposes, but do not establish how often it has been used or whether any particular mobilization occurred.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Connection to road-traffic direction
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One relationship links Article 68 to road-traffic direction, described as addressing emergency mobilization while traffic police direct and control road traffic. Road-traffic direction is separately identified as an activity covered by Article 68. [Data: Entities (4349); Relationships (8427)]

This supports a connection between the legal provision and traffic-control duties, but does not specify particular procedures, operational capabilities, or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Connection to road-traffic accident response
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The other recorded relationship connects Article 68 with road-traffic accident response, describing emergency mobilization in circumstances where traffic police handle accidents. The entity description likewise identifies accident handling as a duty covered by Article 68 and a circumstance in which urgent mobilization may be needed. [Data: Entities (4330, 2837); Relationships (8426)]

The information indicates a public-safety context for the provision; it does not report a particular accident or document that resources were mobilized in response to one.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Emergency mobilization is described as conditional
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provision’s description frames mobilization as applying in urgent circumstances and when necessary to protect national security, maintain social order and safety, or prevent ongoing or imminent harm to society. [Data: Entities (2837)]

Accordingly, the supplied information presents this authority as tied to stated circumstances and purposes. It does not provide further details about decision-making standards, oversight, or limits beyond that description.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records show legal and operational relevance, not compliance outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community links one legal provision to two traffic-police activities, making it relevant to emergency public-safety functions. [Data: Entities (2837, 4330, 4349); Relationships (8426, 8427)]

No supplied record identifies an alleged violation, adjudication, implementation assessment, or specific event. Therefore, the available evidence supports describing the provision and its stated connections, but not drawing conclusions about compliance, reputation, or actual impact in practice.

v.tieu_de: Competent Authorities and Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Competent Authorities and their role in administering road-traffic rules: they detect and handle violations, notify vehicle owners and other relevant parties, direct corrective actions, and coordinate with functional authorities. The surrounding entities describe the regulatory procedures and remedies involved, including penalties, vehicle-document checks, mandatory cargo removal, and cleanup. The records also assign authorities responsibilities for traffic-management support, legal-knowledge testing, and publication of study materials. The data describes regulatory functions and procedures, not evidence of specific violations or misconduct by the entities involved. [Data: Entities (1041, 5448, 4424, 4530, 2963); Relationships (3694, 3684, 3667, 3663, 3679)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and administrative importance because it encompasses traffic enforcement, penalties, and corrective actions, while the records do not establish specific harmful conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Competent Authorities are the central coordinating entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent Authorities connect the community’s enforcement, notification, remedial-action, and traffic-management functions. The records assign them responsibilities ranging from handling detected violations to giving instructions on cleanup and cargo removal, and coordinating recommendations to functional authorities. [Data: Entities (1041, 2375, 4530, 2963, 2962); Relationships (3684, 3667, 3663, 3659, 3666)]

This concentration of responsibilities indicates broad administrative reach across the described road-traffic processes. The available information documents authorized roles and procedures; it does not establish how frequently they are used or whether implementation is effective.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Enforcement includes notice and case-resolution procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
When a violation is detected without an immediate stop, the described procedure includes notifying vehicle owners and potentially other relevant individuals or organizations, directing them to the office or unit of the authorized penalty official, and seeking to identify the driver. [Data: Entities (4530, 5448, 4103, 1345, 1039); Relationships (3684, 3694, 3677, 3659, 3649)]

This procedure creates an administrative pathway from detection to case resolution. The records describe the process but do not provide examples of cases, notification outcomes, or rates of compliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle owners may face penalties and documentation requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle owners may be subject to procedures and penalties when they commit specified violations or when violations are connected with their vehicles. The listed consequences include fines, driver’s-license point deductions, and revocation of relevant vehicle documents, as provided by the applicable regulations. [Data: Entities (5448, 4415, 4463); Relationships (10212, 10249, 10288)]

A separate provision concerns invalid, altered, or mismatched vehicle registration or inspection documents and specifies fines for the described conduct. The records also state that owners of intelligent traffic vehicles have permit-application and permit-related duties. [Data: Entities (273, 5390, 5448); Relationships (960, 3693)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The violations covered extend beyond driving conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The regulatory-violation category includes improper use of roads or sidewalks, environmental violations, carrying too many passengers, exceeding load or dimensional limits, and failing to secure transported goods. The described provisions apply to individuals and organizations, including owners of certain vehicles. [Data: Entities (4424, 2920); Relationships (10210, 8670, 8607)]

This scope links traffic enforcement with road use, environmental conditions, vehicle capacity, and cargo safety. The records identify categories of conduct and associated procedures, but do not quantify their prevalence or describe particular incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Remedial measures include cargo removal and cleanup
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain load or dimensional violations, authorities may direct that overloaded cargo be removed or oversized cargo unloaded at the place where the violation was detected. [Data: Entities (2962, 2920); Relationships (3666, 8670, 8607)]

The records also describe required cleanup for specified violations, including clearing rubbish, waste, materials, or goods according to competent forces’ instructions. A related description covers hazards and objects such as obstacles, sharp objects, slippery substances, vehicles, machinery, and signs. [Data: Entities (2963, 2964, 1001); Relationships (3667, 8671, 3566, 7577)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Authorities have a traffic-management and corrective-action role
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic police may report deficiencies in road and traffic organization to the relevant authorities, which may recommend corrective measures to functional authorities. The records also describe functional authorities as able to instruct the removal of vehicles, machinery, equipment, signs, or advertisements when a violation is discovered. [Data: Entities (2375, 4140, 1041); Relationships (3663, 3679, 7578, 7577)]

This establishes a coordination route for addressing reported problems as well as particular violations. The data does not specify the deficiencies reported, the recommendations made, or whether corrective measures were completed.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical equipment supports detection and traffic response
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent Authorities and functional forces are described as using professional or smart technical equipment to detect violations, direct and control traffic, and help resolve situations. The violation-handling procedure specifically covers cases where equipment detects an administrative violation and the vehicle is not stopped immediately. [Data: Entities (1041, 4530, 1345, 4454); Relationships (3659, 3683, 3684)]

This indicates an operational technology component to enforcement and traffic management. The records do not identify equipment models, technical performance, data-retention practices, or other details that would support a broader assessment of capability.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Public-facing legal information and testing are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent Authorities are responsible for testing knowledge of road-traffic order and safety laws and making relevant study materials publicly available through an electronic information portal under their management. [Data: Entities (1041, 4004, 4536); Relationships (3676, 3685)]

These functions complement enforcement with information and assessment activities. The available data establishes the assigned responsibilities but does not state how often materials are published, how tests are administered, or what outcomes result.

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police and Road-Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Traffic Police and their road-traffic patrol and control functions. The records describe a legally defined public-safety role spanning traffic direction, vehicle inspections, enforcement, accident response, road-user assistance, and protection of road works and safety corridors. Related entities represent the legal authorities, operational activities, technical equipment, licensing coordination, and escort responsibilities connected to that role. The information indicates substantial public impact, but does not provide performance data, independent reputation assessments, or allegations of misconduct. [Data: Entities (5021, 4410, 1555, 2850); Relationships (10206, 6275, 8430, 8502, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the Traffic Police’s broad, legally defined influence over road safety, enforcement, traffic flow, and emergency response, rather than evidence of adverse conduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A broad statutory role in road safety and traffic control
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police are the central entity in this community, with patrol and control identified as a core activity under Article 65 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. The described work includes monitoring road users, vehicles, traffic conditions, and security along road routes, as well as directing traffic and guiding road users. [Data: Entities (5021, 4410); Relationships (10206, 10208, 9462)]

The records also describe accident investigation and resolution, identification of causes of unsafe traffic conditions, and identification of deficiencies in roads or traffic organization. This breadth makes the community relevant to both everyday road operations and broader traffic-safety administration. [Data: Entities (5050, 2499, 2500, 3601); Relationships (10561, 7752, 7753)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Enforcement powers are described alongside legal and procedural limits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that Traffic Police may stop vehicles when legal grounds apply and inspect compliance with traffic, vehicle, driver, load, and road-safety requirements. They may handle administrative and other legal violations, with patrol and violation-handling procedures prescribed by the Minister of Public Security. [Data: Entities (5021, 5495, 2420, 2419); Relationships (10570, 7667, 7665)]

Administrative sanctioning is linked to assigned functions and duties, including authority described in Clause 2 of Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. These records describe statutory powers and procedures; they do not establish how frequently those powers are used or assess the outcomes of enforcement. [Data: Entities (4340, 915); Relationships (10119, 3403)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle removal and congestion response can affect road users directly
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic Police may arrange the movement of vehicles that obstruct or congest traffic or create an accident risk, including in specified circumstances where a driver or owner is absent or does not comply with instructions. The records assign the Traffic Police responsibility for vehicle safety during removal. [Data: Entities (3187, 2542, 4120); Relationships (9097, 7802, 9904)]

The Traffic Police are also described as taking measures to resolve unexpected congestion and, where traffic order and safety cannot otherwise be ensured, directing or controlling traffic or temporarily suspending traffic on a route. These responsibilities give the agency a direct operational role in managing disruptions, though the records provide no incident-level examples or outcome data. [Data: Entities (5233, 1368, 5021); Relationships (10564, 5840)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical equipment supports inspection and enforcement capabilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe Traffic Police using legally specified systems, vehicles, equipment, and data during patrol and control. Article 71 of Law 36/2024/QH15 is associated with professional technical equipment for checking motor-vehicle loads and detecting or handling load-related violations. [Data: Entities (4410, 2838); Relationships (8430, 10206)]

The Traffic Police are also described as equipped with weapons and support tools under the Law on Management and Use of Weapons, Explosives, and Support Tools. This supports a finding of authorized technical and operational capability, but the supplied information does not detail particular equipment deployments, inventory, or technical performance. [Data: Entities (2850); Relationships (8502)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The role includes infrastructure protection and coordination with other authorities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic Police coordinate with road-management agencies to detect and prevent violations affecting road works and road-safety corridors. The patrol-and-control description also includes efforts to prevent violations of laws protecting these assets. [Data: Entities (4522, 4303, 4410); Relationships (10281, 10048)]

The records further connect Traffic Police notifications about violating vehicles and violators with the Driver’s Licence Issuing Authority, which checks relevant data when issuing, exchanging, or reissuing licences. This indicates an information-sharing link between enforcement and licensing processes. [Data: Entities (1555); Relationships (6275)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Public assistance, escort duties, and emergency mobilization extend the operational remit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Assisting people and vehicles when necessary is identified as part of patrol and control. Traffic Police also investigate and resolve road accidents, and the records describe receiving accident-victim statistics from medical facilities. [Data: Entities (4583, 5050, 5021); Relationships (10205, 10327, 10561)]

The Traffic Police may escort domestic delegations and foreign guests under prescribed procedures. Escort vehicles may use specified priority signals, and a convoy led or guided by a Traffic Police vehicle is identified as a priority convoy. In urgent circumstances, civilians, vehicles, or equipment may be mobilized under the described legal framework. [Data: Entities (1439, 2312, 1119, 843, 5031); Relationships (5943, 7413, 3971, 10563, 3310)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied material establishes responsibilities, not reputation or performance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records primarily describe legal authorities, duties, and relationships among Traffic Police functions. They do not provide performance metrics, public-opinion evidence, independent evaluations, or specific allegations of misconduct, so reputation and real-world effectiveness cannot be assessed from this material. [Data: Entities (5021, 4410); Relationships (10206, 10119, 10570)]

v.tieu_de: Motorcycle and Moped Operators: Registration-Certificate Violations
v.tom_tat: This community concerns motorcycle and moped operators and vehicle-registration-certificate requirements. The operators are linked to three specified violations: using a certificate not issued by a competent authority, one with chassis or engine identifiers that do not match the vehicle, or one that has been erased or altered. The associated penalty is a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records describe the violations and fine but do not provide information about enforcement frequency or broader effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate practical importance because it connects vehicle operators to several defined registration-document violations and a specified fine, but the records indicate no broader impact or enforcement scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Motorcycle and moped operators are the central group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motorcycle and moped operators are the primary covered group in this community. The records describe the provision as addressing operators of motorcycles, mopeds, or similar vehicles in relation to vehicle-condition requirements. [Data: Entities (3152)]

All four listed relationships connect this group to the specified fine or to one of the certificate violations, making operators the structural center of the provided information. [Data: Relationships (9074, 9075, 9076, 9077)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A stated fine applies to specified vehicle-condition violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed penalty is a fine of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified vehicle-condition violations. The relationship record states that the fine applies to operators who commit those violations. [Data: Entities (3650); Relationships (9074)]

The records do not specify additional sanctions, how the fine is calculated within that range, or enforcement outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Certificates must be issued by a competent authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One identified violation is using a vehicle-registration certificate that was not issued by an authority empowered to issue it. The provision identifies this as a violation by the covered operators. [Data: Entities (5312); Relationships (9075)]

The supplied information does not identify the issuing authorities or describe how this violation is detected.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle identifiers on the certificate must match the vehicle
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Another identified violation involves a registration certificate whose chassis number or engine number does not match the vehicle. The relationship record connects this violation to motorcycle and moped operators. [Data: Entities (5313); Relationships (9076)]

The records establish the mismatch as a specified violation but do not provide details about investigation procedures or circumstances.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Erased or altered registration certificates are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Use of an erased or altered vehicle-registration certificate is identified as a separate violation for operators of motorcycles, mopeds, and similar vehicles. [Data: Entities (5319); Relationships (9077)]

This is one of the specified vehicle-condition violations associated with the fine range in the records. The supplied data does not state how alteration is assessed or whether other consequences apply. [Data: Entities (3650); Relationships (9074, 9077)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Document Remediation Procedures
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vehicle Document Remediation, a required remedial procedure for specified violations. It links to three measures: license-plate procedures, vehicle registration procedures, and vehicle inspection certification. The supplied descriptions frame these as administrative steps for exchanging, revoking, newly issuing, or obtaining vehicle documents and certificates; the remediation description excludes cases where the vehicle is confiscated. [Data: Entities (5389, 2901, 5485, 5407); Relationships (10635, 10636, 8582)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low-to-moderate because the records describe a defined vehicle-document remediation process and its component procedures, without evidence of broader impacts or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle Document Remediation is the central procedure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle Document Remediation is described as a required remedial procedure for certain violations. It covers completing procedures involving vehicle registration documents, license plates, or technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificates. [Data: Entities (5389)]

The relationships connect this central procedure to all three of the other procedures in the dataset, making it the organizing entity in this community. [Data: Relationships (10635, 10636, 8582)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The process has a defined exception for confiscated vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description of Vehicle Document Remediation explicitly excludes cases in which the vehicle is confiscated. The data does not specify what process applies in those cases, so no further conclusion about the exception can be drawn. [Data: Entities (5389)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-plate procedures are one component
phat_hien.giai_thich: License-Plate Procedures are described as required in specified cases to exchange, revoke, or newly issue vehicle license plates. The relationship record identifies these procedures as one of the remedial measures specified in clause 19. [Data: Entities (2901); Relationships (8582)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle registration procedures address registration documents
phat_hien.giai_thich: Vehicle Registration Procedures concern exchanging, revoking, or newly issuing vehicle registration documents in specified cases. They are linked to Vehicle Document Remediation as a measure specified in clause 19. [Data: Entities (5485); Relationships (10636)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection certification is another specified remedial measure
phat_hien.giai_thich: Vehicle Inspection Certification consists of procedures to obtain a technical safety and environmental protection inspection certificate for a vehicle in specified cases. The relationship data identifies obtaining this certificate as a measure specified in clause 19. [Data: Entities (5407); Relationships (10635)]

v.tieu_de: Roadway and Sidewalk Use Regulations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on ROADWAY and SIDEWALK, which connect to categories of traffic violations, non-traffic uses, temporary permitted activities, and associated penalties. The records describe restrictions on obstructing traffic, unlawful parking, and other hazardous conduct, while also noting that some temporary uses may be allowed with an authorized plan and approval. They provide regulatory descriptions and penalty examples, not evidence that a particular person or organization committed a violation. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 5334, 2122); Relationships (10329, 10349, 10343, 10341)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects public-space use and traffic safety rules with multiple violation categories and penalties, although the records describe rules rather than specific incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: ROADWAY is the central hub for traffic-use rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROADWAY is the most connected entity in the supplied records, with a listed degree of 54, and links to categories including unauthorized use, obstructive parking, spilled materials, sharp objects, and temporary activities. This makes it the principal organizing concept in the community. [Data: Entities (4585); Relationships (10349, 10343, 10340, 10341, 10328)]

Its description treats the roadway as a public area intended for traffic and identifies conduct that may obstruct or endanger traffic. The records establish the scope of the rules described, but do not show that any listed conduct occurred. [Data: Entities (4585)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: SIDEWALK rules distinguish pedestrian use from other uses
phat_hien.giai_thich:
SIDEWALK is described as a pedestrian walkway, with pedestrians generally required to use it where available and drivers generally prohibited from driving on it. The graph links the sidewalk to improper use, unauthorized parking, driving on the sidewalk, and commercial or production activity. [Data: Entities (4641); Relationships (10416, 10413, 6402, 3593, 7854)]

The records also state that temporary use of a sidewalk for other purposes requires an authorized plan and approval. This reflects a distinction between ordinary permitted use and approved temporary use, rather than a blanket prohibition on every non-pedestrian activity. [Data: Entities (4641); Relationships (10411, 10410, 9692, 4049)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary non-traffic uses are subject to authorization
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify political, cultural, and sports activities as possible temporary uses of roadways or sidewalks, provided the required plan is approved. Article 77 is specifically linked to temporary use and road traffic order and safety. [Data: Entities (555, 3823, 1164, 4746, 4890); Relationships (2585, 10337, 9691, 4048)]

The available information therefore describes a conditional route for such activities, not confirmation that any particular event has obtained approval. The records provide no event-specific application, approval, or compliance evidence. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 4890)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Obstruction and hazardous roadway conduct are prominent concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The roadway-related categories include stopping or parking so as to obstruct traffic, unlawful placement or leaving of obstacles, and gathering three or more vehicles. The roadway description also addresses spilling materials and substances or scattering sharp objects that could create hazards. [Data: Entities (5207, 2381, 4793, 5249, 4747); Relationships (10343, 7589, 10340, 10346, 10338)]

These entries describe prohibited or penalized conduct in the regulatory material; they are not reports of observed incidents. The breadth of these categories indicates that the community covers both traffic flow and physical hazards on public roads. [Data: Entities (4585, 2381, 4747)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records give examples of monetary penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The graph associates fines of 400,000 to 600,000 Vietnamese đồng with gathering three or more vehicles, illegal roadway or sidewalk parking, and stopping or parking to obstruct traffic. [Data: Entities (2122, 2381, 2539, 4793); Relationships (7112, 7113, 7114)]

A separate entry states that scattering sharp objects on a roadway is subject to a fine of 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. These amounts are presented in the supplied descriptions as penalties for specified conduct; the records do not establish that a fine was imposed in any actual case. [Data: Entities (4747); Relationships (10338)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commercial, production, and other non-traffic uses are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify displaying or selling machinery, equipment, or supplies and producing or processing goods on roadways or sidewalks as activities subject to fines. They also include drying agricultural products on a roadway and placing a rice-threshing machine there as listed violations. [Data: Entities (1016, 1721, 3747); Relationships (3592, 6580, 9632)]

These categories illustrate that the rules described extend beyond vehicle movement to the use of public road space for commercial, production, or other purposes. The material does not identify particular businesses, operators, or instances of such conduct. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 1016, 5355)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is regulatory in scope, not an incident or actor network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied entities are primarily public-space concepts, legal provisions, conduct categories, and penalty descriptions. The relationships connect those concepts to ROADWAY and SIDEWALK or link specified violations to fines; no individual, business, enforcement case, or actual event is identified. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 5334, 2122); Relationships (10329, 10349, 10416, 7112)]

Accordingly, the material supports an assessment of the regulatory subjects and their potential public-safety relevance, but not conclusions about a specific party’s legal compliance, technical capability, or reputation. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 555)]

v.tieu_de: Road Conduct Violations and Traffic Obstruction
v.tom_tat: This community concerns two road-related acts described as violations under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 12, Clause 2: lying or sitting on a road while obstructing traffic, and gathering a large number of people on a road without authorization. Both are associated with a stated fine of 200,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong; the relationships identify traffic obstruction as a consequence of the lying-or-sitting act and of an unauthorized gathering. The records describe legal provisions and consequences, not specific incidents or offenders. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510, 2170, 5011); Relationships (7767, 7179, 8644, 7178)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is moderate-low because the records describe conduct that can obstruct road traffic and a specified fine, but provide no evidence of an actual incident, broader effects, or greater penalties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two distinct road-related violations are described
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify lying or sitting on a road in a way that obstructs traffic as a violation, and separately identify gathering a large number of people on a road without authorization as a violation. Both descriptions cite Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Article 12, Clause 2. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510)]

These are descriptions of prohibited conduct, not evidence that either act occurred in a particular place or was committed by a particular person. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic obstruction is explicitly linked to both conduct types
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The relationship records state that lying or sitting on a road causes traffic obstruction and that an unauthorized gathering on a road obstructs traffic. [Data: Relationships (8644, 7767)]

The data does not quantify the obstruction, identify affected roads, or describe resulting delays or other consequences. [Data: Entities (5011); Relationships (7767, 8644)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A fine range is specified for each violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described fine is 200,000 to 250,000 Vietnamese dong. The records link this penalty to lying or sitting on a road while obstructing traffic and to an unauthorized gathering on a road. [Data: Entities (2170); Relationships (7179, 7178)]

The supplied information gives a general penalty range but does not provide details about enforcement, individual case outcomes, or other sanctions. [Data: Entities (2170, 2941, 2510); Relationships (7179, 7178)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community is organized around conduct, consequence, and penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The two conduct entities connect to a shared penalty entity, while each is also linked to traffic obstruction. This forms a compact structure relating the specified acts to both their stated consequence and monetary penalty. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510, 2170, 5011); Relationships (7179, 7178, 8644, 7767)]

No organizations, individuals, enforcement bodies, or other entities are included in the supplied records, so the community provides no basis for assessing specific actors or institutional roles. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510, 2170, 5011)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish a narrow, legal-compliance focus
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material is limited to two specified forms of road conduct, their stated connection to traffic obstruction, and the fine range associated with them. It does not provide information about technical capabilities, reputation, actual compliance behavior, or the frequency of these violations. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510, 2170, 5011); Relationships (7767, 7179, 8644, 7178)]

Accordingly, the community's significance is limited to the described regulatory provisions and potential traffic impact; the records do not support claims about realized harm or wider community effects. [Data: Entities (2941, 2510, 2170, 5011); Relationships (7767, 7179, 8644, 7178)]

v.tieu_de: Roadway Stopping Violation Outside Urban Areas
v.tom_tat: This community consists of a traffic violation—stopping or parking in the traveled portion of a road outside an urban area when a shoulder is available—and the urban-area concept used to define where the rule applies. The supplied description cites Article 9, Clause 1 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and states a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 Vietnamese dong. The data provides no further entities or information about enforcement, legal outcomes, or broader effects.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating is low because the community describes a specific traffic violation and stated monetary fine, with no evidence of broader impact or additional associated activity.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A narrowly defined stopping or parking violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity is a traffic violation involving stopping or parking in the traveled portion of a road outside an urban area when the road has a shoulder, including a wide shoulder. The description defines the conduct and location but provides no information about a particular incident or person involved. [Data: Entities (4790)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The urban-area boundary determines the stated scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: The urban-area entity is included to distinguish the covered road section: the violation is specified as occurring outside an urban area. The relationship links that distinction to the violation, rather than describing a separate event or actor. [Data: Entities (5293); Relationships (10461)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied description cites a specific decree and provision
phat_hien.giai_thich: The violation description cites Article 9, Clause 1 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP as the rule associated with the conduct. The provided data does not include the text of the provision or independent confirmation beyond that description. [Data: Entities (4790)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is a monetary fine
phat_hien.giai_thich: The description says a driver may be fined between 100,000 and 200,000 Vietnamese dong for the violation. It does not specify any additional penalty, enforcement procedure, or outcome in an individual case. [Data: Entities (4790)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community has a simple, limited structure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The data contains two entities and one relationship: the violation and the urban-area concept are connected by the location-based distinction in the rule. No organizations, individuals, technical capabilities, reputational claims, or other associated entities are provided. [Data: Entities (4790, 5293); Relationships (10461)]

v.tieu_de: Roadways, Sidewalks, and Article 12 Temporary-Use Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on roadways and sidewalks, whose temporary use for purposes beyond ordinary traffic or pedestrian passage is regulated by Article 12. The entities distinguish authorized temporary use from unauthorized or improper use, including specified activities such as selling goods or washing vehicles. The relationships connect both public-space types to permitted use and to violations involving missing, expired, or breached permits. The material describes regulatory requirements and penalties, but does not establish that any particular violation occurred.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate civic and compliance importance because it concerns public-space access, traffic safety, permits, and penalties, while the data documents rules rather than an actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Roadways and sidewalks are the community’s central regulated spaces
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Roadways and sidewalks are the primary entities, linked to both authorized temporary use and unauthorized-use conduct. The descriptions establish different ordinary functions—traffic on roadways and pedestrian passage on sidewalks—and state that nonstandard temporary use is regulated under Article 12. [Data: Entities (4587, 4642); Relationships (10353, 10419)]

Their centrality in the supplied relationships indicates that the community is organized around controlling how these public spaces may be used, rather than around a particular person, organization, or documented incident. [Data: Relationships (10353, 10419, 10355, 10421)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Temporary use is permitted when authorized and safety conditions are met
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes temporary use for purposes other than ordinary roadway or sidewalk use as permissible when authorized by competent authorities. The permitted-use descriptions also require maintaining traffic order and safety and restoring the space to its original condition afterward. [Data: Entities (4587, 4642, 4889); Relationships (10353, 10419)]

This distinguishes regulated use from a blanket prohibition: authorization and compliance with applicable conditions are central to the described framework. The records do not identify a specific permit holder or instance of authorized use. [Data: Entities (4587, 4642, 4889)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unauthorized use covers specified commercial and other activities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The unauthorized-use entity identifies market activities, food and drink services, displaying or selling goods, vehicle or equipment repairs, vehicle washing, and placing or hanging signs and advertisements as activities that may constitute violations when undertaken without authorization on roadways or sidewalks. [Data: Entities (5216)]

The relationships connect this violation to both roadways and sidewalks, indicating that the described restriction applies to either type of space. These records define conduct addressed by the rules; they do not show that any listed activity actually took place. [Data: Relationships (10355, 10421)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit status and compliance with permit terms are material
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community separately describes improper temporary use as use without a required permit, use under an expired permit, or use contrary to permit terms. The decree is described as prescribing fines for individuals and organizations engaging in this conduct, although no fine amounts or enforcement cases are provided. [Data: Entities (5205)]

Relationships apply this conduct to both roadways and sidewalks. This makes permit validity and adherence to permit conditions distinct compliance considerations alongside the broader category of specified unauthorized activities. [Data: Relationships (10354, 10420)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated framework links compliance to public order and restoration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For authorized temporary uses, the roadway and sidewalk descriptions require maintaining traffic order and safety and restoring the affected space to its original condition afterward. These requirements indicate that the rules address both safe use during the activity and the condition of the space once use ends. [Data: Entities (4587, 4642, 4889)]

The supplied records do not quantify safety outcomes, describe enforcement capacity, or provide evidence of resulting disruption or damage. Accordingly, the community supports an assessment of regulatory significance, but not a conclusion about actual harm. [Data: Entities (4587, 4642, 5205, 5216)]

v.tieu_de: Article 12 and Vietnam Road-Traffic Rules
v.tom_tat: This community is centered on “Article 12,” a label that refers to provisions in several different Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one unified rule. Its linked topics include speed and safe-distance requirements, seat-belt violations, road and sidewalk use, penalties, road-safety data collection, and a circular’s entry into force. The records also contain differing seat-belt penalty amounts, which they associate with different provisions or potentially different applicable rules; the data does not establish which amount applies in every circumstance. [Data: Entities (243, 2059, 5335, 977, 1810); Relationships (762, 753, 779, 743, 752)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it links road-safety duties, enforcement penalties, and data collection, while the records do not establish broader impacts beyond those regulatory topics.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 is a cross-reference, not a single unified provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity description explicitly cautions that “Article 12” refers to different provisions depending on the legal instrument. Its listed subjects include penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, speed and safe-distance rules under Law 36/2024/QH15, road-safety database information under Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, and entry into force under Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT. [Data: Entities (243); Relationships (752, 743, 744, 754)]

Accordingly, the connected topics should be interpreted in the context of their respective instruments. Treating every linked duty or penalty as part of one Article 12 would misstate the supplied information. [Data: Entities (243)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety duties include speed, distance, and driving conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records associate Article 12 of Law 36/2024/QH15 with compliance with speed regulations and safe distance between vehicles. They also specify that operators of specialized motorcycles must observe speed limits and maintain a minimum safe distance from the vehicle ahead. [Data: Entities (243, 3419, 1076); Relationships (762, 744)]

Clause 3 is also linked to observing road conditions and reducing speed in specified circumstances. The provided descriptions do not detail those circumstances, so the scope of these actions cannot be further specified here. [Data: Entities (3283, 4048); Relationships (761, 765)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Roadway and sidewalk misuse is a recurring enforcement topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Several linked entities describe using roads, roadways, or sidewalks for purposes other than their intended traffic-related use. The records associate this conduct with Article 12 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and identify it as subject to penalties. [Data: Entities (5335, 5333, 5338, 5336, 4586); Relationships (779, 777, 781, 780, 770)]

The repeated entries appear to describe overlapping forms of the same general subject—use of roadways or sidewalks for other purposes—rather than distinct organizations or actors. No specific instances of misuse are provided. [Data: Entities (5335, 5333, 5338, 5336, 4586)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Seat-belt penalty records give different amounts and legal contexts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One relationship says Article 12 specifies a fine of VND 350,000 to 400,000 for failure to wear a seat belt in a moving car. The associated entity separately describes a VND 800,000 to 1,000,000 fine under Article 6 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and notes that the lower amount may reflect an earlier or otherwise different applicable regulation. The source data therefore presents different amounts and does not establish a single amount applicable in all cases. [Data: Entities (2059); Relationships (753)]

A separate violation concerns a driver transporting a passenger who is not wearing a provided seat belt; its description states a fine of VND 800,000 to 1,000,000. The linked record also describes that range as the fine imposed for the violation. [Data: Entities (1510, 2579); Relationships (6161, 6162)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records include several penalty amounts but do not fully map them to violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 12 description cites a VND 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 fine for an individual committing one of the specified violations. A linked penalty entity repeats that range, but the supplied relationship does not identify the particular violation to which it applies. [Data: Entities (243, 2190); Relationships (754)]

Other linked entities report VND 500,000 to 1,000,000 fines for individuals and VND 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 fines for organizations for specified violations. The records do not provide enough detail here to reconcile these ranges or assign each to a specific conduct. [Data: Entities (2265, 2267); Relationships (756, 757)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 references also connect to road-safety data collection and cargo rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that information specified in Clause 7 of Article 11 is collected for the Database on Road Traffic Order and Safety, and connect that collection to Article 12 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. They also state that specialized motorcycle operators’ health information may be held in the driver health database. [Data: Entities (977, 3419); Relationships (743)]

Separately, Article 12 is cited in connection with violations of regulations for securing transported goods, with the entity description noting that such violations are addressed in connection with Article 47. The data does not supply further detail about the information collected or the cargo-securing requirements. [Data: Entities (243, 2597); Relationships (758)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The supplied evidence supports regulatory significance, not a reputation assessment
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is primarily a network of legal references, traffic duties, enforcement amounts, and related conduct. Its centrality is reflected by Article 12’s links to numerous topics, but the supplied records do not identify an individual or organization responsible for violations, document actual incidents, or assess public reputation. [Data: Entities (243); Relationships (762, 753, 779, 743, 744)]

The material therefore supports assessing the community as relevant to understanding road-traffic compliance and enforcement, but not drawing conclusions about compliance outcomes, institutional performance, or reputational standing.

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Violations and Related Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS and connects several kinds of transport-related breaches—including load and dimension limits, improper securing of goods, and passenger overcapacity—to corrective measures and supplementary penalties. The records describe excess-cargo removal requirements and possible suspension of a vehicle’s operating insignia, but do not establish that any specific violation occurred or that a penalty was imposed. [Data: Entities (4565, 2970, 1077, 4841, 3560); Relationships (3378, 3888, 7852, 6828, 9436)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes rules and consequences relevant to transport safety and regulatory enforcement, although the records do not document actual incidents or enforcement actions.

phat_hien.tom_tat: ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS is the central category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS is the hub linking multiple specific breaches to provisions and consequences. Its description covers improper road or sidewalk use, environmental-protection violations, passenger overcapacity, load or size limits, and failure to secure transported goods; it also states that Article 12 prescribes fines and supplementary penalties, including driving-license point deductions. [Data: Entities (4565)]

The relationships connect this category to supplementary penalties, compulsory unloading, improper securing of transported goods, and breaches of load and dimension limits. This establishes a broad regulatory structure, but does not show that any particular breach or penalty occurred. [Data: Relationships (3378, 3888, 7852, 6828, 6826)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Excess cargo can trigger corrective removal
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe corrective measures requiring excess-weight cargo to be unloaded or cargo exceeding permitted dimensions to be removed, as directed by competent authorities. They also connect specified load-limit and dimensional violations to MANDATORY REMOVAL OF EXCESS CARGO. [Data: Entities (2970, 1871); Relationships (6827, 6813)]

A separate node, COMPULSORY UNLOADING OF EXCESS GOODS, describes removal at the place where the violation is detected and is linked to the wider road-traffic-violation category. The supplied information does not clarify whether the two corrective-measure labels represent distinct procedures or overlapping descriptions. [Data: Entities (1077); Relationships (3888)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Load, dimension, and cargo-securing breaches are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community identifies exceeding vehicle or road load limits and exceeding vehicle or road dimension limits as covered violations. It separately defines improper securing of transported goods as a violation of transport requirements and links it to ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS. [Data: Entities (1885, 1884, 2609); Relationships (6828, 6826, 7852)]

These categories concern different aspects of carrying goods: permitted weight, permitted dimensions, and securing the load. The records establish that these matters fall within the described regulatory framework, but provide no details about particular vehicles, affected parties, or resulting harm. [Data: Entities (4565, 1885, 1884, 2609)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Supplementary penalties may include insignia suspension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
CLAUSE 18 OF ARTICLE 32 is linked to ROAD-TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS and is described as providing supplementary penalties for specified violations. The associated suspension provision concerns the right to use a vehicle’s operating insignia and sets a period of one to three months, if the vehicle has one. [Data: Entities (897, 4841); Relationships (3378, 3379)]

The records describe a possible legal consequence, not an actual suspension. They do not identify a specific case, vehicle, or determination by an authority. [Data: Entities (897, 4841)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Severe passenger overcapacity is linked to insignia suspension
phat_hien.giai_thich:
PASSENGER OVERCAPACITY EXCEEDING 50% is defined as carrying more than 50% above a vehicle’s permitted passenger capacity. Its relationship to SUSPENSION OF VEHICLE OPERATING INSIGNIA states that this breach can result in suspension for one to three months. [Data: Entities (3560, 4841); Relationships (9436)]

This provides a specific example of a violation linked to a supplementary penalty within the wider framework. The records do not indicate that such overcapacity occurred or that the potential suspension was applied in any actual case. [Data: Entities (3560, 4565, 4841); Relationships (9436)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Road Inspections and Administrative Sanctions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on inspections and administrative sanctioning of road-traffic violations under Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Road inspectors are authorized to inspect transport operators and several transport-related facilities and service providers, and may impose penalties for specified violations within their authority. The network connects the inspection framework to bus stations, parking areas, rest stops, transport units, and transport-support service providers; the supplied entity data also states a fine range for a specified violation by such service providers. [Data: Entities (2679, 4283, 5114); Relationships (2906, 7961, 7962, 7963, 7964, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes an enforcement framework spanning multiple road-transport settings and including administrative penalties, although the supplied data does not establish the frequency or outcomes of enforcement.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulatory inspection and sanctioning framework is central
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity describes activity under Article 41 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP: inspections concerning road transport and related facilities, during which designated officials may sanction specified administrative violations affecting road-traffic order and safety. This makes the community primarily about public regulation and enforcement, rather than a private organization or a single event. [Data: Entities (2679)]

The framework is linked to transport units, bus stations, parking areas, rest stops, and transport-support service providers as inspection locations. [Data: Relationships (2906, 7961, 7962, 7963, 7964)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road inspectors are the operational enforcement actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road inspectors, including people assigned specialized road-inspection duties, are described as able to impose specified administrative penalties while conducting inspections or checks. Their remit includes transport operators, bus stations, parking areas, rest stops, and transport-support service providers. [Data: Entities (4283); Relationships (2907, 9405, 9958, 10023, 10024)]

The data also connects inspectors directly to the general road-inspection and checking activities described in the decree. It does not specify staffing levels, inspection frequency, or enforcement outcomes. [Data: Relationships (10022)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspections cover multiple transport facilities and organizations
