They do not provide evidence of a specific inspection facility’s compliance status, an actual enforcement action, or the reputation of any establishment or inspector. [Data: Entities (441, 5408, 5414, 1990); Relationships (1957, 1962, 1963)]

Accordingly, the community is relevant for understanding the regulatory exposure of vehicle inspection activities, but the information provided is insufficient to assess actual technical capability or the conduct of any particular entity.

v.tieu_de: Testing and Certification Establishments: Personnel and Penalties
v.tom_tat: The community centers on testing and certification establishments that assess motor vehicles, specialized-use motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts during production, assembly, or importation. Its regulatory focus is the assignment of qualified personnel: assigning an unqualified person to testing or certification, inspection, or professional staff duties is identified as a violation. Clause 3 of Article 40 prescribes a fine of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND for covered establishments committing specified violations. The information describes the rules and activities but does not establish that any particular establishment has violated them. [Data: Entities (4907, 598, 3077, 933); Relationships (2747, 2743, 3446)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns regulated vehicle and component certification, personnel qualifications, and a specified financial penalty, although no actual violation is identified.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Establishments are the community's central entities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Testing and certification establishments are the hub connecting the regulated activities, personnel-related violation, fine, and recognition and designation processes. Their description places them in testing and certification during manufacture, production, assembly, or importation. [Data: Entities (4907); Relationships (10509, 10510, 10511, 10512, 9840)]

The source describes recognition and designation as part of the certification process. These relationships show the community's institutional and regulatory structure, but do not identify specific establishments or their compliance status. [Data: Entities (4907, 4043, 1343); Relationships (9840, 5796)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulated scope spans vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and parts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The establishments carry out testing and certification for motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts. The stated context includes production, assembly, or importation, making the community relevant across several product categories and stages. [Data: Entities (4907, 4908, 4909, 4910); Relationships (10510, 10511, 10512)]

The records characterize these as activities regulated by Article 40, including the requirement that personnel meet applicable conditions. They do not provide technical procedures, testing results, or details about individual products. [Data: Entities (4908, 4909, 4910); Relationships (10510, 10511, 10512)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Personnel qualification is the key compliance issue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified violation is assigning people who do not meet required qualifications or conditions to perform testing or certification. The relationship records link this violation directly to covered testing and certification establishments. [Data: Entities (598, 4907); Relationships (2747)]

The violation also includes assigning an unqualified person to act as a motor vehicle inspector or professional staff member. The records define the prohibited assignment but do not state that any particular person or establishment has done so. [Data: Entities (598, 3118, 3910); Relationships (2745, 2746)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40, Clause 3 prescribes a monetary penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The stated fine for covered establishments committing the specified violation is 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND. The data links that penalty both to the unqualified-personnel assignment and to testing and certification establishments. [Data: Entities (3077, 4907); Relationships (9007, 2743)]

Clause 3 of Article 40 is identified as prescribing this fine. The source provides the penalty range, but no enforcement record, assessment, or payment information for a specific establishment. [Data: Entities (933, 3077); Relationships (3446)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Recognition and designation form part of the certification context
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Recognition and designation of testing and certification establishments are identified as activities connected to those establishments and as part of the technical safety and environmental protection certification process. [Data: Entities (4043, 1343, 4907); Relationships (9840, 5796)]

These records establish the procedural context but do not specify criteria, outcomes, or the status of any individual establishment. Accordingly, they support an overview of the regulatory structure, not a conclusion about a particular entity's authorization or compliance. [Data: Entities (4043, 1343, 4907); Relationships (9840, 5796)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Traffic Violations and 1–2 Million Đồng Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on a prescribed fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng, linked to several categories of traffic violations: driver-image recording device offenses, passenger pickup or drop-off in prohibited locations or on obstructed-visibility curves, and operation of a specialized motorcycle outside its prescribed scope. The records also connect specific ambulance device failures and data falsification to the fine. The material describes regulatory obligations and penalties, but does not establish actual violations by any particular person or organization, enforcement outcomes, or broader compliance levels. [Data: Entities (2125, 1528, 4794, 3331); Relationships (6211, 7118, 7121, 7120, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high practical importance because it links multiple traffic-safety and transport-compliance requirements to a defined monetary penalty, while providing no evidence of a specific incident or wider impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single fine connects multiple categories of traffic offenses
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a fine of 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The records associate this range with driver-image recording requirements, passenger pickup or drop-off conduct, and operating a specialized motorcycle outside its prescribed scope. [Data: Entities (2125, 1528, 4794, 3331); Relationships (6211, 7118, 7121, 7120, +more)]

This makes the fine a useful organizing point for the community, but the records do not provide evidence about how frequently the penalties are imposed or the deterrent effect of the amount.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-image recording requirements cover device and data integrity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described driver-image recording violations include operating specified transport vehicles without a required device, participating in traffic with a nonfunctioning device, and falsifying recorded data. The records connect these device-related violations to the fine and associate them with Clause 3 of Article 21. [Data: Entities (1528, 924); Relationships (6211, 3433)]

The records also identify three ambulance-specific examples: failure to install the device, a device that does not function in traffic, and falsification of its data. Each is linked to the same fine range. [Data: Entities (1981, 3269, 2079, 2125); Relationships (6936, 7117, 7065)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger pickup and drop-off restrictions are a distinct offense group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes pickup or drop-off where stopping or parking is prohibited, as well as pickup or drop-off on a curve with obstructed visibility. The records associate both types of conduct with the stated fine, with an exception noted for the curve-related description. [Data: Entities (4794, 3739, 3737, 2125); Relationships (7121, 7120, 9625, 9626)]

Two entity records describe prohibited-place pickup or drop-off in overlapping terms, and another relationship connects the curve-related description with the broader prohibited-place violation entity. The available data therefore indicates related or overlapping descriptions, but does not fully specify how they are legally distinguished. [Data: Entities (4794, 3739, 3737); Relationships (9625, 9626)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized-motorcycle use is included in the penalty network
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Operating a specialized motorcycle outside its prescribed scope is described as a violation under Article 16 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and is linked to the 1,000,000–2,000,000 đồng fine. This is a separate conduct category from the device and passenger-service violations. [Data: Entities (3331, 2125); Relationships (7118)]

The supplied records do not explain which activities fall outside the prescribed scope, so the precise operational boundary cannot be assessed from this information alone.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records associate the fine with more than one statutory provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity describes the amount as prescribed under Clause 5 of Article 20 for specified violations, and a separate entity identifies Paragraph 5 of Article 20 as specifying the range for listed contract-based passenger transport violations. [Data: Entities (2125, 3527); Relationships (7119)]

For driver-image recording offenses, the records also connect Clause 3 of Article 21 to the same fine and to the device-violation category. These are the provisions as represented in the supplied data; the material does not independently verify the statutory text or explain the full scope of each provision. [Data: Entities (924, 1528, 2125); Relationships (3433, 3434, 6211)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes rules and penalties, not specific enforcement events
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe prohibited conduct, device requirements, statutory references, and a fine range. They do not identify a particular driver, transport operator, enforcement action, court decision, or documented incident. [Data: Entities (2125, 1528, 4794, 3331); Relationships (6211, 7121, 7118)]

Accordingly, this community supports an assessment of the regulatory topics represented and their stated penalty, but not conclusions about actual compliance, an individual’s legal status, enforcement frequency, or reputational impact.

v.tieu_de: Article 40 and Motor Vehicle Inspection Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 40 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its regulation of motor vehicle, specialized-use vehicle, motorcycle, and parts inspection. The provision connects inspection activities and inspectors with testing, certification, and inspection facilities, and describes financial penalties for specified violations. The supplied data identifies fines of VND 10–15 million and VND 16–20 million, including a condition involving at least two inspectors penalized under Clause 1 within 12 months. It describes regulatory provisions and potential penalties, but provides no evidence of a particular facility’s violation or compliance status. [Data: Entities (436, 439, 3111, 3119, 5501); Relationships (1917, 1920, 1933, 1913, 9041)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it covers a broad, regulated vehicle-inspection sector and specifies substantial financial penalties, although no actual violation or enforcement event is identified.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40 is the community’s regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40 is the central entity, linking the covered inspection activities, inspectors, facilities, and penalty provisions. Its stated role is to establish rules governing inspection activities and penalties for violations, so the community is structured around a regulatory framework rather than a named organization or incident. [Data: Entities (436, 3111); Relationships (1917, 1920, 1933, 1922, 1921)]

The data refers to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP but does not provide the full text of the provision, independent legal analysis, or information about enforcement outcomes. Conclusions here are therefore limited to the described scope and penalties. [Data: Entities (436, 439)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulation covers several inspection domains
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described scope includes motor vehicles, specialized-use vehicles and motorcycles, and motor-vehicle parts or components. The data separately identifies specialized motorcycle inspection, specialized-use vehicle inspection, and parts inspection as activities covered by Article 40. [Data: Entities (3111, 4700, 4720, 3128); Relationships (1923, 1924, 1921)]

This breadth connects the provision to multiple types of inspection work, but the records do not quantify the number of affected facilities, inspections, or vehicles. [Data: Entities (3111, 4700, 4720, 3128)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Testing and certification facilities are subject to specified penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40, Clause 3 is described as setting penalties for listed violations by vehicle testing and certification facilities. The covered facilities test or certify vehicles, specialized motorcycles, or their components during production, assembly, or import. [Data: Entities (5501, 436); Relationships (1933, 9032, 9746)]

The records also describe a fine of VND 10–15 million for specified facility violations. They do not identify any particular facility that has committed a violation or received a fine. [Data: Entities (436, 3644); Relationships (9508)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A repeated inspector-penalty condition can trigger a facility fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data states that a testing or certification facility may face a VND 10–15 million fine when at least two inspectors have been penalized under Clause 1 within 12 months of the first such penalty. Clause 1 is identified as the basis for the inspector penalties counted by this condition. [Data: Entities (864, 3644, 3119, 5501); Relationships (1902, 3339, 9041, 9508)]

This creates a described link between penalties imposed on inspectors and potential liability for a facility. The supplied records do not establish that the condition has been met by any inspector group or facility. [Data: Entities (3119, 5501, 3644); Relationships (9041, 9508)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The data also identifies a VND 16–20 million penalty range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate entity describes Clause 5 of an Article 40 penalty provision as imposing a fine of VND 16–20 million for specified violations, and a relationship links that range to vehicle inspection facilities. [Data: Entities (439, 2273, 5409); Relationships (1913, 7342)]

The supplied records also describe a VND 10–15 million range for specified facility violations, but do not fully explain how the two ranges differ or which precise violations map to each range. The ranges should therefore be reported as separate descriptions in the data, without inferring their application beyond what is stated. [Data: Entities (436, 439, 3644, 2273); Relationships (1913, 1931, 7342)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory exposure, not proven noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships characterize applicable activities, facilities, penalty conditions, and fine ranges. They do not name an offending facility, document an investigation or enforcement action, or establish that any violation occurred. [Data: Entities (436, 5501, 5409, 3644); Relationships (1933, 1931, 9508, 7342)]

Accordingly, the community indicates potentially meaningful compliance obligations for the covered inspection sector, but the available information is insufficient to assess any individual entity’s actual compliance, reputation, or technical performance. [Data: Entities (3111, 3119, 5501, 5409)]

v.tieu_de: Article 20 Clause 5 Passenger-Transport Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Clause 5 of Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and the VND 1,000,000–2,000,000 fine associated with specified passenger-transport violations. The provisions cover required driver-image recording equipment, passenger pickup or dropoff at unauthorized locations, and carrying luggage or goods beyond a vehicle’s designed load capacity. Related entities describe particular equipment failures and identify passenger-vehicle drivers as the people whose conduct is addressed. The information establishes a regulatory framework, but does not document actual violations, enforcement outcomes, or organizational reputation. [Data: Entities (958, 2236, 300, 3588); Relationships (3508, 1108, 9448)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes concrete traffic-safety and passenger-transport compliance requirements, although the data records rules rather than actual violations or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 5 is the central organizing provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 5 of Article 20 is the main hub connecting the listed conduct to the stated fine, including equipment-related violations, unauthorized passenger pickup or dropoff, and excess loads. It is identified as a subdivision of Article 20 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP. [Data: Entities (958, 300); Relationships (1108, 3508, 3502, 3510, 3019)]

Article 20 is described as setting penalties and driving-license point deductions for drivers of passenger cars and similar vehicles who violate traffic order and safety rules. The supplied records do not specify any particular point deduction for the Clause 5 violations, so no specific deduction can be established here. [Data: Entities (300, 958)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty is VND 1,000,000 to VND 2,000,000
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The fine entity gives a range of VND 1,000,000 to VND 2,000,000, and Clause 5 is linked to that penalty for the specified violations. The records also connect the range to the driver-image equipment violation and unauthorized passenger pickup or dropoff. [Data: Entities (2236, 958); Relationships (3508, 6215, 7296)]

This is a stated administrative monetary penalty in the supplied descriptions. The data does not provide information about case-specific factors, enforcement frequency, or whether this range has been applied in any particular case. [Data: Entities (2236); Relationships (3508)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Driver-image equipment compliance has several distinct failure modes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The driver-image recording equipment violation applies to qualifying passenger cars with at least eight passenger seats, excluding the driver’s seat, when used for passenger transport. The described violation includes missing required equipment, equipment that fails to function or record/store data properly, and altered or falsified equipment data. [Data: Entities (1529, 1982, 2082, 2662); Relationships (3502, 6213, 6214, 6216)]

Clause 5 links failure to install, ineffective equipment, and falsification of data to the VND 1,000,000–2,000,000 fine. These records describe compliance requirements and penalty categories; they do not establish that a particular driver or operator committed any of these violations. [Data: Relationships (3504, 3505, 3509, 6937, 7067, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger pickup and dropoff must follow the applicable contract or designated locations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Unauthorized passenger pickup or dropoff is described as picking up or dropping off passengers somewhere not permitted by the passenger transport contract, or on a route with designated pickup and dropoff locations. The records identify this as conduct concerning passenger-vehicle drivers and connect it to the Clause 5 fine. [Data: Entities (5208, 3588, 2236); Relationships (3510, 7296, 9448)]

Clause 8 of Article 20 is specifically referenced as an exception to the pickup-or-dropoff violation described under Clause 5. The provided data does not give the substance of that exception, so its precise scope cannot be assessed from these records. [Data: Entities (985, 5208); Relationships (3546, 3510)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Exceeding a vehicle’s designed load capacity is also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct includes carrying luggage or goods in a vehicle beyond its designed load capacity. The entity description states that this violation is subject to a fine of VND 1,000,000 to VND 2,000,000, and the relationship data connects it to Clause 5. [Data: Entities (734, 958, 2236); Relationships (3019, 3508)]

This category concerns load capacity rather than the driver-image recording or passenger-location requirements. The records provide no incident details or evidence of an actual overloaded vehicle. [Data: Entities (734); Relationships (3019)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support regulatory analysis, not conclusions about actual compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied information identifies legal provisions, types of conduct, and stated penalties. It does not identify named operators, specific enforcement actions, observed violations, or outcomes, so it cannot establish the compliance status of any particular person or organization. [Data: Entities (958, 2236, 1529, 5208, 734); Relationships (3508, 3502, 3510, 3019, 6215)]

Clause 9a is separately connected to the driver-image equipment violation and is described as specifying fines for organizations and individuals that own certain vehicles. The available records do not provide its penalty amounts or enough detail to determine how it relates in practice to the Clause 5 fine. [Data: Entities (997); Relationships (3563)]

v.tieu_de: Motor Vehicle Inspection and Decree 168/2024/ND-CP
v.tom_tat: This community centers on motor vehicle inspection facilities and the regulated inspection activities they perform. Article 40, Clause 4 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is linked to the facility and to penalties for specified noncompliant inspections, certificate issuance, and motorcycle or moped emissions inspections. Other connected violations include inspecting vehicles that should be refused, failing to update required vehicle records, and improperly issuing modification certificates. The information describes regulatory duties and potential penalties, not evidence that a particular facility has violated them. Inspection data is also described as part of a road-traffic database managed by the Ministry of Transport, with a separate Ministry of Public Security database for specified vehicles.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it concerns vehicle inspections, compliance records, and enforcement, although the data establishes potential violations rather than actual misconduct.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection facilities are the operational center of the community
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility is connected to motor vehicle inspection as the entity conducting the regulated activity, and to multiple categories of conduct that may attract penalties. These links make facilities the principal point where inspection procedures, certificate decisions, refusal rules, and recordkeeping requirements converge. [Data: Entities (3116, 3110); Relationships (9025, 1972, 7830, 7976, 7036)]

The facility description includes inspections of motor vehicles and specialized-use vehicles, as well as possible motorcycle and moped emissions inspections. It also states that facilities are responsible for following applicable laws and technical procedures and issuing certificates only when authorized. [Data: Entities (3116, 3110); Relationships (9037, 9040)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework identifies multiple classes of punishable inspection conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40, Clause 4 is associated with penalties for inspections that do not comply with applicable requirements, and is linked to inspection certificate issuance, motorcycle and moped emissions inspections, and specialized-use motorcycle inspections. The supplied information characterizes these as regulatory violations when performed contrary to applicable regulations, standards, or technical requirements. [Data: Entities (443, 2685, 3147, 4716); Relationships (1970, 1971, 1973, 1974)]

The data describes the applicable rules and consequences; it does not identify a specific facility that committed any of these violations. Accordingly, the community indicates compliance exposure rather than a substantiated record of wrongdoing. [Data: Entities (443); Relationships (1972)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several facility violations carry stated fines of 10–15 million Vietnamese đồng
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied descriptions state that fines of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng apply to listed facility violations. Examples include inspecting a vehicle despite conditions requiring refusal, failing to update required vehicle records, and improperly issuing a modification certificate. [Data: Entities (2600, 2580, 1078, 2050, 3076); Relationships (7842, 3890, 7036, 7830, 9006)]

The facility description also identifies assigning unqualified people to specified duties as conduct that may be fined within this range. These provisions underscore the importance of staffing and procedural controls, but the data does not establish that any facility has incurred a fine. [Data: Entities (3116, 2580)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection records are part of a government-managed information system
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor vehicle inspection information is included in the road traffic database. The Ministry of Transport is described as responsible for constructing and managing the specialized database for vehicle-inspection activity, excluding military and police vehicle data. [Data: Entities (3110)]

Inspection information for motor vehicles and specialized vehicles used by the People’s Public Security is described as covered by a separate database managed by the Ministry of Public Security. This division of database responsibility is a significant administrative feature of the inspection system. [Data: Entities (3110)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Refusal decisions and recordkeeping are key facility controls
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility is required to refuse inspections when regulatory conditions require refusal, and inspecting a vehicle despite those conditions is identified as a punishable violation. This links frontline inspection decisions directly to enforcement exposure. [Data: Entities (3116, 1078); Relationships (3890, 3889)]

Facilities are also required to maintain and update vehicle records as specified; failure to update those records is described as a violation subject to a 10,000,000-to-15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng fine. Together, the refusal and recordkeeping provisions emphasize procedural and administrative controls alongside technical inspection. [Data: Entities (3116, 2050, 2580); Relationships (7036)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community concerns road-safety regulation, but contains no case-specific enforcement evidence
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor vehicle inspection is defined as examination of vehicles and components according to applicable procedures and technical standards, and the described rules address inspections contrary to those requirements. This gives the community public-safety and compliance significance. [Data: Entities (3110, 443); Relationships (1971, 9025)]

However, the records provided describe duties, violations, and potential penalties rather than named facilities, specific enforcement actions, or confirmed inspection failures. The available evidence therefore supports assessing the importance of the regulatory framework, not concluding that a particular entity is noncompliant. [Data: Entities (3116, 3110, 443)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Modification and Registration Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle modification and the associated requirement to change registration certificates and license plates. The rules also identify changes to vehicle paint color, purpose of use, or an organization’s or individual’s name or identification number as triggers for registration changes. Inspection records and modification data must be stored in accordance with regulations, and improper storage is described as punishable by a fine. The information describes regulatory requirements and a potential violation, but does not establish that any violation occurred. [Data: Entities (5427, 792, 2616, 787, 790, +more); Relationships (3138, 7861, 3135, 3136, 3131)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it concerns vehicle registration and inspection-record compliance, including a stated monetary penalty, but provides no evidence of an actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle modification is linked to registration and plate changes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Vehicle modification is defined as an alteration or conversion that changes a registered or imported used vehicle’s type under competent-authority rules. Depending on the vehicle type and applicable requirements, the modification may need to be declared in advance and requires changes to the vehicle’s registration certificate and license plates. [Data: Entities (5427)]

The registration-change procedure is explicitly connected to vehicle modification, making registration documentation a central compliance consideration in this community. [Data: Entities (792); Relationships (3138)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection records and modification data have storage requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The provided description states that related inspection records and data must be stored in accordance with regulations. It also says the relevant database information includes details of the vehicle both before and after modification. [Data: Entities (5427)]

Improperly storing files, documents, or data concerning vehicle inspections or modifications is identified as a violation. The relationship specifically connects that violation to vehicle modification, but the data does not indicate that a particular person or organization committed it. [Data: Entities (2616); Relationships (7861)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Improper storage carries a specified administrative fine
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed penalty for improper storage of vehicle inspection files, documents, or data is a fine of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. This makes records management a significant compliance issue within the community. [Data: Entities (2616)]

The source describes a potential sanction, not an assessment or payment of a fine in any specific case. No actual enforcement action or violation is provided. [Data: Entities (2616)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several other vehicle changes trigger registration updates
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The registration-change procedure also covers changes to vehicle paint color, vehicle purpose of use, and an organization’s or individual’s name or identification number. Each is listed as a circumstance requiring a change to the registration certificate and license plates. [Data: Entities (787, 790, 791, 792); Relationships (3131, 3135, 3136)]

These related triggers show that the community’s registration requirements extend beyond vehicle-type modifications to other specified changes in vehicle status or registered identity. The data does not describe additional requirements beyond the stated certificate and plate changes. [Data: Entities (792); Relationships (3131, 3135, 3136)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The community describes a regulatory framework, not specific actors or incidents
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships concern regulatory concepts and procedures: vehicle modification, registration changes, categories of changes that require updates, and improper storage of inspection records. They do not identify a specific vehicle owner, organization, inspection facility, or enforcement case. [Data: Entities (5427, 792, 2616, 787, 790, +more); Relationships (3138, 7861, 3135, 3136, 3131)]

Accordingly, the information supports an assessment of compliance obligations and potential consequences, but not a conclusion about the reputation, conduct, or compliance status of any particular person or organization. [Data: Entities (5427, 792, 2616)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Testing and Certification Establishments
v.tom_tat: This community centers on establishments that test and certify motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and vehicle parts in production, assembly, and importation contexts. Its relationships connect those activities to an Article 40, Clause 3 provision, a specified documentation-related violation—failure to publicly post required procedures—and a fine of 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND. The available information describes a regulatory framework, not evidence that a particular establishment committed the violation. The Article 40, Clause 3 entity also notes that the same clause number refers to separate provisions in two Vietnamese legal instruments.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it concerns regulated vehicle testing and certification and a defined monetary penalty, while the supplied records do not document an actual violation or broader impact.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Establishments form the community's operational center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity covers establishments that test and certify motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, and motor vehicle parts during production, assembly, or importation. The relationships connect these establishments to the relevant operating contexts and testing and certification activities. [Data: Entities (5369, 3901, 769, 4916); Relationships (1968, 9748, 3084, 10515)]

The records describe the scope and roles of the establishments but do not identify any individual organization or establish that a particular establishment failed to comply. [Data: Entities (5369); Relationships (7002, 1968)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40, Clause 3 is linked to the establishments and the penalty
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied relationships state that Article 40, Clause 3 applies to testing and certification establishments operating in production, assembly, or importation contexts, and that it sets a fine for specified violations. [Data: Relationships (1968, 1966, 9748)]

The entity description cautions that this clause number refers to provisions in two separate Vietnamese legal instruments: one described as setting monetary penalties under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and another as addressing service-life limits under Law 36/2024/QH15. These are described as separate provisions and not as contradictory. [Data: Entities (442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Publicly posting procedures is a stated compliance requirement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify failure to publicly display required testing and certification processes and procedures as a punishable violation for covered establishments. The violation is connected to both testing and certification activities. [Data: Entities (2022); Relationships (1965, 7001, 3083)]

The information establishes a compliance obligation and describes the violation category; it does not show that any establishment in the community actually failed to post the procedures. [Data: Entities (2022, 5369); Relationships (7002, 1965)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fine is 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The specified monetary penalty for the listed violations by vehicle and parts testing and certification establishments is 10,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND. The relationships specifically connect that range to failure to publicly post the required procedures and to Article 40, Clause 3. [Data: Entities (2132); Relationships (7000, 1966)]

The penalty is evidence of a defined regulatory consequence, not evidence that a fine was imposed on a named establishment. [Data: Entities (2132, 5369); Relationships (7000, 1966)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The regulatory scope covers inspection, testing, and certification activities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes motor vehicle and specialized motorcycle inspection, alongside testing and certification of vehicles and parts. The records connect these activities to establishments covered by the relevant regulatory provision. [Data: Entities (3089, 4916, 769, 5369); Relationships (9013, 10515, 3084)]

This scope makes the community relevant to oversight of vehicle-related activities, but the supplied information does not describe technical methods, inspection outcomes, safety incidents, or the performance of any establishment. [Data: Entities (3089, 4916, 769)]

v.tieu_de: Vehicle Inspection Facilities and Administrative Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on vehicle inspection facilities and the regulatory consequences associated with inspection and certification violations. Article 40, clause 4 connects non-compliant vehicle inspections, non-compliant motorcycle emissions inspections, and unlawful refusal of inspection services with a fine of VND 16,000,000–20,000,000. Other records describe a VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 fine for covered establishments and monetary penalties linked to certain vehicle-operation violations. The data describe regulatory categories and penalties, not a specific facility or confirmed violation. [Data: Entities (5410, 952, 2131, 2585, 5244); Relationships (3480, 3481, 3482, 3483, 7129, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high regulatory importance because it covers vehicle inspection compliance and substantial administrative fines, but the records do not identify a specific operator or confirm an actual violation.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle inspection facilities are the community’s central regulated entities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is a general category of establishment that inspects motor vehicles, specialized motorcycles, or vehicle parts. Its description states that it is subject to Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and may face penalties for specified conduct, including improperly refusing inspections or mishandling inspection or vehicle-modification records. [Data: Entities (5410)]

The facility is linked to both monetary penalties and the unlawful-refusal violation, making it the hub of the regulatory relationships in this community. These records establish regulatory exposure, not that any particular facility committed an offense. [Data: Relationships (7129, 7834, 10623)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40, clause 4 covers several inspection-related violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 4 of Article 40 is associated with non-compliant vehicle inspection and certification, non-compliant motorcycle or moped emissions inspection, and unlawful refusal to provide inspection services. [Data: Entities (952, 3252, 3251, 5244); Relationships (3482, 3481, 3483)]

The records describe these as conduct subject to the clause’s penalty. They do not provide case-specific evidence that any of the violations occurred. [Data: Relationships (3481, 3482, 3483)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated Article 40 penalty is VND 16,000,000–20,000,000
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records specify a fine in this range for inspection facilities committing the listed violations under Article 40, clause 4. The fine is connected to non-compliant vehicle inspection and certification, non-compliant motorcycle emissions inspection, and unlawful refusal of inspection services. [Data: Entities (952, 2239); Relationships (3480, 3481, 3482, 3483)]

This amount should be understood as a prescribed penalty associated with specified conduct, rather than a fine shown as having been imposed on an identified facility. [Data: Entities (952, 2239)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Penalty ranges vary across the regulatory records
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A separate entity describes a VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 fine for covered establishments that conduct testing or certification contrary to regulations; a relationship also links that penalty range to vehicle inspection facilities committing a listed violation. [Data: Entities (2131); Relationships (7129)]

The monetary-fine entity separately describes a VND 10,000,000–12,000,000 range for violations under Article 13, clause 7, and VND 16,000,000–20,000,000 for unlawful refusal of inspection services. These ranges are presented for different stated provisions or conduct and should not be treated as interchangeable. [Data: Entities (2585, 5244); Relationships (3480, 10623)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Unlawful refusal is specifically connected to inspection facilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define unlawful refusal as a vehicle inspection facility refusing to provide inspection services contrary to law. The violation is linked both to the facility category and to Article 40, clause 4. [Data: Entities (5244, 5410, 952); Relationships (10623, 3483)]

The monetary-fine information associates unlawful refusal with a VND 16,000,000–20,000,000 penalty. This identifies the potential regulatory consequence but does not document an actual refusal or enforcement action. [Data: Entities (2585, 2239); Relationships (3480, 3483)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The network also includes vehicle-operation violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The monetary-fine entity is linked to operating a temporarily registered vehicle beyond permitted conditions or period, and to operating a restricted-use vehicle beyond its authorized area, route, or time. [Data: Entities (2585, 3336, 3325); Relationships (7833, 7832)]

These links broaden the community beyond inspection-facility conduct to include traffic violations. The supplied relationships do not specify a precise fine amount for either operation violation, so no particular amount can be assigned to them from these records. [Data: Relationships (7833, 7832)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal exposure, not a named operator or confirmed case
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The facility is described generically, and the associated records define violations, provisions, and potential monetary penalties. They do not identify an individual inspection facility, describe a specific incident, or state that a penalty was imposed. [Data: Entities (5410, 952, 2131, 2585, 5244)]

Accordingly, the community is useful for understanding the regulatory framework and possible consequences, but it does not by itself establish non-compliance by any particular operator. [Data: Entities (5410); Relationships (3480, 3481, 3482, 3483, 10623)]

v.tieu_de: Automobile Driver Transport Violations and Sanctions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on automobile drivers and rules governing the transport of dangerous, oversized, or overweight goods. Its relationships describe administrative violations and possible consequences, including fines, driving-license point deductions, circulation-permit withdrawal, and environmental remediation when a violation causes pollution. The records describe regulatory provisions and potential penalties; they do not establish that a particular driver committed a violation or that any pollution event occurred. [Data: Entities (630, 5562, 5570, 5149, 2427); Relationships (2820, 2821, 2819, 2812, 262)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to road safety, hazardous-goods handling, environmental remediation, and meaningful administrative penalties, while the records describe rules rather than confirmed incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Automobile drivers are the central regulated actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community is organized around the automobile driver, linked to violations involving dangerous-goods transport and oversized or overweight cargo, as well as related penalties and possible remediation obligations. These links indicate that the records concern compliance duties and consequences for drivers, rather than a named company or specific individual. [Data: Entities (630, 5562, 5570); Relationships (2820, 2821, 2815)]

The material does not identify a particular driver, vehicle, or actual enforcement case. It therefore supports analysis of the regulatory framework, but not a conclusion that a specific person has violated it. [Data: Entities (630, 5562); Relationships (2820, 2821)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods violations include conduct after transport ends
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One specified violation is failing to clean a vehicle or remove its hazardous-goods warning symbol after hazardous-goods transport has ended. The records characterize this conduct as an administrative violation under Article 23 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (2427, 1952); Relationships (2814, 6903)]

The stated fine for this violation is 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The dataset does not provide evidence of a particular fine being imposed or a specific vehicle failing to meet the requirement. [Data: Entities (2104, 2427); Relationships (7093)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods rule breaches may carry license consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records describe sanctions and driving-license point deductions for automobile drivers who violate dangerous-goods transport rules, including violations associated with Clauses 4 and 5 of Article 23. These are stated as potential or prescribed consequences, not as evidence of a specific driver losing points. [Data: Entities (5562, 4615); Relationships (2815, 10401, 2820)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized or overweight cargo rules impose permit requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes transporting oversized or overweight goods without a valid circulation permit, with an expired permit, or with a permit not issued by a competent authority. The records associate this conduct with a stated fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (5149, 5570); Relationships (2819, 2821)]

For the violation addressed under Article 22, the records also describe possible driving-license point deductions and withdrawal of an expired or unauthorized circulation permit, in addition to other penalties. They do not establish that any permit was actually withdrawn or that a particular driver was penalized. [Data: Entities (101, 5641, 5570); Relationships (262, 263, 10699)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Environmental remediation is conditional on pollution
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records state that the specified dangerous-goods transport violation may cause environmental pollution. If pollution results from the administrative violation, the responsible person must carry out corrective measures to remedy it. This is a conditional obligation; the data do not report an actual pollution incident or completed remediation. [Data: Entities (1819, 1825, 5562); Relationships (6745, 6749, 6744, 2812)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Evidence concerns regulatory obligations, not reputation or technical capability
phat_hien.giai_thich: The available records describe driver-related transport violations, statutory penalties, and a conditional environmental remedy. They provide no information about an identified organization’s reputation, operational or technical capabilities, or history of compliance. Accordingly, no assessment of those attributes, or of actual enforcement outcomes, can be grounded in this dataset. [Data: Entities (630, 5562, 2427, 5149, 5570); Relationships (2820, 2819, 6749, 10699)]

v.tieu_de: Article 22 Oversized-Load Transport Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and rules for automobile drivers transporting oversized or overweight goods. It links three permit-related violations—transporting without a circulation permit, with an expired permit, or with an unauthorized permit—to a fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong. Clause 3 is associated with that fine and a four-point driver's-license deduction; the data also states that violations under Clause 2 result in the same deduction. The records describe regulatory consequences, not specific incidents or drivers.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it describes substantial financial and driving-license consequences for specified transport violations, but provides no evidence of actual incidents or broader effects.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22 is the regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is described as addressing penalties and driving-license point deductions for automobile drivers who violate rules on transporting oversized or overweight goods. Its recorded links connect it to Clause 3 and to each of the three permit-related violations, making it the organizing provision in this community.

The records establish a regulatory framework; they do not identify a particular driver, transport operator, enforcement action, or real-world violation. [Data: Entities (321, 5571); Relationships (1261, 1262, 1263, 1264)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Three permit-related violations are identified
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The listed conduct includes transporting oversized or overweight goods without a circulation permit, with an expired permit, or with a permit not issued by a competent authority. Article 22 is linked to each of these violation categories. [Data: Entities (5148, 5146, 5147); Relationships (1262, 1263, 1264)]

The records characterize these as violations addressed by Article 22, but do not provide details about particular shipments, the circumstances of violations, or how frequently they occur. [Data: Entities (321, 5146, 5147, 5148)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 3 carries a monetary penalty of 13–15 million Vietnamese dong
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 3 of Article 22 is associated with a fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 Vietnamese dong for its listed permit-related violations. The fine is separately linked to transporting without a circulation permit, using an expired permit, and using an unauthorized permit. [Data: Entities (925, 2145, 5146, 5147, 5148); Relationships (3435, 7144, 7145, 7146)]

The supplied information gives a fine range but does not explain how an amount within that range is selected or whether other penalties may apply. [Data: Entities (2145, 925)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A four-point license deduction is linked to Clauses 2 and 3
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that violations specified in Clause 3 result in a four-point deduction from the driver's license. They also state that violations specified in Clause 2 result in the same deduction. [Data: Entities (2363, 909, 925); Relationships (3436, 3396)]

The supplied description of Clause 2 does not specify the underlying conduct, so the scope of its violations cannot be detailed from these records. [Data: Entities (909, 2363); Relationships (3396)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence describes rules, not actual compliance or organizational capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships concern a decree, clauses, penalties, and defined categories of transport violations. They do not identify named individuals or organizations responsible for violations, nor do they record enforcement outcomes or confirmed cases. Accordingly, this community supports an assessment of the stated legal consequences, not a conclusion about any person's or organization's compliance. [Data: Entities (321, 5571, 5146, 5147, 5148); Relationships (1261, 1262, 1263, 1264)]

The supplied records also contain no information about technical capabilities, reputation, or operational practices of a transport entity. [Data: Entities (321, 925, 2145, 5146, 5147)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Transport Penalties and Article 22
v.tom_tat: This community centers on car drivers and Article 22 provisions governing transport-related conduct. The entities connect oversized or overweight cargo transport to administrative penalties and driving-license point deductions, and dangerous-goods transport through certain tunnels to a stated fine and a four-point deduction for specified conduct. Article 22 also refers to a separate provision about permits for signal devices on priority vehicles. The records describe regulatory requirements and consequences, not a particular driver’s conduct or a specific enforcement event. [Data: Entities (695, 320, 323, 1229, 2366); Relationships (1245, 1272, 2954, 2958, 7563)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s meaningful regulatory and road-safety relevance, while the records identify rules and penalties rather than a specific incident or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Car drivers are the central regulated actors
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The car driver is the network’s central entity, linked to Article 22, transport activities, violations, penalties, and license-point deductions. These connections show that the community primarily concerns driver obligations and consequences under transport regulations. [Data: Entities (695); Relationships (1245, 1272, 2954, 2964, 2965)]

The records describe possible penalties for specified conduct; they do not identify a particular driver or establish that any violation occurred. Accordingly, the network supports an assessment of regulatory exposure, not a finding of individual noncompliance. [Data: Entities (695, 5020); Relationships (2964, 2968)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized and overweight cargo is a major regulatory theme
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 22 is linked to violations involving the transport of oversized or overweight cargo, and the records state that these violations can lead to penalties and driving-license point deductions. The regulated transport activity also includes compliance with circulation-permit requirements. [Data: Entities (5575, 3507, 5105); Relationships (1260, 1269, 1276, 2961)]

The network connects the driver directly to the cargo-transport violation and to a traffic penalty, indicating that responsibility is framed around the driver carrying out the regulated activity. It does not supply details about permit procedures or any specific cargo movement. [Data: Entities (695, 5020); Relationships (2964, 2965, 2968)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 22 refers to provisions in two separate decrees
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description distinguishes Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning penalties and license-point deductions for certain car cargo violations, from Article 22 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, concerning permits to use signaling devices on priority vehicles. [Data: Entities (320, 323)]

The relationship records also connect the general Article 22 entity both to cargo-related violations and to the license for priority-vehicle signal devices. This is an important interpretive distinction: the shared article number does not mean the two provisions address the same subject. [Data: Relationships (1255, 1260, 1259)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specified cargo violations carry distinct stated monetary penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For certain violations under Clause 1 of Article 22 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, the supplied entity description gives a fine range of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Entities (323)]

A separate relationship associates the general Article 22 entity with a fine range of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 VND, but the supplied records do not specify which exact violations this range applies to. The two stated ranges therefore should not be treated as interchangeable or assigned to a particular offense beyond what the records establish. [Data: Entities (2147); Relationships (1254)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods transport through qualifying tunnels has significant consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify a violation involving a car driver transporting specified dangerous goods through tunnels at least 100 metres long, with a stated fine of 6,000,000 to 8,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1229, 2102); Relationships (2954, 2957)]

A separate relationship states that conduct specified in Clause 5 carries a four-point deduction from the driver’s license, in addition to the applicable penalty. The records do not provide further detail on the dangerous goods or identify an actual incident. [Data: Entities (2366); Relationships (4205)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Priority-vehicle signaling permits are a separate administrative topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 22 description for Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP concerns permits to use signaling devices on priority vehicles, including issuance and return of permits and permits subject to revocation. The permit may be issued in paper or electronic form and uses Form No. 02a in Appendix II. [Data: Entities (320, 2359, 2897)]

The network links Form No. 02a to the license for using signal devices on priority vehicles. This material concerns permit administration and is distinct from the driver penalties for cargo transport described under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Relationships (1255, 7563); Entities (320)]

v.tieu_de: Article 37 Vehicle Compliance and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 37 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP and its related provisions on vehicle compliance and penalties. The entities connect Article 37 to Clause 4, which prescribes a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for specified violations. The same fine is linked to failure to perform assigned duties during vehicle inspection and certification. Article 37 also describes a separate fine range for driving a foreign-plated vehicle without required approval or a permit. The records describe regulatory requirements and penalties, but do not document particular enforcement actions or cases.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it describes concrete vehicle-compliance duties and financial penalties, while providing no evidence of a specific incident or enforcement action.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 37 is the central regulatory reference
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 37 of Decree 168/2024/ND-CP is the community's central entity. Its description covers penalties for drivers of road motor vehicles bearing foreign license plates and also refers to other specified violations. Clause 4 is explicitly identified as part of Article 37. [Data: Entities (416, 950); Relationships (1766)]

The information therefore provides a regulatory framework rather than evidence that any named driver or organization has committed a violation. No particular enforcement event is included in the records. [Data: Entities (416, 950)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Foreign-plated vehicles require the specified approval or permit
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 37 provides for a fine of 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng when a driver operates a foreign-plated road motor vehicle in traffic in Vietnam without the required written approval or permit from a competent authority. [Data: Entities (416)]

This establishes a specific compliance condition for the described driving activity; the records do not identify a driver, vehicle, or instance in which the condition was breached. [Data: Entities (416)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 4 is associated with a higher fine range
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 4 of Article 37 is described as specifying a fine of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for certain traffic violations. Its description includes driving a right-hand-drive car without the required convoy and support or traffic guidance. [Data: Entities (950, 2227); Relationships (1766, 3477)]

The relationship records connect Clause 4 to the stated fine, and connect Clause 4 to Article 37. The data does not provide further detail about how the penalty is applied in individual cases. [Data: Relationships (1766, 3477)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The same fine is linked to failures in inspection and certification duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Failure to perform assigned duties is defined as not properly carrying out responsibilities in the certification or inspection of motor vehicles, specialized motor vehicles, or motor vehicle parts. The records link this failure to vehicle inspection and certification activity. [Data: Entities (2010, 5405); Relationships (6988)]

A separate relationship states that the 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng fine applies to individuals who commit this violation. The records do not specify an individual or document an actual failure. [Data: Entities (2227); Relationships (6987)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The penalty structure covers distinct described violation contexts
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe both a 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng penalty for operating a foreign-plated vehicle without required written approval or a permit and an 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng penalty associated with specified violations. [Data: Entities (416, 2227, 950)]

The higher fine is linked in the data both to Clause 4 and to failure to perform assigned inspection or certification duties. These records do not establish that the situations are the same violation; they present separate descriptions connected to the stated fine. [Data: Entities (2010, 2227, 950); Relationships (3477, 6987)]

v.tieu_de: Article 34 Vehicle Violations and Penalties
v.tom_tat: This community centers on administrative traffic violations under Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, including oversized and overloaded vehicle operation and tracked-vehicle road use on public roads. The relationships connect these violation types to penalties and driver’s licence point deductions; the records also identify possible bridge or road damage, passenger-carrying motor vehicles within the provision’s scope, and a two-point deduction for specified violations. [Data: Entities (108, 3508, 3487, 4977, 5018); Relationships (307, 311, 306, 310, 305, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns public-road safety, potential infrastructure damage, and regulatory penalties, but the records describe legal provisions rather than a specific incident or actor.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 34 is the community’s regulatory center
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central entity is an administrative traffic violation involving an over-dimensioned or overloaded vehicle, or a tracked vehicle, on a public road, as addressed by Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Its connections to the violation categories and penalty framework make the provision the organizing focus of this community. [Data: Entities (108); Relationships (307, 311, 310, 306)]

The records describe categories covered by a regulation; they do not identify a particular driver, enforcement action, or real-world incident. [Data: Entities (108, 3508, 3487, 4977)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized vehicle operation is a prominent violation category
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Oversized Vehicle Operation refers to using a public road with a vehicle that exceeds permitted size or dimensional limits and is described as covered by Articles 31 and 34. The relationships specifically connect this category to Article 34 penalties and licence-point deductions. [Data: Entities (3508, 5018); Relationships (307, 9390)]

A separate relationship connects oversized operation to the two-point deduction provision, which applies to violations specified in the referenced clauses. [Data: Entities (5183); Relationships (9391)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Overloaded vehicles are also covered
phat_hien.giai_thich: Operating a vehicle whose load exceeds permitted weight limits on a public road is identified as an Article 34 violation. The records link this category to the broader administrative-violation entity and to the penalties and licence-point-deduction framework. [Data: Entities (3487, 108, 5018); Relationships (306, 9381)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tracked-vehicle road use has associated penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Tracked Vehicle Road Use refers to operating or circulating a tracked vehicle on public roads, which the records identify as a traffic violation addressed by Article 34. It is connected to the penalties and licence-point-deduction framework. [Data: Entities (4977, 5018); Relationships (310, 10529)]

The records also link tracked-vehicle road use to the two-point deduction provision for specified violations addressed in the article. [Data: Entities (5183); Relationships (10530)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A two-point licence deduction applies to specified violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The two-point deduction is described as applying under Article 34, Clause 7, to violations described in Clause 1, Clause 3, or Point a of Clause 4. The records connect this provision to oversized vehicle operation and tracked-vehicle road use. [Data: Entities (5183, 3508, 4977); Relationships (9391, 10530)]

The supplied information identifies the specified clauses and point deduction but does not establish that every violation category in the community automatically receives this deduction. [Data: Entities (5183); Relationships (9391, 10530)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Bridge or road damage is identified as a possible consequence
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community includes an entity describing damage to a bridge or road caused by a driver’s administrative violation. The associated relationship states that a violation may cause such damage, indicating a possible infrastructure impact rather than asserting that damage occurred in a specific case. [Data: Entities (674, 108); Relationships (305)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger-carrying motor vehicles are within the provision’s scope
phat_hien.giai_thich: Passenger Vehicle Operation is included because Article 34 explicitly covers passenger-carrying motor vehicles. The relationship connects this vehicle category to the administrative-violation provision, but the supplied records do not specify a particular passenger-vehicle offense or incident. [Data: Entities (3576, 108); Relationships (308)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Traffic and Driver-Training Fine Categories
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around a fine range of 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 Vietnamese dong under provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. The fine connects several distinct categories: failure to follow requirements in a circulation permit, a specified violation by practical driving instructors, and two motorcycle or similar-vehicle yielding violations. Article 39, Clause 1 links the driver-training violation to driver training and driving tests. The available information describes penalty categories, not specific enforcement cases, organizations, or individuals.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s relevance to transport safety and regulatory compliance while accounting for the limited scope of the documented fine categories and the absence of case-specific enforcement information.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A single fine range connects several violation categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The 2,000,000-to-3,000,000-dong fine is the central entity linking the described penalty categories. The records associate it with circulation-permit noncompliance, a driving-instructor violation, and two motorcycle or similar-vehicle yielding violations; the applicable provision and conduct determine which category applies. [Data: Entities (2157); Relationships (6912, 3042, 1880, 7024, 7025)]

The shared amount therefore does not mean the violations are identical: the records describe distinct conduct and legal contexts under the same fine range. [Data: Entities (1959, 746, 2041, 2042, 2157)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circulation-permit noncompliance concerns oversized or overweight transport
phat_hien.giai_thich: The permit-related category is described as failing to follow requirements in a vehicle circulation permit while transporting oversized or overweight goods. The stated fine is subject to applicable exceptions, so the description does not establish that every departure from permit requirements receives this penalty. [Data: Entities (1959, 2157); Relationships (6912)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A driver-training violation is linked to Article 39, Clause 1
phat_hien.giai_thich: The specified training-related conduct is a practical driving instructor carrying people or goods on a driver-training vehicle contrary to regulations. The records associate this violation with the 2,000,000-to-3,000,000-dong fine and identify Article 39, Clause 1 as a provision concerning driver-training and driving-test violations. [Data: Entities (746, 429, 1486, 2157); Relationships (3042, 1880, 1879)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Two yielding violations cover different intersection conditions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
One listed violation concerns a motorcycle or similar-vehicle driver failing to slow down and yield to a vehicle approaching from the left at an intersection with a roundabout-direction sign. [Data: Entities (2041); Relationships (7024)]

The other concerns failure to slow down and yield to a vehicle approaching from the right at an intersection without a roundabout-direction sign. Both are associated with the same fine range under Clause 6 of Article 7 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, while remaining distinct circumstances. [Data: Entities (2042, 2157); Relationships (7025, 7023)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory provisions, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich: The material identifies specified conduct, fine amounts, and connections to provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It does not identify actual offenders, citations, payment status, repeat violations, or enforcement decisions; accordingly, it supports a summary of penalty categories but not conclusions about compliance or enforcement in particular cases. [Data: Entities (1959, 746, 2041, 2042, 2157); Relationships (6912, 3042, 7024, 7025)]

v.tieu_de: Road-Traffic Violations and Restoration Requirements
v.tom_tat: This community describes transport-related administrative violations and their corrective consequences. Its central measure is restoration of the original condition when a covered violation alters or damages a bridge or road. The framework links oversized- or overweight-transport violations and certain vehicle-condition violations to corrective measures, while also identifying sanctions that include driving-license point deductions. The records describe rules and potential consequences, not specific incidents or evidence of actual compliance.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it connects transport violations to infrastructure restoration and driver sanctions, although the records do not establish actual incidents or their scale.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Restoration is the central corrective measure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Restoration of the original condition is the community’s most connected concept. It is described as requiring the responsible person to return a condition altered by an administrative violation to its prior state, with bridges and roads given as examples. [Data: Entities (4193); Relationships (9963, 3351, 4200)]

The requirement is conditional: the records connect restoration to covered violations that cause damage or otherwise alter the relevant condition. They do not establish that any particular restoration has been ordered or completed. [Data: Relationships (9963, 4200, 9964, 2901, 9965)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Oversized- and overweight-transport violations can involve infrastructure damage
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify violations of regulations governing oversized or overweight goods transport and connect such violations to possible damage to bridges or roads. Where the covered violation causes that damage, restoration is described as a required remedial measure. [Data: Entities (3500, 1225, 4193); Relationships (4199, 9386, 9963)]

The relationship between the violation and damage is stated as a possibility, not as a finding that damage necessarily occurs in each case. [Data: Relationships (4199)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Bridge and road damage is the principal infrastructure concern
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Bridges and roads are identified as infrastructure that may be damaged by covered transport violations and may then be subject to restoration. The data thus links individual administrative violations to potential physical impacts on transport infrastructure. [Data: Entities (675, 4584, 1225); Relationships (2902, 10123, 9964, 2901)]

The records describe the types of infrastructure and the remedy, but provide no information about the amount of damage, affected locations, repair costs, or actual incidents.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 11 of Article 13 provides for corrective measures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 11 of Article 13 is described as identifying restoration of the original condition as a corrective measure, in addition to penalties for specified violations. This connects the restoration requirement to a provision concerning drivers who commit the relevant violations. [Data: Entities (876, 4193); Relationships (3351)]

The records also link the clause to vehicle-condition administrative violations, describing corrective measures for the relevant conduct under Point c, Clause 4 of Article 13. They do not provide the full text of either provision or further details about how the measures are applied. [Data: Entities (5508, 876); Relationships (3352, 9965)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle-condition violations are included in the corrective framework
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes administrative violations involving failure to meet vehicle-condition requirements for participation in traffic. The records specifically associate the described conduct with Point c, Clause 4 of Article 13. [Data: Entities (5508); Relationships (9965)]

Clause 11 is described as providing additional corrective measures for drivers committing relevant vehicle-condition violations, and restoration is linked to this category when the violation alters the original condition. [Data: Entities (876, 4193); Relationships (3352, 9965)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Sanctions may include driving-license point deductions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records state that penalties for the specified transport violations include deduction of points from a driver’s license. This is a separate consequence from the corrective obligation to restore damaged or altered infrastructure. [Data: Entities (4607); Relationships (9387)]

The data does not specify the number of points deducted, the full range of penalties, or whether any particular driver has received a sanction.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe regulatory provisions, not observed outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The supplied material defines categories of violations, potential infrastructure damage, corrective restoration, and sanctions. It does not identify named drivers, enforcement actions, completed repairs, or evidence that a particular party complied with or violated these requirements. [Data: Entities (4193, 3500, 5508, 4607); Relationships (9386, 3352, 9387)]

Accordingly, the community is best characterized as a regulatory framework with potential infrastructure and licensing consequences; the available records do not support conclusions about the frequency, severity, or real-world enforcement of these matters.

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 25 Transport and Licensing Rules
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 25, which refers to distinct provisions in multiple Vietnamese legal instruments rather than one unified rule. The supplied relationships connect it to intelligent-traffic-vehicle operating permits and to urban transport violations, including penalties and a two-point driver’s-licence deduction; Article 24 is separately linked to transport violations involving live animals or fresh food and the same deduction framework. The records describe regulatory requirements and sanctions, but do not report any actual violations or enforcement events. [Data: Entities (328, 5180, 327, 2912, 5119); Relationships (1304, 1300, 1305, 1296, 1295)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate importance because it connects transport licensing and administrative penalty rules, but the records describe provisions rather than actual violations or their consequences. [Data: Entities (328, 5180, 2912, 5296); Relationships (1304, 1305, 1306, 1307)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 25 is an ambiguous label for separate legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description explicitly states that “Article 25” refers to provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments, and that their subjects depend on the instrument cited. It identifies Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and Law 36/2024/QH15 as separate sources; these should not be treated as one rule. [Data: Entities (328)]

The supplied relationships focus on licensing and urban transport penalties. The entity description also mentions expressway-entry rules under Law 36/2024/QH15, but those rules are not represented by a relationship in the supplied relationship records. [Data: Entities (328); Relationships (1304, 1300, 1306, 1307)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: One Article 25 branch concerns intelligent-traffic-vehicle operating permits
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 25 of Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP is described as addressing the authorities responsible for issuing operating permits for intelligent traffic vehicles. The relationship records connect Article 25 to the licensing activity. [Data: Entities (328, 2912); Relationships (1304)]

The licensing description says the application must include a certificate of technical safety quality and environmental protection as required by regulations. This is a stated application requirement; the records do not identify any applicant or establish whether a particular application complied. [Data: Entities (2912)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Another Article 25 branch addresses specified urban transport violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Under the supplied descriptions, Article 25 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP sets penalties and licence-point deductions for specified violations involving drivers of environmental sanitation vehicles and waste-carrying cars in urban transport activities. [Data: Entities (328, 1544, 5296, 5297); Relationships (1300, 1306, 1307)]

The records describe the scope of the penalty provision, not a documented violation by a particular driver. They provide no case details, enforcement outcome, or evidence about how frequently these rules are applied. [Data: Entities (1544, 5296, 5297)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A two-point licence deduction is linked to the specified Article 25 violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The two-point driver’s-licence deduction is identified as an administrative sanction under Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. Article 25 is linked to that deduction, and the records state that it applies to the specified urban transport violation alongside the applicable penalty. [Data: Entities (5180, 5296); Relationships (1305, 10616)]

The deduction entity also describes other contexts in which the sanction is prescribed, including certain student-transport and live-animal or fresh-food transport violations. These are described as separate categories and should not be assumed to be the same conduct as the urban transport violations. [Data: Entities (5180)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 24 is a related but distinct transport-penalty provision
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 24 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is described as covering car drivers who violate rules on transporting live animals or fresh food. Its relationship to the transportation-rule violation and the two-point deduction is separate from Article 25’s urban-transport links. [Data: Entities (327, 5119, 5180); Relationships (1295, 1296)]

The records therefore show a shared sanction mechanism across distinct provisions, not a single combined offence. They do not provide details of any individual transport incident or penalty imposed. [Data: Entities (327, 5180); Relationships (1295, 1296)]

v.tieu_de: Motorcycle and Moped Emissions-Inspection Certification
v.tom_tat: This community centers on motorcycle and moped emissions-inspection establishments and the procedures governing their operating eligibility.
