For intelligent-transport vehicles, an owner or legally authorized person may apply to replace a damaged operating permit or reissue a lost one; the competent authority is described as considering the application within two working days. If a permit or operating licence is revoked, the owner must surrender it. The information concerns administrative procedures, not vehicle performance or technical capability. [Data: Reports (1-814); Entities (5439, 4139, 2913, 2721); Relationships (9922, 2788, 8025)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: No specific misconduct, reputational finding, or system-performance evidence is established
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community data is regulatory in character: it identifies duties, violation categories, procedures, and possible consequences, but does not provide evidence that a particular person, organization, or vehicle violated the rules or was sanctioned. Accordingly, it supports assessing the framework’s public-safety and compliance importance, not attributing wrongdoing to a specific party. [Data: Reports (1-814, 1-802, 1-807); Entities (5431, 5439, 4456)]

The material mentions electronic document information, inspection facilities, and specialized databases, but does not assess their capacity, security, reliability, or operational performance. It also contains no supported reputational assessment of the entities involved. [Data: Reports (1-802, 1-814); Entities (5403)]

v.tieu_de: Article 12, Roadways, and Traffic Enforcement
v.tom_tat: This community links Article 12 references, roadway and sidewalk rules, traffic-violation categories, and the authorities responsible for enforcement. Article 12 is not one unified rule: its meaning varies across Vietnamese laws, decrees, and a circular. The records cover traffic safety, public-space use, penalties, conditional temporary use, and administrative procedures, including notice to vehicle owners and technical detection of violations. They describe legal requirements and assigned functions, not evidence of particular violations or enforcement outcomes.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and regulatory importance because it spans roadway conduct, enforcement, and corrective procedures, although the records do not establish actual incidents or noncompliance.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 12 is a cross-reference to provisions in different instruments
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central Article 12 entity explicitly describes provisions in multiple legal instruments, including Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, Law 36/2024/QH15, Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, and Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT. Their subjects include penalties, speed and safe-distance rules, collection of road-safety database information, and a circular’s entry into force. These topics should be interpreted under their respective instruments rather than treated as one unified Article 12. [Data: Entities (243); Reports (1-1068)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the community’s penalty and duty references: the linked material spans separate legal contexts, and the records do not establish that every described rule belongs to the same provision. [Data: Entities (243); Relationships (769, 772, 768)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: ROADWAY and SIDEWALK organize a broad set of public-space rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
ROADWAY is a highly connected concept in the supplied entities, with a listed degree of 54, and is linked to parking, obstruction, spills, sharp objects, non-traffic use, and temporary activities. SIDEWALK is described as primarily for pedestrians; the records generally require pedestrians to use it where available and prohibit drivers from driving on it, while also addressing parking and other uses. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641); Relationships (10329, 10349, 10343, 10340, 10328)]

The rules distinguish ordinary traffic or pedestrian use from other uses of these public spaces. The records establish regulatory categories, not that any person or organization has engaged in the described conduct. [Data: Entities (4585, 4641, 5334); Relationships (769, 772, 10310)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The covered conduct includes obstruction and physical roadway hazards
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The violation categories include unlawful parking or stopping that obstructs traffic, gatherings of vehicles, unauthorized placement of obstructions, and spilling slippery substances, waste, goods, or construction materials onto roads. Scattering sharp objects is also identified as a violation; its entity description gives a fine of VND 35,000,000 to 37,000,000 for an individual. These provisions address potential traffic-flow and roadway-safety concerns, but the source records do not document actual incidents. [Data: Entities (5207, 2381, 4741, 4747, 5273); Relationships (10343, 10340, 10334, 10338)]

Other listed examples include fines of VND 400,000 to 600,000 for illegal roadway or sidewalk parking and for gathering three or more vehicles. These are stated penalty descriptions, not evidence that a fine was imposed in a particular case. [Data: Entities (2539, 2381); Relationships (7589, 7794)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Non-traffic use may be permitted temporarily, subject to authorization
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify political, cultural, sports, and other activities as possible temporary uses of roadways or sidewalks, but state that an authorized plan and approval are required. They connect temporary use to Article 77 of Law No. 36/2024/QH15. [Data: Entities (4890, 3823, 4585, 4641); Relationships (10341, 9691, 10329)]

This is a conditional route for use, not evidence that any particular activity applied for or received approval. The supplied records include no event-specific authorization or compliance information. [Data: Entities (4890, 4585, 4641)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Competent authorities have enforcement and remedial responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Competent Authorities are described as responsible for handling road-law violations, issuing notices in certain cases, and coordinating traffic-management and corrective actions. A listed procedure allows authorities to notify vehicle owners when a violation is detected without an immediate stop and direct them to resolve the case; the process may also seek to identify the driver. [Data: Entities (1041, 5448); Relationships (3694); Reports (1-1061)]

The described remedial measures include directing the removal or unloading of excess or oversized cargo and requiring cleanup of specified hazards or materials. The records describe powers and procedures but do not provide case counts, outcomes, or evidence of implementation effectiveness. [Data: Entities (2962, 2963, 2964); Relationships (3666, 3667, 8673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Technical equipment is part of the stated enforcement capability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Competent Authorities entity describes professional or smart technical equipment used by authorities and functional forces to detect violations, direct and control traffic, and help resolve situations. The supplied enforcement description also covers cases in which equipment detects an administrative violation but the vehicle is not stopped immediately. [Data: Entities (1041, 4530, 1345); Reports (1-1061)]

The records do not identify equipment models, performance, data-retention practices, or operational results, so they support only a limited description of technical capability rather than a detailed assessment.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory significance, not actual compliance or reputation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The material primarily consists of legal references, conduct categories, penalty descriptions, and assigned administrative functions. It does not identify a specific individual or organization as responsible for a violation, document an enforcement case, or assess the reputation of the authorities, vehicle owners, or other parties. [Data: Entities (243, 1041, 5448, 4585); Reports (1-1068, 1-1061, 1-1054)]

Penalty amounts and legal contexts are not always fully mapped to particular conduct in the supplied records; Article 12 itself spans distinct instruments. Accordingly, the evidence supports using this community to understand road-traffic compliance topics and enforcement procedures, but not to draw conclusions about compliance outcomes or institutional performance. [Data: Entities (243, 2216, 4747); Relationships (755, 768); Reports (1-1068)]

v.tieu_de: Driver, Expressway and Road-Traffic Compliance
v.tom_tat: This community is a broad road-safety and regulatory network organized around DRIVER and related traffic rules, violations, and penalties. Its records connect drivers to accident-response duties, tunnel and expressway conduct, document checks, passenger and goods transport, and vehicle-condition requirements. MONETARY FINE is a central enforcement mechanism, alongside possible licence-point deductions, vehicle or document retention, and other administrative sanctions. The material describes rules and potential consequences, not proven violations by particular people or organizations; it provides little basis for judging reputation or technical capabilities.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has high importance because it spans safety-critical road conduct and substantial regulatory consequences, although the records document rules rather than actual violations or harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: DRIVER is the network’s central compliance subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
DRIVER covers people operating multiple kinds of road vehicles and is linked to a wide range of obligations and violations, including accident duties, tunnel maneuvers, inspections, and load limits. Its many direct connections make it the organizing entity for the community. [Data: Entities (1442); Relationships (5998, 5986, 6000, 5958, 5997)]

The description also covers licensing and health conditions, traffic rules, passenger and vehicle safety, and records that may include driver and journey information. These are regulatory descriptions, not evidence about a specific driver’s conduct. [Data: Entities (1442)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Accident response duties link driver conduct to serious safety concerns
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe duties for drivers whose conduct is directly related to an accident, including stopping immediately and preserving the scene. Failure to meet either duty is represented as a traffic violation. [Data: Entities (2045, 2012); Relationships (5958, 5955)]

The material also describes possible blood testing for alcohol, drugs, or other stimulants and assigns healthcare facilities responsibilities for arranging tests or preserving and sending samples when they cannot conduct them. It does not establish that a particular accident, investigation, or test occurred. [Data: Entities (1442, 2479, 654); Relationships (5966, 2857)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Tunnel and expressway rules cover hazardous maneuvers and emergency stops
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Reversing and turning around inside a road tunnel are represented as distinct violations. The records state different fine scopes: Article 8, Clause 5 conduct is described with a 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng fine, while a separate description gives a 800,000–1,000,000 đồng fine for turning around in a tunnel on a motorcycle, moped, or similar vehicle. These amounts should not be treated as interchangeable. [Data: Entities (4208, 5171, 565)]

Emergency-stop rules require drivers to use designated stopping positions where possible, or to signal and report when a vehicle cannot be moved as required. The expressway records also cover safe following distance, access, lane changes, and use of shoulders or emergency stopping lanes. [Data: Entities (1773, 1776, 1989, 5268); Relationships (5950, 5951, 6855, 6854, 6362)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Expressway requirements include exceptions and specified penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The expressway is described as a setting with rules on speed, lane use, entry and exit, stopping, parking, and prohibited maneuvers. The records identify violations including unsafe following distance, improper access, emergency-lane or shoulder use, and unsafe lane changes. [Data: Reports (1-949); Entities (1920, 1989, 1612, 1972, 5268)]

Specified penalties include 2,000,000–3,000,000 đồng for failure to maintain a safe following distance, and 14,000,000–16,000,000 đồng for certain low-speed specialized motor vehicles, subject to a management or maintenance exception. The records also describe an exception for vehicles and workers performing expressway management or maintenance. [Data: Reports (1-949); Entities (4692, 1921, 1922); Relationships (6855, 6852, 6853, 6865)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fines and supplementary sanctions vary by violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
MONETARY FINE connects penalties to drivers, operators, organizations, training and testing activities, and vehicle inspection. Its description gives examples ranging from 800,000–1,000,000 đồng to 20,000,000–30,000,000 đồng, depending on the violation and responsible party; these are prescribed penalties, not proof of fines actually imposed. [Data: Entities (3053); Relationships (5974, 6069, 8986, 8979, 8987)]

Other described consequences include a six-point licence deduction, possible temporary retention of a vehicle and related documents during an inspection, confiscation of a vehicle’s licence plate for specified vehicle-condition violations, and suspension of certain driving or inspection rights. The available records do not establish enforcement frequency or outcomes. [Data: Entities (4657, 5368, 5580, 1093, 4832); Relationships (5993, 6000, 8986, 3925, 8001)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger, goods, and child transport have specific obligations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Drivers transporting goods are described as having to arrange and secure loads safely and signal when a load extends beyond the vehicle. Drivers carrying children under 10 who are shorter than 1.35 meters are subject to seating and safety-device rules. [Data: Entities (1442, 823); Relationships (3208)]

For contract-based passenger transport, the records cover electronic contracts and passenger lists, including violations involving unlisted passengers or inaccessible contract information. A passenger transport business operator is linked to providing equipment that lets the driver access those materials, but the data does not specify the equipment’s design or broader technical capabilities. [Data: Entities (749, 3403, 3566, 3265); Relationships (3045, 5977, 5980)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized vehicle operators and regulated businesses are also in scope
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Specialized vehicle operators are linked to expressway and vehicle-condition requirements, and specialized-motorcycle drivers are connected to monetary fines for specified violations. The records describe categories of regulated conduct rather than identifying any particular operator as noncompliant. [Data: Entities (1469, 5580, 4713); Relationships (6069, 8986, 6947)]

The broader penalty framework also covers organizations, driving-test centers, training facilities, and vehicle-inspection activities. Examples include fines for certain record-retention failures and possible suspension of inspection-certificate rights for specified violations; no particular business or center is shown to have breached these rules. [Data: Reports (1-953); Entities (3436, 5595, 2027, 4832); Relationships (8979, 8987, 7010, 8001)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence establishes regulatory scope, not individual reputation or actual compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Across the records, the community is significant for its connection to road safety, legal duties, and potential administrative consequences. The material does not identify a particular driver or organization as a violator, document an enforcement case, or quantify the frequency or severity of real-world incidents. [Data: Reports (1-939, 1-949, 1-953); Entities (1442, 3053, 4982)]

There is also no supplied evidence for assessing the reputation of a named person or organization. Technical information is limited to the stated provision of access equipment for electronic contracts and passenger lists; its design and capabilities are not described. [Data: Entities (3566); Relationships (5980)]

v.tieu_de: Decree 168/2024 Vehicle-Owner Traffic Sanctions
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its rules for sanctioning individual and organizational vehicle owners for specified road-traffic violations. The entities connect owners to direct operation, permitting employees or representatives to operate vehicles, and procedural penalties, with different fine ranges depending on the provision and owner type. The records also cover vehicle-document violations, transport-related requirements, and towed-trailer cases. They describe a regulatory framework rather than documented incidents; no actual violation or enforcement outcome is provided. [Data: Entities (2647, 3433, 379, 4563, 1290); Relationships (7891, 9323, 1644, 1637, 10306)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate impact because it concerns potentially substantial administrative penalties and road-safety compliance across individuals and organizations, but the records describe rules rather than actual violations or outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A shared enforcement framework for individual and organizational owners
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central structure links both individual and organizational vehicle owners to the road-traffic violation sanctioning procedure under the decree. The records treat these as separate categories of liable owners, not as parties jointly owning a vehicle. [Data: Entities (2647, 3433, 4563); Relationships (7888, 7891, 9323)]

Article 32, Clause 7 is one cited provision specifying fines for both categories of owner. The available material identifies the regulatory relationship but does not establish that any particular owner has been sanctioned. [Data: Entities (383, 1290); Relationships (1644, 1645, 5625, 5626)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Owner liability can arise from direct operation or permitted use
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community describes owner liability where the owner personally operates a vehicle and commits a specified violation, as well as where an employee or representative operates it after being assigned or permitted to use it. These relationships connect owners to employees and representatives through vehicle handover or permission, rather than describing only the driver’s conduct. [Data: Entities (3519, 3703, 155, 593, 1780); Relationships (7889, 7890, 2734, 2736, 498)]

The referenced provisions include Article 34, Clause 2 and specified parts of Article 34 and Article 20. Some underlying conduct is not reproduced in the supplied descriptions, so its precise nature cannot be determined from these records alone. [Data: Entities (406, 947, 3756); Relationships (1715, 1713, 3474, 9591)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Fine amounts vary by provision and owner type
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe multiple fine schedules, not one universal penalty. For the violation associated with Article 32, Clause 14, the stated range is 28,000,000–30,000,000 VND for an individual owner and 56,000,000–60,000,000 VND for an organizational owner. [Data: Entities (380, 3075); Relationships (1637, 1638, 7887, 9004)]

For the specified conduct under Article 32, Clause 11, the listed ranges are 10,000,000–12,000,000 VND for an individual and 20,000,000–24,000,000 VND for an organization. Separately, the records associate Clause 7 with fines of 4,000,000–6,000,000 VND for individuals and 8,000,000–12,000,000 VND for organizations. The applicable amount therefore depends on the provision and conduct at issue. [Data: Entities (5519, 2255, 2642, 3432, 69); Relationships (1631, 1633, 145, 1644, 1645)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Additional rules address vehicle documents and revocation procedures
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The described regulatory scope includes failure to complete required procedures to revoke vehicle registration, license-plate, and inspection documents. Both individual and organizational vehicle owners are linked to this type of violation. [Data: Entities (1954, 383); Relationships (6905, 6906)]

The records also identify erasing, altering, or falsifying vehicle registration documents, and false declarations or forged papers used to obtain replacement registration documents or plates, as conduct subject to administrative penalties when it does not reach the criminal-prosecution threshold described. The supplied information does not report any actual instance of such conduct. [Data: Entities (1290, 2075, 4851); Relationships (1643, 5628, 146)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Transport-vehicle requirements are among the covered violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 32, Clause 11 is linked to passenger-transport vehicle conditions, including adding or removing seats or sleeping berths and luggage-compartment dimensions that do not match the technical specifications on the inspection certificate. These are presented as specified violations with associated owner fine schedules. [Data: Entities (35, 3264, 2250, 2249); Relationships (79, 1632, 80, 9220)]

The sanctioning procedure also connects to transport-order or transport-document violations and to a corresponding Article 26 provision in the stated circumstances. The records do not provide enough detail to characterize the full requirements or establish any noncompliance by a particular operator. [Data: Entities (5113, 1129, 4563); Relationships (10307, 3990, 3991)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Towed-trailer cases may place responsibility on the car owner
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For a violation involving a trailer or semi-trailer towed by a car, the supplied descriptions state that the car owner may be treated as the vehicle owner for sanctioning purposes, even if that person or organization does not own the trailer. This creates a potential responsibility link across separately owned parts of a vehicle combination. [Data: Entities (4965, 699, 706); Relationships (2983, 2974, 10306)]

The records distinguish the car owner from an individual trailer owner or trailer-owning organization, and do not state that the trailer owner is the party sanctioned in this situation. [Data: Entities (5062, 5063); Relationships (10527, 10528)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records define possible consequences, not actual compliance status
phat_hien.giai_thich: The material is primarily a description of provisions, liable parties, procedures, and fine amounts. It contains no identified owner, specific incident, enforcement action, or outcome from which to assess actual compliance or reputation. Accordingly, the community’s significance is regulatory and operational rather than evidence of wrongdoing by a named person or organization. [Data: Entities (379, 4563, 2647, 3433); Relationships (7891, 9323, 7888)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Ministry of Transport and Road-Safety Regulation
v.tom_tat: The community is centered on Vietnam’s Ministry of Transport, with the Minister responsible for regulatory functions spanning road use, vehicle safety and emissions, inspections, driver licensing, training, and road management. Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT translates part of this remit into operating-speed and safe-distance rules, while training and certification establishments support specialized-vehicle operators. The Ministry also manages related databases and has an inspectorate with administrative enforcement authority. The records establish substantial institutional and public-safety importance, but do not assess implementation, compliance outcomes, or reputation. [Data: Entities (3025, 3002, 834, 4572, 4694, +more); Relationships (8740, 8922, 8937, 8940, 3262, +more); Reports (1-1170, 1-1174, 1-1179)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the Ministry’s broad, consequential authority over transport safety, road rules, vehicle oversight, credentials, and related information systems, rather than evidence of wrongdoing or demonstrated harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry is the central coordinating and regulatory institution
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Transport is assigned responsibilities for driver training, testing and licensing; vehicle technical safety and environmental protection; and management of the national highway system and other roads within its remit. The Minister heads the Ministry and holds authority to issue detailed rules and national technical regulations on road transport and vehicles. [Data: Entities (3025, 3002); Relationships (8740, 8925, 8929)]

Its remit also includes licensing and inspection procedures, road signals, vehicle standards and operating requirements, and regulations for testing and inspection facilities. The records show a broad formal mandate, but do not establish how effectively it is implemented. [Data: Entities (3025, 3002, 3214, 3216); Relationships (8927, 8928, 6281)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT provides concrete operating-speed and safe-distance rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT is associated with the Ministry and sets rules on operating speeds and safe distances. It took effect on January 1, 2025, replacing Circular 31/2019/TT-BGTVT and Article 15 of Circular 06/2023/TT-BGTVT. [Data: Entities (834, 833, 830); Relationships (3262, 3259, 3229)]

The circular sets a maximum expressway speed of 120 km/h and a general minimum of 60 km/h, with a specific approach for expressways designed for 60 km/h. It also addresses speeds on non-expressway roads and safe following distances; these are formal requirements, not evidence of enforcement or real-world safety results. [Data: Entities (834); Reports (1-1174)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Vehicle inspection and emissions oversight is supported by certificates and technical rules
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Minister prescribes procedures for issuing, reissuing, suspending, and revoking eligibility certificates for motor vehicle inspection establishments. The records also identify technical regulations for inspecting road-use vehicles and specialized motorcycles, and for facilities conducting motorcycle and moped emissions inspections. [Data: Entities (3114, 2774, 4082, 4223, 4887, +more); Relationships (8922, 8118, 8933, 8935, 8927, +more)]

Article 42 of Law 36/2024/QH15 assigns the Minister responsibilities concerning technical safety and environmental protection requirements, including procedures for motorcycle and moped emissions inspections. The supplied information does not provide inspection results, emissions measurements, or evidence of particular establishments’ compliance. [Data: Entities (450, 2831, 3148, 3213); Relationships (2062, 8412, 8924, 8926)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Training and certification connect the Ministry to specialized-vehicle operators
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes a process for training specialized motor vehicle operators in road-traffic-law knowledge, examining them, and issuing or reissuing certificates. Qualified specialized-operator training establishments conduct the training and examinations, may register applicants, and issue certificates; the Ministry sets standards for these establishments. [Data: Entities (4572, 4694); Relationships (8937, 8940)]

The described credentialing function links operator knowledge with road-safety rules, but the records do not provide examination criteria, pass rates, provider performance assessments, or evidence of safety outcomes. The available evidence therefore supports identifying the function, not judging its effectiveness. [Data: Entities (4572, 4694); Reports (1-1179)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road management extends the Ministry’s influence beyond rulemaking
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry’s management scope includes the national highway system and other roads under its remit. The records also connect the Ministry’s regulatory responsibilities with operational speed-limit signs and road-use rules. [Data: Entities (3025, 3203, 3468); Relationships (8925, 8929)]

Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT links speed rules to road design standards and traffic organization plans. For certain expressways, state-assigned enterprises may manage, operate, and maintain the infrastructure, creating an operational layer alongside the Ministry’s regulatory role. [Data: Entities (834, 1926); Relationships (3262); Reports (1-1174)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Specialized databases support driver, certification, and vehicle-operation administration
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry is responsible for constructing and managing specialized databases that include driver training, testing and licensing; road-traffic-law knowledge certification; and motor vehicle operation. The records describe exclusions for military and police-related information in relevant database descriptions. [Data: Entities (1097, 1489, 1507, 3123, 4363); Relationships (3933, 6115, 6157, 8923, 8936)]

The Ministry’s description says these databases connect with the road traffic order and safety database to support information sharing on matters including insurance, accidents, administrative penalties, registration, and inspection. The records do not specify security controls, access practices, or operational performance. [Data: Entities (3025, 1097); Reports (1-1170)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The Ministry has formal administrative enforcement authority
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Ministry of Transport Inspectorate is part of the Ministry, and the Chief Inspector heads it. The Chief Inspector is authorized to impose specified administrative penalties and remedial measures; the Ministry description states that fines may reach 75,000,000 Vietnamese đồng and that exhibits and vehicles used in administrative violations may be confiscated. [Data: Entities (3025, 3027, 812); Relationships (3181, 8920)]

This establishes an institutional enforcement capability, but the supplied records do not describe individual cases, enforcement frequency, or outcomes. It should not be interpreted as evidence that a violation occurred. [Data: Entities (812, 3027); Relationships (8920); Reports (1-1170)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence establishes regulatory importance, not adverse compliance or reputation findings
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Across the materials, the documented information concerns laws, regulations, assigned duties, administrative processes, and institutional relationships. It does not provide compliance rates, audit results, specific violations, or reputational assessments for the Ministry, establishments, training providers, or operators. [Data: Entities (3025, 3002, 3114, 4694); Reports (1-1170, 1-1179)]

The Minister is described as an unnamed officeholder, so the records support analysis of the office’s authority but not attribution to a named individual. Accordingly, the impact rating reflects the breadth and importance of the community’s documented responsibilities, not a finding of misconduct. [Data: Entities (3002, 3025); Reports (1-1170)]

v.tieu_de: Road Traffic Order and Safety, Traffic Police, and Passenger Transport
v.tom_tat: This community centers on road traffic order and safety, linked to traffic police, passenger transport by automobile, road transport, and the prevention and handling of traffic-law violations. The material describes traffic police patrol and control duties, as well as their roles in crime prevention, public order, emergency response, and rescue. Passenger transport requirements include complying with applicable rules, following registered routes and schedules except in force majeure, using designated pickup and drop-off places, observing capacity limits, instructing passengers on safety equipment, and maintaining vehicle cleanliness. The stated aims extend beyond traffic flow to protection of life, health, property, the environment, national security, national defense, and socioeconomic development. The records describe legal and operational responsibilities; they do not establish specific violations or noncompliance by an identified person or organization.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public importance because it connects road safety and transport operations with life and property protection, enforcement, emergency response, and wider security and development objectives.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road traffic order and safety is the organizing concept
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Road traffic order and safety is the central subject, connected to traffic police, passenger transport, road transport, traffic-law violations, and the objective of maintaining smooth traffic flow. This makes the community a framework for both the desired condition of road traffic and the measures described as supporting it. [Data: Entities (4385); Relationships (10168, 9440, 10156, 10169, 10170)]

The stated principles also associate traffic order and safety with protection of life and health, property, and the environment, as well as national security, national defense, and socioeconomic development. These links indicate broad public significance, rather than a narrow focus on traffic movement alone. [Data: Relationships (9769, 10171, 6747, 9137, 9110, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Traffic police have enforcement, prevention, and public-safety responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic police are described as conducting patrol and control activities to help ensure road traffic order and safety. They are also tasked with combating and preventing crime on road routes and maintaining security and public order in accordance with law. [Data: Entities (4416, 1139, 4631); Relationships (10168, 4023, 10213)]

The described responsibilities further include participating in prevention related to terrorism, disruptive demonstrations, epidemics, natural disasters, and fires, and taking part in rescue operations. These are stated duties and areas of participation; the records do not report a particular incident or operational outcome. [Data: Entities (4416, 4172, 4898, 4264, 1836); Relationships (9948, 9999, 9143, 10214, 6764, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Passenger transport by automobile is subject to operational requirements
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 45 is identified as addressing road traffic order and safety in connection with passenger transport by automobile. The transport activity is described as subject to applicable legal requirements and limits, and as needing to follow its registered schedule and route except in cases of force majeure. [Data: Entities (3567, 4385); Relationships (9440)]

The listed practices include picking up and dropping off passengers at designated places, keeping the vehicle interior clean, and guiding passengers on the use of safety equipment. These records describe requirements, not evidence that a particular operator complied with or breached them. [Data: Entities (3735, 2946, 2708); Relationships (9439, 8649, 8009)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Capacity limits and traffic-law violations are addressed through enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records identify carrying more passengers, baggage, or goods than permitted as a prohibited practice in passenger transport by automobile. They also describe traffic-law violations as conduct that breaches road traffic rules and may be detected and assessed using equipment and handled by competent authorities. [Data: Entities (737, 4373); Relationships (3023, 10156)]

The stated approach is to detect and prevent violations promptly and to deal with identified violations strictly in accordance with law. This indicates an enforcement and remedial framework, but the provided information does not identify specific offenders, cases, penalties, or rates of noncompliance. [Data: Entities (4373, 4385); Relationships (10156)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The framework is linked to emergency response and rescue
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Traffic police participate in rescue and relief operations, and the records connect rescue duties with circumstances involving a state of emergency. Designated vehicles may use flashing blue priority lights for official duties in the described emergency context. [Data: Entities (4416, 4172, 4758); Relationships (9948, 9949)]

The wider emergency-related responsibilities listed for traffic police include participation in preventing natural disasters, fires, and epidemics. These connections show that the community's scope includes public-safety activities beyond routine traffic control, while providing no account of a specific emergency response. [Data: Entities (3223, 2288, 1836, 4416); Relationships (9143, 7356, 6764)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe legal and operational duties, not demonstrated noncompliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The information characterizes the relevant subject as a legal and public condition addressed by Article 3 of Law 36/2024/QH15 and by administrative rules and remedial measures concerning traffic violations. It also describes Article 45 in relation to passenger transport. [Data: Entities (4385, 3567)]

No specific person, transport operator, enforcement action, adjudicated case, or observed breach is identified in the supplied records. Accordingly, the evidence supports describing the community's stated rules and responsibilities, but not drawing conclusions about actual compliance, misconduct, or the effectiveness of enforcement.

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Traffic Regulations: Articles 17 and 18
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Article 17 and Article 18 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and related traffic-law provisions. Its strongest connections concern environmental-protection violations in traffic, associated fines, and motorcycle driver-licensing violations. The records also connect Article 17 to priority-vehicle signaling requirements and rules for passing oncoming vehicles, but the entity descriptions show that these subjects belong to different legal instruments. The information describes regulatory requirements and penalties, not specific violations, enforcement actions, or identified drivers. [Data: Entities (274, 282, 1832, 3160); Relationships (972, 962, 987, 1029)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has substantial public-safety and compliance importance because it covers traffic conduct and penalties, but the records provide no evidence of specific incidents or actors.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 17 is an ambiguous reference, not a single subject
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description explicitly says that “Article 17” refers to provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments, so its meaning depends on the instrument cited. It identifies Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP with environmental-protection penalties, Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP with signal-emitting devices for priority vehicles, and Law 36/2024/QH15 with vehicles passing in opposite directions. [Data: Entities (274)]

The relationship records connect the generic ARTICLE 17 node to all three topics, including environmental violations, priority-vehicle signaling, and yielding while passing. Because the entity description assigns these subjects to different instruments, the links should not be read as evidence that they are all provisions of the same legal text. [Data: Relationships (962, 972, 987, 970)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Environmental-protection violations in traffic are a prominent Article 17 topic
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe covered conduct by drivers of cars, tractors, and similar vehicles, including transporting specified materials or waste without adequate covering, allowing cargo to spill, and carrying goods or waste so that water runs onto the road. The relationships associate these categories with Article 17 and environmental-protection violations in traffic. [Data: Entities (274, 1832, 1828, 5157); Relationships (972, 970, 984, 982)]

The stated fine for listed violations is 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. The Article 17 description also says that clauses 2, 3, and 4 address cleanup of rubbish, waste, materials, or goods; the supplied records do not specify the details of those cleanup requirements. [Data: Entities (2162, 2161, 274); Relationships (974, 973, 975)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 18 addresses driver licensing and related compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP is linked to motorcycle licensing violations, including operating without a licence or with an invalid, altered, unauthorized, unsuitable, or points-exhausted licence. Its description says Clause 5 covers certain two-wheeled motorcycles and similar vehicles, and the linked fine for the described motorcycle licensing violation is 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (282, 3160, 2243); Relationships (1029, 1035, 1033, 7308)]

The records also identify point deductions among the penalties addressed by Article 18. They do not establish that any particular driver committed these violations or received a penalty. [Data: Entities (282, 3386); Relationships (1029, 1030)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Other Article 18 provisions cover distinct vehicle and documentation cases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 18’s description covers requirements for drivers of cars and similar vehicles as well as motorcycles. It identifies failing to carry a driving licence and failing to carry a valid compulsory civil liability insurance certificate among the listed violations, and states a fine range of 8,000,000 to 10,000,000 Vietnamese đồng for the stated violations involving cars and similar vehicles. [Data: Entities (282, 1939, 1946); Relationships (1024, 1025)]

A separate subsection, Article 18(3), is described as imposing a 300,000 to 400,000 đồng fine for a commercial motor-vehicle driver who fails to carry a driving licence, subject to an exception. The source data also contains other fine descriptions linked to Article 18; these should be interpreted in their specified clause and conduct contexts rather than treated as one general penalty. [Data: Entities (286, 1579, 2186, 287); Relationships (1022, 1042, 1043, 1044)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records cover roadway hazards and passing rules as separate legal topics
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes roadway hazards including dragging mud, soil, sand, materials, or waste onto a public roadway, spilling goods, and water running from transported loads onto the road. The stated fine for dragging materials onto a roadway in a way that endangers traffic is 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 Vietnamese đồng. [Data: Entities (1440, 4737, 5631, 2161); Relationships (5945, 5946, 6754, 6757)]

The separate passing rule says that when vehicles travel in opposite directions on a road without separate lanes for each direction, drivers must reduce speed and keep to the right; a vehicle facing an obstacle must give way to one without an obstacle. The entity description assigns this rule to Article 17 of Law 36/2024/QH15, not to the environmental provisions of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. [Data: Entities (274, 633, 5656); Relationships (987, 2827)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some legal references and penalty descriptions require careful verification
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Article 17 entity notes that Article 5 of Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP amends a provision concerning uncovered materials or materials, waste, goods, or water spilling onto a road. The same description distinguishes that amendment from the different Article 17 references, reinforcing the need to verify the instrument and provision before applying a rule. [Data: Entities (274)]

The supplied records also contain multiple fine entities and links for different conduct and clauses. For example, Article 17 environmental violations and motorcycle licensing violations each have a stated 2,000,000 to 4,000,000 đồng penalty, but they are separate regulatory contexts. The data supports describing these stated penalties; it does not establish enforcement frequency, compliance rates, organizational reputation, or technical capabilities. [Data: Entities (2162, 2243, 1832, 3160); Relationships (974, 1028, 7308)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Vehicle License Plate Auction Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s vehicle license plate auction rules and connects auction participants and winners to payment, registration, plate disposition, and inheritance procedures. The framework specifies minimum starting prices, deadlines, and consequences for nonpayment or failure to register; it also directs net auction proceeds to the state budget. The supplied descriptions identify some ambiguity about death-related cancellation deadlines and the scope of provisions concerning transfers and repeat violations, so those details should be read cautiously. [Data: Entities (5418, 5638, 5639, 5476, 690); Relationships (10649, 10650, 10455, +more)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the framework’s broad regulatory and fiscal significance for vehicle registration and auction participants, while the supplied data describes administrative rules rather than a direct security threat.

phat_hien.tom_tat: A regulated auction process with defined eligibility and minimum prices
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The auction is described under Article 37 of Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15, with further rules and procedures to be specified by the Government. The supplied description sets minimum starting prices of 40 million đồng for car plates and 5 million đồng for motorcycle or moped plates, and states that the advance deposit must be at least the applicable starting price. [Data: Entities (5418, 696, 3151)]

A sole registrant, participant, or bidder meeting the starting price may be deemed the winner. These rules define the entry conditions and provide a route to an award even when only one qualifying participant is present. [Data: Entities (5418, 5639); Relationships (10650, 2756)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Winners face strict payment and nonpayment consequences
phat_hien.giai_thich:
A winner must pay the full winning bid within 30 days after notification of the result. Failure to pay in full results in forfeiture of the deposit and amounts already paid, and a 12-month ban on participating in further vehicle plate auctions. [Data: Entities (5638, 2009, 2358, 7, 603); Relationships (6986, 6983, 21, 20, 2757)]

For an unpaid award, the plate may be re-auctioned or transferred to the vehicle registration and management system. The described consequences therefore combine financial loss, temporary exclusion from auctions, and a change in the plate’s disposition. [Data: Entities (4030, 5079); Relationships (6984, 6985, 9834, 10588)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Registration is a separate deadline after confirmation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After confirmation of the winning bid, the winner has 12 months to register a vehicle to which the auctioned plate will be attached. Force majeure or an objective obstacle may extend that period by no more than six months. [Data: Entities (5476, 1081, 2296, 3280); Relationships (2762, 7366, 9232)]

If registration is not completed within the applicable deadline, the plate may be re-auctioned or transferred to the registration and management system, and the payment is not refunded. This is distinct from the nonpayment consequences, which are tied to the 30-day payment deadline. [Data: Entities (5639, 4031, 5081, 3255); Relationships (9835, 10590, 9209, 10591)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Rules distinguish the plate from the vehicle associated with it
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The descriptions say winners may transfer, exchange, give away, or bequeath the vehicle associated with an auction-winning plate. Separately, Clause 2 is described as restricting transfer, exchange, gifting, or bequest of the winning plate itself, subject to an exception in Point c of Clause 1. [Data: Entities (5419, 639, 5078, 912); Relationships (6833, 10587, 7604, 2837, 3400)]

This distinction matters when interpreting the rights attached to an auctioned plate: the supplied material describes permissions concerning the associated vehicle alongside restrictions concerning the plate. The precise application of the exception is not elaborated in the available descriptions. [Data: Entities (863, 912); Relationships (3336, 3338, 3335, 2836)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Qualifying deaths can cancel an auction result and trigger payment to an heir
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes cancellation when a winner dies before completing vehicle-registration steps, and states that an heir may receive the full amount the winner paid. The described heir payment is linked to cancellation of the auction result. [Data: Entities (690, 5640, 3602, 2480); Relationships (2944, 2946, 7722, 9463)]

The records identify more than one relevant timing description: death within 12 months after confirmation before registration, and death within 30 days after result notification but before confirmation. The available information does not reconcile these deadlines, so they should not be treated as a single, universally applicable trigger. [Data: Entities (690, 1254, 5640, 604); Relationships (2943, 2945, 3897, 2758)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Auction proceeds support public funding purposes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
After auction-organization, advertising, and system-administration costs are deducted, proceeds are paid into the central state budget. The description identifies the database and the road-traffic-law knowledge test as funding purposes associated with the budgeted proceeds. [Data: Entities (5418, 4754); Relationships (10455)]

This gives the auction process a public-finance dimension in addition to its role in allocating plates. The supplied records specify the destination and stated purposes of proceeds, but do not provide amounts collected or assess how the funds are used in practice. [Data: Entities (5418, 4754)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Repeat-violation and confiscation descriptions are not fully clear
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe repeat violations under Article 38 as potentially resulting in confiscation of the vehicle operated by the responsible person. However, the act whose repetition triggers that consequence is not identified in the entity description. [Data: Entities (863, 4131); Relationships (3337, 3399)]

There is also an internal ambiguity: Clause 1 is described both as addressing a confiscation-related act and as permitting certain dealings with the associated vehicle, while Clause 2 is described as covering repeat violations and restrictions on the auctioned plate. The available data does not clarify how these descriptions fit together, so the scope of the confiscation rule cannot be established from this material alone. [Data: Entities (863, 912); Relationships (3336, 3338, 3335, 3399)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnamese Article 34 Road-Traffic Provisions
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around Article 34, which the supplied entity description says refers to provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments. The records emphasize Article 34 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and its penalties and corrective measures for road-traffic violations, including oversized or overloaded vehicles, tracked vehicles, and driving outside a permitted route. The community also includes references to vehicle classification under Law 36/2024/QH15 and requirements for foreign drivers under Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP. These records describe regulatory provisions and violation categories, not specific people, operators, or enforcement cases.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The community has moderate-to-high importance because it describes several road-traffic compliance requirements and penalties, but the records do not identify specific incidents or affected parties.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 34 is an umbrella reference to multiple legal provisions
phat_hien.giai_thich: The central entity notes that “Article 34” refers to provisions in several Vietnamese legal instruments, so its meaning depends on the instrument. The description distinguishes foreign-national driving requirements in Decree 151/2024/NĐ-CP, penalties and licence-point deductions in Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP, and vehicle classification in Law 36/2024/QH15. This distinction matters when interpreting the connected penalty and corrective-action records, which concern road-traffic violations under the provisions described in the network. [Data: Entities (401); Relationships (1694, 1688, 1696)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Corrective removal of excess or oversized cargo is a prominent measure
phat_hien.giai_thich: The network links Article 34 to a corrective measure requiring excess-load cargo to be unloaded or oversized cargo to be removed, following guidance from competent authorities where the violation is detected. This measure is connected to multiple clauses and points, including Clauses 1, 2, 4, and 5 and points a, c, and d of Clause 3. The records establish the measure and its cited provisions, but do not describe how often it is applied or any particular case. [Data: Entities (4118, 861, 911, 949, 960); Relationships (1694, 3334, 3398, 3476, 3511, +more)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The covered conduct includes oversized, overweight, and tracked vehicles
phat_hien.giai_thich: Article 34 is connected to road operation of oversized vehicles, overloaded vehicles, and tracked vehicles, as well as a combined category covering oversized or overweight vehicles or tracked vehicles. The entity descriptions characterize these as operation on a road that exceeds permitted dimensions or weight limits, or involves a tracked vehicle. The records identify regulated conduct; they do not establish that any named person or vehicle committed a violation. [Data: Entities (3371, 3338, 3369, 4301); Relationships (1691, 1692, 1693, 1695)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A stated fine is linked to several vehicle-related violations
phat_hien.giai_thich: The community includes a fine of 13,000,000 to 15,000,000 dong and connects it to operating an overloaded vehicle, a tracked vehicle, or an oversized vehicle on a road. Separately, the records specify that driving outside the route in a still-valid circulation permit is subject to the same fine range. These are descriptions of stated penalties, not evidence that a fine was imposed in a specific case. [Data: Entities (2144, 1647); Relationships (1688, 1685, 7141, 7142, 7143)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: A ten-point licence deduction is specified for a particular violation
phat_hien.giai_thich: The records state that a driver committing the violation described in Point b, Clause 5 of Article 34 has 10 points deducted from their driver’s licence. The supplied information does not identify the underlying conduct described by that point, so the deduction should not be generalized to the other listed violations. [Data: Entities (4897); Relationships (1696)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records support regulatory significance, not conclusions about actual compliance
phat_hien.giai_thich: The network provides descriptions of legal requirements, penalties, and corrective measures, including limits on vehicle dimensions or weight and route restrictions. It does not identify drivers, transport companies, enforcement actions, or specific incidents; accordingly, it cannot establish whether any entity complied with or violated the provisions. [Data: Entities (401, 4118, 1647, 1876); Relationships (1685, 1687, 1694)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Traffic Police and Permit-Notification Framework
v.tom_tat: This community describes a road-safety coordination framework under Vietnam’s Law 36/2024/QH15. Its central entities are the Traffic Police Agency of the Ministry of Public Security and agencies responsible for issuing permits, which must promptly notify traffic police about dangerous-goods transports and oversized or overweight vehicles. Traffic police then direct or control traffic and perform inspection or enforcement duties, including on the route-specific road sections. The records describe statutory responsibilities and activities, but do not establish whether particular agencies have complied or report outcomes from actual transport movements. [Data: Entities (5023, 5024, 4590, 2834, 2833); Relationships (8418, 8415, 10573, 2767, 2765)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the framework’s substantial public-safety and regulatory importance across hazardous and oversized transport, while the records provide no evidence of specific violations or adverse outcomes.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Central role of the Ministry of Public Security’s Traffic Police Agency
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The Traffic Police Agency of the Ministry of Public Security is a central recipient of notifications under both Article 51, addressing dangerous-goods transport, and Article 53, addressing oversized or overweight cargo vehicles. The records connect the agency to notification duties and to traffic direction, control, inspection, and enforcement functions. [Data: Entities (5023, 2833, 2834); Relationships (8418, 8415, 10132, 10557)]

This position places the agency at the intersection of the two transport-related processes described in the data. The records set out its assigned role but do not establish the agency’s operational performance in individual cases. [Data: Relationships (10573, 2767, 8418, 8415)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Separate statutory notification pathways for two transport categories
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 51 concerns road vehicles transporting dangerous goods and requires the authority issuing dangerous-goods transport permits to promptly notify relevant traffic police agencies. Article 53 concerns oversized or overweight cargo vehicles and assigns a notification duty to the circulation permit-issuing agency. [Data: Entities (2833, 2834, 607, 5374); Relationships (2765, 8420)]

Both pathways connect permit issuers with traffic police, but the records describe distinct permit-issuing entities and transport categories. This distinction is relevant to interpreting which notification process applies to a given movement. [Data: Relationships (2767, 2766, 10573, 10574)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Prompt notice links permits to traffic management
phat_hien.giai_thich:
For oversized or overweight vehicles, the circulation permit-issuing agency must promptly notify traffic police about the planned route or passage. The described purpose is to enable traffic direction and control, inspection, and handling of violations. [Data: Entities (5374, 5023, 5001, 5009); Relationships (10573, 8420, 10132, 10557)]

The dangerous-goods pathway likewise requires prompt notice from the permit-issuing authority to the relevant traffic police agencies. The records frame notification as a coordination mechanism for managing transport on the roads, rather than providing evidence about how quickly or consistently notices are sent in practice. [Data: Entities (607, 4590, 2833); Relationships (2767, 2766, 8415)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Route-specific agencies have localized safety responsibilities
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The framework identifies traffic police responsible for the road or road segment traversed by a vehicle as notification recipients. For oversized or overweight cargo, the route-responsible agency is described as managing passage and maintaining safety on its assigned section. [Data: Entities (5024, 4590, 4589); Relationships (8419, 10574, 9384)]

The records also associate route-level responsibilities with traffic direction, inspection, and handling legal violations. This indicates a division of work in which central and route-responsible police agencies are connected to the same notification process, with route agencies carrying duties on the relevant section. [Data: Relationships (10131, 10554, 10558, 7660, 10357)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Operational duties include control, inspection, and enforcement
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The traffic-police duties described for notified movements include directing and controlling traffic. The records also identify inspection and control of traffic, as well as handling legal violations, among the associated functions. [Data: Entities (4347, 5001, 5008, 5009, 2415); Relationships (10132, 10553, 10557, 10558, 7660)]

These functions apply across the central and route-responsible agencies in the descriptions. They establish the intended operational scope of the framework, but do not document particular inspections, violations, or enforcement results. [Data: Entities (5023, 5024); Relationships (10357, 10558, 10131, 10557)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Road-safety assurance is the framework’s stated objective
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records characterize road traffic order and safety assurance as an activity covering dangerous-goods transport and oversized or overweight cargo movements. They describe the activity as to be conducted openly and transparently and in a manner convenient for the public. [Data: Entities (4386, 1790, 2834); Relationships (8417, 10173, 6713, 7673)]

For dangerous-goods road transport, the data link safety assurance to the route or road section used by the vehicle and to the responsible traffic police agency. This highlights the public-safety purpose of coordinating notices with route-level oversight. [Data: Entities (1227, 2425, 4589, 4590); Relationships (4202, 4203, 7673)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Dangerous-goods training is noted, but implementation detail is limited
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entity description for hazardous-goods transport training states that drivers and escorts involved in transporting dangerous goods are required to receive such training. The records connect this training topic to hazardous-goods road transport. [Data: Entities (2426, 2425); Relationships (7672)]

This adds a personnel-preparation element to the community’s safety context, alongside permit notification and traffic oversight. The supplied information does not specify training standards, completion rates, or evidence of compliance by particular drivers or escorts. [Data: Entities (2426, 607, 5023); Relationships (7672, 2767)]

v.tieu_de: Article 40 and Vehicle Inspection Facilities
v.tom_tat: This community is organized around Article 40 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP and the vehicle-inspection, testing, and certification activities it regulates. Inspection facilities and testing and certification establishments are connected to defined duties and potential penalties, including ranges of VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 and VND 16,000,000–20,000,000 for specified conduct. The records also describe inspector-related conditions and government management of inspection information. They establish regulatory exposure and public-safety relevance, but do not identify a facility with a confirmed violation or penalty. [Data: Entities (436, 3116, 4907, 3110, 5414); Relationships (1919, 1925, 1916, 1932, 1911)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the framework’s broad road-safety and compliance significance across inspection activities, while the records provide no evidence of a specific violation or enforcement case.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Article 40 is the regulatory hub
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40 is linked to motor vehicle inspection, inspection facilities, testing and certification establishments, inspectors, and multiple penalty provisions. This structure makes it the central organizing entity for the community’s regulatory requirements and consequences. [Data: Entities (436, 3110); Relationships (1916, 1919, 1925, 1932, 1905)]

The described scope includes motor vehicles, specialized-use vehicles and motorcycles, and motor-vehicle parts or components. The records establish this range of regulated activity but do not quantify how many facilities, inspections, or vehicles are affected. [Data: Entities (3111, 4700, 4720, 3128); Relationships (1917, 1923, 1924, 1921)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection facilities have interconnected operational duties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor vehicle inspection facilities are described as responsible for following applicable laws, standards, technical requirements, and procedures; issuing certificates only when authorized; updating required vehicle records; and refusing inspections when required. These duties connect technical inspection decisions with certification and administrative controls. [Data: Entities (3116, 3110); Relationships (9025, 9030, 7976, 7036)]

The records identify potential violations including non-compliant inspections or certificate issuance, non-compliant motorcycle or moped emissions inspections, inspecting a vehicle despite refusal conditions, and failing to update vehicle records. These are described as punishable conduct, not as confirmed actions by a named facility. [Data: Entities (3252, 3251, 1078, 2050, 2685); Relationships (9039, 9038, 3890, 7036, 7976)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated penalty ranges depend on the provision and conduct
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records describe a VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 fine for specified inspection-facility violations, including inspecting a vehicle despite refusal conditions, failing to update required records, and improperly issuing a modification certificate. They separately associate Article 40, Clause 4 with a VND 16,000,000–20,000,000 fine for specified violations. [Data: Entities (441, 2580, 1078, 2050, 2600); Relationships (1909, 3890, 7036, 7842, 1911)]

The Clause 4 range is linked to non-compliant vehicle inspection or certification and non-compliant motorcycle or moped emissions inspection, as well as unlawful refusal of inspection services in the supplied descriptions. The ranges should be treated as separate prescribed penalties; the records do not show that either was imposed on a particular operator. [Data: Entities (952, 2239, 3252, 3251, 3147); Relationships (1905, 1971, 9039, 9038, 1911)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Some provisions connect inspector penalties to establishment liability
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The data describes a condition under which a testing or certification facility may face a VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 fine if at least two inspectors have been penalized under Clause 1 within 12 months of the first such penalty. This links individual inspector enforcement history to potential consequences for an establishment. [Data: Entities (5414, 3119, 864, 78, 4907); Relationships (1932, 1920, 1902, 1963, 1925)]

This is a stated regulatory condition, not evidence that the threshold has been reached or that a facility has been fined. The available records do not identify the inspectors or an establishment involved in a specific case. [Data: Entities (3119, 864, 78, 4907); Relationships (1902, 1933, 1925)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Testing and certification establishments form a related but distinct group
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Article 40 also applies to establishments that test or certify motor vehicles, specialized-use motorcycles, or vehicle parts during manufacture, production, assembly, or importation. These establishments are connected to specified penalties and to requirements concerning the qualifications of personnel assigned to testing or certification. [Data: Entities (4907, 5501, 2131, 598); Relationships (1925, 1933, 9007, 2747)]

The records describe a VND 10,000,000–15,000,000 fine for covered establishments committing specified violations. They do not identify a particular establishment as violating the rules or establish that a penalty was imposed. [Data: Entities (2131, 3077, 933); Relationships (1925, 1933, 9007)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Inspection information is described as part of government-managed databases
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Motor vehicle inspection information is described as included in the road traffic database, with the Ministry of Transport responsible for constructing and managing the specialized database for vehicle-inspection activity, excluding military and police vehicle data. [Data: Entities (3110)]

Inspection information for motor vehicles and specialized vehicles used by the People’s Public Security is described as covered by a separate database managed by the Ministry of Public Security. This indicates divided administrative responsibility for inspection information, but the supplied records do not detail data access, security controls, or system performance. [Data: Entities (3110)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records establish regulatory exposure, not a confirmed compliance failure
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships describe regulated activities, facility duties, violation categories, and possible fines. They do not name an offending facility, document a particular incident or enforcement action, or establish the compliance status of any operator. [Data: Entities (436, 3116, 4907, 5410, 443); Relationships (1919, 1925, 1972, 1933, 1931)]

The community is therefore significant for understanding compliance obligations in a road-safety-related sector, but it does not support conclusions about a specific entity’s reputation, technical performance, or actual legal compliance. [Data: Entities (3110, 3116, 436, 4907); Relationships (1916, 9025, 1919, 1925)]

v.tieu_de: Central Median Strip Use and Article 12 Fines
v.tom_tat: This community centers on the central median strip of a divided road and the specified activities treated as violations when they occupy it: displaying or selling goods, storing construction materials, and parking, watching, or keeping vehicles. Clause 6 of Article 12 identifies these activities as fineable, while a linked road-traffic fine provision states penalties of 500,000–1,000,000 VND for individuals and 1,000,000–2,000,000 VND for organizations. The information describes a focused traffic-regulation and compliance topic; it does not provide evidence about particular violators, enforcement outcomes, or broader effects. [Data: Entities (752, 969, 4534, 1417, 2545); Relationships (3051, 3052, 7806)]
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s practical relevance to road use and regulatory compliance, while the evidence concerns a specific set of violations and fines rather than documented incidents or wider impacts.

phat_hien.tom_tat: The central median strip is the community’s organizing entity
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The central median strip is described as the divider in the middle of a divided road, and as a place whose occupation for specified purposes is prohibited by the cited provision. It is linked to the described violations, making it the central subject of the community. [Data: Entities (752, 1417); Relationships (3051, 3052, 3050, 3055, 3056)]

The data frames the issue as use of this roadway feature, not as a claim about a particular location, person, or enforcement case. [Data: Entities (752, 1417)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 6 identifies the covered activities as fineable violations
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 6 of Article 12 is described as setting fines for specified violations involving occupation of the central median strip. Its relationships identify displaying or selling goods, storing construction materials, and parking, watching, or keeping vehicles as covered activities. [Data: Entities (969); Relationships (3525, 3527, 3528, 3526, 3529)]

The records establish the stated regulatory scope, but do not provide details about how the provision is enforced or whether any particular conduct has resulted in a citation. [Data: Entities (969); Relationships (3525, 3526, 3527, 3528, 3529)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Commercial activity and materials storage are included
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Selling and displaying goods on the central median strip are separately represented as violations, and Clause 6 links both to the fine provision. Leaving construction materials on the strip is also identified as a violation covered by the clause. [Data: Entities (4634, 1407, 4803, 969); Relationships (3054, 3050, 3055, 3527, 3525)]

These records specify types of use subject to the described restriction; they do not indicate the scale or frequency of such activity. [Data: Entities (4634, 1407, 4803)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Several vehicle-related uses are covered
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community distinguishes parking vehicles from watching or keeping vehicles on the central median strip. Both are described as violations, and Clause 6 links each to a fineable offense. [Data: Entities (3539, 5630, 969); Relationships (3053, 3056, 3526, 3529)]

The data therefore describes multiple vehicle-related forms of occupation, without supplying incident counts or evidence about resulting traffic conditions. [Data: Entities (3539, 5630, 2545)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The stated fines vary by whether the violator is an individual or organization
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The road-traffic fine provision is described as part of Article 12, Clause 6 of Decree 168/2024/NĐ-CP. It states a fine range of 500,000–1,000,000 VND for individuals and 1,000,000–2,000,000 VND for organizations for the described violations. [Data: Entities (4534, 969); Relationships (7806)]

The supplied records state these fine ranges but do not provide additional procedural details, exceptions, or information about actual penalties imposed. [Data: Entities (4534)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The evidence supports a focused compliance assessment, not claims about actual offenders
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The records define the location, prohibited categories of use, and associated fine ranges, making the community relevant to understanding the described road-traffic rule. [Data: Entities (752, 969, 4534, 2545); Relationships (3052, 7806)]

No entities or relationships identify specific individuals or organizations that committed these violations, nor do they document enforcement, reputational effects, or technical capabilities. Accordingly, conclusions about those matters are not supported by the supplied data. [Data: Entities (752, 969, 4534); Relationships (7806)]

v.tieu_de: Smart Traffic Permit and License-Plate Violations
v.tom_tat: This community centers on regulatory violations involving smart traffic vehicles and vehicle license plates. It connects three permit-related behaviors—operating without a permit, with an expired permit, or contrary to permit terms—to a broader smart-traffic permit violation, with listed fines for individual and organizational vehicle owners. A second strand covers invalid or unauthorized license plates and unlawful license-plate-altering devices, with separate penalty ranges. Clause 12 is associated with specified vehicle-owner fines, though the records do not fully clarify how all organizational fine entries relate to one another. The information describes legal provisions and penalties; it does not establish that any particular person or organization committed a violation.
v.ly_do_muc_do: The rating reflects the community’s importance as a regulatory framework covering vehicle operation and substantial fines, while the records do not document actual violations or resulting harm.

phat_hien.tom_tat: Permit compliance is the central regulatory theme
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The smart traffic vehicle permit violation is the hub for three specified behaviors: operating without a permit, operating after a permit expires, and operating contrary to permit terms. These are described as distinct ways of violating the operating-permit requirements, rather than evidence that violations have occurred. [Data: Entities (4668, 3375, 3389, 3401); Relationships (9303, 9288, 9297)]

The records associate this permit-related violation with fines for both individual and organizational vehicle owners. [Data: Relationships (7097, 7101)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Listed fines for individual owners vary by violation
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The individual-owner fine entry describes a range of 16,000,000 to 18,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Clause 12 for a specified violation, and 20,000,000 to 26,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the specified license-plate violation. The records treat these as penalties for different specified violations. [Data: Entities (2106); Relationships (3357, 7096)]

The individual fine entry is also linked to unlawful installation or use of a license-plate-altering device, but the relationship itself does not state a penalty amount for that behavior. [Data: Relationships (7098)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Organizational-owner penalties include higher stated ranges
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The organizational vehicle-owner fine entry gives a range of 40,000,000 to 52,000,000 Vietnamese dong for the specified license-plate violation and is linked to the smart traffic permit violation. [Data: Entities (2112); Relationships (7101, 7102)]

A separate organization-owner entry states a fine of 32,000,000 to 36,000,000 Vietnamese dong under Clause 12 for a specified violation. The records do not fully clarify whether this entry and the other organizational fine entry refer to distinct offenses or how their scopes compare. [Data: Entities (2111); Relationships (3358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: License-plate violations form a related but distinct strand
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The community includes operating a vehicle with an invalid or unauthorized license plate, described as using a plate that does not match the registration certificate or was not issued by a competent authority. This violation is linked to a fine of 20,000,000 to 26,000,000 Vietnamese dong for individual owners and 40,000,000 to 52,000,000 Vietnamese dong for organizational owners. [Data: Entities (3350, 2106, 2112); Relationships (7096, 7102)]

Unlawfully installing or using a device to alter a vehicle’s license plate, including on a trailer or semi-trailer, is separately identified as prohibited. It is linked to fine entries for both individual and organizational owners, but the cited relationships do not specify the applicable amounts. [Data: Entities (5241); Relationships (7098, 7103)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: Clause 12 connects specified violations to owner penalties
phat_hien.giai_thich:
Clause 12 is described as part of Article 32 and as providing fines for individuals and organizations that own specified vehicles and violate rules for operating smart traffic vehicles, including rules concerning devices that alter license plates. [Data: Entities (880)]

The relationships associate Clause 12 with individual and organizational fine entries, including the individual range of 16,000,000 to 18,000,000 Vietnamese dong and an organizational range of 32,000,000 to 36,000,000 Vietnamese dong. [Data: Relationships (3357, 3359, 3358)]

phat_hien.tom_tat: The records describe rules and penalties, not enforcement outcomes
phat_hien.giai_thich:
The entities and relationships set out prohibited conduct, owner categories, and fine ranges. They do not identify specific violators, enforcement actions, adjudications, or actual payments, so the information supports an account of the regulatory framework rather than a conclusion that any party has breached it. [Data: Entities (4668, 3350, 5241, 880); Relationships (7097, 7096, 7098)]

The data also does not provide technical specifications or capabilities of smart traffic vehicles or license-plate-altering devices beyond describing the conduct regulated. [Data: Entities (4668, 5241)]

v.tieu_de: Vietnam Law 36/2024/QH15 Road-Traffic Safety Framework
v.tom_tat: This community centers on Vietnam’s Law No. 36/2024/QH15 and the public authorities, service providers, and road users involved in implementing it. The law links Traffic Police and the Traffic Command Center to traffic control, enforcement, and data functions; connects inspection establishments and competent authorities to vehicle inspections and administrative-violation resolution; and sets requirements for driver licensing, training, and level-crossing safety. Government decrees provide related regulatory context. The supplied records describe a broad statutory compliance and safety system, not evidence of a particular violation or adverse conduct by these entities. [Data: Entities (2938, 1205, 5163, 1203, 827); Relationships (4132, 8636, 4093, 2917, 8638)]
